body.text:
nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya
naraṃ caiva narottamam
devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva
tato jayam udīrayet
body.translated_text: Having paid homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men, and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, one should then utter <s>Jaya</s> (the Victory, i.e. the Mahābhārata)

body.text:
dvaipāyanauṣṭhapuṭaniḥsṛtam aprameyaṃ
puṇyaṃ pavitram atha pāpaharaṃ śubhaṃ ca
yo bhārataṃ samadhigacchati vācyamānaṃ
kiṃ tasya puṣkarajalair abhiṣecanena
body.translated_text: Issued from the lips of <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, immeasurable, holy, purifying, sin-removing and auspicious — for one who fully grasps the <s>Bhārata</s> as it is being recited, what need has he of consecration with the waters of <s>Puṣkara</s>?

body.text:
namo vyāsāya gurave
sarvajñāya maharṣaye
pārāśaryāya śāntāya
namo nārāyaṇāya te
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Vyāsa</s>, the teacher, the all-knowing great seer, the son of <s>Parāśara</s>, the tranquil one; homage to you, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

body.text:
kṛtābhiṣekaṃ tanayam
rājñaḥ pārīkṣitasya ha
draṣṭum abhyāyayuḥ prītyā
śaunakādyā maharṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: To behold the son of King <s>Parīkṣit</s>, who had completed his consecration, the great seers headed by <s>Śaunaka</s> came forth with affection

body.text:
tān āgatān sa rājarṣiḥ
pādyārghyādibhir arcitān
sukhopaviṣṭān viśrāntān
kṛtasaṃpraśnasatkathān
body.translated_text: That royal seer, having honored them as they arrived with water for the feet, the guest-offering, and the rest, when they were comfortably seated, rested, and had exchanged courteous inquiries and pleasant talk,

body.text:
tatkathābhiḥ kṛtāhlādaḥ
praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ
śatānīko 'tha papraccha
nārāyaṇakathāṃ parām
body.translated_text: delighted by their conversation, <s>Śatānīka</s>, bowing low with joined palms, then inquired about the supreme tale of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

body.text:
yam āśritya jagannātham
mama pūrvapitāmahāḥ
vipakṣāpahṛtaṃ rājyam
avāpuḥ puruṣottamāḥ
body.translated_text: by taking refuge in whom, the Lord of the world, my forefathers, those best of men, recovered the kingdom that had been seized by their adversaries,

body.text:
drauṇibrahmāstranirdagdho
mama yena pitāmahaḥ
parīkṣit prāṇasaṃyogaṃ
devadevena lambhitaḥ
body.translated_text: by whom — the God of gods — my grandfather <s>Parīkṣit</s>, burned by <s>Droṇi's</s> (the son of Droṇa's) <s>Brahmāstra</s> (Brahma-weapon), was restored to the union with life

body.text:
tasya devasya māhātmyaṃ
devarṣisiddhamanujaiḥ
śrutaṃ subahuśo mayā
stutasyāśeṣajanmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Of that God's greatness, praised through every birth, I have heard very many times from gods, seers, perfected beings, and men

body.text:
kaḥ stotum īśas tam ajaṃ
yasyaitat sacarācaram
avyayasyāprameyasya
brahmāṇḍam udare śayam
body.translated_text: Who is able to praise that unborn one, in whose belly rests this whole world with all that moves and is still, the imperishable, the immeasurable, the cosmic egg (<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>)?

body.text:
rudraḥ krodhodbhavo yasya
prasādāc ca pitāmahaḥ
tasya devasya kaḥ śaktaḥ
pravaktuṃ vā vibhūtayaḥ
body.translated_text: He from whose wrath <s>Rudra</s> arose and from whose favor the Grandsire (<s>Brahmā</s>) came to be — who is able to declare the powers of that God?

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi devasya
tasya sarvātmanaḥ prabhoḥ
śrotum ārādhanaṃ yena
nistareyaṃ bhavārṇavam
body.translated_text: So I wish to hear the means of worshipping that God, the Lord whose self is all, by which I might cross over the ocean of worldly existence,

body.text:
kenopāyena mantrair vā
rahasyaiḥ paricaryayā
dānair vratopavāsair vā
japyair homair athāpi vā
body.translated_text: by what means, or by <s>mantras</s>, by secret rites, by attendant service, by gifts, by vows and fasts, or by recitations, or even by oblations,

body.text:
ārādhitaḥ samastānāṃ
kleśānāṃ hānido hariḥ
śakyaḥ samārādhayituṃ
tan naḥ śaṃsata sattamāḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, when worshipped, the remover of all afflictions, is able to be propitiated — declare that to us, O most excellent ones

body.text:
vidyānām api sā vidyā
śrutānām api tac chrutam
rahasyānāṃ rahasyaṃ tad
yena viṣṇuḥ prasīdati
body.translated_text: Of sciences that is the science, of scriptures that is the scripture, of secrets that is the secret, by which <s>Viṣṇu</s> is made gracious

body.text:
mantrāṇāṃ paramo mantro
vratānāṃ tan mahāvratam
upoṣitaṃ hi tac chreṣṭhaṃ
yena tuṣyati keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: Of <s>mantras</s> the supreme <s>mantra</s>, of vows that great vow, that fasting is the best, by which <s>Keśava</s> is satisfied

body.text:
sā jihvā yā hariṃ stauti
tac cittaṃ yat tadarpaṇam
tāv eva kevalau ślāghyau
yau tatpūjākarau karau
body.translated_text: That tongue alone which praises <s>Hari</s>, that mind which offers itself to him — those two alone are praiseworthy, the two hands that perform his worship

body.text:
sujanma deham atyantaṃ
tad evāśeṣajanmasu
yad eva pulakodbhāsi
viṣṇor nāmābhikīrtanāt
body.translated_text: That birth is a noble birth, surpassing among all births, which becomes thrilled with horripilation from the loud proclaiming of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> name

body.text:
sā hānis tan mahac chidraṃ
sā cāndhajaḍamūkatā
yan muhūrtaṃ kṣaṇaṃ vāpi
vāsudevo na cintyate
body.translated_text: That is the loss, that the great flaw, that the blindness, dullness, and dumbness, when for a moment or even an instant <s>Vāsudeva</s> is not contemplated

body.text:
nūnaṃ tat kaṇṭhaśālūkam
athavā pratijihvikā
rogo vānyo na sā jihvā
yā na vakti harer guṇān
body.translated_text: Surely that is a swelling in the throat, or a second tongue, or some other disease — it is not a tongue, that one which does not speak the virtues of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
santy anekā bilās tadvac
śrotram apy alpamedhasām
dattvāvadhānaṃ yac chabde
vinaiva harisaṃstutim
body.translated_text: Like that there are many holes that serve as the ear too of the dull-witted, who lend attention to sound without any praise of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
dharmārthakāmasaṃprāptau
puruṣāṇāṃ viceṣṭitam
janmany aviphalā saikā
yā govindāśrayā kriyā
body.translated_text: In the attainment of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), among the strivings of men, that one act alone in a lifetime is not fruitless which takes refuge in <s>Govinda</s>

body.text:
durgasaṃsārakāntāram
apāram abhidhāvatām
ekaḥ kṛṣṇanamaskāro
muktitīrasya deśikaḥ
body.translated_text: For those running across the impassable, shoreless wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), a single act of homage to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the guide to the far shore of liberation

body.text:
sarvaratnamayo meruḥ
sarvāścaryamayaṃ nabhaḥ
sarvatīrthamayī gaṅgā
sarvadevamayo hariḥ
body.translated_text: Made of all jewels is <s>Meru</s>, made of all wonders is the sky, made of all sacred fords is the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, made of all gods is <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
evam ādiguṇo bhogaḥ
kṛṣṇasyādbhutakarmaṇaḥ
śruto me bahuśo siddhaiḥ
gīyamānas tathāparaiḥ
body.translated_text: Such, beginning with these qualities, is the enjoyment of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of wondrous deeds, heard by me many times from perfected beings, and sung likewise by others

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi taṃ devaṃ
sarvalokaparāyaṇam
nārāyaṇam aśeṣasya
jagato hṛdy avasthitam
body.translated_text: So I wish to worship that God, the supreme refuge of all worlds, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who abides in the heart of the entire universe,

body.text:
ārādhayitum īśānam
anantam amitaujasam
śaṃkaraṃ jagataḥ prāṇaṃ
smṛtamātrāghahāriṇam
body.translated_text: the Lord, the infinite one, of boundless might, the bestower of peace, the life-breath of the world, who removes sin by the mere recollection of him

body.text:
tan mamādya muniśreṣṭhāḥ
prasādayitum icchataḥ
upadeśapradānena
prasādaṃ kartum arhata
body.translated_text: Therefore today, O most excellent of sages, to me who wish to propitiate him, you ought to do a favor by granting instruction

body.text:
tasyaitad vacanaṃ śrutvā
bhaktim udvahato hareḥ
paritoṣaṃ paraṃ jagmur
munayaḥ sarva eva te
body.translated_text: Hearing this speech of his who bore devotion to <s>Hari</s>, all those sages without exception came to the highest satisfaction

body.text:
sarve ca te muniśreṣṭhā
bhṛguśreṣṭhaṃ ca śaunakam
yathārthaṃ bhagavaṃs tasmai
kathyatām ity acodayan
body.translated_text: And all those most excellent sages urged <s>Śaunaka</s>, the best of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, saying: 'O lord, let it be told to him as it truly is'

body.text:
sarvajñānanidhiḥ sphītas
tvam atra bhṛgunandana
trailokyasarvasaṃdeha-
tamodīpas tapodhana
body.translated_text: 'You are here an abundant treasure-house of all knowledge, O son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>; you are the lamp dispelling the darkness of all doubts in the three worlds, O you rich in austerity'

body.text:
evam ukto munivaraiḥ
prītyā tasya ca bhūpateḥ
bhaktyā ca devadevasya
pravaṇīkṛtamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by the best of sages, his mind made well-disposed by affection for that king and by devotion to the God of gods,

body.text:
kṛtvottarīyaparyaṅkaṃ
śithilaṃ bhagavān atha
pratyuvāca mahābhāgaḥ
śaunakas taṃ mahīpatim
body.translated_text: having made his upper garment into a loose couch-seat, the blessed and greatly fortunate <s>Śaunaka</s> then replied to that lord of the earth:

body.text:
yat pṛcchasi mahīpāla
kṛṣṇasyārādhanaṃ prati
vratopavāsajapyādi
tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: 'What you ask, O protector of the earth, concerning the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — the vows, fasts, recitations, and the rest — hear that here with one-pointed mind'

body.text:
anādimat paraṃ brahma
sarvaheyavivarjitam
vyāpi yat sarvabhūteṣu
sthitaṃ sadasataḥ param
body.translated_text: The supreme <s>Brahman</s>, beginningless, free from all that is to be discarded, all-pervading, which abides in all beings, beyond the existent and the non-existent,

body.text:
pradhānapuṃsor ajayor
yataḥ kṣobhaḥ pravartate
nityayor vyāpinoś caiva
jagadādau mahātmanoḥ
body.translated_text: from whom, the two great souls — <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the <s>Puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), both unborn, eternal, and pervading — there arises agitation at the beginning of the world,

body.text:
tatkṣobhakatvād brahmāṇḍa-
sṛṣṭihetur nirañjanaḥ
ahetur api sarvātmanaḥ
jāyate parameśvaraḥ
body.translated_text: by his agitating of those two, the stainless one becomes, without cause, though the cause of the creation of the cosmic egg, the Supreme Lord whose self is all,

body.text:
pradhānapuruṣatvaṃ ca
tathaiveśvaralīlayā
samupaiti tataś caiva
brahmatvaṃ chandataḥ prabhuḥ
body.translated_text: and likewise by the divine play (<s>līlā</s>) of the Lord he assumes the state of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, and thence the Lord, at will, the state of <s>Brahmā</s>

body.text:
tataḥ sthitau pālayitā
viṣṇutvaṃ jagataḥ kṣaye
rudratvaṃ ca jagannāthaḥ
svecchayā kurute 'vyayaḥ
body.translated_text: Then in maintenance he is the protector, in the dissolution of the world the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the state of <s>Rudra</s> — the imperishable Lord of the world does this by his own will

body.text:
tad ekam akṣaraṃ dhāma
paraṃ sadasator mahat
bhedābhedasvarūpasthaṃ
praṇipatya paraṃ padam
body.translated_text: Having paid homage to that one imperishable abode, supreme, great, beyond the existent and non-existent, abiding in the form of both difference and non-difference, the supreme state,

body.text:
pravakṣyāmi yathā pūrvaṃ
matpitrā kathitaṃ mama
tasyāpi kila tatpitrā
tasmai cāha kilośanāḥ
body.translated_text: I shall declare it as it was formerly told to me by my father, and to him too by his father, and to him <s>Uśanas</s> declared it,

body.text:
tenāpi bhṛgum ārādhya
prāptam ārādhanaṃ hareḥ
sakāśād brahmaṇaḥ prāptaṃ
bhṛguṇāpi mahātmanā
body.translated_text: and he too, having worshipped <s>Bhṛgu</s>, obtained the worship of <s>Hari</s>; and it was obtained by the great soul <s>Bhṛgu</s> too from the presence of <s>Brahmā</s>,

body.text:
marīcimiśraiś ca purā
param etan maharṣibhiḥ
prāptaṃ sakāśād devasya
brahmaṇo vyaktajanmanaḥ
body.translated_text: and formerly this supreme thing was obtained by the great seers, <s>Marīci</s> and the rest, from the presence of the God <s>Brahmā</s> of manifest birth

body.text:
yogaṃ brahmā paraṃ prāha
maharṣīṇāṃ yadā prabhuḥ
samastavṛttisaṃrodhāt
kaivalyapratipādakam
body.translated_text: When the lord <s>Brahmā</s> declared to the great seers the supreme <s>yoga</s>, which through the restraint of all mental activity brings about <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation, liberation),

body.text:
tadā jagatpatir brahmā
praṇipatya maharṣibhiḥ
sarvaiḥ kilokto bhagavān
ātmayoniḥ prajāhitam
body.translated_text: then the lord <s>Brahmā</s>, master of the world, the self-born, having been bowed to by all the great seers, was addressed by them for the welfare of creatures:

body.text:
yo yogo bhavatā prokto
manovṛttinirodhajaḥ
prāptuṃ śakyaḥ sa tv anekaiḥ
janmabhir jagataḥ pate
body.translated_text: 'The <s>yoga</s> that has been declared by you, born of the restraint of mental activity — it is able to be attained, O lord of the world, only through many births'

body.text:
viṣayā durjayā nṝṇām
indriyākarṣaṇāḥ prabho
vṛttayaś cetasaś cāpi
capalā cātidurdharāḥ
body.translated_text: 'The sense-objects are hard for men to conquer, O lord, drawing away the senses; and the activities of the mind too are fickle and exceedingly hard to hold'

body.text:
rāgādayaḥ kathaṃ jetuṃ
śakyā varṣaśatair api
na yogayogyaṃ hi mano
bhavaty ebhir anirjitaiḥ
body.translated_text: 'How can passion and the rest be conquered even in a hundred years? For the mind does not become fit for <s>yoga</s> while these remain unconquered'

body.text:
alpāyuṣaś ca puruṣā
brahman kṛtayuge 'py amī
tretāyāṃ dvāpare caiva
kimu prāpte kalau yuge
body.translated_text: 'And men are short-lived, O <s>Brahman</s>, even in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, in the <s>Tretā</s> and the <s>Dvāpara</s> too — how much more when the <s>Kali</s> age has come?'

body.text:
bhagavaṃs tvam upāyajñaḥ
prasanno vaktum arhasi
anāyāsena yenemam
uttarema bhavārṇavam
body.translated_text: 'O blessed one, you know the means; being gracious, you ought to declare by what means we may cross over this ocean of existence without exertion'

body.text:
duḥkhāmbumagnāḥ puruṣāḥ
prāpya brahma mahāplavam
uttareyur bhavāmbhodhiṃ
tathā tvam anucintaya
body.translated_text: 'Men sunk in the waters of sorrow, having obtained <s>Brahman</s> as a great raft, may cross over the ocean of existence — so do you devise it'

body.text:
evam uktas tadā brahmā
kriyāyogaṃ mahātmanām
teṣām ṛṣīṇām ācaṣṭa
narāṇāṃ hitakāmyayā
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Brahmā</s> then declared to those seers the <s>Kriyāyoga</s> (the yoga of ritual action) of the great souls, out of desire for the welfare of men:

body.text:
ārādhayata viśveśam
nārāyaṇam atandritāḥ
bāhyālambanasāpekṣās
tam ajaṃ jagataḥ patim
body.translated_text: 'Worship the Lord of all, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, untiringly; relying on external supports, that unborn lord of the world,'

body.text:
ijyāpūjānamaskāra-
śuśrūṣābhir aharniśam
vratopavāsair vividhair
brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: 'by sacrifice, worship, homage, and service day and night, by various vows and fasts, and by gratifying the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,'

body.text:
tais taiś cābhimataiḥ kāmair
ye ca cetasi tuṣṭidāḥ
aparicchedyamāhātmyam
ārādhayata keśavam
body.translated_text: 'by these and those desired objects of longing which give satisfaction to the mind — worship <s>Keśava</s> whose greatness cannot be measured'

body.text:
tanniṣṭhās tadgatadhiyas
tatkarmāṇas tadāśrayāḥ
taddṛṣṭayas tanmanasaḥ
sarvasmin sa iti sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Devoted to him, with minds fixed on him, doing his works, taking refuge in him, with eyes upon him and minds upon him — he abides as in all'

body.text:
samastāny atha karmāṇi
tatra sarvātmanātmani
saṃnyasyadhvaṃ sa vaḥ kartā
samastāvaraṇakṣayam
body.translated_text: 'Then renounce all your actions there in the Self that is the soul of all; he is your doer, the destroyer of every covering'

body.text:
etat tad akṣaraṃ brahma
pradhānapuruṣāv ubhau
yato yasmin yathā cobhau
sarvavyāpiny avasthitau
body.translated_text: 'This is that imperishable <s>Brahman</s>; both <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, from whom, in whom, and how both abide pervading all'

body.text:
paraḥ parāṇāṃ paramaḥ
sa ekaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
yasyābhinnam idaṃ sarvam
yac ceṅgaṃ yac ca neṅgati
body.translated_text: 'The supreme of the supreme, the highest, that one <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person), from whom all this is not separate, both what moves and what does not move'

body.text:
tam ārādhya jagannāthaṃ
mokṣakāraṇam avyaktam
acintyam aparigraham
kriyāyogena mucyate
body.translated_text: 'Having worshipped that Lord of the world, the cause of liberation, the unmanifest, the inconceivable, the unattached, one is freed through <s>Kriyāyoga</s>'

body.text:
iti te brahmaṇaḥ śrutvā
rahasyam ṛṣisattamāḥ
narāṇām upakārāya
yogaśāstrāṇi cakrire
kriyāyogaparāṇīha
muktikāryāṇy anekaśaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, O most excellent of seers, having heard this secret from <s>Brahmā</s>, for the benefit of men they composed the <s>yoga-śāstras</s>, devoted to <s>Kriyāyoga</s> here, performing the works of liberation in many ways

body.text:
ārādhyate jagannātho
yadanuṣṭhānatatparaiḥ
paramātmā hṛṣīkeśaḥ
sarveśaḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ
body.translated_text: The Lord of the world is worshipped by those intent on its practice — the Supreme Self, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the Lord of all, the source of all being

body.text:
tāni te nṛpaśārdūla
sarvapāpaharāṇy aham
vakṣyāmi śrūyatām anyad
rahasyam idam uttamam
body.translated_text: Those I shall declare to you, O tiger among kings, as removers of all sin; let another supreme secret be heard

body.text:
saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ
viṣayākrāntacetasām
uttāram icchatāṃ tasmād
bhṛśaṃ yan nāntarair api
viṣṇupotaṃ vinā nānyat
kiṃcid asti parāyaṇam
body.translated_text: For those sunk in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose minds are overpowered by sense-objects, who desire deliverance therefrom — without the ship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> there is nothing else, no supreme refuge even among the innermost things

body.text:
uttiṣṭhaṃś cintaya hariṃ
vrajaṃś cintaya keśavam
bhuñjaṃś cintaya govindam
svapaṃś cintaya mādhavam
body.translated_text: Rising, contemplate <s>Hari</s>; walking, contemplate <s>Keśava</s>; eating, contemplate <s>Govinda</s>; sleeping, contemplate <s>Mādhava</s>

body.text:
evam ekāgracittas tvaṃ
saṃśrito madhusūdanam
janmamṛtyujarāgrāhaṃ
saṃsārāmbhas tariṣyasi
body.translated_text: Thus, with one-pointed mind, having taken refuge in <s>Madhusūdana</s>, you shall cross over the waters of <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose crocodiles are birth, death, and old age

body.text:
anantam īḍyaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ
jagadvidhātāram ajaṃ janitryam
samāśritā ye harim īśitāraṃ
teṣāṃ bhavo nāsti hi muktibhājām
body.translated_text: The infinite, the praiseworthy, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>, the maker of the world, the unborn, the source of birth — those who have taken refuge in <s>Hari</s>, the Lord, for them, sharing in liberation, there is indeed no rebirth

body.text:
śrūyatāṃ kuruśārdūla
saṃvādo 'yam anuttamaḥ
ambarīṣasya rājarṣeḥ
saha devena cakriṇā
body.translated_text: Let it be heard, O tiger of the <s>Kurus</s>, this unsurpassed dialogue between the royal seer <s>Ambarīṣa</s> and the God who bears the discus

body.text:
ambarīṣo mahīpālaḥ
pālayann eva medinīm
udvigna eva dvandvāntam
abhīpsuḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
body.translated_text: King <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, even while protecting the earth, was troubled, that bull among men, desiring the end of the pairs of opposites (<s>dvandva</s>)

body.text:
devadevāt sa govindād
abhīpsur dvandvasaṃkṣayam
tapas tepe nirāhāro
gṛṇan brahma sanātanam
body.translated_text: Desiring the cessation of the pairs of opposites from the God of gods <s>Govinda</s>, he performed austerity, fasting, reciting the eternal <s>Brahman</s>

body.text:
tasya kālena mahatā
bhaktim udvahataḥ parām
tutoṣa bhagavān viṣṇuḥ
sarvalokapatiḥ prabhuḥ
body.translated_text: After a long time, with him bearing supreme devotion, the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord and master of all worlds, was pleased

body.text:
sa rūpam aindram āsthāya
tam uvāca mahīpatim
meghagambhīranirghoṣo
vāraṇendragatis tadā
body.translated_text: He, assuming the form of <s>Indra</s>, then spoke to that king, with a voice deep as a thundercloud and the gait of the lordly elephant:

body.text:
rājarṣe vada yat kāryaṃ
tava cetasy avasthitam
varado 'ham anuprāpto
varaṃ varaya suvrata
body.translated_text: 'O royal seer, declare what task abides in your mind; I have come as a bestower of boons — choose a boon, O you of good vows'

body.text:
evam uktas tato rājā
vilokya ca puraṃdaraṃ
pratyuvācārghyam udyamya
svāgataṃ te 'stv iti prabho
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the king, beholding <s>Purandara</s> (Indra), replied, raising the guest-offering: 'Welcome to you, O lord'

body.text:
nāham ārādhayāmi tvāṃ
tava baddho 'yam añjaliḥ
varārthināṃ tvaṃ varadaḥ
prayacchābhimatān varān
body.translated_text: 'I do not worship you; this joined-palm gesture is bound for you; you are the bestower of boons to those who seek boons — grant the desired boons'

body.text:
varārthāya tvayānyaiś ca
kriyate nṛpate tapaḥ
sa kim arthaṃ tvam asmatto
na gṛhṇāsy abhivāṃchitam
body.translated_text: 'For the sake of boons austerity is performed by you and by others, O king; why then do you not accept from us what is desired?'

body.text:
na varārtham ayaṃ yatnas
tvatto devapate mama
viṣṇor ārādhanārthāya
viddhi māṃ tvaṃ kṛtodyamam
body.translated_text: 'This effort of mine is not for the sake of a boon from you, O lord of the gods; know me to be one who has made his exertion for the sake of worshipping <s>Viṣṇu</s>'

body.text:
ahaṃ hi sarvadevānāṃ
trailokyasya tatheśvaraḥ
pālayanti mamaivājñām
ādityādyāḥ sadā surāḥ
body.translated_text: 'For I am the Lord of all the gods and likewise of the three worlds; the <s>Ādityas</s> and the rest, the gods, ever obey my command'

body.text:
ādityā vasavo rudrā
nāsatyau marutāṃ gaṇāḥ
prajānāṃ patayaḥ sādhyā
viśvedevā maharṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the two <s>Nāsatyas</s>, the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, the lords of creatures, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the great seers,'

body.text:
kurvanty ete mamaivājñāṃ
siddhagandharvapannagāḥ
matto hi ko 'nyo varadaḥ
pratigṛhṇīṣva vāñchitam
body.translated_text: 'these obey my very command, the <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Pannagas</s>; for who other than me is a bestower of boons? Accept what is desired'

body.text:
tvam indraḥ satyam evaitad
devas tribhuvaneśvaraḥ
tvayāpi prāptam aiśvaryaṃ
yatas taṃ toṣayāmy aham
body.translated_text: 'You are <s>Indra</s>, this is true, the god, lord of the three worlds; but the sovereignty obtained even by you comes from him whom I satisfy'

body.text:
trailokyaṃ tava deveśa
vaśe yasya mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: 'The three worlds are in the power, O lord of gods, of that great soul,'

body.text:
saptodare śayā lokās
tam īśaṃ toṣayāmy aham
body.translated_text: 'within whose seven-fold belly the worlds rest — that Lord I satisfy'

body.text:
yasya tvam amaraiḥ sarvaiḥ
samavetāḥ sureśvara
dehaprāpto 'ntarastho vai
taṃ namāmi janārdanam
body.translated_text: 'He of whom you, together with all the immortals assembled, O lord of gods, are embodied and dwelling within — to that <s>Janārdana</s> I bow'

body.text:
nimeṣo brahmaṇo rātrir
unmeṣo yasya vāsaraḥ
tam īḍyam īśam ajaraṃ
praṇato 'smi janārdanam
body.translated_text: 'Whose closing of the eyes is the night of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose opening is the day — to that praiseworthy, undecaying Lord <s>Janārdana</s> I am bowed down'

body.text:
yo hartā jagato devaḥ
kartā pālāyitā ca yaḥ
trayasyāsya ca yo yonis
taṃ viṣṇuṃ toṣayāmy aham
body.translated_text: 'The God who is the destroyer of the world, who is the maker and protector, and who is the source of this triad — that <s>Viṣṇu</s> I satisfy'

body.text:
hiraṇyakaśipuḥ pūrvaṃ
hiraṇyākṣaś ca te ripuḥ
tavānukampayā yena
hatau daityau nato 'smi tam
body.translated_text: '<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> formerly, and <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, were your enemies; by whom, through your compassion, the two <s>Daityas</s> were slain — to him I bow'

body.text:
balināpahṛtaṃ śakra
dattaṃ yena purā tava
trailokyarājyaṃ taṃ baddhvā
taṃ namāmi janārdanam
body.translated_text: He by whom the kingdom of the three worlds, once seized by <s>Bali</s>, was given to you, O <s>Śakra</s>, having bound him — to that <s>Janārdana</s> I bow

body.text:
prasīda śakra gaccha tvam
aham apy atra saṃsthitaḥ
tapas tapsye jagannāthaṃ
draṣṭuṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O <s>Śakra</s>, and go; I too shall remain here and perform <s>tapas</s> (austerity), to behold the Lord of the world, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
evam uktas tatas tena
śakrarūpī janārdanaḥ
punar apy āha taṃ kopāt
pārthivaṃ tapasi sthitam
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by him, <s>Janārdana</s> in the form of <s>Śakra</s> again spoke in anger to that king who was fixed in austerity

body.text:
yadi madvacanād adya
na bhavāṃs tyakṣyate tapaḥ
vajraṃ te prahariṣyāmi
budhyasvaitad yadīcchasi
body.translated_text: If today, at my word, you will not abandon your austerity, I shall hurl my <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) at you — understand this, if you wish

body.text:
nāpy alpam aparādhaṃ te
karomi tridaśeśvara
tathāpi vadhayogyaṃ māṃ
manyase cet kṣipāyudham
body.translated_text: I do you no offence, even a small one, O lord of the thirty gods; yet if you think me deserving of death, hurl your weapon

body.text:
śrūyate kila govinde
bhaktim udvahatāṃ nṛṇām
saṃsārārṇāvabhītānāṃ
tridaśāḥ paripanthinaḥ
body.translated_text: It is heard indeed that for men who bear devotion to <s>Govinda</s>, who fear the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), the gods themselves are adversaries

body.text:
tāpaso 'haṃ kva niḥsaṅgaḥ
kva ca kopas tavedṛśaḥ
vijñātam etad govinda-
bhaktivighnopapāditam
body.translated_text: I am an ascetic, free of attachment — where is such anger of yours? This I have understood: it is contrived as an obstacle to devotion to <s>Govinda</s>

body.text:
bhavanti bahavo vighnā
nare śreyaḥparāyaṇe
govindabhaktyabhyadhikaṃ
śreyaś cānyan na vidyate
body.translated_text: Many are the obstacles for a man intent upon his highest good; and there is no other good greater than devotion to <s>Govinda</s>

body.text:
sa tvaṃ prahara vā mā vā
mayi vajraṃ puraṃdara
nāham utsṛjya govindam
anyam ārādhayāmi bhoḥ
body.translated_text: So, whether you hurl your <s>vajra</s> at me or not, O <s>Puraṃdara</s>, I will not forsake <s>Govinda</s> and worship another, ho!

body.text:
na cāpi vajraṃ vajrī vā
tvaṃ ca nānye surāsurāḥ
śaktā nihantum īśāne
hṛdayasthe janārdane
body.translated_text: Neither the thunderbolt nor you, the wielder of the thunderbolt, nor any other gods or demons are able to slay one in whose heart the Lord <s>Janārdana</s> abides

body.text:
kiṃ ca no bahunoktena
nāhaṃ vakṣyāmy ataḥ paraṃ
yathepsitaṃ kuruṣva tvaṃ
kariṣye 'ham abhīpsitam
body.translated_text: Moreover, what use is much speaking? I shall say nothing beyond this. Do as you wish; I shall do as I desire

body.text:
evam uktvā surapatiṃ
pārthivaḥ sa punas tapaḥ
cacāra maunam āsthāya
tenātuṣyata keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the lord of the gods, the king again performed austerity, observing silence; and by this <s>Keśava</s> was pleased

body.text:
saṃdarśayām āsa tataḥ
svaṃ vapuḥ kaiṭabhārdanaḥ
caturbhujam udārāṅgaṃ
śaṅkhacakragadādharam
body.translated_text: Then the slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> revealed his own form — four-armed, with noble limbs, bearing conch, discus, and mace

body.text:
kirīṭasragdharaṃ spaṣṭaṃ
nīlotpaladalacchavim
airāvataś ca garuḍas
tatkṣaṇāt samadṛśyata
body.translated_text: wearing diadem and garland, manifest, of the hue of the petal of a blue lotus; and in that instant <s>Airāvata</s> and <s>Garuḍa</s> were seen

body.text:
sa ca rājavaro devaṃ
pītavāsasam acyutam
vilokya bhaktiśirasā
sahasaiva mahīṃ yayau
body.translated_text: And that best of kings, beholding the god <s>Acyuta</s> clad in yellow garments, with devotion-bowed head fell at once upon the earth

body.text:
pratyuvāca ca bhūpālaḥ
praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ
romāñcitatanuḥ stotram
padmanābhaṃ tato 'stuvat
body.translated_text: And the king replied, prostrating with folded hands, his body thrilled with rapture; then he praised <s>Padmanābha</s> with this hymn of praise

body.text:
ādideva jayājeya
jaya sargādikāraka
jayāspaṣṭaprakāśāṇḍa
bṛhanmūrte jayākṣara
body.translated_text: Victory, O primal God, O unconquerable; victory, O maker of creation and the rest; victory, O you whose cosmic egg shines unmanifest, O vast-formed one; victory, O imperishable one

body.text:
jaya sarvagatācintya
jaya janmajarāpaha
jaya vyāpiñ jayābheda
sarvabhūteṣv avasthita
body.translated_text: Victory, O all-pervading, inconceivable one; victory, O remover of birth and old age; victory, O pervader; victory, O undivided one, established in all beings

body.text:
jaya yajñapate nātha
havyakavyāśanāvyaya
jaya vijñātasiddhānta
māyāmohaka keśava
body.translated_text: Victory, O lord of sacrifice, O master, O imperishable consumer of <s>havya</s> and <s>kavya</s> (offerings to gods and ancestors); victory, O you who know the established doctrine, O bewilderer through <s>māyā</s> (illusion), <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
lokasthityartham anagha
varāha jaya bhūdhara
nṛsiṃha jaya devāri-
vakṣaḥsthalavidāraṇa
body.translated_text: For the sake of the world's stability, O sinless one, O <s>Varāha</s> (boar), victory, O upholder of the earth; O <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> (man-lion), victory, O render of the breast of the enemy of the gods

body.text:
devānām aribhītānām
ārtināśana vāmana
jaya krāntasamastorvī-
nabhaḥsvarlokabhāvana
body.translated_text: O <s>Vāmana</s> (dwarf), destroyer of the distress of the gods who feared their foes, victory; victory, O you who brought into being the whole earth, sky, and heavenly world by your strides

body.text:
jitaṃ te jagatām īśa
jitaṃ te sarva sarvada
body.translated_text: Victory to you, O lord of the worlds; victory to you, O all, O ever-giving one

body.text:
jitaṃ te sarvabhūteśa
yogidhyeya namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: Victory to you, O lord of all beings, O you who are to be meditated upon by <s>yogins</s>; homage be to you

body.text:
namo 'stv avyapadeśyāya
namaḥ sūkṣmasvarūpiṇe
namas trimūrtaye tubhyaṃ
viśvamūrte namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: Homage to the indefinable one; homage to him of subtle nature; homage to you, the triple-formed one; O you whose form is the universe, homage be to you

body.text:
brahmādyaiś cintyate rūpaṃ
yat tat sadasataḥ paraṃ
viśeṣair aviśeṣyāya
tasmai tubhyaṃ namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: That form which is conceived by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, which is beyond the existent and non-existent — to that you, beyond distinction through distinctions, homage and homage again

body.text:
puruṣākhyaṃ tato rūpaṃ
nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca
prakṛteḥ parataḥ sūkṣmaṃ
tan namasyāmi te hare
body.translated_text: That form called <s>Puruṣa</s>, without qualities yet the enjoyer of qualities, subtle, beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) — that of yours I salute, O <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
avyaktādiviśeṣāntam
atisūkṣmatamaṃ mahat
prākṛtaṃ tava tad rūpaṃ
tasmai deva namāmy aham
body.translated_text: That natural form of yours, the great one, most exceedingly subtle, extending from the unmanifest to the differentiated — to that, O god, I bow

body.text:
rūpair nānāvidhair yaś ca
tadrūpāntaragocaram
līlayā vyavahāras te
tasmai devātmane namaḥ
body.translated_text: He whose play it is, through forms of various kinds, to engage in conduct within the range of those forms — to that one who is the Self of the gods, homage

body.text:
prasīda viṣṇo govinda
śaṅkhacakragadādhara
dharādharāravindākṣa
vāsudeva maheśvara
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O <s>Govinda</s>, bearer of conch, discus, and mace, upholder of the earth, lotus-eyed one, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, great Lord

body.text:
itthaṃ stuto jagannāthaḥ
proktavān iti keśavaḥ
ambarīṣaṃ pṛthivīśaṃ
jagat saṃnādayan girā
body.translated_text: Thus praised, the Lord of the world, <s>Keśava</s>, spoke thus to <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, the lord of the earth, making the world resound with his voice

body.text:
ambarīṣa prasanno 'smi
bhaktyā stotreṇa cānagha
varaṃ vṛṇīṣva dharmajña
yat te manasi vartate
body.translated_text: O <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, I am pleased by your devotion and your hymn, O sinless one; choose a boon, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, whatever is in your mind

body.text:
eṣa eva varaḥ ślāghyo
yad dṛṣṭo 'si jagatpate
tvaddarśanam apuṇyānāṃ
svapneṣv api hi durlabham
body.translated_text: This indeed is the praiseworthy boon, that you have been seen, O Lord of the world; for the sight of you is, even in dreams, hard to attain for those without merit

body.text:
bālyāt prabhṛti yā deva
tvayi bhaktir mamācyuta
vetti tāṃ bhagavān eva
hṛdisthaḥ sarvadehinām
body.translated_text: The devotion which I have had toward you, O god, from childhood onward, O <s>Acyuta</s> — the Lord himself knows it, who abides in the heart of all embodied beings

body.text:
tvatprasādān mameśāna
rājyam avyāhataṃ bhuvi
kośadaṇḍau tathātīva
śarīrārogyam uttamam
body.translated_text: By your grace, O Lord, my kingdom on earth is unobstructed; likewise my treasury and army are abundant, and my bodily health excellent

body.text:
striyo 'nnapānasāmarthyā
hāniḥ svalpāpi nāsti me
balaṃ nāgasahasrasya
dhārayāmy arisūdana
body.translated_text: Women, and the capacity for food and drink — I have not even the slightest loss of these; I bear the strength of a thousand elephants, O slayer of foes

body.text:
saṃtatir nibhṛtā bhṛtyā
sānurāgāś ca me janāḥ
dharmahāniś ca deveśa
na hi me pālane bhuvaḥ
body.translated_text: My lineage is secure, my servants devoted, and the people affectionate toward me; nor is there any decline of <s>dharma</s>, O lord of the gods, in my protection of the earth

body.text:
yad yad icchāmy ahaṃ tat tat
sarvam asti jagatpate
etenaivānumānena
prasanno bhagavān iti
body.translated_text: Whatever I desire, all that I have, O Lord of the world; by this very inference I conclude that the Lord is pleased

body.text:
jñātaṃ mayā hi govinde
nāprasanne vibhūtayaḥ
evaṃ sarvasukhāhlāda-
madhyastho 'pi ca keśava
body.translated_text: For I have understood that prosperity does not arise when <s>Govinda</s> is not pleased; yet, O <s>Keśava</s>, though I dwell amid all the delights of pleasure,

body.text:
punarāvṛttiduḥkhānāṃ
trāsād udvignamānasaḥ
mayi prasādābhimukhaṃ
manas te yadi keśava
tan mām agādhe saṃsāre
magnam uddhartum arhasi
body.translated_text: my mind is agitated through fear of the sorrows of repeated rebirth; if your mind, O <s>Keśava</s>, is inclined toward grace upon me, then you ought to lift me, sunk in the fathomless ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>

body.text:
sukhāni tāni naivānte
yeṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ na tat sukham
yad ante duḥkham āgāmi
kiṃpākasyaiva bhakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: Those pleasures are not so at the end; their pleasure is not pleasure whose end brings coming sorrow — like the eating of the <s>kiṃpāka</s> fruit

body.text:
sa prasādaṃ kuru guro
jagatām tvaṃ janārdana
jñānadānena yenemāṃ
vāgurān nistaremahi
body.translated_text: Show your grace, O teacher, O <s>Janārdana</s> of the worlds, by the gift of knowledge, whereby we may cross beyond this snare

body.text:
ity uktas tasya govindaḥ
kathayām āsa yogavit
yogaṃ nirbījam atyanta-
duḥkhasaṃyogabheṣajam
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Govinda</s>, the knower of <s>yoga</s>, taught him the seedless <s>yoga</s> (<s>nirbīja yoga</s>), the remedy for the utterly painful bondage of sorrow

body.text:
upadiṣṭe tato yoge
praṇipatyācyutaṃ nṛpaḥ
punaḥ prāha mahābāhur
vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, the <s>yoga</s> having been imparted, the king, prostrating to <s>Acyuta</s>, the mighty-armed one, spoke again, standing bowed in humility

body.text:
devadeva tvayā yogo
yaḥ prokto madhusūdana
naiṣa prāpyo mayā nānyair
mānavair ajitendriyaiḥ
body.translated_text: O god of gods, the <s>yoga</s> which you have declared, O <s>Madhusūdana</s> — this is not attainable by me nor by other men whose senses are unconquered

body.text:
viṣayā durjayāḥ puṃbhir
indriyākarṣiṇaḥ sadā
indriyāṇāṃ jayaṃ teṣu
kaḥ śaktānāṃ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: The sense-objects, ever drawing the senses, are hard for men to conquer; who among those subject to the senses will achieve victory over them?

body.text:
ahaṃ mameti cākhyāti
durjayaṃ cañcalaṃ manaḥ
rāgādayaḥ kathaṃ jetuṃ
śakyā janmāntarair api
body.translated_text: The mind, hard to conquer and fickle, proclaims 'I' and 'mine'; how can passion and the rest be conquered, even in many births?

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi deveśa
tvatprasādād anirjitaiḥ
rāgādibhir amartyatvaṃ
prāptuṃ prakṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore I wish, O lord of the gods, through your grace, while passion and the rest remain unconquered, to attain immortality, my impurities exhausted

body.text:
yady evaṃ muktikāmas tvaṃ
naranātha śṛṇuṣva tat
kriyāyogaṃ samastānāṃ
kleśānāṃ hānikārakam
body.translated_text: If you are thus desirous of liberation, O lord of men, then hear that <s>kriyāyoga</s> (the yoga of action) which destroys all afflictions

body.text:
manmanā bhava madbhakto
madyājī māṃ namaskuru
mām evaiṣyasi yuktvaivam
ātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow down to me; thus uniting yourself, intent on me, you shall come to me alone

body.text:
madbhāvanā madyajanā
madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ
mama pūjāparāś caiva
mayi yānti layaṃ narāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who meditate on me, who sacrifice to me, who are devoted to me, intent on me, and devoted to my worship, attain dissolution into me

body.text:
sarvabhūteṣu māṃ paśya
samavasthitam īśvaram
kartāsi kena vairatvaṃ
evaṃ doṣān prahāsyasi
body.translated_text: See me, the Lord, equally established in all beings; being the doer, by what should you have enmity? Thus you shall abandon the faults

body.text:
jaṅgamājaṅgame jñāte
mayy ātmani tathā tava
rāgalobhādināśena
bhavitrī kṛtakṛtyatā
body.translated_text: When the moving and the unmoving are known to be within me, the Self, and likewise within you, by the destruction of passion, greed, and the rest, fulfillment will come to be

body.text:
bhaktyātipravaṇasyāpi
cañcalatvān mano yadi
mayy anāsādavad bhūpa
kuru madrūpiṇīṃ tanum
body.translated_text: If, though exceedingly inclined to devotion, your mind through fickleness has no resting-place in me, O king, make an image in my form

body.text:
suvarṇarajatādyais tvaṃ
śailamṛddārulekhajām
pūjāmaharhair vividhaiḥ
saṃpūjaya ca pārthiva
body.translated_text: With gold, silver, and the like, with stone, clay, or wood-carving, with various worthy offerings, worship it, O king

body.text:
tasyāṃ cittaṃ samāveśya
tyājayānyān vyapāśrayān
pūjitā saiva te bhaktyā
dhyātā caivopakāriṇī
body.translated_text: Fixing your mind upon it, make it abandon other supports; that very image, worshipped with devotion and meditated upon, becomes your benefactor

body.text:
gacchaṃs tiṣṭhan svapan bhuñjaṃs
tām evāgre ca pṛṣṭhataḥ
upary adhas tathā pārśve
cintayāntas tathātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Walking, standing, sleeping, eating — keep it before you and behind, above and below, and at your side; meditate upon it within yourself, O king

body.text:
snānais tīrthodakair hṛdyaiḥ
puṣpagandhānulepanaiḥ
vāsobhir bhūṣaṇair bhakṣyair
gītavādyair manoharaiḥ
body.translated_text: With bathing in delightful waters of holy fords, with flowers, fragrances, and unguents, with garments, ornaments, foods, and pleasing song and music,

body.text:
yac ca yac ca nṛpeṣṭaṃ te
kiṃcid bhojyādi tena tām
bhaktinamro naraśreṣṭha
prīṇayārcāṃ kṛtāṃ mama
body.translated_text: and with whatever food and the like is dear to you, O king — with that, bowed in devotion, O best of men, gratify that worshipped image of mine

body.text:
rāgeṇākṛṣyate ceto
gandharvābhimukhaṃ yadi
mayi buddhiṃ samāveśya
gāyethā mama tāṃ kathām
body.translated_text: If the mind is drawn by passion toward the <s>gandharva</s> arts, then fixing your understanding upon me, sing that tale of mine

body.text:
kathāyāṃ ramate ceto
yadi tatbhāvanā mama
śrotavyā prītiyuktena
avatāreṣu yā kathā
body.translated_text: If the mind delights in stories, then, with that meditation upon me, the tale of my <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations) should be heard with love

body.text:
evaṃ mayy arpitamanāś
cetaso ye vyapāśrayāḥ
heyās tān akhilān bhūpa
parityakṣyasy abhīr bhava
body.translated_text: Thus, with mind offered to me, those supports of consciousness which are to be abandoned — abandon them all, O king, and be fearless

body.text:
akṣīṇarāgadoṣo 'pi
matkriyā paramaḥ param
padam āpsyasi mā bhais tvaṃ
mayy arpitamanā bhava
body.translated_text: Even with the faults of passion undiminished, being devoted supremely to my service, you shall attain the supreme state; do not fear; be one whose mind is offered to me

body.text:
mayi saṃnyasya sarvaṃ tvam
ātmānaṃ yat tavāsti ca
madarthaṃ kuru karmāṇi
mā ca dharmavyatikramam
body.translated_text: Renouncing in me your whole self and whatever is yours, perform actions for my sake, and do not transgress <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
rājyaṃ kuru naraśreṣṭha
nivedya pṛthivīṃ mama
tadvyāghātaparā ye ca
jahi tān avanīpate
body.translated_text: Rule the kingdom, O best of men, offering the earth to me; and those who are bent on obstructing that, slay them, O lord of the earth

body.text:
etenaivopadeśena
vyākhyātam akhilaṃ tava
kriyāyogaṃ samāsthāya
mayy arpitamanā bhava
body.translated_text: By this very instruction the whole has been explained to you; resorting to <s>kriyāyoga</s>, be one whose mind is offered to me

body.text:
maddhitāya jagannātha
kriyāyogāśritaṃ mama
vistareṇedam ākhyāhi
prasannas tvaṃ hi duḥkhahā
body.translated_text: For my benefit, O Lord of the world, declare this in detail, this that is grounded in <s>kriyāyoga</s>, since you, being gracious, are the destroyer of sorrow

body.text:
tvām ṛtena hi no vaktuṃ
samartho 'nyo jagadguro
guhyam etat pavitraṃ ca
tad ācakṣya prasīda me
body.translated_text: Truly no other than you, O teacher of the world, is able to tell it to us; this is secret and holy — declare it, be gracious to me

body.text:
ākhyāsyaty etad akhilaṃ
vasiṣṭhas te purohitaḥ
matprasādād avikalaṃ
sa ca vetsyaty aśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, your <s>purohita</s> (household priest), will tell you all this; by my grace he too shall know it completely, without omission

body.text:
ity uktvāntardadhe devaḥ
sarvalokeśvaro hariḥ
sa ca rājā vanād bhūyo
nijam abhyāgamat puram
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the god <s>Hari</s>, lord of all worlds, vanished; and that king returned again from the forest to his own city

body.text:
rājyasthas tu mahīpālaḥ
praṇipatya purohitam
vasiṣṭhaṃ paripapraccha
viṣṇor ārādhanaṃ prati
body.translated_text: Established in his kingdom, the king, prostrating to his <s>purohita</s> <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, questioned him concerning the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
devadevena bhagavann
ādiṣṭo 'si mahātmanā
kriyāyogāśritaṃ sarvaṃ
vyākhyāsyati bhavān kila
body.translated_text: O blessed one, you have been instructed by the god of gods, the great-souled one; you, it is said, will explain all that is grounded in <s>kriyāyoga</s>

body.text:
sa tvāṃ pṛcchāmy ahaṃ sarvaṃ
kriyāyogena keśavam
saṃtoṣayitum īśānaṃ
yathā śakṣyāmi tad vada
body.translated_text: I ask you all of it: tell me how, by <s>kriyāyoga</s>, I may be able to gratify the Lord <s>Keśava</s>, the ruler

body.text:
devaprasādād akhilā
mamāpi smṛtir āgatā
jñānam etad aśeṣaṃ te
kathayāmi nibodha tat
body.translated_text: By the god's grace all memory has come to me too; this knowledge in its entirety I tell you — hear it

body.text:
bhaktimān abhavad daityo
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ sutaḥ
nārāyaṇe mahāprajñaḥ
sarvalokaparāyaṇe
sa papraccha bhṛguśreṣṭhaṃ
śukram ātmapurohitam
body.translated_text: There was a <s>daitya</s> (demon), the son of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, of great wisdom, devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the refuge of all worlds; he questioned the best of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, his own <s>purohita</s>

body.text:
bhagavan nṛsiṃharūpasya
viṣṇos tātaṃ jighāṃsataḥ
dṛṣṭaṃ dehe mayā sarvaṃ
trailokyaṃ bhūrbhuvādikam
body.translated_text: O blessed one, when <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> sought to slay my father, I saw within his body the whole — the three worlds, earth, atmosphere, and the rest

body.text:
brahmā prajāpatiś cendro
rudraiḥ paśupatiḥ saha
vasavo 'ṣṭau tathādityā
dvādaśāhaḥkṣapā mahī
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> the lord of creatures, and <s>Indra</s>, <s>Paśupati</s> together with the <s>Rudras</s>, the eight <s>Vasus</s>, and likewise the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, day and night, and the earth

body.text:
diśo nabhas tārakaughaṃ
nakṣatragrahasaṃkulam
aśvinau marutaḥ sādhyā
viśvedevās tatha rṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: the directions, the sky, the host of stars thronged with constellations and planets, the <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, and likewise the <s>ṛṣis</s>

body.text:
varṣācalās tathā nadyaḥ
sapta sapta kulācalāḥ
samudrāḥ sapta ṛtavaḥ
kāntārāṇi vanāni ca
nagaragrāmatarubhiḥ
samāvetaṃ ca bhūtalam
body.translated_text: the rain-mountains and the rivers, the seven-fold seven principal mountains, the seven seas, the seasons, the wildernesses and forests, and the surface of the earth covered with cities, villages, and trees

body.text:
etac cānyac ca yat kiṃcid
devarṣipitṛmānavam
satiryagūrdhvapātālaṃ
tasya dṛṣṭaṃ tanau mayā
body.translated_text: this and whatever else there is — divine, sage, ancestral, human — together with the lower, the upper, and the netherworld — all that I saw in his body

body.text:
so 'haṃ tam ajaraṃ devaṃ
duṣṭadaityanivarhaṇam
ārādhayitum icchāmi
bhagavaṃs tvadanujñayā
body.translated_text: So I wish, O blessed one, with your permission, to worship that unaging god, the destroyer of wicked <s>daityas</s>

body.text:
anugrāhyo 'smi yadi te
mamāyaṃ bhaktimān iti
tan mamopadiśādya tvaṃ
mahad ārādhanaṃ hareḥ
body.translated_text: If I am to be favored by you as one devoted, then teach me now the great worship of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
anugrāhyo 'si devasya
nūnam avyaktajanmanaḥ
ārādhanāya daityendra
yat te tatpravaṇaṃ manaḥ
body.translated_text: You are surely to be favored by the god of unmanifest birth, O lord of <s>daityas</s>, in that your mind is inclined to his worship

body.text:
yadi devapatiṃ viṣṇum
ārādhayitum icchasi
bhagavantam anādyantaṃ
bhava bhāgavato 'sura
body.translated_text: If you wish to worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of the gods, the blessed one without beginning or end, become a <s>bhāgavata</s> (devotee), O demon

body.text:
na hy abhāgavatair viṣṇur
jñātuṃ stotuṃ ca tattvataḥ
draṣṭuṃ vā śakyate martyaiḥ
praveṣṭuṃ kuta eva hi
body.translated_text: For by those who are not <s>bhāgavatas</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> cannot truly be known, praised, or seen by mortals — how then can he be entered?

body.text:
janmabhir bahubhiḥ pūtā
narās tadgatacetasaḥ
bhavanti vai bhāgavatās
te viṣṇuṃ praviśanti ca
body.translated_text: Men purified through many births, their minds fixed upon him, become <s>bhāgavatas</s> indeed, and they enter into <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
anekajanmasaṃsāra-
cite pāpasamuccaye
nākṣīṇe jāyate puṃsāṃ
govindābhimukhī matiḥ
body.translated_text: Until the accumulated heap of sin, gathered through the <s>saṃsāra</s> of many births, is exhausted, there does not arise in men a mind turned toward <s>Govinda</s>

body.text:
pradveṣaṃ yāti govinde
dvijān vedāṃś ca nindati
yo naras taṃ vijānīyād
asurāṃśasamudbhavam
body.translated_text: He who goes to hatred toward <s>Govinda</s>, who reviles the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and the <s>Vedas</s> — that man one should know to be born of a portion of the demons

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍeṣu ratiḥ puṃsāṃ
hetuvādānukūlatā
jāyate viṣṇumāyāmbhaḥ-
patitānāṃ durātmanām
body.translated_text: Delight in heretical doctrines, favor for the arguments of mere reasoning — these arise in the wicked-souled who have fallen into the waters of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s>

body.text:
yadā pāpakṣayaḥ puṃsāṃ
tadā vedadvijātiṣu
viṣṇau ca yajñapuruṣe
śraddhā bhavati te yathā
body.translated_text: When there is destruction of the sins of men, then in the <s>Vedas</s>, in the twice-born, and in <s>Viṣṇu</s> the sacrificial Person, faith arises in them, as it has in you.

body.text:
yadā svalpāvaśeṣas tu
narāṇāṃ pāpasaṃcayaḥ
bhavanti te bhāgavatās
tadā daityapate narāḥ
body.translated_text: But when only a small remnant of men's accumulation of sin remains, then, O lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, those men become <s>Bhāgavatas</s> (devotees of the Lord).

body.text:
bhrāmyatām atra saṃsāre
narāṇāṃ karmadurgame
hastāvalambado hy eko
bhaktiprīto janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: For men wandering here in this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), impassable through <s>karma</s>, there is but one support for the hand: <s>Janārdana</s>, who is pleased by devotion.

body.text:
sa tvaṃ bhāgavato bhūtvā
sarvapāpaharaṃ harim
ārādhaya paraṃ bhaktyā
prītim eṣyati keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: So you, having become a <s>Bhāgavata</s>, worship with supreme devotion <s>Hari</s>, the remover of all sins; <s>Keśava</s> will come to be pleased.

body.text:
kiṃlakṣaṇā bhāgavatā
bhavanti puruṣā guro
yac ca bhāgavataiḥ kāryaṃ
tan me kathaya bhārgava
body.translated_text: By what marks do men become <s>Bhāgavatas</s>, O teacher? And what is to be done by <s>Bhāgavatas</s>—tell me that, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.

body.text:
karmaṇā manasā vācā
prāṇināṃ yo na hiṃsakaḥ
bhāvabhaktaś ca govinde
daitya bhāgavato hi saḥ
body.translated_text: He who, by deed, mind, and speech, is no injurer of living beings, and who has true devotion toward <s>Govinda</s>—O <s>Daitya</s>, he indeed is a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
yo brāhmaṇāṃś ca vedāṃś ca
nityam envānumaṃsyati
na ca drogdhā paraṃ vāde
daitya bhāgavato hi saḥ
body.translated_text: He who will always honor the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and the <s>Vedas</s>, and who is no malicious one toward another in debate—O <s>Daitya</s>, he indeed is a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
sarvān devān hariṃ vetti
sarvalokāṃś ca keśavam
tebhyaś ca nānyam ātmānaṃ
daitya bhāgavato hi saḥ
body.translated_text: He who knows all the gods as <s>Hari</s>, and all the worlds as <s>Keśava</s>, and his own self as none other than them—O <s>Daitya</s>, he indeed is a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
devaṃ manuṣyam anyaṃ vā
paśupakṣipipīlikān
tarupāṣāṇakaṣṭhādi
bhūmyambhogaganaṃ diśaḥ
body.translated_text: A god, a human, or another, a beast, bird, or ant, a tree, a stone, a piece of wood, and so on, the earth, the waters, the sky, the directions,

body.text:
ātmānaṃ vāpi deveśān
nātiriktaṃ janārdanāt
yo bhajeta vijānīṣva
taṃ vai bhāgavataṃ naram
body.translated_text: or even his own self and the lords of the gods—he who worships none of these as superior to <s>Janārdana</s>: know that man to be a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
sarvaṃ bhagavato bhāvo
yad bhūtaṃ bhavasaṃsthitam
iti yo vai vijānāti
sa tu bhāgavato naraḥ
body.translated_text: He who truly knows that all this, whatever has come to be and abides in existence, is the being of the Lord—he indeed is a <s>Bhāgavata</s> man.

body.text:
bhavabhītiṃ haraty eṣa
bhaktibhāvena bhāvitaḥ
bhagavān iti bhāvo yaḥ
sa tu bhāgavato naraḥ
body.translated_text: This man, made pure by the disposition of devotion, removes the fear of existence; he in whom the disposition is "He is the Lord"—he indeed is a <s>Bhāgavata</s> man.

body.text:
bhāvaṃ na kurute yas tu
sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam
karmaṇā manasā vācā
sa tu bhāgavato naraḥ
body.translated_text: He who, by deed, mind, and speech, harbors no evil disposition toward all beings—he indeed is a <s>Bhāgavata</s> man.

body.text:
bāhyārthanirapekṣo yo
bhakto bhagavataḥ kriyām
bhāvena niṣpādayati
jñeyo bhāgavatas tu saḥ
body.translated_text: He who, indifferent to external objects, a devotee, accomplishes the rite of the Lord with true feeling—he is to be known as a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
nārayo yasya na snigdhā
na codāsī na vṛttayaḥ
paśyataḥ sarvam evedaṃ
viṣṇuṃ bhāgavato hi saḥ
body.translated_text: He who has neither enemies nor cherished ones, neither indifference nor mundane occupations, seeing all this as <s>Viṣṇu</s>—he indeed is a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
sutapteneha tapasā
yajñair vā bahudakṣiṇaiḥ
tāṃ gatiṃ na narā yānti
yāṃ vai bhāgavatā gatāḥ
body.translated_text: By well-heated <s>tapas</s> (austerity) here, or by sacrifices with abundant gifts, men do not attain that goal which the <s>Bhāgavatas</s> have reached.

body.text:
yogacyutair bhāgavatair
devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ
arvāṅ nirīkṣyate yajñī
kimu ye yogapāragāḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Śatakratu</s>, the king of the gods, the sacrificer, is regarded as inferior to <s>Bhāgavatas</s> who have fallen from <s>yoga</s>—how much more, then, to those who have reached the far shore of <s>yoga</s>?

body.text:
yajñaniṣpattaye vedā
yajño yajñapateḥ kṛte
tattoṣaṇāya bhāvena
tasmād bhāgavato bhava
body.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> are for the accomplishment of sacrifice, sacrifice is for the sake of the lord of sacrifice, and that is for his contentment through devotion—therefore become a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
yena sarvātmanā viṣṇau
bhaktyā bhāvo niveśitaḥ
daityeśvara kṛtārthatvāc
ślāghyo bhāgavato hi saḥ
body.translated_text: He who with his whole self, with devotion, has fixed his disposition upon <s>Viṣṇu</s>—O lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, because of his fulfillment, that <s>Bhāgavata</s> is praiseworthy.

body.text:
api naḥ sa kule dhanyo
jāyate kulapāvanaḥ
bhagavān bhaktibhāvena
yena viṣṇur upāsitaḥ
body.translated_text: Even in our family blessed is he who is born, the purifier of the lineage, by whom, with the disposition of devotion, the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been worshipped.

body.text:
yaḥ kārayati devārcāṃ
hṛdayālambanaṃ hareḥ
sa naro viṣṇusālokyam
upaiti dhūtakalmaṣaḥ
body.translated_text: The man who has the image of the deity made—the support of <s>Hari</s> in the heart—that man, his sins shaken off, attains <s>sālokya</s> (the same world) with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
yaś ca devālayaṃ bhaktyā
viṣṇoḥ kārayati svayam
sa saptapuruṣāṃl lokān
viṣṇor nayati mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: And the man who himself with devotion has a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> made, that man leads seven generations to the worlds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
yāvanty abdāni devārcā
hares tiṣṭhati mandire
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi
viṣṇuloke sa modate
body.translated_text: For as many years as the image of <s>Hari</s> stands in the temple, for that many thousands of years he rejoices in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
devārcā lakṣaṇopetā
tadgṛhaṃ satataṃ divi
niṣkāmaṃ ca mano yasya
sa yāty akṣarasātmyatām
body.translated_text: He whose image of the deity is endowed with the proper marks, and that house ever in heaven, and whose mind is free of desire—he attains identity with the Imperishable.

body.text:
puṣpāṇy atisugandhīni
manojñāni ca yaḥ pumān
prayacchati hṛṣīkeśe
tadbhāvagatamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: The man who offers exceedingly fragrant and pleasing flowers to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, with his mind absorbed in devotion to him,

body.text:
dhūpāṃś ca vividhāṃs tāṃs tān
gandhāḍhyaṃ cānulepanam
dīpāvalyupahārāṃś ca
yac cābhīṣṭam athātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: and various incenses, and unguents rich in scent, and lamp-row offerings, and whatever is desired by himself—

body.text:
naraḥ so 'nudinaṃ yajñaṃ
karoty ārādhanaṃ hareḥ
yajñeśo bhagavān viṣṇur
makhair api hi toṣyate
body.translated_text: that man daily performs sacrifice, the worship of <s>Hari</s>; for the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of sacrifice, is gladdened even by sacrifices.

body.text:
bahūpakaraṇā yajñā
nānāsaṃbhāravistarāḥ
prāpyante te dhanayutair
manuṣyair nālpasaṃcayaiḥ
body.translated_text: Sacrifices with abundant implements, with extensive and varied materials, are attained by men endowed with wealth, not by those of slender means.

body.text:
bhaktyā ca puruṣaiḥ pūjā
kṛtā dūrvāṅkurair api
harer dadāti hi phalaṃ
sarvayajñaiḥ sudurlabham
body.translated_text: But worship performed with devotion by men, even with sprouts of <s>dūrvā</s> grass, gives the fruit of <s>Hari</s> which is most difficult to obtain by all sacrifices.

body.text:
yāni puṣpāṇi hṛdyāni
dhūpagandhānulepanam
dayitaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ yac ca
ye ca kauśeyavāsasī
body.translated_text: Whatever flowers are pleasing, incense, scents, and unguent, whatever beloved ornament, and the two silken garments,

body.text:
yāni cābhyavahārāṇi
bhakṣyāṇi ca phalāni ca
prayaccha tāni govinde
bhavethāś caiva tanmanāḥ
body.translated_text: and whatever foods, delicacies, and fruits—offer these to <s>Govinda</s>, and be one whose mind is upon him.

body.text:
ādyantaṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ
yathāśaktyā prasādaya
ārādhya yāti taṃ devaṃ
tasminn eva naro layam
body.translated_text: Gratify the sacrificial Person, the beginning and end, according to your power; having worshipped that god, a man attains dissolution in him alone.

body.text:
puṇyais tīrthodakair gandhair
madhunā sarpiṣā tathā
kṣīreṇa snāpayed īśam
acyutaṃ jagataḥ patim
body.translated_text: With holy waters of sacred fords, with scents, with honey, with clarified butter, and with milk, one should bathe the Lord, <s>Acyuta</s>, the master of the world.

body.text:
dadhikṣīrahradān puṇyāṃs
tato lokān madhucyutaḥ
prayāsyasy asuraśreṣṭha
nirvṛtiṃ cāpi śāśvatīm
body.translated_text: Then, dripping with honey, you will go, O best of <s>asuras</s>, to the holy lakes of curds and milk, to those worlds, and to eternal bliss as well.

body.text:
stotrair gītais tathā vādyair
brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ
manasaś caikatāyogād
ārādhaya janārdanam
body.translated_text: With hymns, songs, and instrumental music, and with the gratifying of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and through the union of the mind in one-pointedness, worship <s>Janārdana</s>.

body.text:
ārādhya taṃ videhānāṃ
puruṣāḥ saptasaptatiḥ
haihayāḥ pañcapañcāśad
amṛtatvam upāgatāḥ
body.translated_text: Having worshipped him, seventy-seven men of the <s>Videhas</s> and fifty-five of the <s>Haihayas</s> attained immortality.

body.text:
sa tvam ebhiḥ prakārais tam
upavāsaiś ca keśavam
toṣayādyo hi tuṣṭo 'sau
viṣṇur dvandvapraśāntidaḥ
body.translated_text: So you, by these methods and by fasts, gratify <s>Keśava</s>; for that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, when gladdened, is the giver of peace from the pairs of opposites.

body.text:
upavāsair hṛṣīkeśaḥ
kathaṃ tuṣyati bhārgava
parihārāṃs tathācakṣva
ye tyājyāś copavāsinām
body.translated_text: How is <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> gladdened by fasts, O <s>Bhārgava</s>? And tell likewise the abstentions which are to be forsworn by those who fast.

body.text:
yad yat kāryaṃ yathā caiva
keśavārādhane naraiḥ
tat sarvaṃ vistarād brahman
yathāvad vaktum arhasi
body.translated_text: Whatever is to be done, and in what manner, by men in the worship of <s>Keśava</s>—all that in detail, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, you ought to tell duly.

body.text:
smṛtaḥ saṃpūjito dhūpa-
puṣpādyair dayitair hariḥ
bhoginām upakārāya
kiṃ punaś copavāsinām
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, when remembered and well worshipped with incense, flowers, and beloved things, is for the benefit even of those who enjoy pleasures—how much more of those who fast?

body.text:
upāvṛttas tu pāpebhyo
yas tu vāso guṇaiḥ saha
upavāsaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ
sarvabhogavivarjitaḥ
body.translated_text: The dwelling, together with its virtues, that is turned away from sins—that is to be known as a fast, free of all enjoyment.

body.text:
ekarātraṃ dvirātraṃ vā
trirātram athavāparam
upavāsī hariṃ yas tu
bhaktyā dhyāyati mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: For one night, or two nights, or for three nights or more, the man who fasts and meditates with devotion upon <s>Hari</s>,

body.text:
tannāmajāpī tatkarma-
ratis tadgatamānasaḥ
niṣkāmo daitya sa brahma
param āpnoty asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: muttering his name, delighting in his works, his mind fixed on him, free of desire—O <s>Daitya</s>, he attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, without doubt.

body.text:
yaṃ ca kāmam abhidhyāyan
keśavārpitamānasaḥ
upoṣyati tam āpnoti
prasanne garuḍadhvaje
body.translated_text: And whatever desire he longs for while fasting, with his mind offered to <s>Keśava</s>, that he attains, when the one whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s> is pleased.

body.text:
kathyate ca purā vipraḥ
pulastyo brahmavādinā
dālbhyena pṛṣṭo 'kathayad
yathaitad arisūdana
body.translated_text: And it is told, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, that long ago <s>Pulastya</s>, the speaker of <s>Brahman</s>, when asked by <s>Dālbhya</s>, declared how this is, O slayer of foes.

body.text:
brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyair vaiśyaiḥ
śūdraiḥ strībhis tathā mune
saṃsāragartapaṅkasthaiḥ
sugatiḥ prāpyate katham
body.translated_text: O sage, how is a good destination attained by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, <s>śūdras</s>, and women, who are stuck in the mire of the pit of <s>saṃsāra</s>?

body.text:
anārādhya jagannāthaṃ
sarvadhātāram acyutam
nirvyalīkena cittena
kaḥ prayāsyati sadgatim
body.translated_text: Without worshipping <s>Jagannātha</s>, the all-supporter, <s>Acyuta</s>, with an undeceiving mind, who shall go to the good destination?

body.text:
viṣayagrāhi vai yasya
na cittaṃ keśavārpitam
sa kathaṃ pāpapaṅkāṅkī
naro yāsyati sadgatim
body.translated_text: He whose mind, grasping at sense-objects, is not offered to <s>Keśava</s>—how shall that man, marked by the mire of sin, go to the good destination?

body.text:
yadi saṃsāraduḥkhārtaḥ
sugatiṃ gantum icchasi
tadārādhaya sarveśaṃ
jagaddhātāram acyutam
body.translated_text: If, afflicted by the sorrow of <s>saṃsāra</s>, you wish to go to a good destination, then worship the Lord of all, the supporter of the world, <s>Acyuta</s>.

body.text:
puṣpaiḥ sugandhair hṛdyaiś ca
dhūpaiḥ sāgarucandanaiḥ
vāsobhir bhūṣaṇair bhakṣyair
upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: With pleasing fragrant flowers, with incense, aloe, and sandal, with garments, ornaments, and delicacies, intent upon fasting—

body.text:
yadi saṃsāranirvedād
abhivāñchasi sadgatim
tadārādhaya govindaṃ
yac ceṣṭaṃ tava cetasi
body.translated_text: if, from disgust with <s>saṃsāra</s>, you desire a good destination, then worship <s>Govinda</s> with whatever is dear to your heart.

body.text:
puṣpāṇi yadi te na syuḥ
śastaṃ pādapapallavaiḥ
dūrvāṅkurair api brahmaṃs
tadabhāve 'rcayācyutam
body.translated_text: If you have no flowers, leaves of trees are commended, or even <s>dūrvā</s> sprouts, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; in their absence, worship <s>Acyuta</s>.

body.text:
sugandhipuṣpadīpādyair
yaḥ kuryāt keśavālaye
sarvatīrthaphalaṃ tasya
saṃbhavet keśavārcayā
sabāhyābhyantaraṃ yas tu
mārjayed acyutālayam
sabāhyābhyantaraṃ tasya
kāyo niṣkalmaṣo bhavet
body.translated_text: He who in the abode of <s>Keśava</s> would make worship with fragrant flowers, lamps, and the like—for him, by the worship of <s>Keśava</s>, the fruit of all sacred fords would arise. But he who would cleanse the abode of <s>Acyuta</s> within and without—his body within and without would become free of sin.

body.text:
puṣpapatrāmbubhir dhūpair
yathāvibhavam acyutaḥ
pūjitas tuṣṭim atulāṃ
bhaktyāyāty ekacetasām
body.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s>, worshipped according to one's means with flowers, leaves, water, and incense, comes to incomparable contentment with those of single-minded devotion.

body.text:
yaḥ sadāyatane viṣṇoḥ
kurute mārjanakriyām
sa pāṃsubhūmer dehāc ca
sarvapāpaṃ vyapohati
body.translated_text: He who always performs the act of cleansing in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, removes all sin from his body, like dust from the earth.

body.text:
yāvantyaḥ pāṃsukaṇikā
mārjyante keśavālaye
dināni divi tāvanti
tiṣṭhaty astamalo naraḥ
body.translated_text: For as many specks of dust as are swept away in the abode of <s>Keśava</s>, for that many days the man dwells in heaven, free of stain.

body.text:
ahany ahani yat pāpaṃ
kurute dvijasattama
gocarmamātraṃ saṃmārjya
hanti tat keśavālaye
body.translated_text: Whatever sin a man commits day after day, O best of the twice-born, he destroys it by sweeping even a cow's-hide measure in the abode of <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
yaś copalepanaṃ kuryād
viṣṇor āyatane naraḥ
so 'pi lokaṃ samāsādya
modate ca śatakratoḥ
body.translated_text: And the man who would do the plastering in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—he too, attaining the world of <s>Śatakratu</s>, rejoices.

body.text:
mṛdā dhātuvikārair vā
varṇakair gomayena vā
upalepanakṛd yāti
vimānaṃ maṇicitritam
body.translated_text: He who does the plastering with clay, mineral preparations, paints, or cow-dung, goes to a celestial chariot adorned with jewels.

body.text:
udakābhyukṣaṇaṃ viṣṇor
yaḥ karoti tathā gṛhe
so 'pi gacchati yatrāste
bhagavān yādasāṃ patiḥ
body.translated_text: He who likewise performs the sprinkling of water in the house of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—he too goes to where the Lord, the lord of the waters, abides.

body.text:
puṣpaprakaram atyarthaṃ
sugandhaṃ keśavālaye
upalipte naro dattvā
na durgatim avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: Having given an abundant mass of fragrant flowers in the plastered abode of <s>Keśava</s>, a man would not meet with an evil destination.

body.text:
vimānam atividyoti
sarvaratnamayaṃ divi
samāpnoti naro dattvā
dīpakaṃ keśavālaye
body.translated_text: A man, having given a lamp in the abode of <s>Keśava</s>, attains in heaven a celestial chariot exceedingly radiant, made of all jewels.

body.text:
yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ
tilapātraprado naraḥ
dhvajaṃ tu viṣṇave dadyāt
samam etat phalaṃ dvija
body.translated_text: He who for a full year is the giver of a vessel of sesame, and he who would give a banner to <s>Viṣṇu</s>—equal is this fruit, O twice-born.

body.text:
vidhunvan hanti vātena
dātur ajñānataḥ kṛtam
pāpaṃ ketur gṛhe viṣṇor
divārātram asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: The banner in the house of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, fluttering by the wind day and night, destroys without doubt the sin committed by the giver through ignorance.

body.text:
gītavādyādibhir devaṃ
ya upāste janārdanam
gāndharvair gītanṛtyaiḥ sa
vimānastho niṣevyate
body.translated_text: He who worships the god <s>Janārdana</s> with song, instrumental music, and the like—he, dwelling in a celestial chariot, is attended by <s>Gandharvas</s> with song and dance.

body.text:
jātismaratvaṃ medhāṃ ca
tathaivoparame smṛtim
prāpnoti viṣṇvāyatane
puṇyākhyānakathākaraḥ
body.translated_text: The reciter of holy narratives in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> attains recollection of past births, intelligence, and likewise memory at the time of departure.

body.text:
upoṣitaḥ pūjito vā
dṛṣṭo vā namito 'pi vā
pradambha harate (?) pāpaṃ
ko na seved dhariṃ tataḥ
vedavādakriyāyajña-
snānatīrthaphalaṃ param
aṣṭāṅgapraṇipātena
praṇipatya hariṃ labhet
pragamya hṛdā śirasā
pādapadme mahītale
niṣkalmaṣo bhavet sadyo
na nāṭī pādapāṃsunā
ekasya kṛṣṇasya krājataḥ praṇāmo
daśāśvamedhāvabhṛthena tulyaḥ
daśāśvamedhaiḥ punar eti janma
kṛṣṇapraṇāmī na punarbhavāya
body.translated_text: Fasted, worshipped, seen, or bowed to, <s>Hari</s> removes sin... who then would not serve <s>Hari</s>? The supreme fruit of <s>Veda</s>-recitation, ritual action, sacrifice, bathing, and sacred fords—one attains by saluting <s>Hari</s> with the eight-limbed prostration. Bowing with heart and head to the lotus-feet upon the earth, one would at once become free of sin, not... by the dust of the feet. The single prostration of one calling on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is equal to the final ablution of ten horse-sacrifices; by ten horse-sacrifices one comes again to birth, but he who prostrates to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is not for rebirth.

body.text:
evaṃ deveśvaro bhaktyā
yena viṣṇur upāsitaḥ
sa prāpnoti gatiṃ ślāghyāṃ
yāṃ yām icchati cetasā
body.translated_text: Thus, O lord of the gods, he by whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been worshipped with devotion attains the praiseworthy destination, whichever he desires in his mind.

body.text:
devatvaṃ manujaiḥ kaiścid
gandharvatvaṃ tathāparaiḥ
vidyādharatvam aparair
ārādhyāptaṃ janārdanam
body.translated_text: By some men <s>Janārdana</s>, when worshipped, was attained as godhood, by others as the state of a <s>Gandharva</s>, by others as the state of a <s>Vidyādhara</s>.

body.text:
śakraḥ kratuśateneśam
ārādhya garuḍadhvajam
devendratvaṃ gatas tasmān
nānyaḥ pūjyatamaḥ kvacit
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, having worshipped the Lord whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s> with a hundred sacrifices, attained the lordship of the gods; therefore none anywhere is more worthy of worship.

body.text:
devebhyo 'pi hi pūjyas tu
svagurur brahmacāriṇaḥ
tasyāpi yajñapuruṣo
viṣṇuḥ pūjyo dvijottama
body.translated_text: Indeed, the brahmacārin's own teacher is to be worshipped even before the gods; but even before him, the sacrificial Person <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be worshipped, O best of the twice-born.

body.text:
striyaś ca bhartāram ṛte
pūjyam anyan na daivatam
bhartur gṛhasthasya sataḥ
pūjyo yajñapatir hariḥ
body.translated_text: And for women, apart from the husband, no other deity is to be worshipped; but for the husband, a householder, <s>Hari</s>, the lord of sacrifice, is to be worshipped.

body.text:
vaikhānasānām ārādhyas
tapobhir madhusūdanaḥ
dhyeyaḥ parivrājakānāṃ
vāsudevo mahātmanām
body.translated_text: <s>Madhusūdana</s> is to be worshipped with austerities by the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>; <s>Vāsudeva</s> is to be meditated upon by the great-souled wandering ascetics.

body.text:
evaṃ sarvāśramāṇāṃ hi
vāsudevaḥ parāyaṇam
sarveṣāṃ caiva varṇānāṃ
tam ārādhyāpnuyād gatim
body.translated_text: Thus, for all the <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the supreme refuge; and for all the <s>varṇas</s> (classes), having worshipped him, one would attain the destination.

body.text:
śṛṇuṣva gadataḥ kāmyām
upavāsāṃs tathāparān
tat tam āśritya yān kāmān
kurvītepsitam ātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Hear me tell of the desire-bearing fasts and the others, resorting to which a man may accomplish the desires longed for by himself.

body.text:
ekādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣe
phālgune māsi yo naraḥ
japet kṛṣṇeti devasya
nāma bhaktyā punaḥpunaḥ
body.translated_text: On the eleventh day of the bright fortnight, in the month of <s>Phālguna</s>, the man who mutters the god's name "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" with devotion again and again,

body.text:
devārcane cāṣṭaśataṃ
kṛtvaitat tu japec chuciḥ
prātaḥ prasthānakāle ca
utthāne skhalite kṣute
body.translated_text: and in the worship of the deity, having done so a hundred and eight times, should mutter this, pure—at dawn, at the time of setting out, at rising, at stumbling, at sneezing—

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍapatitāṃś caiva
tathaivāntyāvasāyinaḥ
nālapeta tathā kṛṣṇam
arcayec chraddhayānvitaḥ
idaṃ codāharet kṛṣṇe
manaḥ saṃdhāya tatparaḥ
body.translated_text: He should not speak with heretics, the fallen, and likewise outcastes, but should worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> endowed with faith; and he should utter this, fixing his mind on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, intent upon him:

body.text:
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛpālus tvam
agatīnāṃ gatir bhava
saṃsārāntarnimagnānāṃ
prasīda madhusūdana
body.translated_text: "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, you are compassionate; be the refuge of the refugeless. Be gracious, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>, to those sunk within <s>saṃsāra</s>."

body.text:
evaṃ prasādyopāvāsaṃ
kṛtvā niyatamānasaḥ
pūrvāhna eva cānyedyur
gavyaṃ saṃprāsya vai sakṛt
snāto 'rcayitvā kṛṣṇeti
punar nāma prakīrtayet
body.translated_text: Thus having propitiated him and performed the fast with controlled mind, in the forenoon, and on the next day, having once partaken of a cow-product, bathed, and worshipped, he should again proclaim the name "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>."

body.text:
vāridhārātrayaṃ caiva
vikṣiped devapādayoḥ
caitravaiśākhayoś caiva
tadvaj jyeṣṭhe tu pūjayet
body.translated_text: And he should sprinkle three streams of water on the feet of the god; and in <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Vaiśākha</s>, and likewise in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, he should worship thus.

body.text:
martyaloke gatiṃ śreṣṭhāṃ
dālbhya prāpnoti vai naraḥ
utkrāntikāle kṛṣṇasya
smaraṇaṃ ca tathāpnute
body.translated_text: O <s>Dālbhya</s>, a man attains the highest destination in the world of mortals, and likewise attains remembrance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> at the time of departure.

body.text:
āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe caiva
māse bhādrapade tathā
tathaivāśvayuje devam
anena vidhinā naraḥ
body.translated_text: And in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, and in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, and likewise in <s>Āśvayuja</s>, a man, by this rule, worships the god.

body.text:
upoṣya saṃpūjya tathā
keśaveti ca kīrtayet
gomūtraprāśanāt pūrvaṃ
svargalokagatiṃ vrajet
body.translated_text: Having fasted and likewise worshipped, one should proclaim "<s>Keśava</s>"; before drinking the cow's urine, one would attain the journey to the world of heaven

body.text:
ārādhitasya jagatām
īśvarasyāvyāyātmanaḥ
utkrāntikāle smaraṇaṃ
keśavasya tathāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: Of the worshipped Lord of the worlds, of imperishable self, at the time of departure one would thus attain the remembrance of <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
kṣīrasya prāśanaṃ yas tu
vidhiṃ cemaṃ yathoditam
kārttikādi yathānyāyaṃ
kuryān māsacatuṣṭayam
body.translated_text: He who, according to this prescribed rule as declared, drinks milk in due order for the four months beginning with <s>Kārttika</s>,

body.text:
tenaiva vidhinā brahman
viṣṇor nāma prakīrtayet
sa yāti viṣṇusālokyaṃ
viṣṇuṃ smarati ca kṣaye
body.translated_text: by that very rule, O <s>brahman</s>, proclaims the name of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—he attains co-residence with <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>viṣṇusālokya</s>), and remembers <s>Viṣṇu</s> at his death

body.text:
pratimāsaṃ dvijātibhyo
dadyād dānaṃ yathecchayā
cāturmāsye ca saṃpūrṇe
puṇyaṃ śravaṇakīrtanam
body.translated_text: Each month he should give a gift to the twice-born as he wishes, and when the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (four-month vow) is complete, there is the merit of hearing and reciting,

body.text:
kathāṃ vā vāsudevasya
tadgītīr vāpi kārayet
evam etāṃ gatiṃ śreṣṭhāṃ
devanāmānukīrtanāt
body.translated_text: or he should have a tale of <s>Vāsudeva</s> told, or songs about him performed; thus by reciting the names of the god he attains this excellent journey

body.text:
kathitaṃ pāraṇaṃ yat te
kārṣṇaṃ māsacatuṣṭayam
ādhipatyaṃ tathā bhogāṃs
tena prāpnoti mānuṣān
body.translated_text: The <s>kārṣṇa</s> (concerning Kṛṣṇa) breaking-of-the-fast of four months has been told to you; by the first one a man attains lordship and human enjoyments,

body.text:
dvitīyena tathā bhogān
aindrān prāpnoti mānavaḥ
viṣṇor lokaṃ tṛtīyena
pāraṇena tathāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: by the second the man attains the enjoyments of <s>Indra</s>, and by the third breaking-of-the-fast he would attain the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
evam etat samākhyātaṃ
gatiprāpakam uttamam
vidhānaṃ dvijaśārdūla
kṛṣṇatuṣṭipradaṃ nṛṇām
body.translated_text: Thus this excellent ordinance which bestows the journey has been fully declared, O tiger among the twice-born, which gives men the favour of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

body.text:
sugatidvādaśīm etāṃ
śraddadhānas tu yo naraḥ
upoṣya ca tathā nārī
prāpnoti trividhāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: That man who, full of faith, fasts on this <s>sugatidvādaśī</s> (auspicious-journey twelfth), and likewise a woman, attains the threefold journey

body.text:
eṣā dhanyā pāpaharā
tithir nityam upāsitā
ārādhanāya śiṣṭaiṣā
devadevasya cakriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: This blessed, sin-removing lunar day, ever attended upon, was prescribed by the wise for the worship of the <s>Cakrin</s> (discus-bearer), god of gods

body.text:
pañcadaśyāṃ ca śuklasya
phālgunasyaiva sattama
pāṣaṇḍapatitāṃś caiva
tathaivāntyāvasāyinaḥ
body.translated_text: On the fifteenth of the bright fortnight of <s>Phālguna</s>, O most excellent one, the heretics and the fallen, and likewise the lowest outcastes,

body.text:
nāstikān bhinnavṛttīṃś ca
pāpinaś cāpy anālapan
nārāyaṇe gatamanāḥ
puruṣo niyatendriyaḥ
body.translated_text: the unbelievers and those of corrupt conduct, and the sinners—without speaking to them, with mind fixed on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the man of restrained senses,

body.text:
tiṣṭhan vrajan praskhalite
kṣute vāpi janārdanam
kīrtayet tatkriyākāle
saptakṛtvaḥ prakīrtayet
body.translated_text: standing, walking, when he has stumbled, or sneezed, should proclaim <s>Janārdana</s>; at the time of that act he should recite it seven times

body.text:
lakṣmyā samanvitaṃ devam
arcayec ca janārdanam
saṃdhyāvyuparame cendu-
svarūpaṃ harim īśvaram
body.translated_text: He should worship the god <s>Janārdana</s> together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>; and at the close of twilight he should worship <s>Hari</s> the Lord in the form of the moon

body.text:
rātriṃ ca lakṣmīṃ saṃcintya
samyag arghyena pūjayet
naktaṃ ca bhuñjīta naras
tailakṣāravivarjitam
body.translated_text: And meditating on the night and on <s>Lakṣmī</s>, he should worship properly with the <s>arghya</s> (water-offering); at night the man should eat food free of oil and saline substances

body.text:
tathaiva caitravaiśākha-
jyeṣṭheṣu munisattama
arcayīta yathāproktaṃ
prāpte prāpte tu taddine
body.translated_text: Likewise in <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Vaiśākha</s>, and <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, O best of sages, he should worship as prescribed when each such day arrives

body.text:
niṣpāditaṃ bhaved ekam
pāraṇaṃ dālbhya bhaktitaḥ
dvitīyaṃ cāpi vakṣyāmi
pāraṇaṃ dvijasattama
body.translated_text: Thus one breaking-of-the-fast is accomplished with devotion, O <s>Dālbhya</s>; and I shall also tell the second breaking-of-the-fast, O best of the twice-born

body.text:
āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe māsi
prāpte bhādrapade tathā
tathaivāśvayuje 'bhyarcya
śrīdharaṃ ca śriyā saha
body.translated_text: In the months of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, when <s>Bhādrapada</s> arrives, and likewise in <s>Āśvayuja</s>, having worshipped <s>Śrīdhara</s> together with <s>Śrī</s>,

body.text:
samyak candramase dattvā
bhuñjītārghyaṃ yathāvidhi
dvitīyam etad ākhyātaṃ
tṛtīyaṃ pāraṇaṃ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: having duly offered to the moon, he should eat the <s>arghya</s>-food according to rule; this second has been declared—hear now the third breaking-of-the-fast

body.text:
kārttikādiṣu māseṣu
tathaivābhyarcya keśavam
bhūtyā samanvitaṃ dadyāc
śaśāṅkāyārhanaṃ niśi
body.translated_text: In the months beginning with <s>Kārttika</s>, likewise having worshipped <s>Keśava</s> endowed with prosperity, he should give the offering to the moon at night,

body.text:
bhuñjīta ca tathā proktaṃ
tṛtīyam iti pāraṇam
pratipūjāsu dadyāc ca
brāhmaṇebhyaś ca dakṣiṇām
body.translated_text: and he should eat as prescribed; this is declared the third breaking-of-the-fast; and at each worship he should give a fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>

body.text:
pratimāsaṃ ca vakṣyāmi
prāśanaṃ kāyaśodhanam
caturaḥ prathamān māsān
pañcagavyam udāhṛtam
body.translated_text: And I shall tell each month the drinking that purifies the body: for the first four months, the <s>pañcagavya</s> (five products of the cow) is prescribed,

body.text:
kuśodakaṃ tathaivānyad
uktaṃ māsacatuṣṭayam
sūryāṃśutaptaṃ tadvac ca
jalaṃ māsacatuṣṭayam
body.translated_text: <s>kuśa</s>-grass water likewise is prescribed for the next four months, and water heated by the sun's rays for the further four months

body.text:
gītavādyādikaṃ pāṭhyaṃ
tathā kṛṣṇasya vā kathān
kāriyīta ca devasya
pāraṇe pāraṇe gate
body.translated_text: He should have song, instrumental music and the like, and recitation, or tales of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, performed for the god at each completed breaking-of-the-fast

body.text:
evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivat
sapatnīkaṃ janārdanam
nāpnotīṣtaviyogādīn
pumān yoṣid athāpi vā
