body.translated_text: Thus having worshipped <s>Janārdana</s> together with his consort according to rule, a man or a woman does not suffer separation from loved ones and the like

body.text:
janārdanaṃ salakṣmīkam
arcayet prathamaṃ tataḥ
saśrīkaṃ śrīdharaṃ bhaktyā
tṛtīye bhūtikeśavau
body.translated_text: He should worship first <s>Janārdana</s> together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>; then with devotion <s>Śrīdhara</s> with <s>Śrī</s>; in the third, <s>Bhūti</s> and <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
yāvanty etadvidhānena
pāraṇenārcati prabhum
tāvanti janmāny asukhaṃ
nāpnotīṣṭaviyogajam
body.translated_text: For as many breakings-of-the-fast as he worships the Lord by this ordinance, for so many births he does not suffer the misery born of separation from loved ones

body.text:
devasya ca prasādena
maraṇe prāpya tatsmṛtim
body.translated_text: And by the grace of the god, attaining remembrance of him at death,

body.text:
kule satāṃ sphītadhane
bhogabhuj jāyate naraḥ
body.translated_text: the man is born in a family of the good, abounding in wealth, as an enjoyer of pleasures

body.text:
nāriṃ prāpnoti na vyādhiṃ
narakaṃ ca na paśyati
durgamaṃ yamamārgaṃ ca
nekṣate dvijasattama
body.translated_text: He attains no misfortune, no disease, and does not behold hell; nor does he see the impassable path of <s>Yama</s>, O best of the twice-born

body.text:
śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ tāta
yamamārgaṃ sudurgamam
yathā sukhena saṃyānti
mānavās tad vadasva me
body.translated_text: I wish to hear, father, of the most impassable path of <s>Yama</s>; tell me how men travel it with ease

body.text:
pratimāsaṃ tu nāmāni
kṛṣṇasyaitāni dvādaśa
kṛtopavāsaḥ susnātaḥ
pūjayitvā janārdanam
uccārayan naro 'bhyeti
susukhenaiva tatpatham
body.translated_text: Each month these twelve names of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—having fasted, well-bathed, and worshipped <s>Janārdana</s>, uttering them, the man approaches that path with great ease

body.text:
tato viprāya vai dadyād
udakumbhaṃ sadakṣiṇaṃ
upānadvastrayugmaṃ ca
chattraṃ kanakam eva ca
body.translated_text: Then he should give to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> a water-pot with a fee, a pair of sandals and garments, a parasol, and gold as well

body.text:
yad vai māsagataṃ nāma
tatprītiś cāpi saṃvadet
saṃvatsarānte 'py athavā
pratimāsaṃ dvijān budhaḥ
vācayed udakumbhādyair
dānaiḥ sarvān anukramāt
body.translated_text: Whatever name belongs to a given month, may that one's favour bring concord; or even at the year's end, or each month, the wise man should have <s>brāhmaṇas</s> recite, with gifts of the water-pot and the rest, all in due succession

body.text:
keśavaṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu
pauṣe nārāyaṇaṃ tathā
mādhavaṃ māghamāse tu
govindaṃ phālgune tathā
body.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, likewise <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in <s>Pauṣa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s> in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, and likewise <s>Govinda</s> in <s>Phālguna</s>,

body.text:
viṣṇuṃ caitre 'tha vaiśākhe
tathaiva madhusūdanam
jyeṣṭhe trivikramaṃ devam
āṣāḍhe vāmanaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> in <s>Caitra</s>, then in <s>Vaiśākha</s> likewise <s>Madhusūdana</s>, the god <s>Trivikrama</s> in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, and <s>Vāmana</s> likewise in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>,

body.text:
śrāvaṇe śrīdharaṃ caiva
hṛṣīkeśeti cāparam
nāma bhādrapade māsi
gīyate puṇyakāṅkṣibhiḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Śrīdhara</s> in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, and the other name <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s> is sung by those who desire merit,

body.text:
padmanābhaṃ cāśvayuje
dāmodaram ataḥ param
kārttike devadeveśaṃ
stuvaṃs tarati durgatim
body.translated_text: <s>Padmanābha</s> in <s>Āśvayuja</s>, and after that <s>Dāmodara</s>, and in <s>Kārttika</s> the Lord of the gods of gods—praising thus, one crosses over misfortune

body.text:
iha vai svasthatāṃ prāpya
maraṇe smaraṇaṃ tataḥ
yāmyakleśam asaṃprāpya
svargaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: Here attaining health, then remembrance at death, not undergoing the torment of <s>Yama</s>, he is exalted in the world of heaven

body.text:
tato mānuṣyam āsādya
nirātaṅko gatajvaraḥ
dhanadhānyavati sphīte
janma sādhukule 'rhati
body.translated_text: Then reaching human existence, free of affliction, freed of fever, he merits birth in a good family thriving with wealth and grain

body.text:
upavāsavratānīha
keśavārādhanaṃ prati
mamācakṣva mahābhāga
paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
body.translated_text: Tell me, O greatly fortunate one, of the fasting-vows here for the worship of <s>Keśava</s>, for great is my curiosity

body.text:
kāmān yān yān naro bhakto
manasecchati keśavāt
vratopavāsanāt prītas
tāṃs tān viṣṇuḥ prayacchati
body.translated_text: Whatever desires a devoted man wishes in his mind from <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, pleased by his vows and fasting, grants those to him,

body.text:
ratnaparvatam āruhya
yathā ratnaṃ mahāmune
sattvānurūpam adatte
tathā kṛtsnān manorathān
body.translated_text: just as, having climbed a jewel-mountain, O great sage, one takes a jewel according to one's character, so he grants all one's wishes

body.text:
mārgaśīrṣaṃ tu yo māsam
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
kurvan vai viṣṇuśuśrūṣāṃ
sa deśe jāyate śubhe
body.translated_text: He who passes the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> with a single meal a day, performing service to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is born in an auspicious land

body.text:
pauṣamāsaṃ tathā dālbhya
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
śuśrūṣaṇaparaḥ śaurer
na rogī sa ca jāyate
body.translated_text: Likewise, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, he who passes the month of <s>Pauṣa</s> with a single meal, intent on the service of <s>Śauri</s>, is born free of disease

body.text:
māghamāsaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
viṣṇuśuśrūṣaṇaparaḥ
sa kule jāyate satām
body.translated_text: O best of the twice-born, he who passes the month of <s>Māgha</s> with a single meal, intent on the service of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is born in a family of the good

body.text:
kṣapayed ekabhaktena
śuśrūṣur yaś ca phālgunam
saubhāgyaṃ svajanānāṃ sa
sarveṣām eti sonnatim
body.translated_text: He who, serving, passes <s>Phālguna</s> with a single meal, attains good fortune for all his kinsmen, together with eminence

body.text:
caitraṃ viṣṇuparo māsam
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
suvarṇamaṇimuktāḍhyaṃ
sa gārhasthyam avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: He who, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, passes the month of <s>Caitra</s> with a single meal, attains a household life rich in gold, gems and pearls

body.text:
yaḥ kṣaped ekabhaktena
vaiśākhaṃ pūjayan harim
naro vā yadi vā nārī
jñātīnāṃ śreṣṭhatāṃ vrajet
body.translated_text: He who passes <s>Vaiśākha</s> with a single meal, worshipping <s>Hari</s>—whether man or woman—attains pre-eminence among his kinsmen

body.text:
kṛṣṇārpitamanā jyeṣṭham
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
aiśvaryam atulaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ
pumān strī vābhijāyate
body.translated_text: He who, with mind offered to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, passes <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> with a single meal, is born—man or woman—to incomparable, excellent lordship

body.text:
āṣāḍham ekabhaktena
yo nayed viṣṇutanmanāḥ
bahudhānyo bahudhano
bahuputraś ca jāyate
body.translated_text: He who passes <s>Āṣāḍha</s> with a single meal, his mind on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is born rich in grain, rich in wealth, and rich in sons

body.text:
kṣapayed ekabhaktena
śrāvaṇaṃ viṣṇutatparaḥ
dhanadhānyahiraṇyāḍhye
kule sa jñātivardhanaḥ
body.translated_text: Intent on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he who passes <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> with a single meal is born in a family abounding in wealth, grain and gold, increasing his kin

body.text:
ekāhāro bhādrapadaṃ
yaś ca kṛṣṇaparāyaṇaḥ
dhanāḍhyaṃ sphītam acalam
aiśvaryaṃ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: He who, eating once a day, is devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in <s>Bhādrapada</s>, attains wealthy, thriving, unshakable lordship

body.text:
nayaṃś cāśvayujaṃ viṣṇuṃ
pūjayed ekabhojanaḥ
dhanavān vāhanāḍhyaś ca
bahuputraś ca jāyate
body.translated_text: Passing <s>Āśvayuja</s>, he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> eating once a day, and is born wealthy, rich in vehicles, and rich in sons

body.text:
kārttike caikadā bhuṅkte
yaś ca viṣṇuparo naraḥ
śūraś ca kṛtavidyaś ca
bahuputraś ca jāyate
body.translated_text: And the man devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> who eats once in <s>Kārttika</s> is born brave, accomplished in learning, and rich in sons

body.text:
yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇam
ekabhakto bhaven naraḥ
ahiṃsaḥ sarvabhūteṣu
vāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: But the man who for a full year is content with a single meal, harmless to all beings, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

body.text:
namo 'stu vāsudevāyety
ahaś cāṣṭaśataṃ japet
atirātrasya yajñasya
tataḥ phalam avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: and who recites by day one hundred and eight times "Homage be to <s>Vāsudeva</s>," thereby attains the fruit of the <s>atirātra</s> sacrifice

body.text:
daśa varṣasahasrāṇi
svargaloke mahīyate
tatkṣayād iha cāgatya
māhātmyaṃ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: He is exalted in the world of heaven for ten thousand years; on its exhaustion, having come here, he attains greatness

body.text:
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ
strī śūdro vā yathoditān
upavāsān imān kurvan
phalāny etāny avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>, a woman, or a <s>śūdra</s>, performing these fasts as declared, would attain these fruits

body.text:
jagatpatiṃ jagadyoniṃ
jaganniṣṭhaṃ jagadgurum
jayaṃ śaraṇam abhyetya
na janaiḥ śocyate janaḥ
body.translated_text: Going for refuge to the Lord of the world, the source of the world, the abode of the world, the world's teacher, the Victorious one, a man is not lamented by people

body.text:
yasya nāmni smṛte martyaḥ
samutkrānter anantaram
prāpnoti śāśvataṃ sthānaṃ
tataḥ pūjyataro hi saḥ
body.translated_text: He upon the remembrance of whose name a mortal, immediately after departure, attains the eternal abode—he indeed is the more to be worshipped

body.text:
nādir na madhyaṃ naivānto
yasya devasya vidyate
anāditvād amadhyatvād
anantatvāc ca so 'vyayaḥ
body.translated_text: That god for whom there exists no beginning, no middle, and no end—being without beginning, without middle, and without end, he is imperishable

body.text:
parāparaṃ sukṛtavatāṃ parāṃ gatiṃ
svayaṃbhuvaṃ prabhavan nidhānam avyayam
sanātanaṃ yad amṛtam acyutaṃ dhruvaṃ
praviśya taṃ harim amaratvam aśnute
body.translated_text: The higher and the lower, the supreme goal of the virtuous, the self-existent, the all-powerful, the imperishable repository, the eternal, immortal, undecaying, fixed—entering that <s>Hari</s>, one attains immortality

body.text:
śṛṇu dālbhya paraṃ kāmyaṃ
vrataṃ saṃtatidaṃ nṛṇām
yam upoṣya na vicchedaḥ
pitṛpiṇḍasya jāyate
body.translated_text: Hear, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, the supreme desired vow that grants progeny to men, by fasting on which no interruption of the ancestral rice-ball (<s>pitṛpiṇḍa</s>) occurs

body.text:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ caitramāse
snāto niyatamānasaḥ
kṛṣṇam abhyarcya pūjāṃ ca
devakyāḥ kurute tu yaḥ
body.translated_text: He who, on the eighth of the dark fortnight in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, bathed and of restrained mind, having worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, performs also the worship of <s>Devakī</s>,

body.text:
nirāhāro japan nāma
kṛṣṇasya jagataḥ pateḥ
upaviṣṭo japasnāna-
kṣutapraskhalitādiṣu
body.translated_text: fasting, reciting the name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the Lord of the world, while seated—at recitation, bathing, sneezing, stumbling and the like,

body.text:
pūjāyāṃ cāpi kṛṣṇasya
sapta vārān prakīrtayet
pāṣaṇḍino vikarmasthān
nālapec caiva nāstikān
body.translated_text: and during the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he should proclaim it seven times; he should not speak to heretics, those engaged in forbidden acts, or unbelievers

body.text:
prabhāte tu punaḥ snāto
dattvā viprāya dakṣiṇām
bhuñjīta kṛtapūjas tu
kṛṣṇasyaiva jagatpateḥ
body.translated_text: At dawn, bathed again, having given a fee to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having performed the worship, he should eat—the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the Lord of the world

body.text:
vaiśākhajyeṣṭhayoś caiva
pāraṇaṃ hi trimāsikam
upoṣya devadeveśaṃ
ghṛtena snāpayed dharim
body.translated_text: In <s>Vaiśākha</s> and <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> indeed is the three-monthly breaking-of-the-fast; having fasted, he should bathe <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of the gods of gods, with ghee

body.text:
āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe caiva
māse bhādrapade tathā
upoṣite dvitīyaṃ vai
pāraṇaṃ pūrvavat tu tat
body.translated_text: In the months of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, and likewise <s>Bhādrapada</s>, when one has fasted, this is the second breaking-of-the-fast, just as before

body.text:
tathaivāśvayujaṃ cādiṃ
kṛtvā māsatrayaṃ budhaḥ
upoṣya snāpayed devaṃ
haviṣā pāraṇe gate
body.translated_text: Likewise the wise man, having made <s>Āśvayuja</s> the first of three months, having fasted, should bathe the god with an oblation at the breaking-of-the-fast

body.text:
pauṣe māghe phālgune ca
naras tadvad upoṣitaḥ
caturthe pāraṇe pūrṇe
ghṛtena snāpayed dharim
body.translated_text: In <s>Pauṣa</s>, <s>Māgha</s>, and <s>Phālguna</s> the man, likewise fasting, when the fourth breaking-of-the-fast is complete, should bathe <s>Hari</s> with ghee

body.text:
evaṃ kṛtopavāsasya
puruṣasya tathā striyaḥ
na saṃtateḥ paricchedaḥ
kadācid abhijāyate
body.translated_text: Thus, for the man or the woman who has kept the fast, no interruption of progeny ever occurs

body.text:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamīm imāṃ yas tu
naro yoṣid athāpi vā
upoṣyatīha sāhlādaṃ
nṛloke prāpya nirvṛttim
body.translated_text: He or she—man or woman—who fasts on this <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s> with delight, attaining contentment here in the world of men,

body.text:
putrapautrasamṛddhiṃ ca
mṛtaḥ svarge mahīyate
ity etat kathitaṃ dālbhya
mayā kṛṣṇāṣṭaṃīvratam
body.translated_text: and the abundance of sons and grandsons, when dead is exalted in heaven; thus, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, the <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s> vow has been told by me

body.text:
prāvṛṭkāle tu niyamāñ
śṛṇu kāmyān imān mama
body.translated_text: Now hear from me these desired observances for the rainy season

body.text:
prāvṛṭkāle yadā śete
vāsudevaḥ payonidhau
bhogibhoge nijāṃ māyāṃ
yoganidrāṃ ca mānayan
body.translated_text: When in the rainy season <s>Vāsudeva</s> sleeps upon the ocean of milk, upon the coils of the serpent, honouring his own <s>Māyā</s> and the <s>yoganidrā</s> (yogic sleep),

body.text:
viśiṣṭā na pravartante
tadā yajñādikāḥ kriyāḥ
devānāṃ sā bhaved rātrir
dakṣiṇāyanasaṃjñitā
body.translated_text: then the special <s>yajña</s> and other rites are not performed; that becomes the night of the gods, called the southern course (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>)

body.text:
yadā svapiti govindo
yas tu māsaṃ catuṣṭayam
adhaḥśāyī brahmacārī
keśavārpitamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: He who, when <s>Govinda</s> sleeps, for the four months sleeps on the ground, observing chastity, with mind offered to <s>Keśava</s>,

body.text:
namo namo 'stu kṛṣṇāya
keśavāya namo namaḥ
namo 'stu narasiṃhāya
viṣṇave ca namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: "Homage, homage be to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; homage, homage to <s>Keśava</s>; homage be to <s>Narasiṃha</s>; and homage, homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>"—

body.text:
iti prātas tathā sāyaṃ
japed devakriyāparaḥ
śamayaty atiduṣpāraṃ
duritaṃ janmasaṃcitam
body.translated_text: thus reciting at dawn and at dusk, devoted to the worship of the god, he quells the most unsurpassable evil accumulated over births

body.text:
madhu māṃsaṃ ca yo māsāñ
caturas tān nirasyati
devakriyāratir viṣṇor
anusmaraṇatatparaḥ
body.translated_text: He who casts off honey and meat for those four months, delighting in the worship of the god, intent on the remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

body.text:
so 'pi svargaṃ samabhyeti
cyutas tasmāt tu jāyate
arogī dhanadhānyāḍhyaḥ
kulasaṃtatimān naraḥ
body.translated_text: he too goes to heaven; fallen from there, he is born free of disease, rich in wealth and grain, a man endowed with family and progeny

body.text:
samastamandirāṇāṃ ca
yaḥ supte madhusūdane
nirvṛttiṃ kurute so 'pi
devo vaimāniko bhavet
body.translated_text: He who, when <s>Madhusūdana</s> sleeps, brings contentment to all temples—he too becomes a god travelling in celestial cars (<s>vaimānika</s>)

body.text:
anenaiva vidhānena
naro viṣṇukriyāparaḥ
ekāhāro bhaved yas tu
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: By this very ordinance, the man devoted to the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> who eats but once is freed of all sins

body.text:
supte ca sarvalokeśe
naktabhojī bhavet tu yaḥ
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ
svargaloke 'maro bhavet
body.translated_text: When the Lord of all worlds sleeps, he who eats only at night, freed of all sins, becomes immortal in the world of heaven

body.text:
śastaṃ tv anantaraṃ puṃsāṃ
tataś caivekabhojanam
naktabhojanatulyaṃ tu
nopavāsaphalaṃ kvacit
body.translated_text: Praised for men is the eating-but-once that follows next; but the night-eating is equal to it—the fruit of fasting is nowhere lacking

body.text:
tailābhaṅgaṃ ca yo māsāṃś
caturas tān nirasyati
so 'py aṅgalāvaṇyaguṇam
ārogyaṃ ca naro labhet
body.translated_text: And the man who casts away oil-anointing for those four months, he too obtains beauty and excellence of limbs, and health

body.text:
yas tv etāni samastāni
māsān etān naraś caret
sa viṣṇulokam āsādya
viṣṇor anucaro bhavet
body.translated_text: But that man who performs all these observances during these months, having reached the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, becomes an attendant of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
caturbhiḥ pāraṇaṃ māsair
niṣpādyaṃ haritatparaiḥ
brāhmaṇān bhojayed dadyāt
tatas tebhyaś ca dakṣiṇām
body.translated_text: After four months, the breaking of the fast is to be accomplished by those devoted to green vegetables; one should feed <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and bestow upon them, and then a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee)

body.text:
pūjayec ca jagannāthaṃ
sarvapāpaharaṃ harim
prīyasva deva govindety
evaṃ caiva prasādayet
body.translated_text: And one should worship the Lord of the world, <s>Hari</s>, the remover of all sins, and should propitiate him thus: "Be pleased, O Lord <s>Govinda</s>"

body.text:
iti dālbhya samākhyātaṃ
cāturmāsye hi yad vratam
devadevasya suptasya
dvādaśīṃ śṛṇu cāparām
yasyām anantasmaraṇād
anantaphalabhāg bhavet
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, the vow which belongs to the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-month period) has been declared to you; now hear another, the <s>dvādaśī</s> (twelfth day) of the sleeping <s>God of gods</s>, on which, through the remembrance of <s>Ananta</s>, one becomes a partaker of endless fruit

body.text:
māsi proṣṭhapade śukle
dvādaśyāṃ jalaśāyinam
praṇamyānantam abhyarcya
puṣpadhūpādibhiḥ śuciḥ
body.translated_text: In the month of <s>Proṣṭhapada</s>, in the bright fortnight, on the twelfth, having bowed to him who lies upon the waters, having worshipped <s>Ananta</s> with flowers, incense, and the like, being pure

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍādibhir ālāpam
akurvan niyatātmavān
viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā
naktaṃ bhuṅkte tu yo naraḥ
body.translated_text: not holding converse with heretics and the like, of restrained self, having given a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee) to a <s>vipra</s> (brahmin), the man who eats only at night

body.text:
tiṣṭhan vrajan svapaṃś caiva
kṣutapraskhalitādiṣu
anantanāmasmaraṇaṃ
kurvann uccāraṇaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: standing, walking, and sleeping, in moments of sneezing, stumbling, and the like, performing the remembrance of the name of <s>Ananta</s>, and likewise uttering it

body.text:
anenaiva vidhānena
māsān dvādaśa vai kramāt
upoṣya pāraṇe pūrṇe
samabhyarcya jagadgurum
gītavādyena hṛdyena
prīṇayan vyuṣṭim aśnute
body.translated_text: by this very procedure, fasting through the twelve months in succession, when the breaking of the fast is complete, having duly worshipped the <s>Teacher of the world</s>, gladdening him with pleasing song and music, he attains the reward

body.text:
anantaṃ gītavādyena
yataḥ phalam udāhṛtam
tenānantaṃ samabhyarcya
tad eva labhate phalam
body.translated_text: Since the fruit is declared to come from song and music for <s>Ananta</s>, therefore, having worshipped <s>Ananta</s> with these, he obtains that very fruit

body.text:
evaṃ yaḥ puruṣaḥ kuryād
anantārādhanaṃ śuciḥ
nārī vā svargam abhyetya
so 'anantaphalam aśnute
body.translated_text: Thus, whatever man, being pure, performs this worship of <s>Ananta</s>, or whatever woman, having gone to heaven, obtains the endless fruit

body.text:
evaṃ dālbhya hṛṣīkeśo
narair bhaktyā yathāvidhi
phalaṃ dadāty asulabhaṃ
salilenāpi pūjitaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> gives to men, who worship with devotion according to the rule, a reward hard to obtain, even when worshipped with water alone

body.text:
na viṣṇur vittadānena
puṣpair vā na phalais tathā
ārādhyate suśuddhena
hṛdayenaiva kevalam
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not worshipped by the giving of wealth, nor by flowers, nor likewise by fruits; he is worshipped by a thoroughly pure heart alone

body.text:
rāgādyapetaṃ hṛdayaṃ
vāg duṣṭā nānṛtādinā
hiṃsādirahitaḥ kāyaḥ
keśavārādhanatrayam
body.translated_text: A heart free from passion and the rest, speech undefiled by falsehood and the like, a body free from violence and the rest—this is the threefold worship of <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
rāgādidūṣite citte
nāspadī madhusūdanaḥ
karoti na ratiṃ haṃsaḥ
kadācit kardamāmbhasi
body.translated_text: In a mind defiled by passion and the rest, <s>Madhusūdana</s> finds no abode; the swan never takes delight in muddy water

body.text:
na yogyā keśavastutyai
vāg duṣṭā cānṛtādinā
tamaso nāśanāyālaṃ
nendor lekhā ghanāvṛtā
body.translated_text: Speech defiled by falsehood and the like is not fit for the praise of <s>Keśava</s>; the streak of the moon veiled by clouds is not able to dispel the darkness

body.text:
hiṃsādidūṣitaḥ kāyaḥ
keśavārādhane kutaḥ
janacittaprasādāya
na nabhas timirāvṛtam
body.translated_text: How can a body defiled by violence and the rest serve in the worship of <s>Keśava</s>? The sky shrouded in darkness does not gladden the minds of people

body.text:
tasmāc chraddhasva bhāvena
satyabhāvena ca dvija
ahiṃsakena govindo
nisargād eva toṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, have faith with sincere disposition and with a truthful disposition, O twice-born; <s>Govinda</s> is by his very nature gratified by the non-violent man

body.text:
sarvasvam api kṛṣṇāya
yo dadyāt kuṭilāśayaḥ
sa naivārādhayaty enaṃ
sadbhāvenārcayācyutam
body.translated_text: He of crooked intent who would give even all his possessions to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he does not worship him; one worships <s>Acyuta</s> with a sincere disposition

body.text:
rāgādyapetaṃ hṛdayaṃ
kuru tvaṃ keśavārpitam
tataḥ prāpsyasi duḥprāpyam
ayatnenaiva keśavam
body.translated_text: Make your heart, free from passion and the rest, offered to <s>Keśava</s>; then you shall obtain, without effort, <s>Keśava</s> who is hard to attain

body.text:
bhagavan kathitaḥ samyak
kāmyo 'yaṃ keśavaṃ prati
ārādhanavidhiḥ sarvo
bhūyaḥ pṛcchāmi tad vada
body.translated_text: O Lord, the entire procedure of optional worship directed toward <s>Keśava</s> has been rightly told; I ask again—tell me that

body.text:
kule janma tathārogyaṃ
dhanarddhiś ceha durlabhā
tritayaṃ prāpyate yena
tan me vada mahāmune
body.translated_text: Birth in a good family, likewise health, and abundance of wealth are hard to obtain here; tell me, O great sage, that by which the triad is obtained

body.text:
mātāmahaṃ kāṇvam udāravīryaṃ
maharṣim abhyarcya kulaprasūtim
papraccha puṃsām atha yoṣitāṃ ca
duṣvantaputro bharataḥ praṇamya
body.translated_text: Having worshipped his maternal grandfather, the <s>maharṣi</s> <s>Kāṇva</s> of noble valor, <s>Bharata</s> the son of <s>Duṣyanta</s>, bowing down, asked about the good birth-lineage of men and likewise of women

body.text:
yathāvad ācaṣṭa tato mahātmā
sa rājavaryāya yathā kuleṣu
prayānti sūtiṃ puruṣāḥ striyaś ca
yathā ca samyak sukhino bhavanti
body.translated_text: Then that great soul duly explained to the best of kings how men and women come to birth in good families, and how they become thoroughly happy

body.text:
pauṣe site dvādaśame 'hni sārke
tathārkṣayoge jagataḥ prasūtim
saṃpūjya viṣṇuṃ vidhinopavāsī
sraggandhadhūpānnavaropahāraiḥ
body.translated_text: On the bright twelfth day of <s>Pauṣa</s>, when the sun is present together with the proper lunar mansion, having worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is the origin of the world, according to the rule, while fasting, with garlands, perfumes, incense, food, and other offerings

body.text:
gṛhṇīta māsaṃ pratimāsapūjām
dānādiyuktaṃ vratam abdam ekam
dadyāc ca dānaṃ dvijapuṅgavebhyas
tad ucyamānaṃ vinibodha bhūpa
body.translated_text: one should undertake the monthly worship for a month, the vow joined with gift-giving and the rest, for one year; and one should give a gift to the bulls among the twice-born—hear, O king, that which is being told

body.text:
ghṛtaṃ tilān vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ
yavānnam ambhaḥkarakānnapānam
chattraṃ payo 'nnaṃ guḍaphāṇitāḍhyaṃ
srakcandanaṃ vastram anukrameṇa
body.translated_text: ghee, sesame, rice and barley, gold, barley-food, water-pots with food and drink, an umbrella, milk and food rich in raw sugar and molasses, garlands, sandal-paste, and a garment—in order

body.text:
māse ca māse vidhinoditena
tasyāṃ tithau lokaguruṃ prapūjya
aśnīta yāny ātmaviśuddhihetoḥ
saṃprāśanānīha nibodha tāni
body.translated_text: In each and every month, by the procedure declared, having worshipped the <s>Teacher of the world</s> on that lunar day, one should eat those things which are for the sake of one's own purification—hear now of those eatables here

body.text:
gomūtram ambho ghṛtam āmaśākaṃ
dūrvā dadhi vrīhiyavāṃs tilāṃś ca
sūryāṃśutaptaṃ jalam ambu dārbhaṃ
kṣīraṃ ca māsakramaśopayuñjyāt
body.translated_text: cow's urine, water, ghee, raw vegetables, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, curds, rice and barley, and sesame, water heated by the sun's rays, <s>dārbha</s>-grass water, and milk—one should use them in monthly succession

body.text:
kule pradhāne dhanadhānyapūrṇe
vivekavaty astasamastaduḥkhe
prāpnoti janmāvikalendriyaś ca
bhavaty arogo matimān sukhī ca
body.translated_text: In a preeminent family, full of wealth and grain, endowed with discernment, free from all sorrow, one attains birth, and becomes possessed of unimpaired senses, free from disease, intelligent, and happy

body.text:
tasmāt tvam apy etad amoghavid yo
nārāyaṇārādhanam apramattaḥ
kuruṣva viṣṇuṃ bhagavantam īśam
ārādhya kāmān akhilān upaiti
body.translated_text: Therefore you too, knowing this unfailing worship of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, perform it heedfully; having worshipped the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Sovereign, one attains all desires

body.text:
yadā ca śukladvādaśyāṃ
nakṣatraṃ śravaṇaṃ bhavet
tadā sā tu mahāpuṇyā
dvādaśī vijayā smṛtā
body.translated_text: And when on the bright twelfth the lunar mansion <s>Śravaṇa</s> occurs, then that twelfth, being of great merit, is called <s>Vijayā</s>

body.text:
tasyāṃ snātaḥ sarvatīrthaiḥ
snāto bhavati mānavaḥ
saṃpūjya varṣapūjāyāḥ
sakalaṃ phalam aśnute
body.translated_text: Bathing on that day, a man becomes one bathed in all sacred fords; having worshipped, he obtains the entire fruit of the year's worship

body.text:
ekaṃ japtvā sahasrasya
japtasyāpnoti yat phalam
dānaṃ sahasraguṇitaṃ
tathā vai vipra bhojanam
body.translated_text: Having recited once, he obtains the fruit which is obtained by reciting a thousand times; the gift becomes multiplied a thousandfold, and likewise, O <s>vipra</s>, the feeding

body.text:
yat kṣemam api vai tasyāṃ
sahasraṃ śrāvaṇe tu tat
anyasyām eva tithyāṃ
śubhāyāṃ śrāvaṇaṃ yadā
body.translated_text: Whatever welfare-act there is on that day, that becomes a thousandfold under <s>Śravaṇa</s>; when <s>Śravaṇa</s> occurs on any other auspicious lunar day

body.text:
homas tathopavāsaś ca
sahasrākhyaphalapradaḥ
body.translated_text: the oblation and likewise the fast yield the fruit called a thousandfold

body.text:
rohiṇyāś ca yadā kṛṣṇa-
pakṣe 'ṣṭamyāṃ dvijottama
jayantī nāma sā proktā
sarvapāpaharā tithiḥ
body.translated_text: And when <s>Rohiṇī</s> occurs in the dark fortnight on the eighth, O best of the twice-born, that lunar day is proclaimed <s>Jayantī</s> by name, the remover of all sins

body.text:
yad bālye yac ca kaumāre
yauvane vārddhike ca yat
saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ
svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu
body.translated_text: Whatever sin was done in childhood, in boyhood, in youth, and in old age, sin committed in seven births, whether little or much

body.text:
tat kṣālayati govindaṃ
tasyām abhyarcya bhaktitaḥ
homajapyādidānānāṃ
phalaṃ ca śatasaṃmitam
body.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> washes that away when one worships him with devotion on that day; and the fruit of oblations, recitations, and the rest, and of gifts, is reckoned as a hundredfold

body.text:
saṃprāpnoti na saṃdeho
yac cānyan manasecchati
upavāsaś ca tatrokto
mahāpātakanāśanaḥ
body.translated_text: one obtains, there is no doubt, and whatever else one desires in the mind; and the fast there enjoined is the destroyer of great sins

body.text:
ekadaśyāṃ śuklapakṣe
yadā rkṣaṃ vai punarvasuḥ
nāmnā sātijayākhyātā
tithīnām uttamā tithiḥ
body.translated_text: On the eleventh in the bright fortnight, when the mansion is indeed <s>Punarvasu</s>, it is declared by name <s>Atijayā</s>, the highest of lunar days

body.text:
yo dadāti tilaprasthaṃ
tṛṣkālaṃ vatsaraṃ naraḥ
upavāsaṃ ca tasyāṃ yaḥ
karoty etat samaṃ smṛtam
body.translated_text: The man who gives a <s>prastha</s>-measure of sesame thrice at the proper time for a year, and he who keeps a fast on it—that is reckoned as equal

body.text:
tasyāṃ jagatpatir devaḥ
sarvaḥ sarveśvaro hariḥ
pratyakṣatāṃ prayāty alpaṃ
tadānantaphalaṃ smṛtam
body.translated_text: On that day the divine Lord of the world, the all, <s>Hari</s> the Lord of all, comes to manifest presence even slightly; that is reckoned as endless fruit

body.text:
sagareṇa kakutsthena
duṃdhumāreṇa gādhinā
tasyām ārādhitaḥ kṛṣṇo
dattavān nikhilāṃ bhuvam
body.translated_text: By <s>Sagara</s>, by <s>Kakutstha</s>, by <s>Dhundhumāra</s>, by <s>Gādhin</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was worshipped on that day, and he granted the whole earth

body.text:
ayane cottare prāpte
yaḥ snāpayati keśavam
ghṛtaprasthena pāpaṃ saḥ
sakalaṃ vai vyapohati
body.translated_text: When the northward course of the sun has arrived, he who bathes <s>Keśava</s> with a <s>prastha</s> of ghee, he washes away all his sin completely

body.text:
kapilāṃ vipramukhyāya
dadāty anudinaṃ hi yaḥ
ghṛtasnānaṃ ca devasya
tasmin kāle samaṃ hi tat
body.translated_text: Whoever gives daily a tawny cow to a chief among <s>vipras</s>, the bathing of the god with ghee at that time is equal to that indeed

body.text:
snāpyamānaṃ ca paśyati
ye ghṛtenottarāyaṇe
body.translated_text: And those who behold him being bathed with ghee during the northward course of the sun

body.text:
te yānti viṣṇusālokyaṃ
sarvapāpavivarjitāḥ
body.translated_text: they go to the state of dwelling in the same world as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, freed from all sins

body.text:
maitreyī brāhmaṇī pūrvaṃ
yājñavalkyam apṛcchata
praṇipatya mahābhāgaṃ
yogeśvaram akalmaṣam
body.translated_text: Formerly the brahmin woman <s>Maitreyī</s> asked <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, the lord of yoga, the stainless one, having bowed to that greatly fortunate one

body.text:
pāpapraśamanāyālaṃ
yat puṇyasyopavṛṃhakam
manorathapradaṃ yac ca
tad vrataṃ kathyatāṃ mama
body.translated_text: Tell me that vow which is sufficient for the calming of sin, which is an augmenter of merit, and which grants the wish of the heart

body.text:
kāni dānāni śastāni
snānāni ca yatavrata
praśastās tithayaḥ kāś ca
prāśanāni ca śaṃsa me
body.translated_text: Which gifts are praised, and which bathings, O you of restrained vows? And which lunar days are commended? And tell me the eatables as well

body.text:
sarvadānāni śastāni
yāny uddiśya janārdanam
dīyante vipramukhyebhyaḥ
śraddhāpūtena cetasā
body.translated_text: All gifts are praised which, having reference to <s>Janārdana</s>, are given to the chief among <s>vipras</s> with a mind purified by faith

body.text:
tā eva tithayaḥ śastā
yāsv abhyarcya janārdanam
kriyante śradhayā samyag
upavāsavratāḥ sadā
body.translated_text: Those very lunar days are praised on which, having worshipped <s>Janārdana</s>, the fast-vows are always rightly performed with faith

body.text:
prāpyate vividhair yajñair
yat phalaṃ sādhvasādhubhiḥ
upavāsais tad āpnoti
samabhyarcya janārdanam
body.translated_text: Whatever fruit is obtained by various sacrifices, by good and bad men alike, one obtains that by fasts, having worshipped <s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
manorathānāṃ saṃprāpti-
kārakaṃ pāpanāśanam
śrūyatāṃ mama dharmajñe
vratānām uttamaṃ vratam
body.translated_text: the bringer-about of the attainment of the wishes of the heart, the destroyer of sin—let it be heard from me, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, the highest vow among vows

body.text:
yat kṛtvā na jaḍo nāndho
badhiro na ca duḥkhitaḥ
na caiveṣṭaviyogārtiṃ
kaścit prāpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: Having performed which, no man becomes dull, nor blind, nor deaf, nor sorrowful, nor does anyone meet the anguish of separation from what is dear

body.text:
na cāpriyo 'sya lokasya
na daridro na durgatiḥ
sapta janmāni bhavati
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: and he is not unloved by this world, nor poor, nor in misfortune; for seven births he is so, and he is released from all sins

body.text:
viṣṇuvratam idaṃ khyātaṃ
bhāṣitaṃ viṣṇunā svayam
body.translated_text: This is proclaimed the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-vow, spoken by <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself

body.text:
pauṣaśukladvitīyādi
kṛtvā dinacatuṣṭayam
ṣaṇmāsapāraṇaprāyaṃ
gṛhṇīyāt paramaṃ vratam
body.translated_text: Beginning on the second of the bright fortnight of <s>Pauṣa</s>, having done a set of four days, with the breaking of the fast coming after six months, one should undertake the supreme vow

body.text:
pūrvaṃ siddhārthakaiḥ snānaṃ
tataḥ kṛṣṇatilaiḥ smṛtam
vacayā ca tṛtīye 'hni
sarvauṣadhyā tataḥ param
body.translated_text: First, bathing is enjoined with white-mustard seeds, then with black sesame; with sweet-flag on the third day, and thereafter with all healing herbs

body.text:
nāmnā kṛṣṇācyutākhyena
tathānantena pūjayet
tathaiva ca caturthe 'hni
hṛṣīkeśena keśavam
devam abhyarcya puṣpaiś ca
pattrair dhūpānulepanaiḥ
body.translated_text: One should worship him by the name <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, and likewise by <s>Ananta</s>; and likewise on the fourth day one should worship <s>Keśava</s> by <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>—having worshipped the god with flowers, leaves, incense, and unguents

body.text:
udgacchataś ca bālendor
dadyād arghyaṃ samāhitaḥ
puṣpaiḥ pattraiḥ phalaiś caiva
sarvadhānyaiś ca bhaktitaḥ
body.translated_text: and to the rising young moon one should offer, with concentrated mind, an <s>arghya</s> (oblation) with flowers, leaves, and fruits, and with all grains, with devotion

body.text:
dinakrameṇa caitāni
candranāmāni kīrtayet
śaśicandraśaśāṅkendu-
saṃjñāni brahmavādini
body.translated_text: In daily succession one should proclaim these names of the moon: <s>Śaśin</s>, <s>Candra</s>, <s>Śaśāṅka</s>, and <s>Indu</s> by name, O expounder of <s>Brahman</s>

body.text:
naktaṃ bhuñjīta matimān
yāvat tiṣṭhati candramāḥ
astaṃgate na bhuñjīta
vratabhaṅgabhayāc chubhe
body.translated_text: The wise man should eat at night, as long as the moon stands; when it has set he should not eat, for fear of breaking the vow, O auspicious one

body.text:
evaṃ sarveṣu māseṣu
jyeṣṭhānteṣu yaśasvini
kartavyaṃ vai vrataśreṣṭhaṃ
dvitīyādicaturdinam
body.translated_text: Thus in all the months, ending with <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, O illustrious one, the best of vows is to be performed on the four days beginning with the second

body.text:
viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ dadyāt
pañcamyāṃ ca svaśaktitaḥ
evaṃ samāpayen māsaiḥ
ṣaḍbhiḥ prathamapāraṇam
body.translated_text: One should give a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee) to a <s>vipra</s> on the fifth, according to one's own ability; thus one should complete the first breaking-of-the-fast in six months

body.text:
pāraṇante ca devasya
prīṇanaṃ bhaktitaḥ śubhe
yathāśaktyā tu kartavyaṃ
vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet
body.translated_text: And at the end of the breaking-of-the-fast, the gladdening of the god is to be done with devotion, O auspicious one, according to one's ability; one should avoid stinginess with wealth

body.text:
āṣāḍhādidvitīyaṃ tu
ṣaṇmāsena tapodhane
pāraṇaṃ vai samākhyātaṃ
vratasyāsya śubhapradam
body.translated_text: Beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, the second breaking-of-the-fast is declared, after six months, O you rich in austerity, which is the giver of the auspicious result of this vow

body.text:
vratam etad dilīpena
duṣvantena yayātinā
tathānyaiḥ pṛthivīpālair
upavāsavidhānataḥ
caritaṃ munimukhyaiś ca
ṛcīkacyavanādibhiḥ
body.translated_text: This vow was performed by <s>Dilīpa</s>, by <s>Duṣyanta</s>, by <s>Yayāti</s>, and by other protectors of the earth, according to the rule of fasting, and by the chief sages, <s>Ṛcīka</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, and the rest

body.text:
surambhayā sukaikeyyā
śāṇḍilyā dhūmrapiṅgayā
sudeṣṇayāthavā riṇyā
matimatyā kṛtāśayā
body.translated_text: by <s>Surambhā</s>, by <s>Sukaikeyī</s>, by <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>, by <s>Dhūmrapiṅgā</s>, by <s>Sudeṣṇā</s>, or by <s>Riṇī</s>, by <s>Matimatī</s> of resolved heart

body.text:
sāvitryā paurṇamāsyā ca
vairiṇyā ca subhadrayā
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśām
iti strībhir anuṣṭhitam
body.translated_text: by <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and by <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, by <s>Vairiṇī</s>, and by <s>Subhadrā</s>—thus it was practiced by women of the brahmin, kṣatriya, and vaiśya orders

body.text:
urvaśyā rambhayā caiva
saurabheyyā tathā vratam
varāpsarobhir dharmajñe
caritaṃ dharmavāṃchayā
body.translated_text: by <s>Urvaśī</s>, and by <s>Rambhā</s>, and likewise by <s>Saurabheyī</s>, the vow was practiced, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, by the best of <s>apsarases</s> out of desire for <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
prathame pādapūjā syād
dvitīye nābhipūjanam
tṛtīye vakṣasaḥ pūjā
caturthe śiraso hareḥ
body.translated_text: On the first, let there be worship of the feet; on the second, worship of the navel; on the third, worship of the chest; on the fourth, of the head of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
etac cīrtvā samastebhyaḥ
pāpebhyaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ
mucyate sakalāṃś caiva
saṃprāpnoti manorathān
body.translated_text: Having performed this, endowed with faith, one is freed from all sins and attains all the wishes of the heart

body.text:
vratānām uttamaṃ hy etat
svayaṃ devena bhāṣitam
pāpapraśamanaṃ śastaṃ
manorathaphalapradam
body.translated_text: This indeed is the highest of vows, spoken by the god himself, the calming of sin, commended, the giver of the fruit of the heart's wishes

body.text:
yaṃ ca kāmam abhidhyāyan
kriyate niyatavrataiḥ
vratam etan mahābhāge
taṃ tu pūrayate nṛṇām
body.translated_text: And whatever desire one meditates upon while it is performed by those of fixed vows, this vow, O greatly fortunate one, fulfills that for men

body.text:
manorathān pūrayati
sarvapāpaṃ vyapohati
avyāhatendriyatvaṃ ca
sapta janmāni yacchati
body.translated_text: It fulfills the wishes of the heart, washes away all sin, and grants unimpaired senses for seven births

body.text:
māghe snātasya yat puṇyaṃ
prayāge pāpanāśanam
sakalaṃ tad avāpnoti
śrutvā viṣṇuvrataṃ tv idam
body.translated_text: Whatever merit there is of one who has bathed in <s>Māgha</s>, the destruction of sin at <s>Prayāga</s>, all that one obtains by hearing this <s>Viṣṇu</s>-vow

body.text:
sākṣād bhagavatā proktaṃ
paramaṃ pāpanāśanam
body.translated_text: It was spoken directly by the Blessed Lord, the supreme destroyer of sin

body.text:
śuklapakṣe tu pauṣasya
saṃprāptidvādaśīṃ śṛṇu
yām upoṣya samāpnoti
sarvān eva manorathān
body.translated_text: Hear now of the <s>Saṃprāpti-dvādaśī</s> in the bright fortnight of <s>Pauṣa</s>, by fasting on which one attains all the wishes of the heart

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍādibhir ālāpam
akurvan viṣṇutatparaḥ
pūjayet praṇato devam
ekāgramatir acyutam
body.translated_text: Not holding converse with heretics and the like, intent upon <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bowed down, one should worship the god <s>Acyuta</s> with single-minded attention

body.text:
pauṣādipāraṇaṃ māsaiḥ
ṣaḍbhir jyeṣṭhāntakaṃ smṛtam
prathame puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
nāma devasya gīyate
body.translated_text: The breaking-of-the-fast beginning with <s>Pauṣa</s>, ending with <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, is reckoned to be in six months; in the first, the name of the god is sung as <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>

body.text:
dvitīye mādhavākhyaṃ tu
viśvarūpaṃ tu phālgune
puruṣottamākhyaṃ ca tataḥ
pañcame cācyuteti ca
body.translated_text: in the second as <s>Mādhava</s>, in <s>Phālguna</s> as <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, then as <s>Puruṣottama</s>, and in the fifth as <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
ṣaṣṭhe jayeti devasya
guhyaṃ nāma prakīrtyate
pūrveṣu ṣaṭsu māseṣu
snānaprāśanayos tilāḥ
body.translated_text: in the sixth, the secret name of the god is proclaimed as <s>Jaya</s>; in the first six months, sesame is used in the bathing and the eating

body.text:
āṣāḍhādiṣu māseṣu
pañcagavyam udāhṛtam
snāne ca prāśane caiva
praśastaṃ pāpanāśanam
body.translated_text: In the months beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, the <s>pañcagavya</s> (five products of the cow) is declared, in bathing and in eating, to be commended and the destroyer of sin

body.text:
pratimāsaṃ ca devasya
kṛtvā pūjāṃ yathāvidhi
viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ dadyāc
śraddadhānaḥ svaśaktitaḥ
body.translated_text: And having performed the worship of the god each month according to rule, the faithful one should give a fee to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> according to his ability

body.text:
pāraṇānte ca devasya
prīṇanaṃ bhaktipūrvakam
kruvīta śaktyā govinde
sadbhāvābhyarcano yataḥ
body.translated_text: And at the end of the breaking-of-the-fast, he should perform the gratification of the god, preceded by devotion, according to his power—since worship of <s>Govinda</s> rests on right disposition

body.text:
naktaṃ bhuñjīta ca tatas
tailakṣāravivarjitaṃ
ekādaśyām uṣitvaivaṃ
dvādaśyām athavā dine
body.translated_text: Then he should eat at night, free of oil and alkali; having fasted thus on the eleventh (<s>ekādaśī</s>), or else on the twelfth (<s>dvādaśī</s>) day

body.text:
etām uṣitvā dharmajñe
prīṇanaṃ devatatparaḥ
sarvakāmān avāpnoti
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: Having fasted thus, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, intent on the deity, performing the gratification, he attains all desires and is freed from all sins

body.text:
yataḥ sarvam avāpnoti
yad yad icchati cetasā
tato lokeṣu vikhyātā
saṃprāptidvādaśīti vai
body.translated_text: Since one attains all that one desires in mind, it is therefore renowned among the worlds as the "<s>Saṃprāptidvādaśī</s>" (the Attainment-Twelfth)

body.text:
kṛtābhilaṣitā hy eṣā
prārabdhā dharmatatparaiḥ
pūrayaty akhilān kāmān
saṃśrutā ca dine dine
body.translated_text: For this vow, undertaken by those intent on <s>dharma</s> with their wish in mind, fulfills all desires, and even when merely heard of day by day

body.text:
tasminn eva dine puṇye
govindadvādaśīṃ śṛṇu
yasyāṃ samyag anuṣṭhānāt
prāpnoty abhimataṃ phalam
body.translated_text: On that very holy day hear of the <s>Govindadvādaśī</s>, by the right performance of which one attains the desired fruit

body.text:
pauṣamāse site pakṣe
dvādaśyāṃ samupoṣitaḥ
saṃyak saṃpūjya govindaṃ
nāmnā devam adhokṣajam
puṣpadhūpopahārādyair
upavāsaiḥ samāhitaḥ
body.translated_text: In the bright fortnight of the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, fasting on the twelfth, having duly worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, the god <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, by name, with flowers, incense, offerings and the rest, composed in fasting,

body.text:
govindeti japan nāma
punas tadgatamānasaḥ
viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ dadyād
yathāśakti tapodhane
body.translated_text: muttering the name "<s>Govinda</s>," his mind again fixed on him, he should give a fee to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> according to his ability, O ascetic

body.text:
svapan vibuddhaḥ skhalito
govindeti ca kīrtayet
pāṣaṇḍādivikarmasthair
ālāpaṃ ca vivarjayet
body.translated_text: Sleeping, waking, or stumbling, he should proclaim "<s>Govinda</s>," and should avoid conversation with heretics and others engaged in forbidden acts

body.text:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ vāpi
dadhi kṣīram athāpi vā
godehataḥ samutpannaṃ
saṃprāśnītātmaśuddhaye
body.translated_text: He should consume cow's urine, or cow-dung, or curd, or milk, produced from the body of a cow, for the purification of himself

body.text:
dvitīye 'hni punaḥ snātas
tathaivābhyarcya taṃ prabhum
tenaiva nāmnā saṃstūya
dattvā viprāya dakṣiṇām
tato bhuñjīta godeha-
saṃbhūtena samanvitam
body.translated_text: On the second day, bathed again, having likewise worshipped that Lord, having praised him by that same name, having given a fee to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, he should then eat, taking what is produced from the cow's body

body.text:
evam evākhilān māsān
upoṣya prayataḥ śuciḥ
dadyād gavāhnikaṃ bhaktyā
pratimāsaṃ svaśaktitaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, fasting in this very way through all the months, restrained and pure, he should give the daily cow-offering with devotion each month according to his ability

body.text:
pārite ca punar varṣe
yathāśakti gavāhnikam
dattvā paragave bhūyaḥ
śṛṇu yat phalam aśnute
body.translated_text: And when the year is completed, having given the daily cow-offering according to ability, and again given another cow—hear what fruit he obtains

body.text:
suvarṇaśṛṅgāḥ pañca gāḥ
ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca vṛṣabhaṃ naraḥ
pratimāsaṃ dvijāgrebhyo
yad dattvā phalam aśnute
body.translated_text: The man who, having given each month to the foremost of the twice-born five cows with gilded horns and a sixth, a bull—what fruit he obtains,

body.text:
tad āpnoty akhilaṃ samyag
vratam etad upoṣitaḥ
taṃ ca lokam avāpnoti
govindo yatra tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: all that he obtains fully who has duly fasted on this vow; and he attains that world where <s>Govinda</s> dwells

body.text:
govindadvādaśīm etām
upoṣya divi tārakāḥ
vidyotamānā dṛśyante
lokair adyāpi śobhane
body.translated_text: Having fasted on this <s>Govindadvādaśī</s>, the stars are seen shining radiantly in heaven, viewed by people even today, O auspicious one

body.text:
upavāsavratānāṃ tu
vaikalyaṃ yan mahāmune
dānakarmakṛtaṃ tasya
vipāko vada yādṛśaḥ
body.translated_text: But as for the deficiency in fasting-vows, O great sage, tell me of what sort is the ripening of the consequence wrought upon his charitable deeds

body.text:
yajñānām upavāsānāṃ
vratānāṃ ca yatavrate
vaikalyāt phalavaikalyaṃ
yādṛśaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva me
body.translated_text: Of sacrifices, fasts, and vows, O you of restrained vows, the deficiency of fruit that comes from deficiency—hear from me of what sort it is

body.text:
upavāsādinā rājyaṃ
saṃprāpyaṃ te tathā vasu
bhraṣṭaiśvaryā nirdhanāś ca
bhavanti puruṣāḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: By fasting and the like, kingship is to be attained, and likewise wealth; yet men become fallen from lordship and destitute again

body.text:
rūpaṃ tathottamaṃ prāpya
vratavaikalyadoṣataḥ
kāṇāḥ kuṇṭhāś ca bhūyas te
bhavanty andhāś ca mānavāḥ
body.translated_text: Likewise, having attained the highest beauty, through the fault of deficiency in the vow, men again become one-eyed, maimed, and blind

body.text:
upavāsān naraḥ patnīṃ
nārī prāpya tathā patim
viyogaṃ vratavaikalyād
ubhayaṃ tad avāpnute
body.translated_text: By fasting a man attains a wife, and a woman likewise a husband; but through deficiency in the vow both attain separation

body.text:
ye dravye saty adātāras
tathānyenāhitāgnayaḥ
kule ca sati duḥśīlā
dauṣkulāḥ śīlinaś ca ye
body.translated_text: Those who, having wealth, are non-givers, and others who have not established their sacred fires; those who, though of good family, are ill-conducted, and those of bad family who are of good conduct,

body.text:
vastrānulepanair hīnā
bhūṣaṇaiś cātirūpiṇaḥ
virūparūpāś ca tathā
prasādhanaguṇānvitāḥ
body.translated_text: those destitute of garments and unguents and ornaments yet of surpassing beauty, and likewise those misshapen in form yet endowed with the qualities of adornment—

body.text:
te sarve vratavaikalyāt
phalavaikalyam āgatāḥ
guṇino 'pi hi doṣeṇa
saṃyuktāḥ saṃbhavanti te
body.translated_text: all these, through deficiency in the vow, have come to deficiency of fruit; though endowed with merits, they come to be joined with a defect

body.text:
tasmān na vratavaikalyaṃ
yajñavaikalyam eva vā
upavāse ca kartavyaṃ
vaikalyād vikalaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: Therefore deficiency in the vow, or indeed deficiency in the sacrifice, ought not to be made in the fast; from deficiency the fruit is deficient

body.text:
kathaṃcid yadi vaikalyam
upavāsādike bhavet
kiṃ tatra vada kartavyam
acchidraṃ yena jāyate
body.translated_text: If somehow a deficiency should occur in the fasting and the like, tell what is to be done in that case by which it becomes flawless

body.text:
akhaṇḍadvādaśīm etām
aśeṣeṣv eva karmasu
vaikalyapraśamāyālaṃ
śṛṇuṣva gadato mama
body.translated_text: Hear, as I tell of it, this "Unbroken Twelfth" (<s>Akhaṇḍadvādaśī</s>), which suffices to allay deficiency in all rites whatsoever

body.text:
mārgaśīrṣe site pakṣe
dvādaśyāṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ
kṛtopavāso deveśaṃ
samabhyarcya janārdanam
body.translated_text: In the bright fortnight of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, restrained and pure, on the twelfth, having performed the fast and worshipped the Lord of the gods, <s>Janārdana</s>,

body.text:
pañcagavyajalasnātaḥ
pañcagavyakṛtāśanaḥ
yavavrīhibhṛtaṃ pātraṃ
dadyād viprāya bhaktitaḥ
idaṃ coccārayed bhaktyā
devasya purato hareḥ
body.translated_text: bathed in the water of the <s>pañcagavya</s> (five cow-products), eating the <s>pañcagavya</s>, he should give with devotion a vessel filled with barley and rice to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; and he should utter this with devotion before the god <s>Hari</s>:

body.text:
sapta janmāni yat kiṃcid
mayā khaṇḍavrataṃ kṛtam
bhagavaṃs tvatprasādena
tad akhaṇḍam ihāstu me
body.translated_text: "Whatever broken vow I have performed through seven births, O blessed one, by your grace let it be unbroken for me here

body.text:
yathākhaṇḍaṃ jagat sarvam
tvam eva puruṣottama
tathākhilāny akhaṇḍāni
vratāni mama santu vai
body.translated_text: Just as the whole world is unbroken, you alone, O <s>Puruṣottama</s>, so let all my vows be entirely unbroken"

body.text:
evam evānumāsaṃ vai
cāturmāsyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: In this very way, month by month, the ordinance of the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly observance) is taught

body.text:
caturbhir eva māsais tu
pāraṇaṃ prathamaṃ smṛtam
prīṇanaṃ ca hareḥ kuryāt
pārite pāraṇe tataḥ
body.translated_text: After four months the first breaking-of-the-fast is taught; and he should perform the gratification of <s>Hari</s>, when the breaking-of-the-fast is completed thereafter

body.text:
caitrādiṣu ca māseṣu
caturṣv anyaṃ tu pāraṇam
tatrāpi saktupātrāṇi
dadyāc chraddhāsamanvitaḥ
body.translated_text: And in the four months beginning with <s>Caitra</s>, another breaking-of-the-fast; there too he should give vessels of barley-meal, endowed with faith

body.text:
śrāvaṇādiṣu māseṣu
kārttikānteṣu pāraṇam
yatnāt tu ghṛtapātrāṇi
dadyād viprāya bhaktitaḥ
body.translated_text: In the months beginning with <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> and ending with <s>Kārttika</s> is the breaking-of-the-fast; with effort he should give vessels of ghee to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> with devotion

body.text:
evaṃ samyag yathānyāyam
akhaṇḍadvādaśīṃ naraḥ
yad upoṣyaty akhaṇḍaṃ sa
vratasya phalam aśnute
body.translated_text: Thus, rightly and according to rule, the man who fasts on the <s>Akhaṇḍadvādaśī</s> unbrokenly obtains the unbroken fruit of the vow

body.text:
sapta janmasu vaikalyam
yad vratasya kvacit kṛtam
karoty avikalaṃ sarvam
akhaṇḍadvādaśīvratam
body.translated_text: Whatever deficiency of a vow has been somewhere committed in seven births, the <s>Akhaṇḍadvādaśī</s> vow makes it all flawless

body.text:
tasmād eṣātiyatnena
naraiḥ strībhiś ca suvrate
akhaṇḍadvādaśī samyag
upoṣyā phalakāṃkṣibhiḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, O you of good vows, this <s>Akhaṇḍadvādaśī</s> should be duly observed with great effort by men and women who desire the fruit

body.text:
evaṃ purā yājñavalkyaḥ
pṛṣṭaḥ patnyā mahāmuniḥ
ācaṣṭa puṇyaphaladam
upavāsavidhiṃ param
body.translated_text: Thus formerly the great sage <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, questioned by his wife, declared this supreme fasting ordinance which grants the fruit of merit

body.text:
tathā tvam api viprarṣe
keśavārādhane rataḥ
vratopavāsaparamo
bhavethā nānyamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: So you too, O sage among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, delighting in the worship of <s>Keśava</s>, should be wholly devoted to vows and fasting, with no other thought in mind

body.text:
punaś caitan mahābhāga
śrūyatāṃ gadato mama
proktaṃ nareṇa devānāṃ
tithimāhātmyam uttamam
body.translated_text: Again hear this, O greatly fortunate one, as I tell it—the supreme glory of the lunar days (<s>tithimāhātmya</s>), declared by a man for the gods

body.text:
vijayātijayā caiva
jayantī pāpanāśanī
tathottarāyaṇaṃ śastaṃ
sarvadā keśavārcane
body.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Atijayā</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, and <s>Pāpanāśanī</s>, and likewise the northern course (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>), are praised always for the worship of <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
yad anyakāle varṣeṇa
keśavāl labhyate phalam
sakṛd evārcite kṛṣṇe
tad etāsv api labhyate
body.translated_text: Whatever fruit is obtained from <s>Keśava</s> at another time in the course of a year, that is obtained on these days even when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is worshipped but once

body.text:
vijayātijayā caiva
jayantī pāpanāśanī
tathottarāyaṇaṃ caiva
yac chastaṃ keśavārcane
body.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Atijayā</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, and <s>Pāpanāśanī</s>, and likewise the northern course, which are praised in the worship of <s>Keśava</s>—

body.text:
tat sarvaṃ kathayehādya
tithimāhātmyam uttamam
yatra saṃpūjitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
sarvapāpaṃ vyapohati
body.translated_text: tell all that here today, the supreme glory of the lunar days, wherein <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, when worshipped, removes all sin

body.text:
ekādaśyāṃ site pakṣe
puṣyarkṣaṃ yatra sattama
tithau bhavati sā proktā
viṣṇunā pāpanāśanī
body.translated_text: When on the eleventh of the bright fortnight there is the asterism <s>Puṣya</s>, O best one, that lunar day is declared by <s>Viṣṇu</s> to be the <s>Pāpanāśanī</s> (the Sin-Destroying)

body.text:
tasyāṃ saṃpūjya govindaṃ
jagatām īśvareśvaram
saptajanmakṛtāt pāpān
mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: On that day, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, the Lord of the lords of the worlds, one is freed from the sin committed in seven births—there is no doubt here

body.text:
yaś copavāsaṃ kurute
tasyāṃ snāto dvijottama
sarvapāpavinirmukto
viṣṇuloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: And he who, bathed, keeps the fast on that day, O best of the twice-born, freed from all sins, is exalted in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
dānaṃ yad dīyate kiṃcit
samuddiśya janārdanam
homo vā kriyate tasyām
akṣayaṃ labhate phalam
body.translated_text: Whatever gift is given, dedicated to <s>Janārdana</s>, or whatever <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation) is performed on that day, obtains imperishable fruit

body.text:
ekā ṛg devapurato
japtā śraddhāvatā tathā
ṛgvedasya samastasya
japatā yacchate phalam
body.translated_text: A single <s>ṛk</s> verse muttered before the god by the faithful one yields the fruit that the muttering of the whole <s>Ṛgveda</s> grants

body.text:
sāmavedaphalaṃ sāma
yajurvedaphalaṃ yajuḥ
japtam ekaṃ muniśreṣṭha
dadāty atra na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: A <s>sāman</s> grants the fruit of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, a <s>yajus</s> the fruit of the <s>Yajurveda</s>—a single one muttered, O best of sages, grants this here; there is no doubt

body.text:
tārakā divi rājante
dyotamānā dvijottama
samabhyarcya tithāv asyāṃ
devadevaṃ janārdanam
body.translated_text: The stars shine radiantly in heaven, O best of the twice-born, for one who, having worshipped on this day the god of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>,—

body.text:
yataḥ pāpam aśeṣaṃ vai
nāśayaty atra keśavaḥ
puṣyarkṣaikādaśī brahmaṃs
tenoktā pāpanāśanī
body.translated_text: since here <s>Keśava</s> destroys sin without remainder—the <s>Puṣya-Ekādaśī</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, is therefore called the Sin-Destroying

body.text:
tathānyad api dharmajña
śrūyatāṃ gadato mama
padadvayaṃ jagaddhātur
devadevasya śārṅgiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: And another thing too, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, hear as I tell it—the two feet of the world's creator, the god of gods, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow

body.text:
saṃvatsaraḥ pādapīṭhaṃ
tatra nyastaṃ padadvayam
vāsudevena viprendra
bhūtānāṃ hitakāmyayā
body.translated_text: The year is the footstool; thereon the two feet have been set by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O chief of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, out of the wish for the welfare of beings

body.text:
vāmam asya padaṃ brahman
uttarāyaṇasaṃjñitam
devādyaiḥ sakalair vandyaṃ
dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇāyanam
body.translated_text: His left foot, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, is named the northern course (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>), to be revered by the gods and all others; the right is the southern course (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>)

body.text:
tasmin yaḥ prayataḥ samyag
devadevasya mānavaḥ
karoty ārādhanaṃ tasya
toṣam āyāti keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: The man who therein duly and with restraint performs the worship of the god of gods—<s>Keśava</s> comes to contentment with him

body.text:
katham ārādhanaṃ tasya
devadevasya śārṅgiṇaḥ
kriyate muniśārdūla
tan mamākhyātum arhasi
body.translated_text: How is the worship of that god of gods, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, performed, O tiger among sages? That you ought to tell me

body.text:
uttare tv ayane dālbhya
snāto niyatamānasaḥ
ghṛtakṣīrādinā devaṃ
snāpayed dharaṇīdharam
body.translated_text: In the northern course, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, bathed and of restrained mind, he should bathe the god, the upholder of the earth, with ghee, milk and the like

body.text:
cāruvastropahāraiś ca
puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ
samabhyarcya tataḥ samyag
brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ
padadvayavrataṃ samyag
gṛhṇīyād viṣṇutatparaḥ
body.translated_text: With fine garments and offerings, with flowers, incense and unguents, having duly worshipped him, and with libations to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the man devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> should duly undertake the vow of the two feet

body.text:
snāto nārāyaṇaṃ vakṣye
bhuñjan nārāyaṇaṃ tathā
bhuṅktvā nārāyaṇaṃ cāhaṃ
gacchan nārāyaṇaṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: "Bathed, I shall speak of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; eating, likewise <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; having eaten, I too <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; going, then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

body.text:
svapan vibuddhaḥ praṇaman
homaṃ kurvaṃs tathārcanam
nārāyaṇasyānudinaṃ
kariṣye nāmakīrtanam
body.translated_text: Sleeping, waking, bowing, performing the <s>homa</s> and the worship, I shall make day by day the proclamation of the name of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

body.text:
yāvad adyadināt prāptaṃ
kramaśo dakṣiṇāyanam
skhalite 'haṃ kṣute caiva
vedanārto 'thavā sadā
tāvan nārāyaṇaṃ vakṣye
sarvam evottarāyaṇam
body.translated_text: Until, from this day onward, the southern course is reached in due order, when stumbling or sneezing, or afflicted by pain at any time, until then I shall speak of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>—the whole northern course

body.text:
yāvaj jīvavadhaṃ kiṃcid
jñānato 'jñānato 'pi vā
kariṣye 'haṃ tathā caiva
kīrtayiṣyāmi taṃ prabhum
body.translated_text: Whatever harm to a living being I may do, knowingly or unknowingly, even so I shall proclaim that Lord

body.text:
yadā tadānṛtaṃ kiṃcid
atha vakṣyāmi durvacaḥ
ajñānād athavā jñānāt
kīrtayiṣyāmi taṃ prabhum
body.translated_text: Whenever I speak any untruth or harsh speech, whether unknowingly or knowingly, I shall proclaim that Lord

body.text:
ṣaṇmāsam eṣa me jāpo
nārāyaṇamayaḥ paraḥ
taṃ smaran maraṇe yāti
yāṃ gatiṃ sāstu me gatiḥ
body.translated_text: For six months this muttering of mine, supreme, consisting of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>—remembering him at death one goes to a certain destiny; let that be my destiny

body.text:
ṣaṇmāsābhyantare mṛtyur
yady akasmād bhaven mama
tan mayā vāsudevāya
svayam ātmā niveditaḥ
body.translated_text: If within these six months death should come upon me suddenly, then by me the self has been offered to <s>Vāsudeva</s> myself

body.text:
paramārthamayaṃ brahma
vāsudevamayaṃ param
yam ante saṃsmaran yāti
sa me viṣṇuḥ parā gatiḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s> consisting of the supreme truth, supreme, consisting of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, remembering whom at the end one goes—that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is my supreme destiny

body.text:
yadā prātas tadā sāyaṃ
madhyāhne vā mriye hy aham
ṣaṇmāsābhyantare nyāsaḥ
kṛto vratamayo mayā
body.translated_text: Whether at dawn, at dusk, or at midday I die, within these six months the renunciation consisting of the vow has been made by me

body.text:
tathā kuru jagannātha
sarvalokaparāyaṇa
nārāyaṇa yathā nānyaṃ
tvatto yāmi mṛte gatim
body.translated_text: So act, O Lord of the world, refuge of all worlds, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, that I may go to no other destiny than you when dead"

body.text:
evam uccārya ṣaṇmāsa-
pāraṇaṃ pravaraṃ vratam
tāvan niṣpādayed yāvat
saṃprāptaṃ dakṣiṇāyanam
body.translated_text: Having uttered thus, he should carry out the excellent six-month-breaking vow until the southern course is reached

body.text:
tataś ca prīṇanaṃ kuryād
yathāśaktyā jagadguroḥ
bhojayed brāhmaṇān samyag
dadyāt tebhyaś ca dakṣiṇām
body.translated_text: And then he should perform the gratification of the world's teacher according to his ability; he should duly feed <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and give them a fee

body.text:
evaṃ vratam idaṃ dālbhya
yaḥ pārayati mānavaḥ
nārī vā sarvapāpebhyaḥ
ṣaṇmāsād vipra mucyate
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, the man or woman who completes this vow is freed from all sins within six months, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>

body.text:
ṣaṇmāsābhyantare cāsya
maraṇaṃ yadi jāyate
prāpnoty anaśanasyoktaṃ
yat phalaṃ tad asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: And if within these six months death occurs for him, he attains, without doubt, the fruit declared for fasting-unto-death

body.text:
padadvayaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya
samyak tena tathārcitam
body.translated_text: And the two feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> have thus been duly worshipped by him

body.text: harer nāma japan bhaktyā
body.translated_text: muttering the name of <s>Hari</s> with devotion

body.text: sa purā na janeśvara
body.translated_text: He of old, O lord of men,

body.text:
bhagavān ujjagau viṣṇuḥ
purā gārgyāya pṛcchate
body.translated_text: The blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> formerly sang it forth to <s>Gārgya</s>, who asked:

body.text:
phālgunāmalapakṣasya
ekādaśyām upoṣitaḥ
naro vā yadi vā nārī
samabhyarcya jagadgurum
body.translated_text: On the eleventh of the pure fortnight of <s>Phālguna</s>, having fasted, a man or else a woman, having worshipped the world's teacher,

body.text:
harer nāma japed bhaktyā
sapta vārān nareśvara
uttiṣṭhan prasvapaṃś caiva
harim evānukīrtayet
body.translated_text: should mutter the name of <s>Hari</s> with devotion seven times, O lord of men; rising up and falling asleep, he should ever proclaim <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
tato 'nyadivase prāpte
dvādaśyāṃ prayato harim
snātvā samyak tam abhyarcya
dadyād viprāya dakṣiṇām
body.translated_text: Then, when the next day, the twelfth, has come, restrained, having bathed and duly worshipped <s>Hari</s>, he should give a fee to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>

body.text:
harim uddiśya caivāgnau
ghṛtahomakṛtakriyaḥ
praṇipatya jagannātham
iti vāṇīm udīrayet
body.translated_text: And dedicating it to <s>Hari</s>, having performed the rite of the ghee-oblation in the fire, prostrating to the Lord of the world, he should utter this speech:

body.text:
pātālasaṃsthā vasudhā
yaṃ prasādya manorathān
avāpa vāsudevo 'sau
pradadātu manorathān
body.translated_text: "That <s>Vāsudeva</s>, by propitiating whom the earth set in the netherworld attained her heart's desires, let him grant my heart's desires

body.text:
yam abhyarcyāditiḥ prāptā
sakalāṃś ca manorathān
putrāṃś caivepsitān devaḥ
pradadātu manorathān
body.translated_text: He whom <s>Aditi</s> worshipped and attained all her heart's desires, and the desired sons—let that god grant my heart's desires

body.text:
bhraṣṭarājyaś ca devendro
yam abhyarcya jagatpatim
manorathān avāpāgryān
sa dadātu manorathān
body.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, fallen from his kingdom, by worshipping whom, the Lord of the world, attained the foremost of his heart's desires—let him grant my heart's desires"

body.text:
evam abhyarcya pūjāṃ ca
niṣpādya haraye tataḥ
bhuñjīta prayataḥ samyag
haviṣyaṃ manujarṣabha
body.translated_text: Thus having worshipped and completed the worship for <s>Hari</s>, the man should then, restrained, duly eat the sacrificial food, O bull among men

body.text:
phālgunaṃ caitravaiśākhau
jyeṣṭhamāsaṃ ca pārthiva
caturbhiḥ pāraṇaṃ māsair
ebhir niṣpāditaṃ bhavet
body.translated_text: <s>Phālguna</s>, <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Vaiśākha</s>, and the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, O king—by these four months the breaking-of-the-fast would be completed

body.text:
raktapuṣpais tu caturo
māsān kurvīta cārcanam
dahec ca guggulaṃ prāśya
gośṛṅgakṣālanaṃ jalam
body.translated_text: For four months he should perform the worship with red flowers, and should burn <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium incense), consuming the water of the washing of a cow's horn

body.text:
haviṣyānnaṃ ca naivedyam
ātmanaś caiva bhojanam
tataś ca śrūyatām anyad
āṣāḍhādau tu yā kriyā
body.translated_text: and sacrificial food and the food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>) and one's own eating; and thereafter let another thing be heard—the rite which is performed in the months beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>

body.text:
jātīpuṣpāṇi dhūpaś ca
śastaḥ sarjaraso nṛpa
prāśya darbhodakaṃ cātra
śālyannaṃ ca nivedanam
body.translated_text: Jasmine flowers and incense are commended, and the resin of the <s>sarja</s> tree, O king; and here, having eaten <s>darbha</s>-water, the offering is of <s>śāli</s>-rice

body.text:
svayaṃ tad eva cāśnīyāc
śeṣaṃ pūrvavad ācaret
kārttikādiṣu māseṣu
gomūtraṃ kāyaśodhanam
body.translated_text: And one should oneself eat that very thing, and treat the remainder as before; in the months beginning with <s>Kārttika</s>, cow's urine is the cleanser of the body

body.text:
sugandhaṃ cecchayā dhūpaṃ
pūjābhṛṅgārakeṇa ca
kāsāraṃ cātra naivedyam
aśnīyāt tac ca vai svayam
body.translated_text: and fragrant incense at will, and with the worship-vessel; and here the offering is the <s>kāsāra</s> (a milk-dish), and that one should eat oneself

body.text:
pratimāsaṃ ca viprāya
dātavyā dakṣiṇā tathā
prīṇanaṃ cecchayā viṣṇoḥ
pāraṇe pāraṇe gate
body.translated_text: And every month a fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) is likewise to be given to a <s>vipra</s>, and the gladdening of <s>Viṣṇu</s> at will, at each breaking-of-the-fast as it comes

body.text:
yathāśakti yathāprīti
vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet
sadbhāvenaiva govindaḥ
pūjitaḥ prīyate yataḥ
body.translated_text: According to one's ability and according to one's affection, one should avoid stinginess with wealth; for <s>Govinda</s>, worshipped with true feeling alone, is pleased

body.text:
pāraṇānte yathāśaktyā
snāpitaḥ pūjito hariḥ
prīṇitaś cepsitān kāmān
dadāty avyāhatān nṛpa
body.translated_text: At the end of the breaking-of-the-fast, <s>Hari</s>, bathed according to ability, worshipped and gladdened, grants the desired wishes unhindered, O king

body.text:
eṣā dhanyā pāpaharā
dvādaśī phalam icchatām
yathābhilaṣitān kāmān
dadāti manujeśvara
body.translated_text: This blessed, sin-removing twelfth (<s>dvādaśī</s>) grants the desired wishes to those who wish for fruit, O lord of men

body.text:
pūrayaty akhilān bhaktyā
yataś caiṣā manorathān
manorathadvādaśīyaṃ
tato lokeṣu viśrutā
body.translated_text: And since it fulfills all the heart's longings through devotion, this is therefore renowned among the worlds as the <s>Manoratha-dvādaśī</s> (the Heart's-Wish Twelfth)

body.text:
upoṣyaitāṃ tribhuvanaṃ
prāptam indreṇa vai purā
adityā cepsitāḥ putrā
dhanaṃ cośanasā nṛpa
body.translated_text: By fasting on it, the three worlds were obtained by <s>Indra</s> of old, and the desired sons by <s>Aditi</s>, and wealth by <s>Uśanas</s>, O king,

body.text:
dhaumyena cāpy adhyayanam
anyaiś cābhimataṃ phalam
rājarṣibhis tathā vipraiḥ
strībhiḥ śūdraiś ca bhūpate
body.translated_text: and learning by <s>Dhaumya</s>, and the desired fruit by others, by royal seers and by <s>vipras</s>, by women and by <s>śūdras</s>, O lord of the earth

body.text:
yaṃ yaṃ kāmam abhidhyāyed
vratam etad upoṣitaḥ
taṃ tam āpnoty asaṃdigdhaṃ
viṣṇor ārādhanodyataḥ
body.translated_text: Whatever desire one meditates upon while keeping this vow fasting, that one obtains without doubt, being intent on the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
aputro labhate putram
adhano labhate dhanam
rogābhibhūtaś cārogyaṃ
kanyā prāpnoti satpatim
body.translated_text: The sonless obtains a son, the poor obtains wealth, one overcome by disease obtains health, a maiden obtains a good husband,

body.text:
samāgamaṃ pravasitair
upoṣyaitām avāpnute
sarvān kāmān avāpnoti
mṛtaḥ svarge ca modate
body.translated_text: and by fasting on it one obtains reunion with those who have gone abroad; one obtains all wishes, and when dead rejoices in heaven

body.text:
nāputro nādhano neṣṭa-
viyogī na ca nirguṇaḥ
upoṣyaitad vrataṃ martyaḥ
strī jano vāpi jāyate
body.translated_text: By fasting on this vow a mortal—or even a woman—is not born sonless, nor poor, nor separated from what is dear, nor without good qualities

body.text:
ya eva vratasaṃcīrṇo
viṣṇuloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: He who has fully completed the vow is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
svargaloke sahasrāṇi
varṣāṇāṃ manujādhipa
bhogān abhimatān bhuktvā
svargaloke 'bhikāṅkṣitān
body.translated_text: In the world of heaven, for thousands of years, O lord of men, having enjoyed the desired enjoyments coveted in the heavenly world,

body.text:
iha puṇyavatāṃ nṝṇāṃ
dhanināṃ sādhuśīlinām
gṛheṣu jāyate rājan
sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ
body.translated_text: here, in the houses of meritorious men who are wealthy and of good conduct, he is born, O king, free from all diseases

body.text:
aśokapūrṇimāṃ cānyāṃ
śṛṇuśva vadato mama
yām upoṣya naraḥ śokaṃ
nāpnoti strī tathāpi vā
body.translated_text: Hear from me as I tell of another, the <s>Aśoka-pūrṇimā</s> (the Sorrowless Full-Moon), by fasting on which a man—or likewise a woman—does not meet with sorrow

body.text:
phālgunāmalapakṣasya
pūrṇimāsyāṃ nareśvara
mṛjjalena naraḥ snātvā
dattvā śirasi vai mṛdam
body.translated_text: On the full-moon day of the bright fortnight of <s>Phālguna</s>, O lord of men, a man, having bathed with earth and water, and having placed earth upon his head,

body.text:
mṛtprāśanaṃ tathā kṛtvā
kṛtvā ca sthaṇḍilaṃ mṛdā
puṣpaiḥ patrais tathābhyarcya
bhūdharaṃ nānyamānasaḥ
dharaṇīṃ ca tathā devīm
aśokety abhidhīyate
body.translated_text: and likewise having eaten earth, and having made an altar of earth, having worshipped with flowers and leaves the Earth-bearer (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) with mind fixed on no other, and likewise the goddess Earth (<s>Dharaṇī</s>)—she is called <s>Aśokā</s> (the Sorrowless)

body.text:
yathā viśokāṃ dharaṇīṃ
kṛtavāṃs tvaṃ janārdanaḥ
tathā māṃ sarvapāpebhyo
mocayāśeṣadhāriṇi
body.translated_text: 'As you, <s>Janārdana</s>, made the Earth (<s>Dharaṇī</s>) free from sorrow, so free me from all sins, O bearer of all things'

body.text:
yathā samastabhūtānāṃ
dhāraṇaṃ tvayy avasthitam
tathā viśokaṃ kuru māṃ
sakalecchāvibhūtibhiḥ
body.translated_text: 'As the bearing of all beings rests in you, so make me free from sorrow with all desired powers'

body.text:
dhyātamātre yathā viṣṇau
svāsthyaṃ yātāsi medini
tathā manaḥ svasthatāṃ me
kuru tvaṃ bhūtadhāriṇi
body.translated_text: 'As the moment <s>Viṣṇu</s> was meditated upon you came to well-being, O Earth, so make my mind come to well-being, O bearer of beings'

body.text:
evaṃ stutvā tathābhyarcya
candrāyārghyaṃ nivedya ca
upoṣitavyaṃ naktaṃ vā
bhoktavyaṃ tailavarjitam
body.translated_text: Having thus praised and likewise worshipped, and having offered an <s>arghya</s> to the moon, one should fast, or eat at night food free of oil

body.text:
anenaiva prakāreṇa
catvāraḥ phālgunādayaḥ
upoṣyā nṛpate māsāḥ
prathamaṃ tat tu pāraṇam
body.translated_text: By this very procedure four months beginning with <s>Phālguna</s> are to be fasted, O king; that is the first breaking-of-the-fast

body.text:
āṣāḍhādiṣu māseṣu
tadvat snānaṃ mṛdambunā
tad eva prāśanaṃ pūjā
tathaivendos tathārhaṇam
body.translated_text: In the months beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, likewise the bathing with earth and water, that same eating, the worship, and likewise the honoring of the moon

body.text:
caturṣv anyeṣu caivoktaṃ
tathā vai kārttikādiṣu
pāraṇaṃ tritayaṃ caiva
cāturmāsikam ucyate
body.translated_text: And it is declared in the other four likewise, namely those beginning with <s>Kārttika</s>; and the triple breaking-of-the-fast is called the <s>Cāturmāsika</s> (four-monthly)

body.text:
prathamaṃ dharaṇī nāma
stutyai māsacatuṣṭayam
dvitīye medinī vācyā
tṛtīye ca vasuṃdharā
body.translated_text: In the first set of four months she is to be praised by the name <s>Dharaṇī</s>, in the second she is to be called <s>Medinī</s>, and in the third <s>Vasundharā</s>

body.text:
pāraṇe pāraṇe vastra-
pūjayā pūjayen nṛpa
dharaṇīṃ devadevaṃ ca
ghṛtasnānena keśavam
body.translated_text: At each breaking-of-the-fast one should worship, O king, the Earth and the God of gods—<s>Keśava</s>—with worship of cloth and with bathing in ghee

body.text:
vastrābhāve tu sūtreṇa
pūjayed dharaṇīṃ tathā
ghṛtābhāve tathā kṣīraṃ
śastaṃ vā salilaṃ hareḥ
body.translated_text: But in the absence of cloth one should worship the Earth with thread likewise; and in the absence of ghee, milk is commended, or water, for <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
pātālamūlagatayā
cīrṇam etan mahāvratam
dharaṇyā keśavaprītyai
tataḥ prāptā samunnatiḥ
body.translated_text: This great vow was practiced by the Earth, who had gone to the foundation of the nether world, for the affection of <s>Keśava</s>; thereby was her elevation attained

body.text:
devena coktā dharaṇī
varāhavapuṣā tadā
upavāsaprasannena
samuddhṛtya rasātalāt
body.translated_text: And the Earth was addressed then by the god in the form of the boar (<s>Varāha</s>), pleased by her fast, having raised her up from the nether world (<s>Rasātala</s>):

body.text:
vratenānena kalyāṇi
praṇato yaḥ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: 'O auspicious one, he who, taking refuge in this vow, shall make obeisance,'

body.text:
tasya prasādam apy aham
karomi tava medini
tathaiva kurute pūjāṃ
bhaktyā mama śubho janaḥ
tathaiva tava kalyāṇi
praṇato yaḥ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: 'to him also I grant favor, O Earth, on your account; and likewise the auspicious man who performs worship with devotion to me, and likewise, O auspicious one, he who shall make obeisance to you'—

body.text:
vratam etad upāśritya
pāraṇaṃ ca yathāvidhi
body.translated_text: having taken refuge in this vow and the breaking-of-the-fast according to rule,

body.text:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ
sapta janmāntarāṇy asau
viśokaḥ sarvakalyāṇa-
bhājano matimāñ janaḥ
body.translated_text: freed from all sins for seven births, that wise man becomes sorrowless, a vessel of all auspiciousness,

body.text:
sarvatra pūjyaḥ satataṃ
sarveṣām aparājitaḥ
yathāham evaṃ vasudhe
bhavitā nirvṛteḥ padam
body.translated_text: everywhere honored always, unconquered by all; 'as I, O Earth, am the abode of bliss,'

body.text:
tathā tvam api kalyāṇi
bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: 'so you too, O auspicious one, shall become—there is no doubt'

body.text:
evam etan mahāpuṇyaṃ
sarvapāpopaśāntidam
viśokākhyaṃ vrataṃ dhanyaṃ
tat kuruṣva mahīpate
body.translated_text: Thus this greatly meritorious, blessed vow called <s>Viśokā</s> (the Sorrowless), the giver of the calming of all sins—perform that, O lord of the earth

body.text:
strīṇāṃ dharmaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha
upavāsaṃ bhavan mama
kathayeha yathātattvam
upavāsavidhiś ca yaḥ
body.translated_text: O best of the twice-born, tell here truly the <s>dharma</s> of women, the fast befitting me, and what the rule of fasting is

body.text:
kaumārake gṛhasthāyā
vidhavāyāś ca sattama
dharmaṃ prabrūhy aśeṣeṇa
bhagavan prītikārakam
body.translated_text: Declare fully, O blessed one, the affection-bestowing <s>dharma</s> of the maiden, of the married woman, and of the widow, O most excellent one

body.text:
śrūyatām akhilaṃ brahman
yady etad anupṛcchasi
upakārāya ca strīṇāṃ
triṣu lokeṣv anuttamam
body.translated_text: Let the whole be heard, O <s>Brahman</s>, if you ask this—the unsurpassed thing in the three worlds, for the benefit of women

body.text:
praśnam etat purā devī
śailarājasutā patim
papraccha śaṅkaraṃ brahman
kailāsaśikhare sthitam
body.translated_text: This question, O <s>Brahman</s>, the goddess, daughter of the mountain-king, formerly asked her husband <s>Śaṅkara</s>, seated on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>:

body.text:
kumārikābhir deveśa
gṛhasthābhiś ca keśavaḥ
vidhavābhis tathā strībhiḥ
katham ārādhyate vada
body.translated_text: 'O lord of gods, how is <s>Keśava</s> worshipped by maidens, by married women, and by widowed women? Tell me'

body.text:
sādhu sādhvi tvayā pṛṣṭam
etan nārāyaṇāśritam
upavāsādi yat tattvaṃ
śrūyatām asya yo vidhiḥ
body.translated_text: Well asked, O virtuous one, this thing relating to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>—the fast and the rest; let its truth be heard, and what its rule is

body.text:
yogyaṃ patiṃ samāsādya
nārī dharmam avāpnute
duḥśīle 'pi hi kāmārte
nārī prāpnoti bhartari
body.translated_text: Having obtained a suitable husband, a woman attains <s>dharma</s>; even in a husband of bad conduct and afflicted by lust, a woman finds it

body.text:
anārādhya jagannāthaṃ
sarvalokeśvaraṃ harim
katham āpnoti vai nārī
patiṃ śīlaguṇānvitam
body.translated_text: Without worshipping the Lord of the world, the Lord of all worlds, <s>Hari</s>, how indeed does a woman obtain a husband endowed with good character and virtues?

body.text:
sukalatrapradaṃ tasmād
vratam acyutatuṣṭidam
kartavyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tasya
śrūyatāṃ varavarṇini
body.translated_text: Therefore the vow that gives a good wife and gives satisfaction to <s>Acyuta</s> is to be performed; let its description be heard, O you of fair complexion,

body.text:
yac cīrtvā sarvanārīṇāṃ
śreṣṭham āpnoty asaṃśayam
aihikaṃ ca sukhaṃ prāpya
svarge bhuṅkte sukhāny api
body.translated_text: by performing which one obtains, without doubt, the best of all women, and having attained happiness in this world, enjoys happiness in heaven too

body.text:
anujñāṃ prāpya pitṛto
mātṛtaś ca kumārikā
pūjayec ca jagannāthaṃ
bhaktyā pāpaharaṃ harim
body.translated_text: Having obtained permission from her father and from her mother, the maiden should worship the Lord of the world, the sin-removing <s>Hari</s>, with devotion

body.text:
triṣūttareṣu svṛkṣeṣu
patikāmā kumārikā
mādhavākhyaṃ tu vai nāma
japen nityam atandritā
body.translated_text: In the three later mansions, when the asterism is favorable, a maiden desiring a husband should daily, untiringly, recite the name called <s>Mādhava</s>

body.text:
priyaṅguṇā raktapuṣpair
bandhūkakusumais tathā
samabhyarcya tato dadyād
raktam evānulepanam
body.translated_text: Having worshipped with <s>priyaṅgu</s> and red flowers and likewise with <s>bandhūka</s> blossoms, she should then offer a red unguent

body.text:
sarvauṣadhyā svayaṃ snātvā
samabhyarcya jagatpatim
namo 'stu mādhavāyeti
homayen madhusarpiṣī
body.translated_text: Having herself bathed with all healing herbs and worshipped the Lord of the world, she should make oblation of honey and ghee, saying 'Homage be to <s>Mādhava</s>'

body.text:
sa devam uttarāyoge
samabhyarcya janārdanam
śobhanaṃ patim āpnoti
pretya svargaṃ ca gacchati
body.translated_text: Having worshipped the god <s>Janārdana</s> during the northward course of the sun, she obtains a fine husband, and when dead goes to heaven

body.text:
atibālye ca yat kiṃcit
tayā pāpam anuṣṭhitam
tasmāc ca mucyate devi
sukhinī caiva jāyate
body.translated_text: And whatever sin was committed by her in earliest childhood, from that she is freed, O goddess, and she is born a happy woman
