body.text:
abdenaikena tanvaṅgi
dhūtapāpā yad icchati
tad eva prāpnuyād bhadre
nārāyaṇaparāyaṇā
body.translated_text: In a single year, O slender-limbed one, with sins shaken off, whatever she desires, that very thing she may obtain, O blessed one, being devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

body.text:
ṣaṇmāsaṃ prīṇanaṃ kāryaṃ
bhaktyā śaktyā ca vai hareḥ
pāraṇānte mahābhage
tathā brāhmaṇatarpaṇam
body.translated_text: For six months the gladdening of <s>Hari</s> is to be done with devotion and according to ability; and at the end of the breaking-of-the-fast, O greatly fortunate one, likewise the gratifying of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>

body.text:
gārhasthye 'vasthitā nārī
bhaktyā saṃpūjayet patim
sa eva devatā tasyāḥ
pūjyaḥ pūjyataraś ca saḥ
body.translated_text: A woman established in the householder state should worship her husband with devotion; he alone is her deity, to be worshipped, and he the more worthy of worship

body.text:
tasmiṃs tuṣṭe paro dharmas
tasyaiva paricaryayā
toṣam āyāti sarvātmā
paramātmā janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: When he is pleased, that is the highest <s>dharma</s>; by his service alone the soul of all, the Supreme Self <s>Janārdana</s>, comes to satisfaction

body.text:
naiva tasyāḥ pṛthag yajño
na śrāddhaṃ nāpy upoṣitam
bhartṛśuśrūṣaṇenaiva
prāpnoti strī yathepsitam
body.translated_text: For her there is no separate sacrifice, no <s>śrāddha</s>, nor even fasting; by the service of her husband alone a woman obtains what she desires

body.text:
tenaiva sāpy anujñātā
tasya śuśrūṣaṇād anu
toṣayej jagatām īśam
anantam aparājitam
body.translated_text: Permitted by him, after his service, she may gratify the Lord of the worlds, the infinite, unconquered one,

body.text:
vratair nānāvidhair devi
aihikāmuṣmikāptaye
viṣṇuvratādibhir divyais
tathā dānair mano'nugaiḥ
body.translated_text: by various vows, O goddess, for the attainment of this world and the next, by divine <s>Viṣṇu</s>-vows and the rest, and likewise by gifts pleasing to the mind,

body.text:
ghṛtakṣīrābhiṣekaiś ca
brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ
manojñair vividhair dhūpaiḥ
puṣpavastrānulepanaiḥ
body.translated_text: by bathings with ghee and milk, and by gratifying of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, by pleasing various incenses, by flowers, cloths, and unguents,

body.text:
gītavādyais tathā hṛdyair
upavāsaiś ca bhāmini
evam ārādhya govindam
anujñātā yathāvidhi
patinā sakalān kāmān
avāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: by songs and music delightful to the heart, and by fasts, O lovely one; thus having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, permitted according to rule by her husband, she attains all wishes—there is no doubt

body.text:
patinā tv ananujñātā
kiṃcit puṇyaṃ karoti yā
viphalaṃ tad aśeṣaṃ vai
tasyāḥ śailavarātmaje
body.translated_text: But she who, not permitted by her husband, performs some meritorious act—all that is fruitless for her, O daughter of the best of mountains,

body.text:
na ca prasādaṃ kurute
bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ
nānujñātā tu yā nārī
patinārcati keśavam
body.translated_text: and the Blessed <s>Madhusūdana</s> does not bestow favor on the woman who, unpermitted, worships <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
yā tu bhartṛparā nārī
nārāyaṇam atandritā
bhaktyā saṃpūjayed devaṃ
toṣam āyāti keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: But the woman who, devoted to her husband, worships the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> untiringly with devotion—<s>Keśava</s> comes to satisfaction

body.text:
yā tu bhartrā parityaktā
tathā yā mṛtabhartṛkā
pāṣaṇḍānugato vāpi
yasyā bhartā maheśvara
body.translated_text: But she who is abandoned by her husband, and she whose husband is dead, or she whose husband has gone after heretics, O <s>Maheśvara</s>,

body.text:
prāyo dadāti nānujñāṃ
viṣṇor ārādhane tadā
katham ārādhanaṃ kāryaṃ
viṣṇos tad vada śaṃkara
body.translated_text: —if her husband generally gives no permission then in the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—how should the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> be performed? Tell that, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>

body.text:
yā tu bhartrā parityaktā
sā saṃpūjya nijaṃ patim
manasā tanmanaskā ca
tasyaiva hitakāriṇī
body.translated_text: She who is abandoned by her husband should worship her own husband in mind, with her mind on him, and be one who acts for his welfare,

body.text:
na nindākaraṇī tasya
śreyo'bhidhyāyinī tathā
tasyaiva sarvakāleṣu
sarvakalyāṇam icchati
body.translated_text: not one who reviles him, but rather one who meditates on his good, who in all times desires every auspiciousness for him alone

body.text:
ārādhayej jagannāthaṃ
sarvadhātāram acyutam
kṛtopavāsā puṣpādi
nivedya sakalaṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: She should worship the Lord of the world, the supporter of all, <s>Acyuta</s>; having fasted, having offered flowers and all the rest,

body.text:
bhartur manorathāvāptiṃ
prārthayet prathamaṃ varam
svayaṃ yathābhilaṣitaṃ
prārthayet taṃ varaṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: she should first request as a boon the attainment of her husband's heart's wishes; then she should request for herself that boon as she desires

body.text:
evaṃ bhartṛparityaktā
yoṣid ārādhanaṃ hareḥ
kurvāṇā sakalān kāmān
avāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus a woman abandoned by her husband, performing the worship of <s>Hari</s>, attains all wishes—there is no doubt

body.text:
bhartā karoti yac casyāḥ
kiṃcit puṇyam aharniśam
tasya puṇyasya saṃpūrṇam
ardhaṃ prāpnoti sā śubhe
body.translated_text: Whatever bit of merit her husband does day and night, of that merit she obtains a full half, O auspicious one

body.text:
yat tu sā kurute puṇyaṃ
vinā doṣeṇa yojjhitā
tat tasyāḥ sakalaṃ devi
tasyārdhaṃ na labhet patiḥ
body.translated_text: But the merit which she, abandoned without fault, performs—all of that is hers, O goddess; her husband does not obtain a half of it

body.text:
bhartary evaṃ pravasite
tyaktā ca patinā śubhe
kurvītārādhanaṃ nārī
upavāsādinā hareḥ
body.translated_text: Thus when her husband has gone abroad, and when abandoned by her husband, O auspicious one, a woman should perform the worship of <s>Hari</s> by fasting and the rest

body.text:
etat tavoktaṃ yat pṛṣṭaṃ
tvayāhaṃ girinandini
vidhavānām ato dharmaṃ
śrūyatāṃ viṣṇutuṣṭidam
body.translated_text: This which you asked I have told you, O daughter of the mountain; now let the <s>dharma</s> of widows be heard, the giver of satisfaction to <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
mṛte bhartari sādhvī strī
brahmacaryavratoditā
snātā pratidinaṃ dadyāt
svabhartṛsalilāñjalim
body.translated_text: When her husband is dead, a virtuous woman, undertaking the vow of chastity (<s>brahmacarya</s>), having bathed, should daily offer a handful of water for her own husband

body.text:
kuryād yānudinaṃ bhaktyā
devānām api pūjanam
atithes tarpaṇaṃ tadvad
agnihotram amantrakam
body.translated_text: She should perform daily with devotion the worship of the gods too, and likewise the gratifying of guests, the fire-offering (<s>agnihotra</s>) without mantras

body.text:
pūrtadharmāśritaṃ cānyat
kuryān nityam atandritā
nityakarma ṛte cāsyā
neṣṭaṃ karma vidhīyate
body.translated_text: And she should perform untiringly, daily, other acts pertaining to the <s>dharma</s> of pious works (<s>pūrta</s>); apart from the obligatory rites no optional act is enjoined for her

body.text:
viṣṇor ārādhanaṃ caiva
kuryān nityam upoṣitā
dānādi vipramukhyebhyo
dadyāt puṇyavivṛddhaye
upavāsāṃś ca vividhān
kuryāc chāstroditān śubhe
body.translated_text: And she should perform daily, fasting, the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; she should give gifts and the rest to the chief <s>vipras</s> for the increase of merit, and should perform the various fasts declared in the scriptures, O auspicious one

body.text:
lokāntarasthaṃ bhartāram
ātmānaṃ ca varānane
tārayaty ubhayaṃ nārī
yetthaṃ dharmaparāyaṇā
body.translated_text: A woman thus devoted to <s>dharma</s> rescues both her husband, who is in the other world, and herself, O fair-faced one

body.text:
putraiśvaryasthitā nārī
upavāsādinā harim
yā toṣayati siddhiṃ sā
putrebhyo 'pi prayacchati
body.translated_text: A woman who, established in the lordship of her sons, gratifies <s>Hari</s> by fasting and the rest, grants attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) to her sons too

body.text:
śubhāṃl lokāṃs tathā bhartur
ātmanaś ca yathepsitān
sakalaṃ pūrayaty astaṃ
pāpaṃ nayati cākhilam
body.translated_text: and fulfills entirely the auspicious worlds desired for her husband and for herself, and leads away all sin

body.text:
ātmanaś caiva bhartuś ca
nārī paramikāṃ gatim
dadāty ārādhya govindaṃ
saputrā vidhavā ca yā
body.translated_text: A woman who, having sons, though a widow, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, gives the supreme goal both to herself and to her husband

body.text:
tasmād ebhir vidhānais tu
sarvakālaṃ tu yoṣitaḥ
keśavārādhanaṃ kāryaṃ
lokadvayaphalapradam
body.translated_text: Therefore, by these ordinances, at all times the worship of <s>Keśava</s> is to be performed by women, the giver of fruit in both worlds

body.text:
ye narā mṛtapatnikās
tair apy etad aśeṣataḥ
pūrtadharmāśritaṃ kāryaṃ
nityakarma ca kevalam
body.translated_text: Those men whose wives are dead—by them too this whole duty grounded in works of public benefit (pūrta-dharma) is to be done, and the obligatory daily rite alone.

body.text:
putraiśvaryasthitaiḥ samyag
brahmacaryaguṇānvitaiḥ
viṣṇor ārādhanaṃ kāryaṃ
tīrthasthair athavā gṛhe
body.translated_text: By those established in the lordship of sons, duly endowed with the qualities of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be done, whether dwelling at a sacred ford or at home.

body.text:
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ
strī śūdraś ca varānane
anārādhya hṛṣīkeśaṃ
nāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, woman, and <s>śūdra</s>, O fair-faced one, without worshipping <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, do not attain the supreme destination.

body.text:
aiśvaryaṃ saṃtatiṃ śreṣṭhām
ārogyaṃ dravyasaṃpadam
dadāti bhagavān viṣṇur
gatim agryāṃ sutoṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: Lordship, excellent progeny, health, and abundance of wealth the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> grants, and the foremost destination, when well gladdened.

body.text:
evaṃ śailasutā proktā
svayaṃ devena śaṃbhunā
pṛṣṭena samyak kathitaṃ
bhavato 'pi mahāmune
body.translated_text: Thus it was spoken by the daughter of the mountain, told fully by the god <s>Śambhu</s> himself when asked, and now told to you also, O great sage.

body.text:
sarvavarṇais tathā strībhir
anyair api janair hariḥ
ārādhanīyo nātuṣṭe
viṣṇau saṃprāpyate gatiḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> is to be worshipped by all the classes and by women and by other people as well; when <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not gladdened, the destination is not attained.

body.text:
na durgatiṃ rauravādīn
narakāṃś ca na gacchati
yam ārādhyeśvaraṃ vandyaṃ
kas taṃ viṣṇuṃ na pūjayet
body.translated_text: He whom, having worshipped, the Lord worthy of reverence, one does not go to evil destinations, to the <s>Raurava</s> and other hells—who would not worship that <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

body.text:
tasmād amuṣmikān kleśān
narake yāś ca yātanāḥ
sadaivodvijatā dālbhya
samārādhyo janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, by one ever dreading the afflictions of the other world and the torments that are in hell, <s>Janārdana</s> is to be well worshipped.

body.text:
bhagavan yātanā ghorāḥ
śrūyante narakeṣu yāḥ
tāsāṃ svarūpam atyugraṃ
yathāvad vaktum arhasi
body.translated_text: O Blessed One, the dreadful torments that are heard of in the hells—their exceedingly fierce nature you ought to tell duly.

body.text:
śṛṇu dālbhyātighorāṇāṃ
yātanānāṃ mayoditam
svarūpaṃ nārakair yat tu
narakeṣv anubhūyate
body.translated_text: Hear, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, the nature of the exceedingly terrible torments declared by me, which is experienced by the hell-dwellers in the hells.

body.text:
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi
rauravo narako dvija
aṅgārapūrṇamadhyo 'sau
jvālāmālāpariṣkṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: The hell <s>Raurava</s>, O twice-born, is thousands of <s>yojanas</s> in extent; its midst is full of embers, adorned with garlands of flame.

body.text:
tanmadhye patito yāti
yojanāni sahasraśaḥ
satyahānyānṛtī yāti
tatra pāparatir naraḥ
body.translated_text: Fallen into its midst, one goes for thousands of <s>yojanas</s>; there goes the man devoted to sin who destroys truth and speaks falsehood.

body.text:
rauravād dviguṇaś caiva
mahārauvarasaṃjñitaḥ
taptatāmrapuṭāṅgāra-
jvalatpāvakasaṃvṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: And twice the size of <s>Raurava</s> is the one named <s>Mahāraurava</s>, enclosed by blazing fire of heated copper-plates and embers.

body.text:
paropatāpinas tatra
patanti narake narāḥ
nāścaryaṃ dvijaśārdūla
varṣalakṣayutāni ca
body.translated_text: There into that hell fall men who torment others—no wonder, O tiger among the twice-born—for myriads of hundreds of thousands of years.

body.text:
kālasūtreṇa cchidyante
cakrārūḍhāś ca mānavāḥ
kālāṅgulisthena sadā
āpādatalamastakāt
body.translated_text: Men, mounted on a wheel by the noose of <s>Kāla</s> (Death), ever held by the finger of <s>Kāla</s>, are cut from the soles of the feet to the head.

body.text:
kālasūtra iti khyāto
ghoraḥ sa narakottamaḥ
tatrāpi vañcakā yānti
ye caivotkocajīvinaḥ
body.translated_text: That foremost terrible hell is called <s>Kālasūtra</s>; there too go deceivers and those who live by taking bribes.

body.text:
taptakumbhas tathaivānyo
narako bhṛśadāruṇaḥ
tailakumbheṣu pacyante
tatrāpy agnibhṛteṣu te
body.translated_text: And likewise another, the exceedingly cruel hell <s>Taptakumbha</s>; there too they are cooked in cauldrons of oil filled with fire,

body.text:
devavedadvijātīnāṃ
ye nindāṃ kurvate sadā
saṃśṛṇvanti ca ye mūḍhā
ye ca matsariṇo 'dhamāḥ
body.translated_text: those who always make slander of the gods, the <s>Vedas</s>, and the twice-born, and those fools who listen to it, and those lowest, envious ones.

body.text:
karambhavālukākumbha-
saṃjñaṃ ca narakaṃ śṛṇu
paradāraratā ye tu
patanti narake 'dhamāḥ
body.translated_text: Hear of the hell named <s>Karambha-vālukā-kumbha</s>; those lowest ones devoted to the wives of others fall into that hell.

body.text:
hṛtaṃ yaiś ca jalaṃ te 'pi
tasmin yānti narādhamāḥ
gonipāneṣu vighnāni
mūḍhā ye cāpi kurvate
karambhavālukākumbha-
narake te patanti vai
body.translated_text: And those lowest of men by whom water has been stolen go to it; and those fools who make obstacles to the watering-places of cows—they indeed fall into the hell <s>Karambha-vālukā-kumbha</s>.

body.text:
andhe tamasi duṣpāre
śītārtiparikampitāḥ
bhrāmyante mānavā gātraiḥ
samastaiḥ sphuṭitāsthibhiḥ
body.translated_text: In blind darkness impassable, trembling with the affliction of cold, men are made to wander with all their limbs, their bones split open.

body.text:
govadhaḥ strīvadhaḥ pāpaiḥ
kṛtaṃ yaiś ca gavānṛtam
te tatrātimahābhīme
patanti narake narāḥ
body.translated_text: Cow-slaughter, woman-slaughter—and those sinners by whom false witness was given concerning a cow—those men fall there into the exceedingly terrible hell.

body.text:
utpāṭyate tathā jihvā
saṃdaṃśair bhṛśadāruṇaiḥ
ākriśakānāṃ duṣṭānāṃ
sadaivābaddhabhāṣiṇām
body.translated_text: Likewise the tongue is torn out with exceedingly cruel pincers from the abusers, the wicked, who always speak unbridled words.

body.text:
karapatraiś ca pāṭyante
yamasya puruṣais tathā
paradāraparadravya-
hiṃsakāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ
body.translated_text: And by the men of <s>Yama</s> they are sawn with handsaws—the lowest of men, the harmers of others' wives and others' property.

body.text:
āyasīṃ ca śilāṃ taptām
aśeṣāṅgais tathā narāḥ
paradāraratā evaṃ
samāliṅganti pāpinaḥ
body.translated_text: And men devoted to the wives of others, those sinners, thus embrace with all their limbs an iron slab, heated red.

body.text:
sarvāṅgair vikṛtair raktam
udgiranto 'tipīḍitāḥ
yantreṣv anyeṣu pīḍyante
jantupīḍākarā narāḥ
body.translated_text: Greatly tormented, vomiting blood with all their disfigured limbs, the men who cause pain to creatures are crushed in other engines.

body.text:
vṛkaiḥ saṃbhakṣyate pṛṣṭhaṃ
narāṇāṃ pāpakāriṇām
janasya pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ yair
bhakṣitaṃ pāpakāribhiḥ
body.translated_text: The back of sinful men is devoured by wolves—of those evildoers by whom the flesh of another's back was eaten.

body.text:
asipatravanair ghoraiś
chidyante pāpakarmiṇaḥ
sadbhāvapravaṇā yais tu
bhagnā viśrambhino janāḥ
body.translated_text: The doers of sinful deeds are cut by terrible forests of sword-leaves—those by whom trusting people, inclined to good faith, were betrayed.

body.text:
ayomukhaiḥ khagair bhagnāḥ
khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ tathāparaiḥ
vrajanti pāpakarmāṇaḥ
śvaśṛgālais tathāparaiḥ
body.translated_text: The doers of sinful deeds are broken by birds with iron beaks, and by others piece by piece, and likewise by dogs and jackals.

body.text:
sūṣāyām api dhāsyante
jvaladagnicayāvṛtāḥ
pāṣāṇapeṣyaṃ piṣyante
tathānye pāpakarmiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: They are cast also into a crucible, enveloped in heaps of blazing fire; and other doers of sinful deeds are ground as stone-grist.

body.text:
devatātithibhṛtyāṇām
adattvā bhuñjate tu ye
mṛṣāgatās tathāivaikyaṃ
trapuṣā sīsakena ca
prayānti puruṣās tailaiḥ
kvāthyante 'nye punaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: Those who eat without giving to gods, guests, and dependents, and likewise those who, falsely, have become one with theft—men go by way of tin and lead, while others are boiled again and again in oils.

body.text:
varṇadharmaparityāge
naikyaṃ ye puruṣā gatāḥ
te 'pi pāpasamācārā
varṇasaṃkarakāriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who became one with the abandonment of the <s>varṇa</s>-duties—they too, of sinful conduct, are causers of the confusion of classes.

body.text:
svarūpaṃ nārakasyāgneḥ
śṛṇuṣva kathayāmi te
muktas tato 'nyavahnishtaḥ
śete saṃprāpya nirvṛtim
body.translated_text: Hear the nature of the hell-fire; I shall tell you of it. Released from it, scorched by another fire, one lies down, having attained relief.

body.text:
śastradhārās tathaivaitā
mṛṇālaprastaraṃ naraḥ
manyate nārakaiḥ śastrair
vikṣato dvijasattama
body.translated_text: And likewise a man, gashed by hell-weapons, O best of the twice-born, regards these sword-edges as a couch of lotus-fibre.

body.text:
himakhaṇḍacayāchanno
nivātaṃ manyate naraḥ
vimukto nārakāc chītāt
prakāśaṃ tamasas tamaḥ
body.translated_text: Covered by heaps of masses of snow, a man regards it as a windless place—released from the cold of hell, light as compared to darkness, darkness of darkness.

body.text:
protā gudeṣu bhinnāṅgā
ārtā rāvavirāviṇaḥ
śūleṣu loheṣv apare
triśūleṣu tathāpare
body.translated_text: Pierced through the anus, their limbs split, afflicted, crying out with screams—some on iron stakes, others on tridents likewise.

body.text:
yājyopādhyāyadāmpatya-
suhṛnmitrasutādiṣu
kṛto bhedo durācārair
yair alīkoktibhāṣibhiḥ
body.translated_text: Between sacrificer and officiant, between husband and wife, between friends, comrades, sons, and the rest, division was made by the ill-conducted, speakers of false speech.

body.text:
āyasāḥ kaṇṭakās tīkṣṇā
narake kūṭaśālmalau
teṣu protā durātmānaḥ
paradārabhujo narāḥ
body.translated_text: In the hell <s>Kūṭaśālmali</s> there are sharp iron thorns; on them are pierced the evil-souled men who enjoy others' wives.

body.text:
kṛmikīṭajalaukādi-
tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāsyavikṣatāḥ
bhrāmyante cāndhatāmisre
vṛthāmāṃsāśino hi ye
body.translated_text: Gashed by the sharp-fanged mouths of worms, insects, leeches, and the like, they are made to wander in <s>Andhatāmisra</s>—those who indeed eat flesh in vain.

body.text:
etāṃś cānyāṃś ca narakāñ
śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
karmāntaraṃ jano bhuṅkte
pariṇāmāṃś ca cetasaḥ
body.translated_text: These and other hells, by the hundreds and by the thousands, a person enjoys according to his deeds, and the transformations of the mind.

body.text:
yādṛk karma manuṣyāṇāṃ
tādṛg viṣayarūpavat
pariṇāmaṃ mano yāti
śubhāśubhamayaṃ dvija
body.translated_text: As is the deed of men, so, having the form of its object, the mind goes to a transformation made of good and evil, O twice-born.

body.text:
atīvabhīṣaṇān itthaṃ
śastrāgnibhayadān naraḥ
kathaṃ na gacchen narakān
etan me vaktum arhasi
body.translated_text: How should a man not go to the hells, thus exceedingly terrible, giving fear of weapons and fire?—this you ought to tell me.

body.text:
aho 'tikaṣṭapāpānāṃ
vipāko narakasthitaiḥ
puruṣair bhujyate brahmaṃs
tanmokṣaṃ vada sattama
body.translated_text: Alas, the ripening of the exceedingly grievous sins is enjoyed by men dwelling in hell, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; tell their release, O best one.

body.text:
puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ pākaḥ
puṇya eva dvijottama
cetasaḥ pariṇāmottaḥ
svargasthair bhujyate naraiḥ
body.translated_text: The ripening of a meritorious deed is itself meritorious, O best of the twice-born; arising from the transformation of the mind, it is enjoyed by men dwelling in heaven.

body.text:
tathaiva pākaḥ pāpānāṃ
puruṣair narakasthitaiḥ
bhujyate tāvad akhilaṃ
yāvat pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam
body.translated_text: Likewise the ripening of sins is enjoyed by men dwelling in hell, all of it, until the sin has come to its destruction.

body.text:
yadā tu pāpasya jayaḥ
kṣīyate sukṛtaṃ tadā
śubhasya karmaṇo vṛddhau
kṣayam āyāty aśobhanam
body.translated_text: But when there is the prevailing of sin, then good deeds dwindle; with the increase of an auspicious deed, the inauspicious comes to destruction.

body.text:
jaye yateta puruṣas
tasmāt sukṛtakarmaṇaḥ
pāpaṃ karma vinā naiva
narakaprāptir iṣyate
body.translated_text: Therefore a man should strive for the prevailing of good deeds; without sinful deed, the attainment of hell is not held to occur.

body.text:
jayāya dvādaśī śastā
nṝṇāṃ sukṛtakarmaṇām
yām upoṣya dvijaśreṣṭha
na yāti narakaṃ naraḥ
body.translated_text: For the prevailing, the <s>dvādaśī</s> (twelfth lunar day) is commended for men of good deeds, by fasting on which, O best of the twice-born, a man does not go to hell.

body.text:
phālgunāmalapakṣasya
ekādaśyām upoṣitaḥ
dvādaśyāṃ tu dvijaśreṣṭha
pūjayen madhusūdanam
body.translated_text: Fasting on the eleventh of the bright fortnight of <s>Phālguna</s>, one should worship <s>Madhusūdana</s> on the twelfth, O best of the twice-born.

body.text:
ekādaśyāṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ
viṣṇor nāmānukīrtanam
pūjāyāṃ vāsudevasya
kurvīta susamāhitaḥ
body.translated_text: On the eleventh is enjoined the repeated proclamation of the name of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; in the worship of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, one should perform it with full concentration.

body.text:
namo nārāyaṇāyeti
vācyaṃ ca svapatā niśi
body.translated_text: And while sleeping at night one should say, "Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>."

body.text:
krodhaḥ prapañca īrṣyā ca
dambho lobhaś ca varjitaḥ
body.translated_text: Anger, deceitful complication, envy, hypocrisy, and greed are to be shunned.

body.text:
kāmo droho madaś cāpi
mānamātsaryam eva ca
sarvam etat parityajya
viṣṇubhaktena cetasā
body.translated_text: Desire, malice, and intoxication too, pride and jealousy as well—abandoning all this, with a mind devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

body.text:
asāratāṃ ca loke 'smin
saṃsāre bhāvayen matim
body.translated_text: and one should reflect with one's mind on the worthlessness of this world, of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text:
kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca
dambham īrṣyāṃ ca varjayet
mānadrohādidoṣāṃś ca
sarvān dhanamadodbhūtān
bhāvayed viṣṇubhaktāṃś ca
saṃsārāsāratāṃ tathā
evaṃ bhāvitacittena
prāṇināṃ hitam icchatā
body.translated_text: One should shun desire, anger, and greed, hypocrisy and envy, and the faults of pride, malice, and the rest, all born of intoxication with wealth; and one should cherish thoughts devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and likewise the worthlessness of <s>saṃsāra</s>—thus with a mind so disposed, desiring the welfare of living beings.

body.text:
tathaiva kuryād dvādaśyāṃ
nāmnām uccāraṇaṃ dvija
body.translated_text: And likewise on the <s>dvādaśī</s> one should make the utterance of the names, O twice-born.

body.text:
yavapātrāṇi pūrvaṃ tu
dadyān māsacatuṣṭayam
āṣāḍhādidvitīyaṃ tu
pāraṇaṃ yan mahāmate
tatrāpi ghṛtapātrāṇi
dadyāc chraddhāsamanvitaḥ
body.translated_text: First one should give vessels of barley for a set of four months; but in the second, beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, the breaking-of-the-fast, O greatly wise one, there too one should give vessels of ghee, endowed with faith.

body.text:
kārttikādiṣu māseṣu
māghanteṣu tathā tilān
viprāya dadyāt pātrashtān
pratimāsam upoṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: In the months beginning with <s>Kārttika</s> and ending with <s>Māgha</s>, one should give to a <s>vipra</s>, while fasting each month, vessels filled with sesame.

body.text:
nāmatrayam aśeṣeṣu
māsi māsi dinadvayam
tathaivoccārayed dadyād
dvādaśyāṃ ca yavādikam
praṇamya ca hṛṣīkeśaṃ
kṛtapūjaḥ prasādayet
body.translated_text: In all the months, the three names twice a month one should likewise utter, and on the <s>dvādaśī</s> one should give barley and the rest; and having bowed to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, having performed worship, one should gladden him.

body.text:
viṣṇo namas te jagataḥ prasūte
oṃ vāsudevāya namo namas te
nārāyaṇa tvāṃ praṇato 'smy acintya
jayo 'stu me śāśvatapuṇyarāśeḥ
body.translated_text: Homage to you, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, begetter of the world; <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, homage to you; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, I am bowed to you, O inconceivable one; may there be victory to me, the heap of eternal merit.

body.text:
prasīda puṇyaṃ jayam etu viṣṇo
oṃ vāsudeva rddhim upaitu puṇyam
nārāyaṇoṃ bhūtim upaitu puṇyam
prayātu cāśeṣam aghaṃ vināśam
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; may merit come to victory; <s>Oṃ</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, may merit come to prosperity; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Oṃ</s>, may merit come to well-being, and may all evil go to destruction.

body.text:
viṣṇo puṇyodbhavo me 'stu
vāsudevāstu me śubham
nārāyaṇāstu dharmo me
jahi pāpam aśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, may there be for me the arising of merit; <s>Vāsudeva</s>, may there be good for me; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, may there be <s>dharma</s> for me; destroy sin completely.

body.text:
anekajanmajanitaṃ
bālyayauvanavārddhike
puṇyaṃ vivṛddhim āyātu
yātu pāpaṃ tu saṃkṣayam
body.translated_text: May the merit produced in many births, in childhood, youth, and old age, come to increase; and may sin go to destruction.

body.text:
ākāśādiṣu śabdādau
śrotrādau mahadādiṣu
prakṛtau puruṣe caiva
brahmaṇy api ca sa prabhuḥ
yathaika eva sarvātmā
vāsudevo vyavasthitaḥ
body.translated_text: In ether and the rest, in sound and the rest, in hearing and the rest, in the <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, in <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and in <s>Puruṣa</s> (the spirit), and in <s>Brahman</s> too, that Lord—as the one Self of all, <s>Vāsudeva</s> is established.

body.text:
tena satyena me pāpaṃ
narakārtipradaṃ kṣayam
prayātu sukṛtasyāstu
mamānudivasaṃ jayaḥ
pāpasya hāniḥ puṇyaṃ ca
vṛddhim abhyety anuttamām
body.translated_text: By that truth, may my sin, the giver of the anguish of hell, go to destruction; may there be day after day the victory of my good deeds; let the loss of sin and merit come to the unsurpassed increase.

body.text:
evam uccārya viprāya
dattvā yat kathitaṃ tava
bhuñjīta kṛtakṛtyas tu
pāraṇe pāraṇe gate
body.translated_text: Having thus uttered this, and having given to a <s>vipra</s> what has been told to you, one should eat, his duty accomplished, when each breaking-of-the-fast has passed.

body.text:
pāraṇānte ca devasya
prīṇanaṃ śaktito dvija
kurvītākhilapāṣaṇḍair
ālāpaṃ ca vivarjayet
body.translated_text: And at the end of the breaking-of-the-fast one should, according to ability, gladden the god, O twice-born, and should avoid converse with all heretics.

body.text:
ity etat kathitaṃ dālbhya
sukṛtasya jayāvahā
dvādaśī narakaṃ mṛtyo
yām upoṣya na paśyati
body.translated_text: Thus this has been told, O <s>Dālbhya</s>: the <s>dvādaśī</s> is the bringer of the victory of good deeds, by fasting on which a man does not behold the hell of Death.

body.text:
nāgnayo na ca śastrāṇi
na ca lohamūkhāḥ khagāḥ
nārakās taṃ prabādhante
matir yasya janārdane
body.translated_text: Neither fires nor weapons, nor iron-beaked birds, nor the hell-keepers afflict him whose mind is on <s>Janārdana</s>.

body.text:
nāmoccāraṇamātreṇa
viṣṇoḥ kṣīṇo 'ghasaṃcayaḥ
bhavaty apāstapāpasya
narake gamanaṃ kutaḥ
body.translated_text: By the mere utterance of the name of <s>Viṣṇu</s> the accumulation of sin is destroyed; for one whose sin is cast off, how could there be going to hell?

body.text:
namo nārāyaṇa hare
vāsudeveti kīrtayet
na yāti narakaṃ martyaḥ
saṃkṣīṇāśeṣapātakaḥ
body.translated_text: Let one proclaim "Homage, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>"; the mortal whose every transgression is destroyed does not go to hell.

body.text:
tasmāt pāṣaṇḍisaṃsargam
akurvan dvādaśīm imām
upoṣya puṇyopacayī
na yāti narakaṃ naraḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, not making contact with heretics, fasting on this <s>dvādaśī</s>, an accumulator of merit, a man does not go to hell.

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍibhir asaṃsparśam
asaṃbhāṣaṇam eva ca
viṣṇor ārādhanaparair
naraiḥ kāryam upoṣitaiḥ
body.translated_text: Non-contact with heretics and likewise non-conversation is to be observed by men fasting, intent on the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
kiṃ brūhi lakṣaṇaṃ teṣāṃ
yādṛśān varjayed vratī
kathaṃcid yadi saṃlāpa-
darśanasparśanādikam
body.translated_text: Tell, what is the mark of those whom a vow-keeper should shun? And if somehow there be conversation, beholding, touching, and the like,

body.text:
upoṣitānāṃ pāṣaṇḍair
narāṇāṃ vipra jāyate
kiṃ tatra vada kartavyaṃ
yenākhaṇḍaṃ vrataṃ bhavet
body.translated_text: of fasting men with heretics, O <s>vipra</s>, what is to be done there, tell, by which the vow may be unbroken?

body.text:
śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmaṃ
varṇāśramavibhāgajam
ullaṅghya ye pravartante
svecchayā kūṭayuktibhiḥ
body.translated_text: Those who, having transgressed the <s>dharma</s> declared in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, born of the division of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, proceed at their own will by false reasonings,

body.text:
vikarmābhiratā mūḍhā
yuktiprāgalbhyadurmadāḥ
pāṣaṇḍinas te duḥśīlā
narakārhā narādhamāḥ
body.translated_text: fools devoted to forbidden acts, intoxicated with boldness of argument—those heretics of evil conduct, deserving of hell, are the lowest of men.

body.text:
tāṃs tu pāṣaṇḍinaḥ pāpān
vikarmasthāṃś ca mānavān
vaiḍālavratikāṃś caiva
nityam eva tu nālapet
body.translated_text: Those sinful heretics, and the men engaged in forbidden acts, and those of cat-like vows (hypocrites)—one should never speak with them at all.

body.text:
saṃbhāṣyaitāñ śuciṣadaṃ
cintayed acyutaṃ budhaḥ
idaṃ codāharet samyak
kṛtvā tatpravaṇaṃ manaḥ
body.translated_text: Having spoken with these, the wise man should meditate on <s>Acyuta</s> who dwells in the pure, and should rightly utter this, having made his mind inclined toward him:

body.text:
śārīram antaḥkaraṇopaghātaṃ
vācaś ca viṣṇur bhagavān aśeṣam
śamaṃ nayatv astu mameha śarma
pāpād anante hṛdi saṃniviṣṭe
body.translated_text: May the Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> bring to calm wholly the bodily injury, the injury of the inner faculty, and of speech; may there be welfare for me here, when the infinite one is established in the heart, freed from sin.

body.text:
antaḥśuddhiṃ bahiḥśuddhiṃ
śuddho 'ntar mama yo 'cyutaḥ
sa karotv amale tasmiñ
śucir evāsmi sarvadā
body.translated_text: Inner purity, outer purity—may that <s>Acyuta</s> who is pure within me bring about; in that stainless one I am ever pure indeed.

body.text:
bāhyopaghātād anagho
boddhā ca bhagavān ajaḥ
śuddhiṃ nayatv anantātmā
viṣṇuś cetasi saṃsthitaḥ
body.translated_text: Sinless from outer injury, and the knower, the Blessed unborn one—may <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the infinite-souled, established in my heart, lead me to purity.

body.text:
etat saṃbhāṣya japtavyaṃ
pāṣaṇḍibhir upoṣitaiḥ
namaḥ śuciṣadety uktvā
sūryaṃ paśyeta vīkṣitaiḥ
body.translated_text: This is to be muttered, having spoken with heretics, by those fasting; having said "Homage to the one who dwells in purity," one should look at the sun with intent gaze.

body.text:
śrūyate ca purā martyāḥ
svecchayā svargagāminaḥ
babhūvur anaghāḥ sarve
svadharmaparipālanāt
body.translated_text: And it is heard that of old, mortals by their own will became goers to heaven, all sinless, from the protection of their own <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
devāś ca balino martyair
varṇakarmaṇy anuvrataiḥ
yajñādhyayanadāneṣu
vartamānaiś ca mānavaiḥ
body.translated_text: And the gods were made strong by mortals, by men faithful to the duties of their class, abiding in sacrifice, study, and gifts.

body.text:
daiteyāś ca parābhāvam
atuṣṭāv asurā yayuḥ
tataś ca ṣaṇḍo markaś ca
daityendrāṇāṃ purohitau
cakratuḥ karma devānāṃ
vināśāyātibhīṣaṇam
body.translated_text: And the <s>Daiteyas</s> met defeat; the <s>Asuras</s> went away discontented; and then <s>Ṣaṇḍa</s> and <s>Marka</s>, the two domestic priests of the <s>Daitya</s> lords, performed a most terrible rite for the destruction of the gods

body.text:
tatrotpanno 'tikṛṣṇāṅgas
tamaḥprāyo 'tidāruṇaḥ
dambhādhāraḥ śāṭhyasāro
nidrāprakṛtir ulvaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: There was produced a being of utterly black limbs, made mostly of darkness (<s>tamas</s>), exceedingly cruel, having deceit as his support, with treachery for his essence, sloth as his nature, and fierce

body.text:
mahāmoha iti khyātaḥ
kṛtyarūpo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
caturdhā sa vibhaktaś ca
tābhām atra mahīyate
body.translated_text: Known as <s>Mahāmoha</s> (Great Delusion), a terrifying being in the form of a magic spell; and divided fourfold, he is here exalted by those two

body.text:
vedadevadvijātīnām
ekāṃśena sa nindanam
karoty anyena na ratiṃ
yogakarmasu vindati
body.translated_text: With one portion he produces the reviling of the <s>Vedas</s>, the gods, and the twice-born; with another he finds no delight in yogic acts,

body.text:
vikarmaṇy apareṇāpi
saṃyojayati mānavān
jñānāpahāram anyena
karoti dvijasattama
body.translated_text: with yet another he joins men to forbidden acts (<s>vikarma</s>), and with another he carries off knowledge, O best of the twice-born

body.text:
jñānabuddhyā tathājñānaṃ
gṛhṇāty ajñānamohitaḥ
vedavādavirodhena
yā kathā sāsya rocate
body.translated_text: Deluded by ignorance, he grasps ignorance as if it were knowledge by the intellect; whatever discourse contradicts the teaching of the <s>Vedas</s>, that pleases him

body.text:
evaṃ sa tu mahāmohaḥ
ṣaṇḍamarkopapāditaḥ
dambhādidūṣito 'dharma-
svarūpo 'tibhayaṃkara
body.translated_text: Thus that <s>Mahāmoha</s>, brought into being by <s>Ṣaṇḍa</s> and <s>Marka</s>, defiled by deceit and the rest, having the very form of <s>adharma</s>, exceedingly terrifying,

body.text:
sa lokān vividhopāyair
lokeṣv eva vyavasthitaḥ
mohābhibhavaniḥsārāṇ
karoti dvijasattama
body.translated_text: by various means, abiding among the worlds themselves, renders the worlds devoid of essence through the dominance of delusion, O best of the twice-born

body.text:
tanmohitānām acirād
viveko yāti saṃkṣayam
kṣīṇajñānā vikarmāṇi
kurvanty aharaho dvija
body.translated_text: In those whom he deludes, discrimination soon goes to ruin; with knowledge diminished, they perform forbidden acts day after day, O twice-born

body.text:
nijavarṇātmakaṃ dharmaṃ
parityajya vimohitāḥ
dharmabuddhyā tataḥ pāpaṃ
kurvanty ajñānadurmadāḥ
body.translated_text: Deluded, abandoning the <s>dharma</s> proper to their own caste, then, with the notion that it is <s>dharma</s>, they commit sin, maddened by ignorance

body.text:
jñānāvalepas tatraiva
tatas teṣāṃ prajāyate
suhṛdbhir vāryamāṇās te
paṇḍitaiś ca dayālubhiḥ
prayacchanty uttaraṃ ṃūḍhāḥ
kūṭayuktisamanvitam
body.translated_text: And there itself a conceit of knowledge arises in them; restrained by their friends and by the learned and compassionate, the fools give a rejoinder furnished with fallacious arguments

body.text:
tatas te svayam ātmānam
anyaṃ cālpamatiṃ naram
vikarmaṇā yojayantaś
cyavayanti svadharmataḥ
body.translated_text: Then, joining themselves and another man of feeble intellect to forbidden acts, they cause him to fall away from his own <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍino durācārāḥ
parānnaguṇavādinaḥ
asaṃskṛtānnabhoktāro
vrātyāḥ saṃskāravarjitāḥ
body.translated_text: Heretics of wicked conduct, praisers of the qualities of others' food, eaters of unconsecrated food, <s>vrātyas</s> (excommunicates) devoid of the sacraments,

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍāḥ pāpasaṃkalpā
dāmbhikāḥ śaṭhabuddhayaḥ
varṇasaṃkarakartāro
māyāvyājopajīvinaḥ
niḥśaucā vakramatayo
nānyadastītivādinaḥ
body.translated_text: heretics of sinful resolve, hypocrites of crooked mind, makers of caste-confusion, living by deceit and fraud, impure, of perverse intellect, declaring that nothing else exists,

body.text:
evaṃvidhās te sanmārgād
vedaproktād bahiḥsthitāḥ
kriyākalāpaṃ nindanta
ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitam
ātmānaṃ ca parāṃś caiva
kurvanti narakasthitān
body.translated_text: such people, standing outside the good path proclaimed by the <s>Vedas</s>, reviling the body of rites named after the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, place both themselves and others in hell

body.text:
teṣāṃ darśanasaṃbhāṣa-
sparśanāni naraiḥ sadā
parityājyāni dṛṣṭe ca
proktaḥ saṃbhāṣaṇe ca yaḥ
saṃsparśe ca budhaḥ snātvā
śuciḥ śuciṣadaṃ smaret
body.translated_text: The seeing, speaking with, and touching of them are ever to be shunned by men; and when one has seen, or as declared has spoken with, or touched them, the wise man, having bathed, pure, should remember the One who dwells in purity

body.text:
bhavaty ataḥ sadaivaiṣām
ālāpaspar1śanaṃ tyajet
puṇyakāmo mahābhāgaḥ
kiṃ punar yad upoṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore one should ever forsake conversing with and touching them—the greatly fortunate one desiring merit; how much more so when he is fasting!

body.text:
yato hi nindite karmaṇy
abhyāso ratir eva ca
pāṣaṇḍinām aśeṣāṇām
aprītir vedakarmaṇi
te hy adhogāminaḥ proktā
āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ
body.translated_text: Since for the heretics there is application and delight only in censured action, and no liking for the rites of the <s>Vedas</s>—they indeed are declared to be downward-bound, resorting to the demonic (<s>āsura</s>) nature

body.text:
aprāptir na tathā duḥkham
aiśvaryāder dvijottama
yathā manorathair labdhair
vicyutir dharmahānijā
body.translated_text: Not so painful is the non-attainment of lordship and the like, O best of the twice-born, as is the falling away, born of loss of <s>dharma</s>, from wishes once obtained

body.text:
aiśvaryād vittato vāpi
saṃtater devalokataḥ
abhīṣṭād anyato vāpi
padād yena na vicyutim
body.translated_text: From lordship, or from wealth, from progeny, or from the world of the gods, or from any other desired station, by which a man does not suffer a fall—

body.text:
prāpnoti puruṣo brahman
nārī vāpuṇyasaṃkṣayāt
tan mamācakṣva viprarṣe
duḥkham ebhyo hi vicyutiḥ
body.translated_text: tell me, O <s>brahman</s>, by what a man or a woman attains it without exhaustion of merit; for falling away from these is indeed misery, O sage among <s>vipras</s>

body.text:
satyam etan mahābhāga
duḥkhaṃ prāptasya saṃkṣayaḥ
aiśvaryād atha vittasya
bandhuvargasukhasya vā
body.translated_text: This is true, O greatly fortunate one: the exhaustion suffered by one who has attained lordship, or wealth, or the happiness of a circle of kinsmen, is misery

body.text:
tad etac chrūyatāṃ dālbhya
yathā neṣṭāt paricyutiḥ
sargāder jāyate samyag
upavāsavatāṃ satām
body.translated_text: Let it be heard, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, how there is no falling away from what is desired—from creation onward—for the good who properly keep the fasts

body.text:
dvādaśarkṣāṇi viprarṣe
pratimāsaṃ tu yāni vai
tannāmāny acyutaṃ teṣu
samyak saṃpūjayed budhaḥ
body.translated_text: The twelve lunar mansions which fall each month, O sage among <s>vipras</s>, by their names the wise man should properly worship <s>Acyuta</s> in them

body.text:
puṣpair dhūpais tathāmbhobhir
abhīṣṭair aparais tathā
āditaḥ kṛttikāṃ kṛtvā
kārttike munipuṅgava
body.translated_text: with flowers, with incense, and likewise with waters, and with other desired things, having made <s>Kṛttikā</s> the first, in <s>Kārttika</s>, O bull among sages

body.text:
naivedyaṃ kṛsaraṃ pūrvam
annaṃ māsacatuṣṭayam
nivedayet kārttikādi
saṃyāvaṃ ca tataḥ param
body.translated_text: As food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>) he should first present <s>kṛsara</s> (rice and sesame), food for four months beginning with <s>Kārttika</s>, and after that <s>saṃyāva</s> (a wheat dish)

body.text:
āṣāḍhādau ca devāya
pāyasaṃ vai nivedayet
tenaivānnena viprarṣe
brāhmaṇān bhojayed budhaḥ
body.translated_text: And beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, he should offer <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) to the god; with that very food the wise man should feed the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O sage among <s>vipras</s>

body.text:
pañcagavyajalasnātas
tasyaiva prāśanāc chuciḥ
naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyān
naktaṃ saṃpūjite 'cyute
body.translated_text: Bathed in the water of the <s>pañcagavya</s>, pure from drinking that, he should himself eat the food-offering at night when <s>Acyuta</s> has been worshipped

body.text:
evaṃ saṃvatsarasyānte
tataḥ suptotthite 'cyute
saṃyak saṃpūjya viprarṣe
tam eva puruṣottamam
praṇamya prārthayed vidvāñ
śuciḥ snāto yathāvidhi
body.translated_text: Thus at the year's end, then when <s>Acyuta</s> has risen from sleep, having properly worshipped that very <s>Puruṣottama</s>, O sage among <s>vipras</s>, the learned man, pure and bathed according to rule, having bowed, should pray:

body.text:
namo namas te 'cyuta saṃkṣayo 'stu
pāpasya vṛddhiṃ samupaitu puṇyam
aiśvaryavittādi sadākṣayaṃ me
'kṣayā ca me saṃtatir acyutāstu
body.translated_text: "Homage, homage to you, <s>Acyuta</s>; may there be the destruction of sin; may merit attain increase; may my lordship, wealth, and the rest be ever undecaying, and may my progeny be undecaying, <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
yathācyutas tvaṃ parataḥ parasmāt
sa brahmabhūtāt parataḥ parātman
tathācyutaṃ me kuru vāñchitaṃ yan
mayā padaṃ pāpaharāprameya
body.translated_text: As you, <s>Acyuta</s>, are higher than the highest, higher than that which has become <s>Brahman</s>, O supreme Self, so make undecaying (<s>acyuta</s>) for me the station I have desired, O remover of sin, immeasurable one

body.text:
acyutānanta govinda
prasīda yad abhīpsitam
tad akṣayam ameyātman
kuruṣva puruṣottama
body.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, be gracious; make undecaying whatever is desired, O immeasurable Self, <s>Puruṣottama</s>"

body.text:
evam ante samabhyarcya
prārthayitvā tathāśiṣaḥ
yathāvan muniśārdūla
cyutiṃ nāpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, having worshipped at the end and prayed for blessings duly, O tiger among sages, a man suffers no falling away

body.text:
saṃtateḥ svargavittāder
aiśvaryasya tathā mune
yad vābhimatam atyantaṃ
tato na cyavate naraḥ
body.translated_text: From progeny, from heaven, wealth and the rest, and from lordship, O sage, or from whatever is exceedingly cherished, a man does not fall away therefrom

body.text:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena
māsanakṣatrapūjane
yatetākṣayakāmas tu
sadaiva munipuṅgava
body.translated_text: Therefore with all effort one desiring the undecaying should ever strive in the worship of the months and lunar mansions, O bull among sages

body.text:
atrāpi śrūyate siddhā
kācit svarge mahāvratā
nārī tapodhanā bhūtvā
prakhyātā śāmbharāyaṇī
samastasaṃdehaharā
sadā svargaukasāṃ hi sā
body.translated_text: Here too is heard of a certain perfected one in heaven, of great vows, a woman who, having become rich in austerity, was renowned as <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s>, the remover of every doubt, ever for the dwellers in heaven

body.text:
kasyacit tv atha kālasya
devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ
pūrvendracaritaṃ brahman
papracchedaṃ bṛhaspatim
body.translated_text: Now at a certain time, the king of the gods, <s>Śatakratu</s>, asked <s>Bṛhaspati</s> thus, O <s>brahman</s>, about the deeds of the former <s>Indras</s>:

body.text:
pūrvendrā parataḥ pūrve
ye babhūvuḥ sureśvarāḥ
teṣāṃ caritam icchāmi
śrotum āṅgirasāṃ vara
body.translated_text: "The former <s>Indras</s>, the lords of gods who existed before, in earlier times—their deeds I wish to hear, O best of the <s>Āṅgirasas</s>"

body.text:
evam uktas tadā tena
devendreṇāmaladyutiḥ
prāha dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ
paramarṣir bṛhaspatiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by that lord of the gods, the supreme seer <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>, of stainless splendour, spoke:

body.text:
nāhaṃ cirantanān vedmi
devarāja sureśvarān
ātmanaḥ samakālīnaṃ
mām avaihi sureśvara
body.translated_text: "I do not know the ancient lords of gods, O king of the gods; know me, O lord of gods, to be contemporary with myself only"

body.text:
tataḥ papraccha devendraḥ
ko 'smābhir munipuṅgava
praṣṭavyo 'tra mahābhāga
kṛtādivasatir divi
body.translated_text: Then <s>Indra</s> asked: "Who is to be questioned by us here, O bull among sages, O greatly fortunate one, who has dwelt in heaven since the <s>Kṛta</s> age and onward?"

body.text:
bṛhaspatiś ciraṃ dhyātvā
punar āha śacīpatim
tapasvinīṃ mahābhāgāṃ
smṛtvāsau śāmbharāyaṇīm
body.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, having meditated long, again spoke to the husband of <s>Śacī</s>, having remembered that ascetic, the greatly fortunate <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s>:

body.text:
na devā na ca gandharvā
na cānye cirasaṃsthitāḥ
cirantanānāṃ cariteṣv
abhijñā tridaśeśvara
body.translated_text: "Neither the gods nor the <s>Gandharvas</s>, nor others long-established, are acquainted with the deeds of the ancients, O lord of the thirty gods

body.text:
ekaiva cirakālajñā
dharmajñā śakra kevalam
jānāty akhiladevendra-
caritaṃ śāmbharāyaṇī
body.translated_text: One alone, knower of long ages, knower of <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Śakra</s>—only <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s> knows the deeds of every lord of the gods"

body.text:
ity uktas tena devendraḥ
kautūhalasamanvitaḥ
yayau yatra mahābhāgā
tāpasī śāmbharāyaṇī
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, that <s>Indra</s>, filled with curiosity, went to where the greatly fortunate ascetic <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s> was

body.text:
sā tau dṛṣṭvā samāyātau
devarājabṛhaspatī
samyag arghyena saṃpūjya
praṇipatya śubhavratā
body.translated_text: Seeing those two—the king of the gods and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>—arrived, she of auspicious vows, having properly worshipped them with the <s>arghya</s> and bowed down,

body.text:
namo 'stu devarājāya
tathaivāṅgirase namaḥ
yad vāṃ kāryaṃ mahābhāgau
sakalaṃ tad ihocyatām
body.translated_text: [said:] "Homage to the king of the gods, and likewise homage to the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>; whatever business you two have, O greatly fortunate ones, let all of it be spoken here"

body.text:
āvām abhyāgatau praṣṭuṃ
tvām atrātivivekinīm
yac ca kāryaṃ mahābhāge
tat pṛṣṭā kathayeha nau
body.translated_text: "We two have come to ask you, here, who are most discriminating; and whatever business there is, O greatly fortunate one, tell it to us, being asked

body.text:
yadi smarasi kalyāṇi
pūrvendracaritāni nau
tadākhyāhi mahābhāge
devendrasya kutūhalāt
body.translated_text: If you remember, O auspicious one, the deeds of the former <s>Indras</s> for us, then declare them, O greatly fortunate one, out of the curiosity of <s>Indra</s>"

body.text:
yadi śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ
tat kariṣye vimṛṣyatu
body.translated_text: "If it can be done by me, that I shall do; let it be considered"

body.text:
yo vai pūrvaḥ surendrasya
tataś ca prathamo hi yaḥ
tasmāt pūrvataro yaś ca
tasyāpi prathamāś ca ye
body.translated_text: "He who indeed was before the lord of the gods, and then he who was first before that, and he who was earlier than that, and those too who were first before him,

body.text:
teṣāṃ pūrvatarā ye ca
vedmi tān akhilān aham
teṣāṃ ca caritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ
jānāmy āṅgirasāṃ vara
body.translated_text: and those who were earlier than they—I know them all, and the entire deeds of those, I know, O best of the <s>Āṅgirasas</s>

body.text:
manvantarāṇy anekāni
sṛṣṭiṃ ca tridivaukasām
saptarṣīn subahūn deva
manūnāṃ ca sutān nṛpa
tat pṛccha tvaṃ vadāmy eṣā
pūrvendracaritaṃ mune
body.translated_text: the many <s>Manvantaras</s> and the creation of the dwellers in heaven, the very many <s>Saptarṣis</s>, O god, and the sons of the <s>Manus</s>, O king—ask that; I tell it, O sage, the deeds of the former <s>Indras</s>"

body.text:
evam ukte tatas tābhyāṃ
pṛṣṭā sā śāmbharāyaṇī
yathāvad ācaṣṭa tayoḥ
pūrvendracaritaṃ dvija
body.translated_text: When this was thus said by the two, <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s>, being asked, related to those two the deeds of the former <s>Indras</s> duly, O twice-born

body.text:
svāyambhuve yas tu manau
manau svārociṣe tu yaḥ
uttame tāmase caiva
raivate cākṣuṣe tathā
body.translated_text: In the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> <s>Manu</s>, and in the <s>Svārociṣa</s> <s>Manu</s>, and in the <s>Uttama</s>, the <s>Tāmasa</s>, the <s>Raivata</s>, and likewise the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>,

body.text:
yo yo babhūva devendras
tasya tasya tapasvinī
tayor jagāda caritaṃ
yathāvac chāmbharāyaṇī
body.translated_text: whoever became <s>Indra</s> in each, the ascetic <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s> related the deeds of each to those two, duly

body.text:
tataḥ kautūhalaparo
devarāṭ tāṃ tapasvinīm
uvāca jānāsi kathaṃ
tvam etac chāmbharāyaṇi
body.translated_text: Then, full of curiosity, the king of the gods said to that ascetic: "How do you know this, O <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s>?"

body.text:
sarva eva hi devendrāḥ
svargasthā ye manīṣiṇaḥ
babhūvur etac caritam
eteṣāṃ vedmi tena vai
body.translated_text: "All those wise <s>Indras</s> who became dwellers in heaven—this is their deed; therefore I know it of these

body.text:
kiṃ kṛtaṃ vada dharmajñe
tvayā yeneyam akṣayā
svarloke vasatiḥ prāptā
yathā nānyena kenacit
body.translated_text: Tell me, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, what was done by you, by which this undecaying dwelling in the heavenly world was attained as by no other"

body.text:
aho sarvavratānāṃ tad
upoṣitaṃ mahad vratam
pradhānataram atyarthaṃ
svargasaṃvāsadaṃ matam
body.translated_text: "Ah, that fasting is the great vow of all vows, exceedingly the foremost, reckoned the giver of dwelling in heaven

body.text:
caritaṃ ca mayā teṣāṃ
śrutaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tathaiva ca
body.translated_text: And the deed of those [Indras] was heard by me, and likewise seen"

body.text:
evam uktā tatas tena
devendreṇa yaśasvinī
pratyuvāca mahābhāgā
yathāvac chāmbharāyaṇī
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by that <s>Indra</s>, the illustrious, greatly fortunate <s>Śāmbharāyaṇī</s> replied duly:

body.text:
māsarkṣeṣv acyuto devaḥ
pratimāsaṃ sureśvara
yathoktavratayā samyak
sapta varṣāṇi pūjitaḥ
body.translated_text: "In the lunar mansions of the months, the god <s>Acyuta</s>, each month, O lord of gods, was properly worshipped by me with the vow as declared for seven years

body.text:
tasyeyaṃ karmaṇo vyuṣṭir
acyutārādhanasya me
devalokād abhimatā
devarāja yad acyutiḥ
body.translated_text: This is for me the reward of that act, of the worship of <s>Acyuta</s>: the un-falling from the world of the gods, which is cherished, O king of the gods (i.e. <s>acyuti</s>)

body.text:
svargaṃ dravyamayaiśvaryaṃ
saṃtatiṃ vāpi yo 'cyutām
naro vāñchati tenetthaṃ
toṣaṇīyo 'cyutaḥ prabhuḥ
body.translated_text: Whatever man desires heaven, lordship consisting of substance, or undecaying progeny, by him thus the Lord <s>Acyuta</s> is to be gratified

body.text:
etat te pūrvadevendra-
caritaṃ sakalaṃ mayā
svargavāsākṣayatvaṃ ca
māsarkṣācyutapūjanāt
body.translated_text: This deed of the former <s>Indras</s>, the whole of it, by me—and the undecaying nature of dwelling in heaven from the worship of <s>Acyuta</s> in the lunar mansions of the months—

body.text:
yathāvat kathitaṃ deva
pṛcchatas tridaśeśvara
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṃs tu
vāñchatāṃ vibudhādhipa
viṣṇor ārādhanān nānyat
paramaṃ siddhikāraṇam
body.translated_text: has been duly told, O god, to you who ask, O lord of the thirty; but for those desiring <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>, O chief of the wise, there is no supreme cause of success other than the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>"

body.text:
tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā
devarājabṛhaspatī
tāṃ tathety ūcatuḥ sādhvīṃ
ceratuś cāpi tad vratam
body.translated_text: Having heard that speech of hers, the king of the gods and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> said "So be it" to that virtuous one, and they too practiced that vow

body.text:
tasmād dālbhya prayatnena
pratimāsaṃ samāhitaḥ
māsarkṣācyutapūjāyāṃ
bhavethās tanmanāḥ sadā
body.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, with effort, concentrated each month in the worship of <s>Acyuta</s> in the lunar mansions, you should ever be with mind fixed on him

body.text:
bhagavan prāṇinaḥ sarve
viṣarogādyupadravaiḥ
duṣṭagrahopaghātaiś ca
sarvakālam upadrutāḥ
body.translated_text: O Blessed One, all living beings are afflicted at all times by the calamities of poison, disease, and the rest, and by the blows of malignant planets,

body.text:
ābhicārukakṛtyābhiḥ
sparṣarogaiś ca dāruṇaiḥ
sadā saṃpīḍyamānās te
tiṣṭhanti munisattama
body.translated_text: by black-magic rites and spells, and by terrible contagious diseases—they remain ever tormented, O best of sages

body.text:
yena karmavipākena
viṣarogādyupadravāḥ
na bhavanti nṛṇāṃ tan me
yathāvad vaktum arhasi
body.translated_text: By what ripening of action the calamities of poison, disease, and the rest do not befall men—that you ought to tell me duly

body.text:
vratopavāsair yair viṣṇur
nānyajanmani pūjitaḥ
te narā muniśārdūla
graharogādibhāginaḥ
body.translated_text: Those men by whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> was not worshipped with vows and fasts in another birth—they, O tiger among sages, partake of planet-afflictions, diseases, and the like

body.text:
yair na tatpravaṇaṃ cittaṃ
sarvadaiva naraiḥ kṛtam
viṣagrahajvarāṇāṃ te
manuṣyā dālbhya bhājanāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men by whom the mind was not made ever inclined toward him—they, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, are the receptacles of poison, planet-afflictions, and fevers

body.text:
ārogyaṃ paramām ṛddhiṃ
manasā yad yad icchati
tat tad āpnoty asaṃdigdhaṃ
paratrācyutatoṣakṛt
body.translated_text: Whatever health and supreme prosperity one wishes in mind, that one attains, without doubt—the one who gratifies <s>Acyuta</s>—and in the next world too

body.text:
nādhīn prāpnoti na vyādhīn
na viṣagrahabandhanam
kṛtyāsparśabhayaṃ vāpi
toṣite madhusūdane
body.translated_text: He suffers no mental ills, no bodily diseases, no bondage of poison and planets, nor even the fear of the touch of a magic spell, when <s>Madhusūdana</s> is gratified

body.text:
sarvaduṣṭaśamas tasya
saumyās tasya sadā grahāḥ
devānām apradhṛṣyo 'sau
tuṣṭo yasya janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: His is the calming of all that is malignant; the planets are ever benign to him; he is unassailable even by the gods, with whom <s>Janārdana</s> is pleased

body.text:
yaḥ samaḥ sarvabhūteṣu
yathātmani tathāpare
upavādādinā tena
toṣyate madhusūdanaḥ
body.translated_text: He who is equal toward all beings, regarding others as himself, by him <s>Madhusūdana</s> is gratified through the avoidance of slander and the like

body.text:
toṣite tatra jāyante
narāḥ pūṛṇamanorathāḥ
arogāḥ sukhino bhoga-
bhoktāro munisattama
body.translated_text: When he is gratified, men are born there with the wishes of their hearts fulfilled, free of disease, happy, enjoyers of pleasures, O best of sages

body.text:
na teṣāṃ śatravo naiva
sparśarogābhicārukāḥ
graharogādikaṃ vāpi
pāpakāryaṃ na jāyate
body.translated_text: They have no enemies, nor contagious diseases nor black magic; nor does planet-affliction and the like, or any sinful deed, arise [against them]

body.text:
avyāhatāni kṛṣṇasya
cakrādīny ātmayudhāni tam
rakṣanti sakalāpadbhyo
yena viṣṇur upāsitaḥ
body.translated_text: The unimpeded weapons of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the discus and the rest, his own weapons, protect from all calamities him by whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been worshipped

body.text:
anārādhitagovindā
ye narā duḥkhabhāginaḥ
teṣāṃ duḥkhābhibhūtānāṃ
kartavyaṃ yad dayālubhiḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who have not worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, who partake of misery—what is to be done by the compassionate for them, overcome by misery,

body.text:
paśyadbhiḥ sarvabhūtasthaṃ
vāsudevaṃ mahāmune
samadṛṣṭibhir īśeśaṃ
tan mama brūhy aśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: by those who behold <s>Vāsudeva</s> abiding in all beings, O great sage, with the eye of equality, the Lord of lords—tell me that completely

body.text:
kuśamūlasthito brahmā
kuśamadhye janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> abides at the root of the <s>kuśa</s>-grass, <s>Janārdana</s> in the middle of the <s>kuśa</s>,

body.text:
kuśāgre śaṃkaraṃ vidyāt
trayo devā vyavasthitāḥ
body.translated_text: and one should know <s>Śaṃkara</s> at the tip of the <s>kuśa</s>; the three gods are thus established

body.text:
gṛhītvā ca sa mūlāgrān
kuśāñ śuddhān upaspṛśet
body.translated_text: And having taken up pure <s>kuśa</s>-grasses by their root-tips, one should touch water

body.text:
mārjayet sarvagātrāṇi
kuśāgrair dālbhya śāntikṛt
body.translated_text: One should wipe all the limbs with the tips of the <s>kuśa</s>-grass, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, performing the rite of appeasement

body.text:
śarīre yasya tiṣṭhanti
kuśasthajalabindavaḥ
body.translated_text: Upon whose body stand the drops of water that have rested on the <s>kuśa</s>-grass,

body.text:
naśyanti tasya pāpāni
garuḍenaiva pannagāḥ
body.translated_text: his sins perish, just as serpents perish before <s>Garuḍa</s>

body.text:
viṣṇubhaktā viśeṣeṇa
....cidgatamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: the devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in particular, ... whose mind is fixed [on consciousness]

body.text:
rogagrahaviṣārtānāṃ
kuryāc chāntim imāṃ śubhām
body.translated_text: For those afflicted by disease, by planetary influence, and by poison, one should perform this auspicious appeasement

body.text:
nārasiṃhaṃ samabhyarcya
śucau deśe kuśāsane
body.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Narasiṃha</s>, in a pure place upon a seat of <s>kuśa</s>-grass,

body.text:
mantrair etair yathā liṅgaṃ
kuryād digbandham ātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: with these <s>mantras</s>, according to the characteristic, one should make the binding of the directions for oneself

body.text:
vārāhaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ ca
vāmanaṃ viṣṇum eva ca
body.translated_text: Having meditated upon <s>Varāha</s>, <s>Narasiṃha</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, having become concentrated, one should place the names in the directions

body.text:
dhyātvā samāhito bhūtvā
dikṣu nāmāni vinyāset
body.translated_text: Having meditated, becoming concentrated, one should place the names in the directions

body.text:
pūrve nārāyaṇaḥ pātu
vārijākṣas tu dakṣiṇe
body.translated_text: In the east may <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> protect, and in the south <s>Vārijākṣa</s> (the lotus-eyed)

body.text:
pradyumnaḥ paścimasyāṃ tu
vāsudevas tathottare
body.translated_text: <s>Pradyumna</s> in the west, and likewise <s>Vāsudeva</s> in the north

body.text:
īśānyām avatād viṣṇur
āgneyyāṃ ca janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: In the northeast may <s>Viṣṇu</s> guard, and in the southeast <s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
nairṛtyāṃ padmanābhaś ca
vāyavyāṃ caiva mādhavaḥ
body.translated_text: In the southwest <s>Padmanābha</s>, and in the northwest <s>Mādhava</s>

body.text:
ūrdhvaṃ govardhanadharo
adharāyāṃ trivikramaḥ
body.translated_text: Above, <s>Govardhanadhara</s> (the upholder of Govardhana); below, <s>Trivikrama</s>

body.text:
etābhyo daśadigbhyas tu
sarvataḥ pātu keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: From these ten directions may <s>Keśava</s> protect on every side

body.text:
aṅguṣṭhāgre tu govindaṃ
tarjanyāṃs tu mahīdharam
body.translated_text: On the tip of the thumb <s>Govinda</s>, on the forefingers <s>Mahīdhara</s> (the upholder of the earth)

body.text:
madhyamāyāṃ hṛṣīkeśam
anāmikyāṃ trivikramam
body.translated_text: On the middle finger <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, on the ring finger <s>Trivikrama</s>

body.text:
kaṇiṣṭhāyāṃ nyased viṣṇuṃ
karamadhye tu mādhavam
body.translated_text: On the little finger one should place <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and in the middle of the hand <s>Mādhava</s>

body.text:
evaṃ nyāsaṃ purā kṛtvā
paścād aṅgeṣu vinyaset
body.translated_text: Having first done this placement, one should afterward place upon the limbs

body.text:
śikhāyāṃ keśavaṃ nyasya
mūrdhni nārāyaṇaṃ nyaset
body.translated_text: Placing <s>Keśava</s> on the crest-lock, one should place <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> on the head

body.text:
cakṣurmadhye nyased viṣṇuṃ
karṇayor madhusūdanam
body.translated_text: One should place <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the middle of the eyes, <s>Madhusūdana</s> in the ears

body.text:
trivikramaṃ kapālasthaṃ
vāmanaṃ karṇamūlayoḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Trivikrama</s> situated on the skull, <s>Vāmana</s> at the roots of the ears

body.text:
dāmodaraṃ dantavaktrau
vārāhaṃ cibuke nyaset
body.translated_text: <s>Dāmodara</s> on the teeth and face, one should place <s>Varāha</s> on the chin

body.text:
uttaroṣṭhe hṛṣīkeśaṃ
padmanābhaṃ tathādhare
body.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> on the upper lip, and likewise <s>Padmanābha</s> on the lower

body.text:
jihvāyāṃ vāsudevaṃ ca
tālvake garuḍadhvajam
body.translated_text: <s>Vāsudeva</s> on the tongue, and on the palate <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> (he whose banner is Garuḍa)

body.text:
vaikuṇṭhaṃ kanṭhamadhyastham
anantaṃ nāsikopari
body.translated_text: <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> situated in the middle of the throat, <s>Ananta</s> upon the nose

body.text:
dakṣiṇe tu bhuje vipra
vinyaset puruṣottamam
body.translated_text: On the right arm, O <s>vipra</s>, one should place <s>Puruṣottama</s>

body.text:
vāmabhuje mahābhāgaṃ
rāghavaṃ hṛdi vinyaset
body.translated_text: On the left arm the greatly fortunate one; one should place <s>Rāghava</s> on the heart

body.text:
pītāmbaraṃ sarvatanau
hariṃ nābhau tu vinyaset
body.translated_text: <s>Pītāmbara</s> (he of the yellow garment) on the whole body, and one should place <s>Hari</s> on the navel

body.text:
kare tu dakṣiṇe vipra
tataḥ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ nyaset
body.translated_text: On the right hand, O <s>vipra</s>, one should then place <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>

body.text:
vāme vipra hariṃ vidyāt
kaṭimadhye 'parājitam
body.translated_text: On the left, O <s>vipra</s>, one should know <s>Hari</s>; in the middle of the waist <s>Aparājita</s>

body.text:
pṛṣṭhe kṣitidharaṃ vidyād
acyutaṃ skandhayor api
body.translated_text: On the back one should know <s>Kṣitidhara</s> (the upholder of the earth), and <s>Acyuta</s> on the shoulders

body.text:
mādhavaṃ bāhu kukṣau tu
dakṣiṇe yogaśāyinam
body.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s> on the arm and belly, on the right <s>Yogaśāyin</s> (he who reclines in yoga)

body.text:
svayaṃbhuvaṃ meḍhramadhye
ūrubhyāṃ tu gadādharam
body.translated_text: <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> in the middle of the genitals, and <s>Gadādhara</s> (the mace-bearer) on the two thighs

body.text:
cakriṇaṃ jānumadhye tu
jaṅghayor acyutaṃ nyaset
body.translated_text: The bearer of the discus in the middle of the knees, one should place <s>Acyuta</s> on the shanks

body.text:
gulpayor narasiṃhaṃ ca
pādapṛṣṭhe 'mitaujasam
body.translated_text: <s>Narasiṃha</s> on the ankles, and <s>Amitaujas</s> (of immeasurable might) on the backs of the feet

body.text:
śrīdharaṃ cāṅgulīṣu syāt
padmākṣaṃ sarvasandhiṣu
body.translated_text: <s>Śrīdhara</s> may be on the toes, <s>Padmākṣa</s> (the lotus-eyed) on all the joints

body.text:
romakūpe guḍākeśaṃ
kṛṣṇaṃ raktāsthimajjāsu
body.translated_text: <s>Guḍākeśa</s> (the lord of sleep) in the hair-pores, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the blood, bones, and marrow

body.text:
manobuddhyor ahaṃkāreṣv
evaṃ citte janārdanam
body.translated_text: in the mind and intellect, in the ego-principles, and thus <s>Janārdana</s> in the heart-mind

body.text:
nakheṣu mādhavaṃ caiva
nyaset pādatale 'cyutam
body.translated_text: and <s>Mādhava</s> on the nails; one should place <s>Acyuta</s> on the soles of the feet

body.text:
evaṃ nyāsavidhiṃ kṛtvā
sākṣān nārāyaṇo bhavet
body.translated_text: Having thus performed the rite of placement, one becomes <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in visible form

body.text:
tanur viṣṇumayī tasya
yāvat kiṃcin na bhāṣate
body.translated_text: His body is made up of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so long as he speaks not at all

body.text:
evaṃ nyāsaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā
yat kāryaṃ śṛṇu tad dvija
body.translated_text: Having thus performed the placement, hear what is then to be done, O twice-born

body.text:
pādamūle tu devasya
śaṅkhaṃ tatraiva vinyaset
body.translated_text: At the root of the feet of the god, one should there place the conch

body.text:
vanamālāṃ tu vinyasya
sarvadevābhipūjitām
body.translated_text: and having placed the forest-garland, worshipped by all the gods,

body.text:
gadāṃ vakṣaḥsthale caiva
cakraṃ caiva tu pṛṣṭhataḥ
body.translated_text: the mace on the surface of the chest, and the discus on the back

body.text:
śrīvatsāṅgaṃ śiro nyasya
pañcāṅgakavacaṃ nyaset
body.translated_text: Having placed the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>-mark on the head, one should place the five-limbed armor

body.text:
āpādāmastake caiva
vinyaset puruṣottamam
body.translated_text: and from the feet to the crown one should place <s>Puruṣottama</s>

body.text:
oṃ apāmārjanako nyāsaḥ
sarvavyādhivināśanaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—this is the placement called the wiper-away, the destroyer of all diseases

body.text:
viṣṇur ūrdhvam adho rakṣed
vaikuṇṭho vidiśo diśaḥ
body.translated_text: May <s>Viṣṇu</s> guard above and below, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> the intermediate quarters and the directions

body.text:
pātu māṃ sarvato rāmo
dhanvī cakrī ca keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: May <s>Rāma</s> guard me on every side, and <s>Keśava</s> bearing bow and discus

body.text:
pūjākāle tu devasya
japakāle tathaiva ca
body.translated_text: At the time of worship of the god, and likewise at the time of recitation,

body.text:
homārambheṣu sarveṣu
trisaṃdhyāsu ca nityaśaḥ
body.translated_text: in all the commencements of oblation, and at the three twilights constantly,

body.text:
āyur ārogyam aiśvaryaṃ
jñānaṃ vittaṃ phalaṃ bhavet
body.translated_text: long life, health, lordship, knowledge, wealth, and reward shall come to be

body.text:
yad yat sukhakaraṃ proktaṃ
tat sarvaṃ prāpnuyān naraḥ
body.translated_text: Whatever has been declared to bring happiness, all that a man shall attain

body.text:
abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo
viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
body.translated_text: fearlessness from all beings, and he goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
atha dhyānaṃ pravakṣyāmi
sarvapāpapraṇāśanam
body.translated_text: Now I shall declare the meditation, the destroyer of all sins

body.text:
vārāharūpiṇaṃ devaṃ
saṃsmaraty aparājitam
body.translated_text: He recalls the god in the form of <s>Varāha</s>, the unconquered,

body.text:
bṛhattanuṃ bṛhadgātraṃ
bṛhaddaṃṣṭrasuśobhanam
body.translated_text: of huge body, of huge frame, beautiful with huge tusks,

body.text:
samastavedavedāṅgaṃ
yuktāṅgaṃ bhūṣaṇair yutam
body.translated_text: embodying all the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, with well-formed limbs, endowed with ornaments,

body.text:
uddhṛtya bhūmiṃ pātālād
hastābhyām upagṛhṇatām
body.translated_text: having lifted up the earth from the nether world, holding it up with his two arms,

body.text:
āliṅgya bhūmiṃ śirasi
mūrdhni jighrantam āsthitam
body.translated_text: embracing the earth, standing, smelling it upon his head, upon the crown,

body.text:
ratnavaiḍūryamukhyābhir
muktābhir upaśobhitam
body.translated_text: adorned with chief gems, lapis-lazuli, and pearls,

body.text:
pītāmbaradharaṃ devaṃ
śuklamālyānulepanam
body.translated_text: the god wearing a yellow garment, with white garlands and unguents,

body.text:
trayastriṃśakoṭidevaiḥ
stūyamānaṃ mudāniśam
body.translated_text: being praised by the thirty-three crore gods with joy day and night,

body.text:
nṛtyadbhir apsarobhiś ca
gīyamānaṃ ca kinnaraiḥ
body.translated_text: and with dancing <s>apsarases</s>, and being sung to by <s>kinnaras</s>

body.text:
itthaṃ dhyātvā mahātmānaṃ
japen nityaṃ mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Having thus meditated upon the great soul, one should recite ever to the great soul

body.text:
suvarṇamaṇḍapāntasthaṃ
padmaṃ dhyāyet sakesaram
body.translated_text: One should meditate upon a lotus, situated within a golden pavilion, together with its filaments,

body.text:
sakarṇikadalair iṣṭair
aṣṭabhiḥ pariśobhitam
body.translated_text: adorned with eight beloved petals provided with a pericarp

body.text:
karaṃ karahitaṃ devaṃ
pūrṇacandrāptasuprabham
body.translated_text: the god with hand and without hand [unmanifest], of fair luster like the full moon,

body.text:
taḍitsamaśaṭāśobhi
kaṇṭhanālopaśobhitam
body.translated_text: shining with a mane equal to lightning, beautified by the column of his neck,

body.text:
śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣaḥsthaṃ
tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraṃ trilocanam
body.translated_text: with chest marked by the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, with sharp tusks, three-eyed,

body.text:
javākusumasaṃkāśaṃ
raktahastatalānvitam
body.translated_text: resembling the <s>javā</s>-flower, possessing red palms,

body.text:
pītavastraparīdhānaṃ
śuklayastrottarīyakam
body.translated_text: wearing a yellow lower garment, with a white upper garment,

body.text:
karaṃ karahitaṃ devaṃ
pūrṇacandrāptasuprabham
body.translated_text: the god with hand and without hand, of fair luster like the full moon,

body.text:
kaṭisūtreṇa haimena
nūpureṇa virājitam
body.translated_text: resplendent with a golden waist-girdle and anklets,

body.text:
vanamālādiśobhāḍhyaṃ
muktāhāropaśobhitam
body.translated_text: rich with the splendor of forest-garlands and the rest, beautified by a pearl-necklace,

body.text:
anekasūryasaṃkāśaṃ
mukuṭāṭopamastakam
body.translated_text: resembling many suns, his head crowned with the mass of a diadem,

body.text:
śaṅkhacakragṛhītābhyām
udbāhubhyāṃ virājitam
body.translated_text: resplendent with uplifted arms grasping the conch and discus,

body.text:
paṅkajābhaṃ caturhastaṃ
tatpatrābhasulocanam
body.translated_text: lotus-hued, four-handed, with lovely eyes resembling its petals,

body.text:
prātaḥ sūryasamaprakhya-
kuṇḍalābhyāṃ virājitam
body.translated_text: resplendent with two earrings equal to the morning sun,

body.text:
keyūrakāntisasyarddhi-
muktikāratnaśobhitam
body.translated_text: beautified with the splendor of armlets and pearls and gems,

body.text:
jānūparinyastahastaṃ
vararatnanakhāṅkuram
body.translated_text: with a hand laid upon the knee, with sprout-like nails of choice gems,

body.text:
jaṅghābharaṇasasyarddhi-
visphuryatkaṅkanatviṣam
body.translated_text: with the gleam of quivering bracelets rich with the splendor of shank-ornaments,

body.text:
muktāphalābdasamahad-
dantapaṅktivirājitam
body.translated_text: resplendent with a row of teeth great as the mass of pearls,

body.text:
campakāmukulaprakhya-
sunāsāmukhapaṅkajam
body.translated_text: with a lotus-face and fine nose resembling the bud of the <s>campaka</s>,

body.text:
atiraktauṣṭhavadanaṃ
vyāttāsyam atibhīṣaṇam
body.translated_text: with a face whose lips are very red, with gaping mouth, most terrible,

body.text:
vāmāṅkasthaṃ śivabhakta-
śāntidāṃ sunitambinīm
body.translated_text: having upon his left side the giver of peace to the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, of fair hips,

body.text:
arhaṇīyāṃ sujātoruṃ
sunāsāṃ śubhalakṣaṇām
body.translated_text: worthy of worship, of well-formed thighs, of fine nose, of auspicious marks,

body.text:
subhrūṃ sukeśīṃ suśroṇīṃ
suśubhāṃ sudvijānanām
body.translated_text: of fine brows, fine hair, fine hips, most lovely, of fine teeth and face,

body.text:
supratiṣṭhāṃ suvadanāṃ
caturhastāṃ vicintayet
body.translated_text: well-established, of fair countenance, four-handed—one should contemplate her

body.text:
dukūle caiva cārvaṅgīṃ
hāriṇīṃ sarvakāmadām
body.translated_text: with a silken garment, of lovely limbs, captivating, granting all desires,

body.text:
taptakañcanasaṃkāśāṃ
sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām
body.translated_text: resembling heated gold, adorned with all ornaments,

body.text:
suvarṇakalaśaprakhya-
pīnonnatapayodharām
body.translated_text: with full and lofty breasts resembling a golden pitcher,

body.text:
gṛhītapadmayugalaṃ
udbāhubhyāṃ tathānyayoḥ
body.translated_text: grasping a pair of lotuses with two uplifted arms, and in the other two

body.text:
gṛhītamātulaṅgākhyaṃ
jāmbunadakarān tathā
body.translated_text: grasping what is called the citron-fruit, and golden vessels likewise

body.text:
evaṃ devīṃ nṛsiṃhasya
vāmāṅkopari saṃsmaret
body.translated_text: Thus one should recall the goddess upon the left side of <s>Narasiṃha</s>

body.text: ativimalasugātraṃ raupyapātrastham annaṃ
body.translated_text: of most spotless and fair body, with food set in a silver vessel,

body.text: sulalitadadhikhaṇḍaṃ pāṇinā dakṣiṇena
body.translated_text: with a most charming lump of curds in the right hand,

body.text: kalaśam amṛtapūrṇaṃ savyahaste dadhānaṃ
body.translated_text: holding in the left hand a pitcher filled with nectar,

body.text: tadatisakaladuḥkhaṃ vāmanaṃ bhāvayed yaḥ
body.translated_text: he who should contemplate that <s>Vāmana</s>, the remover of all sorrow,

body.text: anyā bhāskarasaprabhābhir akhilair bhābhir diśo bhāsayan
body.translated_text: another, illumining the directions with all his rays of light equal in splendor to the sun,

body.text: bhīmākṣasphuradaṭṭahāsavilasāddaṃṣṭrāgradīptānanaḥ
body.translated_text: with face blazing with the tips of his tusks shining amid the loud laughter that gleams from his terrible eyes,

body.text: dorbhiś cakradharau gadābjamukulau trāsāṃś ca pāśāṅkuśau
body.translated_text: bearing in his arms the discus and the buds of the mace and lotus, and the terrors—the noose and goad,

body.text: bibhratpiṅgaśiro 'ruhoddhatasaṭaś cakravidhāno hariḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, bearing tawny head-hair with bristling mane, in the manner of the discus

body.text:
manobhūtānīndriyāṇi
guṇāḥ sattvaṃ rajas tamaḥ
body.translated_text: Mind, the elements, the senses, the qualities, <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>,

body.text:
trailokyasyeśvaraṃ sarvam
ahaṃkāre pratiṣṭhitāḥ
body.translated_text: all are established in the ego-principle, [under] the Lord of the three worlds

body.text:
oṃ namaḥ paramārthāya
puruṣāya mahātmane
arūpabahurūpāya
vyāpine paramātmane
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the supreme reality, to the <s>Puruṣa</s>, to the great soul, to the formless one of many forms, to the all-pervading, to the supreme self

body.text:
namas te devadevāya
suraśūra namo 'stu te
lokādhyakṣa jagatpūjya
paramātman namas te (!)
body.translated_text: Homage to you, god of gods; homage be to you, hero among gods; O overseer of the world, worshipped by the universe, supreme self, homage to you

body.text:
niṣkalmaṣāya śuddhāya
sarvapāpaharāya ca
body.translated_text: to the stainless, to the pure, and to the remover of all sins

body.text:
namaskṛtvā pravakṣyāmi
yat tat sidhyatu me vacaḥ
body.translated_text: Having paid homage, I shall declare—may that my speech be effective

body.text:
varāhanarasiṃhāya
vāmanāya mahātmane
body.translated_text: to <s>Varāha</s>, to <s>Narasiṃha</s>, to <s>Vāmana</s>, to the great soul,

body.text:
govindapadmanābhāya
vāmadevāya bhūpate
body.translated_text: to <s>Govinda</s>, to <s>Padmanābha</s>, to <s>Vāmadeva</s>, O lord of the earth,

body.text:
nārāyaṇāya devāya
anantāya mahātmane
body.translated_text: to the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, to <s>Ananta</s>, to the great soul,

body.text:
garuḍadhvajāya kṛṣṇāya
pītāmbaradharāya ca
body.translated_text: to <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s>, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and to <s>Pītāmbara</s> (he of the yellow garment),

body.text:
yogīśvarāya siddhāya
guhyāya paramātmane
body.translated_text: to the lord of yogis, to the perfected one, to the secret one, to the supreme self,

body.text:
janārdanāya kṛṣṇāya
upendraśrīdharāya ca
body.translated_text: to <s>Janārdana</s>, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and to <s>Upendra</s> and <s>Śrīdhara</s>,

body.text:
bhaktapriyāya vidhaye
viṣvaksenāya śārṅgine
body.translated_text: to the lover of devotees, to the ordainer, to <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, to the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow,

body.text:
hiraṇyagarbhapataye
hiraṇyakaśipucchide
body.translated_text: to the lord of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, to the slayer of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,

body.text:
cakrahastāya śūlāya
tarjanyapatrāya dhīmate
body.translated_text: to the discus-handed, to the wise one with the spear and the forefinger-blade,

body.text:
ādityāya upendrāya
bhūtānāṃ jīvanāya ca
body.translated_text: to <s>Āditya</s>, to <s>Upendra</s>, and to the life of beings,

body.text:
vāsudevāya vandyāya
varadāya mahātmane
body.translated_text: to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, to the venerable, to the boon-giver, to the great soul,

body.text:
viṣūvṛcchravase tasmai
kṣīrāmbunichiśāyine
body.translated_text: to him of far-reaching renown, to him who reclines on the milk-ocean's waters,

body.text:
adhokṣajāya bhadrāya
śrīdharāyādimūrtaye
body.translated_text: to <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, to the auspicious, to <s>Śrīdhara</s>, to the primordial form,

body.text:
viśveśadvāramūrtiś ca
mṛtyurāyohito 'sti saḥ
body.translated_text: and the form of the door of the Lord of the universe—he is appointed against death

body.text:
nānārāgāṃś ca dakṣāṃś ca
vikaṭāya mahābhītī
body.translated_text: [him of] various passions and the skilled and dreadful ones, to the formidable, to the greatly fearsome,

body.text:
jātupatiṃ vyagrahastaṃ
vararatnanakhākaram
body.translated_text: the lord of birth, with active hand, with sprout-like nails of choice gems,

body.text:
nārāyaṇāya viśvāya
viśveśāyāmbarāya ca
body.translated_text: to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, to the universe, to the Lord of the universe, to the all-encompassing,

body.text:
dāmodarāya devāya
anantāya mahātmane
body.translated_text: to the god <s>Dāmodara</s>, to <s>Ananta</s>, to the great soul,

body.text:
trivikramāya rāmāya
vaikuṇṭhāya narāya ca
body.translated_text: to <s>Trivikrama</s>, to <s>Rāma</s>, to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, and to <s>Nara</s>,

body.text:
namaskṛtvā pravakṣyāmi
yat tat sidhyatu me vacaḥ
body.translated_text: Having paid homage, I shall declare—may that my speech be effective

body.text:
varāhanarasiṃheśa
vāmaneśa trivikrama
hayagrīveśa sarveśa
hṛṣīkeśa harāśubham
body.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Varāha</s> and <s>Narasiṃha</s>, O Lord of <s>Vāmana</s>, O <s>Trivikrama</s>, O Lord of <s>Hayagrīva</s>, O Lord of all, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, remove all that is inauspicious

body.text:
aparājitacakrādyaiś
caturbhiḥ paramāyudhaiḥ
akhaṇḍitaprabhāvais tvaṃ
sarvaduṣṭaharo bhava
body.translated_text: With the four supreme weapons beginning with the unconquered discus, of undivided power, may you be the remover of all the wicked

body.text:
harāmukasya duritaṃ
duṣkṛtaṃ durupoṣitam
mṛtyubandhārtibhayadaṃ
duriṣṭasya ca yat phalam
body.translated_text: Remove the evil, the misdeed, the ill-fasting of this man, that which brings the fear of death, bondage, and affliction, and whatever is the fruit of his ill-performed rite

body.text:
parāpadhyānasahitaṃ
prayuktaṃ cābhicāruka
garasparśamahāyoga-
prayogajarayājara
body.translated_text: joined with the meditation of others on his harm, and the witchcraft directed [against him], O conqueror of the sorcery of poison-touch and great magical operations, O ageless one

body.text:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya
namaḥ kṣṛṇāya śārṅgiṇe
namaḥ puṣkaranetrāya
keśavāyādicakriṇe
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, homage to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, homage to the lotus-eyed, to <s>Keśava</s>, the primordial discus-bearer

body.text:
namaḥ kamalakiñjalka-
pītanirmalavāsase
mahāhavaripuskandha-
ghṛṣṭacakrāya cakriṇe
body.translated_text: Homage to him of pure yellow raiment like the filaments of the lotus, to the discus-bearer whose discus has been ground against the shoulders of foes in great battle

body.text:
daṃṣṭroddhṛtakṣitidhṛte
trayīmūrtimate namaḥ
mahāyajñavarāhāya
śeṣabhogoruśāyine
