body.translated_text: Homage to him who upheld the earth raised on his tusk, who has the form of the threefold <s>Veda</s>, to the great-sacrifice <s>Varāha</s>, who reclines broadly on the coils of <s>Śeṣa</s>

body.text:
taptahāṭakakeśānta
jvalatpāvakalocana
vajrādhikanakhasparśa
divyasiṃha namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: O you whose hair-ends are like molten gold, whose eyes are blazing fire, whose nail-touch surpasses the thunderbolt, divine lion, homage be to you

body.text:
kapila hemāśvaśīrṣa
atiriktavilocana
vidyutsphuritadaṃṣṭrāgra
divyasiṃha namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: O tawny one, golden horse-headed, with eyes exceedingly wide, with tusk-tips flashing like lightning, divine lion, homage be to you

body.text:
kāśyapāyātihrasvāya
ṛgyajuḥsāmabhūṣita
tubhyaṃ vāmanarūpāya
sṛjate gāṃ namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: To the son of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, exceedingly short, adorned with the <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, to you in the form of <s>Vāmana</s>, who creates the earth, homage upon homage

body.text:
varāhāśeṣaduṣṭāni
sarvapāpaharāṇi vai
marda marda mahādaṃṣṭra
marda marda ca tatphalam
body.translated_text: O <s>Varāha</s>, [removing] all wicked things and removing all sins, crush, crush, O great-tusked one, crush, crush also their fruit

body.text:
narasiṃha karālāsya
dantaprāntānalojjvala
bhañja bhañja ninādena
duṣṭāny asyārtināśana
body.translated_text: O <s>Narasiṃha</s>, of gaping mouth, blazing with the fire at the edges of your teeth, break, break with your roar the wicked things of this man, O destroyer of affliction

body.text:
ṛgyajuḥsāmagarbhābhir
vāgbhir vāmanarūpadhṛk
praśamaṃ sarvaduḥkhāni
nayatv asya janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: With words pregnant with the <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, bearing the form of <s>Vāmana</s>, may <s>Janārdana</s> lead all the sorrows of this man to appeasement

body.text:
ekāhikaṃ dvyāhikaṃ ca
tathā tridivasaṃ jvaram
cāturthakaṃ tathātyugraṃ
tathaiva satatajvaram
body.translated_text: the one-day fever and the two-day, likewise the three-day fever, the quartan and likewise the most fierce, and the constant fever,

body.text:
doṣotthaṃ saṃnipātotthaṃ
tathaivāgantukaṃ jvaram
śamaṃ nayāśu govinda
chittvā cchittvā tu vedanām
body.translated_text: the fever arising from the humors, arising from their conjunction, and likewise the adventitious fever—quickly lead to appeasement, O <s>Govinda</s>, cutting, cutting away the pain

body.text:
netraduḥkhaṃ śiroduḥkhaṃ
duḥkhaṃ codarasaṃbhavam
anucchvāsam atiśvāsaṃ
paritāpaṃ savepathuṃ
body.translated_text: eye-pain, head-pain, pain arising in the belly, the absence of breath and excess of breath, the burning, with trembling,

body.text:
gudaghrāṇāṃhrirogāṃś ca
kuṣṭharogaṃ tathā kṣayam
kāmalādīṃs tathā rogān
pramehāṃś cātidāruṇān
body.translated_text: diseases of the anus, nose, and feet, and leprosy, likewise consumption, jaundice and other diseases, and the most terrible urinary disorders,

body.text:
bhagaṃdarātisārāṃś ca
mukharogaṃ savalgulim
aśmarīmūtrakṛcchrāṃś ca
rogān anyāṃś ca dāruṇān
body.translated_text: fistula and dysentery, mouth-disease with swelling, and stones, and difficult urination, and other terrible diseases,

body.text:
ye vātaprabhavā rogā
ye ca pittasamudbhavāḥ
kaphodbhavāś ca ye kecid
ye cānye sāṃnipātikāḥ
body.translated_text: those diseases which arise from wind, and those which arise from bile, and whichever arise from phlegm, and the others arising from their conjunction,

body.text:
āgantavaś ca ye rogā
lūtāvisphoṭakādayaḥ
te sarve praśamaṃ yāntu
vāsudevāpamārjitāḥ
body.translated_text: and the adventitious diseases—spider-poison, eruptions, and the rest—may they all come to appeasement, wiped away by <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
vilayaṃ yāntu te sarve
viṣṇor uccāraṇena ca
kṣayaṃ gacchantu cāśeṣās
te cakrābhihatā hareḥ
body.translated_text: May they all come to dissolution by the utterance of [the name of] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and may they all come to destruction, struck by the discus of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
acyutānantagovinda-
nāmoccāraṇabhīṣitāḥ
naśyantu sakalā rogāḥ
satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmy aham
body.translated_text: Terrified by the utterance of the names <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and <s>Govinda</s>, may all diseases perish—truly, truly I speak

body.text:
sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ vāpi
kṛtrimaṃ vāpi yad viṣam
dantodbhavaṃ nakhabhavam
ākāśaprabhavaṃ viṣam
body.translated_text: whether stationary or moving, or artificial, whatever poison there be, poison arising from teeth, arising from nails, poison arising from the sky,

body.text:
lūtādiprabhavaṃ yac ca
viṣam atyantaduḥkhadam
śamaṃ nayatu tat sarvaṃ
kīrtito 'sya janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: and that poison which arises from spiders and the like, the giver of utmost suffering—may <s>Janārdana</s>, being praised, lead all that to appeasement

body.text:
grahān pretagrahāṃś caiva
tathā vai ḍākinīgrahān
vetālāṃś ca piśācāṃś ca
gandharvān yakṣarākṣasān
body.translated_text: the seizing demons (<s>grahas</s>) and the ghost-demons (<s>preta-grahas</s>), and likewise the <s>ḍākinī</s>-demons, the <s>vetālas</s> and the <s>piśācas</s>, the <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>,

body.text:
śakunīpūtanādyāṃś ca
tathā vaināyakagrahān
mukhamaṇḍinikāṃ krūrāṃ
revatīṃ vṛddharevatīm
body.translated_text: and <s>Śakunī</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, and the rest, and likewise the <s>Vināyaka</s>-demons, the cruel <s>Mukhamaṇḍinikā</s>, <s>Revatī</s> and <s>Vṛddharevatī</s>,

body.text:
vṛddhikākhyān grahāṃś cogrāṃs
tathā mātṛgrahān api
bālasya viṣṇoḥ caritaṃ
hantu bālagrahān imān
body.translated_text: and the fierce demons called <s>Vṛddhikā</s>, and also the Mother-demons (<s>mātṛ-grahas</s>)—may the deeds of the child <s>Viṣṇu</s> destroy these child-seizing demons (<s>bāla-grahas</s>)

body.text:
vṛddhānāṃ ye grahāḥ kecid
ye ca bālagrahāḥ kvacit
narasiṃhasya te dṛṣṭyā
dagdhā ye cāpi yauvane
body.translated_text: Whatever demons there are of the aged, and whatever child-demons there are anywhere, they are burned by the gaze of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, and those too that strike in youth

body.text:
saṭākarālavadano
narasiṃho mahāravaḥ
grahān aśeṣān niḥśeṣān
karotu jagato hitam
body.translated_text: <s>Narasiṃha</s>, with mane and terrible face and a great roar—may he make all the demons utterly without remainder, for the welfare of the world

body.text:
narasiṃha mahāsiṃha
jvālāmālojjvalānana
grahān aśeṣān sarveśa
khāda khādāgnilocana
body.translated_text: O <s>Narasiṃha</s>, great lion, you of face blazing with a garland of flames, devour, devour all the demons, O Lord of all, O you with eyes of fire

body.text:
ye rogā ye mahotpātā
yad viṣaṃ ye mahāgrahāḥ
yāni ca krūrabhūtāni
grahapīḍāś ca dāruṇāḥ
śastrakṣateṣu ye doṣā
jvālāgardabhakādayaḥ
body.translated_text: Whatever diseases there are, whatever great portents, whatever poison, whatever great demons, and whatever cruel beings, and the terrible afflictions of demons, the defects in wounds of weapons, the blazing-ass (<s>jvālāgardabha</s>) and the rest,

body.text:
yāni cāryāṇi bhūtāni
prāṇipīḍākarāṇi vai
body.translated_text: and whatever other beings there are that cause torment to living creatures—

body.text:
tāni sarvāṇi sarvātman
paramātmañ janārdana
kiṃcid rūpaṃ samāsthāya
vāsudeva vināśaya
body.translated_text: all those, O Self of all, O Supreme Self, <s>Janārdana</s>, assuming some form, O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, destroy

body.text:
kṣiptvā sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ
jvālāmālāvibhīṣaṇam
sarvaduṣṭopaśamanaṃ
kuru devavarācyuta
body.translated_text: Having hurled the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus, terrible with its garland of flames, the calmer of all that is wicked—do that, O best of gods, O <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
sudarśana mahācakra
govindasya karāyudha
body.translated_text: O <s>Sudarśana</s>, great discus, hand-weapon of <s>Govinda</s>,

body.text:
jvalatpāvakasaṃkāśa
sūryakoṭisamaprabha
body.translated_text: you who resemble blazing fire, of splendor equal to ten million suns,

body.text:
trailokyarakṣakartṛ tvaṃ
tvaṃ duṣṭadānavadāraṇa
body.translated_text: you are the protector of the three worlds, you are the render of the wicked <s>dānavas</s>,

body.text:
tīkṣṇadhāra mahāvega
chindhi cchindhi mahājvaram
body.translated_text: you of sharp edge and great speed, cut, cut the great fever,

body.text:
chindhi cchindhi mahāvyādhiṃ
chindhi cchindhi mahāgrahān
body.translated_text: cut, cut the great sickness, cut, cut the great demons,

body.text:
chindhi vātaṃ ca dhūtaṃ ca
chindhi ghoraṃ mahāviṣam
body.translated_text: cut the wind-disorder and the shaking (palsy), cut the dreadful great poison,

body.text:
rujadāghaṃ ca śūlaṃ ca
nimiṣajvālagardabham
body.translated_text: the burning ache and the colic, the <s>nimiṣa</s> and the blazing-ass (<s>jvālāgardabha</s>),

body.text:
sudarśana mahājvāla
chindhi cchindhi mamārayaḥ
sarvaduṣṭāni rakṣāṃsi
kṣapayātivibhīṣaṇa
body.translated_text: O <s>Sudarśana</s>, great flame, cut, cut my enemies; destroy all the wicked <s>rākṣasas</s>, O you exceedingly terrible

body.text:
hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭkāreṇa
ṭhadvayena hatadviṣaḥ
body.translated_text: With the cry 'hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ', with the double 'ṭha', the foes are slain;

body.text:
sudarśanasya mantreṇa
grahā yānti diśo diśaḥ
body.translated_text: by the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Sudarśana</s> the demons flee in every direction

body.text:
trailokyasyābhayaṃ kartum
ājñāpaya janārdana
body.translated_text: To make safety for the three worlds, give the command, O <s>Janārdana</s>;

body.text:
sarvaduṣṭāni rakṣāṃsi
kṣayaṃ yānti vibhīṣayā
body.translated_text: all the wicked <s>rākṣasas</s> go to destruction by the terror [of you]

body.text:
prācyāṃ pratīcyāṃ ca diśi
dakṣiṇottaratas tathā
rakṣāṃ karotu sarvātmā
narasiṃhaḥ svagarjitaiḥ
body.translated_text: In the eastern and the western direction, and likewise in the south and north, may the Self of all, <s>Narasiṃha</s>, make protection with his own roars

body.text:
bhūmyantarikṣe ca tathā
pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvato 'grataḥ
body.translated_text: and on the earth and in the atmosphere likewise, behind, at the side, in front,

body.text:
vyāghrasiṃhavarāheṣu
andicorabhayeṣu ca (?)
body.translated_text: in [the perils of] tigers, lions, and boars, and in fears of darkness(?) and thieves,

body.text:
rakṣāṃ karotu bhagavān
bahurūpī janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: may the Blessed <s>Janārdana</s> of many forms make protection

body.text:
yathā viṣṇuṛ jagat sarvaṃ
sadevāsuramānavam
tena satyena duṣṭāni
śamam asya vrajantu vai
body.translated_text: As <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the whole world with its gods, <s>asuras</s>, and men—by that truth may the wicked things of this one indeed come to calm

body.text:
yathā viṣṇau smṛte samyak
saṃkṣayaṃ yāti pātakam
satyena tena sakalaṃ
duṣṭam asya praśāmyatu
body.translated_text: As, when <s>Viṣṇu</s> is rightly remembered, sin goes to destruction—by that truth may all that is wicked in this one be calmed

body.text:
paramātmā yathā viṣṇur
vedānteṣv abhidhīyate
tena satyena sakalaṃ
duṣṭam asya praśāmyatu
body.translated_text: As <s>Viṣṇu</s> is declared in the <s>Vedāntas</s> to be the Supreme Self—by that truth may all that is wicked in this one be calmed

body.text:
yathā yajñeṣvaro viṣṇur
vedeṣv api tu gīyate
tena satyena sakalaṃ
yan mayoktaṃ tathāstu tat
body.translated_text: As <s>Viṣṇu</s> is sung in the sacrifices and in the <s>Vedas</s> too as the lord—by that truth, may all that I have spoken come to be so

body.text:
yathā yajñeśvaro viṣṇur
yajñānte api gīyate
tena satyena sakalaṃ
yan mayoktaṃ tathāstu tat
body.translated_text: As <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of sacrifices, is sung also at the end of sacrifices—by that truth, may all that I have spoken come to be so

body.text:
śāntir astu śivaṃ cāstu
praśāmyatv asukhaṃ ca yat
vāsudevaśarīrotthaiḥ
kuśair nirmārjitaṃ mayā
body.translated_text: May there be peace, and may there be welfare, and may the misery that there is be calmed; by me he has been swept clean with <s>kuśa</s>-grasses sprung from the body of <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
apāmārjati govindo
naro nārāyaṇas tathā
tavāstu sarvaduḥkhānāṃ
praśamo vacanād dhareḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> sweeps away [evil], and likewise <s>Nara-Nārāyaṇa</s>; by the word of <s>Hari</s> may there be for you the calming of all sorrows

body.text:
idaṃ śāstraṃ paṭhed yas tu
saptāhan niyataḥ śuciḥ
body.translated_text: And whoever reads this treatise for seven days, restrained and pure,

body.text:
śāntiṃ samastarogās te
grahāḥ sarve viṣāni ca
bhūtāni ca prayāntv īśe
saṃsmṛte madhusūdane
body.translated_text: his diseases all, those demons all, and the poisons, and the [evil] beings, may they go to calm, when the Lord <s>Madhusūdana</s> is remembered

body.text:
etat samastarogeṣu
bhūtagrahabhayeṣu ca
apamārjanakaṃ śastaṃ
viṣṇunāmābhimantritam
body.translated_text: This sweeping-clean (<s>apāmārjana</s>), consecrated by the name of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is commended in all diseases and in the fears of beings and demons

body.text:
ete kuśā viṣṇuśarīrasaṃbhavā
janārdano 'haṃ svayaṃ eva cāgataḥ
hataṃ mayā duṣṭam aśeṣam asya
svastho bhavaty eṣa vaco yathā hareḥ
body.translated_text: 'These <s>kuśa</s>-grasses are sprung from the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I, <s>Janārdana</s> himself, have come in person; by me all that is wicked in this one has been slain without remainder; this one becomes well'—so [runs] the word of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
śāntir astu śivaṃ cāstu
duṣṭam asya praśāmyatu
yad asya duritaṃ kiṃcit
tat kṣiptaṃ lavaṇārṇave
body.translated_text: May there be peace, and may there be welfare; may the wickedness in this one be calmed; whatever little evil there is of this one, that is cast into the salt ocean

body.text:
svāsthyam asya sadaivāstu
hṛṣīkeśasya kīrtanāt
yata evāgataṃ pāpaṃ
tatraiva pratigacchatu
body.translated_text: May there ever be well-being for him from the proclaiming of <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>; from wherever the sin has come, may it go back there itself

body.text:
etad rogādipīḍāsu
jantūnāṃ hitam icchatā
viṣṇubhaktena kartavyam
apamārjanakaṃ param
body.translated_text: This supreme sweeping-clean is to be performed by the devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> who desires the welfare of creatures in their afflictions of disease and the rest

body.text:
anena sarvaduṣṭāni
praśamaṃ yānty asaṃśayam
sarvabhūtahitārthāya
kuryāt tasmāt sadaiva hi
body.translated_text: By this all wicked things go to calm, without doubt; therefore one should ever perform it, for the welfare of all beings

body.text:
sarvāparādhaśamanam
apāmārjanakaṃ param
body.translated_text: The supreme sweeping-clean, the calmer of all offenses,

body.text:
etat stotram idaṃ puṇyaṃ
paṭhed āyuṣyavardhanam
body.translated_text: this holy hymn, one should read—the augmenter of life,

body.text:
vināśāya ca rogāṇām
avamṛtyukṣayāya ca
body.translated_text: for the destruction of diseases, and for the averting of untimely death

body.text:
vyāghrāpasmārakuṣṭhādi
piśācoragarākṣasāḥ
body.translated_text: Tigers, epilepsy, leprosy, and the rest, <s>piśācas</s>, serpents, and <s>rākṣasas</s>,

body.text:
tasya pārśvaṃ na gacchanti
stotram etad yathā paṭhet
body.translated_text: do not go near his side, who reads this hymn as enjoined

body.text:
smarañ japann idaṃ stotraṃ
sarvavyādhivināśanam
body.translated_text: Remembering and muttering this hymn, which destroys all diseases,

body.text:
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ nityaṃ
viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati
body.translated_text: of those who read and hear it daily, he goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
surūpatā manuṣyāṇāṃ
strīṇāṃ ca dvijasattama
karmaṇā jāyate yena
tan mamākhyātum arhasi
body.translated_text: The fairness of form of men and of women, O best of the twice-born, by what action it arises—that you ought to tell me

body.text:
surūpāṇāṃ sugātrāṇāṃ
suveṣāṇāṃ tathā mune
nyūnaṃ tathādhikaṃ vāpi
kiṃcid aṅgaṃ prajāyate
body.translated_text: Among the fair-formed, the fair-limbed, and likewise the well-dressed, O sage, some limb is born too small or too large

body.text:
samastaiḥ śobhanair aṅgair
narāḥ kecit tathā dvija
kāṇāḥ kubjāś ca jāyante
truṭitaśravaṇās tathā
body.translated_text: Some men, O twice-born, though with all their limbs handsome, are born one-eyed and hunchbacked, and likewise with severed hearing (deaf)

body.text:
narāṇāṃ yoṣitāṃ caiva
samastāṅgsurūpatā
karmaṇā yena bhavati
tat sarvaṃ kathayāmala
body.translated_text: By what action complete beauty of all the limbs arises for men and for women—all that tell, O stainless one

body.text:
lāvaṇyagativākyāni
sati rūpe mahāmate
prayānti cārutāṃ rūpaṃ
tenoktaḥ paramo guṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Loveliness, gait, and speech, when form is present, O greatly wise one, attain to charm; for that reason form is called the supreme quality

body.text:
vākyalāvaṇyasaṃskāra-
vilāsalalitā gatiḥ
viḍambanā kurūpāṇāṃ
strīpuṃsām abhijāyate
body.translated_text: Speech, loveliness, refinement, grace, and elegant gait become a mockery for ugly women and men

body.text:
rūpakāraṇabhūtāya
yateta matimāṃs tataḥ
karmaṇā tan mamācakṣva
karma yac cārurūpadam
body.translated_text: Therefore the wise man should strive for that which is the cause of beauty; tell me by what action that comes about, the action that gives charming form

body.text:
samyak pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā hīdam
upavāsāśritaṃ dvija
kathayāmi yathā proktaṃ
vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
body.translated_text: Rightly indeed has this, resting upon fasting, been asked by you, O twice-born; I shall tell it as it was declared by the great soul <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>

body.text:
vasiṣṭham ṛṣim āsīnaṃ
saptarṣipravaraṃ patim
papracchārundhatī praśnaṃ
yad etad bhavatā vayam
body.translated_text: <s>Arundhatī</s> asked her husband, the seer <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, foremost of the seven seers, as he was seated, this very question which we have [received] from you

body.text:
tasyāḥ sa paripṛcchantyā
jagāda munisattamaḥ
yat tac chṛṇuṣva dharmajña
mameha vadato 'khilam
body.translated_text: To her as she inquired, that best of sages spoke; hear that, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, as I tell it all here

body.text:
śrūyatāṃ mama yat pṛṣṭas
tvayāhaṃ brahmavādini
surūpatā nṛṇāṃ yena
yoṣitāṃ copajāyate
body.translated_text: Let it be heard by me as I was asked by you, O expounder of <s>Brahman</s>, that by which the fairness of form of men and of women arises

body.text:
anabhyarcya yathānyāyam
anārādhya ca keśavam
rūpādikā guṇāḥ kena
prāpyante 'nyena karmaṇā
body.translated_text: Without worshipping <s>Keśava</s> according to rule and without propitiating him, by what other action are qualities such as beauty obtained?

body.text:
tasmād ārādhanīyo vai
viṣṇur eva yaśasvini
paratra prāptukāmena
rūpasaṃpatsutādikam
body.translated_text: Therefore <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is indeed to be worshipped, O illustrious one, by one who desires in the next world an abundance of beauty, sons, and the rest

body.text:
yas tu vāñchati dharmajñe
rūpaṃ sarvāṅgaśobhanam
nakṣatrapuruṣas tena
saṃpūjyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
body.translated_text: But he who, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, desires a form handsome in all its limbs—by him the <s>Nakṣatra-puruṣa</s>, the Supreme Person, is to be worshipped

body.text:
nakṣatrāṅgaṃ yathāhāraḥ
samupoṣyati yo harim
surūpair akhilāṅgaiś ca
rūpavān abhijāyate
body.translated_text: He who fasts upon the limb of the lunar mansion (<s>nakṣatra</s>) as the food, worshipping <s>Hari</s>, is born possessing form with all limbs fair

body.text:
yoṣitā ca paraṃ rūpam
icchantyā jagataḥ patiḥ
sa evārādhanīyo 'tra
nakṣatrāṅgo janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: And by a woman desiring supreme form, that very Lord of the world, the <s>Nakṣatra-puruṣa</s> <s>Janārdana</s>, is here to be worshipped

body.text:
nakṣatrarūpī bhagavān
pūjyate puruṣottamaḥ
mune yena vidhānena
tan mamākhyātum arhasi
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s> in the form of the lunar mansions is worshipped; by what procedure, O sage, that you ought to tell me

body.text:
caitramāsaṃ samārabhya
viṣṇoḥ pādādipūjanam
yathā kurvīta rūpārthī
tan niśāmaya tattvataḥ
body.translated_text: Beginning with the month of <s>Caitra</s>, how one desiring beauty should perform the worship of the feet and the rest of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—hear that truly

body.text:
nakṣatram ekam ekaṃ vai
snātaḥ samyag upoṣitaḥ
nakṣatrapuruṣasyāṅgaṃ
pūjayet sādhvī cakriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Mansion by mansion, bathed and properly fasting, a virtuous person should worship a limb of the discus-bearer as the <s>Nakṣatra-puruṣa</s>

body.text:
mūle pādau tathā jaṅghe
rohiṇīṣv arcayec chubhe
jānunī cāśvinīyoga
āṣāḍhe corusaṃjñite
body.translated_text: Under <s>Mūla</s> the two feet, likewise under <s>Rohiṇī</s> the two shins, O auspicious one; the two knees under the conjunction of <s>Aśvinī</s>, and under <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> what are called the thighs

body.text:
phālgunīdvitaye guhyaṃ
kṛttikāsu tathā kaṭim
pārśve bhadrapadāyugme
dve kukṣī revatīṣu ca
body.translated_text: Under the pair of <s>Phālgunī</s> the privy parts, likewise under the <s>Kṛttikās</s> the hip; under the pair of <s>Bhadrapadā</s> the two sides, and the two bellies under the <s>Revatīs</s>

body.text:
anurādha uraḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ
śraviṣṭhāsv abhipūjayet
bhujayugmaṃ viśākhāsu
haste caiva karadvayam
body.translated_text: Under <s>Anurādhā</s> the chest and back, under the <s>Śraviṣṭhās</s> let him worship; the pair of arms under the <s>Viśākhās</s>, and under <s>Hasta</s> the two hands

body.text:
punarvasāv aṅgulīṃś ca
āśleṣāsu tathā nakhān
jyeṣṭhāyāṃ pūjayed grīvaṃ
śravaṇe śravaṇe tathā
body.translated_text: Under <s>Punarvasu</s> the fingers, and under the <s>Āśleṣās</s> likewise the nails; under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> let him worship the neck, and likewise under <s>Śravaṇa</s>

body.text:
puṣye mukhaṃ tathā svātau
daśanān abhipūjayet
hanvau śatabhiṣāyoge
maghāyoge ca nāsikām
body.translated_text: Under <s>Puṣya</s> the face, and under <s>Svātī</s> let him worship the teeth; the two jaws under the conjunction of <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, and under the conjunction of <s>Maghā</s> the nose

body.text:
mṛgottamāṅge nayane
pūjayed bhaktitaḥ śubhe
citrāyoge lalāṭaṃ ca
bharaṇyāṃ ca tathā śiraḥ
saṃpūjanīyā vidvadbhiś
cādrāsu ca śiroruhāḥ
body.translated_text: Under <s>Mṛga</s> (Mṛgaśiras) the head and the two eyes let him worship with devotion, O auspicious one; under the conjunction of <s>Citrā</s> the forehead, and under <s>Bharaṇī</s> likewise the head; and under <s>Ārdrā</s> the hairs of the head are to be worshipped by the learned

body.text:
nakṣatrayogeṣv eteṣu
pūjito jagataḥ patiḥ
nakṣatrapuruṣākhyo 'yaṃ
yathāvat puruṣottamaḥ
body.translated_text: Worshipped under these conjunctions of the lunar mansions, the Lord of the world, this <s>Puruṣottama</s> called the <s>Nakṣatra-puruṣa</s>, duly

body.text:
pāpāpahāraṃ kurute
samyac chraddhāvatāṃ satām
aṅgopāṅgāni caivāsya
pāpādīni yaśasvini
body.translated_text: removes the sin of the good who are full of faith and rightly [perform it]; and his limbs and minor limbs and the rest, O illustrious one,

body.text:
surūpāny abhijāyante
sapta janmāntarāṇi vai
sarvāṇi caiva bhadrāṇi
śarīrārogyam uttamam
body.translated_text: are born fair for seven births indeed, and all auspicious, and supreme bodily health

body.text:
saṃtatiṃ manasaḥ prītiṃ
rūpaṃ cātīvaśobhanam
vāṅmādhūryaṃ tathā kāntiṃ
yac cānyad abhivāñchitam
body.translated_text: Progeny, contentment of mind, exceedingly handsome form, sweetness of speech and likewise radiance, and whatever else is desired,

body.text:
dadāti nakṣatrapumān
pūjitaś ca janārdanaḥ
upoṣya samyag eteṣu
krameṇa rkṣeṣu śobhane
body.translated_text: the <s>Nakṣatra-puruṣa</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, when worshipped, grants; having fasted rightly under these mansions in order, O auspicious one,

body.text:
saṃpūjanīyo bhagavān
nakṣatrāṅgo janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: the Blessed <s>Janārdana</s>, the <s>Nakṣatra-puruṣa</s>, is to be worshipped

body.text:
gandhapuṣpādisaṃyuktaṃ
pūjayitvā yadāvidhi
jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gatvā
idaṃ codāharet tataḥ
svarūpam ārogyam atīva varcasaṃ
susaṃtatiṃ tv asthitabhaktim acyutām
api sarvam etaṃ protaṃ
sūtre maṇigaṇā iva
ekapuruṣa mahāpuruṣa
ṛkṣapuruṣa namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: Having worshipped him joined with fragrance, flowers, and the rest according to rule, having gone down upon the two knees to the earth, one should then recite this: '[Grant me] fair form, health, exceeding luster, good progeny, and steadfast unfailing devotion; for all this is strung [on you] as gems on a thread—O One Person, Great Person, Mansion-Person (<s>Ṛkṣa-puruṣa</s>), homage be to you'

body.text:
pratinakṣatrayoge ca
bhojanīyā dvijottamāḥ
body.translated_text: And under each conjunction of the lunar mansions, the best of the twice-born are to be fed

body.text:
nakṣatrajñāya viprāya
dadyād dānaṃ ca śaktitaḥ
pārite ca punar dadyāt
strīpūṃsāṃ cāruhāsini
body.translated_text: To a <s>vipra</s> who knows the lunar mansions one should give a gift according to ability; and when [the fast] is completed, one should give again, O you of charming laughter, [a gift] of a man and a woman [figure?],

body.text:
chattropānadyugaṃ caiva
saptadhānyaṃ sakāñcanam
ghṛtapātraṃ ca dharmajñe
yac cānyad ativallabham
body.translated_text: and a parasol and a pair of sandals, and the seven grains together with gold, and a vessel of ghee, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, and whatever else is most dear

body.text:
strī vā sādhvī sadā viṣṇor
ārādhanaparāyaṇā
anenaiva vidhānena
saṃpūjyaitad avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: A woman, or a virtuous person, ever devoted to the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having worshipped by this very procedure, may attain this

body.text:
sarvakāmān avāpnoti
samārādhya janārdanam
prakārair bahubhir brahman
yān yān icchati cetasā
body.translated_text: One attains all wishes, having fully worshipped <s>Janārdana</s>, by many methods, O <s>brahman</s>, whatever things one desires with the mind

body.text:
nṝṇāṃ strīṇāṃ ca viprarṣe
nānyac chokasya kāraṇam
apatyād adhikaṃ kiṃcid
vidyate hy atra janmani
body.translated_text: For men and for women, O seer among <s>vipras</s>, there is no other cause of sorrow [so great]; nothing greater than [the loss of] offspring exists here in this birth

body.text:
aputratā mahad duḥkham
atiduḥkhaṃ kuputratā
aputraḥ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ
hetubhūto mato mama
body.translated_text: Sonlessness is a great sorrow; the having of a bad son is an exceeding sorrow; the sonless one is, in my view, the cause of all sorrows

body.text:
dhanyās te ye sutaṃ prāpya
sarvaduḥkhavivarjitam
śastaṃ praśāntaṃ balinaṃ
parāṃ nirvṛtim āgatāḥ
body.translated_text: Blessed are those who, having obtained a son free of all sorrow, commended, tranquil, strong, have come to the supreme bliss—

body.text:
svakarmanirataṃ nityaṃ
devadvijaparāyaṇam
śāstrajñaṃ dharmatattvajñaṃ
dīnānāthajanāśrayam
body.translated_text: [a son] ever devoted to his own duty, intent on gods and the twice-born, knowing the scriptures, knowing the truth of <s>dharma</s>, a refuge for the poor and helpless,

body.text:
vinirjitāriṃ sarvasya
manohṛdayanandanam
devānukūlatāyuktaṃ
yuktaṃ samyag guṇena ca
body.translated_text: having conquered his enemies, the delight of the mind and heart of all, endowed with favor toward the gods, well endowed with virtue,

body.text:
mitrasvajanasammāna-
labdhanirvāṇam uttamam
yaḥ prāpnoti sutaṃ tasmān
nānyo dhanyataro bhuvi
body.translated_text: [a son] who attains the supreme contentment born of the honor of friends and kinsmen—than he who obtains such a son, no one is more blessed on earth

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi tac chrotuṃ
tvattaḥ karma mahāmune
yenedṛglakṣaṇaḥ putraḥ
prāpyate bhuvi mānavaiḥ
body.translated_text: So I wish to hear from you, O great sage, that action by which a son of such marks is obtained by men on earth

body.text:
evam etan mahābhāga
pitroḥ putrasamudbhavam
duḥkhaṃ prayāty upaśamaṃ
tena yeneha kenacit
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O greatly fortunate one, the sorrow of parents arising from [the lack of] a son goes to calm by some [means] here

body.text:
atrāpi śrūyatāṃ vṛttaṃ
yat pūrvam abhavan mune
utpattau kārtavīryasya
haihayasya mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Here too let the account be heard, of what formerly happened, O sage, at the birth of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, the great soul of the <s>Haihayas</s>

body.text:
kṛtavīryo mahīpālo
haihayānām abhūt purā
tasya śīladhanā nāma
babhūva varavarṇinī
patnī sahasrapravarā
mahiṣī śīlamaṇḍanā
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> was formerly a king of the <s>Haihayas</s>; his wife, of fair complexion, was named <s>Śīladhanā</s>, the foremost of a thousand, the queen, adorned with good conduct

body.text:
sā tv aputrā mahābhāgā
maitreyīṃ paryapṛcchata
guṇavatputralābhāya
kṛtāsanaparigrahām
body.translated_text: But she, sonless though greatly fortunate, asked <s>Maitreyī</s>, taking up the posture [of supplication], for the gaining of a virtuous son

body.text:
tayā ca pṛṣṭā vai samyag
maitreyī brahmavādinī
kathayām āsa paramaṃ
nāmnānantavrataṃ vratam
body.translated_text: And asked rightly by her, <s>Maitreyī</s>, the expounder of <s>Brahman</s>, related the supreme vow named the <s>Anantavrata</s>,

body.text:
sarvakāmaphalāvāpti-
kārakaṃ pāpanāśanam
tasyāḥ sā putralābhāya
rājaputrās tapasvinī
body.translated_text: which brings about the attainment of the fruit of all wishes and is the destroyer of sin; that ascetic [queen, performed it] for the gaining of a son [who would be one of the] royal sons

body.text:
yo 'yam icchen naraḥ kāmaṃ
nārī vā varavarṇini
sa taṃ samārādhya vibhuṃ
samāpnoti janārdanam
body.translated_text: Whatever desire a man, or a woman, O fair-complexioned one, may wish—he, having worshipped that pervading Lord, attains <s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
mārgaśīrṣe mṛgaśiro
bhīru yasmin dine bhavet
tasmin saṃprāśya gomūtraṃ
snāto niyatamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: On whatever day in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> the asterism <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> occurs, O timid one, on that day, having consumed cow's urine, bathed and of restrained mind,

body.text:
puṣpair dhūpais tathā gandhair
upahāraiḥ svaśaktitaḥ
vāmapādam anantasya
pūjayed varavarṇini
body.translated_text: with flowers, incense, and likewise fragrances, with offerings according to his ability, he should worship the left foot of <s>Ananta</s>, O fair-complexioned one

body.text:
anantaḥ sarvakāmānām
anantaṃ bhagavān phalam
dadātv anantaṃ ca punas
tad evāstv anyajanmani
body.translated_text: "<s>Ananta</s> (the Endless) is the endless fruit of all desires; let the Blessed One grant the endless, and again let that very thing be mine in another birth

body.text:
anantapuṇyopacayaṃ
karoty etan mahāvratam
yathābhilaṣitāvāptiṃ
kurvan mā kṣayam etu ca
body.translated_text: Let this great vow produce an endless accumulation of merit, granting the attainment of what is wished; and let it not come to decay"

body.text:
ity uccāryābhipūjyainaṃ
yathāvad vidhinā naraḥ
samāhitamanā bhūtvā
praṇipātapuraḥsaram
body.translated_text: Having uttered thus and worshipped him duly according to rule, the man, his mind concentrated, preceded by prostration,

body.text:
viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ dadyād
anantaḥ prīyatām iti
samuccārya tato naktaṃ
bhuñjīyāt tailavarjitam
body.translated_text: should give a fee to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, saying "Let <s>Ananta</s> be pleased"; having uttered that, he should then eat at night, free of oil

body.text:
tataś ca pauṣe puṣyarkṣe
tathaiva bhagavatkaṭim
vāmām abhyarcayet kṛtvā
gomūtraprāśanaṃ budhaḥ
body.translated_text: And then in <s>Pauṣa</s>, under the asterism <s>Puṣya</s>, likewise the wise one, having performed the consuming of cow's urine, should worship the Blessed One's left hip

body.text:
anantaḥ sarvakāmānām
iti coccārayed budhaḥ
bhuñjīta ca tathā vipraṃ
vācayitvā yathāvidhi
body.translated_text: And the wise one should utter "<s>Ananta</s> is the endless fruit of all desires," and should eat thus, having had a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> recite according to rule

body.text:
māghe maghāsu tadvac ca
bāhuṃ devasya pūjayet
skandhaṃ ca phalgunīyoge
phālgune māsi bhāmini
body.translated_text: In <s>Māgha</s>, under <s>Maghā</s>, likewise he should worship the arm of the god, and the shoulder under the conjunction of <s>Phalgunī</s>, in the month of <s>Phālguna</s>, O lady

body.text:
caturṣv eteṣu gomūtra-
prāśanaṃ nṛpanandini
body.translated_text: In these four [months], the consuming of cow's urine, O delight of the king

body.text:
brāhmaṇāya tathā dadyāt
tilān kanakam eva ca
body.translated_text: And likewise he should give to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> sesame and gold

body.text:
devasya dakṣiṇaskandhaṃ
caitre citrāsu pūjayet
tathaiva prāśanaṃ cātra
pañcagavyam udāhṛtam
body.translated_text: He should worship the right shoulder of the god in <s>Caitra</s>, under <s>Citrā</s>; and likewise here the consuming is declared to be the <s>pañcagavya</s> (five cow-products)

body.text:
vipre vācanake dadyād
yāvan māsacatuṣṭayam
vaiśākhe ca viśākhāsu
bāhuṃ saṃpūjya dakṣiṇam
body.translated_text: He should give to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who recites, for as long as the four-month period; and in <s>Vaiśākha</s>, under <s>Viśākhā</s>, having worshipped the right arm,

body.text:
tathaivoktayavān dadyāt
tadvan naktaṃ bhujikriyā
kaṭipūjāṃ ca jyeṣṭhāsu
jyeṣṭhamūle śubhavrate
body.translated_text: he should likewise give the barley spoken of, and likewise the night-eating practice; and the hip-worship under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, at the root of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, O you of auspicious vows

body.text:
āṣāḍhāsu tathāṣāḍhe
kuryāt pādārcanaṃ śubhe
padadvayaṃ ca śravaṇe
śrāvaṇe subhru pūjayet
body.translated_text: Under <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>, likewise in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, he should perform the worship of the foot, O auspicious one; and the two feet under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, he should worship, O fair-browed one

body.text:
ghṛtaṃ viprāya dātavyaṃ
prāśanīyaṃ tathā dadhi
kārttikānteṣu māseṣu
prāśanaṃ dānam eva ca
body.translated_text: Ghee should be given to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and curd should be consumed; in the months ending with <s>Kārttika</s>, the consuming and the giving as well

body.text:
etad eva samākhyātaṃ
devaṃ tadvac ca pūjayet
body.translated_text: This very thing is declared; and he should worship the god likewise

body.text:
guhyaṃ proṣṭhapadāyoge
māsi bhādrapade 'rcayet
tadvad āśvayuje pūjyaṃ
hṛdayaṃ cāśvinīṣu vai
body.translated_text: He should worship the private parts under the conjunction of <s>Proṣṭhapada</s>, in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>; likewise in <s>Āśvayuja</s> the navel is to be worshipped, and the heart under <s>Aśvinī</s>

body.text:
kuryāt samāhitamanāḥ
snānaprāśanaśaucavān
anantaśirasaḥ pūjāṃ
kārttike kṛttikāsu ca
body.translated_text: With mind concentrated, possessed of the purity of bathing and consuming, he should perform the worship of the head of <s>Ananta</s> in <s>Kārttika</s>, under <s>Kṛttikā</s>

body.text:
yasmin yasmin dine pūjā
tatra tatra tadā dine
nāmānantasya japtavyaṃ
kṣutapraskhalitādiṣu
body.translated_text: On whatever day the worship occurs, then on that day the name of <s>Ananta</s> is to be muttered, at sneezing, stumbling, and the like

body.text:
ghṛtenānantam uddiśya
pūrvamāsacatuṣṭayam
kurvīta homaṃ caitrādau
śālinā kulanandini
body.translated_text: Dedicating it to <s>Ananta</s>, with ghee, for the first four-month period, he should perform the <s>homa</s> (oblation) with rice in <s>Caitra</s> and onward, O delight of the family

body.text:
kṣīreṇa śrāvaṇādau tu
homaṃ māsacatuṣṭayam
śastaṃ tu sarvamāseṣu
haviṣyānnaṃ ca bhojanam
body.translated_text: With milk in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> and onward, the <s>homa</s> for the four-month period; and in all the months sacrificial food is praised as the meal

body.text:
evaṃ dvādaśabhir māsaiḥ
pāraṇaṃ tritayaṃ śubhe
pārite samavāpnoti
sarvān eva manorathān
body.translated_text: Thus in twelve months the threefold breaking-of-the-fast, O auspicious one; when it is completed, one attains all one's heart's desires

body.text:
putrārthibhir vittakāmair
bhṛtyadārān abhīpsubhiḥ
prārthayadbhiś ca kartavyam
ārogyabalasaṃpadam
body.translated_text: By those desiring sons, longing for wealth, wishing for servants and wives, and praying [for them], this is to be done—the fortune of health and strength

body.text:
etad vrataṃ mahābhāge
puṇyaṃ svastyayanapradam
anantavratasaṃjñaṃ vai
sarvapāpapraṇāśanam
body.translated_text: This vow, O greatly fortunate one, is holy, the giver of well-being, named the <s>Ananta</s> vow, the destroyer of all sins

body.text:
tat kuruṣvaiva devi tvaṃ
vrataṃ śīladhane varam
viśiṣṭaṃ sarvalokasya
yadi putram abhīpsasi
body.translated_text: Perform that very vow, O goddess, the best, distinguished above all the world, O you whose wealth is good conduct, if you desire a son

body.text:
iti śīladhanā śrutvā
maitreyīvacanaṃ śubham
cacāraitad vratavaraṃ
susamāhitamānasā
body.translated_text: Thus having heard the auspicious speech of <s>Maitreyī</s>, <s>Śīladhanā</s> performed this excellent vow with mind well concentrated

body.text:
putrārthinyās tatas tasyā
vratenānena suvrata
viṣṇus tutoṣa tuṣṭe ca
viṣṇau sā suṣuve sutam
body.translated_text: Then, through this vow of hers who desired a son, O you of good vows, <s>Viṣṇu</s> was gratified; and when <s>Viṣṇu</s> was pleased, she gave birth to a son

body.text:
tasya vai jātamātrasya
pravavāv anilaḥ śivaḥ
nīrajaskam abhūd vyoma
mudaṃ prāpākhilaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: When he was but newly born, a benign wind blew, the sky became free of dust, and the whole world attained joy

body.text:
devadundubhayo neduḥ
puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papāta ca
prajagur divi gandharvā
nanṛtuś cāpsarogaṇāḥ
dharme manaḥ samastasya
dālbhya lokasya cābhavat
body.translated_text: The drums of the gods resounded, a rain of flowers fell, the <s>Gandharvas</s> sang in heaven and the hosts of <s>Apsarases</s> danced; and the mind of the whole world, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, turned toward <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
tasya nāma pitā cakre
tanayasyārjuneti vai
kṛtavīryasutatvāc ca
kārtavīryo babhūva saḥ
body.translated_text: The father made the name of his son "<s>Arjuna</s>"; and being the son of <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>, he became <s>Kārtavīrya</s>

body.text:
tenāpi bhagavān viṣṇur
dattātreyasvarūpavān
ārādhito 'timahatā
tapasā dālbhya bhūbhṛtā
body.translated_text: By him too the Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in the form of <s>Dattātreya</s>, was worshipped with exceedingly great austerity, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, by that king

body.text:
tasya tuṣṭo jagannāthaś
cakravartitvam uttamam
dadau śauryabale cāti-
sakalāny āyudhāni ca
body.translated_text: Pleased with him, the Lord of the world granted him the supreme state of universal sovereignty, exceeding valour and strength, and all the weapons

body.text:
sa ca vavre varaṃ deva
vadhas tvatto bhaved iti
purānusmaraṇaṃ jñānaṃ
bhītānāṃ cārtināśanam
smaraṇād upakāritvaṃ
jagato 'sya jagatpate
body.translated_text: And he chose this boon: "O god, let my slaying come from you; and the remembrance of former lives, knowledge, the destruction of distress for the fearful, and benefit to this world from being remembered, O Lord of the world"

body.text:
tam āha devadeveśaḥ
puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇaḥ
sarvam etan mahābhāga
tava bhūpa bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: To him the Lord of the gods of gods, whose eyes resemble the lotus, said: "All this, O greatly fortunate one, shall be yours, O king

body.text:
yaś ca prabhāte rātrau ca
tvāṃ naraḥ kīrtayiṣyati
namo 'stu kārtavīryāyety
abhidhāsyati caiva yaḥ
tilaprasthapradānasya
sa naraḥ puṇyam āpsyati
body.translated_text: And the man who, at dawn and at night, shall proclaim you, and who shall say "Homage be to <s>Kārtavīrya</s>"—that man shall obtain the merit of the gift of a <s>prastha</s>-measure of sesame

body.text:
anaṣṭadravyatā caiva
tava nāmābhikīrtanaiḥ
bhaviṣyati mahīpālety
uktvā taṃ prayayau hariḥ
body.translated_text: And there shall be the recovery of lost property through the proclamation of your name, O king"—saying thus, <s>Hari</s> departed

body.text:
sa cāpi varam āsādya
prasannād garuḍadhvajāt
pālayām āsa bhūpālaḥ
saptadvīpāṃ vasuṃdharām
body.translated_text: And he too, having obtained the boon from the gracious one whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s>, the king protected the seven-continent earth

body.text:
teneṣṭaṃ vividhair yajñaiḥ
samāptavaradakṣiṇaiḥ
jitvārivargam akhilaṃ
dharmataḥ pālitāḥ prajāḥ
body.translated_text: By him sacrifice was offered with various <s>yajñas</s> with full sacrificial fees; having conquered the whole host of foes, the subjects were protected according to <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
anantavratamāhātmyād
āsādya tanayaṃ ca tam
pitroḥ putrodbhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ
nāsīt svalpam api dvija
body.translated_text: Through the glory of the <s>Ananta</s> vow, having obtained that son, the sorrow arising from offspring did not befall the parents, not even a little, O twice-born

body.text:
evam etat samākhyātam
anantākhyaṃ vrataṃ tava
yac cīrtvā rājapatnī sā
kārtavīryam asūyata
body.translated_text: Thus this vow named <s>Ananta</s> has been declared to you, by performing which that queen gave birth to <s>Kārtavīrya</s>

body.text:
yaś caitac chṛṇuyāj janma
kārtavīryasya mānavaḥ
strī vā duḥkham apatyotthaṃ
sapta janmāni nāśnute
body.translated_text: And the man or woman who shall hear this birth of <s>Kārtavīrya</s> does not undergo the sorrow arising from offspring for seven births

body.text:
rūpasaṃpat samākhyātā
strīpuṃsāṃ jāyate śubhā
samupoṣya jagannāthaṃ
nakṣatrapuruṣaṃ harim
body.translated_text: The attainment of beauty is declared to arise, auspicious, for women and men, by fasting upon the Lord of the world, <s>Hari</s>, the Asterism-Person (<s>Nakṣatrapuruṣa</s>)

body.text:
vāso'tiśobhanaṃ cāru-
vastrādyābharaṇojjvalam
gṛhaṃ sarvaguṇopetam
aśeṣopaskarānvitam
body.translated_text: A most splendid dwelling, gleaming with fine garments and ornaments, a house endowed with all qualities and furnished with every appurtenance,

body.text:
karmaṇā yena viprarṣe
toṣito madhusūdanaḥ
dadāti bhagavān karma
tan no vistarato vada
body.translated_text: by what act, O sage among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the Blessed <s>Madhusūdana</s> is gratified, and the Lord grants such an act—tell us that in detail

body.text:
yan māṃ pṛcchasi dālbhya tvaṃ
gṛhopaskarabhūṣaṇam
narāṇāṃ jāyate yena
tat sarvaṃ kathayāmi te
body.translated_text: That which you ask me, O <s>Dālbhya</s>—the house, appurtenances, and ornaments by which it arises for men—all that I tell you

body.text:
nandā bhadrā jayā riktā
pūrṇā ca dvijasattama
tithayo vai samākhyātāḥ
pratipatkramasaṃjñayā
body.translated_text: <s>Nandā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Riktā</s>, and <s>Pūrṇā</s>, O best of the twice-born—the lunar days are thus declared by the sequence beginning with the first (<s>pratipad</s>)

body.text:
pañcamī daśamī caiva
tathā pañcadaśī tithiḥ
pūrṇā etāḥ samākhyātāṣ
tithayo munisattama
body.translated_text: The fifth, the tenth, and likewise the fifteenth lunar day—these are declared to be the <s>Pūrṇā</s> lunar days, O best of sages

body.text:
mṛdā dhātuvikārair vā
varṇakair gomayena vā
viṣṇor āyatane tāsu
yaḥ karoty upalepanam
body.translated_text: With clay, or with mineral preparations, or with pigments, or with cow-dung, he who performs the smearing in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> on those days,

body.text:
pravātāvātaguṇavad
varṣāsv atimanoramam
anuliptaṃ śubhākāraṃ
sugṛhaṃ labhate mune
body.translated_text: endowed with the quality of being sheltered from wind, exceedingly delightful in the rains, anointed, of auspicious form—he obtains a fine house, O sage

body.text:
pūrṇaṃ dhānyahiraṇyādyair
maṇimuktāphalojjvalam
pratyāsannajalābhogaṃ
gṛham āpnoti śobhanam
body.translated_text: Full of grain, gold, and the rest, gleaming with gems and pearls, with a stretch of water close at hand, he obtains a beautiful house

body.text:
sāmnatasvajanānāṃ yat
sarveṣām uttamottamam
tad āpnoti gṛhaṃ brahmann
anulepanakṛn naraḥ
body.translated_text: That house which is the very best of all those of his own honoured kin—that, O <s>brahman</s>, the man who performs the smearing obtains

body.text:
yenānulipte tiṣṭhanti
viṣṇvāyatanabhūtale
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśaḥ
śūdrāḥ sādhvyas tathā striyaḥ
tasya pūṇyaphalaṃ dālbhya
śrūyatāṃ yat prajāyate
body.translated_text: On the ground of the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> which has been smeared by whom there stand <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, <s>śūdras</s>, and likewise virtuous women—hear, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, the holy fruit which is produced for him

body.text:
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ
muktāhāragaṇojjvalam
śreṣṭhaṃ sarvavimānānāṃ
svarge dhiṣṇyam avāpnute
body.translated_text: Thronged with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, gleaming with strings of pearls, the best of all celestial cars—a dwelling in heaven he attains

body.text:
yāvatyas tithayo liptaṃ
divyābdāṃs tāvato dvija
tasmin vimāne sa naraḥ
strī vā tiṣṭhati sattama
body.translated_text: For as many lunar days as he has smeared, for so many divine years, O twice-born, that man, or woman, dwells in that celestial car, O best one

body.text:
sugandhagandhasadvastra-
sarvabhūṣaṇabhūṣitaḥ
gandharvāpsarasāṃ saṃbhaiḥ
pūjyamānaḥ sa tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: Adorned with fragrant perfumes, fine garments, and all ornaments, worshipped by the assemblies of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, he abides

body.text:
liptaṃ ca yāvato hastān
viṣṇor āyatanaṃ dvija
tāvadyojanavistīrṇa-
svargasthānādhipo hi saḥ
body.translated_text: And for as many cubits as the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been smeared, O twice-born, he is the lord of a heavenly station extending for that many <s>yojanas</s>

body.text:
pūjyamānaḥ suragaṇaiḥ
śītoṣṇādivivarjitaḥ
manojñagātro viprendras
tiṣṭhaty astāghasaṃhatiḥ
body.translated_text: Worshipped by the hosts of gods, free from cold, heat, and the rest, of charming form, O chief of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, he abides, his mass of sins gone

body.text:
cyutas tasmād ihāgamya
viśiṣṭe jāyate kule
tato 'sya sadgṛhavaraṃ
martyaloke 'bhijāyate
body.translated_text: Fallen from there, having come here, he is born in a distinguished family; then in the world of mortals an excellent good house is born to him

body.text:
na tatra tāvad dāridryaṃ
nopasargā na vā kaliḥ
na cāpi mṛtaniṣkrāntir
yāvaj jīvaty asau dvija
body.translated_text: There is no poverty there, no calamities nor strife, nor even the departure of the dead, as long as he lives, O twice-born

body.text:
viṣṇuḥ samastabhūtāni
sasarjaitāni yāni vai
teṣāṃ madhye jagaddhātur
atīveṣṭā vasuṃdharā
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> created all these beings which exist; among them, the earth is exceedingly dear to the world's creator

body.text:
kṛte saṃmārjane tasyās
tathaivoparilepane
prayāti paramaṃ toṣaṃ
vaiṣṇavīyaṃ mahī yataḥ
body.translated_text: When the sweeping of it is done, and likewise the smearing upon it, one attains the supreme contentment of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since the earth belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
brahman yena vidhānena
devāgāropalepalam
kartavyaṃ puruṣaiḥ samyak
strībhir vā tad udīraya
body.translated_text: O <s>brahman</s>, by what procedure the smearing of the god's house is to be duly performed by men or by women—declare that

body.text:
riktāyās tu tither madhye
kuryāt saṃkalpam ātmanaḥ
upalepanakṛd vipro
viṣṇor āyatane bhuvi
body.translated_text: On the <s>Riktā</s> lunar day, in the middle of it, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who performs the smearing in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> on earth should make a resolve of his own

body.text:
dvitīye 'hni tato devaṃ
praṇamya yatamānasaḥ
dharaṇīpitaraṃ viṣṇum
idaṃ vākyam udīrayet
body.translated_text: Then on the second day, having bowed to the god, with concentrated mind, he should utter this speech to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the father of the earth:

body.text:
tvaṃ sarvabhūtaprabhavo jagatpate
tvayy etad īśeśa jagat pratiṣṭhitam
tvam eva bhūtāni yatas tato 'haṃ
tvām pūjayāmy adya mahīsvarūpam
body.translated_text: "You are the source of all beings, O Lord of the world; in you, O Lord of lords, this world is established; you alone are the beings, since from you they come—therefore I worship you today in the form of the earth

body.text:
tvaṃ mahī jagatāṃ nātha
sarvanātha namo 'stu te
śuśrūṣitaḥ prasīdeśa
bhuvo lepanakarmaṇā
body.translated_text: You are the earth, O Lord of the worlds, O Lord of all; homage be to you; served, be gracious, O Lord, by the act of smearing the earth"

body.text:
ity uccārya kṣitau kṣiptvā
prathamaṃ dhāranītale
puṣpāṇi vā dvijaśreṣṭha
yaḥ karoty anulepanam
na tasya jāyate bhaṅgo
gārhasthyasya kadācana
body.translated_text: Having uttered thus and first cast upon the ground, upon the surface of the earth, flowers, O best of the twice-born, he who performs the smearing—for him there never occurs a breach of householder life

body.text:
yā ca nārī karoty evaṃ
yathāvad anulepanam
nāpnoti sā ca vaidhavyaṃ
gṛhabhaṅgaṃ kadācana
body.translated_text: And the woman who thus duly performs the smearing—she never attains widowhood nor the breach of her house

body.text:
kṛtvopalepanaṃ bhūyaḥ
praṇipatya janārdanam
snāto viṣṇuṃ samabhyarcya
idaṃ vākyam udīrayet
body.translated_text: Having performed the smearing, again prostrating to <s>Janārdana</s>, bathed, having worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he should utter this speech:

body.text:
prasīda bhūdharānanta
mayā yad upalepanam
kṛtaṃ tena samastaṃ me
nāśam abhyetu pātakam
body.translated_text: "Be gracious, O <s>Ananta</s>, upholder of the earth; by the smearing which has been done by me, let all my sin go to destruction"

body.text:
evaṃ saṃpūjya bhuñjīyād
aparāhne dvijottama
svanulipte mahābhāge
bhuktvā limpec ca tat punaḥ
body.translated_text: Having thus worshipped, he should eat in the afternoon, O best of the twice-born; in the well-smeared [place], O greatly fortunate one, having eaten he should smear it again

body.text:
pakṣe pakṣe trirātraṃ tu
yaḥ karoty upalepanam
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ
svargaṃ gacchaty asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: He who, fortnight by fortnight for three nights, performs the smearing, freed from all sins, goes to heaven without doubt

body.text:
tatkṣayāt svargeloke tu
jāto gṛhavaraṃ yathā
samāpnoti yathākhyātaṃ
tat sarvaṃ tava sattama
body.translated_text: On its exhaustion, born in the world of heaven [and then here], he attains an excellent house as has been declared—all that, O best one, is yours

body.text:
sarvābharaṇasaṃpūrṇaṃ
sarvopaskaradhānyavat
gomahiṣyādisaṃbhogaṃ
gṛham āpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: The man obtains a house full of all ornaments, possessed of every appurtenance and grain, with the enjoyment of cattle, buffaloes, and the rest

body.text:
tasmād abhīpsatā samyag
gārhasthyam avikhaṇḍitam
viṣṇor āyatane kāryaṃ
sarvadaivopalepanam
body.translated_text: Therefore, by one desiring unbroken householder life, the smearing in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> should always duly be performed

body.text:
saptadvīpavatīṃ kṛtsnāṃ
yathendras tridivaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: [He attains] the whole seven-continent [earth], just as <s>Indra</s> attained heaven

body.text:
alpopalepanād yasya
māndhātā sakalāṃ mahīm
avāpa viṣṇvāyatanaṃ
nopalimpeta ko hi tat
body.translated_text: By a small smearing of which <s>Māndhātṛ</s> attained the entire earth, who indeed would not smear that temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

body.text:
dīpaṃ prayacchati naro
viṣṇor āyatane hi yaḥ
sadakṣiṇasya yajñasya
phalaṃ prāpnoty asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: The man who offers a lamp in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> obtains, without doubt, the fruit of a sacrifice with its full fees

body.text:
kārttike tu viśeṣeṇa
kaumude māsi dīpakam
dattvā yat phalam āpnoti
dālbhya tat kena labhyate
body.translated_text: But especially in <s>Kārttika</s>, the month of <s>Kaumudī</s>, the fruit which one obtains by giving a lamp—O <s>Dālbhya</s>, by what is that obtained?

body.text:
dālbhyānyad api vakṣyāmi
purāvṛttam idaṃ śṛṇu
vidarbharājatanayā
lalitā yad uvāca ha
body.translated_text: O <s>Dālbhya</s>, I shall tell yet another thing; hear this past event, what <s>Lalitā</s>, the daughter of the king of <s>Vidarbha</s>, indeed said

body.text:
vidarbharāṭ citraratho
babhūvāstraviśāradaḥ
tasya putraśataṃ rājño
jajñe pañcadaśottaram
body.translated_text: The king of <s>Vidarbha</s>, <s>Citraratha</s>, was skilled in weapons; to that king were born a hundred and fifteen sons

body.text:
ekaiva kanyā dālbhyāsīl
lalitā nāmanāmataḥ
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇā
bhrātṝṇāṃ pitur eva ca
body.translated_text: There was one daughter only, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, <s>Lalitā</s> by name, complete in all auspicious marks, [dear] to her brothers and to her father

body.text:
samastabhṛtyavargasya
mātṝṇāṃ svajanasya ca
tathaiva pauravargasya
yaś cānyo dadṛśe śubhām
tasya tasyāticārvaṅgī
babhūveṣṭā dvijottama
body.translated_text: to the whole body of servants, to her mothers, and to her kinsfolk, and likewise to the body of citizens; and whoever else beheld the auspicious one—to each of them that one of exceedingly fair limbs became dear, O best of the twice-born

body.text:
tāṃ dadau kāśirājāya
sa pitā cāruvarmane
upayeme ca tāṃ subhrūṃ
cāruvarmā mahīpatiḥ
body.translated_text: Her the father gave to the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, <s>Cāruvarman</s>; and that king <s>Cāruvarman</s> wedded that fair-browed one

body.text:
śatāny anyāni bhāryāṇāṃ
trīṇy āsaṃś cāruvarmaṇaḥ
tāsāṃ madhye 'gramahiṣī
lalitā tasya cābhavat
body.translated_text: There were three hundred other wives of <s>Cāruvarman</s>; among them <s>Lalitā</s> became his chief queen

body.text:
sā ca nityaṃ jagaddhātur
devadevasya cakriṇaḥ
dīpavartiparā tadvat
tailasyāharaṇodyatā
body.translated_text: And she was ever intent on the lamp-wicks of the upholder of the world, the god of gods, the discus-bearer, and likewise busy with the fetching of oil.

body.text:
viṣṇor āyatane tasyāḥ
sahasraṃ dvijasattama
dīpānāṃ vai prajajvāla
divārātram atandritam
body.translated_text: In the temple of that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of the twice-born, a thousand of her lamps blazed unwearied day and night.

body.text:
tasyā dyutiparābhūtās
tasyā lāvaṇyanirjitāḥ
sarvāḥ sapatnyo lalitāṃ
papracchur idam āditaḥ
body.translated_text: Overcome by her radiance, defeated by her loveliness, all the co-wives questioned <s>Lalitā</s> thus, from the beginning:

body.text:
lalite vada bhadraṃ te
bhadraṃ te lalite vada
kautūhalaparāḥ sarvā
yat pṛcchāmas tad ucyatām
body.translated_text: "<s>Lalitā</s>, speak—blessing upon you; blessing upon you, <s>Lalitā</s>, speak—all of us, full of curiosity; let what we ask be told."

body.text:
viṣaye sati vaktavyaṃ
yan mayā tad ihocyatām
nāhaṃ matsariṇī bhadrā
na ca rāgādidūṣitā
body.translated_text: "When there is a fit subject, what is to be spoken by me, let that be told here; I am not envious, O blessed ones, nor sullied by passion and the rest.

body.text:
bhavatyo mama sarvāsāṃ
bhavatīnām ahaṃ tathā
apṛthagbhartṛsāmanyā
devalokābhikāmukāḥ
body.translated_text: You are to me, all of you, and I likewise am to you; sharing one and the same husband, all desirous of the world of the gods.

body.text:
pūrvaṃ yūyam ahaṃ caiva
bhavatīnāṃ sadharmiṇī
body.translated_text: Formerly you and I likewise—I was the fellow-sharer of duty with you."

body.text:
na tathā puṣpadhūpeṣu
na tathā dvijapūjane
prayatnaṃ tava paśyāmo
viṣṇor āyatane śubhe
body.translated_text: "We do not see your effort in flowers and incense, nor likewise in the worship of the twice-born, in the fair temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

body.text:
yathāhani tathā rātrau
yathā rātrau tathāhani
tava dīpapradānāya
yathā subhru sadodyamaḥ
body.translated_text: as we see, O fair-browed one, that as by day so by night, and as by night so by day, your striving is ever for the giving of lamps.

body.text:
tad etat kathayāsmākaṃ
lalite kautukaṃ param
manyāmo dīpadānasya
bhavatyā viditaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: Therefore tell us this, O <s>Lalitā</s>—a great wonder—for we suppose the fruit of lamp-giving is known to you."

body.text:
evam uktā tatas tābhir
lalitā lalitaṃ vacaḥ
vyājahāra sapatnīs tā
na kiṃcid api bhāminī
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by them, then <s>Lalitā</s>, the lovely one, spoke a lovely word—nothing at all, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, to those co-wives, the fair lady.

body.text:
punaḥ punaś ca sā tābhir
bahuṣo dālbhya coditā
dākṣiṇyasārā lalitā
kathāyām āsa bhāminī
body.translated_text: And again and again, many times urged by them, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, whose essence is graciousness, the fair lady began the tale:

body.text:
kautukaṃ bhavatīnāṃ ced
atīvālpe 'pi vastuni
tad eṣā kathayāmy etad
yad vṛttaṃ mama śobhanāḥ
body.translated_text: "If there is curiosity in you, even concerning a most trifling matter, then I tell you this—what befell me, O fair ones.

body.text:
sauvīrarājasya purā
maitreyo 'bhūt purohitaḥ
tena cāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ
kāritaṃ devikātaṭe
body.translated_text: Of old, <s>Maitreya</s> was the family priest of the king of <s>Sauvīra</s>; and by him a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> was had built on the bank of the <s>Devikā</s>.

body.text:
ahany ahani śuśrūṣāṃ
puṣpadhūpopalepanaiḥ
dīpadānādibhiś caiva
cakre tatra sa vai dvijaḥ
body.translated_text: Day after day that twice-born one performed service there with flowers, incense, and plastering, and with the giving of lamps and the rest.

body.text:
kārttike dīpako brahman
pradattas tena vai tadā
āsīn nirvāṇabhūyiṣṭho
devārcāpurato niśi
body.translated_text: In <s>Kārttika</s>, O <s>brahman</s>, a lamp was then given by him; it had become almost extinguished, before the image of the deity, at night.

body.text:
devatāyatane cāsaṃ
tatrāham api mūṣikā
pradīpavartiharaṇe
kṛtabuddhir varānanāḥ
body.translated_text: And I too was there in the temple of the deity, a mouse, O fair-faced ones, with my mind set on stealing the wick of the lamp.

body.text:
gṛhītā ca mayā vartir
vṛṣadaṃśo nanāda ca
naṣṭā cāhaṃ tadā tasya
mārjārasya bhayāturā
body.translated_text: And the wick was seized by me, and a cat cried out, and I, terrified by fear of that cat, then fled.

body.text:
vartiprāntena naśyantyā
sa dīpaḥ prerito mayā
jajvāla pūrvavad dīptyā
tasminn āyatane punaḥ
body.translated_text: As I was fleeing, that lamp was stirred up by me with the end of the wick, and it blazed again as before with brightness in that temple.

body.text:
mṛtāhaṃ ca tato jātā
vaidarbhī rājakanyakā
jātismarā kāntimatī
bhavatīnāṃ samā guṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: And I died, and then was born a princess of <s>Vidarbha</s>, remembering my former birth, beautiful, equal to you in virtues.

body.text:
eṣa prabhāvo dīpasya
kārttike māsi śobhanāḥ
dattasya viṣṇvāyatane
yasyeyaṃ vyuṣṭir uttamā
body.translated_text: This is the power of a lamp, O fair ones, given in the month of <s>Kārttika</s> in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose excellent result is this.

body.text:
asaṃkalpitam apy asya
preraṇaṃ yat kṛtaṃ mayā
viṣṇvāyatanadīpasya
yasyedaṃ bhujyate phalam
body.translated_text: Even the stirring of it, done by me unintentionally—of the lamp in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose fruit is this that is enjoyed.

body.text:
lobhābhibhūtā hartuṃ taṃ
pradīpam aham āgatā
avaśenaiva tadvartyā
preraṇaṃ tatra me kṛtam
body.translated_text: Overcome by greed, I had come to steal that lamp; only helplessly was the stirring of it done by me there with its wick.

body.text:
tato jātismṛtir janma
mānuṣyaṃ śobhanaṃ vapuḥ
vaśyaḥ patiḥ pṛthivīśaḥ
kiṃ punar dīpadāyinām
body.translated_text: Thence came the recollection of my former birth, a human birth, a beautiful body, and a husband subject to me, a lord of the earth—how much more for those who give lamps?

body.text:
etasmāt kāraṇād dīpān
aham etān aharniśam
prayacchāmi harer dhāmni
jñātam asya hi yat phalam
body.translated_text: For this reason I give these lamps day and night in the abode of <s>Hari</s>, for indeed the fruit of this is known.

body.text:
bhavatīnām idaṃ satyaṃ
mayoktaṃ keśavālaye
mūṣikatvād ahaṃ yena
karmaṇā siddhim āgatā
body.translated_text: This truth has been told by me to you in the abode of <s>Keśava</s>—by which deed I, from being a mouse, came to perfection."

body.text:
eṣa prabhāvo dīpasya
kārttike māsi sattama
viṣṇvāyatanadattasya
jagāda lalitā yathā
body.translated_text: This is the power of a lamp, O best one, given in the month of <s>Kārttika</s> in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as <s>Lalitā</s> declared.

body.text:
dine dine jagannātha
keśaveti samāhitaḥ
dadāti kārttike yas tu
viṣṇvāyatanadīpakam
body.translated_text: Day by day, concentrated, [saying] "<s>Jagannātha</s>, <s>Keśava</s>," he who gives a lamp in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in <s>Kārttika</s>—

body.text:
jātismaratvaṃ prajñāṃ ca
prākāśyaṃ sarvavastuṣu
avyāhatendriyatvaṃ ca
saṃprāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: he attains recollection of his former birth, wisdom, clearness in all matters, and unimpaired senses—there is no doubt.

body.text:
śeṣakāle ca cakṣuṣmān
medhāvī dīpado naraḥ
jāyate narakaṃ vāpi
tamaḥsaṃjñaṃ na paśyati
body.translated_text: And at the final time the lamp-giving man is born endowed with sight, intelligent; nor does he behold the hell named <s>Tamas</s> (darkness).

body.text:
ekādaśīṃ dvādaśīṃ vā
pratipakṣaṃ ca yo naraḥ
dīpaṃ dadāti kṛṣṇāya
tasyāpi śṛṇu yat phalam
body.translated_text: The man who on the eleventh or the twelfth, or each fortnight, gives a lamp to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—hear what is his fruit too.

body.text:
suvarṇamaṇimuktāḍhyaṃ
manojñam atiśobhanam
dīpamālākulaṃ divyaṃ
vimānaṃ so 'dhirohati
body.translated_text: He mounts a divine celestial chariot, rich with gold, gems, and pearls, charming, exceedingly beautiful, thronged with garlands of lamps.

body.text:
tasmād āyatane viṣṇor
dadyād dīpaṃ dvijottama
tāṃś ca dattān na hiṃseta
na ca tailaviyojitān
kurvīta dīpahartā tu
mūko 'ndho jāyate yataḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore one should give a lamp in the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of the twice-born; and one should not harm those given lamps, nor deprive them of oil; for the stealer of a lamp is born mute and blind.

body.text:
jāyate narakaṃ cāpi
tapaḥsaṃjñaṃ sa paśyati
body.translated_text: And he is also born [to behold] hell; he beholds the one named <s>Tapas</s>.

body.text:
andhe tāmasi duṣpāre
narake patitān kila
vikrośamānān kṣutkṣāmāñ
jagāda yamakiṃkaraḥ
body.translated_text: Fallen, indeed, into the hell <s>Andhatāmisra</s>, impassable, crying out, wasted with hunger, the servant of <s>Yama</s> addressed them:

body.text:
vilāpair alam atrāpi
kiṃ vo vilapite phalam
yadā pramādibhiḥ pūrvam
ātmātyantam upekṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: "Enough of laments here too; what fruit is there in your lamenting, when formerly by you, the heedless, the self was utterly disregarded?

body.text:
pūrvam ālocitaṃ naitat
kim apy ante bhaviṣyati
idānīṃ yātanābhogaḥ
kiṃ vilāpaḥ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: It was not pondered before, 'What at all will come to be in the end?' Now there is the experience of torment; what will lamentation do?

body.text:
deho dināni svalpāni
viṣayāś cātidurdharāḥ
etat ko na vijānāti
yena yūyaṃ pramādinaḥ
body.translated_text: The body lasts few days, and the sense-objects are exceedingly hard to control—who does not know this, by which you became heedless?

body.text:
jantujanmasahasrebhya
etasmin mānuṣyo yadi
tatrāpy ativimūḍhatvāt
kiṃ bhogān abhidhāvati
body.translated_text: If, out of thousands of births of creatures, a human birth [is gained], even there, out of utter delusion, why does one run after pleasures?

body.text:
viruddhaviṣayāsvāda-
muditair hasitaṃ ca yat
bhavadbhir āgataṃ duḥkhaṃ
vilāpapariṇāmikam
body.translated_text: And what was laughed at by you, gladdened with the relishing of forbidden objects—the misery that has come, ending in lamentation,

body.text:
adyakālikayā buddhyā
yad āgāmi na cintitam
paritāpāya taj jātaṃ
duḥkhaṃ karmavipākajam
body.translated_text: what was not pondered by the present-minded intellect as to come, that misery born of the ripening of action has arisen for torment.

body.text:
svalpam āyur manuṣyāṇāṃ
tadante paratantratā
bhujyate ca kṛtaṃ pūrvam
etat kiṃ vo na cintitam
body.translated_text: Short is the life of men, at its end dependence; and what was done before is enjoyed—why was this not pondered by you?

body.text:
yad abhūt paradāreṣu
prītaye 'ṅgakucādikam
yātanāduḥkharūpāya
narake ca tad āgatam
body.translated_text: What in others' wives, the limbs, breasts, and the rest, was for pleasure, that has come in hell to the form of the misery of torment.

body.text:
paradāramanohāri
yad bhavadbhir agīyata
hā māta ityādi rutaṃ
tad idānīṃ vilapyate
body.translated_text: What was sung by you, captivating to others' wives, the crying 'Ah mother!' and the like, that now is lamented.

body.text:
saṃdigdhaparalokānām
aihike nihatātmanām
mṛtānāṃ svakṛtaṃ karma
paścāttāpāya kevalam
body.translated_text: For those whose next world is doubtful, who have slain themselves in this world—for the dead, their own done deed is only for after-remorse.

body.text:
muhūrtārdhasukhāsvāda-
lubdhānām akṛtātmanām
anekavarṣakoṭiṣu
duḥkhadaṃ karma jāyate
body.translated_text: For those greedy for the relish of half a moment's pleasure, with unperfected selves, the deed becomes giver of misery for many millions of years.

body.text:
hā mātas tāta tāteti
bhavadbhiḥ kiṃ vilapyate
śubhāśubhaṃ nijaṃ karma
tad adya hy atra bhujyate
body.translated_text: 'Ah mother! father, father!'—why is this lamented by you? One's own good and evil deed is now enjoyed here.

body.text:
putradāragṛhakṣetra-
hitāya satatodyatāḥ
na kurvatni kathaṃ mūḍhāḥ
svalpam apy ātmano hitam
body.translated_text: Ever striving for the benefit of son, wife, house, and field, why do the fools not do even a little benefit for themselves?

body.text:
vañcito 'sau mayā labdham
idam asmād upāyataḥ
body.translated_text: 'He was cheated by me; this was obtained from him by stratagem'—

body.text:
na vetti kaścid ātmārthaṃ
vetti prakramato naraḥ
body.translated_text: no one knows the purpose of the self; man knows from the outset only [worldly schemes].

body.text:
na vetti sūryacandrādīn
kālam ātmānam eva ca
sākṣibhūtān aśeṣasya
śubhasyehāśubhasya ca
body.translated_text: He does not know the sun, moon, and the rest, time, and the self itself, which are the witnesses of the whole, of good and evil here.

body.text:
janmāny anyāni jāyante
putradārādidehinām
tadarthaṃ yat kṛtaṃ karma
tasya janmaśatāni tat
body.translated_text: Other births are born for the embodied ones, son, wife, and the rest; the deed that is done for their sake—that brings hundreds of births.

body.text:
aho mohasya māhātmyaṃ
mamatvaṃ narakeṣv api
krandate mātaraṃ tātaṃ
pīḍyamāno 'pi yat svayam
body.translated_text: Ah, the greatness of delusion! the sense of 'mine' even in the hells, where one cries out for mother and father, though himself being tormented.

body.text:
evam ākṛṣṭacittānāṃ
viṣayāsvādatarṣulaiḥ
nṝṇāṃ na jāyate buddhiḥ
paramārthāvalokinī
tathā ca viṣayāsaktiṃ
karoty avirataṃ manaḥ
body.translated_text: For men whose minds are thus dragged away, thirsting for the relish of sense-objects, the intellect that beholds the supreme truth does not arise; and so the mind ceaselessly makes attachment to sense-objects.

body.text:
ko 'tibhāro harer nāmni
jihvāyāḥ parikīrtane
body.translated_text: What great burden is there to the tongue in the proclaiming of the name of <s>Hari</s>?

body.text:
vartitaile 'lpamaulye 'pi
yad agnir labhyate mudhā
ato 'dhikataro lobhaḥ
ko vaś citte 'bhavat tadā
body.translated_text: Even though by the wick-oil of small price fire is obtained for nothing, greater than this what greed was there in your mind at that time,

body.text:
yeneyaṃ teṣu hasteṣu
svātantrye sati dīpakaḥ
mahāphalo viṣṇugṛhe
na datto narakāpahaḥ
body.translated_text: by which, when freedom was in those hands, the lamp of great fruit, the remover of hell, was not given in the house of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

body.text:
na vo vilapite kiṃcid
idānīṃ dṛśyate phalam
asvātantrye vilapatāṃ
svātantrye 'tipramādinām
body.translated_text: Of your lamenting nothing of fruit is now seen—of those who lament without freedom, who were exceedingly heedless when there was freedom.

body.text:
avaśyaṃpātinaḥ prāṇā
bhoktā jīvo hy aharniśam
dattaṃ ca labhate bhoktā
samaye viṣayān iti
body.translated_text: The breaths inevitably fall away; the soul is the enjoyer day and night; and the enjoyer obtains, when given, the sense-objects in due time.

body.text:
etat svātantryavadbhir vo
yuktam āsīt parīkṣitum
idānīṃ kiṃ vilāpena
sahadhvaṃ yad upāgatam
body.translated_text: This was fitting to be examined by you who had freedom; now what use is lamentation? Bear what has come.

body.text:
yady etad anabhīṣṭaṃ vo
yad duḥkhaṃ samupasthitam
tad bhūyo 'pi matiḥ pāpe
na kartavyā kathaṃcana
body.translated_text: If this misery that has befallen is unwished-for by you, then again the mind is in no way to be set on sin.

body.text:
kṛte 'pi pāpake karmaṇy
ajñānād aghanāśanam
kartavyam avyavasthitaṃ
smaradbhir madhusūdanam
body.translated_text: Even when a sinful deed has been done out of ignorance, the destroying of evil, though undetermined, is to be done by those who remember <s>Madhusūdana</s>."

body.text:
nārakās tadvacaḥ śrutvā
tām ūcur atiduḥkhitāḥ
kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhās tṛṣayā
parisphuṭitatālukāḥ
body.translated_text: The hell-dwellers, hearing that speech of his, exceedingly distressed, with throats wasted by hunger, palates split open by thirst, said to him:

body.text:
bho bho sādho kṛtaṃ karma
yad asmābhis tad ucyatām
narakasthair vipāko 'yaṃ
bhujyate yasya dāruṇaḥ
body.translated_text: "Ho, ho, good one! Let that deed which was done by us be told, the dreadful ripening of which is enjoyed by us dwelling in hell."

body.text:
yuṣmābhir yauvanonmāda-
muditair avivekibhiḥ
dyūtodyotāya govinda-
gṛhād dīpaḥ purā hṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: "By you, gladdened with the intoxication of youth, lacking discrimination, a lamp was of old stolen from the house of <s>Govinda</s> for the kindling of dice-play.

body.text:
tenāsmin narake ghore
kṣuttṛṣṇāparipīḍitāḥ
bhavantaḥ patitās tīvra-
śītavātavidāritāḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore in this terrible hell, tormented by hunger and thirst, you have fallen, torn by the fierce cold wind."

body.text:
etat te dīpadānasya
pradīpaharaṇasya ca
puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ ca kathitaṃ
keśavāyatane dvija
body.translated_text: This, the merit of lamp-giving and the sin of lamp-stealing in the temple of <s>Keśava</s>, has been told to you, O twice-born.

body.text:
sarvatraiva hi dīpasya
pradānaṃ dvija śasyate
viśeṣeṇa jagaddhātuḥ
keśavasya niveśane
body.translated_text: Everywhere the giving of a lamp is praised, O twice-born, but especially in the dwelling of the upholder of the world, <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
ye 'ndhā mūkā niḥśrutā nirvivekā
hīnās tais taiḥ sādhanair vipravarya
tais tair dīpāḥ sādhulokapradattā
devāgārād anyato vipraṇītāḥ
body.translated_text: Those who are blind, mute, deaf, lacking discrimination, deprived of these and those means, O best of <s>vipras</s>—by these and those [people], lamps given to good folk are diverted elsewhere from the temple of the god.

body.text:
āhlādaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ prītiṃ
karoti manasas tathā
keṣāṃcid darśanaṃ brahman
manuṣyāṇām aharniśam
body.translated_text: The sight of certain men, O <s>brahman</s>, gives delight to the eye and likewise pleasure to the mind, day and night.

body.text:
udvejanīyā bhūtānām
animittaṃ tathāpare
vadante vipriyaṃ naiva
prītiṃ kurvanti mānavāḥ
body.translated_text: And others are sources of distress to beings without cause; though they speak no unkind word, men give no pleasure.

body.text:
etad yasya phalaṃ brahman
dānasya tapaso 'thavā
upavāsasya vā tan me
yathāvad vaktum arhasi
body.translated_text: What is the fruit of this, O <s>brahman</s>—of a gift, or of austerity, or of a fast—that you ought to tell me duly.

body.text:
aprītidasya viprarṣe
vipāko yasya karmaṇaḥ
manuṣyāṇām aśeṣaṃ vai
tan mamācakṣva sattama
body.translated_text: O sage among <s>vipras</s>, the entire ripening of which deed of men is that of one who gives no pleasure—tell that to me, O best one.

body.text:
devabrāhmaṇavedeṣu
yajñeṣu ca narādhamaiḥ
yair jugupsā kṛtā dālbhya
manasāpy atimānibhiḥ
body.translated_text: By those lowest of men, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, exceedingly proud, by whom even in mind disgust was made toward the gods, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Vedas</s>, and sacrifices—

body.text:
teṣāṃ saṃdarśanāt sarvo
na sukhaṃ vindate dvija
vadanty apy anukūlāni
na teṣu prīyate janaḥ
body.translated_text: from beholding them no one finds happiness, O twice-born; even though they speak agreeable things, people take no delight in them.

body.text:
sparśād udvijate lokaḥ
kaṭu teṣāṃ ca darśanam
saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ ca nindā vai
kṛtā vedadvijātike
body.translated_text: People are repelled by their touch, and bitter is the sight of them—when conversation and slander were made toward the <s>Vedas</s> and the twice-born.

body.text:
tasmān na nindāṃ vedādau
na jugupsāṃ ca paṇḍitaḥ
yajñādau ca naraḥ kuryād
ya icchec chreya ātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore the wise man should make no slander toward the <s>Vedas</s> and the rest, and no disgust toward sacrifices and the rest, who would desire his own good.

body.text:
yais tu prītiḥ samasteṣu
vedadevadvijātiṣu
yajñādike caiva kṛtā
dālbhya taddarśanaṃ nṛṇām
body.translated_text: But those by whom love was made toward all—the <s>Vedas</s>, the gods, the twice-born, and toward sacrifices and the rest, O <s>Dālbhya</s>—the sight of them for men

body.text:
āhlādaś cakṣuṣaḥ prītir
manaso nirvṛtiḥ parā
saṃbhāṣaṇe tathāhlādaḥ
sarvalokasya jāyate
body.translated_text: is a delight of the eye, a pleasure of the mind, supreme peace; and likewise in conversing there arises delight for all the world.

body.text:
stutāḥ praśastāḥ saṃprītyā
pūjitā bahumānataḥ
śreyaḥ paraṃ prayacchanti
devā vedā makhā dvijāḥ
body.translated_text: Praised, extolled with love, worshipped with great honor, the gods, the <s>Vedas</s>, sacrifices, and the twice-born grant the supreme good.

body.text:
lokadvaye 'pi cāprītiṃ
paśuputradhanakṣayam
kurvanti dvijaśārdūla
eta eva vininditāḥ
body.translated_text: These very ones, O tiger among the twice-born, when reviled, bring about in both worlds displeasure and the loss of cattle, sons, and wealth.

body.text:
eta eva samākhyātāḥ
stavādigrahaṇe guṇāh
nindāyāḥ śravaṇe doṣa
eteṣām evam eva hi
body.translated_text: These very ones have been declared the virtues in taking up praise and the rest; the faults are in the hearing of slander—of these, just so.

body.text:
tasmāt stavyāḥ praśaṃsyāś ca
devā vedā dvijātayaḥ
yajñāś ca manasāpy eṣāṃ
na nindām ācared budhaḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore the gods, the <s>Vedas</s>, the twice-born, and sacrifices are to be praised and extolled; the wise man should not, even in mind, practice slander of them.

body.text:
anāyāsena bhagavan
dānenānyena kenacit
pāpaṃ praśamam āyāti
yena tad vaktum arhasi
body.translated_text: O Blessed One, by what other gift, without exertion, does sin come to calming—that you ought to tell.

body.text:
śṛṇu dālbhya mahāpuṇyāṃ
dvādaśīṃ pāpanāśanīm
yām upoṣya paraṃ puṇyaṃ
prāpnute śraddhayānvitaḥ
body.translated_text: Hear, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, of the greatly meritorious <s>dvādaśī</s>, the destroyer of sin, by fasting on which one endowed with faith attains supreme merit.

body.text:
māghamāse tu saṃprāpta
āṣāḍhārkṣaṃ bhaved yadi
mūlaṃ vā kṛṣṇapakṣasya
dvādaśyāṃ niyatas tadā
body.translated_text: When in the month of <s>Māgha</s> the lunar mansion <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> occurs, or <s>Mūla</s> of the dark fortnight on the <s>dvādaśī</s>, then, controlled,

body.text:
gṛhṇīyāt puṇyaphaladaṃ
vidhānaṃ tasya me śṛṇu
devadevaṃ samabhyarcya
susnātaḥ prayataḥ śuciḥ
body.translated_text: one should take up the merit-fruit-giving observance; hear it from me. Having well worshipped the god of gods, well bathed, restrained, pure,

body.text:
kṛṣṇanāmnā ca saṃstūya
ekādaśyāṃ mahāmate
upoṣito dvitīye 'hni
punaḥ saṃpūjya keśavam
body.translated_text: and having praised with the name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O greatly wise one, fasting on the eleventh, on the second day, again having worshipped <s>Keśava</s>,

body.text:
saṃstūya nāmnā ca tataḥ
kṛṣṇākhyena punaḥ punaḥ
dadyāt tilāṃs tu viprāya
kṛṣṇo me prīyatām iti
snānaprāśanayoḥ śastās
tathā kṛṣṇatilā mune
body.translated_text: and having praised with the name called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> again and again, one should give sesame to a <s>vipra</s>, [saying] "May <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> be pleased with me"; commended in bathing and in eating are black sesame, O sage.

body.text:
tilaprarohe jāyante
yāvatsaṃkhyās tilā dvija
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi
svargaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: As many sesame seeds as sprout in the growth of sesame, O twice-born, for that many thousands of years one is honored in the heavenly world.

body.text:
jātaś cehāpy arogo 'sau
naro janmani janmani
nāndho na badhiraś ceha
na kuṣṭhī na jugupsitaḥ
bhavaty etām uṣitvā tu
tilākhyāṃ dvādaśīṃ naraḥ
body.translated_text: Born here too free of disease, that man in birth after birth is here neither blind nor deaf, neither leprous nor loathsome; thus a man becomes who has observed this twelfth (<s>dvādaśī</s>) called <s>tila</s> (sesame)

body.text:
viṣṇoḥ prīṇanam atroktaṃ
samāpte varṣapāraṇe
pūjāṃ ca kuryād viprāya
bhūyo dadyāt tathā tilān
body.translated_text: The gratifying of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is here enjoined when the year's breaking-of-the-fast is complete; and he should perform worship for a <s>vipra</s>, and again give sesame likewise

body.text:
anena dālbhya vidhinā
tiladānād asaṃśayam
mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvair
nirāyāsena mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: By this rule, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, by the gift of sesame, without doubt a man is freed from all sins without exertion

body.text:
udbhṛtapulakaḥ sarvān
nirāyāsena mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: with the hair of his body bristling [in joy], a man [is freed] from all [sins] without exertion

body.text:
dānavidhis tathā śraddhā
sarvapātakaśāntaye
nārthaḥ prabhūto nāyāsaḥ
śārīro munisattama
body.translated_text: Thus the rule of giving and faith [suffice] for the calming of all sins; no abundant wealth, no bodily exertion [is needed], O best of sages

body.text:
anantasyāprameyasya
vyāpinaḥ paramātmanaḥ
nāmnāṃ nakṣatrabhedena
tithibhedena vā dvija
body.translated_text: Of the infinite, immeasurable, all-pervading Supreme Self, by the difference of the names according to the lunar mansion or the difference of lunar day, O twice-born,

body.text:
dānabhedena cākhyāto
vibhinnaphaladas tvayā
viśeṣaḥ kṣetrabhedena
kathyatāṃ yadi vidyate
body.translated_text: and by the difference of gift, you have declared [the names] as giving differing fruits; let the special distinction by difference of holy place (<s>kṣetra</s>) be told, if it exists

body.text:
yatha rkṣatithibhedena
teṣām eva punaḥ punaḥ
viśeṣaḥ kathito nāmnāṃ
viśeṣaphaladāyakaḥ
tathā kṣetraviśeṣeṇa
bhedaṃ nāmakṛtaṃ vada
body.translated_text: Just as, by difference of lunar mansion and lunar day, again and again, the special distinction of those very names, giving special fruit, has been told, so tell the distinction of names made by the particularity of holy place

body.text:
śṛṇu dālbhya yathākhyātam
arjunāya mahātmane
praṇipātaprasannena
viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
body.translated_text: Hear, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, as it was declared to the great-souled <s>Arjuna</s> by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-powerful, pleased by his obeisance

body.text:
kṛte bhārāvataraṇe
nivṛtte bhārate raṇe
āgamya śibiraṃ viṣṇū
rathasthaḥ prāha phālgunam
body.translated_text: When the unburdening of the earth had been accomplished, when the <s>Bhārata</s> war had ceased, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having come to the camp, standing on the chariot, said to <s>Phālguna</s> (Arjuna):

body.text:
iṣudhīgāṇḍivaṃ caiva
samādāya tvarānvitaḥ
avatīrya rathād vīra
dūre tiṣṭḥa dhanaṃjaya
body.translated_text: "Having taken up the quiver and the <s>Gāṇḍiva</s> bow, in haste, descending from the chariot, O hero, stand at a distance, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>

body.text:
avarokṣyāmy ahaṃ paścād
avatīrṇe tatas tvayi
etat kuru mahābāho
mā vilambasva phālguna
body.translated_text: I shall descend afterward, once you have descended; do this, O mighty-armed one; do not delay, <s>Phālguna</s>"

body.text:
evam uktas tathā cakre
vākyaṃ pārtho gadādhṛtaḥ
