avārohat tataḥ paścāt
svayam eva janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the mace-bearing son of <s>Pṛthā</s> did accordingly; he descended, and then afterward <s>Janārdana</s> himself [descended]

body.text:
avatīrṇe jagannāthe
svasamutthena vahninā
jajvāla sa rathaḥ sadyo
bhasmībhūtaś ca tatkṣaṇāt
sopaskarapatāko 'tha
sadhvajaḥ saha vājibhiḥ
body.translated_text: When the Lord of the world had descended, that chariot at once blazed up with a fire arisen from itself and was reduced to ash that very instant, together with its furnishings and banner, with its flag and with its horses

body.text:
sacchattro vahninā sadyo
ratho bhasmalavīkṛtaḥ
vahninā ca yathā kāṣṭhaṃ
sadyo bhasmalavīkṛtam
body.translated_text: Together with its parasol, the chariot was at once reduced to fragments of ash by the fire, just as wood is at once reduced to fragments of ash by fire

body.text:
tad adbhutaṃ mahad dṛṣṭvā
pārthaḥ papraccha keśavam
hṛṣṭaromā dvijaśreṣṭha
bhayavismayagadgadaḥ
body.translated_text: Seeing that great marvel, the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> asked <s>Keśava</s>, his hair bristling, O best of the twice-born, his voice faltering with fear and astonishment:

body.text:
āścaryaṃ puruṣavyāghra
kim etan madhusūdana
vināgninā ratho 'yaṃ me
dagdhas tṛṇacayo yathā
body.translated_text: "A wonder, O tiger among men, what is this, <s>Madhusūdana</s>? Without fire this chariot of mine has been burnt up like a heap of grass"

body.text:
bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādīnāṃ
karṇādīnāṃ ca phālguna
dagdho 'strair vividhair eṣa
pūrvam eva rathas tava
body.translated_text: "By the various weapons of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s> and the rest, and of <s>Karṇa</s> and the rest, O <s>Phālguna</s>, this chariot of yours was burnt up long before

body.text:
madadhiṣṭhitatvāt kaunteya
na śīrṇo 'yaṃ tadābhavat
pratyahan niśi cakreṇa
mayā nyastena rakṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: Because it was occupied by me, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, it did not then crumble; each day, at night, it was protected by the discus set down by me

body.text:
so 'yaṃ dagdho mahābāho
tvayy adya kṛtakarmaṇi
mayāvatārite cakre
mā pārtha kuru vismayam
body.translated_text: That same chariot is burnt today, O mighty-armed one, when your work is done, the discus having been withdrawn by me; do not be astonished, O son of <s>Pṛthā</s>"

body.text:
kaṃ bhavantam ahaṃ vidyām
atimānuṣaceṣṭitam
karmaṇātyadbhutenāgnir
dhūmenaiveha sūcitaḥ
body.translated_text: "As whom should I know you, of more-than-human deeds? By a most marvellous act, like fire by smoke alone, you are here revealed

body.text:
pūrvam eva yathākhyātaṃ
raṇārambhe tavārjuna
kālo 'smi lokanāśāya
pravṛtto 'haṃ yathādhunā
body.translated_text: Just as was declared before, at the beginning of the war, O <s>Arjuna</s>—'I am Time (<s>Kāla</s>), set in motion for the destruction of the worlds'—as I now [am]

body.text:
tan mayā sādhitaṃ kāryaṃ
tridaśānāṃ tathā bhuvaḥ
bhārāvataraṇārthāya
mama janma mahītale
body.translated_text: thus by me this task has been accomplished, of the thirty gods and of the earth; for the sake of unburdening the earth is my birth on the earth's surface"

body.text:
evam ukto 'rjunaḥ samyak
praṇipatya janārdanam
tuṣṭāva vāgbhir iṣṭābhir
udbhūtapulakas tataḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Arjuna</s>, having properly bowed to <s>Janārdana</s>, then praised him with cherished words, his hair bristling [with joy]:

body.text:
namo 'stu te cakradharograrūpa
namo 'stu te śārṅgadharāruṇākṣa
namo 'stu te 'bhyudyatakhaḍga raudra
namo 'stu vibhrāntagadāntakārin
body.translated_text: "Homage to you, bearer of the discus, of fierce form; homage to you, bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, of reddish eyes; homage to you, of raised sword, terrible; homage to you, ender [of foes] with whirling mace

body.text:
bhayena sanno 'smi savepathena
nāṅgāni me deva vaśaṃ prayānti
vācaḥ samuccārayataḥ skhalanti
keśā hṛṣīkeśa samucchvasanti
body.translated_text: I am sunk in fear, with trembling; my limbs, O god, do not obey me; my words falter as I utter them; my hairs stand on end, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>

body.text:
kālo bhavān kālakarālakarmā
yenaitad evaṃ kṣayam akṣayātman
kṣatraṃ samudbhūtaruṣā samastam
nītaṃ bhuvo bhāravirecanāya
body.translated_text: You are Time, whose deeds are terrible as Time, by whom this whole warrior-class (<s>kṣatra</s>), through arisen wrath, was thus brought to destruction, O imperishable Self, for the unburdening of the earth's load

body.text:
prasīda kartar jaya lokanātha
prasīda sarvasya ca pālanāya
sthitau samastasya ca kālarūpa
kṛtodyameśāna jayāvyayātman
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O Maker, be victorious, Lord of the worlds; be gracious for the protection of all; for the maintenance of all, O form of Time, your effort accomplished, O Lord, be victorious, O imperishable Self

body.text:
na me dṛg eṣā tava rūpam etad
draṣṭuṃ samarthā kṣubhito 'smi cāntaḥ
pūrvasvabhāvasthitavigraho 'pi
saṃlakṣyase 'tyantam asaumyarūpa
body.translated_text: This eye of mine is not able to behold this form of yours; I am agitated within; even though your body abides in its former nature, you appear exceedingly of un-mild form

body.text:
smarāmi rūpaṃ tava viśvarūpaṃ
yad darśitaṃ pūrvam abhūn mamaiva
yasmin mayā viśvam aśeṣam āsīd
dṛṣṭaṃ sayakṣoragadevadaityam
body.translated_text: I remember your form, the Universal Form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>), which was shown before to me alone, in which by me the whole universe entire was seen, with its <s>Yakṣas</s>, serpents, gods, and <s>Daityas</s>

body.text:
sā me smṛtir darśanabhāṣanādi-
prakurvato nātha gatā praṇāśam
kālo 'ham asmīty udite tvayā tu
samāgateyaṃ punar apy ananta
body.translated_text: That memory of mine, as I performed beholding, speaking and the rest, O Lord, did not pass into oblivion; but when 'I am Time' was uttered by you, it has come again, O <s>Ananta</s>

body.text:
kartā bhavān kāraṇam apy aśeṣam
kāryaṃ ca niṣkāraṇa kartṛrūpa
ādau sthitau saṃharaṇe ca deva
viśvasya viśvaṃ svayam eva ca tvam
body.translated_text: You are the Maker; you are also the cause entire and the effect, O causeless one, of the form of the Maker; in the beginning, in the maintenance, and in the dissolution of the universe, O god, you yourself are the universe

body.text:
brahmā bhavān viśvasṛg ādikāle
viśvasya rūpo 'si tathā visṛṣṭau
viṣṇuḥ sthitau pālanabaddhakakṣo
rudro bhavān saṃharaṇe prajānām
body.translated_text: You are <s>Brahmā</s>, creator of the universe, at the beginning of time; you are also the form of the universe in its emission; <s>Viṣṇu</s> in maintenance, girded for protection; you are <s>Rudra</s> in the dissolution of creatures

body.text:
ebhis tribhir nātha vibhūtibhedair
yaś cintyate kāraṇam ātmano 'pi
vedāntavedoditam asti viṣṇoḥ
padaṃ dhruvaṃ tat paramaṃ tvam eva
body.translated_text: By these three distinctions of manifestation (<s>vibhūti</s>), O Lord, that which is contemplated, the cause even of the self—there is the fixed, supreme station of <s>Viṣṇu</s> declared by the <s>Vedānta</s> and the <s>Veda</s>; that too is you alone

body.text:
yan nirguṇaṃ sarvavikalpahīnam
anantam asthūlam arūpagandham
paraṃ padaṃ vedavido vadanti
tvam eva tac chabdarasādihīnam
body.translated_text: That which is without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), free of all alternatives, infinite, subtle, without form or smell, which the knowers of the <s>Veda</s> call the supreme station—that too you are, devoid of sound, savour and the rest

body.text:
yathā hi mūle viṭapī mahādrumaḥ
pratiṣṭhitaskandhavarograśākhaḥ
tathā samastāmaramartyatiryag-
vyomādiśabdādimayaṃ tvayīdam
body.translated_text: For just as a great tree, a forest-lord, is established in its root with its mighty trunk and great fierce branches, so this [universe], consisting of all gods, mortals, beasts, sky, sound and the rest, [is established] in you

body.text:
muñcāmi yāvat paramāyudhāni
vairiṣv anantāhavadurmadeṣu
dṛṣṭvā hi tāvat sahasā patanto
nūnaṃ tavaivācyuta sa prabhāvaḥ
body.translated_text: As soon as I release my supreme weapons against foes maddened in endless battle, no sooner do I see them suddenly falling—surely that is your power alone, O <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
hatā hatās te bhavato dṛśaiva
mayā punaḥ keśava śastrapūgaiḥ
kāh karṇabhīṣmapramukhān vijetuṃ
yuṣmatprasādena vinā samarthaḥ
body.translated_text: Slain, slain are they by your glance alone; how could I again, O <s>Keśava</s>, with my volleys of weapons, be able to conquer those headed by <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s> without your grace?

body.text:
triśūlapāṇir mama yaḥ purastān
niṣūdayan vairibalaṃ jagāma
jñātaṃ mayā sāṃpratam etad īśa
tava prasādasya hi sā vibhūtiḥ
body.translated_text: The trident-handed one who went before me, slaying the army of foes—now I have understood this, O Lord: that was the manifestation of your grace

body.text:
yamendravitteśajaleśavahni-
sūryātmako yaś ca mamāstrapūgaḥ
nāśāya nābhūt patito 'pi kāye
tvatsaṃnidhānasya hi so 'nubhāvaḥ
body.translated_text: That volley of weapons of mine, made up of <s>Yama</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Kubera</s> (lord of wealth), <s>Varuṇa</s> (lord of waters), <s>Agni</s> (fire), and <s>Sūrya</s>—even when it fell upon a body it served not for destruction; that indeed was the effect of your presence

body.text:
bālye bhavān yāni cakāra deva
karmāṇy asahyāni surāsurāṇām
tair eva jānīma na yat paraṃ tvāṃ
doṣaḥ sa nirdoṣo manuṣyatāyāḥ
body.translated_text: The deeds you did in childhood, O god, unbearable to gods and demons—by those very deeds we know you not to be supreme; that fault is the faultless [fault] of [your assumed] humanity

body.text:
tālocchritāgraṃ gurubhārasāram
āyāmavistāravad adyajātaḥ
pādāgravikṣepavibhinnabhāṇḍaṃ
cikṣepa ko 'nyaḥ śakaṭaṃ yathā tvam
body.translated_text: Just born, who other than you flung, like a cart, the wagon (<s>śakaṭa</s>) tall as a palm-top, heavy with weight, of [great] length and breadth, its vessels broken by the kick of your foot's tip?

body.text:
anyena kenācyuta pūtanāyāḥ
prāṇaiḥ samaṃ pītam asṛgvimiśram
tvayā yathā stanyam atīvabālye
goṣṭhe ca bhagnau yamalārjunau tau
body.translated_text: By what other, O <s>Acyuta</s>, was the breast-milk of <s>Pūtanā</s> drunk together with her life, mingled with blood, as by you in earliest infancy; and in the cowherd-station those two, the twin <s>Arjuna</s>-trees, were broken?

body.text:
viṣānaloṣṇāmbunipātabhīmam
āsphoṭya ko vā bhuvi manuṣo 'nyaḥ
nanarta pādābjanipīḍitasya
phaṇaṃ samāruhya ca kāliyasya
body.translated_text: Terrible with the downpour of venom, fire, heat and water, what other man on earth, having clapped [in challenge], danced, mounting upon the hood of <s>Kāliya</s>, who was crushed by your lotus-foot?

body.text:
sureśasaṃdeśavirodhavatsu
varṣatsu megheṣu gavān nimittam
dināni saptāsti ca kasya śaktir
govardhanaṃ dhārayituṃ kareṇa
body.translated_text: When the clouds, opposing the command of the lord of the gods (Indra), rained for seven days on account of the cattle—whose is the power to hold up <s>Govardhana</s> with one hand?

body.text:
pralambacāṇūramukhān nihatya
kaṃsāsuraṃ yasya bibheti śakraḥ
tam aṣṭavarṣo nijaghāna ko 'nyo
nirāyodho nātha manuṣyajanmā
body.translated_text: Having slain <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Cāṇūra</s> and the rest, who other, an eight-year-old, weaponless, of human birth, slew the demon <s>Kaṃsa</s>, of whom even <s>Śakra</s> is afraid, O Lord?

body.text:
bāṇārtham abhyudyatam ugraśūlaṃ
nirjitya saṃkhye tripurārim ekaḥ
sakārttikeyajvaram astrabāhuṃ
karoti ko bāṇam anacyuto 'nyaḥ
body.translated_text: Having alone conquered in battle <s>Bāṇa</s>'s ally, the fierce-tridented foe of <s>Tripura</s> (Śiva), raised up for <s>Bāṇa</s>'s sake, together with <s>Kārttikeya</s>-fever and his weapon-arms—who but the un-fallen (Acyuta) renders <s>Bāṇa</s> [helpless]?

body.text:
kaḥ pārijātaṃ surasundarīṇāṃ
sadopabhogyaṃ vijitendrasainyaḥ
svargān mahīm ucchritavīryadhairyaḥ
samānayām āsa yathā prabho tvam
body.translated_text: Who, having conquered <s>Indra</s>'s army, of exalted heroism and steadfastness, brought from heaven to earth the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree, the perpetual enjoyment of the celestial beauties, as you did, O Lord?

body.text:
hatvā hayagrīvam udāravīryaṃ
niśumbhaśumbhau narakaṃ ca ko 'nyaḥ
jagrāha kanyāpuram ātmano 'rthaṃ
prāgjyotiṣākhye nagare mahātman
body.translated_text: Having slain <s>Hayagrīva</s> of noble valour, <s>Niśumbha</s> and <s>Śumbha</s>, and <s>Naraka</s>—who other seized the maidens' palace for his own sake in the city named <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>, O great-souled one?

body.text:
sthitau sthitas tvaṃ paripāsi viśvaṃ
tais tair upāyair avinītabhītaiḥ
maitrī na yeṣāṃ vinayāya tāṃs tān
sarvān bhavān saṃharate 'vyayātman
body.translated_text: Established in maintenance, you protect the universe by these and those means, fearless before the undisciplined; those with whom there is no friendship that leads to their discipline—all of them you destroy, O imperishable Self

body.text:
hitāya teṣāṃ kapilādirūpiṇā
tvayānuśastā bahavo 'nujīvāḥ
yeṣāṃ na maitrī hṛdi te na neyā
viśvopakārī vadha eva teṣām
body.translated_text: For their benefit, in the form of <s>Kapila</s> and the rest, many living beings were instructed by you; for those in whose heart there is no friendship and who cannot be led [aright], their very slaying benefits the universe

body.text:
itthaṃ bhavān duṣṭavadhena nūnaṃ
viśvopakārāya vibho pravṛttaḥ
sthitau sthitaṃ pālanam eva viṣṇuḥ
karoti hanty antagato 'ntarudraḥ
body.translated_text: Thus you indeed, by the slaying of the wicked, are engaged for the benefit of the universe, O all-pervading one; established in maintenance, <s>Viṣṇu</s> performs protection alone; reaching the end, the inner <s>Rudra</s> destroys

body.text:
etāni cānyāni ca duṣkarāṇi
dṛṣṭāni karmāṇi tathāpi satyam
manyāmahe tvāṃ jagataḥ prasūtiṃ
kiṃ kurma māyā tava mohanīyam
body.translated_text: These and other hard-to-do deeds are seen; yet truly we deem you the source of the world; what can we do—your <s>Māyā</s> is bewildering

body.text:
tvaṃ sarvam etat tvayi sarvam etat
tvattas tathaitat tava caitad īśa
etat svarūpaṃ tava sarvabhūtaṃ
vibhūtibhedair bahubhiḥ sthitasya
body.translated_text: You are all this; all this is in you; from you is all this; and this is yours, O Lord; this is your own nature, being all beings, abiding by many distinctions of manifestation

body.text:
prasīda kṛṣṇācyuta vāsudeva
janārdanānanta nṛsiṃha viṣṇo
manuṣyasāmānyadhiyā yadīśa
dṛṣṭo mayā tat kṣamasvādideva
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>; if by me, O Lord, you have been seen with a mind reckoning you a common man, forgive that, O primeval god

body.text:
na vedmi sadbhāvam ahaṃ tavādya
sadbhāvabhūtasya carācarasya
yo vai bhavān ko 'pi nato 'smi tasmai
manuṣyarūpāya caturbhujāya
body.translated_text: I do not know today your true being, you who are the true being of the moving and unmoving; whoever you indeed are, to that one I have bowed, to the human-formed, four-armed one

body.text:
devadeva jagannātha
sarvapāpaharo bhava
hetumātras tv ahaṃ tatra
tvayaitad upasaṃhṛtam
body.translated_text: O god of gods, Lord of the world, be the remover of all sin; I am there but a mere instrument; by you this [host] was withdrawn

body.text:
prasīdeśa hṛṣīkeśa
akṣauhiṇyā daśāṣṭa ca
tvayā grastā bhuvo bhūtyai
hetubhūtā hi madvidhāḥ
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O Lord, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>; the eighteen <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> (armies) were devoured by you for the welfare of the earth; for those like me are but instrumental causes

body.text:
vayam anye ca govinda
narāḥ krīḍanakās tava
madvidhaiḥ karaṇair deva
karoṣi sthitipālanam
body.translated_text: We and others, O <s>Govinda</s>, men, are your playthings; by instruments such as me, O god, you perform the maintenance and protection [of the world]

body.text:
yad atra sad asad vāpi
kiṃcid uccāritaṃ mayā
bhaktimān iti tat sarvaṃ
kṣantavyaṃ mama keśava
body.translated_text: Whatever here, true or false, anything has been uttered by me—being a devotee—all that of mine is to be forgiven, O <s>Keśava</s>"

body.text:
evaṃ stutas tataḥ prāha
prītimāṃs taṃ janārdanaḥ
pariṣvajya mahābāhuṃ
samāśvāsya ca phālgunam
body.translated_text: Thus praised, then <s>Janārdana</s>, well pleased, spoke to him, having embraced the mighty-armed one and consoled <s>Phālguna</s>

body.text:
prvāca bhagavān devaḥ
prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
body.translated_text: The Blessed Lord, the god, spoke with a greatly delighted inner self:

body.text:
yas tvāṃ vetti sa māṃ vetti
yas tvām anu sa mām anu
abhedenātmanā vedmī
tvām ahaṃ pāṇḍunandana
body.translated_text: "He who knows you knows me; he who follows you follows me; I know you, O son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, as undifferentiated from my own self

body.text:
mamāṃśatvaṃ mahābāho
jagataḥ pālanecchayā
bhuvo bhārāvatārārthaṃ
pṛthak pārtha mayā kṛtam
body.translated_text: Your being a portion of me, O mighty-armed one, was made by me separate, O son of <s>Pṛthā</s>, out of the wish to protect the world, for the sake of unburdening the earth

body.text:
devadaityoragā yakṣā
gandharvāḥ kiṃnarāpsarāḥ
rākṣasāś ca piśācāś ca
paśupakṣisarīsṛpāḥ
body.translated_text: Gods, <s>Daityas</s>, serpents, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Piśācas</s>, beasts, birds, and reptiles,

body.text:
vṛkṣagulmādayaḥ śailāḥ
sarvabhūtāni cārjuna
mamaivāṃśāni bhūtāni
viddhi sarvāṇy ariṃdama
body.translated_text: trees, shrubs and the rest, mountains, and all beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>—know all beings to be portions of me alone, O subduer of foes"

body.text:
bhagavan sarvabhūtātman
sarvabhūteṣu vai bhavān
paramātmasvarūpeṇa
sthitaṃ vedmi tad avyayam
body.translated_text: "O Blessed One, Self of all beings, you indeed abide in all beings in the form of the Supreme Self; that I know to be imperishable

body.text:
kṣetreṣu yeṣu yeṣu tvaṃ
cintanīyo mayācyuta
cetasaḥ praṇidhānārthaṃ
tan mamākhyātum arhasi
body.translated_text: In which holy places (<s>kṣetra</s>) you are to be contemplated by me, O <s>Acyuta</s>, for the sake of fixing my mind—that you ought to declare to me

body.text:
yatra yatra ca yan nāma
prītaye bhavataḥ stutau
prasādasumukho nātha
tan mamāśeṣato vada
body.translated_text: And in whatever place, by whatever name, in praise, [you have] delight, O Lord of gracious countenance—tell me that completely"

body.text:
sarvagaḥ sarvabhūto 'haṃ
na hi kiṃcid mayā vinā
carācare jagaty asmin
vidyate kurusattama
body.translated_text: "I am all-pervading, being all beings; for there is nothing without me in this moving and unmoving world, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>

body.text:
tathāpi yeṣu sthāneṣu
cintanīyo 'ham arjuna
stotavyo nāmabhir yais tu
śrūyatāṃ tad vadāmi te
body.translated_text: Yet in which places I am to be contemplated, O <s>Arjuna</s>, and by which names I am to be praised—let it be heard; that I tell you

body.text:
puṣkare puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
gayāyāṃ ca gadādharam
lohadaṇḍe tathā viṣṇuṃ
stuvaṃs tarati duṣkṛtam
body.translated_text: At <s>Puṣkara</s> [praising] <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, at <s>Gayā</s> <s>Gadādhara</s>, and likewise <s>Viṣṇu</s> at <s>Lohadaṇḍa</s>—praising [these], one crosses over evil-doing

body.text:
kṣvāmācye kumāraṃ
nepāle lokabhāvanam
body.translated_text: [...] <s>Kumāra</s>, in <s>Nepāla</s> the World-creator (<s>Lokabhāvana</s>),

body.text:
rāghavaṃ citrakūṭe tu
prabhāse daityasūdanam
vṛndāvane ca govindaṃ
mā stuvan puṇyabhāg bhavet
body.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> at <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, at <s>Prabhāsa</s> the slayer of the <s>Daityas</s>, and <s>Govinda</s> at <s>Vṛndāvana</s>—praising [these], one would be a partaker of merit

body.text:
mandodapāne vaikuṇṭhaṃ
māhantre cācyutaṃ vibhum
body.translated_text: <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> at <s>Mandodapāna</s>, and the all-pervading <s>Acyuta</s> at <s>Māhantra</s>,

body.text:
jayaṃ jayantyāṃ tadvac ca
jayantaṃ hastināpure
vārāhaṃ kardamāle tu
kāśmīre cakrapāṇinam
body.translated_text: <s>Jaya</s> at <s>Jayantī</s> likewise, and <s>Jayanta</s> at <s>Hastināpura</s>, the Boar (<s>Vārāha</s>) at <s>Kardamāla</s>, and the discus-handed one (<s>Cakrapāṇi</s>) in <s>Kāśmīra</s>,

body.text:
janārdanaṃ ca kubjāmre
mathurāyāṃ ca keśavam
kubjake śrīdharaṃ tadvad
gaṅgādvāre surottamam
body.translated_text: and <s>Janārdana</s> at <s>Kubjāmra</s>, and <s>Keśava</s> at <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s> likewise at <s>Kubjaka</s>, the best of gods at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>

body.text:
śālagrāme mahāyogiṃ
hariṃ govardhanācale
piṇḍārake caturbāhuṃ
śaṅkhoddhāre ca śaṅkhinam
body.translated_text: [Remember] <s>Hari</s> the great yogi at <s>Śālagrāma</s>, at the <s>Govardhana</s> mountain, the four-armed one at <s>Piṇḍāraka</s>, and the conch-bearer at <s>Śaṅkhoddhāra</s>

body.text:
vāmanaṃ ca kurukṣetre
yamunāyāṃ trivikramam
body.translated_text: and <s>Vāmana</s> at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Trivikrama</s> on the <s>Yamunā</s>

body.text:
vanamālaṃ ca kiṣkindhāyāṃ
devaṃ raivatake dvija
kāśījale mahāyogaṃ
devaṃ cāmitatejasam
vaiśākhayūpe ajitaṃ
virajāyāṃ viprakṣayam
body.translated_text: and the forest-garlanded one at <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, the god at <s>Raivataka</s>, O twice-born; the great yogi at the waters of <s>Kāśī</s>, the god of immeasurable splendor; <s>Ajita</s> at the <s>Vaiśākhayūpa</s>, <s>Viprakṣaya</s> at <s>Virajā</s>

body.text:
viśveśvaraṃ tathā śoṇe
kapilaṃ pūrvasāgare
body.translated_text: likewise <s>Viśveśvara</s> at the <s>Śoṇa</s>, <s>Kapila</s> at the eastern ocean

body.text:
śvetadvīpapatiṃ cāpi
gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame
bhūdharaṃ devikānadyāṃ
prayāge caiva mādhavam
body.translated_text: and also the lord of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> at the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the ocean, <s>Bhūdhara</s> on the <s>Devikā</s> river, and <s>Mādhava</s> at <s>Prayāga</s>

body.text:
naranārāyaṇākhyaṃ ca
tathā badarikāśrame
samudre dakṣiṇe stavyaṃ
padmanābheti phālguna
body.translated_text: and him called <s>Nara-Nārāyaṇa</s>, likewise at the <s>Badarikāśrama</s>, to be praised in the southern ocean as <s>Padmanābha</s>, O <s>Phālguna</s>

body.text:
dvārakāyāṃ tathā kṛṣṇaṃ
stuvaṃs tarati durgatim
rāmaṃ nāma mahendrādrau
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tathārbude
body.translated_text: and likewise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> at <s>Dvārakā</s>—praising him, one crosses beyond misfortune; him named <s>Rāma</s> on the <s>Mahendra</s> mountain, likewise <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> at <s>Arbuda</s>

body.text:
aśvatīrthe hayagrīvaṃ
viśvarūpaṃ himācale
nṛsiṃhaṃ kṛtasauce ca
vipāśāyāṃ dvijapriyam
body.translated_text: <s>Hayagrīva</s> at <s>Aśvatīrtha</s>, <s>Viśvarūpa</s> on the <s>Himācala</s>, and <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> at <s>Kṛtasauca</s>, the lover of the twice-born on the <s>Vipāśā</s>

body.text:
naimiṣe yajñapuruṣaṃ
jambūmārge tathācyutam
anantaṃ saindhavāraṇye
daṇḍake śāṅgadhāriṇam
body.translated_text: the sacrifice-Person at <s>Naimiṣa</s>, likewise <s>Acyuta</s> on the <s>Jambūmārga</s>, <s>Ananta</s> in the <s>Saindhava</s> forest, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s>

body.text:
utpalāvartake śauriṃ
narmadāyāṃ śriyaḥ patim
dāmodaraṃ raivatake
nandāyāṃ jalaśāyinam
body.translated_text: <s>Śauri</s> at <s>Utpalāvartaka</s>, the lord of <s>Śrī</s> on the <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Dāmodara</s> at <s>Raivataka</s>, him who reclines on the waters on the <s>Nandā</s>

body.text:
sarvayogeśvaraṃ caiva
sindhusāgarasaṃgame
sahyādrau devadeveśaṃ
vaikuṇṭhaṃ māgadhe vane
body.translated_text: and the Lord of all yoga at the confluence of the <s>Sindhu</s> and the ocean, the Lord of the gods of gods on the <s>Sahya</s> mountain, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> in the <s>Māgadha</s> forest

body.text:
sarvapāpaharaṃ vindhye
uḍreṣu puruṣottamam
hṛdaye cāpi kaunteya
paramātmānam ātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: the remover of all sins in the <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s> among the <s>Uḍras</s>, and also in the heart, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, the supreme self of one's own self

body.text:
vaṭe vaṭe vaiśravaṇaṃ
catvare catvare śivam
parvate parvate rāmaṃ
sarvatra madhusūdanam
body.translated_text: <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in every fig-tree, <s>Śiva</s> in every courtyard, <s>Rāma</s> on every mountain, <s>Madhusūdana</s> everywhere

body.text:
naraṃ bhūmau tathā vyomni
kaunteya garuḍadhvajam
vāsudevaṃ ca sarvatra
saṃsmarañ jyotiṣāṃ patim
body.translated_text: <s>Nara</s> on the earth and likewise in the sky, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s>, and <s>Vāsudeva</s> everywhere—recalling the Lord of the luminaries

body.text:
arcayan praṇamaṃs tu tvaṃ
saṃsmaraṃś ca dhanaṃjaya
eteṣv etāni nāmāni
naraḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: worshipping, bowing, and recalling, O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, [him] in these [places by] these names, a man is released from sins

body.text:
sthāneṣv eteṣu mannāmnām
eteṣāṃ prīṇanaṃ naraḥ
dvijānāṃ prīṇanaṃ kṛtvā
svargaloke 'bhijāyate
body.translated_text: [Uttering] in these places these names of mine, a man, having made the gladdening of these and the gladdening of the twice-born, is reborn in the world of heaven

body.text:
nāmāny etāni kaunteya
sthānāny etāni cātmavān
jayaṃ vai pañcapañcāśat
trisandhyaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: These names, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, and these places—the self-possessed one, the <s>Jaya</s> of fifty-five, [reciting] at the three twilights, devoted to me

body.text:
trīṇi janmāni yat pāpam
avasthātritaye kṛtam
tat kṣālayaty asaṃdigdhaṃ
jāyate ca satāṃ kule
body.translated_text: the sin which was committed in three births, in the threefold state, that he washes away undoubtedly, and he is born in the family of the good

body.text:
dviṣkālaṃ vā japann eva
divārātrau ca yat kṛtam
tasmād vimucyate pāpāt
sadbhāvaparamo naraḥ
body.translated_text: Reciting even twice [a day], he is released from the sin committed by day and by night—the man supremely devoted to sincere being

body.text:
japtāny etāni kaunteya
sakṛcchraddhāsamanvitam
mocayante naraṃ pāpād
yat tatraiva dine kṛtam
body.translated_text: These [names] recited, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, once, joined with faith, release a man from the sin committed on that very day

body.text:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ
jayaṃ kuru kulodvaha
grahānukūlatāṃ caiva
karoty āśu na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: It bestows what is blessed, glorious, life-giving, victory, O upholder of the family, and likewise it quickly brings favorableness of the planets—there is no doubt

body.text:
upoṣito matparamaḥ
sthāneṣv eteṣu mānavaḥ
kṛtāyatanavāsaś ca
prāpnoty abhimataṃ phalam
body.translated_text: Fasting, supremely devoted to me, a man in these places, and dwelling at the established sanctuary, attains the desired fruit

body.text:
utkrāntir apy aśeṣeṣu
sthāneṣv eteṣu śasyate
anyasthānāc chataguṇam
eteṣv anaśanādikam
body.translated_text: Even departure [death] is commended in all these places; in these, fasting and the rest is a hundredfold over [that at] another place

body.text:
yas tu matparamaḥ kālaṃ
karoty eteṣu mānavaḥ
devānām api pūjyo 'sau
mama loke mahīyate
body.translated_text: But that man who, supremely devoted to me, makes his end in these [places], he is to be worshipped even by the gods, and is honored in my world

body.text:
yan na tāpāya vai puṃsāṃ
bhavaty āmuṣmikaṃ kṛtam
tāpāya yac ca bhavati
tad ācakṣva mahāmune
body.translated_text: Tell me, O great sage, that which, done here, is not for the torment of men in the next world, and that which is for torment

body.text:
upavāsaprabhāvaṃ ca
kṛṣṇārādhanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
kathayeha mama brahman
na ca tṛpyāmi kathyate
body.translated_text: and the power of fasting for one who longs for the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—tell it here to me, O <s>brahman</s>; I am not sated though it is told

body.text:
śrūyatāṃ dālbhya yat pṛṣṭāḥ
kautukād bhavatā vayam
āmuṣmikaṃ na tāpāya
yac ca tāpāya jāyate
body.translated_text: Let it be heard, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, what we, asked by you out of curiosity, [shall tell]—what done here is not for torment in the next world, and what comes to be for torment

body.text:
upoṣitaprabhāvaṃ ca
kṛṣṇārādhanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
kathayāmi yathāvṛttaṃ
pūrvam eva mahāmate
body.translated_text: and the power of fasting for one who longs for the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, I tell as it happened, of old, O greatly wise one

body.text:
vaidiśaṃ nāma nagaraṃ
prakhyātam iha sattama
tatra vaiśyo 'bhavat pūrvaṃ
vīrabhadra iti śrutaḥ
body.translated_text: There is a city named <s>Vaidiśa</s>, renowned here, O most excellent one; there formerly was a <s>vaiśya</s> known as <s>Vīrabhadra</s>

body.text:
bhāryājāmātṛduhitṛ-
putrapautrasnuṣānvitaḥ
prabhūtabhṛtyavargaś ca
bahuvyāpārakārakaḥ
body.translated_text: endowed with wife, son-in-law, daughter, son, grandson, and daughter-in-law, and with a great host of servants, doing much business

body.text:
putrapautrādibharaṇa-
vyāsaktamatir eva ca
paralokaṃ prati matis
tasya cātyantadurmukhā
body.translated_text: and his mind was attached to the maintenance of sons, grandsons, and the rest, and his thought toward the next world was exceedingly averse

body.text:
cakārānudinaṃ so 'tha
nyāyānyāyair dhanārjanam
sarvatrānyatra niḥsnehaḥ
parasve cātitarṣulaḥ
body.translated_text: He then made, day after day, the earning of wealth by just and unjust means; everywhere else without affection, and greatly greedy for the wealth of others

body.text:
na juhoty udite kāle
na dadāty atitṛṣṇayā
babhūva codyamas tasya
putrādibharaṇe paraḥ
body.translated_text: He does not offer oblation at the appointed time, he does not give out of excessive greed; and his effort was wholly bent upon the maintenance of sons and the rest

body.text:
nityanaimittikānāṃ ca
hāniṃ cakre svakarmaṇām
tṛṣṇābhibhūto viprarṣe
svavargabharaṇādhṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: He made the loss of his own daily and occasional rites, overcome by greed, O sage among <s>vipras</s>, held fast by the maintenance of his own group

body.text:
kālena gacchatā so 'tha
mṛto vindhyāṭavītaṭe
yātanādehabhṛt preto
grīṣmakāle 'bhavan mune
body.translated_text: Then, as time passed, he died on the bank of the <s>Vindhya</s> forest, and became a <s>preta</s> (departed spirit) bearing a body of torment, in the summer season, O sage

body.text:
taṃ dadarśa mahābhāgo
divyajñānasamanvitaḥ
vedavedāntavid vidvān
pipīto nāma vai dvijaḥ
body.translated_text: Him a greatly fortunate one beheld, endowed with divine knowledge, learned, a knower of the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedānta</s>, a twice-born one named <s>Pipīta</s>

body.text:
bhāskarasyāṃśubhir dīptair
dahyantam anivāraṇaiḥ
prataptavālukāmadhye
tṛṣā cātyantapīḍitam
body.translated_text: being burned by the blazing, unrestrained rays of the sun, exceedingly tormented by thirst in the midst of the heated sands,

body.text:
kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhaṃ śuṣkāsyaṃ
stabdhodvṛttavilocanam
niṣkrāntajihvam aṅgeṣu
visphoṭaiḥ sarvataś citam
body.translated_text: his throat emaciated by hunger, his face dry, his eyes fixed and rolled up, his tongue lolling out, covered all over with eruptions on his limbs,

body.text:
niśvāsāyāsakhedena
viralāsyam anādaram
body.translated_text: with sparse speech through the weariness of the exertion of breathing, without dignity,

body.text:
śrāntaṃ makṣikayākīrṇaṃ
durdagdhaṃ cātidāruṇam
body.translated_text: exhausted, swarmed by flies, badly burned and most terrible,

body.text:
nijena karmaṇā baddham
asamarthaṃ palāyane
body.translated_text: bound by his own deeds, unable to flee

body.text:
taṃ tādṛśam atho dṛṣṭvā
gārdabheyo mahāmuniḥ
pipītaḥ prāha viprarṣiḥ
kāruṇyastimitaṃ vacaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, having seen him in such a state, the great sage <s>Pipīta</s>, the descendant of <s>Gardabha</s>, the sage among <s>vipras</s>, spoke a word soft with compassion

body.text:
jānann api tathā prāptaṃ
tadanuṣṭhānajaṃ phalam
jantos tasyopakārāya
sarvato hlādayann iva
body.translated_text: though knowing the fruit, born of his conduct, to have come about thus, for the benefit of that creature, gladdening him as it were on all sides:

body.text:
adhaḥ sūryāṃśubhis taptair
bahubhir yānapāṃsubhiḥ
upary arkakarair ugrais
tṛṣā cārtas tathā kṣudhā
body.translated_text: "Below by the heated rays of the sun and the abundant dust of vehicles, above by the fierce rays of the sun, afflicted thus by thirst and by hunger,

body.text:
anyais tathādhibhir ghorair
aviṣahyair avāraṇaiḥ
kathayeha yathātattvam
ekākī dahyase katham
body.translated_text: and by other terrible torments, unbearable and unwarded—tell me here truly: how is it that you, alone, are being burned?"

body.text:
tasyaitad vacanaṃ śrutvā
pipītasya savedanam
yātanāstha uvācedaṃ
kṛcchrād ucchvāsya mastakam
body.translated_text: Having heard this word of <s>Pipīta</s>, with pain, he who stood in torment said this, with difficulty lifting up his head by breathing:

body.text:
brahman nālocitaṃ pūrvaṃ
katham ante bhaviṣyati
aśāśvate śāśvatadhīs
tena dahyāmi durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "O <s>brahman</s>, it was not considered before, how it will be in the end; with thought of the eternal in the non-eternal, by that I burn, of evil mind"

body.text:
dhanāpaṇagṛhakṣetra-
putradārahite rataḥ
nātmano 'haṃ hitārambhī
tena dahyāmi durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "Delighting in wealth, shops, house, field, sons, and wife—I was not one who undertook my own welfare; by that I burn, of evil mind"

body.text:
idaṃ kariṣye kṛtvedaṃ
kariṣyāmy aparaṃ tv idam
itīcchāśatasaro 'haṃ
tena dahyāmi durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "'I shall do this; having done this, I shall do yet this other'—thus did I move along a hundred channels of desire; by that I burn, of evil mind"

body.text:
juhomi yadi tan nāsti
dadāmi yadi sīdati
kuṭumbam iti mūḍho 'ham
tena dahyāmi durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "'If I offer oblation, that [for the family] is wanting; if I give, [the family] sinks'—thus, deluded, [thinking] of the household, by that I burn, of evil mind"

body.text:
śītoṣṇavarṣābhibhavaṃ
lobhāt soḍḥaṃ mayāśubham
tad eva hi na dharmārthaṃ
tena dahyāmi durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "The overpowering of cold, heat, and rain was endured by me out of greed, inauspiciously; that itself was not for the sake of <s>dharma</s>; by that I burn, of evil mind"

body.text:
pitṛdevamanuṣyāṇām
adattvāpoṣitā hi ye
te 'nyatra kvāpi vartante
dahyāmy eko 'tra durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "Those who, fed without giving to the fathers, gods, and men, abide somewhere elsewhere; I burn alone here, of evil mind"

body.text:
putrabhṛtyakalatreṣu
mama tv ādṛtamānasaḥ
kṛtvā karmāṇy asādhūni
dahyāmy eko 'tra durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "With my mind devoted to sons, servants, and wives, having done unrighteous deeds, I burn alone here, of evil mind"

body.text:
mṛte mayi dhane tasminn
anyāyopārjite mayā
nūnaṃ mameti vartante
dahyāmy eko 'tra durmatiḥ
body.translated_text: "When I died, of that wealth unjustly earned by me, surely [thinking] 'it is mine' they abide; I burn alone here, of evil mind"

body.text:
na hi naḥ pūjitā gehān
nirgatā dvijasattamāḥ
svavargahitakāmasya
tena dahyāmy aharniśam
body.translated_text: "For the best of the twice-born did not go forth worshipped from our house, of me who desired the welfare of my own group—by that I burn day and night"

body.text:
yan me na pūjitā devāḥ
kuṭumbaṃ poṣītaṃ param
ekākī tena dahyāmi
ye puṣṭās te 'nyato gatāḥ
body.translated_text: "In that the gods were not worshipped by me, [and] the household was greatly nourished, by that I burn alone; those who were nourished have gone elsewhere"

body.text:
nityanaimittikaṃ karma
kṛte yeṣāṃ na ma kṛtam
ekākī tena dahyāmi
tair manye kvāpi ramyate
body.translated_text: "The daily and occasional rites which were not done by me for them, by that I burn alone; by them, I think, [pleasure] is enjoyed somewhere"

body.text:
yan me parijanasyārthe
kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham
ekākī tena dahyāmi
gatās te phalabhoginaḥ
body.translated_text: "Whatever deed, auspicious or inauspicious, was done by me for the sake of my dependents, by that I burn alone; they have gone, the enjoyers of the fruit"

body.text:
dārāḥ putrāś ca bhṛtyāś ca
pāpavyāptyā mayaidhitāḥ
ekākī tena dahyāmi
gatās te phalabhoginaḥ
body.translated_text: "Wives, sons, and servants were nurtured by me through the accumulation of sin; by that I burn alone; they have gone, the enjoyers of the fruit"

body.text:
putradārādibhṛtyārthe
mayānyāyārthasaṃcayāḥ
kṛtās tenātra dahyāmi
bhuñjate 'py anyato gatāḥ
body.translated_text: "For the sake of sons, wife, and servants, accumulations of wealth were made by me unjustly; by that I burn here; though they enjoy [it], they have gone elsewhere"

body.text:
kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ mayā bhuktam
anyais tatkarmasaṃcitam
dahyāmy eko 'ham atyantaṃ
tyaktas taiḥ phalabhogibhiḥ
body.translated_text: "The sin was done by me, the enjoyment by others—what was accumulated by that deed; I burn alone, utterly, abandoned by those enjoyers of the fruit"

body.text:
yan mamatvābhibhūtena
mayā dhanam upārjitam
anyasya te 'dya kasyāpi
kevalaṃ mama duṣkṛtam
body.translated_text: "What wealth was earned by me, overpowered by the sense of 'mine'—today it is some other's; only the misdeed is mine"

body.text:
antarduḥkhena dagdho 'ntar
bahir dahyāmi bhānunā
nāntarduḥkhaṃ na vā bhānuḥ
pāpam eva dvidhā sthitam
body.translated_text: "Burned within by inner sorrow, burned without by the sun—neither the inner sorrow nor the sun, [but] sin itself stands in two forms"

body.text:
kaṃcit karmasamuddhāraṃ
paśyasy asukhasāgarāt
mama yenāham āhlādam
āpnuyāṃ munisattama
body.translated_text: "Do you see any extrication from my deeds, from this ocean of misery, by which I might attain gladness, O most excellent of sages?"

body.text:
alpakālikam uddhāraṃ
tava paśyāmy asaṃśayam
prakṣīṇaprāyam etat te
sukṛtaṃ cāsti te param
body.translated_text: "I see, without doubt, a short-lived extrication of yours; this sin of yours is nearly exhausted, and you have a further merit"

body.text:
atīte daśame janmany
acyutārādhanecchayā
sukarmajayadāṃ bhadra
dvādaśīṃ tvam upoṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: "In a past tenth birth, with the desire to worship <s>Acyuta</s>, O blessed one, you fasted on the <s>dvādaśī</s> that gives the victory of good deeds"

body.text:
tava tasyāḥ prabhāveṇa
pāpam atyantadurjayam
alpair ahobhiḥ saṃkṣīṇaṃ
navapātre yathā jalam
body.translated_text: "By the power of that [dvādaśī], your sin, exceedingly hard to conquer, is in a few days exhausted, like water in a fresh [unbaked] vessel"

body.text:
yad anyaḥ kṣapayed varṣais
tad dinair bhavataḥ kṣayam
gataṃ pāpam ayaṃ tasyāḥ
prabhāvo 'tyantadurlabhaḥ
body.translated_text: "What another would exhaust in years, that has come to exhaustion for you in days; this power of that [dvādaśī] is exceedingly hard to obtain"

body.text:
śamaṃ pāpasya kurute
jayaṃ sukṛtakarmaṇaḥ
satkarmajayadā hy eṣā
tato vai dvādaśī smṛtā
body.translated_text: "It effects the calming of sin, the victory of good deeds; for it is the giver of the victory of good deeds, and therefore it is reckoned the <s>dvādaśī</s>"

body.text:
yac caitad vedanārtena
bhavatā paridevitam
tat tathā nātra saṃdeho
mamatā pāpahetukī
body.translated_text: "And this which you have lamented, pained by suffering, that is so—there is no doubt here; the sense of 'mine' is the cause of sin"

body.text:
pāpam atra kṛtaṃ pretya
bhadra tāpāya jāyate
āhlādāya tathā puṇyam
iha puṇyakṛtāṃ nṛṇām
body.translated_text: "Sin done here comes, after death, to be for torment, O blessed one; and likewise merit, for the gladness here, of men who have done merit"

body.text:
vīrabhadraṃ samāśvāsya
yayāv itthaṃ mahāmuniḥ
so 'py alpenaiva kālena
tato mokṣam avāptavān
body.translated_text: Having consoled <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, the great sage thus departed; and he too, in but a short time, then attained liberation

body.text:
evaṃ dālbhya pare loke
yad atrāsukṛtaṃ kṛtam
tat tāpāya sukhāyoktaṃ
yad atraiva śubhaṃ kṛtam
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, in the other world, whatever non-meritorious deed was done here, that is declared to be for torment, [and] whatever auspicious deed was done here, for happiness

body.text:
upavāsaprabhāvaś ca
kathitas te mahāmune
yenālpair eva divasair
bhūri pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam
body.translated_text: And the power of fasting has been told to you, O great sage, by which in but a few days abundant sin came to exhaustion

body.text:
tasmān nareṇa puṇyāya
patitavyaṃ na pātake
upavāsāś ca kartavyāḥ
sadaivātmahitaiṣiṇā
body.translated_text: Therefore a man should fall to merit, not into sin; and fasts should always be performed by one who seeks his own welfare

body.text:
saṃsārāsāratāṃ jñātvā
viṣayāṃś cātitarṣulān
kartavyaṃ yan mahābhāga
puruṣeṇa tad ucyatām
body.translated_text: Knowing the worthlessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the sense-objects to be exceedingly thirst-provoking, tell what is to be done by a man, O greatly fortunate one

body.text:
saṃsārāsāratāṃ jñātvā
viṣayāṃś cātitarṣulān
gṛddhis teṣv eva saṃtyājyā
tattyāgo guṇavān nṛṇām
body.translated_text: Knowing the worthlessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the sense-objects to be exceedingly thirst-provoking, craving for them alone is to be abandoned; the abandonment of that is meritorious for men

body.text:
yeṣām abdasahasrāṇāṃ
sahasrair api no naraḥ
bhogāt tṛptiṃ samāpnoti
kas tair bhogair virajyate
body.translated_text: Those [enjoyments] from the enjoyment of which a man attains no satisfaction even in thousands of thousands of years—who [could] become disgusted with those enjoyments?

body.text:
yāvato vāñchate bhogān
ahany ahani mānavaḥ
teṣāṃ sahasrabhāge 'pi
dālbhya prāptiṃ na vindati
body.translated_text: Whatever enjoyments a man desires day after day, of those he does not find the attainment even of a thousandth part, O <s>Dālbhya</s>

body.text:
atha cet tan avāpnoti
sahasraguṇitān naraḥ
tathāpy atṛpta evāntam
antakāle gamiṣyati
body.translated_text: And even if a man should obtain those a thousandfold, even then, still unsated, he will go to his end at the time of death

body.text:
tṛptaye ye na saṃprāptāḥ
prāpyante ye na vāñchitāḥ
buddhimān indriyārtheṣu
teṣv asaṅgī sadā bhavet
body.translated_text: Those which are not attained for satisfaction, those which when wished are not attained—the wise man should ever be unattached to those sense-objects

body.text:
yeṣāṃ tṛptir na bhogena
tyāgaś caivopakārakaḥ
upoṣitavidhānena
bhogāntyāgas tato varaḥ
body.translated_text: Of those [enjoyments] of which there is no satisfaction by enjoyment, abandonment is indeed beneficial; therefore, by the rite of fasting, the abandonment of enjoyments is better

body.text:
kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādīni
narais tasmān mumukṣubhiḥ
niṣkāmair dālbhya kāryāṇi
phalāya ca phalepsubhiḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore the <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and the rest are to be performed by men desiring liberation, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, without desire [for fruit], and for [their] fruit by those desiring fruit

body.text:
atrāpy udāharantīmaṃ
munayo munisattama
dasrābhyāṃ saha saṃvādam
ailasya ca mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Here too the sages relate this, O most excellent of sages—the dialogue with the two <s>Dasras</s> [Aśvins] and the great soul, the descendant of <s>Iḍā</s>

body.text:
ailaḥ purūravāḥ pūrvaṃ
babhūva manujeśvaraḥ
cakame yaṃ mahābhāgam
urvaśī surasundarī
body.translated_text: <s>Aila</s> <s>Purūravas</s> was formerly a lord of men, the greatly fortunate one whom <s>Urvaśī</s>, the celestial beauty, loved

body.text:
saṃtyajya tridaśāvāsaṃ
rūpaudāryaguṇānvitam
bheje tam urvaśī dālbhya
budhasya tanayaṃ nṛpam
body.translated_text: Having abandoned the dwelling of the thirty [gods], <s>Urvaśī</s> resorted to that king, the son of <s>Budha</s>, endowed with the qualities of beauty and nobility, O <s>Dālbhya</s>

body.text:
nāsatyadasrau rūpeṇa
devānām adhikau tataḥ
urvaśīlobhanaṃ tasya
rūpaṃ draṣṭuṃ samutsukau
body.translated_text: The two <s>Nāsatya-Dasras</s> [Aśvins], surpassing the gods in beauty, were then eager to behold the beauty of that man which had enticed <s>Urvaśī</s>

body.text:
pratiṣṭhānaṃ puraṃ tasya
budhaputrasya dhīmataḥ
jagmatuḥ sumahābhāgau
tasya dvāstham athocatuḥ
body.translated_text: To <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>, the city of that wise son of <s>Budha</s>, the two greatly fortunate ones went, and then said to his doorkeeper:

body.text:
kṣatto 'smadvacanād ailaṃ
brūhi tvaṃ vasudhādhipam
draṣṭuṃ tavāśvinau prāptau
rūpasaṃpadguṇaṃ ṇrpa
tadehy atra mahābhāga
ihāsmān saṃpraveśaya
body.translated_text: "O doorkeeper, at our word tell <s>Aila</s>, the lord of the earth: the two <s>Aśvins</s> have come to behold your wealth of beauty and quality, O king; therefore come here, O greatly fortunate one, and admit us here"

body.text:
āścaryabhūtaṃ lokeṣu
urvaśīlobhanaṃ vapuḥ
tat kautukaṃ na kurute
kasya pārthivapuṅgava
body.translated_text: "A body that has become a marvel in the worlds, that enticed <s>Urvaśī</s>—in whom would that not arouse curiosity, O bull among princes?"

body.text:
āvāṃ samāgatau tasmāt
tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ manujottama
body.translated_text: "We two have therefore come to behold you, O best of men"

body.text:
dvāsthas tatheti tāv āha
praviveśa ca satvaram
ācacakṣe ca tad rājñe
nāsatyavacanaṃ dvija
body.translated_text: The doorkeeper said "So be it" to those two and entered swiftly; and he reported it to the king, no untrue word, O twice-born

body.text:
tac chrutvā vacanaṃ rājā
dvāstham āha muhūrtakam
vilambyatāṃ mahābhāgau
tau brūhi vacanān mama
body.translated_text: Having heard that speech, the king said to the doorkeeper: "Let it be delayed a moment; say to those two greatly fortunate ones, by my word:

body.text:
vyāyāmatailasaṃsarga-
malino na vibhūṣitaḥ
prasādhanaṃ ca kṛtvāhaṃ
niṣkramāmi tvarānvitaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Soiled by contact with exercise-oil, unadorned—having made my toilet, I shall come out, filled with haste'"

body.text:
niṣkramya sa tato dvāstho
yathoktaṃ bhūbhṛtakhilam
samācaṣṭa tato dālbhya
tau ca bhūyas tam ūcatuḥ
body.translated_text: The doorkeeper then, having gone out, reported the whole as the king had said, O <s>Dālbhya</s>; and those two again said to him:

body.text:
aprasādhitam evāśu
bhavantaṃ vasudhādhipa
paśyāvas tava bhūyo 'pi
tvāṃ drakṣyāvaḥ prasādhitam
body.translated_text: "We shall see you, O lord of the earth, unadorned and at once; and we shall also see you again adorned"

body.text:
ity ukto nirgatas tūrṇaṃ
bhavanād avanīpatiḥ
tailābhyaktatanur dālbhya
vyāyāmaparidhānadhṛk
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the king quickly came out from his palace, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, his body anointed with oil, wearing exercise-garb

body.text:
sa praṇāmaṃ tayoḥ kṛtvā
kiṃcin nataśirā nṛpaḥ
provāca yan mayā kāryaṃ
bhavatos tad ihocyatām
body.translated_text: Having made obeisance to those two, the king, his head somewhat bowed, said: "What is to be done by me for you both—let that be told here"

body.text:
saptadvīpavatī pṛthvī
putradārabalaṃ dhanam
yac cānyad api tat sarvaṃ
yuvayor me niveditam
body.translated_text: "The seven-continent earth, sons, wives, army, wealth, and whatever else there is—all that of mine is offered to you two"

body.text:
ity udāhṛtam ākarṇya
nṛpater aśvināv api
aṅgopāṅgādikaṃ sarvaṃ
śanakais tāv apaśyatām
body.translated_text: Having heard this declared by the king, the two <s>Aśvins</s> too gradually beheld all his limbs, secondary limbs, and the rest

body.text:
śirolalāṭabāhuṃ sa-
nayanādivilokanam
kṛtvā ca taṃ mahīpālam
ūcatus tāv idaṃ surau
body.translated_text: And having made an inspection of his head, forehead, arms, together with his eyes and the rest, those two gods said this to that king:

body.text:
praviśya snāhi bhūpāla
yathārthaiś ca vibhūṣaṇaiḥ
vibhūṣitaṃ tu bhūyas tvāṃ
drakṣyāvo 'vāṃ nareśvara
body.translated_text: "Enter and bathe, O lord of the earth, and with fitting ornaments; adorned, we shall see you again, O lord of men"

body.text:
tatheti coktvā sa nṛpaḥ
praviveśa mahāmune
cakre ca sakalaṃ samyak
snātvā dehaprasādhanam
body.translated_text: Saying "So be it," the king entered, O great sage, and having bathed, he duly performed the entire adornment of his body

body.text:
snāto 'nuliptaḥ sragdhārī
suvastraḥ suvibhūṣitaḥ
nāsatyadasrayoḥ pārśvam
iyāya vasudhādhipaḥ
body.translated_text: Bathed, anointed, wearing a garland, in fine garments, well adorned, the lord of the earth went to the side of the <s>Nāsatyas</s>, the <s>Dasras</s>

body.text:
bhūyo 'pi tau yathā pūrvam
aṅgopāṅgavilokanam
cakratur nṛpates tasya
smitabhinnauṣṭhasaṃpuṭau
body.translated_text: Again those two, as before, made an inspection of the limbs and secondary limbs of that king, their lips parted in a smile

body.text:
tau sahāsau samālakṣya
sa tadā vasudhādhipaḥ
hāsasya kāraṇaṃ deva-
bhiṣajau tāv apṛcchata
body.translated_text: Observing those two laughing, the lord of the earth then asked those two physicians of the gods the cause of their laughter

body.text:
pṛcchantaṃ na tato dālbhya
nṛpatiṃ hāsyakāraṇam
yad ūcatur mahābhāgau
tac chṛṇuṣva vadāmi te
body.translated_text: When the king asked the cause of laughter, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, what those two greatly fortunate ones said—hear that; I tell it to you

body.text:
śṛṇu bhūpāla sakalaṃ
hāsakāraṇam āvayoḥ
yuṣmaddarśanasaṃbhūtaṃ
kṣaṇāpacayahetukam
body.translated_text: "Hear, O lord of the earth, the whole cause of our laughter, arising from the sight of you, occasioned by the diminution of a moment

body.text:
asnātasyābhavad bhūpa
yādṛśī te surūpatā
sāṃprataṃ tādṛśī neyaṃ
bhūṣitasyāpi bhūṣaṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: Such beauty as was yours, O king, when unbathed, that is not now thus, even though you are adorned with ornaments

body.text:
snātaḥ sragdāmadhārī tvaṃ
svanuliptaḥ subhūṣitaḥ
tathāpy asnāta eva prāc
śobhano 'bhūn na sāṃpratam
body.translated_text: Bathed, garland-bearing, well anointed, well adorned are you; yet even unbathed before you were more beautiful, not so now

body.text:
kiṃtu tatkāraṇaṃ yena
vyāyāmamalināmbaraḥ
śobhano 'ham abhūt pūrvam
idānīṃ na vibhūṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: But the cause is this, by which, soiled and in exercise-garb, I was more beautiful before, and now not, though adorned

body.text:
divyena cakṣuṣā bhūpa
kālasyāsya ca tasya ca
vayaḥpariṇatiṃ sūkṣmāṃ
paśyāvo 'pacayapradām
body.translated_text: With the divine eye, O king, we see the subtle ripening of age—of this time and of that—which brings diminution

body.text:
yathā hi nāḍikā pūrṇā
galaty avirataṃ nṛpa
nṝṇāṃ pariṇatas tadvac
śarīragrahaṇād anu
body.translated_text: For just as a full water-clock (<s>nāḍikā</s>) drips away without cease, O king, so do men ripen, following upon the taking of a body

body.text:
janmato 'nantaraṃ bālyaṃ
paugaṇḍatvaṃ tataḥ param
yauvanaṃ madhyadehitvaṃ
vārddhakaṃ ca jarā nṛṇām
sthūladṛṣṭyā tu paśyanti
na tu te sūkṣmadarśinaḥ
body.translated_text: Just after birth, childhood; after that, boyhood; youth, the middle-aged state, old age, and decrepitude for men—but they perceive with gross vision, not they who are subtle-seeing

body.text:
nimeṣaśatabhāgasya
sahasrāṃśaḥ kṣaṇo nṛpa
tasyāpy ayutabhāgāṃśo
bhavaty apacayo nṛṇām
body.translated_text: The thousandth part of the hundredth part of an eye-blink is a moment, O king; and even of that the ten-thousandth fractional part is the diminution of men

body.text:
sūkṣmātisūkṣmāpacayī
bhavaty eṣa pumān nṛpa
pariṇāmaṃ kramād yāti
tṛptiṃ vāri pibann iva
body.translated_text: This man is one who diminishes subtly, most subtly, O king; he goes by degrees to ripening, like one drinking water to satiety

body.text:
tad ahar jātabālyasya
bālasyāpacayo hi saḥ
pratikṣaṇāṃśayā vṛddhir
bālatvaṃ hīyate tayā
body.translated_text: On the day childhood is born, that is the diminution of the child; through the increase by fractions-of-a-moment, childhood is diminished thereby

body.text:
paugaṇḍe yauvane caiva
vārddhake ca mahāmate
hānikramaḥ sa evokto
yo bālye kathitas tava
body.translated_text: In boyhood and in youth and in old age, O greatly wise one, that very sequence of decline is declared which was told to you in childhood

body.text:
kāntir yā nṛpa bālasya
pogaṇḍasya hi sā kutaḥ
tatkāntisaukumāryādyaiḥ
śūnyam eva hi yauvanam
body.translated_text: The radiance which is a child's, O king—whence is it the boy's? Empty indeed of that radiance, tenderness, and the rest is youth

body.text:
kāntyādisaṃpado hāniḥ
paramā nṛpa vārddhake
tatrāpy anukṣaṇaṃ hānir
hānir ā mṛtyuto nṛpa
body.translated_text: Supreme is the loss of the wealth of radiance and the rest in old age, O king; and there too the loss is moment by moment—the loss [continues] up to death, O king

body.text:
evaṃ pratikṣaṇāṃśāṃśo
nṝṇām apacayapradaḥ
kurvataḥ kimu kālas te
mahāsnānaprasādhanam
body.translated_text: Thus the fractional-fraction at each moment brings diminution to men; while time does this to you, what use is your great bathing and adornment?

body.text:
asmaddṛṣṭo bhavān yāvat
praviṣṭo nijamandiram
tāvad dhānim anuprāptaḥ
kimu yāmārdhasaṃsthitaḥ
body.translated_text: For as long as you, seen by us, entered your own palace, for that long you have undergone loss—how much more, having remained half a watch?

body.text:
yādṛśo 'dya bhavāṃs tādṛk
tvaṃ na rūpī nareśvara
paraśvaḥ śastanaṃ naiva
body.translated_text: Such as you are today, of such form you will not be, O lord of men; the day after tomorrow you will not be commended even,

body.text: caturthe 'hni ca tanmayaḥ
body.translated_text: and on the fourth day [you will be] of that very nature [diminished still further]

body.text:
evaṃ samastabhūtāni
sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
pratikṣaṇāṃśāpacayaṃ
prāpnuvanti mahītale
body.translated_text: Thus all beings, the stationary and the moving, undergo on the surface of the earth the diminution by fractions at each moment

body.text:
tasmān na kautukaṃ kāryaṃ
bhavatā tu nareśvara
yat te rūpam abhūt pūrvam
aprasādhitaśobhanam
body.translated_text: Therefore no astonishment should be made by you, O lord of men, that your form was before beautiful when unadorned"

body.text:
rājā purūravā bhūyaḥ
śrutvā vākyam idaṃ tayoḥ
cintayitvā vacaḥ prāha
saṃvegotkampimānasaḥ
body.translated_text: King <s>Purūravas</s> again, having heard this speech of theirs, having reflected, spoke, his mind agitated and trembling:

body.text:
aho bhavadbhyāṃ kathitam
anavasthitasaṃsthitam
svarūpaṃ jagato devau
yena trasto 'smi sāṃpratam
body.translated_text: "Ah, by you two has been declared the unstable, instable nature of the world, O gods, by which I am now terrified

body.text:
ajñānatimirāndhānāṃ
madvidhānāṃ bhavadvidhāḥ
pradīpabhūtāḥ saṃdeho
vidyate nātra kaścana
body.translated_text: For those of my kind, blind with the darkness of ignorance, you of your kind are as lamps; there exists no doubt here at all

body.text:
sadāpacayadoṣeṇa
duṣṭakāyaiḥ surottamau
yat kāryaṃ puruṣais tac ca
kathyatāṃ hitakāmyayā
body.translated_text: O best of gods, by men with bodies spoiled through the fault of constant diminution, what is to be done—let that be told, out of the wish for [our] welfare"

body.text:
atimūḍho 'dhruve kāye
sadāpacayadharmiṇi
naras tadupabhogyāni
dhruvāṇi parimārgati
body.translated_text: "Exceedingly deluded, in a body that is unstable and of the nature of constant diminution, a man seeks as stable the objects to be enjoyed by it

body.text:
āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ
paridhānaṃ gṛhādikam
vāñchaty aho 'timohena
susthiraṃ svayam asthiraḥ
body.translated_text: Seat, bed, vehicle, garment, house and the rest he desires—ah, through great delusion—to be firmly fixed, though himself unstable

body.text:
mūḍho 'dhruvaṃ dhruvamatiḥ
kim ātmānaṃ na budhyate
body.translated_text: The fool, of fixed intellect toward the unstable—why does he not understand himself?

body.text:
bālyāt paugaṇḍatāṃ gatvā
yaḥ punar yauvanaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: He who, having gone from childhood to boyhood, again has gone to youth—

body.text:
bhuvaḥ śailaṃ samārūḍhaḥ
samārūḍhas tato drumam
ārohaṇaṃ sa kim anyad
ṛkṣabhītaḥ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: having climbed from the ground to a mountain, and thence climbed a tree, what other climbing will he do, frightened by a bear?

body.text:
bālyāt paugaṇḍatāṃ yāto
yauvanād vṛddhatāṃ gataḥ
vayo'vasthā tataḥ kānyā
yad bhogāya sthirecchakaḥ
body.translated_text: Gone from childhood to boyhood, gone from youth to old age—what other state of age is there thereafter for which he, of fixed wish, [aims] at enjoyment?

body.text:
tasmād etan manuṣyeṇa
vicāryātmahitaiṣiṇā
śreyasy āmuṣmike yatnaḥ
kartavyo 'harniśaṃ nṛpa
body.translated_text: Therefore, having examined this, by a man desiring his own welfare effort should be made day and night toward the good of the other world, O king

body.text:
bhogeṣv asaktiḥ satataṃ
tathaivātmāvalokanam
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ
kapilaḥ prāha pārthivaḥ
body.translated_text: Constant non-attachment to enjoyments, and likewise the contemplation of the self—this is the supreme good of men, said the king <s>Kapila</s>

body.text:
sarvatra samadarśitvaṃ
nirmamatvam asaṅgitā
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ
prāha pañcaśikho muniḥ
body.translated_text: Equal-mindedness everywhere, the absence of the sense of 'mine,' non-attachment—this is the supreme good of men, said the sage <s>Pañcaśikha</s>

body.text:
āgarbhajanmabālyādi-
vayo'vasthādivedanam
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇām
aṅgāriṣṭho 'bravīn nṛpaḥ
body.translated_text: The awareness of the conditions of age from conception, birth, childhood and the rest—this is the supreme good of men, said the king <s>Aṅgāriṣṭha</s>

body.text:
adhyātmikādiduḥkhānām
atyantādipratikriyā
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ
janako hy āha mokṣavit
body.translated_text: The utter and final counteraction of the spiritual and other miseries—this is the supreme good of men, said <s>Janaka</s>, knower of liberation

body.text:
abhinnayor bhedakaraḥ
pratyayo yaḥ parātmanoḥ
hiraṇyagarbhas tacchāntiṃ
śreyaḥ paramam abravīt
body.translated_text: The cognition which makes a distinction between the supreme Self and the individual self, which are not distinct—the calming of that, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> declared the supreme good

body.text:
kartavyam iti yat karma
ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitam
kriyate tat paraṃ śreyo
jaigīṣavyo 'bravīn muniḥ
body.translated_text: The deed that is named <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, performed as 'it is to be done'—that is the supreme good, said the sage <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>

body.text:
hāniṃ sarvavidhitsānām
ātmanaḥ sukhahetukīm
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ
devalo 'py āha tattvavit
body.translated_text: The cessation of all impulses-to-act of the self, the cause of [its] happiness—this is the supreme good of men, said <s>Devala</s>, knower of truth

body.text:
yad yat tyajati kāmānāṃ
tat sukhasyābhipūryate
etad eva paraṃ śreyo
vijñānaṃ hitakāminām
body.translated_text: Whatever one abandons of desires, by that one is filled with happiness; this very thing is the supreme good, the wisdom of those desiring welfare

body.text:
kāmānusārī puruṣaḥ
kāmān anu vinaśyati
aśreyasaṃ paraṃ caitad
yad bhūpālātikāmitā
body.translated_text: The man who follows desire perishes following desire; and this is the supreme non-good, O lord of the earth, namely excessive desirousness"

body.text:
evaṃ vijñātatattvārthaḥ
sanako yogināṃ varaḥ
narendra prāha viprāṇāṃ
paramārthaparaṃparam
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Sanaka</s>, best of <s>yogins</s>, knowing the meaning of truth, O king, declared the supreme transcendent goal of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>:

body.text:
kriyākalāpaphaladam
ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitam
amuṣmin madhyamaṃ śreyaḥ
prāhuḥ sapta rṣayo nṛpa
body.translated_text: "The giver of the fruit of the collection of rites, named <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>—in the other world the middling good, the seven seers declare it, O king

body.text:
ihaiva phaladaṃ kāmyaṃ
karma yat kriyate naraiḥ
tad āhur aparaṃ śreyo
ṛcīkacyavanādayaḥ
body.translated_text: The optional deed, fruit-giving here itself, which is performed by men—that the lower good they declare, <s>Ṛcīka</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, and the rest"

body.text:
dve karmaṇī naraśreṣṭha
brahmaṇā samudāhṛte
pravṛttākhyaṃ nivṛttaṃ ca
svargamuktiphale hi te
body.translated_text: Two deeds, O best of men, are declared by <s>Brahmā</s>: the one called active (<s>pravṛtta</s>) and the inactive (<s>nivṛtta</s>); they have heaven and liberation as their fruit

body.text:
pravṛttam api mokṣāya
karma pārthiva jāyate
karma svarūpato bhraṣṭam
anākāṅkṣya phalaṃ kṛtam
body.translated_text: Even the active deed becomes for liberation, O king, when the deed, fallen from its own form, is done without longing for fruit

body.text:
sāmānyaṃ cāparaṃ śreyaḥ
sarvavarṇāśrameṣu yat
tac chṛṇuṣva mahīpāla
vadato mama tattvataḥ
body.translated_text: And the common lower good, which is among all classes and life-stages—hear that, O lord of the earth, as I tell it truly:

body.text:
satyaṃ vaktavyaṃ nityaṃ maitreṇa bhāvyaṃ
kāryaṃ ca tyājyaṃ nityam āyāsakāri
loke 'muṣmin yad dhitaṃ ca tathāsmiṃs
tasminn ātmā yojanīyo 'nudhīraiḥ
body.translated_text: Truth is ever to be spoken; one should be friendly; the deed that ever causes toil is to be abandoned; and whatever is beneficial in that other world and in this—to that the self should be yoked by the steadfast

body.text:
tīrthasnānaiḥ sopavāsair ajasraṃ
pātre dānair homajāpaiś ca nityam
śuddhir neyo devatābhyarcanaiś ca
śuddho 'py ātmā saṅgadoṣād aśuddhaḥ
body.translated_text: By bathing at sacred fords, with fasts, ceaselessly by gifts to a worthy recipient, by <s>homas</s> and recitations constantly, purity is to be attained, and by the worship of deities; for the self, though pure, is impure through the fault of contact

body.text:
śuddhaṃ vastraṃ saṅgadoṣād aśuddhaṃ
bhūyaḥ śuddhiṃ śodhyamānaṃ paryāti
etaj jñātvā na pramādo manuṣyaiḥ
śuddhe hy ātmany ātmavidbhir vidheyaḥ
body.translated_text: A pure garment, impure through the fault of contact, again attains purity when cleansed; knowing this, no heedlessness should be practiced by men, by the knowers of the self, regarding the pure self

body.text:
ity uktvā tau narendraṃ tau
tena cārghyādinā pṛthak
samyak saṃpūjitau yātau
nāka pṛṣṭham athāśvinau
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the king, those two, duly worshipped by him separately with the <s>arghya</s> and the rest, departed, the <s>Aśvins</s>, to the vault of heaven

body.text:
sa cāpy anityatām evam
avagamya nareśvaraḥ
niṣkāmo 'nudinam eva
avagamya nareśvaraḥ
niṣkāmo 'nudinaṃ yajñair
iyāja puruṣottamam
body.translated_text: And he too, the lord of men, having thus understood impermanence, free of desire each day, having understood [it], the lord of men, free of desire, day by day worshipped <s>Puruṣottama</s> with sacrifices

body.text:
bhogāsaṅgi mano dālbhya
yadāsīt tasya bhūpateḥ
tad eva bhagavaddhyāna-
paraṃ cakre mahāmune
body.translated_text: The mind which was attached to enjoyments, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, that this lord of the earth made wholly devoted to the meditation upon the Blessed One, O great sage

body.text:
tatyājārtheṣu mamatām
ahaṃkāraṃ tathātmani
samatāṃ sarvabhūteṣu
saṃprāpa pṛthivīpatiḥ
body.translated_text: He abandoned the sense of 'mine' toward objects, and egoism toward the self; the lord of the earth attained equanimity toward all beings

body.text:
yasyātmany api viprarṣe
nāhaṃmāno 'sti kutracit
madāvalepo pūpādau
tasya syād iti kā kathā
body.translated_text: He in whom, O sage among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, there is no sense of 'I' anywhere even toward the self—for him what talk could there be of intoxicated arrogance toward food and the rest?

body.text:
evaṃ dālbhya manuṣyeṇa
samatām anutiṣṭhatā
sarvabhogeṣu saṃtyājyo
dhyeyaś ca puruṣottamaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, by a man practicing equanimity, attachment to all enjoyments is to be abandoned, and <s>Puruṣottama</s> is to be meditated upon

body.text:
kutra tiṣṭhati govindo
bāhyanivṛtacetasi
tasmān niḥsaṅgacittena
śakyaś cintayituṃ hariḥ
body.translated_text: Where does <s>Govinda</s> dwell, in a mind turned away from external things—therefore by a mind free of attachment <s>Hari</s> can be contemplated

body.text:
prītidveṣādayas tyaktvā
maharṣe yasya cetasā
priyātithis taddhṛdaye
viṣṇur mokṣaphalapradaḥ
body.translated_text: Having abandoned love, hatred, and the rest with his mind, O great seer, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is a welcome guest in the heart of such a one, the giver of the fruit of liberation

body.text:
kāryārambheṣu sarveṣu
duḥsvapneṣu ca sattama
amaṅgalyeṣu sarveṣu
yaj japtavyaṃ tad ucyatām
body.translated_text: In all undertakings of deeds, in bad dreams, O best one, and in all inauspicious things, what is to be muttered—let that be told,

body.text:
yenārambhāś ca sidhhyanti
duḥsvapnaṃ copaśāmyati
amaṅgalānāṃ sarveṣāṃ
pratighātaś ca jāyate
body.translated_text: by which undertakings succeed, and the bad dream is allayed, and the warding-off of all inauspicious things arises

body.text:
janārdanaṃ bhūtapatiṃ jagadguruṃ
smaran manuṣyaḥ satataṃ mahāmune
duṣṭāny aśeṣāṇy apahanti sādhayaty
aśeṣakāryāṇi tathā yadīcchati
body.translated_text: Remembering <s>Janārdana</s>, the lord of beings, the teacher of the world, constantly, O great sage, a man dispels all evils and accomplishes all his deeds, likewise, if he so wishes

body.text:
śṛṇuṣva cānyad vadato mamākhilaṃ
vadāmi yat te dvijavarya maṅgalam
sarvārthasiddhiṃ pradadāti yaḥ sadā
nihanty aśeṣāṇi ca pātakāni
body.translated_text: And hear another thing, as I tell the whole; I tell you, O best of the twice-born, that auspicious utterance which ever grants the accomplishment of all aims and destroys all sins:

body.text:
pratiṣṭhitaṃ yatra jagac carācaraṃ
jagac ca yo yo jagataś ca hetuḥ
jagac ca pāty atti ca yaḥ sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: He in whom the world, moving and unmoving, is established, who is the world and the cause of the world, and who ever protects and devours the world—

body.text: mamāstu maṅgalyavivṛddaye hariḥ
body.translated_text: let that <s>Hari</s> be for the increase of my auspiciousness

body.text:
vyomāmbuvāyvagnimahīsvarūpair
vistāravān yo 'ṇutaro 'ṇubhāgāt
sa sthūlasūkṣmaḥ satateśvareśvaro
body.translated_text: He who, in the forms of sky, water, wind, fire, and earth, is of vast extent, [yet] smaller than the smallest fraction of an atom, he the gross and the subtle, the eternal Lord of lords—

body.text:
yasmāt parastāt puruṣād anantād
anādimadhyād akhilaṃ na kiṃcit
sa hetuhetuḥ parameśvareśvaro
body.translated_text: than whom, the supreme, endless, beginningless and middle-less <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is nothing whatever beyond—he the cause of causes, the Lord of the supreme Lord—

body.text:
hiraṇyagarbhācyutarudrarūpī
sṛjaty aśeṣaṃ paripāti hanti
guṇāśrayī yo bhagavān sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: He who, in the forms of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>, creates, sustains, and destroys the whole, the Blessed One who is the support of the <s>guṇas</s>, he ever—

body.text:
paraḥ surāṇāṃ paramo 'surāṇāṃ
paro munīnāṃ paramo yatīnām
paraḥ samastasya ca yaḥ sa devo
body.translated_text: He who is beyond the gods, supreme over the demons, beyond the sages, supreme over the ascetics, and beyond all—that god—

body.text:
dhyāto yatīnām apakalmaṣair yo
dadāti muktiṃ parameśvareśvaraḥ
manobhir ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: He who, meditated upon by the ascetics free of sin, grants liberation, the Lord of the supreme Lord, the primal <s>Puruṣa</s> [reached] by minds, he ever—

body.text:
surendravaivasvatavittapāmbupa-
svarūparūpī paripāti yo jagat
sa śuddhasattvaḥ parameśvareśvaro
body.translated_text: He who, in the forms of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>), the lord of wealth (<s>Kubera</s>), and the lord of waters (<s>Varuṇa</s>), protects the world, he of pure being, the Lord of the supreme Lord—

body.text:
yannāmakīrtanato vimucyate
anekajanmārjitapāpasaṃcayaiḥ
pāpendhanāgniḥ sa sadaiva nirmalo
body.translated_text: He by the proclamation of whose name one is freed from the accumulations of sin gathered over many births, he the fire to the fuel of sin, ever stainless—

body.text:
yenoddhṛteyaṃ dharaṇī rasātalād
aśeṣasattvasthitikāraṇād idam
bibharti viśvaṃ jagataḥ sa mūlavān
body.translated_text: He by whom this earth was raised from the netherworld, the cause of the existence of all beings, who bears the universe, he the root of the world—

body.text:
pādeṣu vedā jaṭhare carācaraṃ
romasv aśeṣā munayo mukhe makhāḥ
yasyeśvareśasya sa sarvadā prabhur
body.translated_text: In whose feet are the <s>Vedas</s>, in whose belly the moving and unmoving, in whose hairs all the sages, in whose mouth the sacrifices—that Lord of lords, he ever the master—

body.text:
samastayajñāṅgamayaṃ vapur vibhor
yasyāṅgam īśeśvarasaṃstutasya
varāharūpo bhagavān sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: Whose body is made of all the limbs of sacrifice, the body of the Lord, a limb of him who is praised by the Lord of lords—in the form of the boar (<s>Varāha</s>), that Blessed One ever [protect the world]

body.text:
vikṣobhya sarvodadhitoyasaṃpadaṃ
dadhāra dhātrīṃ jagataś ca yodbhavaḥ
yajñeśvaro yajñapumān sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: who, having churned up the abundance of all the ocean's waters, upheld the Earth-supporter and was the source of the world—the lord of sacrifice, the sacrifice-person, he ever [protect us]

body.text:
pātālamūleśvarabhogisaṃhatau
vinyasya pādau pṛthivīṃ ca bibhrataḥ
yasyopamānaṃ na babhūva so 'cyuto
body.translated_text: who, setting his two feet upon the coils of the serpent-lord at the root of the nether world (<s>Pātāla</s>) and bearing the earth—he to whom there was no comparison, that <s>Acyuta</s> [protect us]

body.text:
vighargharaṃ yasya ca bṛṃhato muhuḥ
sanandanādyair janalokasaṃsthitaiḥ
śrutaṃ jayetyuktiparaiḥ sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: and whose deep grunting, as he repeatedly grew, was heard by <s>Sanandana</s> and the rest who dwell in the <s>Janaloka</s>, intent on uttering 'Victory!'—he ever [protect us]

body.text:
ekārṇavād yasya mahīyaso mahīm
ādāya vegena samutpatiṣyataḥ
nutaṃ vapur yogivaraiḥ sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: from the single ocean, whose mighty body, taking the earth, was about to spring up with speed, was praised by the best of yogins—he ever [protect us]

body.text:
hato hiraṇyākṣamahāsuraḥ purā
purāṇapuṃsā parameṇa yena
varāharūpaḥ sa patiḥ prajāpater
body.translated_text: by whom the great <s>asura</s> <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was slain of old, by the supreme Ancient Person, in the form of the boar—that lord of <s>Prajāpati</s> [protect us]

body.text:
daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ surabhītināśanaṃ
kṛtvā vapur divyanṛsiṃharūpiṇaṃ
trātaṃ jagad yena sa sarvadā prabhur
body.translated_text: having made a body terrible with tusks, the destroyer of the gods' fear, having the form of the divine man-lion (<s>Narasiṃha</s>), by whom the world was protected—he ever the Lord [protect us]

body.text:
daityendravakṣaḥsthaladāradāruṇaiḥ
karoruhaiḥ śatrurujānukāribhiḥ
ciccheda lokasya bhayāni cāvyayo
body.translated_text: with claws terrible in tearing apart the chest-region of the lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, acting like enemy-diseases, the imperishable one cut through the fears of the world

body.text:
dantāntadīptidyutinirmalāṇi
cakāra sarvāṇi diśaṃ mukhāni
ninādavitrāsitadānavo hy asau
body.translated_text: He made all the faces of the directions free from stain with the radiance and luster of the edges of his teeth, having terrified the <s>dānavas</s> with his roar

body.text:
yannāmasaṃkīrtanato mahābhayād
vimokṣam āpnoti na saṃśayaṃ naraḥ
samastalokārtiharo nṛkesarī
body.translated_text: From the proclaiming of whose name a man attains release from great fear, without doubt—the man-lion (<s>Nṛkesarī</s>), remover of the distress of all the worlds

body.text:
saṭākalāpabhramaṇānilahatāḥ
sphuṭanti yasyāmbudharāḥ samantataḥ
sa divyasiṃhaḥ sphuritākulekṣaṇo
body.translated_text: by the wind of the whirling of whose mass of mane the rain-clouds burst apart on every side—that divine lion, with throbbing, agitated eyes

body.text:
yadīkṣaṇajyotiṣi raśmimaṇḍalaṃ
pralīnam eva na rarāja bhāsvataḥ
kutaḥ śaśāṅkasya sa siṃharūpadhṛṅ
body.translated_text: In whose eye-light the circle of rays of the radiant sun [seems] dissolved and shone not—how much less that of the moon—he who bore the lion's form [protect us]

body.text:
dravanti daityāḥ praṇamanti devatā
naśyanti rakṣāṃsy apayānti cārayaḥ
yatkīrtanāt so 'dbhutarūpakesarī
body.translated_text: The <s>Daityas</s> flee, the gods bow down, the <s>rākṣasas</s> perish, and the foes depart, from the proclaiming of whom—that wondrous-formed lion [protect us]

body.text:
aśeṣadeveśanareśvareśvaraiḥ
sadā stutaṃ yac caritaṃ mahādbhutam
sa sarvalokārtiharo mahāharir
body.translated_text: whose deed, exceedingly wondrous, is ever praised by all the lords of gods and the lords of the lords of men—that remover of the distress of all worlds, the great <s>Hari</s> [protect us]

body.text:
ṛkkāritaṃ yo yajuṣātiśāntimat
sāmadhvanidhvastasamastapātakam
cakre jagad vāmanakaḥ sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: who, made to resound with the <s>Ṛk</s>, full of supreme peace by the <s>Yajus</s>, with all sins destroyed by the sound of the <s>Sāman</s>, made the world—he the dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>) ever [protect us]

body.text:
yatpādavinyāsapavitratāṃ mahī
yayau viyad ṛgyajuṣām udīraṇāt
sa vāmano divyaśarīradhṛk sadā
body.translated_text: by the placing of whose feet the earth attained purity, the sky [purity] from the utterance of the <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Yajus</s>—he the <s>Vāmana</s>, bearer of a divine body, ever [protect us]

body.text:
yasmin prayāte surabhūbhṛto 'dhvaraṃ
nanāma khedād avaniḥ sasāgarā
sa vāmanaḥ sarvajaganmayaḥ sadā
body.translated_text: when whom, gone to the sacrifice of the god-like ruler of the earth, the earth with its oceans bowed down from the strain—he the <s>Vāmana</s>, made of all the world, ever [protect us]

body.text:
mahādyutau daityapater mahādhvaraṃ
yasmin praviṣṭe kṣubhitaṃ mahāsuraiḥ
sa vāmano 'ntasthitasaptalokadhṛṅ
body.translated_text: into whose great sacrifice, when he of great splendor had entered, the lord of the <s>Daityas</s>'s [sacrifice] was agitated by the great <s>asuras</s>—he the <s>Vāmana</s>, bearer of the seven worlds within him [protect us]

body.text:
samastadeveṣṭimayaṃ mahādyutir
dadhāra yo rūpam atīndriyaṃ prabhuḥ
trivikramākrāntajagattrayaḥ sadā
body.translated_text: who of great splendor, the Lord, bore a form beyond the senses, made of the sacrifice of all the gods, who as <s>Trivikrama</s> strode over the three worlds—ever [protect us]

body.text:
saṅghaiḥ surāṇāṃ divi bhūtale sthitais
tathā manuṣyair gagane sa sarvadā
stutaḥ kramād yaḥ pradade sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: praised by the hosts of gods standing in heaven and on the earth's surface, and likewise by men in the sky—he ever, who in three strides gave [the worlds back], ever [protect us]

body.text:
krāntvā dharitrīṃ gaganaṃ tathā divaṃ
marutpater yaḥ pradadau triviṣṭapam
sa devadevo bhuvaneśvareśvaro
body.translated_text: having strode over the earth, the sky, and likewise heaven, who gave to the lord of the <s>Maruts</s> (Indra) the third heaven (<s>Triviṣṭapa</s>)—he the God of gods, the Lord of the lords of the world

body.text:
anugrahaṃ cāpi baler anuttamaṃ
cakāra yaś cendrapadopalakṣaṇaṃ
surāṃś ca yajñasya bhujaḥ sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: and who made also the unsurpassed favor to <s>Bali</s>, marked by the rank of <s>Indra</s>, and [restored] the gods—he, the arm of sacrifice, ever [protect us]

body.text:
rasātalād yena purā samāhṛtāḥ
samastavedā varavājirūpiṇā
sa kaiṭabhārir madhusūdano mahān
body.translated_text: by whom of old all the <s>Vedas</s> were brought back from the nether world (<s>Rasātala</s>), in the form of the excellent horse (<s>Hayagrīva</s>)—he the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, the great <s>Madhusūdana</s>

body.text:
niḥkṣatriyāṃ yaś ca cakāra medinīm
anekaśo bāhuvanaṃ tathāchinat
yaḥ kārtavīryasya sa bhārgavottamo
body.translated_text: and who made the earth free of <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and many times cut down the forest of arms, [the forest of arms] of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>—he the best of the <s>Bhārgavas</s> (Paraśurāma)

body.text:
nihatya vāliṃ ca kapīśvaraṃ hi yo
nibadhya setuṃ jaladhau daśānanam
jaghāna cānyān rajanīcarān asau
body.translated_text: and who, having slain <s>Vālin</s> the lord of monkeys, having bound a bridge over the ocean, slew the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) and the other night-rangers (<s>rākṣasas</s>)

body.text:
cikṣepa bālaḥ śakaṭaṃ babhañja yo
yamalārjunau kaṃsam ariṃ jaghāna
mamarda cāṇūramukhaṃ sa sarvadā
body.translated_text: who as a child hurled the cart and broke it, [broke] the twin <s>Arjuna</s> trees, slew his enemy <s>Kaṃsa</s>, and crushed <s>Cāṇūra</s> and the rest—he ever [protect us]

body.text:
prātaḥ sahasrāṃśumarīcinirmalaṃ
kareṇa bibhrad bhagavān sudarśanam
kaumodakīṃ cāpi gadām anuttamāṃ
body.translated_text: the Blessed One bearing in his hand at dawn the <s>Sudarśana</s>, stainless as the rays of the thousand-rayed [sun], and also the unsurpassed mace <s>Kaumodakī</s>

body.text:
himendukundasphaṭikābhrakomalaṃ
mukhānilāpūritam īśvareśvaraḥ
madhyāhnakāle ca sa śaṅkham uttamam
body.translated_text: [bearing] at midday the excellent conch, soft as snow, moon, jasmine, and crystal, filled with the breath of his mouth—he the Lord of lords

body.text:
tathāparāhne pravikāsipaṅkajaṃ
vakṣaḥsthalena śriyam udvahad vibhuḥ
vistāripadmotpalapatralocano
body.translated_text: and likewise in the afternoon, bearing on his chest the goddess <s>Śrī</s>, [like] a full-blooming lotus—the all-pervading Lord, with eyes [like] the petals of the wide lotus and blue water-lily

body.text:
sarveṣu kāleṣu samastadeśeṣv
aśeṣakāryeṣu tatheśvareśvaraḥ
sarvaiḥ svarūpair bhagavān anādimān
body.translated_text: at all times, in all places, in all undertakings likewise, the Lord of lords, the Blessed One without beginning, with all his forms [protect us]

body.text:
etat paṭhan dālbhya samastapāpair
vimucyate viṣṇuparo manuṣyaḥ
sidhyanti kāryāṇi tathāsya sarvāṇy
arthān avāpnoti tathā yatheṣṭam
body.translated_text: Reading this, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, a man devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is freed from all sins; his undertakings all succeed thus, and he attains wealth as he desires

body.text:
duḥsvapnaṃ praśamam upaiti paṭhyamāne
stotre 'smiñ śravaṇavidhau sadotthitasya
prārambho drutam upayāti siddhim īśaḥ
pāpāni kṣapayati cāsya vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: Bad dreams come to calm when this hymn is recited, in the manner of hearing it, of one who rises [for it] always; an undertaking swiftly comes to success—the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> destroys his sins

body.text:
maṅgalyaṃ paramam idaṃ sadārthasiddhiṃ
nirvighna tv adhikaphalaṃ sadā dadāti
kiṃ loke tad iha paratra cāsti puṃsām
yad viṣṇupravaṇadhiyā na dālbhya sādhyam
body.translated_text: This supreme auspicious [hymn] ever gives the attainment of one's aims unobstructed, and abundant fruit; what is there in the world here and in the next for men, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, that is not achievable by a mind inclined toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

body.text:
devendras tribhuvanam artham ekapiṅgaḥ
sarvarddhiṃ tribhuvanagāṃ ca kārtavīryaḥ
vaidehaḥ paramapadaṃ prasādya viṣṇuṃ
saṃprāptaḥ sakalaphalaprado hi viṣṇuḥ
body.translated_text: The king of gods [obtained] the three worlds as his aim, <s>Ekapiṅga</s> [his wealth], and <s>Kārtavīrya</s> [obtained] all prosperity extending over the three worlds; the king of <s>Videha</s> [obtained] the supreme state, having propitiated <s>Viṣṇu</s>—for <s>Viṣṇu</s> is indeed the giver of every fruit

body.text:
sarvārambheṣu dālbhyaitad
duḥsvapneṣu ca paṇḍitaḥ
japed ekamatir viṣṇau
tathāmaṅgalyadarśane
body.translated_text: In all undertakings, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, and in bad dreams, the wise man, with single mind on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, should mutter [his names], and likewise on the sight of what is inauspicious

body.text:
śamaṃ prayānti duṣṭāni
grahapīḍāś ca dāruṇāḥ
karmārambhāś ca sidhyanti
puṇyam āpnoti cottamam
body.translated_text: Wicked things go to calm, and the dreadful afflictions of planets, and the undertakings of works succeed, and one attains supreme merit

body.text:
harir dadāti bhadrāṇi
maṅgalyastutisaṃstutaḥ
karoty akhilarūpaiś ca
rakṣām akṣataśaktidhṛk
