body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, praised with auspicious praise, gives blessings, and makes protection with all his forms, bearer of undiminished power

body.text:
kurvīta kiṃ pumān sthānaṃ
kaḥ pumān brahmaṇo balam
brahmaṇaś ca kathaṃ bhedo
jñeyo 'bhinnaphalapradaḥ
body.translated_text: What position should a man establish? Who is a man's strength of <s>Brahman</s>? And how is the difference of <s>Brahman</s>, which yet gives undivided fruit, to be known?

body.text:
svakarmaṇā dhanaṃ labdhvā
nityanaimittikāḥ kriyāḥ
kurvīta śuddhim āsthāya
svecchayā ca tathā paraḥ
body.translated_text: Having gained wealth by his own duty, a man should perform the regular and occasional rites, taking up purity, and at his own will likewise the supreme [worship]

body.text:
tyaktvā rāgādikān doṣān
samaḥ sarvatra vai bhavet
sarvatra maitrīṃ kurvīta
dadyād iṣṭāni cārthinām
body.translated_text: Having abandoned the faults of passion and the rest, he should indeed be equal everywhere; he should make friendship everywhere, and give the desired things to those who beseech

body.text:
kuryād dīneṣu karuṇāṃ
duḥśīlān parivarjayet
muditāṃ dharmaśīleṣu
bhāvanāṃ munisattama
body.translated_text: He should make compassion toward the wretched, and shun those of bad conduct; [he should make] gladness in cultivation toward the righteous, O best of sages

body.text:
ekatra vā jagannāthe
bhāvanāṃ puruṣottame
body.translated_text: or [he should make] cultivation in the One, the Lord of the world, the Supreme Person—

body.text: niḥśeṣārthamalāpetāṃ
body.translated_text: [a cultivation] devoid of every taint of [worldly] aims,

body.text: śuddhāṃ kurvīta paṇḍitaḥ
body.translated_text: pure the wise man should make [it]

body.text:
śarīrabāhyatāṃ śaśvad
dhiṃsāṃ kurvīta na kvacit
nindāvamānam anyeṣāṃ
yac cānyad upaghātakam
body.translated_text: Externality to the body he should ever [maintain]; he should never do injury, nor slander and contempt of others, nor whatever else is harmful

body.text:
śarīravāṅmanaḥśuddhiṃ
kurvīta ca sadātmanaḥ
bhūtānām upakāraś ca
tapobhiś cātmakarṣaṇam
body.translated_text: He should ever make purity of body, speech, and mind for himself, and benefit of beings, and the drawing of the self [toward liberation] by austerities

body.text:
eṣa dharmaḥ samāsena
dālbhyākhyāto mayā tava
adharmaś cāyam evokto
viparīto manīṣibhiḥ
body.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s>, in brief, has been declared by me to you, O <s>Dālbhya</s>; and <s>adharma</s> is declared by the wise to be just the opposite of this

body.text:
ete yatra guṇāḥ pūrvaṃ
kathitā jñānasaṃyutāḥ
brahmaṇaḥ sāśrayaḥ śuddha
upacārāt tad eva saḥ
body.translated_text: Where these qualities, joined with knowledge, were declared before—[that is] of <s>Brahman</s>, with its support, pure; by the [right] approach that very [Brahman] is he

body.text:
ekasyaiva satas tasya
brahmaṇo dvijasattama
nāmnāṃ bahutvaṃ lokānām
upakārakaraṃ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: Of that <s>Brahman</s>, who is one alone, O best of the twice-born, hear of the multiplicity of names that does benefit to the worlds

body.text:
nimittaśaktayo nāmno
bhedatas tadudīraṇāt
vibhinnāny eva sādhyante
phalāni kurunandana
body.translated_text: The instrumental powers of the names, through their difference, from their utterance, accomplish different fruits, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>

body.text:
yacchakti nāma tat tasya
tat tasminn eva vastuni
sādhakaṃ puruṣavyāghra
saumyakrūreṣu vastuṣu
body.translated_text: Whatever power a name has, that name [is] effective for it in that very matter, O tiger among men—in matters benign and cruel

body.text:
vāsudevācyutānanta-
satyājyapuruṣottamaiḥ
paramātmeśvarādyaiś ca
stuto nāmabhir avyayaḥ
body.translated_text: The imperishable one is praised by the names <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Satya</s>, <s>Ajya</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, and <s>Paramātman</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and the rest

body.text:
nimittabhāvaṃ bhagavān
vimukter yāty adhokṣajaḥ
tathānyakāryasaṃsiddhau
yad yat tat tan niśāmaya
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Adhokṣaja</s> becomes the instrument of liberation; and likewise in the accomplishing of other tasks, whatever [name does] whatever, hear that

body.text:
dhanakṛd dharmakṛd dharmī
dharmātmā viśvakṛc chuciḥ
śuciṣad viṣṇur abjākṣaḥ
puṣkarākṣo hy adhokṣayaḥ
śuciśravāḥ śipiviṣṭo
yajñeśo yajñabhāvanaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Dhanakṛt</s> (wealth-maker), <s>Dharmakṛt</s>, <s>Dharmin</s>, <s>Dharmātman</s>, <s>Viśvakṛt</s>, <s>Śuci</s>, <s>Śuciṣad</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Abjākṣa</s>, <s>Puṣkarākṣa</s>, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, <s>Śuciśravas</s>, <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, <s>Yajñeśa</s>, <s>Yajñabhāvana</s>—

body.text:
nāmnām ity evam ādīnāṃ
samuccāraṇato naraḥ
dharmaṃ mahāntam āpnoti
pāpabandhakṣayaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: from the uttering of these names and the like, a man attains great <s>dharma</s>, and likewise the destruction of the bond of sin

body.text:
tathārthaprāptaye brahman
devanāmāni me śṛṇu
yeṣāṃ samuccāraṇato
vittam āpnoti bhaktimān
body.translated_text: And for the attainment of wealth, O <s>brahman</s>, hear from me the names of the god, from the uttering of which the devotee attains riches:

body.text:
śrīdaḥ śrīśaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ
śrīdharaḥ śrīniketanaḥ
śriyaḥ patiḥ śrīparamaḥ
śrīmāñ śrīvatsalāñcchanaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Śrīda</s>, <s>Śrīśa</s>, <s>Śrīnivāsa</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, <s>Śrīniketana</s>, <s>Śriyaḥpati</s>, <s>Śrīparama</s>, <s>Śrīmān</s>, <s>Śrīvatsalāñchana</s>,

body.text:
nṛsiṃho duṣṭadāmano
jayo viṣṇus trivikramaḥ
stutaḥ prayacchate cārtham
evam ādibhir acyutaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Duṣṭadāmana</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Trivikrama</s>—<s>Acyuta</s>, praised by these and the like, grants wealth

body.text:
kāmyaḥ kāmapradaḥ kāntaḥ
kāmapālas tathā hariḥ
ānando mādhavaś caiva
kāmasaṃsiddhaye nṛpa
body.translated_text: <s>Kāmya</s>, <s>Kāmaprada</s>, <s>Kānta</s>, and likewise <s>Kāmapāla</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, and <s>Mādhava</s>—[these are to be muttered] for the accomplishing of desire, O king

body.text:
rāmaḥ paraśurāmaś ca
nṛsiṃho viṣṇur eva ca
vikramaś caivam ādīni
japyāny arijigīṣubhiḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Paraśurāma</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> too, and <s>Vikrama</s>—these and the like are to be muttered by those wishing to conquer enemies

body.text:
vidyām abhyasatā nityaṃ
japtavyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
dāmodaraṃ bandhagato
nityam eva japan naraḥ
body.translated_text: By one practicing learning, <s>Puruṣottama</s> is ever to be muttered; one in bondage, ever muttering <s>Dāmodara</s>,

body.text:
keśavaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
puṣkarākṣaṃ tathā japet
netrabādhāsu sarvāsu
hṛṣīkeśaṃ bhayeṣu ca
body.translated_text: should mutter <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, and likewise <s>Puṣkarākṣa</s>; in all eye-troubles and in fears, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>

body.text:
acyutaṃ cāmṛtaṃ caiva
japed auṣadhakarmaṇi
bhrājiṣṇum agnihānau ca
japed ālambane sthitam
body.translated_text: He should mutter <s>Acyuta</s> and <s>Amṛta</s> in the work of medicine; and <s>Bhrājiṣṇu</s> in the loss of fire, and [the Lord] established in a support

body.text:
saṃgrāmābhimukhaṃ gacchan
saṃsmared aparājitam
pātālanarasiṃhaṃ ca
jalaprataraṇe smaret
body.translated_text: Going forth to face battle, one should remember <s>Aparājita</s>; and one should remember <s>Pātāla-Narasiṃha</s> in the crossing of water

body.text:
cakriṇaṃ gadinaṃ caiva
śārṅginaṃ khaḍginaṃ tathā
kṣemārthe prasavan rājan
dikṣu prācyādiṣu smaret
body.translated_text: The discus-bearer, the mace-bearer, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, and the sword-bearer—for the sake of safety when setting out, O king, one should remember [them] in the eastern and other directions

body.text:
ajitaṃ cādhikaṃ caiva
sarvaṃ sarvaśvaraṃ tathā
saṃsmaret puruṣo bhaktyā
vyavahāreṣu sarvadā
body.translated_text: <s>Ajita</s>, and <s>Adhika</s>, and <s>Sarva</s>, and <s>Sarveśvara</s>—a man should remember [these] with devotion, ever in [his] dealings

body.text:
nārāyaṇaṃ sarvakālaṃ
kṣutapraskhalitādiṣu
grahanakṣatrapīḍāsu
devabādhāṭavīṣu ca
body.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at all times—in sneezing, stumbling, and the like, in the afflictions of planets and lunar mansions, in [the perils of] divine assaults and forests,

body.text:
asyuvairinirodheṣu
vyāghrasiṃhādisaṃkaṭe
andhakāre ca tīvre ca
narasiṃham anusmaret
taraty akhiladurgāṇi
tāpārto jalaśāyinam
body.translated_text: in the obstructions of foes, in the danger of tigers, lions, and the like, and in deep darkness, one should remember <s>Narasiṃha</s>; one tormented by suffering crosses all difficulties [by remembering] the one who lies on the water

body.text:
garuḍadhvajānusmaraṇād
āpadbhyo mucyate naraḥ
body.translated_text: From remembering the one with the <s>Garuḍa</s> banner, a man is freed from calamities

body.text:
jvaraduṣṭaśiroroga-
viṣavīryaṃ praśāmyati
body.translated_text: The virulence of fever, foul head-disease, and poison is calmed

body.text:
snāne devārcane home
praṇipāte pradakṣiṇe
kīrtayed bhagavannāma
vāsudeveti tatparaḥ
body.translated_text: In bathing, in worship of the god, in oblation, in obeisance, in circumambulation, one intent thereon should proclaim the name of the Blessed One, '<s>Vāsudeva</s>'

body.text:
sthagane vittadhānyāder
apadhyāne ca duṣṭaje
kurvīta tanmanā bhūtvā
anantācyutakīrtanam
body.translated_text: In the storing of wealth, grain, and the rest, and in evil meditation born of wickedness, having become single-minded thereon, one should perform the proclaiming of <s>Ananta</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
nārāyaṇaṃ śārṅgadharaṃ
śrīdharaṃ puruṣottamam
vāmanaṃ khaḍginaṃ caiva
duḥsvapneṣu ca saṃsmaret
body.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and the sword-bearer—one should remember [these] in bad dreams

body.text:
ekārṇavāhiparyaṅka-
śāyinaṃ ca naraḥ smaret
vāyvagnīgṛhadāhāya
pravṛddhāv upalakṣya ca
body.translated_text: And a man should remember the one who lies on the couch of the serpent in the single ocean, for [protection against] the burning of the house by wind and fire, observing it [when] grown

body.text:
vidyārthī mohavibhrānti-
vegāghūrṇitamānasaḥ
manuṣyo muniśārdūla
sadāśvaśirasaṃ smaret
body.translated_text: The seeker of learning, with mind whirled by the rush of delusion and confusion, O tiger among sages, should remember the one with the horse-head (<s>Hayaśiras</s>) ever

body.text:
balabhadraṃ samṛddhyarthī
sīrakarmaṇi kīrtayet
jagatsūtim apatyārthī
stuvan bhaktyā na sīdati
body.translated_text: One desiring prosperity should proclaim <s>Balabhadra</s> in the work of the plough; one desiring offspring, praising with devotion the source of the world, does not sink

body.text:
japtavyaṃ suprajākhyaṃ tu
devadevasya sattama
dampatyor ātmasaṃbandhe
vivāhākhye punaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: The [name] called <s>Suprajā</s> of the God of gods is to be muttered, O best one, in the self-union of husband and wife, in [the rite] called marriage, again and again

body.text:
śrīśaṃ sarvābhyudayike
karmaṇi saṃprakīrtayet
ariṣṭānteṣv aśeṣeṣu
viśokaṃ ca sadā japet
body.translated_text: One should proclaim <s>Śrīśa</s> in every prosperity-bringing rite; and in all warding-off of misfortunes one should ever mutter <s>Viśoka</s>

body.text:
marutpratāpāgnijala-
bandhanādiṣu mṛtyuṣu
svātantryaparatantreṣu
vāsudevaṃ japed budhaḥ
body.translated_text: In deaths by wind, scorching, fire, water, bondage, and the like, in [matters of] independence and dependence, the wise man should mutter <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
sarvārthaśaktiyuktasya
devadevasya cakriṇaḥ
yad vābhirocate nāma
tat sarvārtheṣu kīrtayet
body.translated_text: Of the God of gods, the discus-bearer, endowed with the power for every aim—whatever name pleases [one], that one should proclaim in all [one's] aims

body.text:
sarvārthasiddhim āpnoti
nāmnām ekārthatā yataḥ
sarvāṇy etāni nāmāni
parasya brahmaṇo 'nagha
body.translated_text: One attains the accomplishment of every aim, since there is oneness of meaning of the names; all these names are of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, O sinless one

body.text:
evam etāni nāmāni
devadevasya kīrtayet
yaṃ yaṃ kāmam abhidhyāyet
taṃ tam āpnoty asaṃśayam
sarvān kāmān avāpnoti
samārādhya jagadgurum
body.translated_text: Thus one should proclaim these names of the God of gods; whatever desire one meditates upon, that one attains without doubt; one attains all desires, having fully worshipped the Guru of the world

body.text:
tanmayatvena govindam
ity etad dālbhya nānyathā
tanmayo vāñchitān kāmān
yad avāpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: by becoming one with him, <s>Govinda</s>—thus this, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, not otherwise—since, become one with him, a man attains the desired wishes

body.text:
nimittaśaktiḥ sā tasya
na bhedo dālbhya mānasaḥ
vāṅmanaḥkāyikaṃ dveṣaṃ
yac ca kurvan prayāty adhaḥ
body.translated_text: That is his instrumental power, not a mental difference, O <s>Dālbhya</s>; and whatever hatred—of speech, mind, or body—one makes, [by that] one goes downward

body.text:
svarūpaśaktiḥ sā tasya
matibhedakṛtaṃ na tad
sa śākto nirguṇaḥ śuddho
brahmabhūto jagadguruḥ
body.translated_text: That is his essential power (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>); that is not made by difference of mind; he is possessed of power, without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), pure, become <s>Brahman</s>, the Guru of the world

body.text:
karmabhir nāmabhir jīvo
dṛśyate dālbhya naikadhā
yathā ca gaṅgāsalilaṃ
sitam atyantanirmalam
body.translated_text: By deeds and by names the soul is seen in many ways, O <s>Dālbhya</s>—just as the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, white and exceedingly pure,

body.text:
ekasvarūpam adhyātmaṃ
puṇyāpuṇyavibhedibhiḥ
bhrāntijñānānvitair miśraṃ
sitāsitaviceṣṭitaiḥ
dṛśyate naikadhā dālbhya
prāṇibhir bhinnabuddhibhiḥ
body.translated_text: one in nature with respect to the inner self, mingled by those who divide it into merit and demerit, by those endowed with deluded knowledge, by white and dark activities, is seen in many ways, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, by living beings of differing understanding.

body.text:
tāpārtās tāpaśamanam
atiprītyatiśītalam
kaphadoṣānvitair nāti-
prītiyuktair niraṃśubhiḥ
body.translated_text: By those afflicted with heat [it is seen as] the calmer of heat, exceedingly pleasing and very cool; by those afflicted with the phlegm-humor [it is seen as] not very pleasing and ray-less;

body.text:
strīyogyam etan netīti
prītyaprītisamanvitaiḥ
madhyasthabuddhyā caivānye
nātiśītātitāpibhiḥ
body.translated_text: 'This is fit for women, this is not,' by those filled with liking and disliking; and others, with a neutral mind, [see it as] neither very cold nor very hot;

body.text:
pavitram ity etad iti
puṇyabuddhyā tathāparaiḥ
mṛṣṭam etad itīty anyair
matsyāḍhyam iti cāparaiḥ
body.translated_text: 'This is pure,' thus by some with a meritorious mind; 'this is clean,' thus by others; 'it is rich in fish,' thus by yet others;

body.text:
tulyabuddhyāpi caivānyair
heyabuddhyā tathāparaiḥ
nātivegātivegaṃ ca
hṛṣṭodvignais tathāparaiḥ
body.translated_text: and by others with an equal mind, and by yet others with a disdaining mind; and by others elated and agitated, [seen] as not too swift or too swift in current;

body.text:
kim eteneti caivānyaiḥ
paradārābhilāṣibhiḥ
dālbhya saṃdṛśyate cānyair
jantubhir bhāyakātaraiḥ
tad eva pūyaṃ paśyanti
pretādyā hṛtipāpinaḥ
body.translated_text: and 'what is this for?' thus by others, those who lust after others' wives; and it is seen by other creatures timid through fear, O <s>Dālbhya</s>; that very same [water] the <s>pretas</s> and other thievish sinners see as pus.

body.text:
etaiś cānyaiś ca bahubhir
viśeṣair bahujantubhiḥ
viśeṣavat karmabhedād
ekam eva hi dṛśyate
body.translated_text: By these and other many beings of many kinds, through the difference of deeds, that which is various—one alone indeed—is seen.

body.text:
naite gaṅgāmbhaso bhedāḥ
prītyaprītipradāyinaḥ
prāṇināṃ cetaso bhedād
dālbhyaite karmayonayaḥ
body.translated_text: These are not differences of the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the givers of liking and disliking; through the difference of the minds of living beings, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, these are the wombs of action.

body.text:
samastakarmaṇā dālbhya
saṃkṣaye bhayam ety asau
viśeṣakāraṇābhāvād
viśeṣābhāva eva hi
body.translated_text: On the destruction of the whole of action, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, this one comes to no [further differentiation]; through the absence of the cause of difference, there is indeed the very absence of difference.

body.text:
viṣṇvākhyam evaṃ tad brahma
śuddham atyantanirmalam
abhedaṃ bahudhā bhinnaṃ
dṛśyate karmabhedibhiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus that <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, pure, exceedingly stainless, undivided, manifoldly divided, is seen by those who differ through their deeds.

body.text:
yogibhir dṛśyate śuddhaṃ
rāgādyupaśamāmalaiḥ
rāgibhir viṣayākāraṃ
tad eva brahma dṛśyate
body.translated_text: By <s>yogins</s>, stainless through the calming of passion and the rest, it is seen as pure; by the passionate, that very same <s>Brahman</s> is seen in the form of sense-objects.

body.text:
karmamārgāśritaiḥ karma-
bhoktṛtve ca tatheṣyate
kim apy astīti caivānyair
avivekibhir ucyate
body.translated_text: By those resorting to the path of action it is held to be in the condition of an enjoyer of action; and 'it is something,' thus it is said by others lacking discrimination.

body.text:
sarvam etat tad eveti
vadanty advaitavādinaḥ
pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyam eveti
vadanty anye duruktibhiḥ
body.translated_text: 'All this is that very one,' say the <s>Advaita</s> (non-dualist) speakers; 'the visible alone is perceptible,' say others with evil speech;

body.text:
vadanty anye tad evāhaṃ
nāstīty anye vadanti tat
tiryaṅmanuṣyadevākhyaṃ
tad anyair abhidhīyate
body.translated_text: others say 'that very one am I'; others say 'it does not exist'; by others it is called by the name beast, human, and god.

body.text:
vandyabuddhyā tu tat kaiścid
dhyeyabuddhyā tathāparaiḥ
gamyabuddhyā tathānyaiś ca
labhyabuddhyā ca jantubhiḥ
body.translated_text: By some with a worshipping mind, by others with a mind of meditation, by yet others with a mind of [it being] attainable, and with a mind of [it being] obtainable by creatures,

body.text:
gṛhyate tat paraṃ brahma
ripubuddhyā tathāparaiḥ
body.translated_text: that supreme <s>Brahman</s> is grasped; and by yet others with the mind of [it being] an enemy,

body.text: ātmaputrasuhṛdbhartṛ-
body.translated_text: [by some] with the mind of self, son, friend, husband,

body.text: parabuddhyā tathāparaiḥ
body.translated_text: and by yet others with the mind of [it being] another,

body.text: parabuddhyā ca naikadhā
body.translated_text: and with the mind of [it being] supreme, in many ways.

body.text:
prāṇibhiḥ karmavaiṣamya-
bhinnabuddhibhir avyayam
tad brahma gṛhyate dālbhya
paramārthaṃ nibodha me
body.translated_text: By living beings of understanding differentiated by the inequality of deeds, that imperishable <s>Brahman</s> is grasped, O <s>Dālbhya</s>; learn from me the supreme truth.

body.text:
bhūtendriyāntaḥkaraṇa-
pradhānapuruṣātmakam
aparaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ
paraṃ dālbhya niśāmaya
body.translated_text: Consisting of the elements, the senses, the inner faculty, <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), and <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit)—that is the lower form of <s>Brahman</s>; behold the higher, O <s>Dālbhya</s>:

body.text:
aheyam akṣaraṃ śuddham
asaṃbhūtinirañjanam
viṣṇvākhyaṃ paramaṃ brahma
yad vai paśyanti sūrayaḥ
body.translated_text: unforsakable, imperishable, pure, free of origination, untainted, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which indeed the wise behold.

body.text:
yathaitad bhavatā proktaṃ
dharmārthādes tu sādhanam
patnī nṝṇāṃ muniśreṣṭha
yoṣitas ca tathā naraḥ
body.translated_text: As this was declared by you to be the means of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and the rest, the wife is for men, O best of sages, and likewise the woman has the man—

body.text:
tac chrotum icche viprarṣe
vidhavā strī na jāyate
upoṣītena yenāgryā
patnyā ca rahito naraḥ
body.translated_text: I wish to hear that, O sage among <s>vipras</s>: a woman does not become a widow, and a man is not deprived of his foremost wife, by fasting on which [vow].

body.text:
aśūnyaśayanā nāma
dvitīyāṃ śṛṇu tāṃ mama
yām upoṣya na vaidhavyaṃ
prayāti strī dvijottama
body.translated_text: Hear from me that second [vow] named <s>Aśūnyaśayanā</s> ('the un-empty bed'), by fasting on which a woman does not go to widowhood, O best of the twice-born,

body.text:
patnīviyuktaś ca naro
na kadācit prajāyate
śete jagatpatiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
śriyā sārdhaṃ yadā dvija
body.translated_text: and a man is never separated from his wife. When the Lord of the world <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> lies down together with <s>Śrī</s>, O twice-born—

body.text:
aśūnyaśayanā nāma
tadā grāhyā hi sā tithiḥ
kṛṣṇapakṣadvitīyāyāṃ
śrāvaṇe dvijasattama
body.translated_text: that lunar day, named <s>Aśūnyaśayanā</s>, is then to be observed: on the second of the dark fortnight in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, O best of the twice-born.

body.text:
idam uccārayen nāma
praṇamya jagataḥ patim
śrīvatsadhāriṇaṃ śrīśaṃ
bhaktyābhyarcya śriyā saha
body.translated_text: One should utter this name, having bowed to the Lord of the world, the bearer of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, the lord of <s>Śrī</s>, having worshipped him with devotion together with <s>Śrī</s>:

body.text:
śrīvatsadhāriñ śrīkānta
śrīdhāma śrīpate 'cyuta
gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me
yātu dharmārthakāmadam
body.translated_text: "O bearer of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, abode of <s>Śrī</s>, lord of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>—may my household life not come to destruction, [my household] the giver of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>.

body.text:
agnayo mā praṇaśyantu
mā praṇaśyantu devatāḥ
pitaro mā praṇaśyantu
matto dāmpatyabhedataḥ
body.translated_text: May my [sacred] fires not perish, may the deities not perish, may the ancestors not perish from me through the breaking-apart of the married couple.

body.text:
lakṣmyā prayujyate deva
na kadācid yathā bhavān
tathā kalatrasaṃbandho
deva mā me vibhidyatām
body.translated_text: As you, O god, are never separated from <s>Lakṣmī</s>, so let my bond with my spouse, O god, never be sundered.

body.text:
lakṣmyā na śūnyaṃ varada
yathā te śayanaṃ sadā
śayyā mamāpy aśūnyāstu
tathaiva madhusūdana
body.translated_text: As your bed, O boon-giver, is never empty of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, so let my bed too never be empty, likewise, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>."

body.text:
evaṃ prasādya pūjāṃ ca
kṛtvā lakṣmyās tathā hareḥ
phalāni dadyāc chayyāyām
abhīṣṭāni jagatpateḥ
body.translated_text: Thus having propitiated and performed worship of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and of <s>Hari</s>, one should give the desired fruits upon the bed of the Lord of the world.

body.text:
naktaṃ praṇamyāyatane
havir bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ
brāhmaṇāya dvitīye 'hni
śaktyā dadyāc ca dakṣiṇām
body.translated_text: At night, having bowed in the temple, one should eat the oblation, with speech restrained; and on the second day one should give a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee) to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> according to ability.

body.text:
evaṃ karoti yaḥ samyag
naro māsacatuṣṭayam
tasya janmatrayaṃ dālbhya
gṛhabhaṅgo na jāyate
body.translated_text: The man who does this rightly for a set of four months—for him, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, for three births there occurs no breaking of the household.

body.text:
aśūnyaśayanaś cāsau
dharmakarmārthasādhakaḥ
bhavaty avyāhataiśvaryaḥ
puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: And that man has an un-empty bed, an accomplisher of <s>dharma</s>, action, and <s>artha</s>; he becomes a man of unimpeded lordship—there is no doubt in this.

body.text:
nārī ca dālbhya dharmajñā
vratam etad yathāvidhi
yā karoti na sā śocyā
bandhuvargasya jāyate
body.translated_text: And a woman knowing <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, who performs this vow according to rule—she does not become one to be grieved over by the circle of kinsmen.

body.text:
vaidhavyaṃ durbhagatvaṃ vā
bhartṛtyāgaṃ ca sattama
nāpnoti janmatritayam
etac cīrtvā pativratā
body.translated_text: She does not attain widowhood, nor ill fortune, nor the abandonment of her husband, O best one, for three births, having performed this, a devoted wife.

body.text:
upavāsāśritaṃ samyag
lokadvayaphalapradam
kathitaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ
yat pṛṣṭo 'si mayā dvija
body.translated_text: All that grounded in fasting, the giver of the fruit of both worlds, has been told by you, about which I asked you, O twice-born.

body.text:
anyad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ
tad bhavān prabravītu me
saṃsārahetuṃ muktiṃ ca
saṃsārān munisattama
body.translated_text: I wish to hear another thing—let your honor declare it to me: the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and the release from <s>saṃsāra</s>, O best of sages.

body.text:
avidyāprabhavaṃ karma
hetubhūtaṃ dvijottama
saṃsārasyāsya tanmuktiḥ
saṃkṣepāc chrūyatāṃ mama
body.translated_text: Action arising from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the cause of this <s>saṃsāra</s>, O best of the twice-born; the release from it—let it be heard from me in brief.

body.text:
svajātivihitaṃ karma
lobhadveṣavivarjitam
kurvataḥ kṣīyate pūrvaṃ
manyubandhaś ca neṣyate
body.translated_text: For one performing the action enjoined for his own caste, free of greed and hatred, the former [accumulated karma] dwindles, and no bond of wrath is incurred.

body.text:
apūrvasaṃbhavābhavāt
kṣayaṃ yāty ādikarmaṇi
dālbhya saṃsāravicchedaḥ
kāraṇābhāvasaṃbhavaḥ
body.translated_text: Through the non-arising of new [karma], it comes to destruction in the primal action; O <s>Dālbhya</s>, the cutting-off of <s>saṃsāra</s> arises from the absence of cause.

body.text:
bhavaty asaṃśayaṃ cānyac
śrūyatām atra kāraṇam
saṃsārān mucyate dālbhya
samāsād vadato mama
body.translated_text: And there is, without doubt, another [cause]; let the cause here be heard—one is released from <s>saṃsāra</s>, O <s>Dālbhya</s>—as I tell it in brief.

body.text:
gṛhītakarmaṇā yena
puṃsāṃ jātir dvijottama
body.translated_text: By the action taken up, by which there is birth for men, O best of the twice-born,

body.text:
tatprāyaścittabhūtaṃ vai
śṛṇu karmakṣayāvaham
body.translated_text: the very thing which is its expiation—hear it, the bringer of the destruction of action.

body.text:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ
śūdrāntyānāṃ ca sattama
svajātivihitaṃ karma
rāgadveṣādivarjitam
body.translated_text: Of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>vaiśyas</s>, of <s>śūdras</s> and the lowest, O best one, the action enjoined for one's own caste, free of passion, hatred, and the rest,

body.text:
jātipradasya kṣayadaṃ
tad evādyasya karmaṇaḥ
jñānakāraṇabhāvaṃ ca
tad eva pratipadyate
body.translated_text: is both the giver of [a new] birth and the destroyer of that very primal action; and that very thing attains the condition of being the cause of knowledge.

body.text:
pumāṃś cādhigatajñāno
bhedaṃ nāpnoti sattama
brahmaṇā viṣṇusaṃjñena
parameṇāvyayātmanā
body.translated_text: And a man who has attained knowledge does not come to difference, O best one, from <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme, of imperishable nature.

body.text:
etat te kathitaṃ dālbhya
saṃsārasya samāsataḥ
kāraṇaṃ bhavamuktiś ca
jāyate yogino yathā
body.translated_text: This has been told to you, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, in brief: the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and the release from existence, how it arises for the <s>yogin</s>.

body.text:
iti dālbhyaḥ pulastyena
yathāvat pratibodhitaḥ
ārādhayām āsa hariṃ
lebhe kāmāṃś ca vāñchitān
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Dālbhya</s>, duly awakened by <s>Pulastya</s>, worshipped <s>Hari</s> and obtained the desires he wished.

body.text:
tathā tvam api daityendra
keśavārādhanaṃ kuru
ārādhya taṃ jagannāthaṃ
na kaścid avasīdati
body.translated_text: So you too, O <s>Daitya</s> lord, perform the worship of <s>Keśava</s>; having worshipped that Lord of the world, no one is brought low.

body.text:
iti śukravacaḥ śrutvā
prahlādo madhusūdanam
ārādhya prāptavān kṛtsnaṃ
trailokaiśvaryam ūrjitam
body.translated_text: Thus, having heard the speech of <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, having worshipped <s>Madhusūdana</s>, obtained the entire mighty sovereignty of the three worlds.

body.text:
etan mayoktaṃ sakalaṃ
tava bhūmipa pṛcchataḥ
anārādhyācyutaṃ devaṃ
kaḥ kāmān prāpnute naraḥ
body.translated_text: All this has been told by me to you who asked, O lord of the earth; without worshipping the god <s>Acyuta</s>, what man attains his desires?

body.text:
ambarīso narapatir
viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam
śrutvā babhūva satataṃ
keśavārpitamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: The king <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, having heard the supreme greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, became ever one whose mind was offered to <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
evaṃ tvam api kauravya
yadi muktim abhīṣyasi
bhogān vā vilupān devāt
tasmād ārādhayācyutam
body.translated_text: So you too, O <s>Kauravya</s>, if you desire release, or pleasures hard to obtain, from the god—therefore worship <s>Acyuta</s>.

body.text:
dadāti vāñchitān kāmān
sakāmair arcito hariḥ
muktiṃ dadāti govindo
niṣkāmair abhipūjitaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, worshipped by those with desires, gives the wished-for objects of desire; <s>Govinda</s>, worshipped by the desireless, gives release.

body.text:
bhagavān avatīrṇo 'bhūn
martyalokaṃ janārdanaḥ
bhārāvataraṇārthāya
bhuvo bhūtapatir hariḥ
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Janārdana</s> descended to the world of mortals; for the sake of removing the burden of the earth, <s>Hari</s>, the lord of beings.

body.text:
mānuṣatve ca govindo
mama pūrvapitāmahaiḥ
cakāra prītim atulāṃ
sāmānyapuruṣo yathā
body.translated_text: And in his human state <s>Govinda</s> showed incomparable love to my forefathers, like an ordinary man.

body.text:
sārathyaṃ kṛtavāṃś caiva
teṣāṃ sarveśvaro hariḥ
nistīrṇo yena bhīṣmaugho
kurusainyamahodadhiḥ
body.translated_text: And <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of all, performed the charioteering for them, by whom the flood of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, the great ocean of the <s>Kuru</s> army, was crossed over.

body.text:
upakārī mahābhāgaḥ
sa teṣāṃ sarvavastuṣu
keśavaḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ
sutānāṃ janako yathā
body.translated_text: That greatly fortunate <s>Keśava</s> was a benefactor to them in all matters, like the begetter of the sons of the <s>Pāṇḍu</s>-sons.

body.text:
dhanyās te kṛtapuṇyāś ca
mama pāṇḍusutā matāḥ
viviśur ye pariṣvaṅge
govindabhujapañjaram
body.translated_text: Blessed and of accomplished merit are those sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, in my judgment, who entered into the embrace, the cage of <s>Govinda</s>'s arms.

body.text:
rājyahetor arīñ jaghnur
akasmāt pāṇḍunandanāḥ
saptalokaikanāthena
ye 'bhavann ekaśāyinaḥ
body.translated_text: For the sake of the kingdom the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> slew their enemies, suddenly, who became single sleepers [protected] by the one Lord of the seven worlds.

body.text:
ātmānam avagacchāmi
bhagavan dhūtakalmaṣam
jātaṃ nirdhūtapāpe 'smin
kule viṣṇuparigrahe
body.translated_text: I regard myself, O Blessed One, as having my sins shaken off, born in this lineage of shaken-off sin, embraced by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
evaṃ devavaras teṣāṃ
prasādasumukho hariḥ
pṛcchatāṃ kaccid ācaṣṭe
kiṃcid guhyaṃ mahātmanām
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Hari</s>, the best of gods, his face gracious with favor toward them, would tell something secret to the great-souled ones when they asked.

body.text:
guhyaṃ janārdanaṃ yāṃs tu
dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
papraccha dharmān akhilāṃs
tan mamākhyātum arhasi
body.translated_text: The secret <s>dharmas</s>, all of them, which <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> the son of <s>Dharma</s> asked of <s>Janārdana</s>—those you ought to relate to me.

body.text:
dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu
yad guhyaṃ madhusūdanaḥ
teṣām avocad bhagavāñ
śrotum icchāmi tat tv aham
body.translated_text: Whatever secret in <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> the Blessed <s>Madhusūdana</s> spoke to them—that I wish to hear.

body.text:
bahūni dharmaguhyāni
dharmaputrāya keśavaḥ
purā provāca rājendra
prasādasumukho hariḥ
body.translated_text: Many secrets of <s>dharma</s> <s>Keśava</s> formerly spoke to the son of <s>Dharma</s>, O lord of kings, <s>Hari</s>, his face gracious with favor.

body.text:
śaratalpagatād bhīṣmād
dharmāñ śrutvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
pṛṣṭavān yaj jagannāthaṃ
tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: Having heard the <s>dharmas</s> from <s>Bhīṣma</s> who lay on the bed of arrows, what <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> then asked of the Lord of the world—hear that as I declare it.

body.text:
pañcamenāśvamedhena
yadā snāto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
tadā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ
praśnam etam apṛcchata
body.translated_text: When <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> was consecrated by a fifth horse-sacrifice, then he asked the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> this question:

body.text:
bhagavan vaiṣṇavā dharmāḥ
kiṃphalāḥ kiṃparāyaṇāḥ
kiṃ kṛtyam adhikṛtyaite
bhavatotpāditāḥ purā
body.translated_text: "O Blessed One, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>dharmas</s>—what is their fruit, what their goal? Concerning what matter were these brought forth by you of old?

body.text:
yadi te pāṇḍuṣu sneho
vidyate madhusūdana
śrotavyāś cen mayā dharmās
tatas tān kathayākhilān
body.translated_text: If affection for the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> exists in you, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>, and if the <s>dharmas</s> are to be heard by me, then relate them all,

body.text:
pavitrāś caiva ye dharmāḥ
sarvapāpapraṇāśanāḥ
tava vaktracyutā deva
sarvadharmeṣv anuttamāḥ
body.translated_text: and the <s>dharmas</s> which are purifying, the destroyers of all sin, fallen from your mouth, O god, unsurpassed among all <s>dharmas</s>,

body.text:
yāñ śrutvā brahmahā goghnaḥ
pitṛghno gurutalpagaḥ
surāpo vā kṛtaghnaś ca
mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
body.translated_text: hearing which the slayer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the cow-killer, the slayer of a father, the violator of the teacher's bed, the drinker of liquor, and the ingrate is freed from all transgressions.

body.text:
etan me kathitaṃ sarvaṃ
sabhāmadhye 'risūdana
vasiṣṭhādyair mahābhāgair
munibhir bhāvitātmabhiḥ
body.translated_text: All this was told to me in the midst of the assembly, O slayer of foes, by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and other greatly fortunate sages of cultivated selves.

body.text:
tato 'haṃ tava deveśa
pādamūlam upāgataḥ
dharmān kathaya tān deva
yady ahaṃ bhavataḥ priyaḥ
body.translated_text: Then I, O lord of gods, have come to the soles of your feet; relate those <s>dharmas</s>, O god, if I am dear to you.

body.text:
śrutā me mānavā dharmā
vāsiṣṭhāś ca mahāmate
parāśarakṛtāś caiva
tathātreyasya dhīmataḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> of <s>Manu</s> have been heard by me, and those of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, O greatly wise one, and those made by <s>Parāśara</s>, and likewise of the wise <s>Ātreya</s>;

body.text:
śrutā gārgyasya śaṅkhasya
likhitasya yamasya ca
jāpāleś ca mahābāho
muner dvaipāyanasya ca
body.translated_text: heard are those of <s>Gārgya</s>, of <s>Śaṅkha</s>, of <s>Likhita</s>, and of <s>Yama</s>, and of <s>Jābāli</s>, O mighty-armed one, and of the sage <s>Dvaipāyana</s>;

body.text:
umāmaheśvarāś caiva
jātidharmāś ca pāvanāḥ
guṇeś ca guṇabāhoś ca
kāśyapeyās tathaiva ca
body.translated_text: and those of <s>Umā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>, and the purifying caste-<s>dharmas</s>, and those of <s>Guṇa</s> and <s>Guṇabāhu</s>, and likewise the <s>Kāśyapeya</s> ones;

body.text:
bahvāyanakṛtāś caiva
śākuneyās tathaiva ca
agastyagītā maudgalyāḥ
śāṇḍilyāḥ saurabhās tathā
body.translated_text: and those made by <s>Bahvāyana</s>, and likewise the <s>Śākuneya</s> ones, those sung by <s>Agastya</s>, the <s>Maudgalya</s>, the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, and the <s>Saurabha</s> ones likewise;

body.text:
bhṛgor aṅgirasaś caiva
kaśyapoddālakās tathā
saumantūgrāyaṇāgrāś ca
pailasya ca mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: those of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and of <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Uddālaka</s> likewise, and the <s>Saumantu</s>, the <s>Ugrāyaṇa</s>, and the foremost ones, and of the great-souled <s>Paila</s>;

body.text:
vaiśampāyanagītāś ca
piśaṅgamakṛtāś ca ye
aindrāś ca vāruṇāś caiva
kauberā vātsyapauṇakāḥ
body.translated_text: and those sung by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, and those made by <s>Piśaṅgama</s>, and the <s>Aindra</s>, the <s>Vāruṇa</s>, the <s>Kaubera</s>, the <s>Vātsya</s>, and the <s>Pauṇaka</s> ones;

body.text:
āpastambāḥ śrutā dharmās
tathā gopālakasya ca
bhṛgvaṅgiraḥkṛtāś caiva
sauryā hārītakās tathā
yājñavalkyakṛtāś caiva
tathā saptarṣayaś ca ye
body.translated_text: the <s>Āpastamba</s> <s>dharmas</s> have been heard, and likewise those of <s>Gopālaka</s>, and those made by <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, the <s>Saurya</s> and the <s>Hārītaka</s> ones, and those made by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, and likewise those of the Seven Seers;

body.text:
etāś cānyāś ca vividhāḥ
śrutā me dharmasaṃhitāḥ
bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi
tava vaktrād viniḥsṛtān
body.translated_text: these and other various collections of <s>dharma</s> have been heard by me; O Blessed One, I wish to hear those issued forth from your mouth."

body.text:
evam uktaḥ sa pārthena
pratyuvāca janārdanaḥ
bahumānāc ca prītyā ca
dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by the son of <s>Pṛthā</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> replied, with great honor and with love, to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> the son of <s>Dharma</s>:

body.text:
iṣṭas tvaṃ hi mahābāho
sadā mama yudhiṣṭhira
paramārthaṃ tava brūyāṃ
kiṃ punar dharmasaṃhitām
body.translated_text: "You indeed are ever dear to me, O mighty-armed <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>; I would tell you the supreme truth—how much more a collection of <s>dharma</s>?

body.text:
paramajñānibhiḥ siddhair
yuñjadbhir api nityaśaḥ
praśāntasyeva dīpasya
gatir mama duratyayā
body.translated_text: Even for the supreme knowers, the perfected, ever engaged [in yoga], my course, like that of a lamp gone calm, is hard to traverse.

body.text:
sarvavedamayaṃ brahma
pavitram ṛṣibhiḥ stutam
kathayiṣyāmi te rājan
dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtām vara
body.translated_text: I shall relate to you, O king, the <s>Brahman</s> consisting of all the <s>Vedas</s>, the purifying, praised by the seers, the <s>dharma</s>, O best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>."

body.text:
evam ukte tu kṛṣṇena
ṛṣayo 'mitatejasaḥ
samājagmuḥ sabhāmadhye
śrotukāmā harer giram
body.translated_text: When this was thus said by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the seers of boundless splendor assembled in the midst of the assembly, desirous of hearing the speech of <s>Hari</s>.

body.text:
devagandharvaṛṣayo
guhyakāś ca mahāyaśāḥ
vālakhilyā mahātmāno
munayaḥ saṃmitavratāḥ
pāvanān sarvadharmebhyo
rahasyān dvijasattama
body.translated_text: the gods, <s>Gandharvas</s> and seers, and the <s>Guhyakas</s> of great fame, the great-souled <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, the sages of measured vows, [praise these dharmas], purifying among all <s>dharmas</s>, secret, O best of the twice-born

body.text:
vaiṣṇavān akhilān dharmān
yaḥ paṭhet pāpanāśanān
bhaveyur akṣayās tasya
lokāḥ satpuṇyabhāginaḥ
body.translated_text: He who reads all these <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>dharmas</s>, the destroyers of sin—for him the worlds become undecaying, partaking of the merit of the good

body.text:
kṛṣṇadṛṣṭihataṃ cāsya
kilbiṣaṃ saṃpraṇaśyati
vaiṣṇavasya ca yajñasya
phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: And his sin, struck down by the glance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, utterly perishes; and the man attains the fruit of a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> sacrifice

body.text:
kautūhalasamāviṣṭaḥ
papracchedaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
yamalokasya cādhvānam
antaraṃ mānuṣasya ca
body.translated_text: Filled with curiosity, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> asked this about the road of the world of <s>Yama</s> and the interval of the human [world]:

body.text:
kīdṛśaṃ kiṃpramāṇaṃ vā
kathaṃ vāntaṃ janārdana
taranti puruṣāḥ kṛṣṇa
kenopāyena saṃśame
body.translated_text: "Of what sort, of what measure, or how [great] is the distance, <s>Janārdana</s>? By what means do men cross it, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in tranquillity?"

body.text:
tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā
vismito madhusūdanaḥ
pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ
dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
body.translated_text: Having heard that speech of his, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, astonished, replied to the great-souled <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s>:

body.text:
sādhu sādhur ayaṃ praśnaḥ
śrūyatāṃ bho yudhiṣṭhira
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi
yojanānāṃ narādhipa
body.translated_text: "Excellent, excellent is this question; let it be heard, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>—eighty-six thousand <s>yojanas</s>, O lord of men,

body.text:
yamalokasya cādhvānam
antaraṃ mānuṣasya ca
tāmrapātram ivātaptaṃ
śūlavyāmiśrakaṇṭakam
body.translated_text: is the road of the world of <s>Yama</s>, and the interval of the human [world]; like an unheated copper vessel, mixed with spikes and thorns,

body.text:
dvādaśādityasaṃkāśaṃ
bhairavaṃ duratikramam
na tatra vṛkṣā na cchāyā
pānīyaṃ ketanāni ca
body.translated_text: resembling twelve suns, terrible, hard to traverse; there are no trees there, no shade, no water and no shelters,

body.text:
yatra viśramate śrāntaḥ
puruṣo 'dhvānako nṛpa
yāmyair dūtair nīyamāno
yamasyājñākarair balāt
body.translated_text: where the weary, road-worn man might rest, O king, being led by force by the <s>Yāmya</s> messengers, the executors of <s>Yama</s>'s command

body.text:
avaśyaṃ ca mahārāja
sa gantavyo mahāpathaḥ
naraiḥ strībhis tathā tiryaiḥ
pṛthivyāṃ jīvasaṃjñakaiḥ
body.translated_text: And inevitably, O great king, that great path must be travelled by men, by women, and by beasts on earth, by those called living beings

body.text:
ekaviṃśac ca narakā
yamasya viṣaye smṛtāḥ
ye tu duṣkṛtakarmāṇas
te patanti pṛthak pṛthak
body.translated_text: And twenty-one hells are recorded in the domain of <s>Yama</s>; those who are doers of evil deeds fall into them severally

body.text:
narako rauravo nāma
mahāraurava eva ca
kṣuradhārā mahāraudraḥ
sūkaras tāla eva ca
body.translated_text: The hell named <s>Raurava</s>, and <s>Mahāraurava</s> too, <s>Kṣuradhārā</s>, <s>Mahāraudra</s>, <s>Sūkara</s>, and <s>Tāla</s>,

body.text:
vajrakumbho mahāghoraḥ
śālmalo 'tha vimohanaḥ
kīṭādaḥ kṛmibhakṣaś ca
śālmaliś ca mahādrumaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrakumbha</s> the most dreadful, <s>Śālmala</s>, then <s>Vimohana</s>, <s>Kīṭāda</s>, <s>Kṛmibhakṣa</s>, and the great tree <s>Śālmali</s>,

body.text:
tathā pūyavahaḥ pāpā
rudhirāndho mahattamaḥ
agnijvālo mahānādaḥ
saṃdāmśaḥ śunabhojanaḥ
tathā vaitaraṇī coṣṇā
asipattravanaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: likewise the sinful <s>Pūyavaha</s>, <s>Rudhirāndha</s> the most dark, <s>Agnijvāla</s>, <s>Mahānāda</s>, <s>Saṃdaṃśa</s>, <s>Śunabhojana</s>, and likewise the hot <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, and the <s>Asipattravana</s> (sword-leaf forest)

body.text:
viṣṇos tad vacanaṃ śrutvā
papāta bhuvi pāṇḍavaḥ
sa saṃjñaś ca muhūrtena
bhūyaḥ keśavam abravīt
body.translated_text: Having heard that speech of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> fell to the ground; and recovering consciousness in a moment, he again spoke to <s>Keśava</s>:

body.text:
bhītaś cāsmi mahābāho
śrutvā mārgasya vistaram
kenopāyena taṃ mārgaṃ
taranti puruṣāḥ sukham
body.translated_text: "I am afraid, O mighty-armed one, having heard the extent of the road; by what means do men cross that road with ease?"

body.text:
brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradānāni
nānārūpāṇi pārthiva
yo dadyāc chraddhayā yuktaḥ
sukhaṃ yāti mahāpatham
body.translated_text: "He who, endowed with faith, gives gifts of various kinds to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O prince, travels that great path with ease

body.text:
upānahapradā yānti
sukhaṃ chāyāsu cchattradāḥ
na teṣām aśubhaṃ kiṃcic
śūlādi na ca kaṇṭakāḥ
body.translated_text: Givers of sandals travel at ease; givers of parasols [travel] in shade; for them there is nothing inauspicious, no spikes and the rest, and no thorns

body.text:
upānahau yo dadāti
pātrabhūte dvijottame
aśvataryaḥ pradātāram
upatiṣṭhanti taṃ naram
body.translated_text: He who gives sandals to a worthy, most excellent twice-born—mules wait upon that man as a giver [of mounts]

body.text:
vitṛṣṇāś cāmbudātāras
tarpitāś cānnadās tathā
auprāvṛtā vastradāś ca
nagnā vai yānty avastradāḥ
body.translated_text: Givers of water [travel] free of thirst, and givers of food [travel] satisfied; givers of garments [travel] clothed, but the givers of no garments go naked indeed

body.text:
hiraṇyadāḥ sukhaṃ yānti
puruṣāḥ svābhyalaṃkṛtāḥ
gopradā yānti ca sukhaṃ
vimuktāḥ sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
body.translated_text: Givers of gold travel at ease, men well adorned [in their own ornaments]; and givers of cows travel at ease, released from all sins

body.text:
bhūmidāḥ sukham adhante
sarvakāmaiḥ sutarpitāḥ
yānti caivāparikliṣṭā
narāḥ śayyāsanapradāḥ
body.translated_text: Givers of land go happily, well satisfied with all desires; and men who are givers of beds and seats travel untroubled

body.text:
tataḥ sukhataraṃ yānti
vimāneṣu gṛhapradāḥ
kṣīrapradā hi divyābhiḥ
sasarpibhis tathaiva ca
body.translated_text: Then more happily, in celestial cars (<s>vimāna</s>), travel the givers of houses; and the givers of milk, likewise with celestial [women] and with ghee,

body.text:
gopradātā labhet tṛptiṃ
tasmin deśe sudurlabhām
ārāmaropī cchāyāsu
śītalāsu sukhaṃ vrajet
body.translated_text: The giver of a cow obtains satisfaction in that land, hard to obtain; the planter of a grove travels at ease in cool shades

body.text:
sugandhigandhino yānti
gandhamālyapradā naraḥ
adattadānā gacchanti
padbhyāṃ yānena yānadāḥ
dīpapradāḥ sukhaṃ yānti
dīpayantaś ca tatpatham
body.translated_text: Fragrant of sweet scent travel the givers of perfumes and garlands; those who have not given travel on foot, while givers of conveyances [travel] by conveyance; givers of lamps travel at ease, lighting up that path

body.text:
vimānair haṃsayuktais tu
yānti māsopavāsinaḥ
cakravākaprayuktena
pañcarātropavāsinaḥ
tato barhiṇayuktena
ṣaḍrātram upavāsinaḥ
body.translated_text: By celestial cars yoked with swans travel the month-long fasters; by [a car] yoked with <s>cakravāka</s> birds, the five-night fasters; then by [a car] yoked with peacocks, the six-night fasters

body.text:
trirātram ekabhaktena
kṣapayed yas tu pāṇḍava
anantaraṃ ca yo 'śnīyāt
tasya lokā yathā mama
body.translated_text: He who passes three nights with a single meal, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, and who eats [only] thereafter—his worlds are as mine

body.text:
panīyaṃ paralokeṣu
pāvanaṃ paramaṃ smṛtam
pānīyasya pradānena
tṛptir bhavati śāśvatī
pānīyasya guṇā divyāḥ
pretaloke sukhāvahāḥ
body.translated_text: Water in the other worlds is recorded as the supreme purifier; by the gift of water there is eternal satisfaction; the divine qualities of water are bringers of happiness in the world of the departed

body.text:
tatra puṇyodakā nāma
nadī teṣāṃ pravartate
śītalaṃ salilaṃ tatra
pibanti hy amṛtopamam
body.translated_text: There a river named <s>Puṇyodakā</s> flows for them; cool water they drink there, like nectar

body.text:
ye ca duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ
pūyaṃ teṣāṃ pravartate
eṣā nadī mahārāja
sarvakāmadughā śubhā
body.translated_text: And for those who are doers of evil deeds, pus flows for them; this river, O great king, is auspicious, yielding all desires

body.text:
adhvani khinnagātras tu
dvijo yaḥ kṣuttṛṣṇānvitaḥ
pṛcchan sadānnadātāram
abhyeti gṛham āśayā
taṃ pūjaya prayatnena
so 'tithir brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: When a twice-born, his body wearied on the road, beset by hunger and thirst, asking for a giver of good food, approaches a house with hope—honour him with effort; he is recorded as a guest, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>

body.text:
pitaro devatāś caiva
ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ
pūjitāḥ pūjite tasmin
nirāśe tu nirāśakāḥ
body.translated_text: The fathers and the deities, and the seers rich in austerity, are honoured when he is honoured; but when he is disappointed, they are disappointed

body.text:
tam eva gacchantam anuvrajanti
devāś ca sarve pitaras tathaiva
tasmin dvije pūjite pūjitās te
gate nirāśe pratiyānti nāśam
body.translated_text: As he goes away, the gods all follow after him, and likewise the fathers; when that twice-born is honoured, they are honoured; when he goes disappointed, they go to ruin

body.text:
ahany ahani dātavyaṃ
brāhmaṇebhyo yudhiṣṭhira
āgamiṣyati yat pātraṃ
tat pātraṃ tārayiṣyati
body.translated_text: Day after day [gifts] should be given to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>; whatever worthy recipient (<s>pātra</s>) shall come, that recipient will deliver [you]

body.text:
na tathā haviṣo homair
na puṣpair nānulepanaiḥ
agnau vā suhute rājan
yathā hy atithipūjane
body.translated_text: Not so by oblations of <s>haviṣ</s>, nor by flowers, nor by unguents, nor by fire well-fed, O king, [is one purified] as by the honouring of a guest

body.text:
kapilāyāṃ tu dattāyāṃ
yat phalaṃ jyeṣṭhapuṣkare
tat phalaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha
viprāṇāṃ pādaśaucane
body.translated_text: Whatever fruit there is when a tawny cow is given at <s>Jyeṣṭhapuṣkara</s>, that fruit, O best of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, [is gained] in the washing of the feet of <s>vipras</s>

body.text:
dvijapādodakaklinnā
yāvat tiṣṭhati medinī
tāvat puṣkarapātreṣu
pibanti pitaro jalam
body.translated_text: As long as the earth remains moist with the foot-water of the twice-born, so long do the fathers drink water from lotus-leaf vessels

body.text:
devamālyāpanayanaṃ
dvijocchiṣṭāpamārjanam
śrāntasaṃvāhanaṃ caiva
dīnasya paripālanam
ekaikaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha
gopradānād viśiṣyate
body.translated_text: The removing of the god's garlands, the wiping away of the twice-born's leavings, the massaging of the weary, and the protection of the wretched—each single one, O best of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, surpasses the gift of a cow

body.text:
pādaśaucaṃ tathābhyaṅgaṃ
dīpam annaṃ pratiśrayam
dadanti ye mahārāja
nopasarpanti te yamam
body.translated_text: Those who give the washing of the feet and likewise anointing, a lamp, food, and shelter, O great king, do not approach <s>Yama</s>

body.text:
svāgatenāgnayaḥ prītā
āsanena śatakratuḥ
pitaraḥ pādaśaucena
annādyena prajāpatiḥ
body.translated_text: The fires are pleased by a welcome, <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra) by a seat, the fathers by the washing of the feet, <s>Prajāpati</s> by food and eatables,

body.text:
abhayasya pradānena
bhavet prītir mamātulā
body.translated_text: [and] by the gift of safety (<s>abhaya</s>) there would be incomparable pleasure for me

body.text:
yeṣāṃ taḍāgāni bahūdakāni
prapāś ca kūpāś ca pratiśrayāś ca
annapradānaṃ madhurā ca vāṇī
yamasya te nirvacanā bhavanti
body.translated_text: Those whose tanks have abundant water, and wells and watering-sheds and shelters, [who give] the gift of food and [speak] sweet speech—they become free from the reproach of <s>Yama</s>

body.text:
savṛṣaṃ gośataṃ tena
dattaṃ bhavati śāśvatam
body.translated_text: By that a hundred cows together with a bull is given, eternally

body.text:
pāpaṃ karma ca yat kiṃcid
brahmahatyāsamaṃ bhavet
śochayet kapilāṃ dattvā
etad vai nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: And whatever sinful deed there may be, equal to the slaying of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one would cleanse [it] by giving a tawny cow; of this there is no doubt here

body.text:
prāsādā yatra sauvarṇā
vasordhārā ca syandate
gandharvāpsaraso yatra
tatra gacchanti gopradāḥ
body.translated_text: Where there are golden palaces, and the stream of wealth (<s>vasordhārā</s>) flows, where there are <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>—there go the givers of cows

body.text:
prayacchate yaḥ kapilāṃ savatsāṃ
kāṃsyopadohāṃ kanakāgraśṛṅgīm
yān yān hi kāmān abhivāñchate 'sau
tāṃs tān avāpnoty amalāṃś ca lokān
body.translated_text: He who gives a tawny cow with its calf, with a bronze milking-pail and gold-tipped horns—whatever desires that man longs for, those he attains, and the stainless worlds

body.text:
yāvad vatsasya dvau pādau
śiraś caiva pradṛśyate
tāvad gauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā
yāvad garbhaṃ na muñcati
tasmin kāle pradātavyā
vidhinā yā mayoditā
body.translated_text: As long as the calf's two feet and head are visible [emerging], so long the cow is to be known as the earth, as long as she has not released the [whole] foetus; at that time she is to be given by the rule which has been declared by me

body.text:
antarikṣagato vatso
yāvad yonyāṃ pradṛśyate
tāvad gauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā
yāvad garbhaṃ na muñcati
body.translated_text: As long as the calf, suspended in the air, is visible in the womb, so long the cow is to be known as the earth, as long as she has not released the foetus

body.text:
yāvanti tasya romāṇi
tāvadvarṣāṇi mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: As many hairs as she has, for so many years [is exalted] the man

body.text:
haṃsayuktena yānena
yuktenāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: by a conveyance yoked with swans, joined with the throngs of <s>Apsarases</s>,

body.text:
gandharvāpsarasodgītaiḥ
svargaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: amid the songs of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, he is exalted in the world of heaven

body.text:
tiladhenuṃ pravakṣyāmi
yaś cāsyā vidhir uttamaḥ
suvarṇanābhiṃ yaḥ kṛtvā
sukhūraṃ kṛṣṇamārgaṇām
body.translated_text: I shall declare the <s>tiladhenu</s> (sesame-cow) and what is its excellent rule: having made a golden navel, an easy [calf], in the figure of black [sesame],

body.text:
kutapaprastarasthāṃ tu
tilāṃ kṛtvā prayatnataḥ
tilaiḥ prasthādi tāṃ dadyāt
sarvaratnair alaṃkṛtām
body.translated_text: and having carefully placed the sesame upon a <s>kutapa</s>-blanket spread out, he should give it with a <s>prastha</s>-measure of sesame and the rest, adorned with all jewels

body.text:
sasamudradrumā caiva
saśailavanakānanā
caturantā bhaved dattā
pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: And [thereby] the earth, with its oceans and trees, with its mountains, forests and groves, bounded on four sides, would be given; of this there is no doubt here

body.text:
kṛṣṇājine tilāṃ kṛtvā
kṛṣṇāṃ vā yadi vetarām
body.translated_text: Having placed sesame on a black antelope-skin, whether black or otherwise,

body.text:
rājateṣu tu pātreṣu
koṇeṣu madhusarpiṣī
body.translated_text: and in silver vessels, in the corners honey and ghee,

body.text:
prīyatāṃ dharmarājeti
yad vā manasi vartate
yāvaj jīvakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ
tena dānena pūyate
body.translated_text: [saying] "May the King of <s>Dharma</s> (Yama) be pleased," or whatever is in the mind—by that gift, the sin done in a whole lifetime is purified

body.text:
dhanaṃ prāpnoti puṇyena
maunenājñāṃ prayacchati
upabhogaṃ tu dānena
jīvitaṃ brahmacaryayā
body.translated_text: By merit one attains wealth; by silence one grants command; enjoyment [is attained] by giving, [long] life by chastity

body.text:
ahiṃsayā paraṃ rūpam
dīkṣayā kulajanma ca
phalamūlāśanād rājyaṃ
svargaḥ parṇāśano bhavet
body.translated_text: By non-injury [one attains] supreme beauty, and birth in [a good] family by initiation; by eating fruits and roots, kingship; heaven by eating leaves

body.text:
payobhakṣa divaṃ yānti
snānena draviṇādhikāḥ
śākaṃ sādhayato rājyaṃ
nākapṛṣṭham anāśanāt
body.translated_text: By eating only milk they go to heaven; by bathing they exceed in wealth; by cooking [only] vegetables, kingship; the vault of heaven by fasting

body.text:
sthaṇḍile ca śayānasya
gṛhāṇi śayanāni ca
cīravalkaladhāriṇāṃ
vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca
body.translated_text: For one sleeping on the bare ground, houses and couches [are gained]; for the wearers of rags and bark, garments and ornaments,

body.text:
śayanāsanayānāni
ye gatā hi tapovanam
agnipraveśī niyataṃ
brahmaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: couches, seats and conveyances [are gained by] those who have gone to the penance-grove; the enterer of fire is surely exalted in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>

body.text:
rasānāṃ pratisaṃhārāt
saubhāgyam abhijāyate
āmiṣapratiṣedhāt tu
bhavaty āyuṣmatī prajā
body.translated_text: By the withdrawal from the savours [of food], good fortune is born; and by the prohibition of meat, one's offspring become long-lived

body.text:
udavāsaṃ vased yas tu
nāgānām adhipo bhavet
satyavādī naraśreṣṭha
devataih saha modate
body.translated_text: He who dwells immersed in water becomes the lord of the <s>Nāgas</s>; the truth-speaker, O best of men, rejoices together with the deities

body.text:
kīrtir bhavati dānena
ārogyaṃ cāpy ahiṃsayā
body.translated_text: Fame is gained by giving, and health too by non-injury

body.text:
dvijaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ
dvijatvaṃ cāpi puṣkalam
body.translated_text: By service to the twice-born, kingship, and twice-born status too in abundance

body.text:
dvijaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ
divyarūpam avāpnute
body.translated_text: By service to the twice-born, kingship; he attains a celestial form

body.text:
annapānapradānena
kāmabhogais tu tṛpyate
dīpālokapradānena
cakṣuṣmāñ jāyate naraḥ
body.translated_text: By the gift of food and drink, one is satisfied with the enjoyments of desire; by the gift of lamp-light, a man is born possessed of [good] eyes

body.text:
gandhamālyapradānena
tuṣṭir bhavati puṣkalā
keśaśmaśrūn dhārayato hy
agrā bhavati saṃtatiḥ
body.translated_text: By the gift of perfume and garlands, satisfaction becomes abundant; for one who [vows to] wear [unshorn] hair and beard, the foremost progeny comes to be

body.text:
vākśaucaṃ manasaḥ śaucaṃ
yac ca śaucaṃ jalāśrayam
tribhiḥ śaucair upeto yaḥ
sa svargī nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: Purity of speech, purity of mind, and the purity that has water for its resort—he who is endowed with the three purities is heaven-bound; of this there is no doubt

body.text:
tāmrāyasānāṃ bhaṇḍānāṃ
dātā ratnādhipo bhavet
labhate tu paraṃ sthānaṃ
balavān puṣyate sadā
body.translated_text: The giver of copper and iron vessels becomes a lord of jewels; he obtains the supreme station, and strong, ever prospers

body.text:
dhānyaṃ krameṇārjitavittasaṃcayaṃ
vipre suśīle te prayacchate yaḥ
vasuṃdharā tasya bhavet sutuṣṭā
dhārā vasūnāṃ pratimuñcatīha
body.translated_text: He who gives to a well-conducted <s>vipra</s> grain, a store of wealth earned in due order—for him <s>Vasundharā</s> (the earth) becomes well pleased and pours forth here a stream of treasures

body.text:
puṣpopabhogaṃ ca phalopabhogaṃ
yaḥ pādapaṃ sparśayate dvijāya
sa śrīsamṛddhaṃ bahuratnapūrṇaṃ
labhaty adhiṣṭhānavaraṃ samṛddham
body.translated_text: He who causes a tree [yielding] the enjoyment of flowers and the enjoyment of fruits to be touched [given] to a twice-born, he obtains an excellent, prosperous abode rich in fortune and full of many jewels

body.text:
indhanāni ca yo dadyād
dvijebhyaḥ śiśirāgame
kāyāgnidīptiṃ saubhāgyam
aiśvaryaṃ cādhigacchati
body.translated_text: And he who gives firewood to the twice-born at the onset of cold attains the kindling of the body's fire (digestion), good fortune, and lordship

body.text:
chattrapradānena gṛhaṃ variṣṭhaṃ
rathaṃ tathopānahasaṃpradānāt
dhuryapradānena gavām tathaiva
lokān avāpnoti puraṃdarasya
svargīyam apy āha hiraṇyadānam
tathā variṣṭhaṃ kanakapradānam
body.translated_text: By the gift of a parasol [one attains] the best house; by the gift of a chariot and sandals likewise [a chariot]; by the gift of a beast of burden and of cows likewise, one attains the worlds of <s>Indra</s>; the gift of gold too is said [to be] heavenly, and likewise the best is the gift of gold

body.text:
naiveśikaṃ sarvaguṇopapannaṃ
prayacchate yaḥ puruṣo dvijāya
svādhyāyacāritraguṇānvitāya
tasyāpi lokāḥ pravarā bhavanti
body.translated_text: He who gives a homestead endowed with all good qualities to a twice-born endowed with the qualities of recitation and good conduct—for him too the worlds become most excellent

body.text:
yo brahmadeyāṃ pradadāti kanyāṃ
bhūmipradānaṃ ca karoti vipre
hiraṇyadānaṃ ca tathā viśiṣṭaṃ
sa śakro lokaṃ labhate durāpam
body.translated_text: He who gives a maiden as a <s>brahma-deya</s> gift, and makes the gift of land to a <s>vipra</s>, and likewise the excellent gift of gold, attains the hard-to-reach world of <s>Śakra</s>

body.text:
sucitravastrābharaṇopadhānaṃ
dadyān naro yaḥ śayanaṃ dvijāya
rūpānvitāṃ dakṣavatīṃ manojñāṃ
bhāryām ayatnopacitāṃ labhet saḥ
body.translated_text: The man who gives to a twice-born a bed with fine variegated cloth, ornaments, and pillows, obtains a wife endowed with beauty, capable, charming, [and] nurtured without effort

body.text:
lavaṇasya tu dātāras
tilānāṃ sarpiṣas tathā
tejasvino 'bhijāyante
bhoginaṣ cirajīvinaḥ
body.translated_text: The givers of salt, of sesame, and likewise of ghee, are born radiant, enjoyers of pleasures, long-lived

body.text:
svarge 'psarobhiḥ saha bhuktabhogas
tataś cyutaḥ śīlavatīṃ sa bhāryām
rūpānvitāṃ dakṣavatīṃ suraktāṃ
sukhena dharmeṇa tathāpi kāle
tasyaiva sārdhaṃ suralokam eti
tasyaiva cānyat punar eti janma
body.translated_text: In heaven, having enjoyed pleasures together with the <s>Apsarases</s>, and fallen thence, he [obtains] a virtuous wife, endowed with beauty, capable, deeply devoted, [enjoying] with ease and righteousness; and at the proper time he goes together with her very self to the world of the gods, and again obtains another birth together with her

body.text:
kīdṛgvidhāsv avasthāsu
dattaṃ dānaṃ janārdana
ihalokeṣv anubhavet
puruṣas tad bravīhi me
body.translated_text: "In what sorts of conditions does a man experience, in this world, the gift that has been given, O <s>Janārdana</s>? Tell me that

body.text:
garbhasthāsyāthavā bālye
yauvane vārddhake 'pi vā
avasthāṃ kṛṣṇa kathaya
paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
body.translated_text: Whether [while] situated in the womb, or in childhood, in youth, or in old age—tell the condition, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; for great is my curiosity"

body.text:
vṛthājanmāni catvāri
vṛthādānāni ṣoḍaśa
aputrāṇāṃ vṛthā janma
ye ca dharmabahiṣkṛtāḥ
parapākaṃ ca ye 'śnanti
paradāraratāś ca ye
body.translated_text: Four births are in vain, sixteen gifts are in vain: the birth of the sonless is in vain, and those who are cast out of <s>dharma</s>, and those who eat another's cooking, and those who delight in another's wife

body.text:
pary asthānaṃ vṛthā dānaṃ
sadoṣaṃ parikīrtitam
ārūḍhapatite caiva
anyāyopārjitaṃ ca yat
body.translated_text: A gift [given] out of place is declared faulty and in vain, and [a gift] to one who has fallen from his [vow], and that which is earned by unrighteous means

body.text:
vyarthaṃ cābrāhmaṇe dānaṃ
patite taskare tathā
guroś cāprītijanake
kṛtaghne grāmayājake
body.translated_text: And a gift to a non-brahmin is vain, likewise to a fallen man, to a thief, to one who causes displeasure to one's teacher, to an ingrate, to a village-priest,

body.text:
brahmabandhau ca yad dattaṃ
yad dattaṃ vṛṣalīpatau
vedavikrayiṇe caiva
yasya copapatir gṛhe
body.translated_text: and what is given to a brahmin by birth only [brahmabandhu], what is given to the husband of a low-caste woman, and to a seller of the <s>Veda</s>, and in whose house there is a paramour,

body.text:
strīnirjiteṣu yad dattaṃ
vyālagrāhe tathaiva ca
paricārake ca yad dattaṃ
vṛthādānāni ṣoḍaśa
body.translated_text: what is given to those subdued by women, and likewise to a snake-catcher, and what is given to a menial servant—these are the sixteen vain gifts

body.text:
tamovṛtas tu yo dadyād
bhayāt krodhāt tathaiva ca
vṛthā dānaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ
bhuṅkte garbhastha eva tu
body.translated_text: He who, enveloped in <s>tamas</s> (darkness), should give out of fear and likewise out of anger—all that gift is vain; he enjoys [its fruit] only while still in the womb

body.text:
serṣyāmanyumanāś caiva
dambhārthaṃ cārthakāraṇāt
yo dadāti dvijātibhyaḥ
sa bālatve tad aśnute
body.translated_text: He who, with a mind possessed by envy and resentment, gives to the twice-born for the sake of ostentation and from a [selfish] motive of gain, he enjoys that in childhood

body.text:
yaḥ śuddhiḥ prayato bhūtvā
prasannamānasendriyaḥ
pradadāti dvijātibhyo
yauvanasthas tad aśnute
body.translated_text: He who, having become pure and restrained, with serene mind and senses, gives to the twice-born—standing in youth, he enjoys that

body.text:
deśe deśe ca pātre ca
yo dadāti dvijātiṣu
manasā parituṣṭena
yauvanasthas tad aśnute
body.translated_text: In every land and to a worthy recipient he who gives to the twice-born with a thoroughly contented mind—standing in youth, he enjoys that

body.text:
tasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu
sarvadānāni pārthiva
dātavyāni dvijātibhyaḥ
svargamargam abhīpsatā
body.translated_text: Therefore in all conditions, O king, all gifts are to be given to the twice-born by one who desires the path to heaven

body.text:
trailokya kṛṣṇa bhūtānāṃ
sarvalokātmako hy asi
nṝṇāṃ yaduvaraśreṣṭha
tuṣyase kena karmaṇā
body.translated_text: "O three-worlds [-encompassing] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, you are indeed the self of all worlds of beings; by what deed of men, O best and foremost of the <s>Yadus</s>, are you pleased?"

body.text:
brāhmaṇaiḥ pūjitair nityaṃ
pūjito 'haṃ na saṃśayaḥ
nirbhartsitaiś ca nirbhagnas
tasyāhaṃ sarvakarmasu
body.translated_text: "When the brahmins are worshipped, I am worshipped daily, there is no doubt; and when they are reviled, I am thwarted in all my works"

body.text:
viprāparā gatir mahyaṃ
yas tān pūjayate nṛpa
tam ahaṃ tena rūpeṇa
prapaśyāmi yudhiṣṭhira
body.translated_text: "The brahmin is the supreme goal for me; he who worships them, O king, him I behold in that [brahmin] form, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>"

body.text:
kāṇāḥ kubjāś ca khañjāś ca
daridrā vyādhitāś ca ye
nāvamanyed dvijān prājño
mama rūpaṃ hitaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: "The one-eyed, the hunchbacked, the lame, the poor, and those who are diseased—the wise man should not despise the twice-born, [for they are] likewise my beneficent form"

body.text:
bahavo 'pi na jānante
narā jñānabahiṣkṛtāḥ
yathāhaṃ dvijarūpeṇa
carāmi pṛthivītale
body.translated_text: "Many men too, excluded from knowledge, do not know how I roam upon the surface of the earth in the form of the twice-born"

body.text:
ye kecit sāgarāntāyāṃ
pṛthivyāṃ kīrtitā dvijāḥ
tad rūpaṃ hi paraṃ mahyaṃ
yo 'rcayed arcayet tu saḥ
body.translated_text: "Whatever twice-born are renowned upon the earth bounded by the ocean, that is indeed my supreme form; he who would worship [them], he worships [me]"

body.text:
tadrūpān ghnanti ye viprān
vikarmasu ca yuñjanti
apreṣaṇe preṣayanto
dāsatvaṃ kārayanti hi
body.translated_text: "Those who slay the twice-born in that form, and engage them in wrong actions, sending them on improper errands, who indeed make them perform servitude"

body.text:
mṛtāṃs tān karapattrena
yamadūtā mahābalāḥ
nikṛntanti yathā kāṣṭhaṃ
sūtramārgeṇa śilpinaḥ
body.translated_text: "those men, when dead, the messengers of <s>Yama</s> of great might cut apart with a saw, as carpenters [cut] wood along the line of the chalk-string"

body.text:
ye caivāślakṣṇayā vācā
tarjayanti narādhamāḥ
vadanti krodhaniḥsparśaṃ
pādenābhihananti ca
body.translated_text: "And those vilest of men who threaten with harsh speech, who speak [words] devoid of [restraint upon] anger and harm, and who strike with the foot"

body.text:
mṛtāṃs tān yamalokeṣu
nihatya dharaṇītale
uraḥ pādena cākramya
krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
agnivarṇaiś ca saṃdaṃśair
jihvām uddharate yamaḥ
body.translated_text: "those, when dead, in the worlds of <s>Yama</s>, having struck them down upon the ground, treading on the chest with his foot, his eyes red with anger, with fire-colored tongs <s>Yama</s> tears out their tongue"

body.text:
pāpāś ca nārake vahnau
dhāsyante yamakiṃkaraiḥ
body.translated_text: "and the sinners shall be cast into the fire in hell by the servants of <s>Yama</s>"

body.text:
ye tu viprān nirīkṣanti
pāpāḥ pāpena cakṣuṣā
abrahmaṇyāḥ śruter bāhyā
nityaṃ brahmadviṣo narāḥ
body.translated_text: "And those sinners who look upon the twice-born with a sinful eye, irreverent toward <s>brahman</s>, outside the <s>śruti</s>, men ever hating <s>brahman</s>"

body.text:
teṣāṃ ghorā mahākāyā
vajratuṇḍā bhayānakāḥ
uddharanti muhūrtena
cakṣuḥ kākā yamājñayā
body.translated_text: "their eyes the terrible, huge-bodied, dreadful crows with thunderbolt-beaks tear out in a moment by the command of <s>Yama</s>"

body.text:
yas tāḍayati viprāṃs tu
kṣataṃ kuryāt saśoṇitam
asthibhaṅgaṃ ca yaḥ kuryāt
prāṇair vāpi viyojayet
body.translated_text: "He who strikes the twice-born, who would make a wound with blood, who would cause the breaking of a bone, or would separate [them] from their life-breaths"

body.text:
brahmaghnaḥ so 'nupūrveṇa
narake vasudhādhipa
kīlair vinihataḥ pāpo
mīrāyāṃ pacyate bhṛśam
body.translated_text: "that slayer of a brahmin, in due succession, O lord of the earth, the sinner struck down by stakes, is cooked grievously in the [hell] <s>Mīrā</s>"

body.text:
subahūni sahasrāṇi
varṣāṇāṃ kleśabhāg bhavet
ravān muñcati durbuddhir
na tasmai niṣkṛtiḥ smṛtā
body.translated_text: "He becomes a partaker of suffering for very many thousands of years; the evil-minded one cries out, [yet] for him no expiation is reckoned"

body.text:
tasmād viprā naraśreṣṭha
namaskāryāś ca nityaśaḥ
annapānapradānais tu
pūjārhāḥ satataṃ dvijāḥ
body.translated_text: "Therefore the twice-born, O best of men, are to be revered constantly, and by the gift of food and drink the twice-born are ever worthy of worship"

body.text:
āmantrayitvā yo viprān
gandhair mālyaiś ca mānavaḥ
tarpayec chraddhayā yuktaḥ
sa mām arcayate sadā
sa māṃ prasādayec caiva
sa ca māṃ paritoṣayet
body.translated_text: "The man who, having invited the twice-born, gratifies them with perfumes and garlands, endowed with faith, he worships me always; he indeed propitiates me, and he satisfies me"

body.text:
tapodamānviteṣv eva
nityaṃ pūjāṃ prayojayet
body.translated_text: "Worship should ever be directed only toward those endowed with austerity and self-restraint"

body.text:
ye brāhmaṇāḥ so 'ham asaṃśayaṃ nṛpa
teṣv arciteṣv arcito 'haṃ yathāvat
teṣv eva tuṣṭeṣv aham eva tuṣṭo
vairaṃ ca tair yasya mamāpi vairam
body.translated_text: "Whatever brahmins [there are], that am I, without doubt, O king; when they are worshipped, I am duly worshipped; when they are pleased, I myself am pleased; and with whomever they have enmity, with him is my enmity too"

body.text: sugandhidhūpādibhir abhyarcya vipraṃ
body.translated_text: "Having worshipped a brahmin with fragrant incense and the rest,"

body.text: tam acyutaṃ nārcayate sadaiva
body.translated_text: "[he who does so] does not always [fail to] worship that <s>Acyuta</s>"

body.text: yo bhakṣatoyādibhir annapānair
body.translated_text: "He who, with eatables, water, and the rest, with food and drink,"

body.text: anulepācamanapradānaiḥ
body.translated_text: "with the gifts of unguents and water-for-sipping,"

body.text: yaḥ pūjayed bhojayitvā dvijāgryān
body.translated_text: "he who would worship, having fed, the foremost of the twice-born,"

body.text: saṃpūjayitvā paritoṣayec ca
body.translated_text: "having worshipped them well and satisfied them,"

body.text:
arghyādinā ye 'bhipūjya
pūjayanti sadācyutam
body.translated_text: "those who, having worshipped [the brahmins] with <s>arghya</s> and the rest, ever worship <s>Acyuta</s>,"

body.text:
tenaiva mām eva sadā
pūjayanti na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: "by that very [act] they ever worship me alone, there is no doubt"

body.text:
virūpāś ca surūpāś ca
vijanān niṣkalān api
body.translated_text: "the deformed and the well-formed, the friendless and the imperfect [in limb] too"

body.text:
kṛpayā bhāvitātmāno
ye 'rcayanti dvijottamān
body.translated_text: "those of cultivated self who, out of compassion, worship the best of the twice-born,"

body.text:
anasūyā hitātmāno
viprān ārādhate kvacit
body.translated_text: "free from spite, of beneficent self, [he who] worships the twice-born anywhere,"

body.text:
asaṃśayaṃ sadā bhaktyā
mām evārcayate hi saḥ
body.translated_text: "without doubt he ever, with devotion, worships me alone"

body.text:
tataḥ pavitram atulaṃ
na puṇyam adhikaṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: "Than that there is no purifier unequalled, no merit greater than that"

body.text:
yaś candanaiḥ sāgarugandhamālyair
abhyarcayed dārumayīṃ mamārcām
nāsau mamārcām arcayate 'rcayan vai
viprārcanād arcita eva cāham
body.translated_text: "He who would worship my wooden image with sandal, fine aloe-perfume, and garlands—he, worshipping, does not [merely] worship my image; for through the worship of a brahmin I am indeed worshipped"

body.text:
vipraprasādān madha eva cāhaṃ
vipraprasādād asurāñ jayāmi
vipraprasādāt puruṣottamatvaṃ
vipraprasādād ajito 'smi nityam
body.translated_text: "By the grace of brahmins am I sweet [pleased]; by the grace of brahmins I conquer the <s>asuras</s>; by the grace of brahmins [comes] the state of being <s>Puruṣottama</s>; by the grace of brahmins I am ever unconquered"

body.text:
sāyaṃ prātaś ca yaḥ saṃdhyām
upāste 'skannamānasaḥ
japan hi pāvanīṃ devīṃ
gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram
body.translated_text: He who, evening and morning, attends upon the twilight with unwavering mind, reciting the purifying goddess <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the mother of the <s>Veda</s>,

body.text:
sa tayā pāvito devyā
brāhmaṇaḥ pūtakilbiṣaḥ
na sīdet pratigṛhṇānaḥ
pṛthivīṃ tu sasāgarām
body.translated_text: that brahmin, purified by that goddess, his sins cleansed away, would not sink even when receiving as a gift the earth together with its oceans

body.text:
ye cānye dāruṇāḥ kecid
grahāḥ sūryādayo divi
te cāsya saumyā jāyante
śivāḥ śivatamāh sadā
body.translated_text: And whatever other fierce planets there are—the sun and the rest—in the sky, they become benign to him, ever auspicious, most auspicious

body.text:
yatratatragataṃ cainaṃ
dāruṇāḥ piśitāśanāḥ
ghorarūpā mahākāyā
na karṣanti dvijottamam
body.translated_text: And the fierce, flesh-eating [beings], of terrible form and huge body, do not drag away that best of the twice-born, gone wherever [he may be]

body.text:
yāvantaś ca pṛthivyāṃ hi
cīrṇavedavratā dvijāḥ
acīrṇavratavedā vā
vikarmapatham āśritāḥ
body.translated_text: And however many twice-born there are upon the earth who have fulfilled the Vedic vows, or who have not fulfilled the vows and the <s>Veda</s>, [and] have resorted to the path of wrong action,

body.text:
teṣāṃ tu pāvanārthaṃ hi
nityam eva yudhiṣṭhira
dve saṃdhye hy upatiṣṭheta
tad askannaṃ mahāvratam
body.translated_text: for their purification, indeed, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, one should ever attend upon the two twilights—that is the unwavering great vow

body.text:
nāsti kiṃcin naravyāghra
duṣkṛtaṃ brāhmaṇasya tu
yatra sthitaḥ sadādhyātme
dve saṃdhye hy upatiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: There is nothing, O tiger among men, [counted as] misdeed of a brahmin who, ever fixed in the inner self, attends upon the two twilights

body.text:
pūrṇāhutiṃ vā prāpnoti
juhute ca trayo 'ghnayaḥ
dahanti duṣkṛtaṃ tasya
agnayo nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: He attains, as it were, the full oblation, and the three fires offer oblation; the fires burn up his misdeed, there is no doubt here

body.text:
evaṃ sarvasya viprasya
kilbiṣaṃ nirdahāmy aham
ubhe saṃdhye hy upāsinas
tasmāt sarvaśucir dvijaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus I burn up the sin of every brahmin who attends upon both twilights; therefore the twice-born is wholly pure

body.text:
daive pitrye ca yatnena
niyoktavyo 'jugupsitaḥ
jugupsitas tu tac chrāddhaṃ
dahaty agnir ivendhanam
body.translated_text: In the rites for the gods and for the fathers, one not to be despised should be carefully employed; but a despised one—that <s>śrāddha</s> burns [his line], as fire burns fuel

body.text:
purāṇaṃ mānavā dharmāḥ
sāṅgo vedaś cikitsitam
ājñāsiddhāni catvāri
na hantavyāni hetubhiḥ
hatvā hy etāni saṃmūḍhaḥ
kalpaṃ tamasi pacyate
body.translated_text: The <s>Purāṇa</s>, the laws of <s>Manu</s>, the <s>Veda</s> with its <s>aṅgas</s>, and medicine—these four are established by command and are not to be assailed by [mere] arguments; for having assailed these, the deluded one is cooked in darkness for a <s>kalpa</s>

body.text:
na brāhmaṇaṃ parīkṣeta
śrāddhakāle hy upasthite
sumahān parivādo hi
brāhmaṇānāṃ parīkṣaṇe
body.translated_text: One should not scrutinize a brahmin when the time of <s>śrāddha</s> has arrived; for there is very great censure in the scrutinizing of brahmins

body.text:
kāṇāḥ kuṇṭhāś ca ṣaṇḍāś ca
daridrā vyādhitās tathā
sarve śrāddhe niyoktavyā
miśritā vedapāragaiḥ
akṣayaṃ tu bhavec chrāddham
etad dharmavido viduḥ
body.translated_text: The one-eyed, the maimed, the impotent, the poor, and likewise the diseased—all should be employed in the <s>śrāddha</s>, mixed in with those who have mastered the <s>Veda</s>; the <s>śrāddha</s> would become imperishable—this the knowers of <s>dharma</s> understand

body.text:
brāhmaṇo hi mahad bhūtaṃ
janmanā saha jāyate
lokā lokeśvarāś cāpi
sarve brāhmaṇapūjakāḥ
body.translated_text: For the brahmin is a great being, born together with his birth; the worlds and the lords of the worlds too, all are worshippers of the brahmin

body.text:
brāhmaṇāḥ kupitā hanyur
bhasma kuryuś ca tejasā
lokān anyān sṛjeyuś ca
lokapālāṃs tathāparān
body.translated_text: Brahmins, enraged, could slay and reduce to ashes by their splendor; they could create other worlds and likewise other world-guardians

body.text:
brāhmaṇā hi mahātmāno
virajāḥ svargasaṃkramāḥ
brāhmaṇānāṃ parīvādād
asurāḥ salileśayāḥ
body.translated_text: For brahmins are great souls, passionless, traversing to heaven; from the censure of brahmins the <s>asuras</s> [came to] lie in the waters

body.text:
apeyaḥ sāgaro yais tu
kṛtaḥ kopān mahātmabhiḥ
yeṣāṃ kopāgnir adyāpi
daṇḍake nopaśāmyati
body.translated_text: By whom, the great souls, the ocean was made undrinkable out of wrath, whose fire of wrath even today is not appeased in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s>

body.text:
ete svargasya netāro
bhūmidevāḥ sanātanāḥ
ebhiś cādhikṛtaḥ panthā
devayānaḥ sa ucyate
body.translated_text: These are the leaders to heaven, the eternal gods on earth; and the path ordained by these is called the <s>devayāna</s> (way of the gods)

body.text:
te pūjyās te namaskāryās
teṣu sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
te vai lokān imān sarvān
dhārayanti parasparam
body.translated_text: They are to be worshipped, they are to be revered; in them all is established; they indeed uphold all these worlds mutually

body.text:
pramāṇaṃ sarvalokānāṃ
niyatā brahmacāriṇaḥ
tān apāśritya tiṣṭhante
trayo lokāḥ sanātanāḥ
body.translated_text: The measure of all the worlds [are] the disciplined <s>brahmacārins</s>; resting upon them stand the three eternal worlds

body.text:
gūḍhasvādhyāyatapaso
brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
vidyāsnātā vratasnātā
anapāśrityajīvinaḥ
body.translated_text: Brahmins of secret self-study and austerity, of sharpened vows, bathed in knowledge, bathed in vows, living without resorting [to others],

body.text:
āśīviṣā iva kruddhā
upacaryā hi brāhmaṇāḥ
tapasā dīpyamānās te
daheyuḥ sāgarān api
body.translated_text: like enraged venomous serpents are the brahmins to be served; blazing with austerity, they could burn up even the oceans

body.text:
brāhmaṇeṣu ca tuṣṭeṣu
tuṣyante sarvadevatāḥ
brāhmaṇānāṃ namaskāraiḥ
sūryo divi virājate
brāhmaṇānāṃ parīvādāt
pateyur api devatāḥ
body.translated_text: And when brahmins are pleased, all the deities are pleased; by the homage of brahmins the sun shines in the sky; from the censure of brahmins even the deities would fall

body.text:
dhuri ye nāvasīdanti
praṇīte yajñavahnayaḥ
bhojanācchādanair dānais
tārayanti tapodhanāḥ
body.translated_text: Those who do not sink under the yoke, the sacrificial fires having been kindled, who by food, clothing, and gifts deliver [others]—those rich in austerity,

body.text:
te gatiḥ sarvabhūtānām
adhyātmagaticintakāḥ
ādimadhyāvasānānāṃ
jñānānāṃ chinnasāmśayāḥ
body.translated_text: they are the goal of all beings, the ponderers of the inner-self goal, of free doubts concerning the knowledges of beginning, middle, and end,

body.text:
parāparaviśeṣajñā
netāraḥ paramāṃ gatim
avadhyā brāhmaṇās tasmāt
pāpeṣv api ratāḥ sadā
body.translated_text: knowers of the distinction between the higher and the lower, leaders to the supreme goal—therefore brahmins are inviolable, even when ever engaged in sins

body.text:
yaś ca sarvam idaṃ hanyād
brāhmaṇaṃ vāpi tatsamam
body.translated_text: And he who would slay all this [universe], or a brahmin who is equal to it—

body.text:
so 'gniḥ so 'rko mahātejā
viṣaṃ bhavati kopitaḥ
bhūtānāṃ agrabhug vipro
