varṇaśreṣṭhaḥ pitā guruḥ
body.translated_text: that [brahmin], when angered, becomes fire, becomes the sun of great splendor, becomes poison; the <s>vipra</s> is the first eater among beings, the best of the varṇas, father, teacher

body.text:
na skandate na vyathate
na ca naśyati karhicit
variṣṭham agnihotrād dhi
brāhmaṇasya mukhe hutam
body.translated_text: It is never spilled, never disturbed, and never perishes at any time, for that offered into the mouth of a brahmin is superior to the <s>agnihotra</s>

body.text:
avidyo vā savidyo vā
brāhmaṇo mama daivatam
praṇītaś cāpraṇītaś ca
yathāgnir daivataṃ mahat
body.translated_text: Whether unlearned or learned, the brahmin is my deity; whether consecrated or unconsecrated, [he is] like fire, a great deity

body.text:
evaṃ vidvān avidvān vā
brāhmaṇo daivataṃ mahat
body.translated_text: Thus, whether learned or unlearned, the brahmin is a great deity

body.text:
śmaśāneṣv api tejasvī
pāvako naiva duṣyati
havyakavyavyapeto 'pi
brāhmaṇo naiva duṣyati
body.translated_text: Even in cremation-grounds the splendid fire is not defiled; even though devoid of [knowledge of] oblations to gods and ancestors, the brahmin is not defiled

body.text:
sarvathā brāhmaṇāḥ pūjyāḥ
sarvathā daivataṃ mahat
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena
rakṣed āpatsu brāhmaṇān
śakro 'pi hi dvijendrāṇāṃ
bibheti vibudhādhipaḥ
body.translated_text: In every way brahmins are to be worshipped, in every way a great deity; therefore with every effort one should protect brahmins in calamities; even <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, fears the chief of the twice-born

body.text:
dānaṃ devāḥ praśaṃsanti
iti dharmavido viduḥ
nānādānavidhiṃ tasmāc
śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ
body.translated_text: The gods praise gift-giving—this the knowers of <s>dharma</s> understand; therefore hear, well-concentrated, the manifold rule of gift-giving

body.text:
hiraṇyadānaṃ godānaṃ
pṛthivīdānam eva ca
etāni vai pavitrāṇi
tārayanti paratra ca
body.translated_text: The gift of gold, the gift of a cow, and the gift of land—these are indeed purifying and bring deliverance in the next world too

body.text:
yad yad iṣṭatamaṃ loke
yac cāsti dayitaṃ gṛhe
tat tad guṇavate deyaṃ
tad evākṣayam icchatā
body.translated_text: Whatever is most desired in the world, and whatever is dear in the house, that very thing is to be given to a worthy person by one who desires that [merit] to be imperishable

body.text:
suvarṇadānaṃ godānaṃ
pṛthivīdānam eva ca
etat prayacchamāno vai
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: The gift of gold, the gift of a cow, and the gift of land—he who bestows this is indeed released from all sins

body.text:
yad dadāsi viśiṣṭebhyo
yac cāśnāsi dine dine
tat te vittam ahaṃ manye
śeṣaṃ kasyāpi rakṣasi
body.translated_text: What you give to distinguished persons, and what you enjoy day by day, that I deem your wealth; the rest you are guarding for someone else

body.text:
tulyanāmāni śastāni
trīṇi tulyaphalāni ca
nityaṃ deyāni rājendra
gāvaḥ pṛthvī sarasvatī
body.translated_text: Three things of equal name [praise] are commended and of equal fruit, ever to be given, O lord of kings: cows, earth, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> (speech/learning)

body.text:
tadvaj jalam amitraghna
tat tulyaphalanāmataḥ
dattvā tṛptim avāpnoti
yatratatrābhijāyate
body.translated_text: Likewise water, O slayer of foes—that is of equal fruit and name; having given it, one attains satisfaction and is reborn well wherever [he goes]

body.text:
saṃkalpavihito yo 'rtho
brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradīyate
arthibhyo hy arthahetubhyo
manasvī tena jāyate
body.translated_text: The wealth which, ordained by a resolve, is given to the brahmins, to suppliants who [come] for the sake of wealth—by that [the giver] becomes high-minded

body.text:
sīdate dvijamukhyāya
yo 'rthine na prayacchati
amarthe sati durbuddhir
narakāyopapadyate
body.translated_text: He who does not bestow upon a chief of the twice-born when he sinks, who is a suppliant, the evil-minded one, when wealth exists, comes to hell

body.text:
dhenavo 'naḍuhaś caiva
chattraṃ vastram upānahau
deyāni yācamānebhyaḥ
pānam annaṃ tathaiva ca
evaṃ dānaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ
vyuṣṭimat tārakaṃ param
body.translated_text: Milk-cows and oxen, an umbrella, a garment, sandals, are to be given to those who beg, and likewise drink and food; thus is the gift declared—fruitful, supremely delivering

body.text:
eṣa te vihito yajñaḥ
śraddhāpūtaḥ sadakṣiṇaḥ
viśiṣṭaḥ sa ca yajñeṣu
dadatām anasūyayā
body.translated_text: This sacrifice, purified by faith, with sacrificial fees, has been enjoined for you; and it is distinguished among sacrifices, for those who give without spite

body.text:
dānavidbhiḥ kṛtaḥ panthā
yena yānti manīṣiṇaḥ
yair dānais tarpayiṣyanti
śraddhāpūtair dvijottamān
body.translated_text: The path made by the knowers of giving, by which the wise go, by which gifts purified by faith they will gratify the best of the twice-born

body.text:
yathā hi sukṛte kṣetre
phalaṃ vindati kṣetrikaḥ
evaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇebhyo
dātā phalam upāśnute
body.translated_text: For just as in a well-tilled field the farmer finds fruit, so, having given to the brahmins, the giver enjoys the fruit

body.text:
brāhmaṇāś caiva vidyante
satyavanto bahuśrutāḥ
na dadāti ca dānāni
moghaṃ tasya dhanārjanam
body.translated_text: And brahmins are found, truthful and greatly learned, and he [who] does not give gifts—vain is his earning of wealth

body.text:
utthāyotthāya boddhavyaṃ
kim adya sukṛtaṃ mayā
dattaṃ vā dāpitaṃ vāpi
votsāhyam api vā kṛtam
body.translated_text: Rising up again and again, one should reflect: "What good have I done today? What has been given, or caused to be given, or what zeal has been [shown]?"

body.text:
utthāyotthāya dātavyaṃ
brāhmaṇebhyo yudhiṣṭhira
āgamiṣyati yat pātraṃ
tat pātraṃ tārayiṣyati
body.translated_text: Rising up again and again, one should give to the brahmins, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>; whatever worthy recipient shall come, that recipient will bring deliverance

body.text:
yac ca vedamayaṃ pātraṃ
yac ca pātraṃ tapomayam
asaṃkīrṇaṃ ca yat pātraṃ
tat pātraṃ tārayiṣyati
body.translated_text: And the recipient who is made of the <s>Veda</s>, and the recipient who is made of austerity, and the recipient who is unmixed [in conduct]—that recipient will bring deliverance

body.text:
adhyāyaṃ tapaso vakṣye
tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
tapaso hi paraṃ nāsti
tapasā vindate phalam
body.translated_text: I shall declare the chapter on austerity (<s>tapas</s>); hear it from me as I recite it; for there is nothing higher than austerity—by austerity one finds the fruit

body.text:
ṛṣayas tapa āsthāya
modante daivataiḥ saha
tapasā prāpyate svargaṃ
tapasā prāpyate yaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The seers, resorting to austerity, rejoice together with the deities; by austerity heaven is attained, by austerity fame is attained

body.text:
āyuḥprakarṣaṃ bhogāṃś ca
tapasā vindate naraḥ
jñānaṃ vijñānam āstikyaṃ
saubhāgyaṃ rūpam uttamam
body.translated_text: Length of life and enjoyments a man finds by austerity; knowledge, discernment, piety, good fortune, the highest beauty—

body.text:
tapasā labhyate sarvaṃ
manasā yad yad icchati
nātaptatapaso yānti
brahmalokaṃ kadācana
body.translated_text: by austerity all is obtained, whatever one desires in mind; those who have not performed austerity never go to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>

body.text:
yat kāryaṃ kiṃcid āsthāya
puruṣas tapyate tapaḥ
sarvaṃ tat samavāpnoti
paratreha ca mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: Resorting to whatever task, a man performs austerity—all that he attains, the man, both here and in the other world

body.text:
surāpaḥ pāradārī ca
bhrūṇahā gurutalpagaḥ
tapasā tarate sarvaṃ
sarvataś ca vimucyate
body.translated_text: The drinker of liquor, the adulterer, the slayer of an embryo, the violator of the guru's bed—by austerity he crosses over all and is freed from everything

body.text:
api sarveśvaraḥ sthāṇur
viṣṇuś caiva sanātanaḥ
brahmā hutāśanaḥ śakras
tapasyanti sanātanāḥ
body.translated_text: Even the Lord of all, <s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and <s>Viṣṇu</s> the eternal, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hutāśana</s> (<s>Agni</s>), and <s>Śakra</s>, the eternal ones, perform austerity

body.text:
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi
munīnām ūrdhvaretasām
tapasā divi modante
sametā daivataiḥ saha
body.translated_text: Eighty-six thousand sages of upward-flowing seed rejoice in heaven through austerity, assembled together with the deities

body.text:
tapasā prāpyate rājyaṃ
śakraḥ sarvasureśvaraḥ
tapasā pālayan sarvam
ahany ahani vṛtrahā
body.translated_text: By austerity kingship is attained; <s>Śakra</s>, lord of all the gods, by austerity protecting all, day by day, is the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>

body.text:
sūryācandramasau devau
sarvalokahite ratau
tapasaiva prakāśete
nakṣatrāṇi grahās tathā
body.translated_text: The two gods sun and moon, devoted to the welfare of all the worlds, shine by austerity alone, and likewise the lunar mansions and the planets

body.text:
na cāsti tat sukhaṃ loke
yad vinā tapasā kila
tapasaiva sukhaṃ sarvam
iti dharmavido viduḥ
body.translated_text: And there is no happiness in the world which is without austerity indeed; all happiness is by austerity alone—thus the knowers of <s>dharma</s> know

body.text:
viśvāmitraś ca tapasā
brāhmaṇatvam upāgataḥ
body.translated_text: And <s>Viśvāmitra</s> by austerity attained brāhmaṇahood

body.text:
sarvaṃ ca tapasābhyeti
sarvaṃ ca sukham aśnute
tapas tapyati yo 'raṇye
munir mūlaphalāśanaḥ
ṛcam ekāṃ api paṭhan
sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: And one attains all by austerity, and enjoys all happiness; the sage who performs austerity in the forest, eating roots and fruits, reciting even a single <s>ṛk</s> verse, goes to the supreme destiny

body.text:
tasmāt tapaḥ samāsthāya
prārthayed yad abhīpsitam
body.translated_text: Therefore, resorting to austerity, one should pray for whatever is desired

body.text:
satyam eva paraṃ brahma
satyam eva paraṃ tapaḥ
satyam eva paro yajñaḥ
satyam eva paraṃ śrutam
satyaṃ deveṣu jāgarti
muktiḥ satyataroḥ phalam
body.translated_text: Truth alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; truth alone is the supreme austerity; truth alone is the supreme sacrifice; truth alone is the supreme sacred lore; truth keeps watch among the gods; liberation is the fruit of the tree of truth

body.text:
tapo yaśaś ca puṇyaṃ ca
pitṛdevarṣipūjanam
ādyo vidhiś ca vidyā ca
sarvaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitam
body.translated_text: Austerity, fame, and merit, the worship of ancestors, gods, and seers, the primal rule and knowledge—all is established in truth

body.text:
satyaṃ yajñas tathā vedā
mantrā devī sarasvatī
vratacaryā tathā satyam
oṃkāraḥ satyam eva ca
body.translated_text: Truth is the sacrifice and likewise the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>mantras</s>, the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, vow-observance, and likewise truth; truth is the <s>Oṃkāra</s> as well

body.text:
satyena vāyur abhyeti
satyena tapate raviḥ
satyena cāgnir dahati
svargaṃ satyena gacchati
satyena cāpaḥ kṣipati
parjanyaḥ pṛthivītale
body.translated_text: By truth the wind moves, by truth the sun gives heat, and by truth the fire burns; by truth one goes to heaven; and by truth <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-cloud) sends the waters upon the surface of the earth

body.text:
pāraṇaṃ sarvavedānāṃ
sarvatīrthāvagahanah
satyaṃ ca vadato loke
tat samaṃ syān na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: The completion of all the <s>Vedas</s>, the bathing at all sacred fords, and the speaking of truth in the world—that would be equal to it; there is no doubt

body.text:
aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca
satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam
aśvamedhasahasrād dhi
satyam etad viśiṣyate
body.translated_text: A thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were weighed in a balance; for truth surpasses a thousand horse-sacrifices

body.text:
munayaḥ satyaniratā
munayaḥ satyavikramāḥ
munayaḥ satyaprapathāḥ
parāṃ siddhim ito gatāḥ
body.translated_text: Sages devoted to truth, sages whose valour is truth, sages whose path is truth, have gone from here to the supreme perfection

body.text:
satyena devāḥ prīyante
pitaro brāhmaṇās tathā
satyam āhuḥ paraṃ dharmaṃ
tasmāt satyaṃ na lopayet
body.translated_text: By truth the gods are pleased, and the ancestors and the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> likewise; they call truth the supreme <s>dharma</s>; therefore one should not violate truth

body.text:
munayaḥ satyaniratās
tasmāt satyaṃ viśiṣyate
svarge satyaparā nityaṃ
modante devatā iva
body.translated_text: The sages are devoted to truth; therefore truth surpasses [all]; those devoted to truth ever rejoice in heaven like the deities

body.text:
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇair
vimānair upayānti te
vaktavyaṃ hi sadā satyaṃ
na satyād vidyate param
body.translated_text: They go in celestial cars thronged with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>; truth indeed is ever to be spoken; there is nothing higher than truth

body.text:
etat pramāṇaṃ yaḥ kuryāt
sarvayajñaphalaṃ labhet
body.translated_text: He who makes this his standard obtains the fruit of all sacrifices

body.text:
agādhe vimale śuddhe
satyatīrthe hrade śubhe
snātavyaṃ manasā yuktaiḥ
snānaṃ tat paramaṃ smṛtam
body.translated_text: In the fathomless, stainless, pure, auspicious lake of the ford of truth one should bathe—those who are yoked with the mind; that bathing is reckoned supreme

body.text:
ātmārthe ca parārthe vā
putrārthe vāpi pārthiva
ye 'nṛtaṃ nābhibhāṣante
te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
body.translated_text: For one's own sake, or for another's sake, or even for a son's sake, O king, those men who do not speak untruth are bound for heaven

body.text:
api cedaṃ purā gītaṃ
dharmavidbhir yudhiṣṭhira
yaḥ satyavādī puruṣo
nānṛtaṃ paribhāṣate
body.translated_text: And this too was sung of old by the knowers of <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>: the man who is a truth-speaker, who does not speak untruth,

body.text:
saṃprāpya virajāṃl lokān
uṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe
jāyate sumahāmatiḥ
body.translated_text: having attained the stainless worlds, having dwelt there for eternal years, is born of very great wisdom in the house of the pure and prosperous

body.text:
vidyārogyasukhaiśvaryair
yukto yogaparo bhavet
body.translated_text: Endowed with learning, health, happiness, and lordship, he becomes devoted to <s>yoga</s>

body.text:
ādityacandrāv analānilau ca
dyaur bhūmir āpo hṛdayaṃ yamaś ca
ahaś ca rātriś ca ubhe ca saṃdhye
dharmaś ca jānāti narasya vṛttam
body.translated_text: The sun and moon, fire and wind, the sky, the earth, the waters, the heart, and <s>Yama</s>, day and night, the two twilights, and <s>Dharma</s>—they know a man's conduct

body.text:
tasmān na vācyam anṛtaṃ hi sadbhir
evaṃvidhair dharmavido vadanti
satyaṃ vadaṃs tejasā dīpyamāno
na hīyate dharmayaśo 'rthakāmaiḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore untruth is not to be spoken by the good; the knowers of <s>dharma</s>, being of such a kind, declare [thus]; speaking truth, blazing with splendour, a man is not diminished in <s>dharma</s>, fame, wealth, or desires

body.text:
eṣa vāṇīkṛto dharmo
vaidiko dharmaniścaye
evam etad yathānyāyaṃ
satyādhyāye prakīrtitam
tat pramāṇaṃ budhaḥ kuryān
na satyād vidyate param
body.translated_text: This is the <s>dharma</s> put into words, the Vedic one, in the determination of <s>dharma</s>; thus this has been duly proclaimed in the chapter on truth; the wise man should make it his standard; there is nothing higher than truth

body.text:
sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ
pravakṣyāmi yudhiṣṭhira
upoṣitaiś ca kaunteya
yat prayojyaṃ yathāvidhi
body.translated_text: Of all the classes indeed I shall declare, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, and, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, what is to be undertaken by those fasting according to rule

body.text:
phalaṃ yad upavāsasya
tan nibodha ca pāṇḍava
avāpnoti yathā kāmān
upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: And the fruit of fasting—learn it, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>—how one devoted to fasting attains his desires

body.text:
mayaite nṛpate kāmyā
vihitā hitam icchatā
upavāsā manuṣyāṇāṃ
mayy evārpitacetasām
body.translated_text: These optional fasts, O king, have been ordained by me, desiring the welfare of men whose minds are offered to me alone

body.text:
pañcamīṃ caiva ṣaṣṭhīṃ ca
paurṇamāsīṃ ca pāṇḍava
upoṣya rūpavān dhanyaḥ
subhagaś caiva jāyate
body.translated_text: Having fasted on the fifth, the sixth, and the full-moon day, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, one is born beautiful, fortunate, and handsome

body.text:
aṣṭamīṃ caiva kaunteya
śuklapakṣe caturdaśīm
upoṣya vyādhirahito
vīryavāṃś caiva jāyate
body.translated_text: And having fasted on the eighth, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, and the fourteenth of the bright fortnight, one is born free of disease and possessed of vigour

body.text:
mārgaśīrṣaṃ tu yo māsaṃ
nityam ekāśano bhavet
kṛṣibhāgī bhaved rājan
bahuputraś ca jāyate
body.translated_text: But he who in the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> is constantly one who eats but once, becomes a sharer in agriculture, O king, and is born with many sons

body.text:
pauṣamāse tu rājendra
bhaktenaikena yaḥ kṣapet
subhago darśanīyaś ca
jñānabhāgī ca jāyate
body.translated_text: And in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, O lord of kings, he who passes [it] with a single meal is born fortunate, fair to behold, and a sharer in knowledge

body.text:
pitṝn uddiśya māghaṃ tu
yaḥ kṣaped ekabhojanam
māsena puruṣavyāghra
so 'nantyaṃ phalam aśnute
body.translated_text: But he who, dedicating it to the ancestors, passes <s>Māgha</s> with a single meal, in a month, O tiger among men, enjoys endless fruit

body.text:
bhagadaivatamāsaṃ tu
yaḥ kṣaped ekabhojanam
strīṣu vallabhatāṃ yāti
vaśyāś cāsya bhavanti tāḥ
body.translated_text: But he who passes the month whose deity is <s>Bhaga</s> [Phālguna] with a single meal attains dearness among women, and they become subject to him

body.text:
caitraṃ tu puruṣavyāghra
yaḥ kṣaped ekabhojanam
body.translated_text: But <s>Caitra</s>, O tiger among men, he who passes with a single meal—

body.text:
māsena puruṣavyāghra
maunan tu phalam aśnute (?)
bhagadaivatamāsaṃ tu
yaḥ kṣaped ekabhojanaḥ
strīṣu vallabhatāṃ yāti
vaśyāś cāsya bhavanti tāḥ
caitraṃ tu puruṣavyāghra
yaḥ kṣaped ekabhojanaḥ
body.translated_text: in a month, O tiger among men, he enjoys the fruit of silence; but he who passes the month whose deity is <s>Bhaga</s> with a single meal attains dearness among women, and they become subject to him; and <s>Caitra</s>, O tiger among men, he who passes with a single meal—

body.text:
suvarṇamaṇimuktāḍhye
kule mahati jāyate
body.translated_text: is born in a great family rich in gold, gems, and pearls

body.text:
nistared ekabhaktena
vaiśākhaṃ yo narādhipa
body.translated_text: He who crosses through <s>Vaiśākha</s> with a single meal, O lord of men—

body.text:
naro vā yadi vā nārī
jñātīnāṃ śreṣṭhatāṃ vrajet
body.translated_text: whether a man or a woman—attains pre-eminence among kinsmen

body.text:
jyeṣṭhamāsam apānīyam
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
aiśvaryaṃ puruṣavyāghra
strībhāgī copajāyate
body.translated_text: He who passes the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> without water, with a single meal—lordship, O tiger among men, and a share of women come to be

body.text:
āṣāḍhaṃ bharataśreṣṭha
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
śūraś ca bahudhānyaś ca
bahuputraś ca jāyate
body.translated_text: He who passes <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, O best of <s>Bharatas</s>, with a single meal, is born brave, rich in grain, and rich in sons

body.text:
śrāvaṇaṃ tu naravyāghra
bhaktenaikena yaḥ kṣapet
yatra yatropapadyeta
tatra syāj jñātivardhanaḥ
body.translated_text: But <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, O tiger among men, he who passes with a single meal—wherever he is born, there he becomes an increaser of his kin

body.text:
māsaṃ bhādrapadaṃ rājann
ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet
dhanāḍhyo vīryavāṃś caiva
aiśvaryaṃ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: He who passes the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, O king, with a single meal, becomes rich in wealth and possessed of vigour, and attains lordship

body.text:
yaḥ kṣaped ekabhaktena
māsam āśvayujaṃ naraḥ
dhanavān vāhanāḍhyaś ca
bahuputraś ca jāyate
body.translated_text: The man who passes the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s> with a single meal is born rich in wealth, rich in vehicles, and rich in sons

body.text:
kārttikaṃ tu naro māsaṃ
nityam ekāśano bhavet
śūraś ca bahubhāryaś ca
kīrtimāṃś caiva jāyate
body.translated_text: But the man who is constantly one who eats once in the month of <s>Kārttika</s> is born brave, having many wives, and renowned

body.text:
ete māsā naraśreṣṭha
ekabhaktena kīrtitāḥ
tithīnāṃ niyamāṃś caiva
tāñ śṛṇuṣva narādhipa
body.translated_text: These months have been proclaimed [with the practice] of a single meal, O best of men; and the rules of the lunar days—hear those, O lord of men

body.text:
pakṣe pakṣe caturthaṃ tu
bhaktaṃ yaḥ kṣapayen naraḥ
vipulaṃ dhanam āpnoti
bhagavān agnir abravīt
body.translated_text: But the man who passes every fourth meal fortnight by fortnight obtains abundant wealth—the Blessed <s>Agni</s> declared [this]

body.text:
māse māse caturthaṃ tu
bhaktam ekaṃ tu yaḥ kṣapet
kṛṣibhāgī yaśobhāgī
tejasvī cāpi jāyate
body.translated_text: But he who passes a single fourth meal month by month is born a sharer in agriculture, a sharer in fame, and full of splendour

body.text:
pakṣe pakṣe trirātraṃ tu
yaḥ kṣapen narapuṅgava
gaṇe ghoṣe pure grāme
māhātmyaṃ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: But he who passes three nights fortnight by fortnight, O bull among men, attains greatness in a host, a settlement, a city, or a village

body.text:
māse māse trirātraṃ tu
bhaktenaikena yaḥ kṣapet
gaṇādhipatyaṃ labhate
niḥsapatnam akaṇṭakam
body.translated_text: But he who passes three nights month by month with a single meal obtains lordship over a host, without rival and without thorn

body.text:
yas tu sāyaṃ tathā kalyaṃ
bhuṅkte naivāntarā pibet
ahiṃsānirato nityaṃ
juhvāno jātavedasam
body.translated_text: But he who eats at dusk and at dawn and does not drink in between, ever devoted to non-injury, offering oblations to <s>Jātavedas</s> (the fire),

body.text:
ṣaḍbhir eva tu varṣais tu
sidhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
agniṣṭomasya yajñasya
phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: succeeds in just six years; there is no doubt here—the man obtains the fruit of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice

body.text:
aṣṭamena tu bhaktena
rājan saṃvatsaraṃ nayet
gavāmayasya yajñasya
phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: But by an eighth meal, O king, he who passes a year, the man obtains the fruit of the <s>Gavāmayana</s> sacrifice

body.text:
haṃsasārasayuktena
vimānena sa gacchati
pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu
svargaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: He goes in a celestial car yoked with swans and cranes, and for a full thousand years is exalted in the world of heaven

body.text:
ārto vā vyādhito vāpi
gacched anaśanaṃ tu yaḥ
pade pade yajñaphalaṃ
tasya mannāmakīrtanāt
body.translated_text: He who, whether afflicted or diseased, undertakes fasting-unto-death—at each step there is the fruit of a sacrifice for him, through the proclamation of my name

body.text:
divyaṛkṣaprayuktena
vimānena sa gacchati
śatam apsarasāṃ caiva
ramayantīha taṃ naram
body.translated_text: He goes in a celestial car yoked with divine asterisms, and a hundred <s>Apsarases</s> here delight that man

body.text:
sahasraśatasaṃyukte
vimāne sūryavarcase
ārūḍhastrīśatākīrṇe
viharan sukham edhate
body.translated_text: Mounted on a celestial car endowed with a hundred thousand [adornments], with the splendour of the sun, thronged with a hundred women, sporting, he thrives in happiness

body.text:
na kruddho vyādhito nārtaḥ
prasannamanasendriyaḥ
gacched anaśanaṃ yas tu
tasyāpi śṛṇu yat phalam
body.translated_text: But he who, not angry, not diseased, not afflicted, with mind and senses serene, undertakes fasting-unto-death—of him too hear what the fruit is

body.text:
śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ
svargaloke mahīyate
svasthaḥ saphalasaṃkalpaḥ
sukhī vigatakalmaṣaḥ
strīsahasrasamākīrṇe
suprabhe sukham edhate
body.translated_text: For a hundred thousand years he is exalted in the world of heaven, healthy, his resolves fruitful, happy, free of sin; in a radiant car thronged with a thousand women he thrives in happiness

body.text:
yāvanti romakūpāni
tasya gātreṣu bhārata
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi
divyāni divi modate
body.translated_text: As many hair-pores as there are on his limbs, O <s>Bhārata</s>, for that many thousands of divine years he rejoices in heaven

body.text:
nāsti vedāt paraṃ śāstraṃ
nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ
na dharmāt paramo lābhas
tapo nānaśanāt param
body.translated_text: There is no <s>śāstra</s> higher than the <s>Veda</s>; there is no guru equal to a mother; there is no gain higher than <s>dharma</s>; there is no austerity higher than fasting

body.text:
brāhmaṇebhyaḥ paraṃ nāsti
divi ceha ca pāvanam
upavāsais tathā tulyaṃ
tapo hy anyan na vidyate
body.translated_text: There is nothing higher than the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, purifying in heaven and here; and there is no other austerity equal to fasts indeed

body.text:
upoṣya vidhivad devās
tridivaṃ pratipedire
munayaś ca parāṃ siddhim
upavāsair avāpnuvan
body.translated_text: Having fasted according to rule, the gods attained the third heaven, and the sages attained the supreme perfection through fasts

body.text:
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu
viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā
kṣāntam ekena bhaktena
yena vipratvam āgataḥ
body.translated_text: A divine thousand years was endured by the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s> with a single meal, whereby he attained brāhmaṇahood

body.text:
cyavano jamadagniś ca
vasiṣṭho gautamo bhṛguḥ
sarve hy ete divaṃ prāptāḥ
kṣamāvanto bahuśrutāḥ
vidhinānena rājendra
yo mayā parikīrtitaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Cyavana</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>—all these forbearing, much-learned ones attained heaven by this rule, O lord of kings, which has been proclaimed by me

body.text:
paṭheta yo vai śṛṇuyāc ca bhaktyā
na vidyate tasya narasya pāpam
upadravair mucyate sarvāṅgikair
na cāpi pāpair abhibhūyate naraḥ
body.translated_text: He who shall recite or hear this with devotion—for that man there exists no sin; he is freed from afflictions in all his limbs, and a man is not overcome by sins

body.text:
brāhmaṇatvaṃ suduṣprāpaṃ
nisargād brāhmaṇo bhavet
kṣatriyo vāthavā vaiśyo
nisargād eva jāyate
body.translated_text: Brāhmaṇahood is very hard to attain; by nature one becomes a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; or else a <s>kṣatriya</s> or a <s>vaiśya</s> is born by nature alone

body.text:
duṣkṛtena tu duṣṭātmā
sthānād bhraśyati mānavaḥ
śreṣṭhaṃ sthānaṃ samāsādya
tasmād rakṣeta paṇḍitaḥ
body.translated_text: But by evil deeds the wicked-souled man falls from his station; having attained the best station, the wise man should therefore guard it

body.text:
yas tu vipratvam utsṛjya
kṣatriyatvaṃ niṣevate
brāhmaṇyāt sa paribhraṣṭaḥ
kṣatrayonyāṃ prasūyate
body.translated_text: But he who, abandoning brāhmaṇahood, follows the way of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, fallen from brāhmaṇahood, is born in a <s>kṣatriya</s> womb

body.text:
vaiśyakarmāṇi vā kurvan
vaiśyayonau prajāyate
śūdrakarmāṇi kurvāṇaḥ
śūdratvam upapadyate
body.translated_text: Or, performing the deeds of a <s>vaiśya</s>, he is born in a <s>vaiśya</s> womb; performing the deeds of a <s>śūdra</s>, he attains śūdrahood

body.text:
sa tatra durgatiṃ prāpya
sthānād bhraṣṭo yudhiṣṭhira
śūdrayonim anuprāpto
yadi dharmaṃ na sevate
body.translated_text: There, having attained misfortune, fallen from his station, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, having reached a <s>śūdra</s> womb, if he does not follow <s>dharma</s>,

body.text:
mānuṣyāt sa paribhraṣṭas
tiryagyonau prajāyate
adharmasevanān mūḍhas
tamopahatacetanaḥ
body.translated_text: fallen from human existence, he is born in an animal womb, deluded through following <s>adharma</s>, his awareness destroyed by darkness

body.text:
jātyantarasahasrāṇi
tatraiva parivartate
tasmāt prāpya śubhaṃ sthānaṃ
pramādān na tu nāśayet
body.translated_text: He revolves there itself through thousands of other births; therefore, having attained an auspicious station, one should not destroy it through heedlessness

body.text:
śūdrānnenāvaśeṣeṇa
yo mriyej jaṭhare dvijaḥ
āhitāgnis tathā yajvā
sa śūdragatibhāg bhavet
body.translated_text: A twice-born who would die with the remainder of a <s>śūdra</s>'s food in his belly, even though he has established the sacred fires and offered sacrifice, becomes a sharer in the destiny of a <s>śūdra</s>

body.text:
kṣatrānnenāvaśeṣeṇa
kṣatratvam upapadyate
vaiśyānnenāvaśeṣeṇa
vaiśyatvam upapadyate
tāṃ yoniṃ labhate vipro
bhuktvānnaṃ yasya vai mṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: With the remainder of a <s>kṣatriya</s>'s food he attains kṣatriyahood; with the remainder of a <s>vaiśya</s>'s food he attains vaiśyahood; that womb the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> obtains in whose [house], having eaten food, he has died

body.text:
brāhmaṇatvaṃ śubhaṃ prāpya
durlabhaṃ yo 'vamanyate
bhojyābhojyaṃ na jānāti
sa bhavet kṣatriyo dvijaḥ
body.translated_text: He who, having attained the auspicious, hard-to-get brāhmaṇahood, despises it, and does not know what is to be eaten and not eaten—he, the twice-born, becomes a <s>kṣatriya</s>

body.text:
karmaṇā yena medhāvī
śūdro vaiśyo 'bhijāyate
tat te vakṣyāmi nikhilaṃ
yena varṇottamo bhavet
body.translated_text: By what deed the wise one is born a <s>śūdra</s> or a <s>vaiśya</s>—that I shall tell you entirely, by which one becomes the best of classes

body.text:
śūdrakarma yathoddiṣṭaṃ
śūdro bhūtvā samācaret
yathāvat paricaryāṃ tu
triṣu varṇeṣu nityadā
kurute 'vimanā yas tu
sa śūdro vaiśyatāṃ vrajet
body.translated_text: Having become a <s>śūdra</s>, he should practice the <s>śūdra</s>'s deeds as prescribed; but he who, without ill-will, duly performs service to the three [higher] classes constantly—that <s>śūdra</s> proceeds to vaiśyahood

body.text:
kṣatriyatvaṃ yathā vaiśyas
tad vakṣyāmy anupūrvaśaḥ
caukṣaḥ pāpajanadveṣṭā
śeṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ
body.translated_text: How a <s>vaiśya</s> [attains] the state of a <s>kṣatriya</s>—that I shall tell in order. Clean, a hater of sinful people, eating food made of the remnants [offered to gods and guests],

body.text:
agnihotram upādāya
juhvānaś ca yathāvidhi
sa vaiśyaḥ kṣatriyakule
jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: taking up the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation) and offering it according to rule—that <s>vaiśya</s> is born in a <s>kṣatriya</s> lineage; there is no doubt in this.

body.text:
kṣatriyo brahmayonyāṃ tu
jāyate śṛṇu tad yathā
dadāti yajate yajñair
vidhivac cāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
adhīte svargam anvicchaṃs
tretāgniśaraṇaḥ sadā
body.translated_text: And how a <s>kṣatriya</s> is born in a brahmin womb, hear that, how it is: he gives, he sacrifices with sacrifices duly endowed with full <s>dakṣiṇās</s>; he studies, desiring heaven, ever taking refuge in the three <s>Tretā</s> fires;

body.text:
ārtahastaprado nityaṃ
prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
ṛtukāle tu svāṃ bhāryām
abhigacchan vidhānataḥ
body.translated_text: ever giving with hand outstretched to the afflicted, protecting the people by <s>dharma</s>, going to his own wife at the proper season according to the rule,

body.text:
sarvātithyaṃ trivargasya
dīyatāṃ bhujyatām iti
śūdrāṇāṃ yācakānāṃ ca
nityaṃ siddhim iti bruvan
body.translated_text: [saying] 'Let hospitality be given to all the three classes; let it be enjoyed,' ever saying 'success' to <s>śūdras</s> and to beggars,

body.text:
gobrāhmaṇasya cārthāya
raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ
tretāgnimantrapūtātmā
kṣatriyo brāhmaṇo bhavet
vidhijñaḥ kṣatriyakule
yājakaḥ sa tu jāyate
body.translated_text: and for the sake of cow and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> slain in battle facing the foe—that <s>kṣatriya</s>, his self purified by the mantras of the three <s>Tretā</s> fires, becomes a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; he is born in a brahmin lineage knowing the rules, a sacrificer.

body.text:
prāpyate 'vikalaḥ svargo
varṇaiḥ satpatham āsthitaiḥ
brāhmaṇatvaṃ suduṣprāpaṃ
kṛcchreṇāsādyate naraiḥ
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena
rakṣed brāhmaṇyam uttamam
body.translated_text: Unimpaired heaven is attained by the classes who keep to the good path; brahminhood, exceedingly hard to attain, is reached by men only with difficulty; therefore by all effort one should guard the supreme brahminhood.

body.text:
suvarṇaṃ paramaṃ dānaṃ
suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇā parā
etat pavitraṃ paramam
etat svastyayanaṃ mahat
body.translated_text: Gold is the highest gift, gold the supreme <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; this is the supreme purifier, this the great means of well-being.

body.text:
daśa pūrvāparān vaṃśān
ātmānaṃ ca viśāmyate
api pāpaśataṃ kṛtvā
dattvā vipreṣu tārayet
body.translated_text: It purifies ten generations before and after, and oneself; even having committed a hundred sins, by giving [gold] among <s>vipras</s> one would deliver [them].

body.text:
suvarṇaṃ ye prayacchanti
narāḥ śuddhena cetasā
devatās te prayacchanti
samastā iti naḥ śrutam
body.translated_text: Those men who give gold with a pure mind—they give all the deities together, so we have heard.

body.text:
agnir hi devatāḥ sarvāḥ
suvarṇaṃ ca hutāśanaḥ
tasmāt suvarṇaṃ dadatā
dattāḥ sarvāś ca devatāḥ
body.translated_text: For fire is all the deities, and gold is the fire-god; therefore by one giving gold, all the deities are given.

body.text:
agnyabhāve ca kurvanti
vahnisthāneṣu kāñcanam
sarvavedapramāṇajñā
vedaśrutinidarśanāt
body.translated_text: And in the absence of fire they make gold in the places of fire—those who know the authority of all the <s>Vedas</s>, from the testimony of <s>Veda</s> and <s>śruti</s>.

body.text:
ye tv enaṃ jvālayitvāgnim
ādityodayanaṃ prati
dadyur vai vratam uddiśya
sarvān kāmān avāpnuyuḥ
body.translated_text: And those who, having kindled this fire toward the rising of the sun, would give [gold] with reference to a vow, would attain all their desires.

body.text:
suvarṇadaḥ svargaloke
kāmān iṣṭān upāśnute
virajāmbarasaṃvītaḥ
pariyāti yatas tataḥ
body.translated_text: The gold-giver, in the world of heaven, enjoys the desired pleasures; clad in stainless garments, he travels hither and thither,

body.text:
vimānenārkavarṇena
bhāsvareṇa virājatā
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇe
bhāsvatā svena tejasā
body.translated_text: in a celestial chariot of sun-color, radiant and shining, thronged with bands of <s>apsarases</s>, blazing with his own splendor,

body.text:
haṃsabarhiṇayuktena
kāmagena narottamaḥ
divyagandhavahaḥ svarge
parigacched itas tataḥ
body.translated_text: yoked with swans and peacocks, going at will—that best of men, bearing divine fragrance, travels in heaven hither and thither.

body.text:
tasmāt svaśaktyā dātavyaṃ
kāñcanaṃ mānavair bhuvi
na hy ataḥ paramaṃ loke
sadyaḥ pāpavimocanam
body.translated_text: Therefore gold is to be given by men on earth according to their own ability; for there is no greater immediate release from sin than this in the world.

body.text:
suvarṇasya tu śuddhasya
suvarṇaṃ yaḥ prayacchati
bahūny abdasahasrāṇi
svargaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: He who gives gold of pure gold—he is honored in the world of heaven for many thousands of years.

body.text:
lokāṃs tu sṛjatā pūrvaṃ
gāvaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā
prītyarthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ
tasmāt tā mātaraḥ smṛtāḥ
body.translated_text: When creating the worlds of old, cows were created by the Self-existent for the delight of all beings; therefore they are remembered as mothers.

body.text:
tās tu dattvā saurabheyīḥ
svargaloke mahīyate
tasmāt tā varṇayiṣyāmi
dānaṃ cāsāṃ yathāvidhi
body.translated_text: Having given those daughters of <s>Surabhi</s>, one is honored in the world of heaven; therefore I shall describe them, and their gift according to rule:

body.text:
yādṛśī vidhinā yena
dātavyā yādṛśāya ca
dvijāya poṣaṇārthaṃ tu
homadhenukṛte na vai
body.translated_text: of what kind, by what rule, and to what kind of twice-born, [a cow] is to be given for the purpose of nourishment—not indeed for the homa-milch-cow.

body.text:
prathamā gaurakapilā
dvitīyā gaurapiṅgalā
tṛtīyā raktakapilā
caturthī nīlapiṅgalā
pañcamī śuklapiṅgākṣī
ṣaṣṭhī tu śuklapiṅgalā
saptamī citrapiṅgākṣī
aṣṭamī babhrurohiṇī
navamī śvetapiṅgākṣī
daśamī śvetapiṅgalā
tādṛśā ye 'py anaḍvāhaḥ
kapilās te prakīrtitāḥ
brāhmaṇo vāhayet tāṃs tu
nānyo varṇaḥ kadācana
body.translated_text: The first is white-tawny, the second white-brown, the third red-tawny, the fourth blue-brown, the fifth white with brown eyes, the sixth white-brown, the seventh dappled with brown eyes, the eighth brown-red, the ninth white with brown eyes, the tenth white-brown; and those bulls likewise are proclaimed 'tawny.' A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should yoke them, never any other class.

body.text:
dhenuṃ dattvā suvratāṃ sopadhānāṃ
kalyāṇavatsāṃ ca payasvinīṃ ca
yāvanti romāṇi bhavanti dhenvā
duhyeta kāmān nṛpa varṣāṇi tāvat
body.translated_text: Having given a cow of good vows with a cushion, with an auspicious calf and rich in milk—as many as are the hairs of the cow, for that many years, O king, one would milk one's desires.

body.text:
prayacchate yaḥ kapilāṃ savatsāṃ
kāṃsyopadohāṃ kanakāgraśṛṅgīm
tais tair guṇaiḥ kāmdughā hi bhūtvā
naraṃ pradātāram upaiti sā gauḥ
body.translated_text: He who gives a tawny cow with calf, with a bronze milking-pail, her horns tipped with gold—that cow, having become a yielder of desires through those very qualities, comes to the man who is her giver.

body.text:
gosahasraṃ tu yo dadyāt
sarvakāmair alaṃkṛtam
parāṃ vṛddhiṃ śriyaṃ prāpya
svargaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: But he who gives a thousand cows adorned with all that is desired, attaining supreme increase and fortune, is honored in the world of heaven.

body.text:
daśa cobhayataḥ pretya
mātāmahapitāmahaiḥ
gacchet sukṛtināṃ lokān
gāvo dattvā yathāvidhi
body.translated_text: And ten on both sides—with his maternal grandfathers and paternal grandfathers—after death he would go to the worlds of the meritorious, having given cows according to rule.

body.text:
dāyādalabdhair arthair yo
gavāḥ krītvā prayacchati
tasyāpi cākṣayā lokā
bhavantīha paratra ca
body.translated_text: He who, with wealth obtained as inheritance, buys cows and gives them—for him too the worlds become imperishable, here and in the next world.

body.text:
yo dyūtena dhanaṃ jitvā
krītvā gāvaḥ prayacchati
sa gacched virajāṃl lokān
gopradānaphalārjitān
body.translated_text: He who, having won wealth by gambling, buys cows and gives them—he would go to the stainless worlds gained by the fruit of cow-giving.

body.text:
pratigṛhya tu yo dadyād
gāvaḥ śuddhena cetasā
sa gatvā durgamaṃ sthānam
amaraiḥ saha modate
body.translated_text: And he who, having accepted [a gift], gives cows with a pure mind—he, having gone to a place hard to reach, rejoices together with the immortals.

body.text:
yaś cātmavikrayaṃ kṛtvā
gāvo dadyād yathāvidhi
sa gatvā virajāṃl lokān
sukhaṃ vasati devavat
body.translated_text: And he who, having sold himself, gives cows according to rule—he, having gone to the stainless worlds, dwells happily like a god.

body.text:
saṃgrāme yas tanuṃ tyaktvā
gāvaḥ krītvā prayacchati
dehavikrayamūlyas tāḥ
śāśvatāḥ kāmadohanāḥ
body.translated_text: He who, having given up his body in battle, buys cows and gives them—those [cows], the price of the sale of his body, are eternal yielders of desire.

body.text:
rūpānvitāḥ śīlavayopapannāḥ
sarvāḥ praśastā hi sugandhavatyaḥ
yathā hi gaṅgā saritāṃ variṣṭhā
tathārjunīnāṃ kapilā variṣṭhā
body.translated_text: Endowed with beauty, possessed of good character and age, all praised and fragrant; for as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is the best of rivers, so among the silvery ones the tawny cow is the best.

body.text:
antarjātāḥ sukrayajñānalabdhāḥ
prāṇāṃs tyaktvā sodakāḥ sodvahāś ca
kṛcchrotsṛṣṭāḥ poṣaṇāyābhyupetā
dvārair etair goviśeṣā variṣṭhāḥ
body.translated_text: Inwardly born, obtained by purchase, sacrifice, and knowledge, [given by one] having relinquished his life, with water-libation and with [a calf] to be carried along, released [from another] with difficulty, undertaken for nourishment—by these ways the special cows are the best.

body.text:
tisro rātryaś cāpy upoṣyeha dātā
tṛptā gā vai tarpitebhyaḥ prayacchet
vatsaiḥ pītāḥ sopadhānās tryahaṃ ca
dattvā gā vai gorasair vartitavyam
body.translated_text: And the giver, having fasted here three nights, should give well-satisfied cows to the satisfied [recipients]; and having given for three days cows suckled by their calves and with cushions, one should live upon cow-products.

body.text:
loke jyeṣṭhā lokavṛttāntavṛttā
vedair gītāḥ somaniṣyandabhūtāḥ
saumyāḥ puṇyāḥ kāmadāḥ prāṇadāś ca
gāvo dattvā sarvadā santi santaḥ
body.translated_text: Eldest in the world, conversant with the affairs of the world, sung by the <s>Vedas</s>, being the flowing of <s>Soma</s>, gentle, holy, givers of desires and givers of life—the good, having given cows, exist forever.

body.text:
na caivāsāṃ dānamātraṃ praśastaṃ
pātraṃ kālo goviśeṣo vidhiś ca
dṛṣṭvā gāvaḥ pāvakādityabhūtāḥ
svādhyāyāḍhye pātravarye viśiṣṭe
body.translated_text: And not merely the giving of them is praised; the worthy recipient, the time, the special cow, and the rule—having seen cows that are like fire and sun, [given] to an excellent recipient distinguished by the wealth of <s>Veda</s>-study—

body.text:
vaitānasthaṃ satyavākyaṃ kṛtajñaṃ
goṣu kṣāntaṃ gośaraṇyaṃ suvṛttaṃ
śastaṃ pātraṃ gopradānasya bhūmes
tathā suvarṇasya ca sarvakālam
body.translated_text: established in the <s>vaitāna</s> [rites], of true speech, grateful, forbearing toward cows, a refuge for cows, of good conduct—such a worthy recipient is praised for the gift of a cow, of land, and likewise of gold, at all times.

body.text:
bhikṣādānaṃ cādhikaṃ saṃpraśastaṃ
pāthodānaṃ cānnadānaṃ tathā ca
body.translated_text: And the giving of alms is highly praised, and the giving of water, and likewise the giving of food.

body.text:
bhikṣate bahubhṛtyāya
śrotriyāyāhitāgnaye
dātavyā gauḥ prayatnena
ekāpy atiphalā hi sā
body.translated_text: To one who begs, who has many to support, learned in the <s>Veda</s> and maintaining the sacred fires, a cow is to be given with effort; for even one [cow] yields surpassing fruit.

body.text:
tāṃ ced vikrīṇate rājan
vacasā kaluṣīkṛtām
nāsau praśasyate vipro
brāhmaṇo naiva sa smṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: If, O king, he sells her, defiled in [his] word—that <s>vipra</s> is not praised; he is not reckoned a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> at all.

body.text:
tasyādharmapravṛttasya
lubdhasyānṛtavādinaḥ
havyakavyavyapetasya
na deyā gauḥ kathaṃcana
body.translated_text: To that one given to unrighteousness, greedy, a speaker of falsehood, devoid of the <s>havya</s> and <s>kavya</s> offerings, a cow is in no way to be given.

body.text:
jīrṇāṃ caivopabhuktāṃ ca
jaratkūpam ivāphalām
tamaḥ praviśate dātā
dvijaṃ kleśena yojayan
body.translated_text: An old and used-up [cow], fruitless like an old well—the giver enters into darkness, yoking the twice-born to affliction.

body.text:
duṣṭāḥ kṛśāś caiva pālayatīś ca
naitādṛśā dānayogyā bhavanti
kleśair vipraṃ yo 'phalaiḥ saṃyunakti
gacchet sa tiryag viphalāṃś ca lokān
body.translated_text: Wicked and emaciated cows, and ones still tending [calves]—such are not fit for gift; he who yokes a <s>vipra</s> to fruitless afflictions—he would go to the [rebirth as a] beast and to fruitless worlds.

body.text:
anaḍvāhaṃ suvrataṃ yo dadāti
halasya voḍhāram anantavīryam
yugaṃdharaṃ balavantaṃ yuvānaṃ
prāpnoti lokān daśadhenudasya
body.translated_text: He who gives a well-conducted ox, a bearer of the plow of boundless strength, a yoke-bearer, mighty and young, attains the worlds of one who gives ten cows.

body.text:
prayacchate yaḥ puruṣo dvijāya
svādhyāyacāritraguṇānvitāya
balena yuktaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ tu nīlaṃ
ṣaḍāṅgavaṃ prītikaraṃ surūpam
body.translated_text: The man who gives to a twice-born endowed with the qualities of <s>Veda</s>-study and conduct a blue bull endowed with strength, six-limbed, pleasing, of fair form,

body.text:
yuvānaṃ balinaṃ śyāmaṃ
śatena saha yūthapam
gavendraṃ brāhmaṇendrāya
bhūriśṛṅgam alaṃkṛtam
body.translated_text: young, mighty, dark, a herd-leader together with a hundred [cows], a lord of cattle for a lord of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, with abundant horns, adorned—

body.text:
vṛṣabhaṃ ye prayacchanti
śrotriyāyāhitāgnaye
body.translated_text: those who give a bull to one learned in the <s>Veda</s> who maintains the sacred fires—

body.text:
te gatvā tadgavāṃ lokaṃ
devalokān mahattaram
tatra sthitvā tu suciraṃ
sarvakāmaiḥ sutarpitāḥ
body.translated_text: they, having gone to that world of cows, far greater than the world of the gods, and having dwelt there for a very long time, well-satisfied with all desires,

body.text:
aiśvarye te 'bhijāyante
jāyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: are born into lordship, being born again and again.

body.text:
sadakṣiṇāṃ kāñcanarūpyaśṛṅgīṃ
kāṃsyopadohāṃ kanakottarīyām
dhenuṃ tilānāṃ kanakottarīyām
lokā vasūnām acalā bhavanti
body.translated_text: [Having given] a cow with <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, with horns of gold and silver, with a bronze milking-pail, with a golden upper-cloth—a cow [given with] sesame, with a golden upper-cloth—the worlds of the <s>Vasus</s> become immovable [for the giver].

body.text:
tilālābhe tu yo dadyād
ghṛtadhenuṃ yatavrataḥ
sa durgāt tārito dhenvā
brahmaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: In the absence of sesame, he who gives a ghee-cow, of restrained vows—he, delivered from peril by the cow, is honored in the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
ghṛtālābhe tu yo dadyāj
jaladhenuṃ yatavrataḥ
sa sarvaṃ tarate durgaṃ
jalaṃ divyaṃ samaśnute
body.translated_text: In the absence of ghee, he who gives a water-cow, of restrained vows—he crosses over all peril and attains the divine water.

body.text:
brāhmaṇāś caiva gāvaś ca
kulam ekaṃ dvidhākṛtam
ekatra mantrās tiṣṭhanti
havir ekatra tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and cows are one lineage made into two; in the one the mantras abide, in the other the oblation abides.

body.text:
upagamya tu yo dadyād
gāvaḥ śuddhena cetasā
yāvanti tāsāṃ romāṇi
tāvat svarge mahīyate
body.translated_text: And he who, having approached, gives cows with a pure mind—as many as are their hairs, for that many [years] he is honored in heaven.

body.text:
śṛṇu tvaṃ me gavāṃ lokā
yādṛśā yatra vā sthitāḥ
manojñā ramaṇīyāś ca
sarvakāmadughāḥ sadā
body.translated_text: Hear from me what the worlds of cows are like, and where they are situated—charming and delightful, ever yielders of all desires,

body.text:
puṇyāḥ pāpaharāś caiva
gavāṃ lokā na saṃśayaḥ
atyantasukhinas tatra
sarvapāpavivarjitāḥ
body.translated_text: holy and removers of sin—the worlds of cows, no doubt; there men are exceedingly happy, free of all sin.

body.text:
pramodante mahāsthāne
narā vigatakalmaṣāḥ
te vrajante vimāneṣu
grahā divi gatā iva
body.translated_text: Men freed of stain rejoice in that great place; they travel in celestial chariots like planets moving in the sky.

body.text:
evaṃ yair dattasatkārāḥ
surabhyaś cārcitāḥ sadā
kāmarūpā mahātmānaḥ
pūtā vigatakilbiṣāḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, those by whom honor is given to cows and they are ever worshipped—the great-souled ones, of forms-at-will, purified, freed of sin,

body.text:
tulyaprabhāvā devais te
modante 'psarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
gandharvair upagīyante
gośaraṇyā na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: equal in power to the gods, they rejoice with bands of <s>apsarases</s>; they are sung to by <s>Gandharvas</s>—the refuges of cows, no doubt.

body.text:
brahmaṇyāḥ sādhuvṛttāś ca
dayāvanto 'nukampinaḥ
ghṛṇinaḥ śubhakarmāṇo
modante te 'maraiḥ saha
body.translated_text: Devoted to <s>brahman</s>, of good conduct, compassionate, pitying, tender-hearted, of auspicious deeds—they rejoice together with the immortals.

body.text:
yathaiva salile matsyaḥ
salilena sahohyate
gobhiḥ pāpakṛtaṃ karma
dṛḍham eva mayohyate
body.translated_text: Just as a fish in water is borne along by the water, so the sinful deed done [by a man] is firmly borne away by cows—thus by me [it is said].

body.text:
mātaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ
prajāsaṃrakṣaṇe smṛtāḥ
brahmaṇā lokasāreṇa
gāvaḥ pāpabhayāpahāḥ
body.translated_text: The mothers of all beings, remembered as [serving] in the protection of progeny, [created] by <s>Brahmā</s> as the essence of the world—the cows, the removers of the fear of sin.

body.text:
tāsu dattāsu rājendra
kiṃ na dattaṃ bhaved iha
kṛśāya tu viśeṣeṇa
vṛttiglānāya sīdate
body.translated_text: When they are given, O lord of kings, what here would not have been given? But especially [a cow given] to an emaciated [brahmin] failing for want of livelihood, who is sinking.

body.text:
bhūdānena samaṃ dānaṃ
na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati
iti dharmavidaḥ prāhus
tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: There is not, nor will there be, a gift equal to the gift of land—thus the knowers of <s>dharma</s> declare; hear that as I relate it.

body.text:
ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇi
svarge vasati bhūmidaḥ
ācchettā cānumantā ca
tāny eva narake vaset
body.translated_text: For sixty thousand years the giver of land dwells in heaven; but the seizer and the approver of [its seizure] dwell for those same [years] in hell.

body.text:
atidānaṃ tu sarveṣāṃ
bhūmidānam ihocyate
acalā hy akṣayā bhūmiḥ
sarvān kāmān prayacchati
body.translated_text: The supreme of all gifts is here declared to be the gift of land; for land is immovable and imperishable, and grants all desires.

body.text:
bhūmidaḥ svargam āruhya
śāśvatīr edhati samāḥ
punaś ca janma saṃprāpya
bhaved bhūmipatir dhruvam
body.translated_text: The giver of land, having ascended to heaven, prospers for eternal years; and again, having attained birth, he becomes assuredly a lord of the earth.

body.text:
yathā bhūmiḥ sadā devī
dātāraṃ kurute patim
evaṃ sadakṣiṇā dattā
kurute gaur janādhipam
body.translated_text: As the goddess Earth ever makes her giver her husband, so a cow given with <s>dakṣiṇā</s> makes [the giver] a lord of men.

body.text:
api pāpakṛtaṃ prāpya
pratigṛhṇīta bhūmidam
mahīṃ dadan pavitrī syāt
puṇyā hi jagatī yataḥ
body.translated_text: Even one who has committed sin may accept the giver of land [as worthy]; one giving the earth would become purified, for the earth is holy.

body.text:
nāma vai priyadatteti
guhyam etat sanātanam
tad asyāḥ satataṃ prītyai
kīrtanīyaṃ prayacchatā
body.translated_text: The name 'Beloved-given' (Priyadattā) is this eternal secret [of the earth]; that is ever to be proclaimed by the giver for her gratification.

body.text:
yat kiṃcit kurute pāpaṃ
puruṣo vṛttikarṣitaḥ
api gocarmamātreṇa
bhūmidānena śudhyati
body.translated_text: Whatever sin a man, harassed by livelihood, commits, even by the gift of land of a cow's-hide measure he is purified.

body.text:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ
maṇimuktāvasūni ca
sarvān etān mahāprājña
dadāti vasudhāṃ dadan
body.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, gems, pearls, and wealth—all these, O greatly wise one, he gives who gives the earth.

body.text:
tapo yajñāḥ śrutaṃ śīlam
alobhaḥ satyavāditā
gurudaivatapūjā ca
nātikramanti bhūmidam
body.translated_text: Austerity, sacrifices, learning, good character, freedom from greed, truthfulness, and the worship of teacher and deity—these do not surpass the giver of land.

body.text:
bhartur niḥśreyase yuktās
tyaktātmāno raṇe hatāḥ
brahmalokagatāḥ santo
nātikrāmanti bhūmidam
body.translated_text: Those devoted to the highest good of their lord, who have given up their selves, slain in battle, gone to the world of <s>Brahman</s>, being good—they do not surpass the giver of land.

body.text:
phalakṛṣṭāṃ mahīṃ dattvā
sodakāṃ saphalānvitām
sodakaṃ vāpi śaraṇaṃ
prāpnoti mama saṃpadam
body.translated_text: Having given plow-cultivated land with water and endowed with fruit, or even a watered refuge, one attains my fortune.

body.text:
ratnopakīṛṇāṃ vasudhāṃ
yo dadāti dvijātaye
muktaḥ sa kaluṣaiḥ sarvaiḥ
svargaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: He who gives the earth strewn with jewels to a twice-born—he, freed from all defilements, is honored in the world of heaven.

body.text:
ikṣubhiḥ saṃtatāṃ bhūmiṃ
yavagodhūmaśāḍbalām
ye prayacchanti viprebhyo
nopasarpanti te yamam
body.translated_text: Those who give to <s>vipras</s> land covered with sugar-cane, grassy with barley and wheat—they do not approach <s>Yama</s>.

body.text:
sarvakāmadughāṃ dhenuṃ
sarvasasyasamudbhavām
yo dadāti dvijendrāya
brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati
body.translated_text: He who gives to a lord of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> a cow yielding all desires, the source of all crops—he goes to the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
bhūmidānaṃ naraḥ kurvan
mucyate mahato bhayāt
na bhūyo bhūmidānād dhi
dānam anyad viśiṣyate
body.translated_text: A man performing the gift of land is freed from great fear; for no other gift surpasses the gift of land.

body.text:
puṇyāṃ sarvarasāṃ bhūmiṃ
yo dadāti nararṣabha
na tasya lokāḥ kṣīyante
bhūmidasya mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: He who gives holy land of all flavors, O bull among men—the worlds of that great-souled giver of land do not perish.

body.text:
yathā janitrī puṣṇāti
kṣīreṇa svasutaṃ nṛpa
evaṃ sarvaguṇā bhūmir
dātāram anupuṣyati
body.translated_text: As a mother nourishes her own son with milk, O king, so the earth of all good qualities nourishes its giver.

body.text:
agniṣṭomādibhir yajñair
iṣṭvā vipuladakṣiṇaiḥ
na tat phalaṃ avāpnoti
yad dattvā vasudhāṃ nṛpa
body.translated_text: Having sacrificed with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and other sacrifices with abundant fees, one does not attain that fruit which [one attains] by giving land, O king

body.text:
mṛtyor hi kiṃkarā daṇḍā hy
agnitāpāḥ sudāruṇāḥ
ghorāś ca vāruṇāḥ pāśā
nopasarpanti bhūmidam
body.translated_text: For the rods of the servants of Death, the most terrible fire-torments, and the dreadful nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s>, do not approach the giver of land

body.text:
pitaraḥ pitṛlokasthā
devaloke divaukasaḥ
saṃtarpayanti dātāraṃ
bhūmeḥ prabhavatāṃ vara
body.translated_text: The fathers situated in the world of the fathers, [and] the dwellers in heaven in the world of the gods, gratify the giver of land, O best of those that come to be

body.text:
kṛśāya kṛśabhṛtyāya
vṛttikṣīṇāya sīdate
bhūmiṃ vṛttikārīṃ dattvā
sattrī bhavati mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: Having given land that provides a livelihood to one who is emaciated, who has emaciated dependents, whose means are exhausted and who sinks down, a man becomes [a sharer in the fruit of] a sacrificial session

body.text:
siṃhāsanaṃ tathā cchattraṃ
varāśvā varavāraṇāḥ
bhūmidānasya puṣpāṇi
phalaṃ svargaṃ tathaiva ca
body.translated_text: A lion-throne, and a parasol, fine horses, fine elephants, are the flowers of the gift of land, and heaven likewise is its fruit

body.text:
ādityā iva dīpyante
tejasā divi mānavāḥ
ye prayacchanti vasudhāṃ
brāhmaṇāyāhitāgnaye
body.translated_text: Like the <s>Ādityas</s> they shine with splendour in heaven, those men who give land to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has established the sacred fires

body.text:
yathā bījāni rohanti
prakīrṇāni mahītale
tathā kāmādhirohanti
bhūmidānaguṇārjitāḥ
body.translated_text: As seeds scattered upon the earth sprout up, so [their] desires sprout up, won by the merit of the gift of land

body.text:
āsphoṭayanti pitaraḥ
pravalganti pitāmahāḥ
bhūmido naḥ kule jātaḥ
sa naḥ saṃtārayiṣyati
body.translated_text: The fathers clap their hands, the grandfathers leap for joy: "A giver of land is born in our family; he will deliver us"

body.text:
ādityā vasavo rudrā hy
aśvinau vasubhiḥ saha
śūlapāṇiś ca bhagavān
abhinandanti bhūmidam
body.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s> together with the <s>Vasus</s>, and the Blessed Trident-bearer (Śiva) rejoice at the giver of land

body.text:
sa naḥ kulasya puruṣaḥ
sa no bandhuḥ sa no gatiḥ
sa dātā sa ca vikrānto
yo dadāti vasuṃdharām
body.translated_text: He is the [true] man of our family, he is our kinsman, he is our refuge, he is the giver and he the valiant one, who gives the earth

body.text:
dātāram anugṛhṇāti
yathā dattena rocate
pūrvadattāṃ haran bhūmiṃ
narakāyopapadyate
body.translated_text: He favours the giver as he delights in what is given; but he who carries off land formerly given is born for hell

body.text:
vindhyāṭavīṣv atoyāsu
śuṣkakoṭaravāsinaḥ
kṛṣṇasarpā hi jāyante
ye haranti vasuṃdharām
body.translated_text: In the waterless <s>Vindhya</s> forests, dwellers in dry hollows, they are born as black serpents who carry off the earth

body.text:
patanty aśrūṇi rudatāṃ
dīnānām avasīdatām
brāhmaṇānāṃ hṛtaṃ kṣetraṃ
hanyāt tripuruṣaṃ kulam
body.translated_text: The tears of the weeping, wretched, sinking-down <s>brāhmaṇas</s> fall; the field carried off from <s>brāhmaṇas</s> destroys a family of three generations

body.text:
sādhubhyo bhūmim ākṣipya
na bhūtiṃ vindate kvacit
dattvā hi bhūmiṃ sādhubhyo
vindate bhūtim uttamām
body.translated_text: Having snatched land from the good, one never finds prosperity; but having given land to the good, one finds the highest prosperity

body.text:
pūrvadattāṃ dvijātibhyo
yatnād rakṣa yudhiṣṭhira
mahīṃ mahībhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha
dānāc chreyo 'nupālanam
body.translated_text: Land formerly given to the twice-born guard with effort, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, O best of earth-rulers; the preservation [of a gift] is more meritorious than the gift

body.text:
yatraiṣaḥ paṭhyate śrāddhe
bhūmidānasya saṃstavaḥ
na tatra rakṣasāṃ bhāgo
nāsurāṇāṃ kathaṃcana
body.translated_text: Where this praise of the gift of land is recited at a <s>śrāddha</s>, there is no share for the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, nor for the <s>Asuras</s> in any way

body.text:
akṣayaṃ tu bhavec chrāddhaṃ
pitṝṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
tasmād viśrāvayed enaṃ
śrāddheṣu brāhmaṇān sadā
body.translated_text: And the <s>śrāddha</s> for the fathers would become undecaying; there is no doubt here; therefore one should always have it proclaimed to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> at <s>śrāddhas</s>

body.text:
evam etad yathoddiṣṭaṃ
pitṝṇāṃ dattam akṣayam
bhūmidānaṃ mahārāja
sarvapāpāpahaṃ śubham
body.translated_text: Thus this, as declared, given for the fathers, is undecaying: the gift of land, O great king, the auspicious remover of all sins

body.text:
agniṣṭomādibhir yajñair
iṣṭvā vipuladakṣiṇaiḥ
na tat phalam avāpnoti
saṃgrāme yad avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: Having sacrificed with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and other sacrifices with abundant fees, one does not attain that fruit which one would attain in battle

body.text:
iti yajñavidaḥ prāhur
yajñakarmaviśāradāḥ
tasmāt tat te pravakṣyāmi
yat phalaṃ śastrajīvinām
body.translated_text: So say the knowers of sacrifice, the experts in sacrificial rites; therefore I shall declare to you that fruit which belongs to those who live by the sword

body.text:
dharmalābho 'rthalābhaś ca
yaśolābhas tathaiva ca
yaḥ śūro vadhyate yuddhe
vimṛdan paravāhinīm
tasya dharmārthakāmāś ca
yajñāś caivāptadakṣiṇāḥ
body.translated_text: There is gain of <s>dharma</s>, gain of <s>artha</s>, and gain of fame likewise: the hero who is slain in battle while crushing the enemy's host—his are <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and sacrifices with their fees fully obtained

body.text:
paraṃ hy abhimukhaṃ hatvā
tadyānaṃ yo 'dhirohati
viṣṇukrāntaṃ sa yajata
evaṃ yudhyan raṇājire
aśvamedhān avāpnoti
caturas tena karmaṇā
body.translated_text: Having slain a foe facing him, he who mounts that one's vehicle—he sacrifices [a sacrifice] traversed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>; thus fighting in the arena of battle, by that deed he attains four <s>aśvamedhas</s>

body.text:
yas tu śastram anutsṛjya
vīryavān vāhinīmukhe
saṃmukho vartate śūraḥ
sa svargān na vivartate
body.translated_text: But the hero who, valiant, without casting away his weapon, remains facing [the foe] at the head of the army, does not turn back from heaven

body.text:
rājānaṃ rājaputraṃ vā
senāpatim athāpi vā
hanyāt kṣatreṇa yaḥ śūras
tasya loko 'kṣayo dhruvaḥ
body.translated_text: The hero who slays in kṣatriya-fashion a king, or a prince, or a general—his world is undecaying and fixed

body.text:
yāvanti tasya śastrāṇi
bhindanti tvacam āhave
tāvato labhate lokān
sarvakāmadugho 'kṣayān
body.translated_text: As many of his weapons as pierce the skin in battle, so many undecaying worlds, yielding all desires, he obtains

body.text:
vīrāsanaṃ vīraśayyā
vīrasthānasthitiḥ sthirā
gavārthe brāhmaṇārthe vā
svāmyarthe tu kṛtaṃ ca yaiḥ
te gacchanty amalaṃ sthānaṃ
yathā sukṛtinas tathā
body.translated_text: The hero's seat, the hero's bed, the firm standing in the hero's place—those who have done [this] for the sake of cows, or for the sake of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, or for the sake of their lord, they go to the stainless station, just as the doers of good deeds [do]

body.text:
abhagnaṃ yaḥ paraṃ hanyād
bhagnaṃ ca parirakṣati
yasmin sthite palāyanti
so 'pi prāpnoti svargatim
body.translated_text: He who slays an unbroken foe and protects the broken, at whose standing [firm] [the foes] flee—he too attains the journey to heaven

body.text:
ūrdhvaṃ tiryak ca yaś cārvāk
prāṇān saṃtyajate yudhi
hatāśvaś ca pated yuddhe
sa svargān na nivartate
body.translated_text: Upward, sideways, or downward, he who casts away his life-breaths in battle, and who, his horse slain, falls in the battle—he does not return from heaven

body.text:
yasya cihnīkṛtaṃ gātraṃ
śaraśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ
devakanyās tu taṃ vīraṃ
ramayanti ramanti ca
body.translated_text: He whose body is marked by arrows, spears, swords and lances—the divine maidens delight that hero and take their pleasure with him

body.text:
varāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi
śūram āyodhane hatam
tvaritāny abhidhāvanti
mama bhartā mameti ca
body.translated_text: Thousands of fine <s>Apsarases</s> run swiftly toward the hero slain in combat, [each saying] "He is my husband, mine!"

body.text:
hatasyābhimukhasyājau
patitasyānivartinaḥ
hriyate yat parair dravyaṃ
naramedhaphalaṃ tu tat
body.translated_text: Of one slain facing [the foe] in battle, fallen, not turning back, whatever property is carried off by the foes—that is [reckoned as] the fruit of a human sacrifice (<s>naramedha</s>)

body.text:
bhūyo gatiṃ pravakṣyāmi
raṇe ye 'bhimukhā hatāḥ
body.translated_text: Further I shall declare the destiny of those who are slain facing [the foe] in battle

body.text:
śakyaṃ tv iha samṛddhais tu
yaṣṭuṃ kratuśatair naraiḥ
ātmadehaṃ tu viprārthe
tyaktuṃ yuddhe suduṣkaram
body.translated_text: It is possible here for prosperous men to sacrifice with hundreds of sacrifices, but it is most difficult to give up one's own body in battle for the sake of a <s>vipra</s>

body.text:
yāṃ yajñasaṃghais tapasā ca viprāḥ
svargaiṣiṇas tatra cayaiḥ prayānti
kṣaṇena tām eva gatiṃ prayānti
mahāhave svāṃ tanuṃ saṃtyajantaḥ
body.translated_text: That goal to which the <s>vipras</s> desiring heaven proceed there by hosts of sacrifices and by austerity and accumulations [of merit]—in a moment they reach that very goal, giving up their own body in great battle

body.text:
sarvāṃś ca vedān saha ṣaḍbhir aṅgaiḥ
sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca vane ca vāsam
etān guṇān eka evātiśete
saṃgrāmadhāmny ātmatanuṃ tyajed yaḥ
body.translated_text: All the <s>Vedas</s> together with the six limbs, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the <s>Yoga</s>, and dwelling in the forest—one [deed] alone surpasses these merits: that one should give up his own body in the abode of battle

body.text:
imāṃ giraṃ citrapadāṃ śubhākṣarāṃ
subhāṣitāṃ vṛtabhidāṃ divaukasām
camūmukhe yaḥ smarate dṛḍhasmṛtir
na hanyate hanti ca so 'raṇe ripūn
body.translated_text: This speech of varied words, of auspicious syllables, well-spoken, the destroyer of [enemy] hosts, of the dwellers in heaven—he who, of firm memory, remembers it at the head of the army, is not slain, and he slays his foes in battle

body.text:
eṣa puṇyatamaḥ svargyaḥ
suyajñaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ
sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ
kṣatriyasya viśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: This is the most meritorious, heaven-bestowing, excellent sacrifice, facing in all directions, for all the classes indeed, and for the <s>kṣatriya</s> in particular

body.text:
bhūyaś caiva pravakṣyāmi
bhīṣmavākyam anuttamam
yādṛśāya prahartavyaṃ
yādṛśaṃ parivarjayet
body.translated_text: And further I shall declare the unsurpassed word of <s>Bhīṣma</s>: at what sort [of foe] one should strike, and what sort one should avoid

body.text:
ātatāyinam āyāntam
api vedāntagaṃ raṇe
jighāṃsantaṃ jighāṃsīyān
na tena brahmahā bhavet
body.translated_text: One should slay an aggressor (<s>ātatāyin</s>) who comes on in battle, even one who has reached the end of the <s>Veda</s>, [if he is] seeking to slay—one seeking to slay [him]; by that he does not become a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-slayer

body.text:
hatāśvaś ca na hantavyaḥ
pānīyaṃ yaś ca yācate
vyādhito durbalaś caiva
rathahīnas tathaiva ca
body.translated_text: And one whose horse is slain is not to be slain, and one who begs for water, and one diseased and weak, and likewise one who has lost his chariot,

body.text:
bhagnadhanvācchinaguṇaḥ
prāṇepsuḥ kṛpaṇaṃ bruvan
vimuktakeśo dhāved yo
yaś conmattākṛtir bhavet
body.translated_text: one whose bow is broken, whose bowstring is severed, who desiring life speaks piteously, who runs with loosened hair, and one who is of mad appearance,

body.text:
parṇaśākhātṛṇagrāhī
tavāsmīti ca yo vadet
brāhmaṇo 'smīti yaś cāha
bālo vṛddho napuṃsakaḥ
body.translated_text: one who grasps leaves, branches, or grass [in surrender], and who says "I am yours," and who says "I am a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>," a child, an old man, a eunuch—

body.text:
tasmād etān parihared
yathoddiṣṭān raṇājire
hato na hanyate sadbhir
hatā eva hi bhīravaḥ
body.translated_text: therefore one should avoid these as declared in the arena of battle; one [thus] slain is not slain [in guilt] by the good, for cowards are indeed [as good as] already slain

body.text:
amāṃsabhakṣaṇe rājan
yo dharmaḥ kurupuṅgava
tan me śṛṇu yathātathyaṃ
yaś cāsya vidhir uttamaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> in not eating meat, O king, O bull among <s>Kurus</s>, hear that from me as it truly is, and what is its excellent rule

body.text:
māsi māsy aśvamedhena
yo yajeta śataṃ samāḥ
na ca khādati yo māṃsaṃ
samam etad yudhiṣṭhira
body.translated_text: He who would sacrifice with the <s>aśvamedha</s> month after month for a hundred years, and he who does not eat meat—these two are equal, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>

body.text:
sadā yajati sattreṇa
sadā dānaṃ prayacchati
sadā tapasvī bhavati
madhumāṃsavivarjanāt
body.translated_text: He ever sacrifices with a sacrificial session, he ever bestows gifts, he is ever an ascetic, through the abstention from honey and meat

body.text:
sarvavedā na tat kuryuḥ
sarvadānāni caiva hi
yo māṃsarasam āsvādya
sarvamāṃsāni varjayet
body.translated_text: All the <s>Vedas</s> could not do that, nor indeed all the gifts, [which] he [does] who, having tasted the savour of meat, abandons all meats

body.text:
duṣkaraṃ hi rasajñena
māṃsasya parivarjanam
caturvratam idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ
prāṇināṃ mṛtyubhīruṇām
body.translated_text: For the abandonment of meat is hard for one who knows its savour; this is the best fourfold vow for living beings who fear death

body.text:
tadā bhavati loke 'smin
prāṇināṃ jīvitaiṣiṇām
viśvāsyaś copagamyaś ca
na hi hiṃsārudir yadā
body.translated_text: Then, in this world, he becomes trustworthy and approachable for living beings desirous of life, when he has no inclination to injury

body.text:
duṣṭarāṃs tarate ma....āṃ
māṃsasya parivarjanāt
body.translated_text: He crosses hard-to-cross [oceans of misery] through the abandonment of meat

body.text:
prāṇā yathātmano 'bhīṣṭā
bhūtānām api te tathā
ātmaupamyena gantavyaṃ
buddhimadbhir mahātmabhiḥ
body.translated_text: As the life-breaths are dear to oneself, so are they too to [other] beings; the wise and great-souled should proceed by comparison with oneself

body.text:
ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ
satyam eva ca pāṇḍava
ahiṃsā caiva satyaṃ ca
dharmo hi paramaḥ smṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Non-injury is the highest <s>dharma</s>, and truth indeed, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>; non-injury and truth—that is recorded as the highest <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
na hi māṃsaṃ tṛṇāt kāṣṭhād
upalād vāpi jāyate
body.translated_text: For meat does not arise from grass, from wood, or even from stone;

body.text:
jīvād utpadyate māṃsaṃ
tasmād garhanti tad budhāḥ
body.translated_text: meat is produced from a living being; therefore the wise condemn it

body.text:
yadi vai khādako na syān
na tadā ghātako bhavet
body.translated_text: If indeed there were no eater, then there would be no slayer

body.text:
lobhād vā buddhimohād vā
yo māṃsāny atti mānavaḥ
nirghṛṇaḥ sa hi mantavyaḥ
saddharmaparivarjitaḥ
body.translated_text: The man who, from greed or from delusion of mind, eats meat, is to be deemed pitiless, devoid of true <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsena
yo vardhayitum icchati
udvignavāse vasati
yatratatrābhijāyate
body.translated_text: He who wishes to increase his own flesh with the flesh of another dwells in a troubled state wherever he is born

body.text:
dhanena krāyako hanti
upabhogena khādakaḥ
ghātako vadhabandhābhyām
ity eṣa trividho vadhaḥ
body.translated_text: The buyer slays with wealth, the eater [slays] by [his] enjoyment, the slayer [slays] by killing and binding—thus this slaying is threefold

body.text:
bhakṣayitvā tu yo māṃsaṃ
paścād api nivartate
tasyāpi sumahān dharmo
yaḥ pāpād vinivartate
body.translated_text: But he who, having eaten meat, afterward turns away [from it]—his too is a very great <s>dharma</s>, who turns back from sin

body.text:
varam ekasya sattvasya
dadyād akṣayadakṣiṇām
na tu viprasahasrasya
gosahasraṃ sakāñcanam
yo dadyāt kāñcanaṃ meruṃ
kṛtsnāṃ vāpi vasuṃdharām
abhakṣaṇaṃ ca māṃsasya
na tu tulyaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
body.translated_text: Better that one give an undecaying fee for [the sparing of] a single creature than [give] to a thousand <s>vipras</s> a thousand cows together with gold; he who would give a golden <s>Meru</s>, or even the whole earth—the non-eating of meat is not equal to it, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>

body.text:
idam anyat pravakṣyāmi
purāṇam ṛṣinirmitam
body.translated_text: This other [matter] I shall declare, an ancient [tale] made by the seers

body.text:
śrūyate ca purākalpe hy
ṛṣīṇāṃ vrīhayaḥ paśuḥ
yajante yena vai yajñān
ṛṣayaḥ puṇyakarmiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: And it is heard that in the former age the sacrificial victim of the seers was rice; with that the seers of meritorious deeds sacrificed their sacrifices

body.text:
ṛṣibhiḥ saṃśayaṃ pṛṣṭo
vasū rājā tataḥ purā
abhakṣyaṃ bhakṣyam iti vai
māṃsam āha narādhipa
body.translated_text: Being asked his doubt by the seers, King <s>Vasu</s> then, in former time, declared meat to be "to-be-eaten" though it is not-to-be-eaten, O lord of men

body.text:
ākāśān medinīṃ prāptas
tataḥ sa pṛthivīpatiḥ
etad eva punaś coktvā
viveśa dharaṇītalam
body.translated_text: Having reached the earth from the sky, that lord of the earth, then saying this very thing again, entered the surface of the earth

body.text:
kaumudaṃ tu viśeṣeṇa
śuklapakṣe narādhipa
varjayet sarvamāṃsāni
dharmo hy atra vidhīyate
body.translated_text: But [in the month] of <s>Kaumuda</s> (Kārttika) in particular, in the bright fortnight, O lord of men, one should avoid all meats; for <s>dharma</s> is here enjoined

body.text:
caturo vārṣikān māsān
yo māṃsaṃ parivarjayet
catvāri bhadrāṇy āpnoti
kīrtir āyur yaśo balam
body.translated_text: He who abstains from meat for the four months of the rainy season attains four blessings: fame, long life, glory, and strength

body.text:
apy ekam iha yo māsaṃ
sarvamāṃsāni varjayet
atītya sarvaduḥkhāni
sukhaṃ jīven nirāmayaḥ
body.translated_text: Even he who here for a single month abstains from all meats, having passed beyond all sorrows, lives happily, free of disease

body.text:
yo hi varṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ
tapas tapyet sudāruṇam
apy ekaṃ varjayen māsaṃ
māṃsam etat samaṃ matam
body.translated_text: He who would practice the most terrible austerity for a full hundred years, [and he who] would abstain from meat for even a single month—this is reckoned equal

body.text:
yo varjayati māṃsāni
māsaṃ pakṣam athāpi vā
sa vai hiṃsānivṛttas tu
brahmaloke mahīyate
body.translated_text: He who abstains from meats for a month or even a fortnight—he, ceasing from injury, is exalted in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>

body.text:
sarvakālaṃ tu māṃsāni
varjitāni maharṣibhiḥ
manvā kṣupeṇa śvetena
tathaivekṣvākunāpi ca
body.translated_text: Meats were avoided at all times by the great seers, by <s>Manu</s>, by <s>Kṣupa</s>, by <s>Śveta</s>, and likewise by <s>Ikṣvāku</s>,

body.text:
bhṛguṇā nalarāmābhyāṃ
dilīparaghupauravaiḥ
āyuṣā caiva gārgyeṇa
janakaiś cakravartibhiḥ
body.translated_text: by <s>Bhṛgu</s>, by <s>Nala</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, by <s>Dilīpa</s>, <s>Raghu</s>, and the <s>Pauravas</s>, and by <s>Āyus</s>, by <s>Gārgya</s>, by the <s>Janakas</s>, by the universal emperors,

body.text:
dhundhumārāmbarīṣābhyāṃ
nahuṣeṇa ca dhīmatā
gādhinā purukutsena
kuruṇā puruṇā tathā
body.translated_text: by <s>Dhundhumāra</s> and <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and by the wise <s>Nahuṣa</s>, by <s>Gādhin</s>, by <s>Purukutsa</s>, by <s>Kuru</s>, and likewise by <s>Puru</s>,

body.text:
mucukundena māndhātrā
sagareṇa mahātmanā
śibinā cāśvapatinā
vīrasenādibhis tathā
body.translated_text: by <s>Mucukunda</s>, by <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, by the great-souled <s>Sagara</s>, by <s>Śibi</s>, by <s>Aśvapati</s>, and likewise by <s>Vīrasena</s> and the rest,

body.text:
saṃjayenātha bhīṣmeṇa
puṣkareṇātha pāṇḍunā
suvarṇaṣṭhīvinā caiva
duṣvantanṛgarohitaiḥ
body.translated_text: by <s>Saṃjaya</s>, then by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, by <s>Puṣkara</s>, then by <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, and by <s>Suvarṇaṣṭhīvin</s>, by <s>Duṣyanta</s>, <s>Nṛga</s>, and <s>Rohita</s>,

body.text:
etaiś cānyaiś ca bahubhiḥ
sarvair māṃsaṃ na bhakṣitam
śaratkaumudikaṃ māsaṃ
tataḥ svargaṃ gatā nṛpāḥ
sarvakāmasamṛddhās te
vasanti divi saṃsthitāḥ
body.translated_text: by these and many others—by all, meat was not eaten in the autumn month of <s>Kaumuda</s> (Kārttika); then the kings went to heaven; prosperous with all desires, they dwell established in heaven

body.text:
brahmaloke ca pūjyante
jvalamānāḥ śriyāvṛtāḥ
upāsyamānā gāndharvaiḥ
strīsahasrasamanvitāḥ
body.translated_text: And in the world of <s>Brahmā</s> they are honoured, blazing, encompassed by splendour, attended by <s>Gandharvas</s>, accompanied by a thousand women

body.text:
tad evam uttamaṃ dharmam
ahiṃsālakṣaṇaṃ śubhan
ye rakṣanti mahātmāno
nākapṛṣṭhe vasanti te
body.translated_text: Thus those great souls who guard this highest <s>dharma</s>, auspicious, characterized by non-injury, dwell on the vault of heaven

body.text:
madhu māṃsaṃ ca ye nityaṃ
varjayantīha mānavāḥ
janmaprabhṛti madyaṃ ca
sarve te munayaḥ smṛtāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who here ever avoid honey and meat, and wine from birth onward—all those are recorded as sages

body.text:
āpannaś cāpado mucyed
baddho mucyeta bandhanāt
vyādhito mucyate rogād
duḥkhān mucyeta duḥkhitaḥ
body.translated_text: One in misfortune is freed from misfortune; one bound is freed from bondage; one diseased is freed from disease; one in sorrow is freed from sorrow [by this dharma]

body.text:
yaś cainaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ
prayatnād bharatarṣabha
ghoraṃ saṃtarate durgaṃ
svargavāsaṃ ca vindati
tiryagyoniṃ na gacchec ca
rūpavāṃś caiva jāyate
body.translated_text: And he who recites this constantly with effort, O bull among <s>Bharatas</s>, crosses over the terrible, impassable [path], and finds dwelling in heaven, and does not go to an animal womb, and is born beautiful

body.text:
etat te kathitaṃ rājan
māṃsasya parivarjanam
pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca
pramāṇam ṛṣisattamaiḥ
body.translated_text: This abstention from meat has been told to you, O king, [together with] the authority of the best of seers regarding both engagement [in eating] and abstention

body.text:
gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya
cāturvarṇyahitāya ca
aśiṣṭanigrahārthāya
śiṣṭānāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca
yudhiṣṭhirasya rājarṣer
evaṃ nārāyaṇo 'bravīt
body.translated_text: For the benefit of cows and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, for the benefit of the four classes, for the restraint of the unruly and for the protection of the disciplined—thus <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> spoke to the royal seer <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>

body.text:
pañca rūpāṇi rājāno
dhārayanty amitaujasaḥ
agner indrasya somasya
yamasya varuṇasya ca
body.translated_text: Kings of immeasurable might bear five forms: of <s>Agni</s>, of <s>Indra</s>, of <s>Soma</s>, of <s>Yama</s>, and of <s>Varuṇa</s>

body.text:
tān na hiṃsen na cākrośen
nākṣipen nāpriyaṃ vadet
devā mānuṣarūpeṇa
caranti pṛthivīm imām
body.translated_text: One should not injure them, nor revile them, nor abuse them, nor speak what is unpleasant; the gods in human form roam this earth

body.text:
indrāt prabhutvaṃ jvalanāt pratāpaṃ
krauryaṃ yamād vaiśravaṇāt prabhāvam
sattvasthitiṃ rāmajanārdanābhām
ādāya rājñaḥ kriyate śarīram
body.translated_text: Taking lordship from <s>Indra</s>, majesty from fire, cruelty from <s>Yama</s>, power from <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), [and] the steadfastness of goodness from the splendour of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Janārdana</s>, the body of the king is made

body.text:
na cāpi rājā mantavyo
manuṣyo 'yam iti prabho
mahatī devatā hy eṣā
nararūpeṇa tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: Nor should the king be thought 'this is a man,' O Lord; for this is a great deity that stands in the form of a man

body.text:
svayam indro naro bhūtvā
pṛthivīm anuśāsati
na hi pālayituṃ śakto
manuṣyaḥ pṛthivīm imām
body.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> himself, having become a man, governs the earth; for a [mere] man is not able to protect this earth

body.text:
yat prajāpālanaiḥ puṇyaṃ
prāpnuvantīha pārthivāḥ
na tat kratusahasreṇa
prāpnuvanti dvijottamāḥ
body.translated_text: The merit which kings obtain here by the protection of subjects—not by a thousand sacrifices do they obtain that, O best of the twice-born

body.text:
adhītahutataptasya
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasya ca
ṣaṣṭhaṃ labhati bhāgaṃ tu
prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
body.translated_text: Of the meritorious deed of [a subject's] study, oblation, and austerity, the king obtains a sixth part, protecting the subjects according to <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
grāmādhipatyaṃ nagarādhipatyaṃ
deśādhipatyaṃ pṛthivīpatitvam
na prāpnuvantīha manuṣyamātrā
ye devatānāṃ na bhavanti bhāgāḥ
body.translated_text: Lordship of a village, lordship of a city, lordship of a region, and sovereignty of the earth—mere men do not attain these here who are not portions of the deities

body.text:
na tad asti vrataṃ loke
yad rājñaś caritopamam
na tad vedarahasyaṃ vā
yad rājñaḥ phalato 'dhikam
evaṃvṛttās tu rājāno
devabhāgā na mānuṣāḥ
body.translated_text: There is no vow in the world equal to the conduct of a king, nor any Vedic secret superior in fruit to a king's; kings of such conduct are portions of the gods, not human

body.text:
caturvedyaṃ hutaca..na
yo hiṃseta narādhipaḥ
daṇḍasyaite bhayād bhītā
na khādanti parasparam
ja..daṇḍabhayāt ke...
na durvanti hi pātakam
yamadaṇḍabhayād anye
na durvanti parasparam
nābhīto yajate kāṃścan (?)
nābhīto daṇḍam icchati
body.translated_text: The king who would [restrain]... the man who would do harm—through fear of his punishment, the frightened ones do not devour one another; through fear of [the king's] rod some do not commit sin; through fear of <s>Yama</s>'s rod others do not [harm] one another; one unafraid does not sacrifice to any, one unafraid does not desire the rod

body.text:
ya eva devā hantāras
tāṃl loko 'rcayate bhṛśam
hantā śakraś ca rudraś ca
hantā vaiśravaṇo yamaḥ
varuṇo vāyur ādityaḥ
parjanyo 'gnir bṛhaspatiḥ
body.translated_text: Those very gods who are slayers, them the world worships exceedingly; the slayer <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, the slayer <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>—

body.text:
etān devān namasyanti
pratāpapraṇatā janāḥ
na brahmāṇaṃ na dhātāraṃ
na pūṣāṇaṃ kathaṃcana
body.translated_text: these gods people bow to, bent low by their majesty—not <s>Brahmā</s>, not <s>Dhātṛ</s>, not <s>Pūṣan</s> in any way

body.text:
daṇḍagrastaṃ jagat sarvaṃ
vaśyatvam anugacchati
nāyaṃ klībasya loko 'sti
na paraḥ pārthivottama
body.translated_text: The whole world, gripped by the rod, comes to subjection; this world is not for the impotent, nor the next, O best of kings

body.text:
na hi paśyāmi jīvantaṃ
rājan kaṃcid ahiṃsayā
udake jantavo nityaṃ
pṛthivyāṃ ca phaleṣu ca
na hatvā lipyate rājā
