prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
body.translated_text: For I do not see anyone living, O king, by non-injury; there are creatures ever in water, and on the earth, and in fruits; the king is not stained by killing, protecting the subjects according to <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
yadi daṇḍo na vidyeta
durvinītās tatho narāḥ
hanyuḥ paśūn manuṣyāṃś ca
yājñiyāni haviṃṣi ca
body.translated_text: If the rod did not exist, then ill-disciplined men would slay cattle and men and the sacrificial oblations

body.text:
vṛkavat kṣapayeyuś ca
yo yasya balavattaraḥ
body.translated_text: and would destroy [each other] like wolves—whoever is stronger than whom

body.text:
tasmāt prāṇihite daṇḍe
hiṃsādoṣo na bādhate
body.translated_text: Therefore, when the rod is set over creatures, the fault of injury does not afflict

body.text:
naivostrā na balīvardā
nāśvāśvataragardabhāḥ
yuktā vaheyur yānāni
daṇḍaś cen nodyato bhavet
body.translated_text: Neither camels nor bullocks, nor horses, mules, and asses, yoked, would draw vehicles, were the rod not held aloft

body.text:
satyaṃ kilaitad yad uvāca śakro
daṇḍaḥ prajā rakṣati sādhuvṛttaḥ
yasyāgnayaḥ pratimāsasya bhītāḥ
saṃtarjitā daṇḍabhayāj jvalanti
body.translated_text: Truly it is, that which <s>Śakra</s> said: the rod, of good conduct, protects the subjects; he whose monthly fires, frightened, threatened, blaze through fear of the rod

body.text:
yatra śyāmo lohitākṣo
daṇḍaś carati pāpahā
prajās tatra na muhyante
netā cet sādhu paśyati
body.translated_text: Where the dark, red-eyed rod, the slayer of sin, moves, there the subjects are not deluded, if the leader sees rightly

body.text:
daṇḍanītau sunītāyāṃ
sarve sidhyanty upakramāḥ
daṇḍaś cen na pravarteta
vinaśyeyur imāḥ prajāḥ
body.translated_text: When the science of punishment is well administered, all undertakings succeed; were the rod not to operate, these subjects would perish

body.text:
vṛkavad bhakṣayeyuś ca
yo yasya balavattaraḥ
kākādyāś ca purodāśaṃ
śvā caivāvalihed dhaviḥ
body.translated_text: and would devour [each other] like wolves—whoever is stronger than whom; and crows and the like [would devour] the sacrificial cake, and a dog would lick up the oblation

body.text:
svāmyaṃ ca na syāt kasmiṃścit
pravartetādharottaram
cāturvarṇyavimokṣāya
durvinītabhayāya ca
body.translated_text: And there would be ownership over nothing; the lower and the higher would be reversed—for the deliverance of the four classes and through fear of the ill-disciplined,

body.text:
daṇḍena niyato loko
dharmasthānaṃ ca rakṣati
sarvo daṇḍajito loko
durlabho hi śucir janaḥ
body.translated_text: the world, restrained by the rod, guards also the abode of <s>dharma</s>; the whole world is conquered by the rod, for a pure person is hard to find

body.text:
daṇḍasya hi bhayād bhītā
narās tiṣṭhanti śāsane
ti 'pi bhogāya kalpante
daṇḍenoparipīḍitāḥ
body.translated_text: For men, frightened through fear of the rod, abide in [the king's] rule; they too become fit for enjoyment, being pressed down by the rod

body.text:
gurur ātmavatāṃ śāstā
śāstā rājā durātmanāṃ
ihapracchannapāpānāṃ
śāstā vaivasvato yamaḥ
body.translated_text: The guru is the chastiser of the self-controlled; the king is the chastiser of the wicked-souled; of those whose sins are hidden here, <s>Vaivasvata</s> <s>Yama</s> is the chastiser

body.text:
pāpānām atha mūḍhānāṃ
paradravyāpahāriṇām
paradāraratā ye ca
ye ca pātakasaṃjñitāḥ
teṣāṃ tu śāsanārthāya
mayaitat samudāhṛtam
body.translated_text: But for the sinful and the deluded, the seizers of others' property, those who are addicted to others' wives, and those who are named [great] sinners—for the chastisement of them this has been declared by me

body.text:
brāhmaṇyaṃ duṣkaraṃ jñātvā
tasya daṇḍaṃ nipātayet
karmānurūpo daṇḍaḥ syād
gohiraṇyādiko bhavet
avadhyo brāhmaṇo rājan
strī vṛddho bāla eva ca
body.translated_text: Knowing brāhmaṇahood to be hard to perform, he should inflict punishment on him [accordingly]; the punishment should be in keeping with the deed, consisting of cattle, gold, and the like; a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is not to be slain, O king, nor a woman, an aged man, or a child

body.text:
yaś cared aśubhaṃ karma
pāpaṃ rājavigarhitam
pātakeṣu ca varteta
nigrahaṃ tasya kārayet
body.translated_text: He who practices an inauspicious deed, a sin condemned by the king, and engages in [great] sins—of him let [the king] cause restraint

body.text:
śiraso muṇḍanaṃ kṛtvā
gomayenānulepayet
kharayānena nagaraṃ
ḍiṇḍimena tu bhrāmayet
rājanirdiṣṭadaṇḍasya
prāyaścittaṃ na vidyate
body.translated_text: Having shaved his head, he should smear it with cow-dung, and parade him through the city on a donkey-conveyance with a drum; for one whose punishment is decreed by the king there is no [further] expiation

body.text:
eṣa te kathito daṇḍo
brāhmaṇasya yudhiṣṭhira
kṣatriyasya tu yo daṇḍas
taṃ vakṣyāmy anupūrvaśaḥ
body.translated_text: This punishment of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has been told to you, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>; but the punishment which is of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, that I shall declare in order

body.text:
paradravyādiharaṇe
paradārābhimardane
pātakeṣu ca sarveṣu
yo hi varteta kṣatriyaḥ
tasya daṇḍaṃ pravakṣyāmi
tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: The <s>kṣatriya</s> who engages in the seizing of others' property and the rest, in the violation of others' wives, and in all the [great] sins—his punishment I shall declare; hear it from me as I recite it

body.text:
hastapādaparicchedaṃ
karṇanāsāvakartanam
sarvasvaharaṇaṃ kṛtvā
pararāṣṭrāya preśayet
body.translated_text: Having cut off his hands and feet, severed his ears and nose, and seized all his property, [the king] should send him to a foreign realm

body.text:
rājyaṃ kāṅkṣeta yo mūḍho
rājapatnīm athāpi vā
śarais tu rājā vidhyeta
śakticakragadādibhiḥ
body.translated_text: The fool who would covet the kingdom, or else the king's wife—him the king should pierce with arrows, with spear, discus, mace, and the rest

body.text:
kṣatriyasya tu duṣṭasya
daṇḍa eṣa vidhīyate
vaiśyasyāpi ca yo daṇḍas
taṃ pravakṣyāmi bhārata
body.translated_text: This punishment is ordained for a wicked <s>kṣatriya</s>; and the punishment which is of a <s>vaiśya</s> too I shall declare, O <s>Bhārata</s>

body.text:
pātakeṣv eva krūreṣu
yas tu vaiśyaḥ pravartate
paradāre paradravye
tasya nigraham ādiśet
body.translated_text: The <s>vaiśya</s> who engages in cruel [great] sins, against another's wife and another's property—for him [the king] should decree restraint

body.text:
śūlāyāṃ bhedanaṃ tasya
vṛkṣaśākhāvalambanam
etad vaiśyasya nirdiṣṭaṃ
śūdrasyāpy anupūrvaśaḥ
body.translated_text: His impaling on a stake, or hanging from a tree-branch—this is ordained for a <s>vaiśya</s>; and for a <s>śūdra</s> too, in order

body.text:
śūle śūdrasya yo duṣṭas
tasyaikasya vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ
kuñjareṇābhimardeta
mīnīyām atha pācayet
etac chūdrasya nirdiṣṭaṃ
nānyo daṇḍo vidhīyate
body.translated_text: A <s>śūdra</s> who is wicked—for that single one death is enjoined on the stake; he should be crushed by an elephant, or else cooked [in oil] [like a fish]; this is ordained for a <s>śūdra</s>; no other punishment is prescribed

body.text:
naikasyārthe kulaṃ hanyān
na rāṣṭraṃ na ca grāmakam
body.translated_text: [The king] should not slay a family for the sake of one [offender], nor a realm, nor a village

body.text:
dhanalobhān na moktavyo
rāgād vā śāsanaṃ vinā
body.translated_text: [An offender] is not to be released out of greed for wealth, nor out of partiality, without chastisement

body.text:
ekaṃ suśiṣṭitaṃ kṛtvā
śeṣaṃ kośaṃ praveśayet
body.translated_text: Having made an example of one [duly] chastised, he should bring the rest [of the wealth] into the treasury

body.text:
yudhiṣṭhirasya rājarṣer
evaṃ nārāyaṇo 'bravīt
samāsena yathānyāyaṃ
daṇḍanītim anuttamām
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> spoke to the royal seer <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, in brief and according to rule, the unsurpassed science of punishment

body.text:
uttamādhamakāryeṣu
sameṣu viṣameṣu ca
rājadharmāṃs tu paśyeta
viṣṇunā samudāhṛtān
body.translated_text: In the highest and lowest tasks, in equal and unequal ones, one should regard the duties of a king (<s>rājadharma</s>) as declared by <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
etān dharmāñ jagannāthaḥ
pāṇḍuputrāya pṛcchate
jagāda puruṣavyāghra
kim anyac chrotum icchasi
body.translated_text: These duties the Lord of the world declared to the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> who asked; O tiger among men, what else do you wish to hear?

body.text:
bhagavan vahatāṃ bhaktiṃ
devadeve janārdane
yat phalaṃ kathitaṃ tajjñais
tan me vistarato vada
body.translated_text: O Blessed One, the fruit which is told by those who know it for those who bear devotion to <s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods—that tell me in detail

body.text:
yat phalaṃ vahatāṃ bhaktim
acyute bhavati prabho
na tad varṇayituṃ śakyaṃ
hariḥ sarvepsitapradaḥ
body.translated_text: The fruit which comes to those who bear devotion to <s>Acyuta</s>, O Lord, cannot be described; <s>Hari</s> is the granter of all that is desired

body.text:
yādṛk sattvaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ
tādṛg ārādhya keśavam
phalam icchanti tādṛc ca
labhyate tair nareśvara
body.translated_text: As is the disposition of men, so, having worshipped <s>Keśava</s>, they desire fruit accordingly, and such is obtained by them, O lord of men

body.text:
muktikāmā narā muktiṃ
svargaṃ devatvam īpsavaḥ
gandharvayakṣasiddhānāṃ
vṛṇvanty anye salokatām
body.translated_text: Men desiring liberation [obtain] liberation; those wishing for heaven, godhood; others choose co-residence with the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Siddhas</s>

body.text:
varṣeṣv abhīpsavo viṣṇuṃ
pātāleṣu tathāpare
bhogān abhīpsavo viṣṇuṃ
toṣayaṇti narādhipa
body.translated_text: Those desiring <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the [heavenly] regions, and others likewise in the netherworlds, those desiring enjoyments gratify <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O lord of men

body.text:
tathāpare naraiśvaryam
ārogyaṃ guṇavad bhuvi
prārthayanty acyutaṃ devam
ārādhya jagato gatim
body.translated_text: And others pray to the god <s>Acyuta</s>, the refuge of the world, for human lordship and excellent health on earth, having worshipped him

body.text:
dharmopadeśād acalāṃ
vahan bhaktiṃ janārdane
saśarīro gataḥ svargaṃ
dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
body.translated_text: Bearing unshakable devotion to <s>Janārdana</s> through the teaching of <s>dharma</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, went to heaven in his own body

body.text:
tathaiva janakaḥ kṛṣṇe
viniveśya svamānasam
avāpa paramāṃ siddhiṃ
vasuḥ prāyāt tripiṣṭapam
body.translated_text: Likewise <s>Janaka</s>, having fixed his mind on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, attained the supreme perfection; <s>Vasu</s> went to the third heaven

body.text:
anye ca ye ye munayo
ye ye ca vasudhādhipāḥ
avāpur atulān kāmāṃs
te te saṃtoṣya keśavam
body.translated_text: And whatever other sages there were, and whatever lords of the earth, they all attained matchless desires by gratifying <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
anārādhya jagannāthaṃ
sarvapāpaharaṃ harim
sadgatiḥ kena saṃprāptā
bhogāś cāpi manoramāḥ
body.translated_text: Without worshipping the Lord of the world, <s>Hari</s> the remover of all sin, by whom has a good destiny been attained, and delightful enjoyments too?

body.text:
drauṇibrahmāstranirdagdhas
tava rājan pitāmahaḥ
viṣṇoḥ kāryamanuṣyasya
darśanād utthitaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: Your grandfather, O king, burned by <s>Drauṇi</s>'s <s>brahmāstra</s>, rose up again through the sight of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose human deeds [serve his purpose]

body.text:
nāmasaṃkīrtanād yasya
pāpam anyair upadravaiḥ
samaṃ vināśam āyāti
devaḥ ko 'bhyadhikas tataḥ
body.translated_text: He by the proclamation of whose name sin, together with other calamities, goes to destruction—what god is superior to him?

body.text:
rāṣṭrasya śaraṇaṃ rājā
pitarau bālakasya ca
dharmaḥ samastamartyānāṃ
sarvasya śaraṇaṃ hariḥ
body.translated_text: The king is the refuge of the realm; the parents, of a child; <s>dharma</s>, of all mortals; <s>Hari</s> is the refuge of all

body.text:
muktihetum anādyantam
ajam akṣayam acyutam
namasyan sarvalokasya
namasyo jāyate naraḥ
body.translated_text: Bowing to the cause of liberation, beginningless and endless, unborn, undecaying, <s>Acyuta</s>, a man becomes worthy of the homage of all the world

body.text:
na hi tasya guṇāḥ sarve
sarvair munigaṇair api
vaktuṃ śakyā viyuktasya
sattvādyair akhilair guṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: For all his qualities cannot be uttered even by all the hosts of sages—of him who is dissociated from all the qualities [of matter], beginning with <s>sattva</s>

body.text:
śrutaṃ mayā yathā pūrvam
āryako me yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
saśarīro gataḥ svargaṃ
jitam ātmīyakarmabhiḥ
body.translated_text: I have heard, as before, that my forefather <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> went to heaven in his own body, won by his own deeds

body.text:
yat tv etad bhagavān āha
sa yathā pāṇdupūrvajaḥ
dharmopadeśād govindam
ārādhayata tad vada
body.translated_text: But that which the Blessed One said—how the forebear of the <s>Pāṇḍus</s> worshipped <s>Govinda</s> through the teaching of <s>dharma</s>—that tell

body.text:
purā śāsati dharmajñe
dharmaputre yudhiṣṭhire
tasyaiva vaiśvadevānte
caṇḍālo 'bhyāgamat kila
body.translated_text: Formerly, when the son of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the knower of <s>dharma</s>, was ruling, at the end of his <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [offering] a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> arrived, it is said

body.text:
samupetya gṛhaṃ tasya
dharmaputrasya vismitaḥ
uvāca śvapaco dvāḥsthaṃ
praśrayāvanatasthitaḥ
body.translated_text: Having approached the house of that son of <s>Dharma</s>, the dog-cooker (<s>śvapaca</s>), amazed, said to the doorkeeper, standing bowed in humility:

body.text:
kasyaitad bhavanaṃ divyaṃ
maṇiratnavibhūṣitam
śuddhasphaṭikasopānaṃ
maṇikāñcanatoraṇam
body.translated_text: "Whose is this divine mansion, adorned with gems and jewels, with steps of pure crystal and arched gateways of gems and gold?

body.text:
aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi
brāhmaṇānāṃ dine dine
yudhiṣṭhiram ṛte bhūpaṃ
bhuñjate kasya veśmani
body.translated_text: Eighty-eight thousand <s>brāhmaṇas</s> day by day, apart from King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, eat in whose house?"

body.text:
katham etan na jānīṣe
candrabimbam ivāparam
yudhiṣṭhirasya bhavanaṃ
devarājagṛhopamam
body.translated_text: "How do you not know this mansion of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, like a second orb of the moon, resembling the house of the king of the gods?

body.text:
abalasya balaṃ rājā
bālasya ruditaṃ balam
balaṃ mūrkhasya vai maunaṃ
taskarasyānṛtaṃ balam
body.translated_text: The king is the strength of the powerless; weeping is the strength of a child; silence indeed is the strength of a fool; untruth is the strength of a thief"

body.text:
gaccha jalpa svarājānaṃ
pratīhāra vaco mama
duḥkhārtaḥ kāryavān rājaṃś
caṇḍālo dvāri tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: "Go, doorkeeper, tell your king my word: a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, afflicted with sorrow and having business, O king, stands at the door,

body.text:
kenāpi hetumātreṇa
bhavantaṃ duṣṭam āgataḥ
body.translated_text: having come to you, the wicked one, for some certain cause"

body.text:
ity ukto dharmarājasya
pratīhāro yathoditam
nivedayām āsa tathā
dharmarājo 'bravīd idam
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the doorkeeper of the <s>Dharma</s>-king reported it as had been said; and the <s>Dharma</s>-king said this:

body.text:
kiṃ rūpaṃ kīdṛśaṃ śīlaṃ
ko 'syārthaḥ kiṃ prayojanam
brūhi dvāḥstha yathāvan me
naras tiṣṭhati kīdṛśaḥ
body.translated_text: "What is his form, of what kind his character, what is his object, what his purpose? Tell me duly, doorkeeper—the man who stands [there], of what sort is he?"

body.text:
kākakokilakṛṣṇāṅgo
bhagnanāsāruṇekṣaṇaḥ
yavamadhyaḥ kṛśagrīvo
vakrapādo mahāhanuḥ
body.translated_text: "His body black as a crow, a cuckoo, with broken nose and reddish eyes, slender in the middle like a barley-grain, thin-necked, crook-footed, large-jawed

body.text:
brūhi gaccha durācāraṃ
caṇḍālaṃ pāpakarmiṇam
devakāryasya velāyāṃ
dutas tvaṃ pratyupasthitaḥ
body.translated_text: Tell [him]: 'Go, ill-conducted <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, evil-doer; at the time of the rite for the gods you, a messenger, have presented yourself'"

body.text:
caṇḍālapatitau dṛṣṭvā
naraḥ paśyeta bhāskaram
snātas tv etāv athālokya
sacailasnānam arhati
body.translated_text: "Seeing a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> and an outcaste, a man should look at the sun; but if bathed, having beheld these two, he deserves to bathe again together with his clothes"

body.text:
ity ājñapte tathoktas tu
caṇḍālas tena vai tataḥ
pratyuvāca pratīhāram
īṣan manyupariplutaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus commanded and so addressed by him, the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> then replied to the doorkeeper, somewhat overcome with anger:

body.text:
kiṃ devakāryeṇa narādhipasya
kṛtvā hi manyuṃ viṣayasthitānām
tad devakāryaṃ sa ca yajñahomo
yad aśrupātā na patanti rāṣṭre
body.translated_text: "What [need] has the lord of men of a rite for the gods, having made anger toward those who dwell in [his] realm? That is the rite for the gods and the sacrificial oblation, namely that tears of distress do not fall in the realm

body.text:
idaṃ vacanam avyagraṃ
pratīhāra tvarā mama
nivedaya svarājendraṃ
yatheṣṭaṃ sa karotu vai
ity uktaḥ satvaraṃ gatvā
dharmarājaṃ tathā tathaṃ (?)
kathayām āsa tat sarvaṃ
cāṇḍālena yad īritam
suśobhanam idaṃ vākyaṃ
na bhaved antyajātiṣu
cintayitvā tato rājā
nirjagāma yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
body.translated_text: This calm utterance, doorkeeper, [report] in my haste; report it to your king of kings; let him do as he wishes"; thus addressed, [the doorkeeper] going swiftly, reported to the <s>Dharma</s>-king all that, just so, which had been spoken by the <s>Caṇḍāla</s>: "This excellent speech would not be [expected] among the lowest-born"; then the king, having reflected, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> came out

body.text:
ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā
nirjagāma yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
pratyuvāca ca caṇḍālam
īṣan kopasamanvitaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus having heard this speech, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> came out and replied to the <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, somewhat filled with anger:

body.text:
kutas te bhayam utpannaṃ
yena tvaṃ gṛham āgataḥ
āvādhākāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ
yathāvat kathayasva me
body.translated_text: "Whence has fear arisen for you, by which you have come to [my] house? Tell me duly the whole cause of [your] distress,

body.text:
tad ahaṃ te pratijñāya
caṇḍakarmakarakṣaṇam
apāsya devakāryārthaṃ
praviśyāmy antaraṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: so that I, having promised you protection from one who does cruel deeds, may, setting aside the rite for the gods, enter within again"

body.text:
na bhuñjate brāhmaṇā me
sarvāś codvijate janaḥ
prāṇihiṃsā ca no vṛttir
deva puṣṇāti me 'nṛtam
body.translated_text: "The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> do not eat at my [house], and all people are repelled [by me]; injury to living beings is my livelihood—O god, my untruth nourishes me

body.text:
anekajanmasāhasrīṃ
prāpya saṃsārapaddhatim
mānuṣye kutsitāṃ jātim
āpanno muṣito 'smi bhoḥ
body.translated_text: Having attained the path of <s>saṃsāra</s> of many thousands of births, having reached a despised birth among humans, I have been robbed, ho!

body.text:
karmabhūmim imāṃ rājan
prārthayanti divaukasaḥ
tāṃ saṃprāpya vṛthājanmā
muṣṭo 'smi kurusattama
body.translated_text: This land of [meritorious] action, O king, the dwellers in heaven pray for; having attained it, of futile birth, I have been robbed, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>

body.text:
duḥkhe duḥkhādhikān paśyet
sukhe paśyet sukhādhikān
ātmānaṃ śokaharṣābhyāṃ
śatrubhyām iva nārpayet
body.translated_text: In sorrow one should look upon those more sorrowful, in happiness one should look upon those more happy; one should not surrender oneself to grief and joy as to two enemies

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi vijñātum
atiduṣkṛtakarmakṛt
vaktum arhasi dharmajña
kaḥ pāpiṣṭhataro mayā
body.translated_text: So I wish to know, I who do exceedingly evil deeds—you ought to tell, O knower of <s>dharma</s>—who is more sinful than I?"

body.text:
adhvānam upari śrāntaṃ
brāhmaṇaṃ gṛham āgatam
anarcayitvā yo bhuṅkte
sa pāpiṣṭhataras tvayā
body.translated_text: He who eats without having honored a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> wearied upon the road who has come to his house, he is more sinful than you

body.text:
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva
vikalaṃ netradurbalam
yo nābhyuddharate putraḥ
sa pāpiṣṭhataras tvayā
body.translated_text: The son who does not support his mother and father when they are infirm and weak of eye, he is more sinful than you

body.text:
godhanasya tṛṣārtasya
jalārthaṃ paridhāvataḥ
vighnam ācarate yas tu
sa pāpiṣṭhataras tvayā
body.translated_text: But he who makes an obstacle for the cattle-wealth that is thirst-stricken and running about for the sake of water, he is more sinful than you

body.text:
vivāhayitvā yaḥ kanyāṃ
kulajāṃ śīlamaṇḍanām
vinā tyajati doṣeṇa
sa pāpiṣṭhataras tvayā
body.translated_text: He who, having married a maiden of good family adorned with good conduct, abandons her without fault, he is more sinful than you

body.text:
āśākāras tv adātā yo
dātuś ca pratiṣedhakaḥ
dattaṃ ca yaḥ kīrtayati
sa pāpiṣṭhataras tvayā
body.translated_text: He who raises hope but does not give, and who hinders a giver, and who proclaims what has been given, he is more sinful than you

body.text:
bahubhṛtyair daridraiś ca
dhanaṃ santaṃ dvijottamaiḥ
yācito na prayacched yaḥ
sa pāpiṣṭhataras tvayā
body.translated_text: He who, having wealth, being begged by the best of the twice-born who have many dependents and are poor, would not bestow it, he is more sinful than you

body.text:
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vāpi
vaiśyaḥ śūdro 'pi vā naraḥ
svadharmaṃ saṃtyajed yas tu
sa pāpiṣṭhataras tvayā
body.translated_text: Whether a man be a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>, or even a <s>śūdra</s>, he who abandons his own <s>dharma</s>, he is more sinful than you

body.text:
kṛtārtho 'haṃ gamiṣyāmi
yaśodharmam avāpnuhi
tuṣṭo 'smy ahaṃ svayā yonyā
mattaḥ proktās tvayādhamāḥ
body.translated_text: 'I shall go, my purpose accomplished; attain fame and <s>dharma</s>; I am pleased by my own birth (lineage); the base ones have been declared by you, [learned] from me'

body.text:
devatānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca
pitṝṇāṃ ca kṛtaṃ mayā
sāṃprataṃ deśakālo 'yaṃ
tvam evātra bhavātithiḥ
body.translated_text: '[The duty] toward the gods, the seers, and the ancestors has been done by me; now this is the [right] place and time—you yourself be here the guest'

body.text:
caṇḍālo 'haṃ mahārāja
patito lokavarjitaḥ
kathaṃ nihīno varṇebhyo
bhokṣyāmi bhavato gṛhe
body.translated_text: 'I am a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, O great king, fallen, shunned by the world; how, being lowest among the classes, shall I eat in your house?'

body.text:
caṇḍālo bhava pāpo vā
śatrur vā pitṛghātakaḥ
deśakālābhyupetaṃ tvāṃ
bharaṇīyaṃ hi vedmy aham
body.translated_text: 'Be a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, or sinful, or an enemy, or a slayer of [your] father—you, come at [this] place and time, I know indeed to be one to be cared for'

body.text:
daśasūnāsamaṃ cakraṃ
daśacakrasamo dhvajaḥ
daśadhvajasamā veśyā
daśaveśyāsamo nṛpaḥ
body.translated_text: A slaughtering-block (<s>cakra</s>) equals ten slaughter-houses (<s>sūnā</s>); a banner (a tavern-sign) equals ten slaughtering-blocks; a courtesan equals ten banners; a king equals ten courtesans

body.text:
daśa sūnāsahasrāṇi
kurute yo hi saunikaḥ
tena tulyaḥ smṛto rājā
ghoras tasya pratigrahaḥ
body.translated_text: For whatever butcher makes ten thousand slaughter-houses, the king is reckoned equal to him—terrible is the acceptance of [gifts from] him

body.text:
nānāgotrādicaraṇā
bhuñjate brāhmaṇā mama
na te vadanti vāgduṣṭaṃ
yathaitat kīrtitaṃ tvayā
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of various <s>gotras</s>, schools, and observances eat [at] my [table]; they do not speak this fault of speech as it has been proclaimed by you

body.text:
lobhātmāno na jānīyur
brāhmaṇā rājakilbiṣam
varaṃ svamāṃsam attavyaṃ
na tu rājapratigraham
body.translated_text: Greedy-souled <s>brāhmaṇas</s> do not know the sin of [accepting from] a king; better that one's own flesh be eaten than the acceptance of [gifts from] a king

body.text:
rājakilbiṣadagdhānāṃ
brāhmaṇānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
chinnānām iva bījānāṃ
punarjanma na vidyate
body.translated_text: Of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> burned by the sin of [accepting from] a king, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, like seeds that have been cut, there is no rebirth

body.text:
rājapratigraho ghoro
madhvāsvādo viṣopamaḥ
budhena pratihartavyaḥ
svamāṃsasyeva bhakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: The acceptance of [gifts from] a king is terrible, like the taste of honey resembling poison; it is to be warded off by the wise like the eating of one's own flesh

body.text:
adhītya caturo vedān
sarvaśāstrārthatattvavit
narendrabhavane bhuṅktvā
viṣṭhāyāṃ jāyate kṛmiḥ
body.translated_text: Having studied the four <s>Vedas</s>, knowing the truth of the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s>, having eaten in the house of a lord of men, one is born as a worm in excrement

body.text:
nindase sarvarājāno
na cātmānaṃ praśaṃsasi
body.translated_text: 'You revile all kings, and yet you do not praise yourself'

body.text:
dhairyavān ātmano 'nindyo
nāśvāsārthaṃ ca pṛcchasi
vimuktakrodhaharśaś ca
ko 'py atra pratibhāsi naḥ
anindyo nindyarūpeṇa
mahātmā tvaṃ hi me mataḥ
ko bhavān brūhi satyaṃ me
kimartham iha cāgataḥ
bhavān upendraḥ śakro vā
śarvo vā tvaṃ pinākadhṛk
body.translated_text: 'Steadfast, blameless of self, you do not ask for the sake of reassurance, and freed from anger and joy—who indeed do you appear to us here? Blameless, in a blameworthy form, you are, I think, a great soul; who are you? Tell me truly—for what purpose have you come here? Are you <s>Upendra</s>, or <s>Śakra</s>, or are you <s>Śarva</s> the bearer of the <s>Pināka</s>?'

body.text:
athavā nindyarūpeṇa
pitā nas tvam ihāgataḥ
body.translated_text: 'Or, in a blameworthy form, have you, our father, come here?'

body.text:
jñāto 'smi pṛthivīpāla
tuṣṭaś ca tava darśanāt
nandantu bhūmibhāgās te
yeṣu tvaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ
body.translated_text: 'I am known [to you], O protector of the earth, and pleased by the sight of you; may those portions of the earth rejoice in which you are the lord of the earth'

body.text:
nirjitya parasainyāni
kṣitiṃ dharmeṇa pālaya
svalpam apy astu te velāṃ
mā govindojjhitaṃ manaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Having conquered the armies of others, protect the earth with <s>dharma</s>; let there be even a little time for you—let not your mind be one that abandons <s>Govinda</s>'

body.text:
kiṃ me rājyena bhos tāta
viṣayair jīvitena vā
yo 'haṃ sūnāsahasrais tu
daśabhiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ
body.translated_text: 'What use to me is the kingdom, O father, or the sense-objects, or life, since I am surrounded by ten thousand slaughter-houses?'

body.text:
mā viṣādaṃ naraśreṣṭha
samupaihi yudhiṣṭhira
yajñeśvaraṃ yajñamūrtiṃ
tvaṃ ca viṣṇuṃ samāśritaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Do not come to despondency, O best of men, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>; you have taken refuge in the Lord of sacrifice, the embodiment of sacrifice, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'

body.text:
yeṣāṃ na viṣaye viprā
yajñair yajñapatiṃ harim
yajanti bhūbhujas teṣām
etat sūnoditaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: 'In whose realm the <s>vipras</s> do not worship with sacrifices <s>Hari</s>, the lord of sacrifice—of those rulers of the earth, this is the fruit declared as [that of] the slaughter-house'

body.text:
yeṣāṃ pāṣaṇḍasaṃkīrṇaṃ
na rāṣṭraṃ brāhmaṇotkaṭam
te tu sūnāsahasrāṇāṃ
daśānāṃ bhāgino nṛpāḥ
body.translated_text: 'Those kings whose realm is mingled with heretics and not abounding in <s>brāhmaṇas</s>—they are sharers in ten thousand slaughter-houses'

body.text:
yeṣāṃ na yajñapuruṣaḥ
kāraṇaṃ puruṣottamaḥ
te tu pāpasamācārāḥ
sūnāpāpaughabhāginaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Those for whom the sacrifice-person, the Supreme Person, is not the cause [of all]—they are of sinful conduct, sharers in the flood of slaughter-house sin'

body.text:
tvaṃ tu matprabhavas tāta
viṣṇubhaktas tathaiva ca
iṣṭir vaiśvānarī pāpam
upahaṃsyati te 'khilam
body.translated_text: 'But you are sprung from me, O son, and likewise a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> oblation will destroy all your sin'

body.text:
avaśyaṃ viṣaye kaścid
brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśritavrataḥ
iṣṭiṃ vaiśvānarīṃ kḷptāṃ
nirvaped abdaparyaye
tasya ṣaḍbhāgamātreṇa
tvaṃ pāpaṃ nirdahiṣyasi
body.translated_text: 'If unfailingly some <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in [your] realm who has taken up the vow offers the prescribed <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> oblation at the year's turn, by a mere sixth part of it you will burn away your sin'

body.text:
sa tvaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te
varaṃ yan manasecchasi
samyak śraddhāsamācārād
aham ārādhitas tvayā
body.translated_text: 'So you, blessings on you, choose the boon that you desire in your mind; through your right faith and conduct I have been propitiated by you'

body.text:
atha pātakabhītas tvaṃ
sarvabhāvena bhārata
vimuktānyasamārambho
nārāyaṇaparo bhava
body.translated_text: 'Now, you who are afraid of sin, O <s>Bhārata</s>, with your whole being, freed of other undertakings, become devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'

body.text:
paraḥ parāṇām ādyo 'sau
jñeyo dhyeyo janārdanaḥ
tadartham api karmāṇi
kurvan pāpaṃ vyapohati
body.translated_text: '<s>Janārdana</s>, the supreme of the supreme, the first, is to be known and to be meditated upon; even doing actions for his sake, one drives away sin'

body.text:
lobhādivyāptahṛdayo
yat pāpaṃ kurute naraḥ
vilayaṃ yāti tat sarvam
acyute hṛdaye sthite
body.translated_text: 'Whatever sin a man does, his heart pervaded by greed and the rest, all that goes to dissolution when <s>Acyuta</s> is established in the heart'

body.text:
śamāyālaṃ jalaṃ vahnes
tamaso bhāskarādayaḥ
kṣāntiḥ kaler aghaughasya
nāmasaṃkīrtanaṃ hareḥ
body.translated_text: 'Water suffices for the calming of fire, the sun and the rest for [calming] darkness; the proclaiming of the name of <s>Hari</s> [suffices] for the forbearance of the flood of sin of the <s>Kali</s> age'

body.text:
prasanno yadi me tāta
varārho yadi cāpy aham
varaṃ tad ekam evaitaṃ
prāptum icchāmy ahaṃ pitaḥ
body.translated_text: 'If you are pleased with me, O father, and if I am worthy of a boon, that one boon alone I wish to obtain, O father:'

body.text:
jāgratsvapnasuṣupteṣu
yogasthasya sadā mama
yā kācin manaso vṛttiḥ
sā bhavatv acyutāśrayā
body.translated_text: 'In waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, for me ever established in <s>yoga</s>, whatever activity of the mind there is, may it have <s>Acyuta</s> as its refuge'

body.text:
yā yā jāyeta me buddhir
yāvaj jīvāmy ahaṃ pitaḥ
sā sā chinattu saṃdehān
kṛṣṇāptau paripanthinaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Whatever awareness arises for me, as long as I live, O father, may it cut away the doubts that obstruct the attainment of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'

body.text:
yathā govindam ārādhya
saśarīraḥ surālayam
prāpnuyām iti me tāta
prayaccha pravaraṃ varam
body.translated_text: 'So that, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, I may attain in my [own] body the abode of the gods—O father, grant [me] this excellent boon'

body.text:
evam etad aśeṣaṃ te
matprasādād bhaviṣyati
nāsti govindabhaktānāṃ
vāñchitaṃ bhuvi durlabham
body.translated_text: 'Thus all this shall come to be for you by my grace; for the devotees of <s>Govinda</s> there is nothing desired that is hard to obtain on earth'

body.text:
iti dharmopadeśena
sarvadevavaraṃ harim
ārādhya pāṇḍavo yātaḥ
saśarīraḥ surālayam
body.translated_text: Thus, by [this] instruction in <s>dharma</s>, having worshipped <s>Hari</s>, the best of all the gods, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> went in his [own] body to the abode of the gods

body.text:
bhūyaś ca śṛṇu rājendra
janakena mahātmanā
yad gītaṃ vahatā bhaktiṃ
jñānam āsādya keśave
body.translated_text: And hear further, O king of kings, what was sung by the great soul <s>Janaka</s>, who bore devotion, having attained knowledge of <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
sarvatra samadṛṣṭiṃ taṃ
janakaṃ mithileśvaram
paśyantam acyutamayaṃ
sarvaṃ ca sacarācaram
body.translated_text: To that <s>Janaka</s>, lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, of equal vision everywhere, beholding all this, with what moves and is still, as made of <s>Acyuta</s>,

body.text:
dvijarūpaṃ samāsthāya
devadevo janārdanaḥ
upatasthe mahābhāgaṃ
pratyuvāca ca pārthivam
body.translated_text: assuming the form of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the God of gods <s>Janārdana</s> approached that greatly fortunate one and replied to the king:

body.text:
rājañ janaka bhadraṃ te
yad bravīmi nibodha tat
kuruṣva ca mahābuddhe
yadi sādhu mataṃ tava
body.translated_text: 'O king <s>Janaka</s>, blessings on you—understand that which I say, and do it, O greatly wise one, if it seems good to your mind'

body.text:
pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpālaḥ
pālayitvā pitā tava
svargaṃ gatas tathā bhrātā
samyak satyadhvajo nṛpaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Your father, protector of the earth, having protected the earth, went to heaven, and likewise your brother, the king <s>Satyadhvaja</s>, rightly'

body.text:
tvaṃ punar nirabhīmānaḥ
sarvatra samadarśanaḥ
ripumitrādivargeṣu
katham etad bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: 'But you, free of self-conceit, of equal vision everywhere toward the groups of enemies, friends, and the rest—how will this [kingship] come to be?'

body.text:
mitreṣu mitravan na tvaṃ
nāhiteṣv arivad bhavān
madhyasthabhāg na caiva tvaṃ
tathodāsīnavṛttiṣu
body.translated_text: 'You are not like a friend toward friends, nor like an enemy toward the hostile, nor are you a partisan of the neutral, and likewise [not] toward those of indifferent conduct'

body.text:
śabdādayo ye viśayās
te vairāgyaphalā nṛpa
nītyā vihīnas tu bhavān
kathaṃ rājyaṃ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: 'Sound and the other sense-objects, those are the fruit of dispassion, O king; but you, devoid of statecraft (<s>nīti</s>)—how will you rule the kingdom?'

body.text:
sarvair nītiṃ samāsthāya
yathā te prapitāmahaiḥ
kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tathā bhūpa
kuru mātijaḍo bhava
body.translated_text: 'Taking up statecraft, as the kingdom was ruled by all your great-grandfathers, so do, O king; do not be too dull-witted'

body.text:
tava prajñā matā hy eṣā
mama moho mahīpate
trivargasādhanaṃ prajñā
na dharmādivirodhinī
body.translated_text: 'This is held to be your wisdom, but my delusion, O lord of the earth—wisdom is the means to the three aims [of life], not opposed to <s>dharma</s> and the rest'

body.text:
samyag āha bhavān vipra
vācyam evaṃ bhavadvidhaiḥ
mamāpi śrūyatāṃ vākyaṃ
bhavato yadi rocate
body.translated_text: 'Rightly have you spoken, O <s>vipra</s>; thus indeed it is to be said by those of your sort; but let my speech too be heard, if it pleases you'

body.text:
yadā sarvagato viṣṇuḥ
paramātmā prajāpatiḥ
tadā mitrādimadhyastha-
saṃjñā keṣu nipātyatām
body.translated_text: 'When <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Supreme Self, the Lord of creatures, is all-pervading, then upon whom is the designation of friend, [foe], neutral, and the rest to be laid down?'

body.text:
pitā mātā tathā bhrātā
yadā nānyaj janārdanāt
pitṛmātṛmayīṃ saṃjñāṃ
tadā kutra karomy aham
body.translated_text: 'When father, mother, and brother are nothing other than <s>Janārdana</s>, then where do I make the designation consisting of father and mother?'

body.text:
so 'haṃ bravīmi yad vākyaṃ
tan nibodha dvijottama
anekarūparūpo 'yaṃ
viṣṇur evākhilaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: 'So I declare the speech that [I shall], understand it, O best of the twice-born: this <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of manifold forms, is the entire world'

body.text:
viṣṇuḥ pitā me jagataḥ pratiṣṭhā
viṣṇur mātā viṣṇur evāgrajo me
viṣṇur gatir viṣṇumayas tathāsmi
viṣṇau sthito 'smy akṣagataś ca viṣṇuḥ
body.translated_text: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is my father, the foundation of the world; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is my mother, <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed my elder brother; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is my goal, and I am made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I am established in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> is present in my senses'

body.text:
yo me mamatvopagataḥ sa viṣṇur
yaś cāribhūto mama so 'pi viṣṇuḥ
divaṃ viyad bhūḥ kakubhaś ca viṣṇur
bhūtāni viṣṇur bhuvanāni viṣṇuḥ
body.translated_text: 'He who has become an object of my sense of "mine," that is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; and he who has become my enemy, he too is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; heaven, sky, earth, and the quarters are <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the beings are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the worlds are <s>Viṣṇu</s>'

body.text:
paśyāmi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyac
śṛṇomi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyat
spṛśāmi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyaj
jighrāmi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyat
body.translated_text: 'I see <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that; I hear <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that; I touch <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that; I smell <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that'

body.text:
rasāmi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyan
manye ca viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyat
body.translated_text: 'I taste <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that; and I think <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that'

body.text:
jighrāmi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyac
namāmi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyat
body.translated_text: 'I smell <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that; I bow to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that'

body.text:
budhyāmi viṣṇuṃ na paraṃ tato 'nyat
sarvaṃ hi viṣṇur na paraṃ tato 'nyat
body.translated_text: 'I know <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that; for all is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nothing else higher than that'

body.text:
viṣṇuḥ samastaṃ na paraṃ tato 'sti
viṣṇuḥ samastaṃ na paraṃ ca devaḥ
body.translated_text: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is everything, there is nothing higher than that; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is everything, and the god [there is] nothing higher'

body.text: viṣṇuḥ sthārīyān na paraṃ tato 'sti
body.translated_text: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the most stable, there is nothing higher than that'

body.text:
viṣṇur laghīyān na paraṃ tato 'sti
viṣṇur garīyān na paraṃ tato 'nyat
body.translated_text: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the lightest, there is nothing higher than that; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the weightiest, nothing else higher than that'

body.text:
yathā na viṣṇuvyatiriktam anyac
śṛṇomi paśyāmi tathā spṛśāmi
satyena tenopaśamaṃ prayāntu
doṣā vimukteḥ paripanthino ye
body.translated_text: 'As I hear, see, and likewise touch nothing other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>—by that truth may the faults that obstruct liberation go to calm'

body.text:
na me 'sti bandhur na ca me 'sti śatrur
na bhūtavargo na jano madanyaḥ
tvaṃ cāhaṃ anye ca śarīrabhedair
vibhinnam īśasya hareḥ svarūpam
body.translated_text: 'I have no kinsman, nor have I an enemy, no host of beings, no person other than me; you and I and others, by the divisions of body, are the divided essential nature of the Lord <s>Hari</s>'

body.text:
mūrtāmūrtiviśeṣaṃ tu
paśyatas tanmayaṃ dvija
krodhaharṣādayo bhāvāḥ
sthāsyanti hṛdaye katham
body.translated_text: 'For one who beholds the distinction of the embodied and the bodiless as made of him (Viṣṇu), O twice-born, how will the states of anger, joy, and the rest abide in the heart?'

body.text:
sa tvaṃ prasīda moho 'yam
atha cen mama suvrata
tathāpi mā ruṣaṃ kārṣīr
acikitsyā hi mohitāḥ
body.translated_text: 'So be gracious; and if this is delusion of mine, O you of good vows, even so do not be angry, for the deluded are not to be cured [by anger]'

body.text:
bahurūpas tato rūpaṃ
śaṅkhacakragadādharam
darśayām āsa suprīto
janakāya janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: Thereupon the One of many forms, well pleased, showed to <s>Janaka</s> [his] form bearing the conch, discus, and mace—<s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
tatas taddarśanād bhūpaṃ
śirasā praṇataṃ prabhuḥ
ādyaḥ prajāpatipatiḥ
pratyuvācācyuto hariḥ
body.translated_text: Then, at the sight of him, to the king bowed down with his head, the first one, the lord of the Lord of creatures, the imperishable <s>Hari</s>, replied:

body.text:
varaṃ varaya bhūpāla
parituṣṭo 'smi te 'nagha
mayy arpitamanobuddheḥ
sadaivāhaṃ na durlabhaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Choose a boon, O protector of the earth; I am well pleased with you, O sinless one; to one whose mind and intellect are fixed on me, I am ever not hard to attain'

body.text:
yadi deva prasanno 'si
samyag ārādhito mayā
tad vṛṇomi varaṃ bhaktis
tvayy evāstu sadā mama
body.translated_text: 'If, O god, you are pleased, [and] rightly worshipped by me, then I choose this boon: may devotion to you alone ever be mine'

body.text:
evaṃ bhaviṣyatīty uktvā
gato 'ntardhānam īśvaraḥ
so 'pi lebhe layaṃ viṣṇau
bhaktyā yogisudurlabham
body.translated_text: Having said 'Thus it shall be,' the Lord went to disappearance; and that one too attained absorption (<s>laya</s>) in <s>Viṣṇu</s> through devotion, which is very hard for yogins [to attain]

body.text:
iti kṛṣṇe naravyāghra
kurvan bhaktiṃ naraḥ sadā
prāpnoti puruṣavyāghra
muktiṃ cāpy atidurlabhām
body.translated_text: Thus, O tiger among men, a man ever making devotion toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> attains, O tiger among men, liberation too, which is exceedingly hard to attain

body.text:
jagaddhātur anantasya
vāsudevasya bhārgava
mamāvatārān akhilāñ
śrotum icchā pravartate
body.translated_text: Of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the supporter of the world, the infinite, O <s>Bhārgava</s>, the desire arises in me to hear all the incarnations

body.text:
yathā yathā hi kṛṣṇasya
katheyaṃ kathyate tvayā
jāyate manasaḥ prītir
udbhūtapulakas tathā
body.translated_text: For just as this tale of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is told by you, delight of the mind arises, and likewise the rising of horripilation

body.text:
manaḥprītir anāyāsād
apuṇyacayasaṃkṣayaḥ
prāpyate puruṣair brahmañ
śṛṇvadbhir bhagavatkathām
body.translated_text: Delight of the mind without exertion, [and] the destruction of the heap of demerit, are attained by men, O <s>brahman</s>, who hear the tale of the Blessed One

body.text:
sa kuruṣvāmalamate
prasādapravaṇaṃ manaḥ
avatārān sureśasya
viṣṇor icchāmi veditum
body.translated_text: So make, O you of stainless mind, [your] mind inclined to grace; I wish to know the incarnations of the lord of gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
jagadguruṃ jagadyonim
anantam udakeśayam
nārāyaṇaṃ purākalpe
pṛṣṭavān kamalodbhavaḥ
body.translated_text: The Guru of the world, the source of the world, the infinite one lying on the waters, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>—the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) questioned in the former <s>kalpa</s>

body.text:
vinirjagmur mukhebhyas tu
brahmaṇo vyaktajanmanaḥ
oṃkārapravaṇā vedā
jagmus te ca rasātalam
body.translated_text: From the mouths of <s>Brahmā</s> of manifest birth issued forth the <s>Vedas</s>, intent on the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, and they went to the nether world (<s>Rasātala</s>)

body.text:
ekārṇave jagaty asmin
brahmaṇy amitatejasi
kṛṣṇanābhihradodbhūta-
kamalodaraśāyini
body.translated_text: In this world become a single ocean, while <s>Brahman</s> of immeasurable splendor lay in the heart of the lotus sprung from the lake of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s navel,

body.text:
bhogiśayyāśayaḥ kṛṣṇo
dvitīyāṃ tanum ātmanaḥ
kṛtvā mīnamayīṃ sadyaḥ
praviveśa rasātalam
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lying on the serpent-couch, having made at once a second body of himself made of a fish (<s>Matsya</s>), entered the nether world

body.text:
vedamūrtis tato vedān
āninye brahmaṇo 'ntikam
madhukaiṭabhābhyāṃ ca punar
bhogiśayyāgato hariḥ
hṛtān hayaśirā bhūtvā
vedān āhṛtavān rasāt
body.translated_text: Then, embodied as the <s>Veda</s>, he brought the <s>Vedas</s> to the presence of <s>Brahmā</s>; and again, [the Vedas] carried off by <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, <s>Hari</s>, lying on the serpent-couch, having become the horse-headed one (<s>Hayagrīva</s>), brought back the stolen <s>Vedas</s> from the nether world

body.text:
āhṛteṣv atha vedeṣu
devadevaṃ pitāmahaḥ
tuṣṭāva praṇato bhaktyā
tasya cāvir babhau hariḥ
body.translated_text: Then, when the <s>Vedas</s> had been brought back, the Grandsire (<s>Brahmā</s>), bowed down, praised the God of gods with devotion, and <s>Hari</s> became manifest to him

body.text:
athāmaraguruṃ viṣṇum
anantam ajam avyayam
uvāca prakaṭībhūtaṃ
praṇipatyābjasaṃbhavaḥ
body.translated_text: Then to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the guru of the immortals, the infinite, unborn, imperishable one become manifest, the lotus-born, having bowed down, spoke:

body.text:
namaḥ sūkṣmātisūkṣmāya
namas tubhyaṃ trimūrtaye
bahurūpādimadhyānta
pariṇāmavivarjita
body.translated_text: 'Homage to the subtlest of the subtle, homage to you of the triple form, O you free of transformation, [yet] of manifold beginning, middle, and end'

body.text:
jagadīśasya sarvasya
jagataḥ sarvakāmada
aham ātmabhavo deva
tvayādhyakṣo nirūpitaḥ
body.translated_text: "Of the Lord of the universe, of all, the granter of all desires of the world, I, the self-born god, have been appointed overseer by you;"

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi taṃ jñātum
ātmānaṃ prabhavāvyayam
viśvasya ca virūpasya
sthāvarasya carasya ca
body.translated_text: "that very self I wish to know, the source [yet] imperishable, of the universe—the multiform, the stationary, and the moving;"

body.text:
yadi te 'nugrahakṛtā
mayi buddhir janārdana
tan māṃ bhakta iti jñātvā
kathayātmānam acyuta
body.translated_text: "if your mind, O <s>Janārdana</s>, is favorably disposed toward me, then, knowing me as a devotee, declare your self, O <s>Acyuta</s>"

body.text:
kathayāmi tavātmānam
anākhyāgodaraṃ param
na vācāṃ viṣaye yo 'sāv
aviśeṣaṇalakṣaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: "I shall declare to you my self, the supreme, beyond the range of names, which is not within the province of words, characterized by the absence of distinctions;"

body.text:
prasādasumukhaḥ so 'ham
imaṃ yacchāmi te varam
anākhyātasvarūpaṃ māṃ
bhavāñ jñāsyati yogataḥ
body.translated_text: "I, with face gracious in favor, grant you this boon: you shall know me, whose nature is unnamed, through <s>yoga</s>"

body.text:
bhakto māṃ tattvato vetti
mayi bhaktiś ca te parā
majjijñāsā parā brahmaṃs
tena jātā matis tava
body.translated_text: "A devotee knows me in truth, and supreme is your devotion to me; the supreme desire to know me, O <s>brahman</s>, has by that arisen [as] your resolve"

body.text:
evam uktas tato brahmā
viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
viṣṇoḥ svarūpaṃ jijñāsur
yuyojātmānam ātmanā
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the mighty Lord, <s>Brahmā</s>, desiring to know the true form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, yoked his self by his self

body.text:
sa dadarśātisūkṣmaṃ ca
sūkṣmajyotiṣy ajaṃ vibhum
niyutārdhārdhamātreṇa
vyāptāśeṣacarācaram
body.translated_text: He beheld, exceedingly subtle, within a subtle light, the unborn, all-pervading Lord, who, by [but] a quarter of a quarter of a fraction, had pervaded the entire moving and unmoving [world]

body.text:
ātmānam indrarudrārka-
candrāśvivasumārutān
khādīny atha ca śabdādīn
dadṛśe ca sa tanmayān
body.translated_text: [He saw] as his self <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the sun, the moon, the <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s>, the [elements] beginning with ether, and the [qualities] beginning with sound—and he saw them as consisting of him

body.text:
ye vyaktā ye tathāvyaktā
bhāvā ye cāpi pauruṣāḥ
tāṃś ca tatrātisūkṣmo 'pi
dṛṣṭavān akhilān vibhuḥ
body.translated_text: Whatever states are manifest, and likewise unmanifest, and whatever are of the <s>Puruṣa</s>—those too the all-pervading [Brahmā], though exceedingly subtle, beheld there in their entirety

body.text:
tataḥ praṇamya deveśam
ajam ārtiharaṃ harim
pitāmahaḥ prahvatanur
vākyam etad uvāca ha
body.translated_text: Then, having bowed to the Lord of gods, the unborn, the remover of affliction, <s>Hari</s>, the Grandsire, his body bent low, spoke this word:

body.text:
jñātaṃ svarūpam ajñāta-
svarūpa bhagavaṃs tava
mayā na yad vāgviṣaye
tatrasthaṃ cākhilaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: "Your form, O Lord of unknown form, has been known by me, [the form] which is not within the province of words, [and] the entire world abiding therein;"

body.text:
dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi
svarūpaṃ yan mayā tava
bhagavañ jñātam ajñātam
anantāja namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: "I am blessed, I am favored, in that your form has been known by me, O Lord—[the form both] known [and] unknown; O endless unborn one, homage be to you"

body.text:
yadi prasādaṃ deva tvaṃ
prakaroṣi mamāparam
paramaṃ cāvatāreṣu
yad rūpaṃ tad vadasva me
body.translated_text: "If, O god, you grant me a further favor, tell me that form of yours which is supreme among the incarnations;"

body.text:
keṣu keṣu mayā jñeyaḥ
sthāneṣu tvam adhokṣaja
saṃbhūtayo mamācakṣva
yā bhaviṣyanti te bhuvi
body.translated_text: "in what places you are to be known by me, O <s>Adhokṣaja</s>—declare to me your manifestations which shall come to be on the earth;"

body.text:
devaloke nṛloke vā
pātāle khe 'nyato 'pi vā
saṃbhūtayo yās tu bhavān
kariṣyati vadasva tāḥ
body.translated_text: "in the world of the gods or the world of men, in the nether world, the sky, or elsewhere too—those manifestations which you shall make, declare them"

body.text:
tvaṃ kartā sarvabhūtānāṃ
saṃhartā ceśvareśvaraḥ
tavāpi kartā nānyo 'sti
svecchayā krīḍate bhavān
ahaṃ vedmi bhavantaṃ hi
na tavānyo 'sti veditā
body.translated_text: "You are the maker of all beings, and the destroyer, the Lord of lords; of you too there is no other maker; you sport at your own will; for I [alone] know you, [yet even I do not fully]; there is no other knower of you"

body.text:
yan māṃ tvaṃ pṛcchasi brahman
avatārāśritaṃ param
tat te samyak pravakṣyāmi
nibodha mama suvrata
body.translated_text: "That about which you ask me, O <s>brahman</s>, the supreme [matter] concerning the incarnations, that I shall rightly declare to you; understand from me, O you of good vows"

body.text:
mama prakṛtyā saṃyogaḥ
svecchayā saṃpravartate
deveṣu nṝṣu tiryakṣu
sthāvareṣu careṣu ca
mamāvatārāḥ kāryārthaṃ
jagataś copakāriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: "My conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) proceeds by my own will; among gods, men, beasts, the stationary, and the moving, my incarnations [come about] for the sake of [some] purpose and as benefactors of the world"

body.text:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya
glāniḥ samupajāyate
abhyutthānam adharmasya
tadātmāṅgaṃ sṛjāmy aham
body.translated_text: "Whenever indeed a decline of <s>dharma</s> arises [and] an uprising of <s>adharma</s>, then I send forth a portion of my self"

body.text:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ
vināśāya ca duṣkṛtāṃ
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya
saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge
body.translated_text: "For the protection of the good and for the destruction of the evil-doers, for the sake of establishing <s>dharma</s>, I come into being age after age"

body.text:
pūrvotpanneṣu bhūteṣu
nṛdevādiṣu cāpy aham
anupraviśya dharmasya
karomi paripālanam
body.translated_text: "Among beings previously created—men, gods, and the rest too—I, having entered in, effect the preservation of <s>dharma</s>"

body.text:
praviśya ca tathā pūrvaṃ
tanuṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
jagato 'sya jagatsṛṣṭiṃ
karomi sthitipālanam
body.translated_text: "And having thus entered, of old, a body, O best of the bearers of <s>dharma</s>, I effect the creation of this world and its maintenance and preservation"

body.text:
devatve devikā ceṣṭā
tiryaktve mama tāmasī
icchayā mānuṣatve ca
vicarāmi nṛceṣṭayā
body.translated_text: "In godhood, [my] activity is divine; in beast-hood, mine is <s>tāmasī</s> (of darkness); and in human-hood, by [my] will I move about with human activity"

body.text:
pratikṣaṇaṃ ca bhūteṣu
sṛjāmi jagataḥ sthitim
karomi vidyamāneṣu
dharmasaṃsthāpaneṣu ca
body.translated_text: "And at every instant I create, among beings, the maintenance of the world; I act [thus] among existing things and in the establishments of <s>dharma</s>"

body.text:
yad vai dharmopakārāya
yac ca duṣṭanivarhaṇam
caritaṃ mānuṣādīnāṃ
tad vai jānīhi matkṛtam
body.translated_text: "Whatever is for the benefit of <s>dharma</s> and whatever is the slaying of the wicked, the conduct of men and the rest—know that indeed to be done by me"

body.text:
yac ca pṛcchasi māṃ brahman
kāḥ kāḥ saṃbhūtayas tava
tāḥ śṛṇuṣva samāsena
yā bhaviṣyanti sāṃpratam
body.translated_text: "And what you ask me, O <s>brahman</s>—what are your manifestations—hear those in brief which shall come to be presently"

body.text:
matsyena bhūtvā pātālāt
tava vedāḥ samuddhṛtāḥ
madhukaiṭabhābhyāṃ ca hṛtā
dattāśvaśirasā mayā
body.translated_text: "Having become a fish, your <s>Vedas</s> were rescued by me from the nether world, and, carried off by <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, [restored] by me with a horse's head"

body.text:
tvam apy atra mahābhāga
madaṃśaḥ kamalodarāt
mannābhisaṃbhavāj jātaḥ
prajāsṛṣṭikaraḥ paraḥ
body.translated_text: "You too here, O greatly fortunate one, [are] my portion, born from the navel-lotus, arisen from my navel, the supreme maker of the creation of creatures"

body.text:
ekārṇavaṃ ca yad idaṃ
brahman paśyasy aśeṣataḥ
asmin vasumatīṃ devīṃ
magnāṃ pātālam āgatām
body.translated_text: "And this single ocean which you, O <s>brahman</s>, behold entirely—in it the goddess Earth, sunken, has gone to the nether world;"

body.text:
vedapādo yūpadaṃṣṭraḥ
kratudantaś citīmukhaḥ
agnijihvo darbharomā
brahmaśīrṣo mahātapāḥ
body.translated_text: "[I shall become the boar] whose feet are the <s>Vedas</s>, whose tusk is the sacrificial post, whose teeth are the rites, whose mouth is the fire-altar, whose tongue is fire, whose hair is <s>darbha</s>-grass, whose head is <s>brahman</s>, of great austerity,"

body.text:
ahorātrekṣaṇadharo
vedāṅgaśrutibhūṣaṇaḥ
ājyanāsaḥ śruvastuṇḍaḥ
sāmaghoṣasvaro mahān
body.translated_text: "bearing day and night as his two eyes, ornamented by the <s>Vedāṅgas</s> and <s>śruti</s>, whose nose is the clarified butter, whose snout is the sacrificial ladle, whose voice is the sound of the <s>Sāman</s>, the mighty one,"

body.text:
prāgvaṃśakāyo dyutimān
nānādīkṣābhir ācitaḥ
dakṣiṇāhṛdayo yogī
mahāsattramayo mahān
body.translated_text: "whose body is the eastern sacrificial shed, radiant, heaped with various consecrations, whose heart is the sacrificial fee, the yogi, consisting of the great sacrificial session, the mighty one,"

body.text:
upakarmeṣṭiruciraḥ
pravargāvartabhūṣaṇaḥ
nānācchandogatipatho
brahmoktikarmavikramaḥ
body.translated_text: "resplendent with the supplementary rites and oblations, ornamented by the <s>pravargya</s> ceremony, whose path is the gait of various meters, whose prowess is the rites enjoined by <s>brahman</s>"

body.text:
bhūtvā yajñavarāho 'ham
iti brahman rasātalāt
pṛthivīm uddhariṣyāmi
sthāpayaiṣyāmi ca sthitau
body.translated_text: "Having become the sacrifice-boar, thus, O <s>brahman</s>, from the netherworld I shall lift up the earth and establish it in its [proper] state"

body.text:
parvatānāṃ nadīnāṃ ca
dvīpādīnāṃ ca yā sthitiḥ
tāṃ ca tadvat kariṣyāmi
śailādīnām anukramāt
body.translated_text: "And the [proper] state of mountains and rivers and continents and the rest, that too I shall likewise make, of mountains and the rest in due order"

body.text:
hiraṇyākṣaṃ ca durvṛttaṃ
kaśyapasyātmasaṃbhavam
tenaiva ghātayiṣyāmi
rūpeṇāhaṃ prajāpate
body.translated_text: "And <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, the wicked one, born of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, him by that very form I shall cause to be slain, O <s>Prajāpati</s>"

body.text:
utpādya pṛthivīṃ samyak
sthāpayitvā yathā purā
sṛṣṭiṃ tataḥ kariṣyāmi
tvām āviśya prajāpatim
body.translated_text: "Having rightly raised up the earth [and] established it as before, I shall then effect creation, having entered you, the <s>Prajāpati</s>"

body.text:
jānāsi kāpilaṃ rūpaṃ
prathamaṃ pauruṣaṃ mama
sarvavidyāpraṇetāraṃ
tvayā vedeṣu darśitam
ravimaṇḍalamadhyastham
agner yat paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: "You know the <s>Kāpila</s> form, my first <s>Puruṣa</s>-form, the propounder of all knowledge, shown by you in the <s>Vedas</s>, situated in the midst of the sun's disc, which is the supreme abode of fire"

body.text:
tata utsṛjya rūpāṇi
amarādivibhedataḥ
vyāpayiṣyāmi lokāṃs tu
bhūlokādīm aśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: "Thence, sending forth forms by the distinctions of the immortals and the rest, I shall pervade the worlds, beginning with the earth-world, entirely"

body.text:
sṛṣṭaṃ jagad idaṃ deva-
mānuṣyādiviśeṣaṇam
hiraṇyakaśipur daityas
tāpayiṣyati vikramāt
body.translated_text: "When this world, distinguished into gods, men, and the rest, has been created, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> the <s>daitya</s> will torment [it] by his prowess"

body.text:
vyaṃsayitvā varāṃs tasya
tais tair hetubhir ātmavān
nṛsiṃharūpaṃ kṛtvāhaṃ
ghātayiṣyāmi taṃ ripum
body.translated_text: "Having frustrated his boons by these and those means, self-possessed, having made the man-lion form, I shall cause that foe to be slain"

body.text:
kṣīrābdau kūrmarūpo 'haṃ
devānāṃ kamalodbhava
mandaraṃ dhārayiṣyāmi
pṛṣṭhenāmṛtamanthane
body.translated_text: "In the milk-ocean I [shall become] of tortoise-form, O lotus-born one, of the gods; I shall bear <s>Mandara</s> upon my back in the churning for nectar"

body.text:
hariṣyati ca devānāṃ
yajñabhāgān yadā baliḥ
tadāhaṃ vāmano bhūtvā
gatvā tasya mahādhvaram
body.translated_text: "And when <s>Bali</s> shall carry off the sacrificial shares of the gods, then I, having become <s>Vāmana</s>, having gone to his great sacrifice,"

body.text:
vañcayitvāsurapatiṃ
kariṣyāmi tripiṣṭapam
baliṃ cāpi kariṣyāmi
pātālatalavāsinam
body.translated_text: "having deceived the lord of the <s>asuras</s>, I shall make the triple-heaven [secure], and I shall make <s>Bali</s> a dweller in the floor of the nether world"

body.text:
atrer dattvā varaṃ caiva
tasya putratvam āgataḥ
dattātreyo bhaviṣyāmi
nihaṃsyāmi tathāsurān
body.translated_text: "And having given a boon to <s>Atri</s>, attaining sonhood to him, I shall become <s>Dattātreya</s>, and likewise shall slay the <s>asuras</s>"

body.text:
sattvānām upakārāya
pradhānapuruṣāntaram
darśayiṣyāmi lokeṣu
kāpilaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ
body.translated_text: "For the benefit of beings, I shall display in the worlds the inner [reality], distinct from <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, having assumed the <s>Kāpila</s> form"

body.text:
kārtavīryādibhiś cānyaiś
caturdaśabhir anvitāḥ
bhaviṣyanti madaṃśena
tretāyāṃ cakravartinaḥ
body.translated_text: "And [men] joined with <s>Kārtavīrya</s> and other fourteen [worthies] shall come to be, by my portion, universal sovereigns in the <s>Tretā</s> age"

body.text:
tataś ca bhārgavo rāmo
gṛhītaparaśur dvijaḥ
bhūtvā kṣatriyahīnāṃ ca
kariṣyāmi vasuṃdharām
body.translated_text: "And then, having become <s>Bhārgava</s> <s>Rāma</s>, the twice-born one bearing the axe, I shall make the earth devoid of <s>kṣatriyas</s>"

body.text:
punaś ca rāghavo rāmo
bhūtvā daśarathātmajaḥ
baddhvā mahodadhiṃ kartā
rākṣasānāṃ kulakṣayam
body.translated_text: "And again, having become <s>Rāghava</s> <s>Rāma</s>, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, having bound the great ocean, I shall be the maker of the destruction of the family of the <s>rākṣasas</s>;"

body.text:
uttīrya ca paraṃ pāraṃ
laṅkām āsādya durjayām
nihatya rāvaṇaṃ vīraṃ
varadānena darpitam
māyāvināṃ mahāvīryaṃ
rakṣasāṃ vanaśāyinām
lakṣmaṇānucaro rāmaḥ
kariṣyāmi kulakṣayam
body.translated_text: "and having crossed to the far shore, having reached the unconquerable <s>Laṅkā</s>, having slain the hero <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, made proud by the granting of boons—of the masters of illusion, of great might, the <s>rākṣasas</s> dwelling in the forest, [I,] <s>Rāma</s> attended by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, shall effect the destruction of their family"

body.text:
aṣṭāviṃśatime prāpte
dvāpare kaṃsam ucchritam
keśinaṃ dhenukaṃ caiva
śakuniṃ pūtanāṃ tathā
ariṣṭaṃ ca haniṣyāmi
muruṃ narakam eva ca
body.translated_text: "When the twenty-eighth <s>Dvāpara</s> has arrived, I shall slay the haughty <s>Kaṃsa</s>, and <s>Keśin</s>, and <s>Dhenuka</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>, and likewise <s>Pūtanā</s>, and <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Muru</s>, and <s>Naraka</s> as well"

body.text:
niśumbhaṃ sahayagrīvaṇ
tathānyāṃś cāsureśvarān
haniṣyāmi sudurvṛttāṃl
lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
body.translated_text: "<s>Niśumbha</s> together with <s>Hayagrīva</s>, and likewise the other lords of the <s>asuras</s>, the very wicked ones, I shall slay out of desire for the welfare of the worlds"

body.text:
pravarṣati sa devendre
mahobhaṅgavirodhite
govardhanaṃ girivaraṃ
dhārayiṣyāmi bāhunā
body.translated_text: "When the lord of the gods [<s>Indra</s>] rains down, provoked by the breaking of his pride [the sacrifice], I shall hold up <s>Govardhana</s>, the best of mountains, with my arm"

body.text:
bhārākrāntām imām urvīṃ
dhanaṃjayasahāyavān
ghātayitvākhilān bhūpāṃl
laghvīṃ kartāsmi sattama
body.translated_text: "This earth, oppressed by [its] burden, with <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> [Arjuna] as my helper, having caused all the kings to be slain, I shall make light, O most excellent one"

body.text:
prāpte kaliyuge kṛtsnam
upasaṃhṛtya vai kulam
dvārakāṃ plāvayiṣyāmi
utsrakṣyāmi manuṣyatām
body.translated_text: "When the <s>Kali</s> age has arrived, having wholly withdrawn the family [Yādava], I shall flood <s>Dvārakā</s> [and] cast off [my] human existence"

body.text:
dvitīyo yo mamāṃśas tu
rāmo 'nantaḥ sa lāṅgalī
so 'pi saṃtyajya vasudhāṃ
rasātalam upeṣyati
body.translated_text: "And that second portion of mine, <s>Rāma</s> the endless one [<s>Ananta</s>], the plough-bearer, he too, abandoning the earth, shall go to the nether world"

body.text:
tataḥ kaliyuge ghore
saṃprāpte 'bjasamudbhava
śuddhodanasuto buddho
bhaviṣyāmi vimatsaraḥ
body.translated_text: "Then, when the dreadful <s>Kali</s> age has arrived, O lotus-born one, I shall become <s>Buddha</s>, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, free of envy"

body.text:
bauddhaṃ dharmam upāśritya
kariṣye dharmadeśanām
narāṇām atha nārīṇāṃ
dayāṃ bhūteṣu darśayan
body.translated_text: "Resorting to the Buddhist <s>dharma</s>, I shall make a teaching of <s>dharma</s>, showing compassion toward beings, both men and women"

body.text:
raktāmbarā hy āñjitākṣāḥ
praśāntamanasas tataḥ
śūdrā dharmaṃ pravakṣyanti
mayi buddhatvam āgate
body.translated_text: "Then, clad in red garments, their eyes anointed, of tranquil mind, <s>śūdras</s> shall expound <s>dharma</s>, when I have attained buddhahood"

body.text:
eḍūkacihnā pṛthivī
na devagṛhabhūṣitā
bhavitrī prāyaśo brahman
mayi buddhatvam āgate
body.translated_text: "The earth, marked with <s>eḍūka</s>-monuments [Buddhist stūpas], not adorned with temples of the gods, shall come to be for the most part, O <s>brahman</s>, when I have attained buddhahood"

body.text:
skandhadarśanamātraṃ hi
paśyantaḥ sakalaṃ jagat
śūdrāḥ śūdreṣu dāsyanti
mayi buddhatvam āgate
body.translated_text: "Merely by the sight of [their] shoulders [or relic-mounds], [men] seeing the whole world, <s>śūdras</s> shall give [gifts] among <s>śūdras</s>, when I have attained buddhahood"

body.text:
alpāyuṣas tato martyā
mohopahatacetasaḥ
narakārhāṇi karmāṇi
kariṣyanti prajāpate
body.translated_text: "Then men of short life, their minds smitten by delusion, shall perform deeds deserving of hell, O <s>Prajāpati</s>"

body.text:
svādhyāyeṣv avasīdanto
brāhmaṇāḥ śaucavarjitāḥ
antyapratigrahādānaṃ
kariṣyanty alpamedhasaḥ
body.translated_text: "<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, sinking in their self-study, devoid of purity, of little wit, shall accept gifts and take [them] from the lowest [people]"

body.text:
na śroṣyanti pituḥ putrāḥ
śvaśrūśvaśurayoḥ snuṣāḥ
na bhāryā bhartur īśasya
na bhṛtyā vinayasthitāḥ
body.translated_text: "Sons shall not heed their father, daughters-in-law their mother-in-law and father-in-law; a wife shall not [heed] her husband, the lord, nor servants stand in discipline"

body.text:
varṇasaṃkaratāṃ prāpte
loke 'smin dasyutāṃ gate
brāhmaṇādiṣu varṇeṣu
bhaviṣyaty adharottaram
body.translated_text: "When this world has reached the state of caste-confusion [and] gone to brigandage, among the classes beginning with the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the lower shall become uppermost"

body.text:
dharmakañcukasaṃvītā
vidharmarucayas tathā
mānuṣān bhakṣayiṣyanti
mlecchāḥ pārthivarūpiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: "Wrapped in the cloak of <s>dharma</s>, but with a taste for false <s>dharma</s>, <s>mlecchas</s> in the guise of kings shall devour human beings"

body.text:
tataḥ kaliyugasyānte
vedo vājasaneyakaḥ
daśa pañca ca vai śākhāḥ
pramāṇena bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: "Then at the end of the <s>Kali</s> age, the <s>Vājasaneya</s> <s>Veda</s> shall be, in extent, [only] fifteen branches"

body.text:
tato 'haṃ saṃbhaviṣyāmi
brāhmaṇo haripiṅgalaḥ
kalkī viṣṇuyaśaḥputro
yājñavalkyapurohitaḥ
body.translated_text: "Then I shall come to be a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, tawny like <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kalkī</s>, the son of <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>, with <s>Yājñavalkya</s> as [my] domestic priest"

body.text:
mlecchān utsādayiṣyāmi
gṛhītāstraḥ kuśāyudhaḥ
sthāpayiṣyāmi maryādāś
cāturvarṇye yathoditāḥ
body.translated_text: "I shall root out the <s>mlecchas</s>, weapon in hand, armed with <s>kuśa</s>-grass; I shall establish the boundaries [of conduct] in the fourfold class-order, as they have been declared"

body.text:
tathāśrameṣu sarveṣu
brahmacārivratādikāḥ
sthāpayitvā tataḥ sarvāḥ
prajāḥ saddharmavartmani
kalkirūpaṃ parityajya
divam eṣyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: "And likewise in all the <s>āśramas</s>, the vows of the <s>brahmacārin</s> and the rest—having established all these, [and set] the people on the path of true <s>dharma</s>, having cast off the <s>Kalkī</s> form, I shall go again to heaven"

body.text:
tataḥ kṛtayugaṃ bhūyaḥ
pūrvavat saṃpravartsyate
varṇāśramāś ca dharmeṣu
dveṣu sthāsyanti sattama
body.translated_text: "Then the <s>Kṛta</s> age shall again proceed as before, and the classes and stages of life shall stand in their two <s>dharmas</s>, O most excellent one"

body.text:
evaṃ sarveṣu kalpeṣu
sarvamanvantareṣu ca
mamāvatārāḥ śataśo
ye bhavanti jagaddhitāḥ
body.translated_text: "Thus in all the <s>kalpas</s> and in all the <s>manvantaras</s>, my incarnations, in their hundreds, come to be for the welfare of the world"

body.text:
saṃkarṣaṇātmajaś caiva
kalpānte ca rasātalāt
samutpatsyet tadā rudraḥ
kālāgnir iti yaḥ śrutaḥ
body.translated_text: "And the son of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, shall arise from the nether world—then [comes] <s>Rudra</s>, who is heard of as <s>Kālāgni</s> (the fire of time)"

body.text:
tataḥ kṣayaṃ kariṣyāmi
jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam
bhūyaś caiva hi svapsyāmi
jagaty ekārṇave sthite
tvadrūpī ca tato bhūtvā
jagat srakṣyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: "Then I shall effect the destruction of the world, the stationary and the moving; and again I shall sleep, the world standing as a single ocean; and then, having become of your form, I shall create the world again"

body.text:
etat saṃkṣepato brahman
mayākhyātaṃ yathātatham
aṃśāvataraṇaṃ sarvaṃ
mattaḥ saṃkṣepataḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: "This, in brief, O <s>brahman</s>, has been declared by me as it truly is; the whole descent by portions—hear it from me in brief"

body.text:
yad dṛśyaṃ yac ca vai spṛśyaṃ
yad ghreyaṃ rasyate ca yat
yac chravyaṃ yac ca mantavyaṃ
bodhavyaṃ cāham aṃśagaḥ
body.translated_text: "Whatever is to be seen, and whatever is to be touched, whatever is to be smelled and whatever is tasted, whatever is to be heard and whatever is to be thought [and] to be cognized—that am I, present by [my] portion"

body.text:
yat tu buddheḥ parataram
anākhyeyam anopamam
tad ahaṃ brahma nirdvandvaṃ
yad vai paśyanti sūrayaḥ
body.translated_text: "But that which is beyond the intellect, unnameable, incomparable—that am I, <s>brahman</s>, free of duality, which the wise indeed behold"

body.text:
idaṃ janmarahasyaṃ me
yo naraḥ kīrtayiṣyati
sulabho 'haṃ bhaviṣyāmi
tasya janmani janmani
body.translated_text: "This secret of my births—the man who shall recount it, for him I shall become easy to attain, birth after birth"

body.text:
paṭhann etad brahmahā tu
surāpo gurutalpagaḥ
steyī kṛtaghno goghnaś ca
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: "Reciting this, even a slayer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a liquor-drinker, a violator of his guru's bed, a thief, an ingrate, and a cow-killer, is released from all sins"

body.text:
garbhiṇī janayet putraṃ
kanyā vindati satpatim
labhante 'bhimatān kāmān
narās tāṃs tān yathepsitān
body.translated_text: "A pregnant woman shall bear a son, a maiden finds a good husband; men obtain their desired wishes, this and that, as they wish"

body.text:
iti devātidevena
brahmaṇo vyaktajanmanaḥ
rahasyam idam ākhyātaṃ
tavāpi kathitaṃ mayā
body.translated_text: Thus, by the god above the gods, this secret of <s>Brahmā</s> of manifest birth has been declared, and it has been told to you too by me

body.text:
viṣṇuḥ sarvagato 'nantaḥ
sarvaṃ tatra pratiṣṭhitam
sa ca sarvam idaṃ rājan
na tato vidyate param
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is all-pervading, endless; in him all is established; and he is all this, O king; there is nothing higher than him

body.text:
etat pavitraṃ paṭhitaṃ
tathā duḥsvapnanāśanam
jātismaratvaṃ prajñāṃ ca
dadāti paṭhatāṃ nṛṇām
body.translated_text: This holy [text], recited, is likewise the destroyer of evil dreams; it grants, to the men who recite it, the memory of [past] births and wisdom

body.text:
mayā hi devadevasya
viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ
śrutāḥ saṃbhūtayaḥ sarvā
gadatas tava suvrata
body.translated_text: By me indeed have all the manifestations of the god of gods <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of boundless splendor, been heard, as you related them, O man of good vows.

body.text:
yadi prasanno bhagavān
anugrāhyo 'smi vā yadi
tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi
nṝṇāṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam
body.translated_text: If the Blessed One is pleased, or if I am one to be favored, then I wish to hear that which destroys the bad dreams of men.

body.text:
svapnā hi sumahābhāga
dṛśyante ye śubhāśubhāḥ
phalāni te prayacchanti
tadguṇāny eva bhārgava
body.translated_text: For dreams, O greatly fortunate one, which are seen as auspicious and inauspicious, give their fruits according to their nature, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.

body.text:
yad yat puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ ca
nṝṇām atiśubhapradam
duḥsvapnopaśamāyālaṃ
tan me vistarato vada
body.translated_text: Whatever is holy and purifying and grants exceedingly auspicious things to men, and is sufficient for the quelling of bad dreams—that tell me in detail.

body.text:
idam eva mahārāja
pṛṣṭavāṃs te pitāmahaḥ
bhīṣmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ
dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
body.translated_text: This very thing, O great king, your grandfather <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> the son of <s>Dharma</s> asked of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, the best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
devavrataṃ mahāprājñaṃ
sarvaśāstraviśāradam
vinayenopasaṃgamya
paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
body.translated_text: Having approached with humility <s>Devavrata</s> [Bhīṣma], greatly wise, skilled in all the <s>śāstras</s>, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> questioned him:

body.text:
duḥsvapnadarśanaṃ ghoram
avekṣya bharatarṣabha
prayataḥ kiṃ japej japyaṃ
vibuddhaḥ kim anusmaret
body.translated_text: "Having beheld a terrible vision of a bad dream, O bull of the <s>Bharatas</s>, what muttered-prayer should the restrained one mutter? On awakening, what should he recall?

body.text:
pitāmaha mahābuddhe
buddher bhedo mahān ayam
tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi
brūhi me vadatāṃ vara
body.translated_text: O grandfather of great intellect, this is a great division of intellect; that I wish to hear—tell me, O best of speakers."

body.text:
śṛṇu rājan mahābāho
vartayiṣyāmi te 'khilam
duḥsvapnadarśane japyaṃ
yad vai nityaṃ samāhitaiḥ
body.translated_text: "Hear, O mighty-armed king, I shall relate to you the whole—the muttered-prayer in the seeing of a bad dream, which is to be [muttered] ever by the concentrated.

body.text:
atrāpy udāharantīmam
itihāsaṃ purātanam
gajendramokṣaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ
kṛṣṇasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: On this point they relate this ancient tale, the holy releasing of the elephant-king by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of untiring deeds.

body.text:
sarvaratnamayaḥ śrīmāṃs
trikūṭo nāma parvataḥ
sutaḥ parvatarājasya
sumeror bhāskaradyuteḥ
body.translated_text: There is a glorious mountain named <s>Trikūṭa</s>, made of all jewels, a son of <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, of sun-like splendor,

body.text:
kṣīrodajalavīcyagrair
dhautāmalaśilātalaḥ
utthitaḥ sāgaraṃ bhittvā
devarṣigaṇasevitaḥ
body.translated_text: its stainless rock-surface washed by the crests of the waves of the Ocean of Milk, risen up having pierced the sea, served by the bands of gods and seers,

body.text:
apsarobhiḥ samākīrṇaḥ
śrīmān prasravaṇākulaḥ
gandharvaiḥ kiṃnarair yakṣaiḥ
siddhacāraṇapannagaiḥ
body.translated_text: thronged with <s>apsarases</s>, glorious, abounding in springs, [served] by <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, and serpents,

body.text:
vidyādharaiḥ sapatnikaiḥ
saṃyataiś ca tapasvibhiḥ
body.translated_text: by <s>Vidyādharas</s> with their wives, and by restrained ascetics,

body.text:
mṛgair dvīpair dvijaiś caiva
vṛtaḥ sauvarṇarājataiḥ
puṃnāgaiḥ karṇikāraiś ca
puṣpitair upaśobhitaḥ
body.translated_text: encircled by deer, lions, and birds, golden and silver, made beautiful by blossoming <s>Puṃnāga</s> and <s>Karṇikāra</s> trees,

body.text:
cūtanīpakadambaiś ca
candanāgarucampakaiḥ
śālais tālais tamālaiś ca
kuṭajaiś cārjunais tathā
body.translated_text: and by mango, <s>Nīpa</s>, and <s>Kadamba</s> trees, by sandal, aloe, and <s>Campaka</s>, by <s>Śāla</s>, palm, and <s>Tamāla</s> trees, by <s>Kuṭaja</s> and likewise <s>Arjuna</s> trees—

body.text:
evaṃ bahuvidhair vṛkṣaiḥ
sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ
nānādhātūjjvalaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ
prasravadbhiḥ samantataḥ
body.translated_text: thus adorned on all sides by manifold trees, with peaks blazing with various minerals, streaming on all sides,

body.text:
mṛgaiḥ śākhāmṛgaiḥ siṃhair
mātaṃgaiś ca sadāmadaiḥ
jīvaṃjīvakasaṃghuṣṭaṃ
cakoraśikhināditam
body.translated_text: [loud] with deer, monkeys, lions, and elephants ever in rut, resounding with <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds, sounded by <s>cakoras</s> and peacocks.

body.text:
tasyaikaṃ kāñcanaṃ śṛṅgaṃ
sevate yad divādaraḥ
nānāpuṣpasamākīrṇaṃ
nānāgandhasamākulam
body.translated_text: One golden peak of it the radiant Day [the sun] frequents, strewn with various flowers, abounding in various fragrances.

body.text:
dvitīyaṃ rājataṃ śṛṅgaṃ
sevate yan niśākaraḥ
pāṇḍurāmbudasaṃkāśaṃ
tuṣāracayasaṃnibham
body.translated_text: The second, silver peak the Night-maker [the moon] frequents, resembling a pale cloud, like a heap of frost.

body.text:
vajrendranīlavaiḍūrya-
tejobhir bhāsayan nabhaḥ
tṛtīyaṃ brahmasadanaṃ
prakṛṣṭaṃ śṛṅgam uttamam
body.translated_text: Illumining the sky with the splendor of diamond, sapphire, and beryl, the third is the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, an exalted, supreme peak.

body.text:
na tat kṛtaghnāḥ paśyanti
na nṛśaṃsā na nāstikāḥ
nātaptatapasaḥ śailaṃ
taṃ vai paśyanti mānavāḥ
body.translated_text: The ungrateful do not behold it, nor the cruel, nor the unbelievers, nor those who have not practiced austerity—such men do not behold that mountain.

body.text:
tasya sānumataḥ pṛṣṭhe
saraḥ kāñcanapaṅkajam
kāraṇḍavasamākīrṇaṃ
rājahaṃsopaśobhitam
body.translated_text: On the back of that mountain, possessed of peaks, is a lake with golden lotuses, thronged with <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, made beautiful by royal swans,

body.text:
mattabhramarasaṃghuṣṭaṃ
phullapaṅkajaśobhitam
kumudotpalakalhāra-
puṇḍarīkopaśobhitam
body.translated_text: humming with intoxicated bees, made beautiful with full-blown lotuses, adorned with <s>kumuda</s>, <s>utpala</s>, <s>kalhāra</s>, and <s>puṇḍarīka</s> [lilies and lotuses],

body.text:
utpalaiḥ śatapattraiś ca
kāñcanaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam
pattrair maṇidalaprakhyaiḥ
puṣpaiḥ kāñcanasaṃnibhaiḥ
gulmaiḥ kīcakaveṇūnāṃ
samantāt parivāritam
body.translated_text: adorned with hundred-petaled lotuses, golden, with leaves like slabs of gem, with flowers resembling gold, surrounded all around by thickets of hollow bamboos.

body.text:
tasmin sarasi duṣṭātmā
virūpo 'ntarjalāśayaḥ
āsīd grāho gajendrāṇāṃ
durādharṣo mahābalaḥ
body.translated_text: In that lake there was an evil-souled, misshapen crocodile, a dweller within the water, an inveterate foe of elephant-kings, hard to assail, of great strength.

body.text:
atha dantojjvalamukhaḥ
kadācid gajayūthapaḥ
ājagāmāsitābhrābhaḥ
kareṇuparivāritaḥ
body.translated_text: Then once a leader of an elephant-herd, his face bright with tusks, came—dark like a black cloud, surrounded by his she-elephants,

body.text:
madasrāvī mahāraudraḥ
pādacārīva parvataḥ
vāsayan madagandhena
girim airāvatopamaḥ
body.translated_text: rut-flowing, exceedingly fearsome, like a walking mountain, perfuming the mountain with the scent of his rut, resembling <s>Airāvata</s>.

body.text:
sa gajo 'ñjanasaṃkāśo
madāc calitamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: That elephant, like collyrium [in color], his mind agitated by rut,

body.text:
gandhahastīti vikhyātaḥ
saraḥ samabhigamya tat
tṛṣitaḥ sa jalaṃ prāpya
kusumākaraśītalam
apibat sahasā rājan
kareṇuparivāritaḥ
body.translated_text: renowned as the scent-elephant, having approached that lake, thirsty, having reached the water cool [as] a treasury of flowers, drank suddenly, O king, surrounded by his she-elephants.

body.text:
salīlaṃ paṅkajavane
yūthamadhyagato 'vrajat
body.translated_text: Sportively, gone into the midst of his herd, he moved in the lotus-grove.

body.text:
gṛhītas tena raudreṇa
grāheṇāvyaktamūrtinā
paśyantīnāṃ kareṇūnāṃ
krośantīnāṃ ca dāruṇam
body.translated_text: He was seized by that fearsome crocodile of indistinct form, while the she-elephants looked on and cried out terribly.

body.text:
kriyate paṅkajavane
grāheṇātibalīyasā
body.translated_text: He is dragged about in the lotus-grove by the exceedingly powerful crocodile.

body.text:
gajaś cākarṣate tīraṃ
grāhaś cākarṣate jalam
tayor dvandva mahāyuddhaṃ
divyavarṣasahasrikam
body.translated_text: And the elephant pulls toward the shore, and the crocodile pulls toward the water; between the two there was a great combat, lasting a thousand divine years.

body.text:
vāruṇaiḥ saṃyataḥ pāśair
niḥprayatnagatiḥ kṛtaḥ
veṣṭyamānaḥ sughorais tu
pāśair nāgo dṛḍhais tathā
body.translated_text: Bound by the nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s>, his movement made effortless, the elephant, being wound about by exceedingly terrible, firm nooses,

body.text:
visphurjya ca yathāśakti
vikruśya ca mahāravān
vyathitaḥ saṃnirutsāho
gṛhīto ghorakarmaṇā
body.translated_text: having burst forth according to his strength and cried out great roars, distressed, his vigor gone, seized by the doer of the terrible deed,

body.text:
paramāpadam āpanno
manasācintayad dharim
sa tu nāgavaraḥ śrīmān
nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: fallen into the supreme calamity, meditated in his mind upon <s>Hari</s>; that glorious best of elephants, intent upon <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

body.text:
tam eva paramaṃ devaṃ
gataḥ sarvātmanā tadā
ekāgraṃ cintayām āsa
viśuddhenāntarātmanā
body.translated_text: then went with his whole self to that very supreme god, and meditated one-pointedly with a purified inner self.

body.text:
janmajanmāntarābhyāsād
bhaktimān garuḍadhvaje
ādyaṃ devaṃ mahātmānaṃ
pūjayām āsa keśavam
body.translated_text: Through the practice of birth after birth, devoted to the one whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s>, he worshipped the primal god, the great-souled <s>Keśava</s>,

body.text:
navameghapratīkāśaṃ
śaṅkhacakragadādharam
sahasraśubhanāmānam
ādidevam ajaṃ param
body.translated_text: resembling a fresh cloud, the bearer of conch, discus, and mace, of a thousand auspicious names, the primal god, unborn, supreme,

body.text:
digbāhuṃ sarvamūrdhānaṃ
bhūpādaṃ gaganodaram
ādityacandranayanaṃ
samagraṃ lokasākṣiṇam
body.translated_text: whose arms are the directions, whose head is all, whose feet are the earth, whose belly is the sky, whose eyes are the sun and moon, entire, the witness of the world.

body.text:
bhagavantaṃ prasanno 'haṃ
viṣṇum apratimaujasam
body.translated_text: [He said:] "I am gladdened toward the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> of incomparable might."

body.text:
pragṛhya puṣkarāgreṇa
kāñcanaṃ kamalottamam
āpadvimokṣam anvicchan
gajaḥ stotram udairayat
body.translated_text: Having grasped with the tip of his trunk a golden best-of-lotuses, seeking release from calamity, the elephant raised up a hymn of praise:

body.text:
oṃ namo mūlaprakṛtaye
ajitāya mahātmane
body.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the Root-<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), to the unconquered, the great-souled;

body.text:
