anāśritāya devāya
niḥspṛhāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: to the unsupported god, to the desireless—homage, homage.

body.text:
nama ādyāya bījāya
śivāya ca praśāntāya
body.translated_text: Homage to the primal one, to the seed, to the auspicious, to the perfectly calm;

body.text:
ārṣeyāya pravartine
niścalāya yaśasvine
body.translated_text: to the descendant of seers, to the initiator, to the unmoving, to the glorious;

body.text:
anantarāya caikāya
sanātanāya pūrvāya
body.translated_text: to the one without another, to the one, to the eternal, to the ancient;

body.text:
avyaktāya namo namaḥ
purāṇāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: to the unmanifest—homage, homage; to the ancient one—homage, homage.

body.text: namo guhyāya gūḍhāya
body.translated_text: Homage to the secret, to the hidden;

body.text: guṇāyāguṇavartine
body.translated_text: to the qualified one who abides beyond the qualities;

body.text: atarkyāyāprameyāya
body.translated_text: to the unfathomable, to the immeasurable;

body.text: anantāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: to the infinite—homage, homage.

body.text: namo devātidevāya
body.translated_text: Homage to the god beyond the gods;

body.text: aprabhāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: to the lusterless [i.e. beyond ordinary radiance]—homage, homage.

body.text:
namo jagatprasthitāya
govindāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: Homage to the one established in the world, to <s>Govinda</s>—homage, homage.

body.text:
namo 'stu padmanābhāya
sāṃkhyayogodbhavāya ca
body.translated_text: Homage be to <s>Padmanābha</s>, and to the source of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>;

body.text:
viśveśvarāya devāya
śivāya haraye namaḥ
body.translated_text: to the god, lord of the universe, to the auspicious <s>Hari</s>—homage.

body.text:
namo 'stu tasmai devāya
nirguṇāya guṇātmane
body.translated_text: Homage be to that god, to the quality-less one who is the soul of the qualities,

body.text:
nārāyaṇāya viśvāya
devānāṃ paramātmane
body.translated_text: to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, to the universe, to the supreme soul of the gods.

body.text:
namo namaḥ kāraṇavāmanāya
nārāyaṇāyāmitavikramāya
śrīśārṅgacakrāsigadādharāya
namo 'stu tasmai puruṣottamāya
body.translated_text: Homage, homage to the cause, to the dwarf, to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> of measureless valor, to the bearer of <s>Śrī</s>, the <s>Śārṅga</s>-bow, discus, sword, and mace—homage be to that <s>Puruṣottama</s>.

body.text:
ādyāya vedanilayāya mahodarāya
siṃhāya daityanidhanāya caturbhujāya
brahmendrarudramunicāraṇasaṃstutāya
devottamāya varadāya namo 'cyutāya
body.translated_text: To the primal one, the abode of the <s>Vedas</s>, the great-bellied, to the lion [Narasiṃha], the destroyer of the <s>Daityas</s>, the four-armed, to the one praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the sages, and the <s>Cāraṇas</s>, to the best of gods, the boon-giver—homage to <s>Acyuta</s>.

body.text:
nāgendrabhogaśayanāsanasupriyāya
gokṣīrahemaśukanīlaghanopamāya
pītāmbarāya madhukaiṭabhanāśanāya
body.translated_text: To him whose dear seat and couch is the coiled body of the serpent-king, resembling cow's-milk, gold, a parrot, and a dark cloud, clad in yellow, the destroyer of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>,

body.text: viśvāya cārumukuṭāya namo 'kṣarāya
body.translated_text: to the universe, to the one with a beautiful diadem—homage to the imperishable.

body.text: bhaktipriyāya varadīptasudarśanāya
body.translated_text: To the lover of devotion, to the boon-giver of the blazing <s>Sudarśana</s> [discus],

body.text:
nābhiprajātakamalasthacaturmukhāya
kṣīrodakārṇavaniketayaśodhanāya
nānāvicitramukuṭāṅgadabhūṣaṇāya
sarveśvarāya varadāya namo varāya
body.translated_text: to him on whose lotus born from the navel stands the four-faced [Brahmā], to him whose abode is the ocean of milk, the purifier of glory, to him adorned with various wondrous diadem and armlets, to the lord of all, the boon-giver—homage to the excellent one.

body.text:
viśvātmane paramakāraṇakāraṇāya
phullāravindavimalāyatalocanāya
devendradānavaparīkṣitapauruṣāya
yogeśvarāya vijayāya namo varāya
body.translated_text: To the soul of the universe, to the cause of the supreme cause, to him of long pure eyes like blossomed lotuses, to him whose manhood is tested by <s>Indra</s> of the gods and the <s>Dānavas</s>, to the lord of <s>yoga</s>, to victory—homage to the excellent one.

body.text:
lokāyanāya tridaśāyanāya
brahmāyanāyātmabhavāyanāya
dharmāyanāyaikajalāyanāya
mahāvarāhāya sadā nato 'smi
body.translated_text: To the resort of the worlds, the resort of the thirty gods, the resort of <s>Brahmā</s>, the resort of the Self-born, the resort of <s>dharma</s>, the sole resort upon the [primal] waters, to the great Boar [Varāha]—I am ever bowed.

body.text:
acintyam avyaktam anantarūpaṃ
nārāyaṇaṃ kāraṇam ādidevam
yugāntaśeṣaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ
taṃ vāsudevaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye
body.translated_text: The inconceivable, the unmanifest, of infinite form, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the cause, the primal god, the remainder at the end of the aeon, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>—to that <s>Vāsudeva</s> I go for refuge.

body.text:
yogeśvaraṃ cāruvicitramaulim
ājñeyamaukhyaṃ prakṛteḥ parastham
kṣetrajñam ātmaprabhavaṃ vareṇyaṃ
taṃ vāsudevaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye
body.translated_text: The lord of <s>yoga</s>, of beautiful wondrous diadem, the foremost knowable, standing beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>, the knower of the field, self-arisen, most excellent—to that <s>Vāsudeva</s> I go for refuge.

body.text:
adṛśyam acchedyam anādimadhyaṃ
maharṣayo brahmavidaḥ sureśam
vadanti yaṃ vai puruṣaṃ sanātanaṃ
taṃ vāsudevaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye
body.translated_text: The invisible, the uncleavable, without beginning or middle, whom the great seers, knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, the lord of gods, declare to be the eternal <s>Puruṣa</s>—to that <s>Vāsudeva</s> I go for refuge.

body.text:
yad akṣaraṃ brahma vadanti sarvagaṃ
niśāmya yaṃ mṛtyumukhāt pramucyate
tam īśvaraṃ tṛptam anopamair guṇaiḥ
parāyaṇaṃ viṣṇum upaimi śāśvatam
body.translated_text: That which they call the imperishable, all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>, hearing of which one is released from the mouth of death—to that Lord, contented, of incomparable qualities, the supreme refuge, the eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I come.

body.text:
kāryaṃ kriyākāraṇam aprameyaṃ
hiraṇyanābhaṃ varapadmanābham
mahābalaṃ vedanidhiṃ surottamaṃ
vrajāmi viṣṇuṃ śaraṇaṃ janārdanam
body.translated_text: The effect, the cause of action, the immeasurable, the golden-naveled, the excellent <s>Padmanābha</s>, of great strength, the treasury of the <s>Vedas</s>, best of gods—to <s>Viṣṇu</s> I go for refuge, <s>Janārdana</s>.

body.text:
vicitrakeyūramahārhaniṣkaṃ
ratnottamālaṃkṛtasarvagātram
pītāmbaraṃ kāñcanabhakticitraṃ
mālādharaṃ keśavam abhyupaimi
body.translated_text: Him of wondrous bracelets and most precious neck-ornament, all his limbs adorned with the best of jewels, clad in yellow, variegated with golden tracery, the wearer of garlands—to <s>Keśava</s> I come.

body.text:
bhavodbhavaṃ vedavidāṃ variṣṭhaṃ
yogātmānaṃ sāṃkhyavidāṃ variṣṭham
ādityacandrāśvivasuprabhāvaṃ
prabhuṃ prapadye 'cyutam ātmabhūtam
body.translated_text: The source of existence, best of the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, the soul of <s>yoga</s>, best of the knowers of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, of the splendor of the sun, moon, <s>Aśvins</s>, and <s>Vasus</s>—to the Lord <s>Acyuta</s> who has become the [universal] self I go for refuge.

body.text:
śrīvatsāṅkaṃ mahādevaṃ
vedaguhyam anuttamam
prapadye sūkṣmam acalaṃ
bhaktānām abhayapradam
body.translated_text: The bearer of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, the great god, the secret of the <s>Vedas</s>, the unsurpassed—I go for refuge to the subtle, the unmoving, the giver of fearlessness to devotees.

body.text:
prabhavaṃ sarvalokānāṃ
nirguṇaṃ parameśvaram
prapadye muktasaṃgānāṃ
yatīnāṃ paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: The source of all the worlds, the quality-less supreme Lord—I go for refuge to the supreme goal of the ascetics whose attachments are released.

body.text:
bhagavantaṃ surādhyakṣam
akṣaraṃ puṣkarekṣaṇam
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ bhaktyā
prapadye brāhmaṇapriyam
body.translated_text: The Blessed One, the overlord of the gods, the imperishable, the lotus-eyed, the granter of refuge—with devotion I go for refuge to the refuge, the lover of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text:
trivikramaṃ trilokeśam
ādyam ekam anāmayam
bhūtātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ
prapadye madhusūdanam
body.translated_text: <s>Trivikrama</s>, the lord of the three worlds, the primal one, the one, the diseaseless, the soul of beings, the great-souled—I go for refuge to <s>Madhusūdana</s>.

body.text:
ādidevam ajaṃ śambhuṃ
vyaktāvyaktaṃ janārdanam
body.translated_text: The primal god, the unborn, <s>Śambhu</s>, the manifest-and-unmanifest, <s>Janārdana</s>,

body.text:
kṣetrajñaṃ puruṣaṃ yajñaṃ
triguṇātītam avyayam
nārāyaṇam aṇīyāṃsaṃ
prapadye parameśvaram
body.translated_text: the knower of the field, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the sacrifice, the one beyond the three <s>guṇas</s>, the imperishable, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the most subtle—I go for refuge to the supreme Lord.

body.text:
ekāya lokatrayāya
parataḥ paramātmane
namaḥ sahasraśirase
anantāya mahātmane
body.translated_text: To the one, to the three worlds, to the supreme soul beyond the beyond, homage to the thousand-headed, to the infinite, the great-souled.

body.text:
vareṇyam anaghaṃ devam
ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ
kīrtayanti ca yaṃ sarve
taṃ prapadye sanātanam
body.translated_text: The most excellent, the sinless god, whom the seers who have reached the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s> all proclaim—to that eternal one I go for refuge.

body.text:
namas te puṇḍarīkākṣa
bhaktānām abhayaprada
subrahmaṇya namas te 'stu
trāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam
body.translated_text: Homage to you, O lotus-eyed, giver of fearlessness to devotees; <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>, homage be to you; save me, who have come for refuge."

body.text:
bhaktiṃ tasyānusaṃcintya
nāgasyāmoghasaṃstavam
prītimān abhavad rājañ
śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ
sāṃnidhyaṃ kalpayām āsa
tasmin sarasi mādhavaḥ
body.translated_text: Meditating upon the devotion of that elephant, his unfailing hymn of praise, the bearer of conch, discus, and mace became gladdened, O king; <s>Mādhava</s> brought about his presence at that lake.

body.text:
grāhagrastaṃ gajaṃ taṃ ca
saṃgṛhya salilāśayāt
ujjahārāprameyātmā
tarasaivārisūdanaḥ
body.translated_text: And having grasped that elephant seized by the crocodile from the water-receptacle, the immeasurable-souled slayer of foes drew him up at once with swiftness.

body.text:
sthalasthaṃ dārayām āsa
grāhaṃ cakreṇa mādhavaḥ
mokṣayām āsa ca gajaṃ
pāśebhyaḥ śaraṇāgatam
body.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s> rent with his discus the crocodile placed on dry land, and released the elephant who had come for refuge from the nooses.

body.text:
sa hi devalaśāpena
hūhū gandharvasattamaḥ
gajatvam agamat kṛṣṇān
mokṣaṃ prāpya divaṃ gataḥ
śāpād vimuktaḥ sadyaś ca
gajo gandharvatāṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: For he, by the curse of <s>Devala</s>, was <s>Hūhū</s>, the best of <s>Gandharvas</s>, who had gone to the state of an elephant; having obtained release from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he went to heaven; freed from the curse at once, the elephant attained the state of a <s>Gandharva</s>.

body.text:
grāho 'pi yakṣatāṃ yāto
yaḥ kṛṣṇena nipātitaḥ
tasyāpi śāpamokṣo 'sau
jaigīṣavyakṛto 'bhavat
body.translated_text: And the crocodile too, who was struck down by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, attained the state of a <s>Yakṣa</s>; for him too that release from the curse was the one wrought by <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>.

body.text:
prītimāṃs trāti govindaḥ
sadyaḥ saṃsārasāgarāt
kruddho 'pi nighnan devatvam
arātīnāṃ prayacchati
body.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s>, gladdened, saves at once from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>; even when angered, slaying [his foes], he grants godhood to his enemies.

body.text:
tau ca svaṃ svaṃ vapuḥ prāpya
praṇipatya janārdanam
gandharvarāṭ tathā yakṣaḥ
parāṃ nirvṛtim āgatau
body.translated_text: And those two, having attained each his own form, having bowed to <s>Janārdana</s>—the <s>Gandharva</s>-king and the <s>Yakṣa</s>—came to supreme bliss.

body.text:
idaṃ caiva mahābāho
devadevo 'bhyabhāṣata
dṛṣṭvā muktau gajagrahau
bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ
body.translated_text: And this too, O mighty-armed one, the god of gods spoke, having seen the elephant and crocodile released, the Blessed <s>Madhusūdana</s>:

body.text:
yo grāhaṃ nāgarājaṃ ca
māṃ caiva praṇidhānavān
smariṣyati saraś cedaṃ
yuvayor mokṣaṇaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: "He who, with concentration, will remember the crocodile and the serpent-king [the elephant] and me, and this lake, and the release of you two,

body.text:
gulmaṃ kīcakaveṇūnāṃ
taṃ ca śailavaraṃ tathā
aśvatthaṃ bhāskaraṃ gaṅgāṃ
naimiṣāraṇyam eva ca
body.translated_text: the thicket of hollow bamboos, and that best of mountains, the <s>aśvattha</s> tree, the sun, the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the <s>Naimiṣa</s> forest—

body.text:
saṃsmariṣyanti ye martyāḥ
samyak śroṣyanti vāpi ye
na te duḥsvapnapāpasya
bhoktāro matparigrahāt
body.translated_text: those mortals who will remember [these], or who will rightly hear [of them], are not, by my grace, enjoyers of the sin of bad dreams.

body.text:
sarvapāpaiḥ pramokṣyante
kalyāṇānāṃ ca bhāginaḥ
bhaviṣyanti tathā puṇyāṃ
gatiṃ yāsyanti mānavāḥ
duḥsvapnaṃ ca nṛṇāṃ teṣāṃ
susvapnaṃ ca bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: They will be released from all sins, and become partakers of blessings; and men will likewise go to a holy destination; and the bad dream of those men will become a good dream."

body.text:
kaurmaṃ mātsyaṃ ca vārāhaṃ
vāmanaṃ tārkṣyam eva ca
nārasiṃhaṃ tathā rūpaṃ
sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakam
body.translated_text: [Remembering] the Tortoise, the Fish, the Boar, the Dwarf, and <s>Tārkṣya</s> [Garuḍa], and likewise the Man-Lion form, the maker of creation and dissolution—

body.text:
etāni prātar utthāya
saṃsmariṣyanti ye narāḥ
sarvapāpavinirmuktās
te yānti paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: Those men who, rising at dawn, shall remember these [names], freed from all sins, go to the supreme destiny

body.text:
evam uktvā tu rājendra
devadevo janārdanaḥ
aspṛśad gajagandharvaṃ
grāhayakṣaṃ ca taṃ tadā
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, O lord of kings, the god of gods <s>Janārdana</s> touched that elephant-gandharva and the crocodile-yakṣa then

body.text:
tena spṛṣṭāv ubhau sadyo
divyamālyāmbarānvitau
vimāne 'bhimate prāpya
jagmatus tridaśālayam
body.translated_text: Touched by him, both at once, endowed with divine garlands and garments, having attained a desired celestial car, went to the abode of the thirty gods

body.text:
tato devapatiḥ kṛṣṇo
mokṣayitvā gajottamam
ṛṣibhiḥ stūyamāno hi
guhyair vedapadākṣaraiḥ
gataḥ sa bhagavān viṣṇur
durvijñeyagatiḥ prabhuḥ
body.translated_text: Then the lord of the gods, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having liberated the best of elephants, being praised by the seers with the secret syllables of the Vedic verses—he, the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord whose course is hard to know, departed

body.text:
gajendramokṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā
sarve cendrapurogamāḥ
brahmāṇam agrataḥ kṛtvā
sarve prāñjalayo 'bhavan
body.translated_text: Having seen the liberation of the lord of elephants, all [the gods] led by <s>Indra</s>, having placed <s>Brahmā</s> in front, all became with folded hands

body.text:
vavandire mahātmānaṃ
prabhuṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim
vismayotphullanayanāḥ
prajāpatipuraḥsarāḥ
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ
prātar utthāya mānavaḥ
prāpnuyāt paramāṃ siddhiṃ
duḥsvapnas tasya naśyati
body.translated_text: They worshipped the great-souled Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>, their eyes wide with wonder, led by <s>Prajāpati</s>; the man who shall ever hear this, rising at dawn, would attain the supreme perfection, and his bad dream perishes

body.text:
gajendramokṣaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ
sarvapāpapramocanam
śrāvayet prātar utthāya
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: He should cause to be heard, rising at dawn, the holy liberation of the lord of elephants (<s>Gajendramokṣaṇa</s>), the releaser from all sins; he is freed from all sins

body.text:
śraddhayā hi kuruśreṣṭha
smṛtena kathitena ca
gajendramokṣaṇeneha
dīrgham āyur avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: By faith, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>, [whether] remembered or recounted, through this Gajendramokṣaṇa here one would attain long life

body.text:
mayā te kathitaṃ divyaṃ
pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam
kīrtayasva mahābāho
mahāduḥsvapnanāśanam
body.translated_text: By me has been told to you the divine, holy, sin-destroying [text]; proclaim it, O mighty-armed one, the destroyer of great bad dreams

body.text:
kīrtyamānaṃ ca viprebhyaḥ
śṛṇu bhaktyā yathoditam
body.translated_text: And when it is proclaimed to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, hear it with devotion as declared

body.text:
gajendramokṣaṇaṃ śrutvā
kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
bhīṣmād bhagīrathīputrāt
pūjayām āsa keśavam
body.translated_text: Having heard the Gajendramokṣaṇa, the son of <s>Kuntī</s>, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, from <s>Bhīṣma</s> the son of <s>Bhagīrathī</s> [Gaṅgā], worshipped <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
ye cāpi pāṇḍuputrasya
samīpasthā dvijottamāḥ
te 'pi bhīṣmasya pārśvasthaṃ
vāsudevaṃ praṇemire
body.translated_text: And those best of the twice-born too who were near the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, they too bowed to <s>Vāsudeva</s> who stood at <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s side

body.text:
varaṃ vareṇyaṃ varapadmanābhaṃ
nārāyaṇaṃ brahmanidhiṃ sureśam
taṃ devaguhyaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ
vavandire brahmavidāṃ variṣṭham
body.translated_text: The boon, the choicest, the excellent <s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the treasure of <s>Brahman</s>, the lord of the gods—that god-secret, ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>, the best of the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, they worshipped

body.text:
etat puṇyaṃ mahārāja
narāṇāṃ pāpakarmaṇām
duḥsvapnadarśane ghore
śrutvā pāpāt pramucyate
bhaktimān puṇḍarīkākṣe
gajo duḥkhād vimocitaḥ
body.translated_text: This is holy, O great king, for men of sinful deeds; on the sight of a terrible bad dream, having heard [it], one is freed from sin; the elephant, devoted to the lotus-eyed one, was released from misery

body.text:
tathā tvam api rājendra
prapadya śaraṇaṃ harim
vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ
prāpsyase paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: So you too, O lord of kings, going for refuge to <s>Hari</s>, freed from all sins, will attain the supreme destiny

body.text:
mahāmate mahāprājña
sarvaśāstraviśārada
akṣīṇakarmabandhas tu
puruṣo dvijasattama
body.translated_text: O greatly wise one, of great wisdom, skilled in all the <s>śāstras</s>, but [for] a man whose bondage of [past] deeds is not exhausted, O best of the twice-born—

body.text:
maraṇe yaj japañ japyaṃ
yac ca bhāvaṃ anusmaran
paraṃ padam avāpnoti
tan me vada mahāmune
body.translated_text: what recitation he should recite at death, and what state remembering, he attains the supreme abode—that tell me, O great sage

body.text:
śrīvatsāṅkaṃ jagadbījam
anantaṃ lokabhāvanam
purā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ
nāradaḥ paryapṛcchata
body.translated_text: Formerly <s>Nārada</s> questioned the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, the seed of the world, the endless, the creator of the world:

body.text:
bhagavan bhūtabhavyeśa
śraddadhānair jitendriyaiḥ
kathaṃ bhaktair vicintyo 'si
maraṇe pratyupasthite
body.translated_text: "O Blessed One, lord of past and future, how are you to be contemplated by the faithful, sense-conquering devotees when death is at hand?

body.text:
kiṃ vā japyaṃ japen nityaṃ
kalyam utthāya mānavaḥ
svapan vibudhyan dhyāyaṃś ca
tan me brūhi sanātana
body.translated_text: Or what recitation should a man ever recite, rising at dawn, sleeping, waking, and meditating—that tell me, O eternal one"

body.text:
śrutvā tasya tu devarṣer
vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
provāca bhagavān viṣṇur
nāradaṃ jagato gatiḥ
body.translated_text: Having heard the speech of that divine seer, the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, skilled in speech, the refuge of the world, spoke to <s>Nārada</s>:

body.text:
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi
mune divyām anusmṛtim
maraṇe yām anusmṛtya
prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: "Ah, I shall tell you, O sage, the divine recollection (<s>anusmṛti</s>), remembering which at death one attains the supreme destiny

body.text:
oṃkāram āditaḥ kṛtvā
mām anusmṛtya manmanāḥ
ekāgraprayato bhūtvā
idaṃ mantram udīrayet
body.translated_text: Placing the <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the start, having remembered me with mind on me, becoming one-pointed and restrained, he should utter this <s>mantra</s>:

body.text:
avyaktaṃ śāśvataṃ devam
anantaṃ puruṣottamam
prapadye prāñjalir viṣṇum
acyutaṃ parameśvaram
body.translated_text: 'I take refuge, with folded hands, in the unmanifest, eternal god, the endless <s>Puruṣottama</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, the supreme Lord

body.text:
purāṇaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇum
adbhutaṃ lokabhāvanam
prapadye puṇḍarīkākṣam
īśaṃ bhaktānukampinam
body.translated_text: I take refuge in the ancient, supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the wondrous, the creator of the world, the lotus-eyed Lord, compassionate to his devotees

body.text:
lokanāthaṃ prapanno 'smi
akṣaraṃ paramaṃ padam
bhagavantaṃ prapanno 'smi
bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhum
body.translated_text: I have gone for refuge to the Lord of the worlds, the imperishable supreme abode; I have gone for refuge to the Blessed One, the Lord of past, future, and present

body.text:
sraṣṭāraṃ sarvabhūtānām
anantabalapauruṣam
padmanābhaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ
papadye satyam avyayam
body.translated_text: I take refuge in the creator of all beings, of endless strength and prowess, <s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the true, the imperishable

body.text:
hiraṇyagarbhaṃ bhūgarbham
amṛtaṃ viśvatomukham
ābhāsvaram anādyantaṃ
prapadye bhāskaradyutim
body.translated_text: I take refuge in <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the womb of the earth, the immortal, facing all directions, shining, beginningless and endless, of the splendour of the sun

body.text:
sahasraśirasaṃ devaṃ
vaikuṇṭhaṃ tārkṣyavāhanam
prapadye sūkṣmam acalaṃ
vareṇyam abhayapradam
body.translated_text: I take refuge in the thousand-headed god, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, whose mount is <s>Tārkṣya</s> [Garuḍa], the subtle, the unmoving, the choicest, the giver of fearlessness

body.text:
nārāyaṇaṃ naraṃ haṃsaṃ
yogātmānaṃ sanātanam
śaraṇyaṃ sarvalokānāṃ
prapadye dhruvam īśvaram
body.translated_text: I take refuge in <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Nara</s>, the <s>Haṃsa</s>, the eternal one whose self is <s>yoga</s>, the refuge of all the worlds, the fixed Lord'

body.text:
yaḥ prabhuḥ sarvalokānāṃ
yena sarvam idaṃ tatam
body.translated_text: He who is the Lord of all the worlds, by whom all this is pervaded—

body.text:
carācaragurur devaḥ
sa no viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu
body.translated_text: the god, the teacher of the moving and unmoving—may that <s>Viṣṇu</s> be gracious to us

body.text:
yasmāj jātaḥ purā brahmā
padmayoniḥ pitāmahaḥ
prasīdatu sa no viṣṇuḥ
pitā mātā pitāmahaḥ
body.translated_text: From whom <s>Brahmā</s> the grandsire, the lotus-born, was born of old—may that <s>Viṣṇu</s> be gracious to us, father, mother, and grandsire

body.text:
yaḥ purā pralaye prāpte
naṣṭe loke carācare
ekas tiṣṭhati yogātmā
sa no viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu
body.translated_text: He who, of old, when dissolution had come and the world, moving and unmoving, was destroyed, alone remains, his self being <s>yoga</s>—may that <s>Viṣṇu</s> be gracious to us

body.text:
caturbhiś ca caturbhiś ca
dvābhyāṃ pañcabhir eva ca
hūyate ca punar dvābhyāṃ
sa no viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu
body.translated_text: He who is offered oblation with four [syllables] and four [syllables], with two and with five, and again with two—may that <s>Viṣṇu</s> be gracious to us

body.text:
parjanyaḥ pṛthivī sasyaṃ
kālo dharmaḥ kriyā phalam
guṇākaraḥ sa no babhrur
vāsudevaḥ prasīdatu
body.translated_text: The rain-cloud, the earth, the grain, time, <s>dharma</s>, action, and fruit—the mine of qualities, that tawny one, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, may he be gracious

body.text:
yogāvāsa namas tubhyaṃ
sarvāvāsa varaprada
yajñagarbha mahābhāga
pañcayajña namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: O abode of <s>yoga</s>, homage to you, abode of all, boon-giver; O womb of sacrifice, O greatly fortunate one, O five-sacrifices, homage be to you

body.text:
caturmūrte jagaddhāma
lakṣmyāvāsa varaprada
sarvāvāsa namas te 'stu
sākṣibhūta jagatpate
body.translated_text: O four-formed one, abode of the world, abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, boon-giver, abode of all, homage be to you, O witness-become, Lord of the world

body.text:
ajeya khaṇḍaparaśo
viśvamūrte vṛṣākape
trigarte pañcakālajña
namas te jñānasāgara
body.translated_text: O unconquerable one, axe-of-fragments [<s>Khaṇḍaparaśu</s>], O universe-formed, <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, O <s>Trigarta</s>, knower of the five times, homage to you, O ocean of knowledge

body.text:
avyaktād aṇḍam utpannam
avyaktādyaḥ paraḥ prabhuḥ
yasmāt parataraṃ nāsti
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: From the unmanifest the [cosmic] egg arose; he is the Lord supreme, prior to the unmanifest, than whom there is nothing higher—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
cintayanto hi yaṃ nityaṃ
brahmeśānādayaḥ prabhum
niścayaṃ nādhigacchanti
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: He whom <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and the rest, contemplating ever as the Lord, do not reach certainty about—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
jitendriyā mahātmāno
jñānadhyānaparāyaṇāḥ
yaṃ prāpya na nivartante
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: He whom the sense-conquering, great-souled ones devoted to knowledge and meditation, having attained, do not return [from]—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
ekāṃśena jagat sarvaṃ
yo 'vaṣṭabhya vibhuḥ sthitaḥ
agrāhyo nirguṇaḥ śāstā
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: He who, the pervading Lord, having propped up the whole world with a single portion, abides, ungraspable, quality-less, the chastiser—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
divākarasya saumyaṃ hi
madhye jyotir avasthitam
kṣetrajñam iti yaṃ prāhuḥ
sa mahātmā prasīdatu
body.translated_text: The gentle light which is established in the midst of the sun-maker [the sun's disc], whom they call the <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field)—may that great-souled one be gracious

body.text:
avyaktam anavasthāno
durvijñeyaḥ sanātanaḥ
āsthitaḥ prakṛtiṃ bhuṅkte
sa mahātmā prasīdatu
body.translated_text: The unmanifest, the stationless, the hard-to-know, the eternal, who, having taken his stand, enjoys <s>Prakṛti</s>—may that great-souled one be gracious

body.text:
kṣetrajñaḥ pañcadhā bhuṅkte
prakṛtiṃ bahubhir guṇaiḥ
manoguṇāṃś ca yo bhuṅkte
sa mahātmā prasīdatu
body.translated_text: The <s>Kṣetrajña</s> enjoys <s>Prakṛti</s> fivefold, with its many qualities; he who enjoys the qualities of the mind—may that great-souled one be gracious

body.text:
sāṃkhyā yogāś ca ye cānye
siddhāś caiva maharṣayaḥ
yaṃ viditvā vimucyante
sa mahātmā prasīdatu
body.translated_text: The followers of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, and others, the perfected ones and the great seers, knowing whom are liberated—may that great-souled one be gracious

body.text:
namas te sarvatobhadra
sarvato'kṣiśiromukha
nirvikāra namas te 'stu
sākṣibhūta hṛdi sthita
atīndriya namas tubhyaṃ
liṅgebhyas tvaṃ pramīyase
body.translated_text: Homage to you, O auspicious-on-all-sides, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side; O changeless one, homage be to you, O witness-become, abiding in the heart; O beyond-the-senses, homage to you, you are inferred from the marks

body.text:
ye tu tvāṃ nābhijānanti
saṃsāre saṃsaranti te
rāgadveṣavinirmuktaṃ
lobhamohavivarjitam
aśarīraṃ śarīrasthaṃ
samaṃ sarveṣu dehiṣu
body.translated_text: But those who do not know you wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>—[you] free of passion and hatred, devoid of greed and delusion, bodiless [yet] abiding in the body, the same in all embodied beings

body.text:
avyaktaṃ buddhyahaṃkārau
mahābhūtendriyāṇi ca
tvayi tāni na teṣu tvaṃ
teṣu tvaṃ tāni na tvayi
body.translated_text: The unmanifest, the intellect and the ego, the great elements and the senses—these are in you, [but] you are not in them; in them are you [yet] they are not in you

body.text:
sraṣṭā bhoktāsi kūṭastho
guṇānāṃ prabhur īśvaraḥ
akartā heturahitaḥ
prabhuḥ svātmany avasthitaḥ
body.translated_text: You are the creator, the enjoyer, the immovable, the Lord and master of the qualities; the non-doer, the cause without cause, the Lord, abiding in your own self

body.text:
namas te puṇḍarīkākṣa
punar eva namo 'stu te
īśvaro 'si jagannātha
kim ataḥ param ucyate
bhaktānāṃ yad dhitaṃ deva
tad dhyāya tridaśeśvara
body.translated_text: Homage to you, O lotus-eyed one; again and again homage be to you; you are the Lord, O Lord of the world; what higher than this is to be said? Whatever is beneficial for your devotees, O god, think of that, O lord of the thirty gods

body.text:
mā me bhūteṣu saṃyogaḥ
punar bhavatu janmani
ahaṃkāreṇa buddhyā vā
tathā sattvādibhir guṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: Let there not again be for me, in birth, conjunction with the elements, with ego or intellect, and likewise with the qualities beginning with <s>sattva</s>

body.text:
mā me dharmo hy adharmo vā
punar bhavatu janmani
viṣayair indriyair vāpi
mā me bhūyāt samāgamaḥ
body.translated_text: Let there not be for me again, in birth, <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s>; with sense-objects or with the senses let there not be for me a coming-together

body.text:
pṛthivīṃ yātu me ghrāṇaṃ
yātu me rasanā jalam
cakṣur hutāśanaṃ yātu
sparśo me yātu mārutam
body.translated_text: Let my smelling go to the earth, let my tasting go to the water, let my eye go to the fire, let my touch go to the wind

body.text:
śabdo hy ākāśam abhyetu
mano vaikārikaṃ tathā
ahaṃkāraś ca me buddhiṃ
tvayi buddhiḥ sametu ca
body.translated_text: Let sound go to the ether, and the mind to the source-of-modification; and let my ego [go] to the intellect, and let the intellect merge in you

body.text:
viyogaḥ sarvakaraṇair
guṇair bhūtaiś ca me bhavet
sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva
prakṛtiṃ praviśantu me
body.translated_text: Let there be for me separation from all the organs, the qualities, and the elements; let <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> enter into <s>Prakṛti</s> for me

body.text:
niṣkevalaṃ padaṃ caiva
prayāmi paramaṃ tava
ekībhāvas tvayaivāstu
mā me janma bhavet punaḥ
body.translated_text: And I go to your supreme, utterly absolute abode; let there be oneness with you alone; let there not be birth for me again

body.text:
namo bhagavate tasmai
viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave
tvanmanas tvadgatapṛāṇas
tvadbhaktas tvatparāyaṇaḥ
tvām evānusmare deva
maraṇe pratyupasthite
body.translated_text: Homage to that Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-powerful; with mind on you, my breath gone to you, your devotee, devoted to you, I remember you alone, O god, when death is at hand

body.text:
pūrvadehakṛtā ye me
vyādhayas te viśantu mām
ārdayantu ca duḥkhāni
pravimuñcāmi yad ṛṇam
body.translated_text: Whatever diseases were made by me through a former body, let them enter into me; let the sorrows torment [me]; I am releasing the debt that there is

body.text:
upatiṣṭhantu me rogā
ye mayā pūrvasaṃcitāḥ
anṛṇo gantum icchāmi
tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: Let the diseases which were heaped up by me before come upon me; free of debt I wish to go—that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
ahaṃ bhagavatas tasya
mama cāsau sureśvaraḥ
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi
sa ca me na praṇaśyati
body.translated_text: I am that Blessed One's, and that lord of the gods is mine; I do not perish from him, and he does not perish from me

body.text:
namo bhagavate tasmai
yena sarvam idaṃ tatam
tam eva ca prapanno 'smi
mama yo yasya cāpy aham
body.translated_text: Homage to that Blessed One by whom all this is pervaded; and to him I have gone for refuge, who is mine and whose I am'

body.text:
imām anusmṛtiṃ nityaṃ
vaiṣṇavīṃ pāpanāśanīm
svapañ jāgrat paṭhed yas tu
trisaṃdhyaṃ vāpi yaḥ smaret
body.translated_text: This eternal Vaiṣṇava recollection, the sin-destroyer, who shall recite sleeping or waking, or who shall remember it at the three twilights,

body.text:
maraṇe cāpy anuprāpte
yas tv imāṃ samanusmaret
api pāpasamācāraḥ
so 'pi yāti parāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: and when death too has come, who shall remember this—even one of sinful conduct, he too goes to the supreme destiny

body.text:
arcayann api yo devaṃ
gṛhe vāpi baliṃ dadet
juhvad agniṃ smared vāpi
labhate sa parāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: Even worshipping the god, or offering an oblation (<s>bali</s>) at home, or offering into the fire while remembering [it], he attains the supreme destiny

body.text:
paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāṃ
dvādaśyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
śrāvayec chraddadhānaṃs tu
ye cānye mām upāśritāḥ
body.translated_text: On the full-moon, the new-moon, and especially on the twelfth, one should cause it to be heard by the faithful, and by others who have taken refuge in me

body.text:
nama ity eva yo brūyān
madbhaktaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ
tasya syur akṣayā lokāḥ
śvapākasyāpi nārada
body.translated_text: He who, my devotee, endowed with faith, should say merely 'Homage,' for him the worlds would be imperishable—even for a dog-cooker, O <s>Nārada</s>

body.text:
kiṃ punar ye yajante māṃ
sādhavo vidhipūrvakam
dhyāyanti ca yathānyāyaṃ
te yānti paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: How much more those good ones who sacrifice to me according to rule, and meditate [on me] duly—they go to the supreme destiny

body.text:
aśvamedhasahasrāṇāṃ
yaḥ sahasraṃ samācaret
nāsau tat padam āpnoti
madbhaktair yad avāpyate
body.translated_text: He who would perform a thousand of a thousand horse-sacrifices does not attain that abode which is attained by my devotees

body.text:
iṣṭaṃ dattaṃ tapo 'dhītaṃ
vratāni niyamāś ca ye
sarvam etad vināśāntaṃ
jñānasyānto na vidyate
body.translated_text: Sacrifice offered, gift given, austerity, study, the vows and observances—all this ends in destruction; of knowledge there is no end

body.text:
tasmāt pradeyaṃ sādhubhyo
dharmyaṃ sattvābhayaṃkaram
dānādīny antavantīha
madbhakto nāntam aśnute
body.translated_text: Therefore the righteous, fear-removing-of-beings [gift] is to be given to the good; gifts and the rest are finite here; my devotee does not reach an end

body.text:
yo dadyād bhagavajjñānaṃ
kuryād vā dharmadeśanām
kṛtsnāṃ vā pṛthivīṃ dadyān
na tu tulyaṃ kathaṃcana
body.translated_text: He who would give the knowledge of the Blessed One, or make a teaching of <s>dharma</s>, or give the whole earth—[the latter] is in no way equal [to the former]

body.text:
kāntāravanadurgeṣu
kṛcchreṣv āpatsu saṃbhrame
dasyubhiḥ saṃniruddhaś ca
nāmabhir māṃ prakīrtayet
body.translated_text: In wildernesses, forests, and strongholds, in difficulties, calamities, and confusion, and hemmed in by brigands, one should proclaim me by [my] names:

body.text:
varāho rakṣatu jale
viṣameṣu ca vāmanaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Let <s>Varāha</s> protect [me] in the water, and <s>Vāmana</s> in rough places

body.text:
rāmo rāmaś ca rāmaś ca
trāyantāṃ dasyudoṣataḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, let them protect [me] from the danger of brigands

body.text:
aṭavyāṃ nārasiṃhas tu
sarvataḥ pātu keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: In the forest let <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, and on all sides let <s>Keśava</s> protect [me]'

body.text:
baddhaḥ parikaras tena
mokṣāya gamanaṃ prati
sakṛd uccāritaṃ yena
harir ity akṣaradvayam
body.translated_text: By him the girdle is bound for going toward liberation, by whom is once uttered the two syllables 'Hari'

body.text:
janmāntarasahasrāṇi
tapojñānasamādhibhiḥ
narāṇāṃ kṣīṇapāpānāṃ
kṛṣṇe bhaktiḥ prajāyate
gatvā gatvā nivartane
candrasūryādayo grahāḥ
adyāpi na nivartante
dvādaśākṣaracintakāḥ
na vāsudevāt param asti maṅgalaṃ
na vāsudevāt paramaṃ pavitram
na vāsudevāt param asti daivataṃ
na vāsudevaṃ praṇipatya sīdati
body.translated_text: Over thousands of births, through austerity, knowledge, and meditation, in men whose sin is exhausted devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> arises; going and going to setting, the moon, sun, and the other planets even today do not turn back [from the cycle], [whereas] those who contemplate the twelve syllables [do]; there is no auspiciousness higher than <s>Vāsudeva</s>, nothing more purifying than <s>Vāsudeva</s>, no deity higher than <s>Vāsudeva</s>; having bowed to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, one does not sink

body.text:
tasmān mām eva devarṣe
dhyāyasvātandritaḥ sadā
avāpsyasi tataḥ siddhiṃ
padaṃ drakṣyasi ca dhruvam
body.translated_text: Therefore meditate, O divine seer, on me alone, ever unwearied; thereby you will attain perfection, and you will surely behold [my] abode

body.text:
evaṃ sa devadevena
nāradaḥ pratibodhitaḥ
cakāra keśave bhaktiṃ
tasmāt tvaṃ kuru bhūpate
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Nārada</s>, awakened by the god of gods, made devotion to <s>Keśava</s>; therefore do you [the same], O lord of the earth

body.text:
yaḥ paṭhet parayā bhaktyā
sa gacched viṣṇusāmyatām
etat puṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ
dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam
body.translated_text: He who shall recite [it] with supreme devotion would go to equality with <s>Viṣṇu</s>; this is holy, sin-removing, blessed, the destroyer of bad dreams

body.text:
pāpaṃ praṇaśyate yena
puṇyaṃ yena vivardhate
yaj japan sugatiṃ yāti
śṛṇvaṃś ca mama tad vada
body.translated_text: That by which sin perishes, by which merit increases, reciting which one goes to a good destiny, and hearing which—tell that to me

body.text:
kaścid āsīd dvijadrogdhā
piśunaḥ kṣatriyādhamaḥ
parapīḍārucir duṣṭaḥ
svabhāvād eva nirghṛṇaḥ
body.translated_text: There was a certain injurer of the twice-born, a slanderer, a base <s>kṣatriya</s>, taking delight in tormenting others, wicked, pitiless by his very nature

body.text:
paribhūtāḥ sadā tena
pitṛdevadvijātayaḥ
paradāreṣu caivāsya
babhūvābhirataṃ manaḥ
body.translated_text: By him the fathers, the gods, and the twice-born were ever despised, and his mind was constantly enamoured of others' wives

body.text:
sa tv āyuṣi parikṣīṇe
jajñe ghoro niśācaraḥ
tena vai karmadoṣeṇa
svena pāpakṛtāṃ varaḥ
body.translated_text: But he, when his lifespan was exhausted, was born a dreadful night-roamer (<s>rākṣasa</s>), by that very fault of his own deeds, [he] the foremost of doers of sin

body.text:
krūrair eva tato vṛttiṃ
rākṣasatve viśeṣataḥ
cakāra karmabhiḥ pāpaḥ
sarvaprāṇivihiṃsakaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, especially in the state of a <s>rākṣasa</s>, the sinful one made his livelihood by cruel deeds, a slayer of all living beings

body.text:
tasya pāparatasyaivaṃ
jagmur varṣaśatāni vai
tena vai karmadoṣeṇa
nānyā vṛttir arocata
body.translated_text: Thus of him devoted to sin, hundreds of years passed by; by that very fault of his deeds, no other livelihood pleased him

body.text:
yad yat paśyati sattvaṃ sa
tat tad ādāya rākṣasaḥ
cakhāda puruṣavyāghra
bāhugocaram āgatam
body.translated_text: Whatever creature he sees, that the <s>rākṣasa</s> seizes and devours, O tiger among men, when it has come within range of his arms

body.text:
evaṃ tasyātiduṣṭasya
kurvataḥ prāṇināṃ vadham
jagāma sumahān kālaḥ
pariṇāmaṃ tathā vayaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, while that exceedingly wicked one wrought the slaying of living beings, a very long time passed, and his age [reached its] decline

body.text:
sa dadarśa tapasyantaṃ
tāpasaṃ saṃśritavratam
ūrdhvabāhuṃ mahābhāgaṃ
kṛtarakṣaṃ samantataḥ
body.translated_text: He saw an ascetic practicing austerity, devoted to his vow, with arms upraised, the greatly fortunate one, who had made a protective spell (<s>rakṣā</s>) on all sides

body.text:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa tu durbuddhir
brāhmaṇaṃ rākṣasādhamaḥ
samabhyadhāvad vegena
samādātuṃ cikhādiṣuḥ
body.translated_text: Seeing him, that evil-minded one, the basest of <s>rākṣasas</s>, rushed with speed at the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, wishing to seize and devour him

body.text:
tena rakṣā ca yā dikṣu
brāhmaṇenābhavat kṛtā
tayā nirastaṃ tad rakṣo
nipapātāvidūrataḥ
body.translated_text: But by that protective spell which the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> had made in [all] the directions, that <s>rākṣasa</s>, repelled, fell down not far off

body.text:
bhagavan kīdṛśīṃ rakṣāṃ
sa cakāra dvijottamaḥ
yayā nirdhūtavīryo 'sau
nirasto rajanīcaraḥ
body.translated_text: "O Blessed One, what kind of protective spell did that best of the twice-born make, by which, his might struck down, that night-roamer was repelled?"

body.text:
ekāgracitto govinde
taj japaṃs tatparāyaṇaḥ
tapaś cacāra vipro 'sau
praviṣṭo viṣṇupañjaram
body.translated_text: With single-pointed mind on <s>Govinda</s>, reciting that, devoted to him, that <s>vipra</s> practiced austerity, having entered the <s>Viṣṇupañjara</s> (Viṣṇu's cage/armour)

body.text:
viṣṇupañjaram icchāmi
śrotuṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
sadā sarvabhayebhyas tu
rakṣā yā paramābhavat
body.translated_text: "I wish to hear the <s>Viṣṇupañjara</s>, O best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>, which was ever the supreme protection from all dangers"

body.text:
tripuraṃ jaghnuṣaḥ pūrvaṃ
brahmaṇā viṣṇupañjaraḥ
śaṃkarasya kuruśreṣṭha
rakṣaṇāya nirūpitaḥ
body.translated_text: Formerly, when [Śiva] slew <s>Tripura</s>, the <s>Viṣṇupañjara</s> was devised by <s>Brahmā</s> for the protection of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>

body.text:
vāgīśena tu śakrasya
balaṃ hantuṃ prayāsyataḥ
tasya rūpaṃ pravakṣyāmi
tan nibodha mahīpate
body.translated_text: By the Lord of Speech [Brahmā], for [Śiva] who was about to go to destroy the army of <s>Śakra</s>—its form I shall declare; learn that, O lord of the earth

body.text:
viṣṇuḥ prācyāṃ sthitaś cakrī
viṣṇur dakṣiṇato gadī
pratīcyāṃ śārṅgadhṛg viṣṇur
viṣṇuḥ khaḍgī mamottare
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> the discus-bearer stands in the east; <s>Viṣṇu</s> the mace-bearer to the south; in the west <s>Viṣṇu</s> bearing the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow; <s>Viṣṇu</s> the sword-bearer to my north

body.text:
hṛṣīkeśo vikoṇeṣu
tacchidreṣu janārdanaḥ
kroḍarūpī harir bhūmau
narasiṃho 'mbare mama
body.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> in the intermediate corners; <s>Janārdana</s> in the gaps of those [corners]; <s>Hari</s> of boar-form on the earth [below]; <s>Narasiṃha</s> in the sky above me

body.text:
kṣurāntam amalaṃ cakraṃ
bhramaty etat sudarśanam
asyāṃśumālā duḥprekṣā
hantu pretaniśācarān
body.translated_text: This stainless discus <s>Sudarśana</s>, razor-edged, whirls about; its garland of rays, hard to look upon—may it slay the departed spirits and night-roamers

body.text:
gadā ceyaṃ sahasrārcir
udvamatpāvakolvaṇā
rakṣobhūtapiśācānāṃ
ḍākiṇīnāṃ ca nāśanī
body.translated_text: And this mace of a thousand flames, fierce with the fire it vomits forth, is the destroyer of <s>rākṣasas</s>, ghosts, <s>piśācas</s>, and <s>ḍākiṇīs</s>

body.text:
śārṅgavisphūrjitaṃ caiva
vāsudevasya madripūn
tiryaṅmanuṣyakūṣmāṇḍa-
pretādīn hantv aśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: And the twang of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow of <s>Vāsudeva</s>—may it slay my foes entirely: beasts, men, <s>kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, departed spirits, and the rest

body.text:
khaḍgadhārājvalajjyotsnā-
nirdhūtā ye samāhatāḥ
te yāntu saumyataṃ sadyo
garuḍeneva pannagāḥ
body.translated_text: Those who are smitten, scattered by the blazing moonlight of the sword's edge—may they at once become benign, like serpents [tamed] by <s>Garuḍa</s>

body.text:
ye kūṣmāṇḍās tathā yakṣā
ye daityā ye niśācarāḥ
pretā vināyakāḥ krūrā
manuṣyā jambhakāḥ khagāḥ
body.translated_text: Those <s>kūṣmāṇḍas</s> and <s>Yakṣas</s>, those <s>Daityas</s>, those night-roamers, the ghosts, the cruel <s>Vināyakas</s>, men, <s>Jambhakas</s>, birds,

body.text:
siṃhādayo ye paśavo
dandasūkāś ca pannagāḥ
sarve bhavantu te saumyāḥ
kṛṣṇaśaṅkharavāhatāḥ
body.translated_text: lions and other beasts, and biting serpents—may they all become benign, struck by the sound of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s conch

body.text:
cittavṛttiharā ye me
ye janāḥ smṛtihārakāḥ
balaujasāṃ ca hartāraś
chāyāvibhraṃśakāś ca ye
body.translated_text: Those who steal the workings of my mind, those people who steal [my] memory, and the stealers of [my] strength and vigour, and those who cause the loss of [my] shadow [vitality],

body.text:
ye copabhogahartāro
ye ca lakṣaṇanāśakāḥ
kūṣmāṇḍās te praṇaśyantu
viṣṇucakrarayāhatāḥ
body.translated_text: and those who are stealers of [my] enjoyments, and those who are destroyers of [my] auspicious marks—may those <s>kūṣmāṇḍas</s> perish, struck by the speed of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus

body.text:
buddhisvāsthyaṃ manaḥsvāsthyaṃ
svāsthyam aindriyakaṃ tathā
mamāstu devadevasya
vāsudevasya kīrtanāt
body.translated_text: May there be for me health of intellect, health of mind, and likewise health of the senses, from the proclaiming [of the name] of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the god of gods

body.text:
pṛṣṭhe purastān mama dakṣiṇottare
vikoṇagaś cāstu janārdano hariḥ
tad īḍyam īśānam anantam īśvaraṃ
janārdanaṃ praṇipatito na sīdati
body.translated_text: Behind, before, to my right and left, and in the corners, may <s>Janārdana</s> <s>Hari</s> be; having bowed to that praiseworthy, sovereign, endless Lord <s>Janārdana</s>, one does not sink down

body.text:
yathā paraṃ brahma haris tathā paraṃ
jagatsvarūpaś ca sa eva keśavaḥ
ṛtena tenācyutanāmakīrtanāt
praṇāśam etu trividhaṃ mamāśubham
body.translated_text: As <s>Hari</s> is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, so he, <s>Keśava</s>, is of the form of the universe; by that true proclaiming of the name of <s>Acyuta</s>, let my threefold misfortune go to destruction

body.text:
ity asāv ātmarakṣārthaṃ
nyastavān viṣṇupañjaram
tenāsādhyaḥ sa duṣṭānāṃ
babhūva nṛpa rakṣasām
body.translated_text: Thus, for the sake of self-protection, he set up the <s>Viṣṇupañjara</s>; by it he became unassailable by the wicked <s>rākṣasas</s>, O king

body.text:
etayārakṣayā rakṣo
nirdhūtaṃ bhuvi pātitam
japyāvasāne vipro 'sau
dadarśa vigataujasam
body.translated_text: By this protection the <s>rākṣasa</s> was repelled [and] cast down upon the earth; at the end of his recitation, that <s>vipra</s> saw [him] bereft of might

body.text:
dṛṣṭvā ca kṛpayāviṣṭaḥ
samāśvāsya niśācaram
papracchāgamane hetuṃ
taṃ cācaṣṭa yathātatham
kathayitvā ca tat sarvaṃ
rākṣasaḥ punar abravīt
body.translated_text: And seeing [him], filled with compassion, having consoled the night-roamer, he asked the reason for his coming; and [the rākṣasa] told it to him as it truly was; and having recounted all that, the <s>rākṣasa</s> spoke again:

body.text:
prasīda vipravarya tvaṃ
nirviṇṇasyātipāpinaḥ
pāpapraśamanāyālam
upadeśaṃ prayaccha me
body.translated_text: "Be gracious, O best of <s>vipras</s>; to me, despairing, an exceeding sinner, give an instruction sufficient for the calming of sin

body.text:
bahūni pāpāni mayā
kṛtāni bahavo hatāḥ
kṛtāḥ striyaś ca me bahvyo
vidhavā hataputrikāḥ
anāgasāṃ ca sattvānām
anekānāṃ kṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Many sins were done by me, many were slain; many women were made by me widows, their sons slain; and the destruction of many innocent creatures was wrought

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi viprarṣe
prasādāt tava suvrata
pāpasyāsya kṣayaṃ kartuṃ
kuru me dharmadeśanām
body.translated_text: I, such as I am, wish, O sage among <s>vipras</s>, by your grace, O you of good vows, to effect the destruction of this sin; give me the teaching of <s>dharma</s>"

body.text:
kathaṃ krūrasvabhāvasya
satas tava niśācara
sahasaiva samāyātā
jijñāsā dharmavartmani
body.translated_text: "How, for you who are of cruel nature, O night-roamer, has there suddenly come this desire to know the path of <s>dharma</s>?"

body.text:
tvām attum āgataḥ kṣipto
rakṣayā kṛtayā tvayā
tatsaṃsparśāc ca me brahman
sādhv etan manasi sthitam
body.translated_text: "Come to devour you, I was repelled by the protection you had made, and from the touch of it, O <s>brahman</s>, this good [intention] is fixed in my mind

body.text:
kā sā rakṣā na tāṃ vedmi
vedmi nāsyāḥ parāyaṇam
kiṃtv asyāḥ saṃgam āsādya
nirvedaṃ prāpitaṃ param
body.translated_text: What that protection is, I do not know; I do not know its supreme refuge; but having attained contact with it, I have been brought to supreme disgust [with my life]

body.text:
sa kṛpāṃ kuru dharmajña
mayy anukrośam āvaha
yathā pāpāpanodo me
bhavaty ārya tathā kuru
body.translated_text: Show compassion, O knower of <s>dharma</s>; bring forth pity for me; act, O noble one, in such a way that the removal of my sin may come about"

body.text:
ity evam uktaḥ sa muniḥ
sadayas tena rakṣasā
pratyuvāca mahābhāga
vimṛśya suciraṃ tadā
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by that <s>rākṣasa</s>, that sage, compassionate, replied, O greatly fortunate one, having reflected for a very long time then:

body.text:
yat tvam ātthopadeśārthaṃ
nirviṇṇaḥ svena karmaṇā
yuktam etan na pāpānāṃ
nivṛtter upakārakam
body.translated_text: "In that you, disgusted by your own deeds, speak for the sake of instruction—this is fitting; it is helpful for the cessation of sins

body.text:
kariṣye yātudhānānāṃ
na tv ahaṃ dharmadeśanām
tāṃs tvaṃ pṛccha dvijān saumya
ye vai pravacane ratāḥ
body.translated_text: But I shall not give the teaching of <s>dharma</s> to the <s>yātudhānas</s> [rākṣasas]; ask those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O gentle one, who are devoted to the exposition [of scripture]"

body.text:
evam uktvā yayau vipraś
cintām āpa ca rākṣasaḥ
kathaṃ pāpāpanodaḥ syād
ity asau vyākulendriyaḥ
body.translated_text: Having said this, the <s>vipra</s> went away, and the <s>rākṣasa</s> fell into thought: "How might there be a removal of sin?"—thus he, with senses agitated

body.text:
na tadā khādate sattvān
kṣudhā saṃpīḍito 'pi san
ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe tadā kāle
jantum ekam abhakṣayat
body.translated_text: Then he did not devour living beings, even though tormented by hunger; then at every sixth mealtime he ate but a single creature

body.text:
sa kadācit kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ
paryaṭan vipine vane
dadarśātha phalāhāram
agrataḥ kauśikaṃ dvijam
body.translated_text: Once, beset by hunger, wandering in a desolate forest, he saw before him a <s>Kauśika</s> twice-born [brāhmaṇa], living on fruits

body.text:
taṃ jagrāha ca bhakṣārthaṃ
ṣaṣṭhe kāle bubhukṣitaḥ
guror arthe phalāhāram
āgataṃ brahmacāriṇam
body.translated_text: And he seized him for the purpose of eating, hungry at the sixth mealtime—the <s>brahmacārin</s> who had come [bearing] fruit-food for the sake of his guru

body.text:
gṛhīto rakṣasā tena
sa tadā munidārakaḥ
nirāśo jīvite prāha
sāmapūrvaṃ niśācaram
body.translated_text: Seized by that <s>rākṣasa</s>, that young sage then, despairing of life, spoke to the night-roamer with conciliatory words first:

body.text:
bho bhadramukha yatkāryaṃ
gṛhīto 'ham iha tvayā
tad bravīhi yathātattvam
ayam asmy anuśādhi mām
body.translated_text: "O gracious-faced one, whatever the purpose for which I have been seized here by you, tell that as it truly is; here I am, instruct me

body.text:
ṣaṣṭhe kāle mamāhāraḥ
kṣudhitasya tvam āgataḥ
niḥśūkasyātipāpasya
nirghṛṇasya dvijadruhaḥ
body.translated_text: You have come [as] my food at the sixth mealtime, [I being] hungry—[the food] of one merciless, exceedingly sinful, pitiless, an injurer of the twice-born"

body.text:
yady avaśyaṃ tvayādhyāhaṃ
bhakṣaṇīyo niśācara
āyāsyāmi tad adyaiva
nivedya gurave phalam
body.translated_text: "If I must inevitably be eaten by you, O night-roamer, I shall come this very [moment], having presented the fruit to my guru

body.text:
gurumūle tad āgatya
yat phalagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam
mamātra niṣṭhāṃ prāptasya
tat pāpāya niveditam
body.translated_text: Having gone to the feet of my guru, [presenting] the gathering of fruit that was done [by me]—for me who have reached my end here, that has been offered for [the sake of avoiding] sin

body.text:
sa tvaṃ muhūrtamātraṃ mām
atraiva pratipālaya
nivedya gurave yāvad
ihāgacchāmy ahaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: So you, just for a moment, wait for me right here, while, having presented the fruit to my guru, I come back here"

body.text:
ṣaṣṭhe kāle na me brahman
kaścid grahaṇam āgataḥ
pramucyate nibodhaitad
iti me pāpajīvikām
body.translated_text: "At the sixth mealtime no one has come [as] a seizing [meal] for me, O <s>brahman</s>; understand this, [yet] he is released—such is my sinful livelihood

body.text:
eka evātra mokṣasya
tava hetuḥ śṛṇuṣva tam
muñcāmy aham asaṃdigdhaṃ
yadi tat kurute bhavān
body.translated_text: Here there is but one cause of your release; hear it; I release [you] without doubt, if your honour does that

body.text:
guror yan na virodhāya
yan na dharmoparodhakam
tat kariṣyāmy ahaṃ rakṣo
yan na vrataharaṃ mama
body.translated_text: That which is not in opposition to my guru, that which is not an obstruction to <s>dharma</s>, that I shall do, O <s>rākṣasa</s>, that which is not a destroyer of my vow"

body.text:
mayā nisargato brahmañ
jātidoṣād viśeṣataḥ
nirvivekena pāpena
pāpaṃ karma sadā kṛtam
body.translated_text: "By me, by nature, O <s>brahman</s>, [and] especially through the fault of birth, sin—a sinful deed—was always done without discrimination, by [me], a sinner

body.text:
ā bālyān mama pāpeṣu
na puṇyeṣu rataṃ manaḥ
tatpāpasaṃcayān mokṣaṃ
prāpnuyāṃ yena tad vada
body.translated_text: From childhood my mind has been devoted to sins, not to meritorious acts; by what means I might attain release from that accumulation of sin, tell that"

body.text:
yāni pāpāni karmāṇi
bālatvāc caritāni me
duṣṭāṃ yonim imāṃ prāpya
tanmuktiṃ kathaya dvija
body.translated_text: "Whatever sinful deeds were practiced by me through childishness, having attained this wicked birth—tell the release from that, O twice-born

body.text:
yady etad dvijaputra tvaṃ
mamākhyāsyasy aśeṣataḥ
tat kṣudhārtāt samārtas tvaṃ
niyataṃ mokṣam āpsyasi
body.translated_text: If you, O son of a twice-born, will tell me this entirely, then you, distressed by hunger and pain, will certainly attain release [from me]

body.text:
na caitat pāpaśīlo 'ham
adya tvāṃ kṣutpipāsitaḥ
ṣaṣṭhe kāle nṛśaṃsātmā
bhakṣayiṣyāmi nirghṛṇaḥ
body.translated_text: And I, of sinful disposition, today afflicted by hunger and thirst, at the sixth mealtime, of cruel self, pitiless, shall [otherwise] devour you"

body.text:
evam ukto munisutas
tena ghoreṇa rakṣasā
cintām avāpa mahatīm
aśaktas tad udīritum
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by that dreadful <s>rākṣasa</s>, the sage's son fell into great thought, unable to declare that

body.text:
vimṛśya suciraṃ vipraḥ
śaraṇaṃ jātavedasam
jagāma jñānadānāya
saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: Having reflected for a very long time, the <s>vipra</s> went for refuge to <s>Jātavedas</s> (the fire) for the giving of knowledge, having reached supreme doubt:

body.text:
yadi śuśrūṣito vahnir
guroḥ śuśrūṣaṇād anu
vratāni vā sucīrṇāni
saptārciḥ pātu māṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: "If the fire has been served [by me], following the service of my guru, or if my vows have been well-performed, then may the seven-flamed [fire] protect me

body.text:
na mātaraṃ na pitaraṃ
gauraveṇa yathā gurum
yathāham avagacchāmi
tathā māṃ pātu pāvakaḥ
body.translated_text: As I regard neither mother nor father with the reverence [I give] my guru, so may the fire protect me

body.text:
yathā guruṃ na manasā
karmaṇā vacasāpi vā
avajānāmy ahaṃ tena
pātu satyena pāvakaḥ
body.translated_text: As I do not, by mind, deed, or speech, disregard my guru—by that truth may the fire protect me"

body.text:
ity evaṃ śapathān satyān
kurvatas tasya tat punaḥ
saptārciṣā samādiṣṭā
prādurāsīt sarasvatī
sā covāca dvijasutaṃ
rākṣasagrahaṇākulam
body.translated_text: Thus, as he made these true oaths, again, commanded by the seven-flamed [fire], <s>Sarasvatī</s> appeared; and she spoke to the twice-born's son agitated by the rākṣasa's seizing:

body.text:
mā bhair dvijasutāhaṃ tvāṃ
mokṣayāmy atisaṃkaṭāt
body.translated_text: "Fear not, O son of a twice-born; I shall release you from this great peril

body.text:
yad asya rakṣasaḥ śreyo
jihvāgre 'haṃ sthitā tava
tat sarvaṃ kathayiṣyāmi
tato mokṣam avāpsyasi
body.translated_text: Whatever is the welfare of this <s>rākṣasa</s>, I, seated on the tip of your tongue, shall tell all that; thereby you shall attain release"

body.text:
adṛśyā rakṣasā tena
proktvetthaṃ taṃ sarasvatī
adarśanam itā so 'pi
dvijaḥ prāha niśācaram
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus to him, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, unseen by that <s>rākṣasa</s>, became invisible; and that twice-born too spoke to the night-roamer:

body.text:
śrūyatāṃ tava yac chreyas
tathānyeṣāṃ ca pāpinām
samastapāpaśuddhyarthaṃ
puṇyopacayadaṃ ca yat
body.translated_text: "Let it be heard, what is your welfare and likewise that of other sinners, for the purification of all sins and which grants the accumulation of merit

body.text:
prātar utthāya satataṃ
madhyāhne 'hnaḥ kṣaye 'pi vā
ayaṃ śastaḥ sadā jāpaḥ
sarvapāpopaśāntidaḥ
body.translated_text: Rising at dawn always, at midday, or at the close of day, this recitation is ever commended, the bestower of the calming of all sins:

body.text:
hariṃ kṛṣṇaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ
vāsudevaṃ janārdanam
praṇato 'smi jagannāthaṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, the Lord of the world—may he remove my sin

body.text:
viśveśvaram ajaṃ viṣṇum
aprameyaparākramam
praṇato 'smi prajāpālaṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to the Lord of the universe, the unborn <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of immeasurable prowess, the protector of creatures—may he remove my sin

body.text:
viṣṇum acyutam īśānam
anantam aparājitam
praṇato 'smi mahātmānaṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, the Sovereign, the endless, the unconquered, the great-souled one—may he remove my sin

body.text:
carācaraguruṃ nāthaṃ
govindaṃ śeṣaśāyinam
praṇato 'smi paraṃ devaṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to the teacher of the moving and unmoving, the Lord, <s>Govinda</s>, who sleeps upon <s>Śeṣa</s>, the supreme god—may he remove my sin

body.text:
govardhanadharaṃ dhīraṃ
gobrāhmaṇahite sthitam
praṇato 'smi gadāpāṇiṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to the bearer of <s>Govardhana</s>, the steadfast one, established in the welfare of cows and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the mace-handed one—may he remove my sin

body.text:
śaṅkhinaṃ cakriṇaṃ śāntaṃ
śārṅgiṇaṃ sragdharaṃ param
praṇato 'smi patiṃ lakṣmyāḥ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to the bearer of the conch, the discus, the tranquil one, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, the wearer of the supreme garland, the lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>—may he remove my sin

body.text:
dāmodaram udārākṣaṃ
puṇḍarīkākṣam avyayam
praṇato 'smi stutaṃ stutyaiḥ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to <s>Dāmodara</s>, of noble eyes, the lotus-eyed, the imperishable one, praised by those worthy of praise—may he remove my sin

body.text:
nārāyaṇaṃ naraṃ śauriṃ
mādhavaṃ madhusūdanam
praṇato 'smi dharādhāraṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Nara</s>, <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, the supporter of the earth—may he remove my sin

body.text:
keśavaṃ keśihantāraṃ
kaṃsāriṣṭanisūdanam
praṇato 'smi caturbāhuṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to <s>Keśava</s>, the slayer of <s>Keśin</s>, the destroyer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, the four-armed one—may he remove my sin

body.text:
śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ śrīśaṃ
śrīdharaṃ śrīniketanam
praṇato 'smi śriyaḥ kāntaṃ
sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: I am bowed to the one with <s>Śrīvatsa</s> on his chest, the lord of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, the abode of <s>Śrī</s>, the beloved of <s>Śrī</s>—may he remove my sin

body.text:
yam īśaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ
dhyāyanti yatayo 'kṣaram
vāsudevam anirdeśyaṃ
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: He whom, the Lord of all beings, the imperishable, the ascetics meditate upon, <s>Vāsudeva</s> the indefinable—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
samastālambanebhyo 'yaṃ
saṃhṛtya manaso gatim
dhyāyanti vāsudevākhyaṃ
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: Withdrawing the movement of the mind from all supports, [the ascetics] meditate upon him named <s>Vāsudeva</s>—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
sarvagaṃ sarvabhūtaṃ ca
sarvasyādhātam īśvaram
vāsudevaṃ paraṃ brahma
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: The all-pervading, being all things, the support of all, the Lord, <s>Vāsudeva</s> the supreme <s>Brahman</s>—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
paramātmānam avyaktaṃ
yaṃ prayānti sumedhasaḥ
karmakṣaye 'kṣayaṃ devaṃ
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: The Supreme Self, the unmanifest, to whom the wise proceed, the undecaying god at the destruction of [their] karma—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
puṇyapāpavinirmuktā
yaṃ praviśya punarbhavam
na yoginaḥ prāpnuvanti
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: He, having entered whom, the <s>yogins</s>, freed of merit and sin, do not attain rebirth—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
brahmā bhūtvā jagat sarvaṃ
sadevāsuramānuṣam
yaḥ sṛjaty acyuto devas
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: He who, having become <s>Brahmā</s>, creates the whole world with its gods, <s>asuras</s>, and men, the imperishable god <s>Acyuta</s>—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
brahmatve yasya vaktrebhyaś
caturvedamayaṃ vapuḥ
sūtaṃ prabho purā jajñe
tam asmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: In whose state of <s>Brahman</s>, from whose mouths, O Lord, the body made of the four <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Sūta</s> (the bard), was born of old—to him I have gone for refuge

body.text:
brahmarūpadharaṃ devaṃ
jagadyoniṃ janārdanam
sraṣṭṛtve saṃsthitaṃ sṛṣṭau
praṇato 'smi sanātanam
body.translated_text: The god bearing the form of <s>Brahmā</s>, the source of the world, <s>Janārdana</s>, established in the role of creator in creation—to that eternal one I am bowed down

body.text:
yaḥ pāti sṛṣṭaṃ ca vibhuḥ
sthitāv asurasūdanaḥ
tam ādipuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇato 'smi sanātanam
body.translated_text: He, the all-pervading, who protects what is created in maintenance, the slayer of <s>asuras</s>—to that first Person <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the eternal, I am bowed down

body.text:
dhṛtā mahī hatā daityāḥ
paritrātās tathāmarāḥ
yena taṃ viṣṇum ādyeśaṃ
praṇato 'smi sanātanam
body.translated_text: By whom the earth was upheld, the <s>Daityas</s> slain, and the immortals likewise rescued—to that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the primal Lord, the eternal, I am bowed down

body.text:
yajñair yajanti yaṃ viprā
yajñeśaṃ yajñabhāvanam
taṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇato 'smi sanātanam
body.translated_text: Whom the <s>vipras</s> worship with sacrifices, the lord of sacrifice, the bringer-about of sacrifice—to that sacrifice-Person <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the eternal, I am bowed down

body.text:
varṇāśramān sthitāv ādyo
yaḥ sthāpayati vartmani
tam ādipuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇato 'smi sanātanam
body.translated_text: The first one, who in maintenance establishes the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> upon the [right] path—to that first Person <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the eternal, I am bowed down

body.text:
kalpānte rudrarūpo yaḥ
saṃharaty akhilaṃ jagat
tam ādipuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇato 'smi janārdanam
body.translated_text: He who at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, in the form of <s>Rudra</s>, withdraws the entire world—to that first Person <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, I am bowed down

body.text:
pātālavīthībhūrādīṃs
tathā lokān bibharti yaḥ
tam antapuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇato 'smi janārdanam
body.translated_text: He who upholds the paths of <s>Pātāla</s>, the earth-worlds, and the [other] worlds—to that final Person <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, I am bowed down

body.text:
saṃbhakṣayitvā sakalaṃ
yathā sṛṣṭam idaṃ jagat
yo nṛtyaty atiraudrātmā
praṇato 'smi janārdanam
body.translated_text: Having devoured the whole of this world as it was created, he who dances, of exceedingly terrible nature—to [him], <s>Janārdana</s>, I am bowed down

body.text:
surāsurāḥ pitṛgaṇā
yakṣagandharvarākṣasāḥ
yasyāṃśabhūtā devasya
sarvagaṃ taṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: The gods and <s>asuras</s>, the hosts of ancestors, the <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>, who are portions of that god—to him, the all-pervading, I bow

body.text:
samastadevāḥ sakalā
mānuṣāṇāṃ ca jātayaḥ
yasyāṃśabhūtā devasya
sarvagaṃ taṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: All the gods entire and the races of men, who are portions of that god—to him, the all-pervading, I bow

body.text:
vṛkṣagulmādayo yasya
tathā paśumṛgādayaḥ
ekāṃśabhūtā devasya
sarvagaṃ taṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: Trees, shrubs, and the rest, and likewise cattle, beasts, and the rest, who are a single portion of that god—to him, the all-pervading, I bow

body.text:
yasmān nānyat paraṃ kiṃcid
yasmin sarvaṃ mahātmani
yaḥ sarvam avyayo 'nantaḥ
sarvagaṃ taṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: Than whom there is nothing else higher, in whom is all, the great soul, who is all, imperishable, infinite—to him, the all-pervading, I bow

body.text:
yathā sarveṣu bhūteṣu
sthāvareṣu careṣu ca
viṣṇur eva tathā pāpaṃ
mamāśeṣaṃ praṇaśyatu
body.translated_text: As <s>Viṣṇu</s> is in all beings, stationary and moving, so may my sin be utterly destroyed

body.text:
yathā viṣṇumayaṃ sarvaṃ
yat sarvendriyagocaram
yac ca jñānaparicchedyaṃ
pāpaṃ naśyatu me tathā
body.translated_text: As all is made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whatever is the range of all the senses, and whatever is to be discerned by knowledge—so may my sin be destroyed

body.text:
pravṛttaṃ ca nivṛttaṃ ca
karma viṣṇumayaṃ yathā
anekajanmakarmotthaṃ
pāpaṃ naśyatu me tathā
body.translated_text: As action both engaged (<s>pravṛtta</s>) and ceased (<s>nivṛtta</s>) is made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—so may my sin arising from the deeds of many births be destroyed

body.text:
yan niśāyāṃ tathā prātar
yac ca madhyāparāhṇayoḥ
saṃdhyayoś ca kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ
karmaṇā manasā girā
body.translated_text: Whatever sin was done at night and likewise at dawn, and whatever at midday and in the afternoon, and at the two twilights, by deed, by mind, by speech,

body.text:
tiṣṭhatā vrajatā yac ca
śayyāsanagatena ca
kṛtaṃ yad aśubhaṃ karma
kāyena manasā girā
body.translated_text: and whatever inauspicious deed was done standing, walking, or while lying on a bed or sitting on a seat, by body, by mind, by speech,

body.text:
ajñānato jñānato vā
vāsudevasya kīrtanāt
tat sarvaṃ vilayaṃ yātu
toyasthaṃ lavaṇaṃ yathā
body.translated_text: whether out of ignorance or knowingly—by the proclaiming of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, may all that go to dissolution, as salt placed in water

body.text:
paradāraparadravya-
vāñchādrohodbhavaṃ ca yat
paripīḍodbhavaṃ nindāṃ
kurvato yan mahātmanām
body.translated_text: And what arises from desire for another's wife and another's wealth, and from treachery, and the slander, born of harming, that I, [though] of great souls, commit,

body.text:
yac ca bhojye tathā peye
yac ca kaṇḍūyanādiṣu
tad yātu vilayaṃ toye
yathā lavaṇabhājanam
body.translated_text: and what [sin] there is in food and likewise in drink, and what in scratching and the like—may that go to dissolution in water, as a vessel of salt

body.text:
yad bālye yac ca kaumāre
yat pāpaṃ yauvane mama
vayaḥpariṇatau yac ca
yac ca janmāntareṣu me
body.translated_text: Whatever sin of mine [was done] in childhood, and in boyhood, and in youth, and in the ripening of age, and whatever in [my] other births,

body.text:
tan nārāyaṇagovinda-
harikṛṣṇeśakīrtanāt
prayātu vilayaṃ toye
yathā lavaṇabhājanam
body.translated_text: may that go to dissolution in water, as a vessel of salt, by the proclaiming of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord

body.text:
viṣṇave vāsudevāya
haraye keśavāya ca
janārdanāya kṛṣṇāya
namo bhūyo namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, to <s>Hari</s>, and to <s>Keśava</s>, to <s>Janārdana</s>, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, homage again, homage, homage

body.text:
idaṃ sārasvataṃ stotram
aśeṣāghavināśanam
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva
sarvapāpavināśanam
body.translated_text: This <s>Sārasvata</s> hymn (Sarasvatī's hymn) is the destroyer of all sins, for those who recite it and likewise hear it the destroyer of every sin

body.text:
idaṃ yaḥ prātar utthāya
praṇipatya janārdanam
japaty ekamanāḥ pāpaṃ
samastaṃ sa vyapohati
body.translated_text: He who, having risen at dawn and bowed to <s>Janārdana</s>, mutters this with single mind drives away all his sin

body.text:
yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ
sāyaṃ prātaḥ samāhitaḥ
japaty etan naraḥ puṇyaṃ
kṛtvā manasi keśavam
body.translated_text: But the man who, for a full year, at evening and dawn, concentrated, mutters this holy [hymn], having set <s>Keśava</s> in his mind—

body.text:
śārīraṃ mānasaṃ vāgjaṃ
jñānato 'jñānato 'pi vā
kṛtaṃ tena tu yat pāpaṃ
sapta janmāntarāṇi vai
body.translated_text: whatever sin done by him, of body, of mind, of speech, whether knowingly or unknowingly, for seven births indeed,

body.text:
mahāpātakam alpaṃ vā
tathā yac copapātakam
sakalaṃ nāśayaty etat
tathānyat puṇyam ṛcchati
body.translated_text: a great sin or a small one, and likewise what minor sin there is, all this it destroys, and likewise he attains other merit

body.text:
viprāya suviśiṣṭāya
tilapātrāṇi ṣoḍaśa
ahany ahani yo dadyāt
paṭhaty etac ca tat samam
body.translated_text: He who, day after day, should give sixteen vessels of sesame to a most excellent <s>vipra</s>, and he who recites this—that [merit] is equal

body.text:
aviplutamatiś cānte
saṃprāpya smaraṇaṃ hareḥ
viṣṇulokam avāpnoti
satyam etan mayoditam
body.translated_text: And at the end, of unshaken mind, having attained the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>, he attains the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—this is true, [as] declared by me

body.text:
yathainaṃ paṭhati nityaṃ
stavaṃ sārasvataṃ pumān
api pāpasamāyukto
mokṣaṃ prāpnoty asāv api
body.translated_text: Inasmuch as a man recites this <s>Sārasvata</s> hymn daily, even though joined with sin, he too attains liberation

body.text:
yathaitat satyam uktaṃ me
nātrālpam api vai mṛṣā
rākṣasagrastasarvāṅgaṃ
tathā mām eṣa muñcatu
body.translated_text: As this has been truly spoken by me, [with] not even a little falsehood here—so may this [rākṣasa] release me, all of whose limbs are seized by the rākṣasa

body.text:
evam uccārite muktaḥ
sa tadā tena rakṣasā
akāmena dvijo bhūyas
tam āha rajanīcaram
body.translated_text: When this was thus uttered, the twice-born was then released by that rākṣasa, unwilling [though it was]; and again he said to that night-ranger:

body.text:
etad bhadramukhākhyātaṃ
tava pātakanāśanam
viṣṇoḥ sārasvataṃ stotraṃ
yaj jagāda sarasvatī
body.translated_text: 'This, O fair-faced one, that has been declared—the destroyer of your sin, the <s>Sārasvata</s> hymn of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which <s>Sarasvatī</s> spoke,'

body.text:
hutāśanena prahitā
mama jihvāgrasaṃsthitā
jagādemaṃ stavaṃ viṣṇoḥ
sarvapāpapraśāntidam
body.translated_text: 'sent by the fire-bearer (<s>Agni</s>), established on the tip of my tongue, she spoke this hymn of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the giver of calming of all sin'

body.text:
anenaiva jagannāthaṃ
tvam ārādhaya keśavam
tataḥ pāpāpanodaṃ tu
stute prāpsyasi keśave
body.translated_text: 'By this very [hymn] worship the Lord of the world, <s>Keśava</s>; then, when <s>Keśava</s> is praised, you will attain the removal of sin'

body.text:
aharniśaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ
stavenānena rākṣasa
stauhi bhaktiṃ parāṃ kṛtvā
tataḥ pāpād vimokṣyase
body.translated_text: 'Day and night, O rākṣasa, praise <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> with this hymn, having made supreme devotion; then you will be freed from sin'

body.text:
stuto hi sarvapāpāni
nāśayiṣyaty asaṃśayam
bhaktyā rākṣasaśārdūla
sarvapāpaharo hariḥ
body.translated_text: 'For when praised, <s>Hari</s>, the remover of all sin, will destroy all sins without doubt, through devotion, O tiger among rākṣasas'

body.text:
tataḥ praṇamya taṃ vipraṃ
prasādya ca niśācaraḥ
śālagrāmaṃ mahārāja
tadaiva tapase yayau
body.translated_text: Then, having bowed to that <s>vipra</s> and propitiated him, the night-walker went at once, O great king, to <s>Śālagrāma</s> for austerity

body.text:
tatrāharniśam evaitaj
japañ japyaṃ narādhipa
devakriyāratir bhūtvā
tapas tepe sa rākṣasaḥ
body.translated_text: There, day and night muttering this thing-to-be-muttered, O lord of men, having become one delighting in the rites of the god, that rākṣasa performed austerity

body.text:
ārādhya ca jagannāthaṃ
sa tatra puruṣottamam
sarvapāpavinirmukto
viṣṇulokam avāptavān
body.translated_text: And having worshipped there the Lord of the world, the Supreme Person, freed from all sin, he attained the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
tathā tvam api rājarṣe
sarvapāpapraśāntidam
ārādhaya hṛṣīkeśaṃ
japan sārasvataṃ stavam
body.translated_text: So you too, O royal seer, worship <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the giver of calming of all sin, muttering the <s>Sārasvata</s> hymn

body.text:
ya etat paramaṃ stotraṃ
vāsudevasya mānavaḥ
paṭhiṣyati sa sarvebhyaḥ
pāpebhyo mokṣam āpsyati
body.translated_text: The man who shall recite this supreme hymn of <s>Vāsudeva</s> will attain liberation from all sins

body.text:
brahmann asāre saṃsāre
rogādivyāptamānasaḥ
śabdādilubdhaḥ puruṣaḥ
kiṃ kurvan nāvasīdati
body.translated_text: O <s>brahman</s>, in this worthless <s>saṃsāra</s>, his mind pervaded by disease and the rest, a man greedy for sound and the other [sense-objects]—doing what does he not sink down?

body.text:
sve mahimni sthitaṃ devam
aprameyam ajaṃ vibhum
śokamohavinirmuktaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god established in his own greatness, the immeasurable, unborn, all-pervading, freed from sorrow and delusion, one does not sink

body.text:
aprāṇacitikaṃ brahma
vedānteṣu prakāśitam
ādyaṃ puruṣam īśānaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the breathless, thoughtless <s>Brahman</s> revealed in the <s>Vedāntas</s>, the first Person, the Lord, one does not sink

body.text:
aśanādyair asaṃspṛṣṭaṃ
sevitaṃ yogibhiḥ sadā
sarvadoṣavinirmuktaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, untouched by food and the rest, ever served by yogins, freed from all faults, one does not sink

body.text:
dhāmatrayavinirmuktaṃ
suprabhātaṃ sunirmalam
niṣkalaṃ śāśvataṃ devaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, freed from the three abodes [states], of fair dawning [splendor], very stainless, partless, eternal—the god—one does not sink

body.text:
kṣarākṣaravinirmuktaṃ
janmamṛtyuvivarjitam
abhayaṃ satyasaṃkalpaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, freed from the perishable and imperishable, devoid of birth and death, fearless, of true resolve, one does not sink

body.text:
amṛtaṃ sādhanaṃ sādhyaṃ
yaṃ paśyanti manīṣiṇaḥ
jñeyākhyaṃ paramātmānaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the immortal, the means and the end, whom the wise behold, called the knowable, the Supreme Self, one does not sink

body.text:
atulaṃ sukhadharmāṇaṃ
vyomadehaṃ sanātanam
dharmādharmavinirmuktaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the incomparable, of the nature of bliss, with the sky for his body, eternal, freed from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, one does not sink

body.text:
vyāsādyair munibhiḥ sarvair
dhyānayogaparāyaṇaiḥ
arcitaṃ bhāvakusumair
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, worshipped with the flowers of [right] feeling by <s>Vyāsa</s> and all the other sages devoted to the yoga of meditation, one does not sink

body.text:
viṣṇvaṣṭakam idaṃ puṇyaṃ
yogināṃ prītivardhanam
yaḥ paṭhet parayā prītyā
sa gacched viṣṇusātmyatām
body.translated_text: This holy <s>Viṣṇvaṣṭaka</s> (the eight-versed hymn to Viṣṇu) increases the affection of yogins; he who recites it with supreme affection goes to identity with <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
etat puṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ
dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva
viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam
body.translated_text: This is holy, sin-removing, blessed, the destroyer of bad dreams; for those who recite and likewise hear it, [it is] the supreme greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
kurvan bhaktiṃ hṛṣīkeśe
mānavo bhṛgunandana
nirvāṇaṃ samavāpnoti
yādṛśaṃ tad vadasva me
body.translated_text: Making devotion toward <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, O delight of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, a man attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>—of what sort that is, tell me

body.text:
dṛśyante puruṣā bhaktim
udvahanto janārdane
tathāpy anekadehārti-
manastāpāturā mune
body.translated_text: Men are seen bearing devotion toward <s>Janārdana</s>, yet they are afflicted with the distress of many bodies and the burning of the mind, O sage

body.text:
smṛtamātraḥ surendrasya
yo 'rtihā madhusūdanaḥ
tasyāpi karmābhiratā
duḥkhabhājaḥ kathaṃ narāḥ
body.translated_text: Even of <s>Madhusūdana</s>, the remover of distress for the king of gods by mere remembrance—[even] of him, how do men devoted to [his] worship become sharers in misery?

body.text:
kaiś ca dānair jagatsvāmī
svāmī nārāyaṇo nṛṇām
upakārāya bhaktānāṃ
jāyate sa mahāmune
body.translated_text: And by what gifts does <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the master of the world, the master of men, become [a giver] for the benefit of [his] devotees, O great sage?

body.text:
tvadyukto 'yam anupraśno
mahārāja śṛṇuṣva tam
yathā pṛṣṭam idaṃ samyak
kathyamānaṃ yathākhilam
body.translated_text: This further-question is fitting for you, O great king; hear it—as it is rightly asked, [so it is] being told to you entirely

body.text:
pṛthivīṃ ratnasaṃpūrṇāṃ
yaḥ kṛṣṇāya prayacchati
tasyāpy anyamanaskasya
sulabho na janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: He who gives to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the earth filled with jewels—even for him, if his mind is on another, <s>Janārdana</s> is not easy to attain

body.text:
nārādhyate 'cyuto dānair
na homair bhāvavarjitaiḥ
aikātmyaṃ puruṣair yāti
tanmayair eva mādhavaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s> is not worshipped by gifts, nor by oblations devoid of [right] feeling; <s>Mādhava</s> comes to oneness only with those men who are made of him

body.text:
śrūyate ca purākhyāto
rājoparicaro vasuḥ
iyāja subahūn yajñāñ
śraddhāpūtena cetasā
body.translated_text: And it is heard that the king <s>Uparicara</s> <s>Vasu</s>, declared of old, offered very many sacrifices with a mind purified by faith

body.text:
sa vipraśāpād rājarṣiḥ
kasmiṃścit kāraṇāntare
ākāśacārī sahasā
praviveśa rasātalam
body.translated_text: That royal seer, through the curse of a <s>vipra</s>, in some other matter, while traveling through the sky, suddenly entered the nether world (<s>Rasātala</s>)

body.text:
rasātalam anuprāptas
tathāpi jagataḥ prabhum
tuṣṭāva tanmayo bhūtvā
divyair mantrair janārdanam
body.translated_text: Having reached the nether world, even so he praised the Lord of the world, having become made of him, <s>Janārdana</s>, with divine <s>mantras</s>

body.text:
devānām eṣa yajñāṃśair
yajvī pakṣavivardhanaḥ
cedirāḍ iti daityānāṃ
matir āsīd rasātale
body.translated_text: 'This one, sacrificing with the gods' shares of sacrifice, is an augmenter of [our] wing [enemies]; the king of the <s>Cedis</s>'—such was the thought of the <s>Daityas</s> in the nether world

body.text:
anena vividhair yajñais
tarpitas tridaśeśvaraḥ
jaghāna daityān vadhyo 'yaṃ
prāpto 'smadgocaraṃ ripuḥ
body.translated_text: 'By this one the lord of the thirty [gods] has been gratified with various sacrifices, [and so] has slain the <s>Daityas</s>; this enemy, fit to be killed, has come within our reach'

body.text:
iti saṃmantrya te daityāś
cedirājajighāṃsavaḥ
tatsamīpam anuprāptā
gṛhītavividhāyudhāḥ
body.translated_text: Thus having taken counsel, those <s>Daityas</s>, desiring to slay the king of the <s>Cedis</s>, reached his vicinity, having taken up various weapons

body.text:
paramāmarṣasaṃyuktās
tatas te cedipuṅgavam
hantuṃ na śekuḥ śastrais tu
yatnavanto 'pi pārthivam
body.translated_text: Joined with supreme fury, then those [Daityas], though making effort, were not able with their weapons to slay that bull of the <s>Cedis</s>, the king

body.text:
sa cāpi vasur āsīnaḥ
keśavārpitamānasaḥ
jajāpa mantram oṃkāraṃ
praṇavaṃ dvādaśākṣaram
body.translated_text: And that <s>Vasu</s>, seated, his mind offered to <s>Keśava</s>, muttered the <s>mantra</s>, the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the <s>praṇava</s> of twelve syllables
