body.text:
dadarśa ca sa viśveśaṃ
dhyānāvasthitamānasaḥ
kṛtvānyaviṣayatyāgi
cittam atyantaniścalam
body.translated_text: And he, his mind fixed in meditation, beheld the Lord of all, having made his mind, abandoning [all] other objects, exceedingly motionless

body.text:
prāg īśam akṣaraṃ dhyānaṃ
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jagadgurum
saṃcintya vāsudevākhyam
anirdeśyaṃ parāyaṇam
body.translated_text: First meditating on the imperishable Lord, [as] meditation, knowledge, the knowable, the Guru of the world, contemplating the one called <s>Vāsudeva</s>, indescribable, the supreme refuge,

body.text:
tato 'ntaryāmirupeṇa
prākṛtena ca saṃsthitam
brahmaviṣṇuśivānāṃ ca
svarūpaiḥ saṃsthitaṃ tridhā
body.translated_text: then [contemplating him] established in the form of the inner-controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) and in the form of primordial matter (<s>prākṛta</s>), established threefold in the forms of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,

body.text:
punaś ca devagandharva-
siddhādimanujādiṣu
sthāvarānteṣu bhūteṣu
sarveṣv eva samāsthitam
body.translated_text: and again established in all beings—gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>siddhas</s>, and the rest, and men and the rest, down to the stationary [plants]—

body.text:
dikṣv ambaradharābhūbhṛt-
toyavāyvanalādiṣu
dṛśyādṛśyeṣu caiveśaṃ
cintayām āsa pārthivaḥ
body.translated_text: in the directions, in the sky, the earth, the mountains, in water, wind, fire, and the rest, and in things visible and invisible, the king contemplated the Lord

body.text:
sarvatra dṛṣṭvā taṃ devam
ātmany api ca sarvagam
sarvaṃ ca tanmayaṃ dṛṣṭvā
virarāma samādhitaḥ
body.translated_text: Having seen that god everywhere, and all-pervading even in himself, and having seen all as made of him, he ceased [from activity], absorbed in <s>samādhi</s>

body.text:
indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu
pūrvavat sa narādhipaḥ
viniveśya tato 'paśyad
asurān udyatāyudhān
body.translated_text: Then that lord of men, having set the senses upon the sense-objects as before, beheld the <s>asuras</s> with weapons raised

body.text:
tān sa dṛṣṭvā gṛhītārghya
ekaikasyaiva pārthivaḥ
pādyapūrveṇa vidhinā
pūjayām āsa bhaktimān
body.translated_text: Having seen them, that king, taking the <s>arghya</s>, worshipped each one severally, full of devotion, by the procedure beginning with water-for-the-feet:

body.text:
prasādaṃ kuru bhadraṃ vo
bhagavāñ jagataḥ patiḥ
vāsudevo bhavān prāpto
mamānugrahakāmyayā
body.translated_text: 'Be gracious, blessings on you; the Blessed Lord of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [in the form of] you, has come out of desire to favor me'

body.text:
ity evaṃ cedirājo 'sāv
ekaikasya ca dānavān
pūjayām āsa pādyādi
nivedya vacasā tathā
body.translated_text: Thus that king of the <s>Cedis</s> worshipped each one of the <s>dānavas</s>, offering water-for-the-feet and the rest, and likewise with [this] speech

body.text:
te 'pi taṃ cedirājānaṃ
papracchur asurās tadā
kva vāsudevo 'tra vayaṃ
prāptā dākṣāyaṇīsutāḥ
body.translated_text: They too, the <s>asuras</s>, then asked that king of the <s>Cedis</s>: 'Where is <s>Vāsudeva</s>? We who have come here are the sons of <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> (Diti)'

body.text:
ity evaṃ vadato daityān
sa jagāda punar vasuḥ
praṇāmanamro rājendra
sarvadarśī mahāmatiḥ
body.translated_text: To the <s>Daityas</s> speaking thus, <s>Vasu</s> spoke again, bent low in obeisance, O king of kings, the all-seeing one of great mind:

body.text:
vāsudevo jagat sarvaṃ
yac ceṅgaṃ yac ca neṅgati
brahmādiṣu tṛṇānteṣu
sa evaiko jagadguruḥ
body.translated_text: '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is the whole world, whatever moves and whatever does not move; among [all beings] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, he alone is the one Guru of the world'

body.text:
ahaṃ bhavanto devādyā
manuṣyāḥ paśavaś ca ye
te 'pi devā jagaddhātur
vyatiriktā na keśavāt
body.translated_text: 'I, you, the gods and the rest, men and the beasts there are—those gods too of the supporter of the world are not separate from <s>Keśava</s>'

body.text:
tenaiva māyā vitatā
vaiṣṇavī bhinnadarśanī
tayā svāṅgeṣu devo 'sau
pradarśayati sarvaśaḥ
body.translated_text: 'By him alone is the <s>Vaiṣṇavī māyā</s> (the illusion of Viṣṇu) spread out, showing diverse appearances; by it that god displays in all ways within his own limbs [these forms]'

body.text:
tad yūyam aham anye ca
yac ca sthāvarajaṅgamam
vāsudevātmakaṃ sarvam
iti matvā namo 'stu vaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Therefore you, I, and others, and whatever is stationary and moving—knowing all to have <s>Vāsudeva</s> as its essence—homage be to you'

body.text:
ity uktās tena te daityā
na śaktā manujeśvaram
yatnavanto 'pi taṃ hantuṃ
prayayuḥ svān athālayān
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by him, those <s>Daityas</s>, not able, though making effort, to slay that lord of men, then went to their own abodes

body.text:
tataḥ purohitaṃ sarve
kāvyaṃ nītiviśāradam
sametya te yathāvṛttaṃ
sarvam asmai nyavedayan
body.translated_text: Then all of them, having gone to their domestic priest <s>Kāvya</s> (Śukra), skilled in statecraft, reported to him all that had happened, as it occurred:

body.text:
asmākam atyantaripur
ayaṃ prāpto rasātalam
devānām upakṛd brahman
yajvā cedipatir vasuḥ
body.translated_text: 'This one, our exceeding enemy, has reached the nether world, the benefactor of the gods, O <s>brahman</s>, the sacrificer, <s>Vasu</s> the lord of the <s>Cedis</s>'

body.text:
asmatpakṣakṣayāyaiṣa
devānāṃ pakṣavardhanaḥ
tatra yat pratipattavyaṃ
tan no brūhi mahāmate
body.translated_text: "This [king] is the increaser of the gods' party, for the destruction of our party; what is to be done in that matter, tell us, O greatly wise one"

body.text:
svagocaram ariḥ prāptaḥ
śatrupakṣopakārakaḥ
na hantavya itīdaṃ ko
nītimān pravadiṣyati
body.translated_text: "A foe has come within one's reach, [yet] he is a benefactor of the enemy's party—'he is not to be slain': who that is versed in statecraft would say this?"

body.text:
tasmāt pragṛhya divyāni
sarvāstrāṇy amarārdanāḥ
nipātayata taṃ gatvā
cedirājaṃ svagocare
body.translated_text: "Therefore, having taken up all the divine weapons, O tormentors of the immortals, having gone, strike him down—the Cedi king within his own domain"

body.text:
sarvam etan mahābhāga
tasminn asmābhir udyataiḥ
kṛtaṃ na śakito hantuṃ
niryatno 'pi hi pārthivaḥ
body.translated_text: "All this, O greatly fortunate one, was done by us, exerting ourselves against him; that king could not be slain, even though he made no effort [to resist]"

body.text:
kiṃ tad yogaphalaṃ tasya
kiṃ vā japaphalaṃ mune
tapaso vā muniśreṣṭha
vistarāt tad vadasva naḥ
body.translated_text: "What is that fruit of his <s>yoga</s>, or what the fruit of his recitation, O sage, or of his austerity, O best of sages? Tell us that in detail"

body.text:
nityaṃ saṃcintayaty eṣa
yogayukto janārdanam
sāsya rakṣā parā manye
ko hinasty acyutāśrayam
body.translated_text: "This [king] constantly contemplates <s>Janārdana</s>, joined in <s>yoga</s>; that, I think, is his supreme protection; who can harm one who has taken refuge in <s>Acyuta</s>?"

body.text:
kīrtitaḥ saṃsmṛto dhyātaḥ
pūjitaḥ saṃstutas tathā
aihikāmuṣmikīṃ rakṣāṃ
karoti bhagavān hariḥ
body.translated_text: "Praised, remembered, meditated upon, worshipped, and likewise lauded, the Blessed <s>Hari</s> makes protection in this world and the next"

body.text:
yad durlabhaṃ yad aprāpyaṃ
manaso yan na gocare
tad apy aprārthitaṃ dhyāto
dadāti madhusūdanaḥ
body.translated_text: "What is hard to obtain, what is unattainable, what is not within [reach of] the mind—even that, unasked, when meditated upon, <s>Madhusūdana</s> grants"

body.text:
śarīrārogyam arthāṃś ca
bhogāṃś caivānuṣaṅgikān
dadāti dhyāyatāṃ nityam
apavargaprado hariḥ
body.translated_text: "Bodily health and wealth and the attendant enjoyments <s>Hari</s>, the granter of final release, gives to those who meditate constantly"

body.text:
yad idaṃ cedirājānaṃ
hantum icchatha dānavāḥ
tad asya keśavāc cittam
upāyenāpanīyatām
body.translated_text: "This Cedi king whom you wish to slay, O <s>dānavas</s>—let his mind be drawn away from <s>Keśava</s> by a stratagem"

body.text:
tatas te tadvacaḥ śrutvā
dānavāḥ kurupuṅgava
brahmarūpapraticchannā
jagmur yatra sthito vasuḥ
body.translated_text: Then, having heard that word of his, the <s>dānavas</s>, O bull of the Kurus, concealed in the form of brahmins, went to where <s>Vasu</s> [the Cedi king] stood

body.text:
dadṛśus te mahātmānaṃ
praṇataṃ cedipuṅgavam
kṛtapūjaṃ jagaddhātur
vāsudevasya pārthivam
body.translated_text: They beheld that great soul, the bull of the Cedis, bowed down, having made worship of the world-supporter <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the king,

body.text:
saṃstutāv udyataṃ śāntaṃ
sarvatra samadarśinam
kṛṣṇārpitamanovṛttiṃ
jānubhyām avaniṃgatam
body.translated_text: engaged in praise, tranquil, regarding all things with an equal eye, his mental activity offered to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, gone down to the ground upon his knees

body.text:
tataḥ saṃśṛṇvatāṃ teṣāṃ
tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam
tannāmasmaraṇodbhūta-
pulakaś cedipuṅgavaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, while they listened, the bull of the Cedis, the hairs of his body bristling [with rapture] arisen from the remembrance of his name, praised <s>Madhusūdana</s>

body.text:
jagāda yaṃ sa rājarṣiḥ
stavaṃ kṛṣṇasya śaunaka
śṛṇvatāṃ dānavendrāṇāṃ
tan me pāpaharaṃ vada
body.translated_text: The hymn which that royal sage uttered of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Śaunaka</s>, while the lords of the <s>dānavas</s> listened—tell me that, the remover of sin

body.text:
śṛṇu yad devadevasya
viṣṇor adbhutakarmaṇaḥ
stotraṃ jagāda rājāsau
rasātalatalaṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: Hear the hymn of the god of gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s> of wondrous deeds, which that king, gone to the floor of the nether world, uttered:

body.text:
staumi devam ajaṃ nityaṃ
pariṇāmavivarjitam
avṛddhikṣayam īśānam
acyutaṃ parataḥ param
body.translated_text: "I praise the god, unborn, eternal, free of transformation, without growth or decay, the Lord, <s>Acyuta</s>, higher than the highest,"

body.text:
kalpanākṛtanāmānam
anirdeśyam ajaṃ vibhum
mūlahetum ahetuṃ tvāṃ
vāsudevaṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: "whose names are made by [our] imagining, who is indefinable, unborn, all-pervading—you, the root-cause, [yet] causeless, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, I bow to"

body.text:
paramārthaparair īśaś
cintyate yaḥ prajākaraiḥ
taṃ vāsudevam īśeśaṃ
namāmy adya guṇaṃ param
body.translated_text: "the Lord who is contemplated by those intent on the supreme reality, the makers of creatures—that <s>Vāsudeva</s>, Lord of lords, I bow to today, the supreme quality"

body.text:
yasmād idaṃ yatra cedam
idaṃ yo viśvam avyayam
taṃ vāsudevam amalaṃ
namāmi parameśvaram
body.translated_text: "He from whom is this [universe], in whom is this, who is this imperishable universe—that stainless <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the supreme Lord, I bow to"

body.text:
jñeyaṃ jñātāram ajaraṃ
bhoktāraṃ prakṛteḥ prabhum
puruṣasvarūpiṇaṃ devaṃ
nato 'smi puruṣaṃ param
body.translated_text: "the knowable, the knower, the ageless, the enjoyer, the lord of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the god in the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>—I am bowed to the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>"

body.text:
pradhānādiviśeṣānta-
svarūpam ajam avyayam
sthūlasūkṣmamayaṃ sarvaṃ-
vyāpinaṃ taṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: "whose nature ranges from <s>pradhāna</s> to the [last] particular, unborn, imperishable, consisting of the gross and the subtle, all-pervading—him I bow to"

body.text:
sraṣṭā pālayitā cānte
yaś ca saṃhārakārakaḥ
trayīmayaṃ taṃ triguṇaṃ
nato 'smi puruṣottamam
body.translated_text: "the creator, the preserver, and at the end the maker of dissolution, consisting of the threefold [Veda], having the three qualities—I am bowed to <s>Puruṣottama</s>"

body.text:
ābrahmasthāvarānte ca
yo jagaty atra saṃsthitaḥ
vyaktarūpī ca taṃ devaṃ
nato 'haṃ viṣṇum avyayam
body.translated_text: "who abides in this world from <s>Brahmā</s> to the stationary [things] at the end, and [is] of manifest form—I am bowed to that god, <s>Viṣṇu</s> the imperishable"

body.text:
namo namo 'stu te deva
jagatām īśvareśvara
paramārtha parācintya
vidhātaḥ parameśvara
body.translated_text: "Homage, homage be to you, O god, Lord of the lords of the worlds, supreme reality, beyond thought, O ordainer, supreme Lord"

body.text:
tvam ādir anto madhyaṃ ca
jagato 'sya jagatpate
jagat tvayi jagac ca tvaṃ
jagat tvatto jaganmaya
body.translated_text: "You are the beginning, the end, and the middle of this world, O Lord of the world; the world is in you, and you are the world; the world is from you, O world-consisting one"

body.text:
tavāgnir āsaṃ vasudhāṅghriyugmaṃ
nabhaḥ śiraś candraravī ca netre
samastalokā jaṭharaṃ bhujāś ca
diśaś catasro bhagavan namas te
body.translated_text: "Your fire was [my offering], your two feet the earth, the sky your head, the moon and sun your two eyes, all the worlds your belly and your arms, the four directions—O Lord, homage to you"

body.text:
yad bhūgataṃ yad gaganāntarāle
yad vā nabhasy akhilalokagaṃ ca
yat sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ paratas tato 'pi
yad asti yan nāsti ca tat tvam īśa
body.translated_text: "What is on the earth, what is in the middle region of the sky, or what in the heavens, pervading all worlds, what is gross, subtle, and beyond even that, what exists and what does not exist—that are you, O Lord"

body.text:
vedāś ca vedyaṃ ca bhagavān ananto
vedāntavedyaś ca samastaheto
vadanti tat tvā munayaḥ pareśaṃ
tvayi prasanne paramārthadṛśye
body.translated_text: "The <s>Vedas</s> and the knowable, the Blessed endless one, and the one knowable through <s>Vedānta</s>, the cause of all—the sages call you that, the supreme Lord, when you are gracious, [you who are] to be seen as the supreme reality"

body.text:
namo hṛṣīkeśa tavāprameya
namaś ca tubhyaṃ paramārthasāra
viṣṇo namas te 'stu parāpareśa
kṛṣṇācyutānanta jagannivāsa
body.translated_text: "Homage, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, immeasurable; and homage to you, essence of the supreme reality; <s>Viṣṇu</s>, homage be to you, Lord of the higher and lower, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, abode of the world"

body.text:
namo 'stu tubhyaṃ parameśvarāya
namas tathāntaḥkāraṇasthitāya
pradhānabhūtāya namaś ca tubhyam
vyaktasvarūpeṇa ca saṃsthitāya
body.translated_text: "Homage be to you, the supreme Lord, and likewise to him who abides in the inner organ, and homage to you who are [the source] of <s>pradhāna</s>, and to him who abides in a manifest form"

body.text:
saṃhṛtya viśvaṃ jalaśāyine namo
namaś ca te kaiṭabhasūdanāya
svanābhipadmodaraśāyine ca
brahmasvarūpopanatāya caiva
body.translated_text: "Homage to him who reclines on the waters, having withdrawn the universe, and homage to you, slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, and to him who reclines within the lotus of his own navel, and to him who has become embodied in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>"

body.text:
sraṣṭre namaḥ pālayitre sthitau ca
sarveśa tubhyaṃ puruṣottamāya
rudrāya cānte kṣayahetave te
nato 'smi saṃhārakarāya viṣṇo
body.translated_text: "Homage to the creator, to the preserver in [the world's] maintenance, O Lord of all, to you, <s>Puruṣottama</s>; and at the end [I] am bowed to you, <s>Rudra</s>, the cause of destruction, the maker of dissolution, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>"

body.text:
jaya prapannārtiharāprameya
jayāgnivasvaśvimaya prajeśa
rudrendracandrastuta devadeva
jayāmarāṇām ariśātanāya
body.translated_text: "Victory, O immeasurable remover of the affliction of those who take refuge! Victory, O lord of creatures, consisting of fire, the <s>Vasus</s>, and the <s>Aśvins</s>! O god of gods praised by <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the moon, victory to you, the destroyer of the foes of the immortals!"

body.text:
jitaṃ tvayā sarvaga sarvasāraṃ
sarvātmabhūtākhila vedavedya
jitaṃ jitākṣāmalacittadṛśya
carācarādhāra dharādhareḍya
body.translated_text: "Conquered by you, O all-pervading one, is the essence of all, O self of all, entire, knowable through the <s>Veda</s>; conquered, O you of conquered senses, to be seen by the stainless mind, support of the moving and unmoving, upholder of the earth, to be praised"

body.text:
yajñāśrayo yajñapumān aśeṣa
deveśa martyāsurayajñabhoktaḥ
tvam īḍyamāno 'bhimataṃ dadāsi
dharādhareśācyuta vāsudeva
body.translated_text: "the refuge of sacrifice, the sacrifice-Person, entire, Lord of gods, enjoyer of the sacrifice of mortals and <s>asuras</s>—you, being praised, grant the desired [boon], O upholder of the earth, Lord, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>"

body.text:
namas te devadeva tvaṃ
yathā pāsy akhilaṃ jagat
sthitau tathā samastebhyo
doṣebhyo māṃ samuddhara
body.translated_text: "Homage to you, god of gods; as you protect the entire world in [its] maintenance, so deliver me from all faults"

body.text:
kṛṣṇācyuta hṛṣīkeśa
sarvabhūteśa keśava
mahātmaṃs trāhi māṃ bhaktaṃ
vāsudeva prasīda me
body.translated_text: "O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, Lord of all beings, <s>Keśava</s>, O great soul, save me, [your] devotee; O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, be gracious to me"

body.text:
iti stotrāvasāne taṃ
cedirājaṃ tato 'surāḥ
jahasuḥ satalākṣepaṃ
procuś ca dvijarūpiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, at the end of the hymn, the <s>asuras</s> then laughed at that Cedi king with derision, and the ones in brahmin-form said:

body.text:
prājñaḥ kila prajāpālaś
cedirāṭ saṃśruto bhuvi
tas asya jñānam akhilaṃ
viparītārtham īdṛśam
body.translated_text: "Wise, indeed, [and] a protector of his people, the Cedi king is reputed on earth; but this entire knowledge of his is of such a perverse purport"

body.text:
kva vāsudevaḥ kva bhavān
imām antyāṃ daśāṃ gataḥ
yo bhavān vipraśāpena
rasātalatalāśrayaḥ
body.translated_text: "Where is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [and] where are you, gone to this last condition—you who, by a brahmin's curse, dwell on the floor of the nether world?"

body.text:
bhaviṣyati smṛto devas
trātā kila tavācyutaḥ
yo 'sāv āpyāyyate viprair
adhvareṣu haviḥsravaiḥ
body.translated_text: "That god, when remembered, will be your savior, indeed—<s>Acyuta</s>—he who is gratified by brahmins in sacrifices with the flowing of oblations"

body.text:
yo 'nyatras trāṇakāmo vā
yajñabhāgam abhīpsate
sa trātā tava govindo
bhaviṣyaty ativismayaḥ
body.translated_text: "He who elsewhere, desirous of protection, or longing for his sacrificial share, [exists]—that savior of yours, <s>Govinda</s>, will be a great marvel [indeed]!"

body.text:
yadā tvaṃ bhagavadbhakto
vipraśāpān nipātitaḥ
tadā sa vāsudevas te
kva gato 'lpaśruto 'vyayaḥ
body.translated_text: "When you, a devotee of the Lord, have been cast down by a brahmin's curse, then where has that <s>Vāsudeva</s> of yours gone—the little-renowned, imperishable one?"

body.text:
na vāsudevo na harir
na govindo na keśavaḥ
śāpaṃ dadatsu vipreṣu
paritrāṇaparo bhavet
body.translated_text: "Neither <s>Vāsudeva</s> nor <s>Hari</s>, nor <s>Govinda</s> nor <s>Keśava</s>, would be intent on saving [you] when brahmins gave the curse"

body.text:
sa tvam ārtapralāpebhyo
viramādya yadīcchasi
kubuddhim etāṃ saṃtyajya
svapauruṣaparo bhava
body.translated_text: "So you, today, if you wish, cease from these afflicted ravings; abandoning this evil thought, be intent on your own manliness"

body.text:
na vayaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
nānantaṃ nācyutaṃ harim
saṃśritā na ca sīdāmaḥ
svapauruṣam upāśritāḥ
body.translated_text: "We have not taken refuge in <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, nor <s>Ananta</s>, nor <s>Acyuta</s> <s>Hari</s>, and we do not sink, [for we are] relying on our own manliness"

body.text:
yady asmadvacanaṃ vīra
na mohena viśaṅkase
tadāśrayasva svaṃ vīryaṃ
parityajya vimūḍhatām
body.translated_text: "If, O hero, you do not, out of delusion, doubt our word, then rely on your own valor, abandoning this folly"

body.text:
ity udīritam ākarṇya
sa teṣāṃ cedipuṅgavaḥ
ajñānapaṭalacchannān
hṛdayena śuśoca tān
body.translated_text: Having heard this uttered by them, that bull of the Cedis grieved at heart for them, covered over by a film of ignorance,

body.text: uvāca cedirājo vai hṛdaye kṛtamatsaraḥ
body.translated_text: and the Cedi king spoke, having made the resentment in his heart [vanish]:

body.text:
aho moho 'yam eteṣām
ahaṃkārasamudbhavaḥ
yena sarveśvare viṣṇāv
eteṣām āvṛtā matiḥ
body.translated_text: "Alas, this delusion of theirs, arisen from egotism, by which the mind of these [men] toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of all, is veiled!"

body.text:
prakāśaṃ ca sa tān āha
dānavān prītipūrvakam
pāpatas tatparitrāṇaṃ
cikīrṣur vasudhādhipaḥ
body.translated_text: And openly he addressed those <s>dānavas</s> with affection, the lord of the earth desiring to make their deliverance from sin:

body.text:
maivaṃ bho bhagavadbhaktiṃ
kurudhvaṃ dvijasattamāḥ
saṃsārābdhau manuṣyāṇām
ekaḥ poto janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: "Not so, sirs! Practice devotion to the Blessed Lord, O best of the twice-born; in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> alone is the boat for men"

body.text:
yūyaṃ vayaṃ tathaivānye
tasya sarve vibhūtayaḥ
brahmādisthāvarāntaṃ hi
tasya devasya vistṛtiḥ
body.translated_text: "You, we, and likewise others—all are his manifestations; for, from <s>Brahmā</s> to the stationary [things] at the end, [all] is the extension of that god"

body.text:
sukhaduḥkhamayo nṝṇāṃ
vipākaḥ karmaṇāṃ ca yaḥ
saṃśuddhihetuḥ svacchandāt
so 'pi viprāḥ pravartate
body.translated_text: "That ripening of men's deeds, consisting of pleasure and pain, which is the cause of [their] purification—that too, O brahmins, proceeds by his own will"

body.text:
parīkṣāṃ ca jagannāthaḥ
karoty adṛḍhacetasām
narāṇām arthavidhvaṃsa-
nikāśeṣu janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: "And the Lord of the world makes a test of men of unsteady mind, <s>Janārdana</s>, in [situations] resembling the destruction of [their] aims"

body.text:
alpayatnena cāyānti
vimuktiṃ keśavāśrayāt
tadvighātāya śakrādyā
yatante vighnahetubhiḥ
body.translated_text: "And [men] come to liberation with little effort through reliance on <s>Keśava</s>; to thwart that, <s>Śakra</s> and the rest strive with causes of obstruction"

body.text:
yadā janārdane bhaktiṃ
vahan sīdati mānavaḥ
nirviṇṇacetāḥ śaithilyaṃ
manasaḥ kurute tadā
body.translated_text: "When a man bearing devotion to <s>Janārdana</s> sinks, then, his mind despondent, he makes a slackening of the mind"

body.text:
devānāṃ mahatī śaṅkā
bhaktiyuktā janārdane
muktibhājo bhaviṣyantīty
atas te paripanthinaḥ
body.translated_text: "The gods have a great fear: 'Those endowed with devotion to <s>Janārdana</s> will become partakers of liberation'—therefore they are the adversaries"

body.text:
prāyo bhavanti govinde
bhaktivyāghātahetavaḥ
vighnāś cittavighātā hi
vimuktiparipanthinaḥ
body.translated_text: "They generally become, [in respect] to <s>Govinda</s>, causes of the thwarting of devotion; for obstacles, the destroyers of the mind, are the adversaries of liberation"

body.text:
satyaṃ śatena vighnānāṃ
sahasreṇa tathā tapaḥ
vighnāyutena govinde
nṝṇāṃ bhaktir nivāryate
body.translated_text: "Truly, by a hundred obstacles, and austerity by a thousand, and devotion to <s>Govinda</s> by a myriad obstacles, is warded off in men"

body.text:
svaṃ cāpi karma puruṣaḥ
śubhāśubham upāgatam
bhuṅkte kim atra devasya
garhyate yena keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: "And a man enjoys his own deed, auspicious or inauspicious, that has come [to fruition]; what fault of the god is there in this, by which <s>Keśava</s> is to be blamed?"

body.text:
maryādāṃ ca kṛtāṃ tena
yo bhinatti sa mānavaḥ
na viṣṇubhakto mantavyaḥ
sādhu dharmārcano hariḥ
body.translated_text: "And the man who breaks the boundary [of conduct] made by him is not to be regarded as a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; <s>Hari</s> is well-worshipped by [right] <s>dharma</s>"

body.text:
na puṣpair na ca dhūpena
nopahārānulepanaiḥ
toṣaṃ prayāti govindaḥ
svakarmābhyarcito yathā
body.translated_text: "Not by flowers, nor by incense, nor by offerings and unguents does <s>Govinda</s> come to satisfaction, as [he does when] worshipped by one's own [proper] deeds"

body.text:
brāhmaṇā devadevena
mukhāt sṛṣṭā mahātmanā
devānām api saṃpūjya
bhūmidevā dvijottamāḥ
anuvṛttiḥ sadā kāryā
teṣāṃ varṇair anuvrataiḥ
body.translated_text: "The brahmins were created from his mouth by the god of gods, the great soul; worthy of worship even of the gods, the best of the twice-born are gods on earth; compliance with them is ever to be rendered by the [other] classes, following their vows"

body.text:
te pūjyās te namaskāryās
toṣaṇīyāś ca yatnataḥ
teṣu tuṣṭeṣv aśeṣāṇāṃ
devānāṃ prītir uttamā
body.translated_text: "They are to be worshipped, they are to be revered, and to be gratified with effort; when they are pleased, supreme is the delight of all the gods"

body.text:
teṣāṃ mayā yad ajñānāj
jñānād vā kṛtam apriyam
tenāpi tuṣṭa evāhaṃ
viṣṇor aṃśā dvijottamāḥ
body.translated_text: "Whatever displeasing thing was done to them by me out of ignorance or knowingly—by that too I am pleased indeed, [for you are] portions of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of the twice-born"

body.text:
kriyāvān mama poto 'yaṃ
bhūtalād yo rasātale
patitasyātibhīme 'smin
duruttāre bhavārṇave
body.translated_text: "This active boat of mine [carries me], who have fallen from the surface of the earth to the nether world, in this most dreadful, hard-to-cross ocean of existence"

body.text:
rasātalatalottāraṃ
na hi vāñchāmy ahaṃ dvijāḥ
saṃsāragartād uttāraṃ
vṛṇomy ārādhanād dhareḥ
body.translated_text: "I do not wish, O brahmins, for [mere] deliverance from the floor of the nether world; I choose deliverance from the pit of <s>saṃsāra</s> through the worship of <s>Hari</s>"

body.text:
yathāhaṃ nābhivāñchāmi
bhogān ārādhya keśavam
tena satyena viṣṇur me
sarvadoṣān vyapohatu
body.translated_text: "As I do not, having worshipped <s>Keśava</s>, long for enjoyments—by that truth may <s>Viṣṇu</s> remove all my faults"

body.text:
yathā na mātā na pitā
nātmā na suhṛdaḥ sutāḥ
kṛṣṇālāpāt priyatarās
tathā māṃ pātu keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: "As neither mother, nor father, nor self, nor friends, nor sons are dearer than talk of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—so may <s>Keśava</s> protect me"

body.text:
yathā viṣṇumayaṃ sarvam
etat paśyāmy ahaṃ jagat
tathā mama manodoṣān
aśeṣān sa vyapohatu
body.translated_text: "As I behold this whole world as consisting of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—so may he remove all the faults of my mind, without remainder"

body.text:
jātā viṣṇuvilomeṣu
bhavatsv api dayā mama
yathā tenādya satyena
bhavantaḥ santu tanmayāḥ
body.translated_text: "Compassion of mine has arisen even toward you, who are hostile to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; by that truth today may you become consisting of him"

body.text:
yathā nāhaṃ bhavaddveṣān
na saṃharṣād bravīmy aham
kṛpayaiva tathā sarve
bhavantaḥ santu tanmayāḥ
body.translated_text: "As I speak not out of hatred of you, nor out of joy [at your downfall], but out of compassion alone—so may you all become consisting of him"

body.text:
yo yo na bhakto govinde
tatra tatra kṛpā yathā
mamārivarge 'pi tathā
bhaktir vo 'stu janārdane
body.translated_text: "Whoever is not a devotee of <s>Govinda</s>, toward him [is] compassion as [shown]; so even toward the host of my foes, may there be devotion of yours to <s>Janārdana</s>"

body.text:
evam uccārite teṣāṃ
daityānāṃ tatkṣaṇāt tathā
tasmin rājany abhūn maitrī
tathānyeṣu ca jantuṣu
body.translated_text: When this was thus uttered, of those <s>daityas</s>, at that very instant, there arose friendliness toward that king and likewise toward other creatures,

body.text:
devadeve 'py abhūd bhaktir
bhāvo naṣṭas tathāsuraḥ
svarūpadhāriṇaś cainaṃ
praṇamyāsurapuṅgavāḥ
pratyūcuḥ pārthivaṃ viṣṇu-
bhaktaṃ sadbrahmacāriṇam
body.translated_text: and there arose devotion even to the god of gods; their <s>asura</s>-nature was thus destroyed; and bearing their own forms, those bulls among the <s>asuras</s>, having bowed to him, replied to the king, the devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the true <s>brahmacārin</s>:

body.text:
cedibhūpāla bhadraṃ te
bhavato 'tulavikrama
saṃsāre tvatsamaiḥ saṅgaḥ
puṇyabhājāṃ pravartate
body.translated_text: "O lord of the Cedis, blessing upon you, of unequalled prowess; in <s>saṃsāra</s>, association with [those] equal to you arises [only] for those who partake of merit"

body.text:
vayaṃ svajātidoṣeṇa
devapakṣavirodhinaḥ
bhavantam āgatā hantuṃ
devaprīṇanatatparam
body.translated_text: "We, through the fault of our own birth-nature, hostile to the party of the gods, came to slay you, who are intent on the gratification of the gods"

body.text:
yadā na śaktito hantum
asmābhis tvaṃ nirāyudhaḥ
viṣṇudhyānamahārakṣā-
kakṣāntaragataḥ prabho
body.translated_text: "When you could not be slain by us, [you being] without weapons, gone within the enclosure of the great protection that is the meditation upon <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O Lord—"

body.text:
tyājayadbhis tathā bhaktiṃ
keśavād iti darśitam
vaiphalyam atipuṇyeṣu
viṣṇuśuśrūṣaṇā nṛṇām
body.translated_text: "by us seeking to make [you] abandon devotion to <s>Keśava</s>, it was [instead] shown [to us]: the fruitlessness, among the greatly meritorious, of [attempts to disrupt] men's service of <s>Viṣṇu</s>"

body.text:
sa tvaṃ devātidevasya
viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ
anugrāhyo yathā teyam
acyute niścalā matiḥ
body.translated_text: "You are one to be favored by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god above gods, of immeasurable splendor, as [shown by] this unwavering mind of yours toward <s>Acyuta</s>"

body.text:
diṣṭyā krodhābhibhūtānām
asmākaṃ tvannivarhaṇe
matir jātā yataḥ prāptā
tvatsaṅgād durlabhā matiḥ
body.translated_text: "By [good] fortune, in us, overcome by anger at your destruction, a [right] mind has arisen, since from association with you the hard-to-get mindset has been attained"

body.text:
kuruṣva ca prasādaṃ tvaṃ
praṇatānāṃ nareśvara
śatrāv api kṛpāśīlaṃ
yan no duṣṭam abhūn manaḥ
body.translated_text: "And do you, O lord of men, show grace to [us] who bow down, [we] whose mind was wicked toward you, [yet you] of compassionate disposition even toward a foe"

body.text:
diśāṃ vaimalyaṃ vimalaṃ
cakṣuṣaś copapāditam
bhavatā duṣṭatāṃ etām
āsurīm apamārjatā
body.translated_text: The clearness of the directions, pure, and of the eye too has been brought about by you, who wipe away this wicked, demonic nature of ours.

body.text:
duṣṭāḥ sma varṣapūgāni
yad yātāni vṛthaiva naḥ
viṣayākṣiptacittānāṃ
kṛṣṇe bhaktim akurvatām
body.translated_text: We have been wicked, in that these heaps of years of ours have passed in vain, for us whose minds were dragged off by sense-objects, who made no devotion toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
karmabhūmau manuṣyāṇāṃ
tad eva viphalaṃ dinam
yad acyutakathālāpa-
dhyānārcārahitaṃ gatam
body.translated_text: In the field-of-action of men, that very day is fruitless which has passed devoid of converse about <s>Acyuta</s>, and of meditation and worship.

body.text:
ity uktvā te 'surā bhūyaḥ
prasādya ca tathā vasum
viṣṇau bhaktiparā yātās
tīvrasaṃyogino 'layan
body.translated_text: Having said this, those <s>asuras</s>, having again propitiated <s>Vasu</s>, went their way devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, freed [from delusion], [now] of intense union.

body.text:
sa cāpi cedirāṭ tasmād
devadevena cakriṇā
pātālād uddhṛtaḥ paścāt
saṃsāragahanād api
body.translated_text: And that king of <s>Cedi</s> too was afterward, by the god of gods the discus-bearer, drawn up from the netherworld, and from the dense thicket of <s>saṃsāra</s> as well.

body.text:
ity etat sarvam ākhyātaṃ
yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
yathāvasīdanti narā
bhaktimanto 'pi keśave
body.translated_text: Thus all this has been related, which you ask of me—how men, even though devoted, are brought low in regard to <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
dṛḍhā janārdane bhaktir
yadaivāvyabhicāriṇī
tadā kiyat svargasukhaṃ
saiva nirvāṇahetukī
body.translated_text: When devotion to <s>Janārdana</s> is firm and unwavering, then how [great] is the happiness of heaven? That very [devotion] is the cause of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (final release).

body.text:
ity etad asuraiḥ sārdhaṃ
saṃvādaṃ yaḥ purā vasoḥ
paṭhiṣyaty akhilaṃ bhaktyā
sa tallokam upaiṣyati
body.translated_text: He who, with devotion, will recite this entire dialogue of old, of <s>Vasu</s> with the <s>asuras</s>, he will attain that [Viṣṇu's] world.

body.text:
jagatprabhuṃ devadevam
aśeṣeśam janārdanam
praṇipatyāham etaṃ tvāṃ
yat pṛcchāmi tad ucyatām
body.translated_text: Having bowed to the Lord of the world, the god of gods, the lord of all, <s>Janārdana</s>—what I ask of you, let that be told:

body.text:
yair upāyaiḥ pradānair vā
narāṇām amarārcitaḥ
prītimān puṇḍarīkākṣo
bhavaty ācakṣva tan mama
body.translated_text: By what means or gifts of men does the lotus-eyed one, worshipped by the immortals, become gladdened—tell that to me.

body.text:
ye svadharme sthitā varṇā
viprādyāḥ kurunandana
vidharmeṣu na vartante
prītimāṃs teṣu keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: Those classes—<s>vipras</s> and the rest, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>—who, established in their own <s>dharma</s>, do not engage in contrary practices: toward them <s>Keśava</s> is gladdened.

body.text:
brahmacārigṛhasthādyā
na cyavanty āśramāc ca ye
svadharmato haris teṣāṃ
prītimān eva sarvadā
body.translated_text: Those <s>brahmacārins</s>, householders, and the rest who do not fall from their stage of life—toward them <s>Hari</s> is ever gladdened on account of their own <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
ye na dambhena vartante
narā bhūteṣv alolupāḥ
tyaktagrāmyādisaṃgāś ca
teṣu prītiḥ parā hareḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who do not act with hypocrisy, who are not greedy toward beings, who have given up village [worldly] attachments and the rest—toward them is the supreme love of <s>Hari</s>.

body.text:
dātāro nāpahartāraḥ
parasvānām amāyinaḥ
ye narās teṣu govindaḥ
putreṣv iva sadā hitaḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who are givers, not takers of others' property, free of guile—toward them <s>Govinda</s> is ever benevolent as toward sons.

body.text:
yeṣāṃ narāṇāṃ na matir
jihvā vāsatyam ujjhati
te priyā vāsudevasya
ye ca dvijaparāyaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men whose mind and whose tongue do not abandon truth—they are dear to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and those who are devoted to the twice-born.

body.text:
karmaṇā manasā vācā
ye na hiṃsānuvartinaḥ
te narā vāsudevasya
priyāḥ pāṇḍukulodvaha
body.translated_text: Those men who, by deed, mind, and speech, are not followers of injury—those men are dear to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O upholder of the <s>Pāṇḍu</s> lineage.

body.text:
sarvadeveṣu ye viṣṇuṃ
sarvabhūteṣv avasthitam
manyante vāsudevasya
te priyāḥ putravat sadā
body.translated_text: Those who regard <s>Viṣṇu</s> as abiding in all the gods and in all beings—they are dear to <s>Vāsudeva</s> ever, like sons.

body.text:
brahmādyaṃ sthāvarāntaṃ ca
bhūtagrāmaṃ janārdanāt
ye ca paśyanty abhedena
te viṣṇoḥ satataṃ priyāḥ
body.translated_text: And those who behold the host of beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the unmoving, as not different from <s>Janārdana</s>—they are ever dear to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
devavedadvijātīnāṃ
nindāyāṃ ye na mānavāḥ
prītibhājo bhavantīṣṭās
te sadā śārṅgadhanvinaḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who are not [engaged] in the slander of the gods, the <s>Vedas</s>, and the twice-born—they become partakers of love, dear ever to the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow.

body.text:
priyāṇām atha sarveṣāṃ
devadevasya sa priyaḥ
āpatsv api sadā yasya
bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī
body.translated_text: Now, of all the dear ones, that one is dear to the god of gods whose devotion, even in calamities, is ever unwavering.

body.text:
tasmāt priyatvaṃ kṛṣṇasya
vāñchatā nijadharmajaiḥ
guṇair ātmā sadā yojyo
na dūre guṇino hariḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, by one desiring the dearness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the self is ever to be joined with the qualities born of one's own <s>dharma</s>; <s>Hari</s> is not far from the virtuous.

body.text:
yeṣāṃ na gṛddhiḥ pārakye
dāre dravye ca cetasaḥ
hiṃsāyāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ
te kṛṣṇenāvalokitāḥ
body.translated_text: Those whose minds have no craving for another's wife and property, nor [inclination] toward the injury of men—they are looked upon [with favor] by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ smṛtayo
yeṣāṃ sanmārgasevinām
paropakārasaktānāṃ
te kṛṣṇenāvalokitāḥ
body.translated_text: Those for whom the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>smṛtis</s> are the authority, who serve the good path, who are intent on benefiting others—they are looked upon by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
kalikalmaṣadoṣeṇa
yeṣāṃ nopahatā matiḥ
pāṣaṇḍānugatā naiva
te kṛṣṇenāvalokitāḥ
body.translated_text: Those whose intellect is not stricken by the fault of the defilement of the <s>Kali</s> [age], who do not follow heretics—they are looked upon by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
yeṣāṃ kleśo guror arthe
devaviprodbhavo 'pi vā
na vivitsāsamudbhūtas
te kṛṣṇenāvalokitāḥ
body.translated_text: Those whose effort is for the sake of the teacher, or arising in [service of] gods and <s>vipras</s>, and is not born of [self-serving] desire-to-know—they are looked upon by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
svapantaḥ saṃsthitā yāntas
tiṣṭhantaś ca janārdanam
ye cintayanty avirataṃ
te kṛṣṇenāvalokitāḥ
body.translated_text: Those who, sleeping, sitting, going, and standing, meditate ceaselessly upon <s>Janārdana</s>—they are looked upon by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
yathātmani tathāpatye
yeṣāṃ adrohiṇī matiḥ
samastasattvajāteṣu
te kṛṣṇenāvalokitāḥ
body.translated_text: Those whose mind is non-malicious—as toward oneself, so toward offspring—in regard to all the classes of living beings—they are looked upon by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
devapūjām anudinaṃ
guruviprārthasatkriyām
ye kurvanti narā viddhi
te kṛṣṇenāvalokitāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who daily perform the worship of the god, and honorable service for the sake of teacher and <s>vipra</s>—know them to be looked upon by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
suvarṇaṃ ratnam athavā
pārakyaṃ vijane vane
vilokya naiti yo lobhaṃ
taṃ avaihi hareḥ priyam
body.translated_text: He who, beholding gold or a jewel belonging to another in a lonely forest, comes not to greed—know him to be dear to <s>Hari</s>.

body.text:
devān pitṝṃs tathāpannān
atithīñ jāmayo 'dhvagān
yo bibharti vijānīhi
taṃ naraṃ bhagavatpriyam
body.translated_text: He who supports the gods, the ancestors, the afflicted, guests, kinswomen, and travelers—know that man to be dear to the Blessed One.

body.text:
na krodham eti kruddhebhyaḥ
sahate yo nirākriyām
taṃ vijānīhi bhartavyaṃ
devadevasya śārṅginaḥ
body.translated_text: He who comes not to anger toward the angry, who endures disrespect—know him to be supported by the god of gods, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s>.

body.text:
paralokapratīkāra-
karaṇāya sadodyamam
kurvann ālakṣyatām eti
keśavenāvalokitaḥ
body.translated_text: Ever making effort to bring about the counter-measure [provision] for the next world, [such a one] comes to be regarded, looked upon by <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
nātmasaṃstavam anyeṣāṃ
na nindāṃ cārthalipsayā
karoti puruṣavyāghra
yasya nārāyaṇo hṛdi
body.translated_text: He in whose heart is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> makes no self-praise, nor slander of others out of desire for gain, O tiger among men.

body.text:
sarvabhūtadayāṃ satyam
akrodhaṃ dharmaśīlatām
bhajante puruṣā deve
govinde hṛdaye sthite
body.translated_text: Men resort to compassion toward all beings, to truth, to freedom from anger, to a righteous character, when the god <s>Govinda</s> abides in the heart.

body.text:
na kalau na paradravye
paradārāśritā matiḥ
narāṇāṃ jāyate rājan
govinde hṛdayasthite
body.translated_text: Neither in [the vices of] the <s>Kali</s> [age], nor toward another's property, nor toward another's wife does the mind of men incline, O king, when <s>Govinda</s> abides in the heart.

body.text:
kṣamāṃ karoti kruddheṣu
dayāṃ mūḍheṣu mānavaḥ
mudaṃ ca dharmaśīleṣu
govinde hṛdaye sthite
body.translated_text: A man practices forbearance toward the angry, compassion toward the deluded, and joy toward those of righteous character, when <s>Govinda</s> abides in the heart.

body.text:
yadā bibhety adharmāder
dharmādīṃś ca yadecchati
tadā kuruvaraśreṣṭha
naraḥ kṛṣṇena vīkṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: When one fears unrighteousness and the rest, and desires righteousness and the rest, then, O best of the chief <s>Kurus</s>, that man is regarded by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
putradāragṛhakṣetra-
dravyāder mamatāṃ naraḥ
nāyāsyati jagannāthe
hṛṣīkeśe parāṅmukhe
body.translated_text: A man will not come to the sense of 'mine' toward son, wife, house, field, property, and the rest, when the Lord of the world <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> is averted [from him].

body.text:
kalau kṛtayugaṃ teṣāṃ
kleśās teṣāṃ sukhādhikāḥ
yeṣāṃ śarīragrahaṇe
hariśuśrūṣaṇe matiḥ
body.translated_text: For those in whose taking-on of a body the mind is on the service of <s>Hari</s>, in the <s>Kali</s> [age] there is the <s>Kṛta</s> age; their afflictions are surpassed by happiness.

body.text:
yadā necchati pāpāni
yadā puṇyāni vāñchati
jñeyas tadā manuṣyeṇa
hṛdaye 'sya hariḥ sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: When one desires not sinful deeds, when one wishes for meritorious ones, then it is to be known by a man that <s>Hari</s> abides in his heart.

body.text:
paramārthe matiḥ puṃsām
asāre tu bhavārṇave
kathaṃ bhavati rājendra
viṣvaksena parāṅmukhe
body.translated_text: How does the mind of men [turn] to the supreme truth, in the worthless ocean of existence, O lord of kings, when <s>Viṣvaksena</s> is averted [from them]?

body.text:
śraddadhāno dayāśīlaḥ
samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ
parārthe mānavaḥ kṛṣṇe
prasanne nṛpa jāyate
body.translated_text: A man becomes faithful, compassionate by nature, equal toward clod, stone, and gold, [devoted] to the welfare of others, O king, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is pleased.

body.text:
vahato 'pi sadā kṛṣṇe
bhaktim avyabhicāriṇīm
pāṇiṣv asamadṛgbuddheḥ
sulabho naiva keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: Even for one ever bearing unwavering devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in his hands [i.e. in act], <s>Keśava</s> is by no means easily attained for one whose understanding is not of equal vision.

body.text:
ye dāmbhikā bhinnavṛttā
ye ca dharmadhvajocchrayāḥ
durlabho bhagavān devas
teṣāṃ suyatatām api
body.translated_text: Those who are hypocritical, of broken conduct, and who raise high the banner of <s>dharma</s> [for show]—the Blessed god is hard to attain for them, even though they strive well.

body.text:
kāmalobhāśritaṃ yeṣāṃ
cittaṃ krodhādidūṣitam
teṣāṃ janmasahasre 'pi
na matiḥ keśavāśrayā
body.translated_text: Those whose mind is given over to desire and greed, sullied by anger and the rest—for them, even in a thousand births, the mind takes no refuge in <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
heyāṃ kṛṣṇāśrayāṃ vṛttiṃ
manyante hetusaṃśritāḥ
aviyopahatajñānā
ye 'jñāne jñānamāninaḥ
body.translated_text: Those who, relying on [mere] causes, regard the way of life taking refuge in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as fit to be abandoned, whose knowledge is struck by ignorance, who fancy themselves knowing amid ignorance,

body.text:
vedavādavirodhena
kūṭayuktim apāśritāḥ
ye keśavas taddhṛdaye
na kadācit priyātithiḥ
body.translated_text: who, in contradiction to the teaching of the <s>Vedas</s>, rely on false reasoning—in their heart <s>Keśava</s> is never a dear guest.

body.text:
mānuṣaṃ taṃ manuṣyatve
manyamānāḥ kubuddhayaḥ
karmāṇi ye 'sya nindanti
na teṣāṃ niṣkṛtir nṛṇām
body.translated_text: Those of evil understanding who, regarding him in his human form as [merely] human, slander his deeds—for those men there is no expiation.

body.text:
kecid vadanti taṃ devaṃ
manuṣyaṃ cālpamedhasaḥ
tiryaktvaṃ cāpare viṣṇuṃ
māyayā tasya mohitāḥ
body.translated_text: Some, of little wisdom, call that god a human, and others [call] <s>Viṣṇu</s> [merely] an animal, deluded by his <s>māyā</s> (magic power).

body.text:
devatvam api kṛṣṇasya
yasya nindā mahātmanaḥ
stutiṃ tasya kathaṃ śaktāḥ
kartum īśasya mānavāḥ
body.translated_text: He whose slander is [made] even of the godhood of the great-souled <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—how are men able to make praise of that Lord?

body.text:
vyāpitvaṃ śāśvatatvaṃ ca
janmabhāvavivarjitam
yadāsya procyate kāsya
stutir arthe tathā sthitau
body.translated_text: When his all-pervasiveness, his eternity, free of birth and existence, is proclaimed, of what is the praise, and where its abiding [object]?

body.text:
sarveśvareśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
procyate yadi paṇḍitaḥ
tathāpi svalpam evoktaṃ
bhūtārthe katamā stutiḥ
body.translated_text: If a learned man declares <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the Lord of all lords, even then that is said but slightly; in the matter of the real, what praise [can suffice]?

body.text:
ābrahmastambaparyante
saṃsāre yasya saṃsthitiḥ
nindāpi tasya na nṛbhiḥ
kartum īśasya śakyate
body.translated_text: He whose abiding is in <s>saṃsāra</s>, from <s>Brahmā</s> to a clump of grass at its end—even slander of that Lord cannot be made by men.

body.text:
yadā kāṇāś ca kūṇṭhāś ca
mūḍho durbuddhir āturaḥ
sarvagatvāt sa evaikas
tadāsau nindyate katham
body.translated_text: When [a being is] one-eyed and crippled, deluded, of evil intellect, diseased—since he [Viṣṇu] alone is all-pervading, how then is he slandered [in slandering such beings]?

body.text:
sraṣṭā pālayitā hartā
jagato 'sya jagac ca saḥ
yaṣṭā yājayitā yājyaḥ
sa eva bhagavān hariḥ
body.translated_text: The creator, the protector, the destroyer of this world, and he is the world itself; the sacrificer, the one who causes sacrifice, and the object of sacrifice—he alone is the Blessed <s>Hari</s>.

body.text:
dātā dānaṃ tathādātā
kartā kāryaṃ tathā kriyāḥ
hantā ghātayitā hiṃsyo
hāryaṃ hartā ca yaḥ svayam
body.translated_text: The giver, the gift, and likewise the non-giver; the doer, the deed, and likewise the actions; the slayer, the one who causes slaughter, and the slain; that which is to be carried off, the carrier-off, and he himself.

body.text:
sarvakāraṇabhūtasya
tasyeśasya mahātmanaḥ
kaḥ karoti stutiṃ viṣṇor
nindāṃ vā pṛthivīpate
body.translated_text: Of that Lord, the great-souled, who is the cause of all causes—who makes praise or slander of that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O lord of the earth?

body.text:
tasmāt sarveśvaro viṣṇur
na stotuṃ na ca ninditum
śakyate sarvabhūtatvāc
cokṣācokṣasvarūpiṇā
body.translated_text: Therefore the Lord of all, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, can neither be praised nor slandered, because he is all beings, having the nature of the clean and the unclean.

body.text:
stuteḥ pādād yato nānyad
utkṛṣṭam upalabhyate
tasyāpy uccāraṇeneśo
na stotuṃ śakyate hariḥ
body.translated_text: Since nothing else more excellent is found than [even] a quarter of [his] praise, even by the uttering of that, the Lord <s>Hari</s> cannot be praised.

body.text:
bhūtārthavādastutaye
na nindāyai vidhīyate
yato 'taḥ sarvabhūtasya
kā nindā tasya kā stutiḥ
body.translated_text: [Speech] is enjoined for the praise that states the real, not for slander; therefore, of him who is all beings, what slander is there, what praise?

body.text:
yena sarvātmanā tatra
hṛdayaṃ saṃniveśitam
api maunavatas tasya
sulabho 'yaṃ janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: He by whom, with his whole self, the heart has been settled there [on Viṣṇu]—even for that man of [mere] silence, this <s>Janārdana</s> is easily attained.

body.text:
tasmāt tvaṃ kuruśārdūla
svadharmaparipālanam
kuru viṣṇuṃ ca hṛdaye
sarvavyāpinam īśvaram
body.translated_text: Therefore you, O tiger of the <s>Kurus</s>, perform the protecting of your own <s>dharma</s>, and [hold] in your heart <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-pervading Lord.

body.text:
tanmanā bhava tadbhaktas
tadyājī taṃ namaskuru
viṣṇor evaṃ priyatvaṃ tvam
āśu yāsyasi pārthiva
body.translated_text: Be one whose mind is on him, his devotee, his sacrificer; bow to him; thus you will quickly attain the dearness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O king.

body.text:
yaṃ stuvan stavyatām eti
vandyamānaś ca vandyatām
tam īśvareśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ
hṛdaye saṃniveśaya
body.translated_text: Him by praising whom one becomes praiseworthy, and by reverencing whom one becomes worthy of reverence—that Lord of lords <s>Viṣṇu</s> settle in your heart.

body.text:
saṃpūjya yaṃ pūjyatamo
bhavaty atra jagattraye
tam īśvareśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ
hṛdaye kuru pārthiva
body.translated_text: Him by worshipping whom one becomes most worthy of worship here in the three worlds—that Lord of lords <s>Viṣṇu</s> hold in your heart, O king.

body.text:
svavarṇakarmābhirataḥ
kuru citte janārdanam
eṣa śāstrārthasadbhāvaḥ
kim uktair bahuvistaraiḥ
body.translated_text: Devoted to the action of your own class, hold <s>Janārdana</s> in your mind; this is the true essence of the <s>śāstra</s>'s meaning—what use are words of great extent?

body.text:
yasmin prasannacittas tvaṃ
yasmin kopam upaiṣi ca
tāv ubhāv api tadbhūtau
cintayan siddhim eṣyasi
body.translated_text: He in whom you are of gladdened mind, and he toward whom you come to anger—both of these too being [filled with] him, contemplating [thus] you will attain perfection.

body.text:
yatra yatra sthitaṃ cetaḥ
prītyā snehena vā tava
taṃ taṃ cintaya govindaṃ
manasaḥ sthairyakāraṇāt
body.translated_text: Wherever your mind is fixed, with love or with affection, that very <s>Govinda</s> contemplate, for the sake of the steadiness of the mind.

body.text:
svapan vibuddhyann uttiṣṭhan
sthito bhuñjan piban vrajan
sarvagaṃ sarvakartāraṃ
viṣṇuṃ sarvatra cintaya
body.translated_text: Sleeping, awakening, rising, standing, eating, drinking, going—contemplate everywhere <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-pervading, the maker of all.

body.text:
yathāgnisaṃgāt kanakam
apadoṣaṃ prajāyate
saṃśliṣṭaṃ vāsudevena
manuṣyāṇāṃ tathā manaḥ
body.translated_text: As from contact with fire gold becomes free of defect, so [becomes] the mind of men joined with <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

body.text:
yajvino yaṃ namasyanti
yaṃ namasyanti devatāḥ
yogino yaṃ namasyanti
taṃ namasyaṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: Him to whom the sacrificers bow, to whom the deities bow, to whom the <s>yogins</s> bow—to that one worthy of homage I bow.

body.text:
bhūyaś ca śṛṇu rājendra
yaj jagāda janārdanaḥ
nāgaparyaṅkaśayane
pṛṣṭaḥ kṣīrābdhikanyayā
body.translated_text: And hear further, O lord of kings, what <s>Janārdana</s> related, when asked by the daughter of the Ocean of Milk [Lakṣmī], on the serpent-couch.

body.text:
purā śayānaṃ govindaṃ
prāvṛṭkāle mahodadhau
śeṣabhogimahābhoge
vīcyambukaṇaśītale
body.translated_text: Of old, <s>Govinda</s> lying in the rainy season on the great ocean, on the great coiled body of <s>Śeṣa</s>, cool with the spray of the waves—

body.text:
vakṣaḥsthalasthitā devī
jaganmātā jagatpatim
body.translated_text: the goddess situated on his breast, the mother of the world, [asked] the Lord of the world,

body.text:
ananyāsaktadṛṣṭiṃ ca
kim apy ekāgramānasam
body.translated_text: his gaze fixed on nothing else, his mind somehow one-pointed—

body.text:
śrīvatsavkṣasaṃ lakṣmīḥ
karasaṃvāhanādṛtā
body.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, honored with the stroking of his <s>Śrīvatsa</s>-marked breast by her hand,

body.text:
yoganidrāvasānastham
acyutaṃ jagataḥ patim
papraccha puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
puṇḍarīkakarā harim
body.translated_text: asked the lotus-eyed <s>Hari</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, the Lord of the world, situated at the end of his <s>yoga</s>-slumber, she of lotus-hands:

body.text:
sṛṣṭaṃ jagad idaṃ sarvaṃ
bahuśaś copasaṃhṛtam
tvayā jagatpate cātra
kiṃ kaścid dayitas tava
body.translated_text: "This whole world is created by you, and many times withdrawn, O Lord of the world; in this [matter], is anyone dear to you?

body.text:
devān manuṣyān gandharvān
yakṣavidyādharāsurān
sṛṣṭvā sṛṣṭān nirghṛṇatvād
upasaṃharate bhavān
body.translated_text: Having created gods, humans, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>asuras</s>, you withdraw the created ones out of pitilessness.

body.text:
kaścid eteṣu bhūteṣu
devādiṣu tavācyuta
dveṣo 'sti prītir athavā
samaḥ sarvatra vā bhavān
body.translated_text: Among these beings, the gods and the rest, is there anyone, O <s>Acyuta</s>, [toward whom you have] hatred, or love—or are you the same everywhere?"

body.text:
samo 'smi sarvabhūteṣu
na me dveṣyo 'sti na priyaḥ
tathāpi guṇagṛhyo 'haṃ
pratyekahṛdayasthitaḥ
body.translated_text: "I am the same toward all beings; none is hateful to me, none dear; nevertheless I am to be grasped through [their] qualities, abiding in each individual heart.

body.text:
antarātmani sarvasya
lokasyāham avasthitaḥ
puṇyāpuṇyakṛtau teṣu
prītidveṣau śubhe mama
body.translated_text: I am situated as the inner self of all the world; toward those who do merit and demerit, my love and hatred are [merely] reflections in [their] good and evil.

body.text:
puṇyaṃ prītyanubhāvena
sādhu buddhiṣu vartate
dveṣānubhāvenāpuṇyaṃ
phaladaṃ teṣu bhāmini
body.translated_text: Merit, through the effect of [my] love, abides in good intellects; through the effect of [my] hatred, demerit is fruit-giving in them, O lovely one.

body.text:
śrūyatāṃ ca mahābhāge
nareṣu śubhacāriṣu
satataṃ yeṣu me prītis
tathāprītir varānane
body.translated_text: And let it be heard, O greatly fortunate one: among men of auspicious conduct, those toward whom my love is constant, and likewise [those toward whom there is] no-love, O fair-faced one.

body.text:
pralayotpattitattvajñā
ātmajñānaparāś ca ye
ete svakarmaṇā bhadre
mama prītipathaṃ gatāḥ
body.translated_text: Those who know the truths of dissolution and origination, and who are intent on knowledge of the self—these, by their own action, O blessed one, have gone the path of my love.

body.text:
vāṅmanaḥkāyikīṃ hiṃsāṃ
ye na kurvanti kutracit
sarvamaitrā narā lakṣmi
dayitās te sadā mama
body.translated_text: Those who do not anywhere commit injury of speech, mind, or body—men friendly to all, O <s>Lakṣmī</s>—they are ever dear to me.

body.text:
svakīyadravyasaṃtuṣṭā
nivṛttāś cauryakarmaṇaḥ
satyaśīladayāyuktā
narā mama sadā priyāḥ
body.translated_text: Men content with their own property, abstaining from the act of theft, endowed with truth, good character, and compassion, are ever dear to me.

body.text:
mātṛsvasṛsutātulyān
paradārāṃś ca ye narāḥ
manyante te ca me lakṣmi
dṛḍhaṃ priyatamāḥ sadā
body.translated_text: Those men who regard others' wives as equal to mother, sister, and daughter—they too, O <s>Lakṣmī</s>, are firmly and ever most dear to me.

body.text:
na kāmān na ca saṃrambhān
na dveṣād ye ca bhāmini
saṃtyajanti svakaṃ karma
te 'tīva dayitā mama
body.translated_text: Those who abandon their own [allotted] duty neither out of desire, nor out of passion, nor out of hatred, O lovely one—they are exceedingly dear to me.

body.text:
viśvāsyāḥ sarvabhūtānām
ahiṃsrāś ca dayālavaḥ
tyaktānṛtakathā devi
manuṣyā dayitā mama
body.translated_text: Trustworthy to all beings, non-injurious and compassionate, having given up false talk, O goddess—[such] men are dear to me.

body.text:
dharmalabdhāṃs tu ye bhogān
bhuñjate nātikīkaṭāḥ
paralokāvirodhena
te mamātipriyā narāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who, not too greedy, enjoy enjoyments obtained by <s>dharma</s>, without conflict with the other world—they are exceedingly dear to me

body.text:
na lobhe na ca kārpaṇye
na steye na ca matsare
yeṣāṃ matir manuṣyāṇāṃ
te 'tīva dayitā mama
body.translated_text: Those men whose mind is not in greed, nor in miserliness, nor in theft, nor in envy—they are exceedingly beloved of me

body.text:
dharmalabdheṣu dāreṣu
ṛtukālābhigāminaḥ
gṛhasthakarmābhiratā
narās te dayitā mama
body.translated_text: Those men who go to wives obtained by <s>dharma</s> at the proper season, delighting in the duties of the householder—they are beloved of me

body.text:
pararandhreṣu jātyandhāḥ
paradāreṣv apuṃsakāḥ
parāpavāde ye mūkā
dayitās te narā mama
body.translated_text: Those who are born blind toward others' faults, impotent toward others' wives, dumb at the censure of others—those men are beloved of me

body.text:
parāpavādaṃ nindāṃ ca
paramarmāvaghaṭṭanam
ye na kurvanti puruṣās
te devi mama vallabhāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who do not engage in censure of others, slander, and the wounding of others' vital points—they, O goddess, are my favorites

body.text:
satyāṃ ślakṣṇāṃ nirābādhāṃ
madhurāṃ prītidāyinīm
ye vācam īrayanti sma
te manuṣyā mama priyāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who utter speech that is true, smooth, harmless, sweet, and affection-giving—they are dear to me

body.text:
ye brāhmaṇārthe saṃtyajya
sadyaḥ svam api jīvitam
yatante parayā bhaktyā
te devi dayitā mama
body.translated_text: Those who, abandoning at once even their own life for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s sake, strive with supreme devotion—they, O goddess, are beloved of me

body.text:
sākṣād devam ivāyāntaṃ
yā patiṃ nityam arcati
pādaśaucādibhir nārī
tasyā nāhaṃ sudurlabhaḥ
body.translated_text: The woman who ever worships her husband, coming as if a god in person, with washing of his feet and the rest—to her I am not very hard to attain

body.text:
pūrṇacandram ivodyataṃ
bhartāraṃ yā gṛhāgatam
hṛṣṭā paśyati tāṃ viddhi
dayitāṃ yoṣitaṃ mama
body.translated_text: The woman who, delighted, beholds her husband come home like the risen full moon—know her to be a woman dear to me

body.text:
te bhaktā ye sadā viprān
pūjayanty abdhisaṃbhave
yathāvibhavato bhaktyā
svakarmābhiratā narāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men are my devotees who ever worship the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O ocean-born one, according to their means with devotion, delighting in their own duties

body.text:
śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmaṃ
manasāpi na ye narāḥ
samullaṅghya pravartante
te bhaktā mama bhāmini
body.translated_text: Those men who do not transgress, even in mind, the <s>dharma</s> declared in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, and [thus] act—they are my devotees, O lady

body.text:
brahmarūpadharasyāsyān
mama vedā viniḥsṛtāḥ
manvādirūpiṇaś caiva
samastāḥ smṛtayaḥ smṛtāḥ
body.translated_text: From this mouth of mine bearing the form of <s>Brahmā</s> the <s>Vedas</s> issued forth, and all the <s>smṛtis</s>, in the forms of <s>Manu</s> and the rest, are remembered [as mine]

body.text:
śrutiḥ smṛtir mamaivājñā
tām ullaṅghya yajec chubhe
sarvasvenāpi māṃ devi
nāpnoty ājñāvighātakṛt
body.translated_text: <s>Śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> are my very command; transgressing that, if one should worship [me], O auspicious one, even with all his wealth, O goddess, he, the violator of my command, does not attain me

body.text:
yaḥ svadharmān na calati
hiṃsādhau yo na sajyate
vahatas tasya madbhaktiṃ
sadaivāhaṃ na durlabhaḥ
body.translated_text: He who does not stray from his own duties, who is not attached to injury and the rest, who bears devotion to me—to him I am never hard to attain

body.text:
etad devi mayākhyātaṃ
yat pṛṣṭo 'ham iha tvayā
priyāṇāṃ mama sarveṣāṃ
śṛṇu yo 'titaraṃ priyaḥ
body.translated_text: This, O goddess, has been declared by me, since I was asked here by you; of all those dear to me, hear who is exceedingly dear:

body.text:
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ
śūdraś ca varavarṇini
svadharmād acalan devi
dayāvān sarvajantuṣu
body.translated_text: the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>kṣatriya</s>, the <s>vaiśya</s>, and the <s>śūdra</s>, O fair-complexioned one, who does not stray from his own duty, O goddess, compassionate toward all creatures,

body.text:
satyavāc chaucasaṃpanno
na drohī na ca matsarī
vāṅmanaḥkarmabhiḥ śānto
dayitaḥ satataṃ mama
body.translated_text: truth-speaking, endowed with purity, not malicious nor envious, tranquil in speech, mind, and deeds—[he is] ever dear to me

body.text:
evaṃ śrīr devadevena
prāg uktā harimedhasā
tavāpi hi naraśreṣṭha
yathāvat kathitaṃ mayā
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Śrī</s> was addressed of old by the god of gods, the wise <s>Hari</s>; and to you too, O best of men, it has been duly told by me

body.text:
saṃvādam etad devasya
saha lakṣmyā jagatpateḥ
yaḥ śṛṇoti sa pāpebhyaḥ
samastebhyaḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: He who hears this dialogue of the god, the Lord of the world, together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, is freed from all sins

body.text:
bhūyo 'khilaṃ jagaddhātur
vāsudevasya bhārgava
samyagārādhanāyālaṃ
kriyāyogaṃ bravīhi me
body.translated_text: Again, the whole [way] of duly worshipping the world's creator, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O <s>Bhārgava</s>—tell me the <s>kriyāyoga</s> sufficient [for it]

body.text:
yat phalaṃ keśavasyārcāṃ
pratiṣṭhāpya labhen naraḥ
yac ca devakulaṃ viṣṇoḥ
kārayitvā phalaṃ labhet
body.translated_text: The fruit which a man would obtain by installing an image of <s>Keśava</s>, and the fruit he would obtain by having a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> built,

body.text:
yad dīpadhūpapuṣpāṇāṃ
gandhānāṃ ca nivedane
dhvajādidāne yat puṇyaṃ
yat puṇyaṃ gītavādite
body.translated_text: the merit there is in offering lamps, incense, flowers, and fragrances, the merit in the giving of banners and the rest, the merit in song and instrumental music,

body.text:
tathā pavitrapaṭhane
jayaśabdādyudīraṇe
saṃmārjanādau yat puṇyaṃ
namaskāre pradakṣiṇe
body.translated_text: and likewise in reciting the sacred [texts], in uttering shouts of victory and the rest, the merit there is in sweeping and the rest, in obeisance and circumambulation,

body.text:
śīrṇasphuṭitasaṃskāra-
karaṇe cāpi yat phalam
tan me vistarataḥ sarvaṃ
bhagavan vaktum arhasi
body.translated_text: and the fruit too there is in performing the repair of what is worn and broken—all that you ought to tell me in detail, O Blessed One

body.text:
yaiś copavāsair bhagavān
narair ārādhyate hariḥ
teṣāṃ phalaṃ ca yat kṛtsnaṃ
tan mamācakṣva vistarāt
body.translated_text: And by what fasts the Blessed <s>Hari</s> is worshipped by men, and the whole fruit of theirs—that tell me in detail

body.text:
saṃkṣepāt pūrvam evaitad
bhavataḥ kathitaṃ mayā
vistareṇa mahārāja
śrūyatāṃ bruvato mama
body.translated_text: This was told to you before only in brief; in detail, O great king, let it be heard as I tell it

body.text:
aditir nāma devānāṃ
mātā paramaduścaram
tapaś cacāra varṣāṇāṃ
sahasraṃ pṛthivīpate
body.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s> by name, the mother of the gods, performed most-difficult-to-do austerity for a thousand years, O lord of the earth,

body.text:
ārādhanāya kṛṣṇasya
vāgyatā vāyubhojanā
daityair nirākṛtān dṛṣṭvā
tanayān kurunandana
body.translated_text: for the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with restrained speech, feeding on wind; seeing her sons rejected by the <s>daityas</s>, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>,

body.text:
vṛthāputrāham asmīti
nirvedāt praṇatā harim
tuṣṭāva vāgbhir iṣṭābhiḥ
paramārthāvabodhinī
body.translated_text: [thinking] 'I am one whose sons are in vain,' out of despair, bowed to <s>Hari</s>, she praised [him] with desired words, awakened to the supreme truth:

body.text:
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇatā bhaktavatsalam
body.translated_text: Bowed to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the refuge worthy of refuge, fond of his devotees,

body.text:
devadaityanṛpaśvāpa-
vyomavāyvādirūpiṇam
body.translated_text: [him] of the form of gods, <s>daityas</s>, kings, beasts, sky, wind, and the rest:

body.text:
namaḥ smṛtārtināśāya
namaḥ puṣkaramāline
namaḥ paramakalyāṇa-
kalyāṇāyādivedhase
body.translated_text: 'Homage to the destroyer of distress when remembered; homage to the lotus-garlanded one; homage to the supremely auspicious, [source of] auspiciousness, the primal creator

body.text:
namaḥ paṅkajanetrāya
namaḥ paṅkajanābhaye
namaḥ paṅkajasaṃbhūti-
saṃbhavāyātmayonaye
body.translated_text: Homage to the lotus-eyed one; homage to the lotus-naveled one; homage to the self-born one, the source of the origin of the lotus [Brahmā]

body.text:
śriyaḥ kāntāya dāntāya
dāntadṛśyāya cakriṇe
namaḥ śaṅkhāsihastāya
namaḥ kanakaretase
body.translated_text: To the beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, the self-controlled, the seen-by-the-controlled, the discus-bearer; homage to him with conch and sword in hand; homage to him of golden seed

body.text:
tathātmajñānavijñāna-
yogacittātmayogine
nirguṇāya viśeṣāya
haraye brahmarūpiṇe
body.translated_text: and to the yogin whose self is the yoga of mind in self-knowledge and discernment, to the quality-less, the distinct, <s>Hari</s>, of the form of <s>Brahman</s>

body.text:
jagat pratiṣṭhitaṃ yatra
jagatā yo na dṛśyate
namaḥ sthūlātisūkṣmāya
tasmai devāya śaṅkhine
body.translated_text: He in whom the world is established, who is not seen by the world—homage to that god, the conch-bearer, the gross and the most subtle

body.text:
yaṃ na paśyanti paśyanto
jagad apy akhilaṃ narāḥ
apaśyadbhir jagad yac ca
dṛśyate svahṛdi sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: He whom men, though seeing the whole world entire, do not see, and who, by those not seeing the world, is seen abiding in their own heart;

body.text:
bahirjyotiṣi lakṣyo yo
lakṣyate jyotiṣaḥ paraḥ
body.translated_text: he who, perceptible in the outer light, is perceived [as] beyond the light;

body.text:
yasminn etad yataś caitad
yaś caitad akhilaṃ jagat
tasmai samastajagatām
ādhārāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: in whom this [all is], from whom this [all is], and who is this whole world—to that support of all the worlds, homage and homage

body.text:
ādyaḥ prajāpatipatir
yaḥ pitṝṇāṃ paraḥ patiḥ
patiḥ surāṇāṃ yas tasmai
namaḥ kṛṣṇāya vedhase
body.translated_text: The primal lord of <s>Prajāpati</s>, who is the supreme lord of the ancestors, who is the lord of the gods—to that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the creator, homage

body.text:
yaḥ pravṛttair nivṛttaiś ca
karmabhir vibhur ijyate
svargāpavargaphalado
namas tasmai gadādhṛte
body.translated_text: He, the pervading one, who is worshipped by active and inactive deeds, the giver of the fruit of heaven and final release—homage to that mace-bearer

body.text:
yaś cintyamāno manasā
sadyaḥ pāpaṃ vyapohati
namas tasmai viśuddhāya
parasmai harimedhase
body.translated_text: He who, being contemplated by the mind, at once removes sin—homage to that utterly pure, supreme, wise <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
yaṃ praviśyākhilādhāram
īśānam ajam avyayam
na punar janmamaraṇe
prāpnuvanti namāmi tam
body.translated_text: He, entering whom—the support of all, the Lord, the unborn, the imperishable—[men] do not again attain birth and death—I bow to him

body.text:
yo yajñe yajñaparamair
ijyate yajñasaṃsthitiḥ
taṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ
namāmi prabhum īśvaram
body.translated_text: He who in sacrifice is worshipped by those supreme in sacrifice, the very establishment of sacrifice—that sacrifice-Person <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord and master, I bow to

body.text:
gīyate sarvavedeṣu
vedavidbhir vidāṃ gatiḥ
yas tasmai vedavedyāya
viṣṇave jiṣṇave namaḥ
body.translated_text: He who is sung in all the <s>Vedas</s> by the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, the goal of the wise—to that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the victorious, knowable through the <s>Vedas</s>, homage

body.text:
yato viśvaṃ samudbhūtaṃ
yasmiṃś ca layam eṣyati
viśvodbhavapratiṣṭhāya
namas tasmai mahātmane
body.translated_text: From whom the universe arose, and in whom it will go to dissolution—to that great-souled one, the origin and ground of the universe, homage

body.text:
brahmādistambaparyantaṃ
vinā yena tatām imām
māyāṃ nālaṃ samuttartuṃ
tam upendraṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: He without whom one is not able to cross over this <s>māyā</s> spread out from <s>Brahmā</s> to a clump of grass—to that <s>Upendra</s> I bow

body.text:
yam ārādhya viśuddhena
manasā karmaṇā girā
haraty avidyām akhilāṃ
tam upendraṃ namāmy aham
viṣādatoṣaroṣādyair
yo 'jasraṃ sukhaduḥkhajaiḥ
nṛtyaty akhilabhūtasthas
tam upendraṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: He whom, having worshipped with pure mind, deed, and speech, removes all ignorance—to that <s>Upendra</s> I bow; he who, abiding in all beings, dances ceaselessly with despair, contentment, anger, and the rest born of pleasure and pain—to that <s>Upendra</s> I bow

body.text:
yo 'nnatoyasvarūpastho
bibharty akhilam īśvaraḥ
viśvaṃ viśvapatiṃ viṣṇuṃ
taṃ namāmi prajāpatim
body.translated_text: He who, abiding in the form of food and water, the Lord, sustains all—that universe, the Lord of the universe, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I bow to, the <s>Prajāpati</s>

body.text:
mūrtaṃ tamo 'suramayaṃ
tadvadhād vinihanti yaḥ
rātrijaṃ sūryarūpī ca
tam upendraṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: He who, embodied as the demon-natured darkness, slays it by its slaying, and [slays] the night-born [darkness] in the form of the sun—to that <s>Upendra</s> I bow

body.text:
kapilādisvarūpastho
yaś cājñānamayaṃ tamaḥ
hanti jñānapradānena
tam upendraṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: He who, abiding in the form of <s>Kapila</s> and the rest, slays the ignorance-made darkness by the gift of knowledge—to that <s>Upendra</s> I bow

body.text:
yasyākṣiṇī candrasūryau
sarvalokaśubhāśubham
paśyete karma satataṃ
tam upendraṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: He whose two eyes are the moon and sun, which ever behold the good and evil deeds of all the world—to that <s>Upendra</s> I bow

body.text:
yasmin sarveśvare sarvaṃ
satyam etan mayoditam
nānṛtaṃ tam ajaṃ viṣṇuṃ
namāmi prabhavāvyayam
body.translated_text: He, the Lord of all, in whom all this that I have spoken is true, not false—that unborn <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the imperishable source, I bow to

body.text:
yathaitat satyam uktaṃ me
bhūyaś cāto janārdanaḥ
satyena tena sakalāḥ
pūryantāṃ me manorathāḥ
body.translated_text: As this has been spoken truly by me, and further [I praise] <s>Janārdana</s>—by that truth let all my heart's desires be fulfilled'

body.text:
evaṃ stuto 'tha bhagavān
vāsudeva uvāca tām
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ
tasyāḥ saṃdarśane sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus praised, the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, invisible to all beings, [yet] standing within her sight, said to her:

body.text:
manorathāṃs tvam adite
yān icchasy abhipūritān
tāṃs tān prāpsyasi dharmajñe
matprasādād asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: 'Whatever heart's desires you wish, O <s>Aditi</s>, [those] fulfilled you shall obtain, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, by my grace, without doubt

body.text:
śṛṇuṣva ca mahābhāge
varaṃ yas te hṛdi sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: And hear, O greatly fortunate one, the boon that is in your heart;

body.text:
taṃ prayacchāmi niyataṃ
mātra kāryā vicāraṇā
body.translated_text: that I grant surely—no deliberation is to be made over it

body.text:
maddarśanaṃ hi viphalaṃ
na kadācid bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: For the sight of me shall never be fruitless'

body.text:
yadi deva prasannas tvaṃ
bhaktāyā bhaktavatsala
trailokyādhipatiḥ putras
tad astu mama vāsavaḥ
body.translated_text: 'If you, O god, are pleased with [me] your devotee, O lover of devotees, let my son be <s>Vāsava</s> [Indra], the lord of the three worlds

body.text:
hṛtarājyo hṛtaś cāsya
yajñabhāgo mahāsuraiḥ
tvayi prasanne varada
taṃ prāpnotu suto mama
body.translated_text: His kingdom is taken and his sacrificial share taken by the great <s>asuras</s>; you being pleased, O boon-giver, let my son regain it

body.text:
hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ na duḥkhāya
mama putrasya keśava
sapatnād āyatibhraṃśo
bādhāṃ naḥ kurute hṛdi
body.translated_text: The kingdom taken is not [the cause] of sorrow for my son, O <s>Keśava</s>; the loss of future prospects from a rival makes affliction in our heart'

body.text:
kṛtaḥ prasādo hi mayā
tava devi yathepsitaḥ
svāṃśena caiva te garbhe
saṃbhaviṣyāmi kaśyapāt
body.translated_text: 'A favor has indeed been done by me to you, O goddess, as desired; and with a portion of myself I shall come into being in your womb, from <s>Kaśyapa</s>

body.text:
tava garbhasamudbhūtaḥ
sutas te ye surārayaḥ
tān ahaṃ nihaniṣyāmi
nirvṛtā bhava nandini
body.translated_text: Arisen from your womb, [as] your son, I shall slay those enemies of the gods who are yours; be at ease, O joyful one'

body.text:
prasīda devadeveśa
namas te viśvabhāvana
nāhaṃ tvām udareṇeśa
voḍhuṃ śakṣyāmi keśava
body.translated_text: 'Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods; homage to you, O creator of the universe; I shall not be able, O Lord, to bear you with my belly, O <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
yasmin pratiṣṭhitaṃ viśvaṃ
yo viśvaṃ svayam īśvara
tad ahaṃ nodareṇa tvāṃ
voḍhuṃ śakṣyāmi durdharam
body.translated_text: He in whom the universe is established, who himself is the universe, the Lord—him, the unbearable one, I shall not be able to bear with my belly'

body.text:
satyam āttha mahābhāge
mayi sarvam idaṃ jagat
pratiṣṭhitaṃ na māṃ śaktā
voḍhuṃ sendrā divaukasaḥ
body.translated_text: 'You speak truly, O greatly fortunate one: in me all this world is established; the dwellers in heaven, with <s>Indra</s>, are not able to bear me

body.text:
kintv ahaṃ sakalāṃl lokān
sadevāsuramānuṣān
jaṅgamājaṅgamaṃ sarvaṃ
tvāṃ ca devi sakāśyapām
dhārayiṣyāmi bhadraṃ te
tava garbhaśayo 'dite
body.translated_text: But I shall bear all the worlds, with their gods, <s>asuras</s>, and men, all the moving and unmoving, and you too, O goddess, together with <s>Kaśyapa</s>—blessings on you—[I,] lying in your womb, O <s>Aditi</s>

body.text:
na te glānir na te khedo
garbhasthe bhavitā mayi
dākṣāyaṇi prasādaṃ te
karomy anyaiḥ sudurlabham
body.translated_text: There shall be for you no weariness, no fatigue, when I am in your womb; O <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, I do you a favor very hard for others to obtain

body.text:
garbhasthe mayi putrāṇāṃ
tava yo 'rir bhaviṣyati
tejasas tasya hāniṃ ca
kariṣye mā vyathāṃ kṛtāḥ
body.translated_text: When I am in your womb, the enemy of your sons—his splendour I shall diminish; be not distressed'

body.text:
evam uktvā tataḥ sadyo
gato 'ntardhānam īśvaraḥ
sāpi kālena taṃ garbham
avāpa kurusattama
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the Lord then at once went to disappearance; and she too, in time, conceived that embryo, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>

body.text:
garbhasthite tataḥ kṛṣṇe
cacāla sakalā kṣitiḥ
cakampire mahāśailā
jagmuḥ kṣobham athābdhayaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was in the womb, the whole earth shook, the great mountains quaked, and the oceans went into agitation

body.text:
yato yato 'ditir yāntī
dadāti lalitaṃ padam
tatas tataḥ kṣitiḥ khedān
nanāma vasudhādhipa
body.translated_text: Wherever <s>Aditi</s>, going, set her graceful foot, there and there the earth bowed down from the strain, O lord of the earth

body.text:
daityānām api sarveṣāṃ
garbhasthe madhusūdane
babhūva tejaso hānir
yathoktaṃ parameṣṭhinā
body.translated_text: And of all the <s>daityas</s> too, when <s>Madhusūdana</s> was in the womb, there came a loss of splendour, as had been declared by the Supreme One

body.text:
nistejaso 'surān dṛṣṭvā
samastān asureśvaraḥ
prahrādam atha papraccha
balir ātmapitāmaham
body.translated_text: Seeing all the <s>asuras</s> bereft of splendour, the lord of the <s>asuras</s>, <s>Bali</s>, then asked <s>Prahlāda</s>, his own grandfather:

body.text:
tāta nistejaso daityā
nirdagdhā iva vahninā
kim ete sahasaivādya
brahmadaṇḍahatā iva
body.translated_text: 'Father, the <s>daityas</s> are bereft of splendour, as if burned by fire; why are these, all at once today, as if struck by the rod of <s>Brahmā</s>?

body.text:
duriṣṭaṃ kiṃ nu daityānāṃ
kiṃ kṛtyā vairinirmitā
nāśāyaiṣāṃ samudbhūtā
yena nistejaso 'surāḥ
body.translated_text: Is it some ill-performed sacrifice of the <s>daityas</s>? Or is it a [magic] rite fashioned by an enemy, arisen for their destruction, by which the <s>asuras</s> are bereft of splendour?'

body.text:
ity āsuravaras tena
pṛṣṭaḥ pautreṇa pārthiva
ciraṃ dhyātvā jagādedam
asurendraṃ tadā balim
body.translated_text: Thus asked by that grandson, O king, the best of <s>asuras</s>, having meditated long, then said this to <s>Bali</s>, the lord of <s>asuras</s>:

body.text:
calanti girayo bhūmir
jahāti sahajāṃ dhṛtim
sadyaḥ samudrāḥ kṣubhitā
daityā nistejasaḥ kṛtāḥ
body.translated_text: 'The mountains move, the earth abandons its natural steadiness, the oceans are suddenly agitated, the <s>daityas</s> are made bereft of splendour;

body.text:
sūryādayo yathā pūrvaṃ
tathā gacchanti na grahāḥ
devānāṃ ca parā lakṣmīḥ
kāraṇair anumīyate
body.translated_text: the sun and the rest, the planets, do not move as before; and the supreme fortune of the gods is inferred from [these] causes

body.text:
mahad etan mahābāho
kāraṇaṃ dānaveśvara
na hy alpam iti mantavyaṃ
tvayā kāryaṃ surārdana
body.translated_text: Great is this cause, O mighty-armed lord of the <s>dānavas</s>; it is not to be thought small; action must be taken by you, O afflicter of the gods'

body.text:
ity uktvā dānavapatiṃ
prahrādaḥ so 'surottamaḥ
atyantabhakto deveśaṃ
jagāma manasā harim
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the lord of the <s>dānavas</s>, that best of <s>asuras</s> <s>Prahlāda</s>, exceedingly devoted to the Lord of the gods, went with his mind to <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
sa dhyānapathagaṃ kṛtvā
prahrādaḥ svaṃ mano 'suraḥ
vicārayām āsa tato
yato devo janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: That <s>asura</s> <s>Prahlāda</s>, having set his mind on the path of meditation, then considered where the god <s>Janārdana</s> [was]

body.text:
sa dadarśodare 'dityāḥ
prahrādo vāmanākṛtim
antaḥsthān bibhrataṃ sapta
lokān ādiprajāpatim
body.translated_text: <s>Prahlāda</s> beheld in the womb of <s>Aditi</s> a dwarf form, bearing within the seven worlds, the primal <s>Prajāpati</s>,

body.text:
tad antaś ca vasūn rudrān
aśvinau marutas tathā
sādhyān viśve tathādityān
gandharvoragarākṣasān
body.translated_text: and within that, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, and likewise the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Gandharvas</s>, serpents, and <s>rākṣasas</s>,

body.text:
virocanaṃ satanayaṃ
baliṃ cāsuranāyakam
jambhaṃ kujambhaṃ narakaṃ
bāṇam anyāṃs tathāsurān
body.translated_text: <s>Virocana</s> with his son, and <s>Bali</s> the leader of the <s>asuras</s>, <s>Jambha</s>, <s>Kujambha</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, and likewise the other <s>asuras</s>,

body.text:
ātmānam urvīgaganaṃ
vāyum ambho hutāśanam
samudrādridrumasarit-
sarāṃsi paśavo mṛgān
body.translated_text: himself, the earth and sky, the wind, the water, the fire, the seas, mountains, trees, rivers, lakes, cattle, beasts,

body.text:
vayomanuṣyān akhilāṃs
tathaiva ca sarīsṛpān
samastalokasraṣṭāraṃ
brahmāṇaṃ bhavam eva ca
body.translated_text: birds, all men, and likewise the reptiles, the creator of all the worlds <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Bhava</s> [Śiva] as well,

body.text:
grahanakṣatratārāś ca
dakṣādyāṃś ca prajāpatīn
saṃpaśyan vismayāviṣṭaḥ
prakṛtisthaḥ kṣaṇāt punaḥ
body.translated_text: and the planets, lunar mansions, and stars, and <s>Dakṣa</s> and the other <s>Prajāpatis</s>—beholding [all this], filled with wonder, he became restored to his natural state again in a moment

body.text:
prahrādaḥ prāha daityendraṃ
baliṃ vairocaniṃ tadā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Prahlāda</s> spoke to the lord of <s>daityas</s>, <s>Bali</s> the son of <s>Virocana</s>:

body.text:
vatsa jñātaṃ mayā sarvaṃ
yadarthaṃ bhavatām iyam
tejaso hānir utpannā
tac chṛṇu tvam aśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: 'O child, all has been known by me—the reason for which this loss of splendor has arisen for you; hear that entirely

body.text:
devadevo jagadyonir
ayonir jagadādikṛt
anādir ādir viśvasya
vareṇyo varado hariḥ
body.translated_text: The God of gods, the source of the world, the unborn, the first maker of the world, beginningless, the beginning of all, the choicest, the boon-giver, <s>Hari</s>,

body.text:
parāparāṇāṃ paramaḥ
paraḥ paravatām api
prabhuḥ pramāṇaṃ mānānāṃ
saptalokaguror guruḥ
body.translated_text: the supreme of the higher and lower, supreme even of the supreme, the Lord, the measure of measures, the guru of the guru of the seven worlds,

body.text:
sthitiṃ kartuṃ jagannāthaḥ
so 'dityā garbhatāṃ gataḥ
body.translated_text: to effect the maintenance [of the world], that Lord of the world has entered the womb of <s>Aditi</s>

body.text:
prabhuḥ prabhūṇām paramaḥ parāṇām
anādimadhyo bhagavān anantaḥ
trailokyam aṃśena sanātham eṣa
kartuṃ mahātmāditijo 'vatīrṇaḥ
body.translated_text: The Lord, supreme of lords, supreme of the higher [beings], the Blessed One without beginning or middle, the infinite—he, the great soul, born of <s>Aditi</s>, has descended by a portion to make the three worlds possessed of a [true] master

body.text:
na yasya rudro na ca padmayonir
nendro na sūryendumarīcimiśrāḥ
jānanti daityādhipa yat svarūpaṃ
sa vāsudevaḥ kalayāvatīrṇaḥ
