body.translated_text: Whose essential nature neither <s>Rudra</s> nor the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), nor <s>Indra</s>, nor the sun, moon, and their rays [combined] know, O lord of the <s>daityas</s>—that <s>Vāsudeva</s> has descended with a fraction [of himself]

body.text:
yo 'sau kalāṃśena nṛsiṃharūpī
jaghāna pūrvaṃ pitaram aśeṣaḥ
yaḥ sarvayogīśamanonivāsaḥ
sa vāsudevaḥ kalayāvatīrṇaḥ
body.translated_text: He who of old, by a fraction of a portion, in the man-lion form, slew your [great-grand]father, the entire one, who is the dwelling-place of the minds of all lords of yogins—that <s>Vāsudeva</s> has descended with a fraction

body.text:
yam akṣaraṃ vedavido viditvā
viśanti taṃ jñānavidhūtapāpāḥ
yasmin praviṣṭā na punar bhavanti
taṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmi devam
body.translated_text: Whom the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, having known [him] as the imperishable, enter, their sins shaken off by knowledge, in whom having entered they are not [reborn] again—to that <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the god, I bow

body.text:
bhūtāny aśeṣāṇi yato bhavanti
yathormayas toyanidher ajasram
layaṃ ca yasmin pralaye prayānti
taṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmy acintyam
body.translated_text: From whom all beings ceaselessly arise, as waves from the ocean of waters, and into whom they go to dissolution at the dissolution—to that inconceivable <s>Vāsudeva</s> I bow

body.text:
na yasya rūpaṃ na balaṃ prabhāvo
na ca svabhāvaḥ paramasya puṃsaḥ
vijñāyate sarvapitāmahādyais
taṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmy acintyam
body.translated_text: Whose form, strength, power, and likewise nature—of the supreme Person—is not [fully] comprehended by all [the gods] beginning with the Grandsire—to that inconceivable <s>Vāsudeva</s> I bow

body.text:
rūpasya cakṣur grahaṇe tvag eṣā
sparśagrahītrī rasanā rasasya
śrotraṃ ca śabdagrahaṇe narāṇāṃ
ghrāṇaṃ ca gandhagrahaṇe niyuktam
body.translated_text: The eye [is appointed] for the grasping of form, this skin the grasper of touch, the tongue of taste, and the ear for the grasping of sound for men, and the nose appointed for the grasping of smell;

body.text:
na ghrāṇacakṣuḥśravaṇādibhir yaḥ
sarveśvaro veditum avyayātmā
śakyas tam īḍyaṃ manasaiva devaṃ
grāhyaṃ nato 'haṃ harim īśitāram
body.translated_text: he who, the Lord of all, of imperishable nature, cannot be known by smell, sight, hearing, and the rest—to that praiseworthy god, to be grasped by the mind alone, <s>Hari</s> the Lord, I am bowed down

body.text:
yenaikadaṃṣṭrāgrasamuddhṛteyaṃ
dharācalā dhārayatīha sarvam
grastvā sa śete sakalaṃ jagad yas
tam īḍyam īśaṃ praṇato 'smi viṣṇum
body.translated_text: By whom this earth, lifted up on the tip of a single tusk, holds up all things here, [and] who, having swallowed the whole world, lies [in sleep]—to that praiseworthy Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> I am bowed down

body.text:
aṃśāvatīrṇena ca yena garbhe
hṛtāni tejāṃsi mahāsurāṇām
namāmi taṃ devam anantam īśam
aśeṣasaṃsārataroḥ kuṭhāram
body.translated_text: By whom, descended by a portion in the womb, the splendors of the great <s>asuras</s> were taken away—I bow to that god, the infinite Lord, the axe to the tree of all <s>saṃsāra</s>

body.text:
devo jagadyonir ayaṃ mahātmā
sa ṣoḍaśāṃśena mahāsurendra
surendramātur jaṭharaṃ praviṣṭo
hṛtāni vas tena bale vapūṃṣi
body.translated_text: This god, the source of the world, the great soul, by a sixteenth portion, O great lord of <s>asuras</s>, has entered the belly of the mother of the lord of gods (<s>Aditi</s>); by him your bodies' [splendors] have been taken away, O <s>Bali</s>

body.text:
tāta ko 'yaṃ harir nāma
yato na bhayam āgatam
santi me śataśo daityā
vāsudevabalādhikāḥ
body.translated_text: 'O father, who is this <s>Hari</s> by name, from whom fear has come [to you]? I have hundreds of <s>daityas</s> superior to <s>Vāsudeva</s> in strength:

body.text:
vipracittiḥ śibiḥ śaṅkur
ayaḥśaṅkus tathaiva ca
ayaḥśirā aśvaśirā
bhaṅgakāro mahāhanuḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vipracitti</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, <s>Śaṅku</s>, and likewise <s>Ayaḥśaṅku</s>, <s>Ayaḥśiras</s>, <s>Aśvaśiras</s>, <s>Bhaṅgakāra</s>, <s>Mahāhanu</s>,

body.text:
pratāpī praghasaḥ śaṃbhuḥ
kurkurākṣaś ca durjayaḥ
ete cānye ca me santi
daiteyā dānavās tathā
body.translated_text: <s>Pratāpin</s>, <s>Praghasa</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, and <s>Kurkurākṣa</s>, and <s>Durjaya</s>—these and others are mine, the <s>Daiteyas</s> and the <s>Dānavas</s> likewise,

body.text:
mahābalā mahāvīryā
bhūbhāradharaṇakṣamāḥ
yeṣām ekaikaśaḥ kṛṣṇo
na vīryārdhena saṃmitaḥ
body.translated_text: of great strength, of great valor, capable of bearing the burden of the earth, with whom, [taking each] one by one, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is not equal even to half [their] valor'

body.text:
pautrasyaitad vacaḥ śrutvā
prahrādo daityapuṅgavaḥ
dhig dhig ity āha sa baliṃ
vaikuṇṭhākṣepavādinam
body.translated_text: Having heard this speech of his grandson, <s>Prahlāda</s>, the bull among <s>daityas</s>, said 'Fie, fie!' to that <s>Bali</s>, who spoke disparagement of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>:

body.text:
vināśam upayāsyanti
manye daiteyadānavāḥ
yeṣāṃ tvam īdṛśo rājā
durbuddhir avivekavān
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Daiteyas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> will go to destruction, I think, whose king is one such as you—of evil mind, lacking discrimination

body.text:
devadevaṃ mahābhāgaṃ
vāsudevam ajaṃ vibhum
tvām ṛte pāpasaṃkalpaṃ
ko 'nya evaṃ vadiṣyati
body.translated_text: Who else but you, of sinful resolve, would thus speak of the God of gods, the greatly fortunate <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the unborn, the all-pervading Lord?

body.text:
ya ete bhavatā proktāḥ
samastā daityadānavāḥ
sabrahmakās tathā devāḥ
sthāvarāntāś ca bhūtayaḥ
body.translated_text: These whom you have named, all the <s>daityas</s> and <s>dānavas</s>, and the gods together with <s>Brahmā</s>, and the creatures down to the stationary,

body.text:
tvaṃ cāhaṃ ca jagac cedaṃ
sādridrumanadīnadam
samudradvīpalokāś ca
yac ceṅgaṃ yac ca neṅgati
body.translated_text: and you and I and this world with its mountains, trees, rivers, and streams, and the oceans, islands, and worlds, and whatever moves and does not move—

body.text:
yasyātivandyavandyasya
vyāpinaḥ paramātmanaḥ
ekāṃśāṃśakalājanma
kas tam evaṃ pravakṣyati
body.translated_text: of him, the most venerable of the venerable, the all-pervading Supreme Self, [all these] have their birth from a single portion of a portion of a fraction; who would thus speak of him?

body.text:
ṛte vināśābhimukhaṃ
tvām ekam avivekinam
durbuddhim ajitātmānaṃ
vṛddhānāṃ śāsanātigam
body.translated_text: —except you alone, facing destruction, undiscerning, of evil mind, of unconquered self, transgressing the instruction of elders

body.text:
śocyo 'haṃ yasya vai gehe
jātas tava pitādhamaḥ
yasya tvam īdṛśaḥ putro
devadevāvamanyakaḥ
body.translated_text: I am pitiable, in whose house your base father was born, [you] of whom you are such a son, a despiser of the God of gods

body.text:
tiṣṭhatv anekasaṃsāra-
saṃhṛtāghavināśanī
kṛṣṇe bhaktir ahaṃ tāvad
avekṣyo bhavato na kim
body.translated_text: Let that devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the destroyer of accumulated sin of many [rounds of] <s>saṃsāra</s>, stand [aside]—am I, at least, not to be regarded by you?

body.text:
na me priyataraḥ kṛṣṇād
api deho 'yam ātmanaḥ
iti jānāty ayaṃ loko
bhavāṃś ca ditijādhamaḥ
body.translated_text: There is for me nothing dearer than <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, not even this body of mine—thus this [whole] world knows, and [so do] you, O basest of the sons of <s>Diti</s>

body.text:
jānann api priyataraṃ
prāṇebhyo 'pi hariṃ mama
nindāṃ karoṣi ca katham
akurvan gauravaṃ mama
body.translated_text: Even knowing <s>Hari</s> to be dearer to me than [my] very breaths, how do you make disparagement [of him], showing no respect to me?

body.text:
virocanas tava gurur
gurus tasyāpy ahaṃ bale
mamāpi sarvajagatāṃ
gurur nārāyaṇo guruḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Virocana</s> is your guru, and I am the guru even of him, O <s>Bali</s>; and the guru of me too, and of all the worlds, is the guru <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

body.text:
nindāṃ karoṣi tasmiṃs tvaṃ
kṛṣṇe guruguror gurau
yasmāt tasmād ihaiśvaryād
acirād bhraṃśam eṣyasi
body.translated_text: You make disparagement of him, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the guru of the guru of gurus; therefore, from this lordship here, you will fall before long

body.text:
mā devo mā jagannātho
bale māsau janārdanaḥ
bhavatv aham avekṣyas te
prītimān atra me guruḥ
body.translated_text: 'Let not the god, let not the Lord of the world, let not that <s>Janārdana</s>, O <s>Bali</s>, [be regarded]; let me be [the one] regarded by you—my guru is affectionate to me here'

body.text:
etāvanmātram apy atra
nindatā jagato gurum
nāpekṣitā vayaṃ yasmāt
tasmāc chāpaṃ dadāmi te
body.translated_text: 'Even by just this much—by you disparaging the guru of the world—since we are not regarded, therefore I give you a curse:

body.text:
yathā me śirasaś chedād
idaṃ gurutaraṃ bale
tvayoktam acyutākṣepi
rājyabhraṣṭas tathā pata
body.translated_text: as this, more grievous to me than the cutting off of my head, has been spoken by you, O <s>Bali</s>, you reviler of <s>Acyuta</s>—so fall, deprived of [your] kingdom!

body.text:
yathā na kṛṣṇād aparaṃ
paritrāṇaṃ bhavārṇave
tathācireṇa paśyeyaṃ
bhavantaṃ rājyavicyutam
body.translated_text: As there is no deliverance in the ocean of existence other than <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—so may I before long see you fallen from [your] kingdom'

body.text:
iti daityapatiḥ śrutvā
guror vacanam apriyam
prasādayām āsa guruṃ
praṇipatya puṇaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: Having heard this unpleasant speech of his guru, the lord of the <s>daityas</s> propitiated the guru, bowing down again and again:

body.text:
prasīda tāta mā kopaṃ
kuru mohahate mayi
balāvalepamattena
mayaitad vākyam īritam
body.translated_text: 'Be gracious, O father; do not be angry with me, smitten by delusion; intoxicated by pride of strength, this speech was uttered by me

body.text:
mohopahatavijñānaḥ
pāpo 'haṃ ditijottama
yac chapto 'smi durācāras
tat sādhu bhavatā kṛtam
body.translated_text: My understanding struck down by delusion, I am sinful, O best of the sons of <s>Diti</s>; that I have been cursed, of evil conduct, that has been rightly done by you

body.text:
rājyabhraṃśaṃ vasubhraṃśaṃ
saṃprāpsyāmīti na tv aham
viṣaṇṇo 'smi yathā tāta
tavaivāvinaye kṛte
body.translated_text: Not that I shall attain loss of kingdom [and] loss of wealth [do I grieve]—I am despondent, O father, [only] because this transgression has been done against you

body.text:
trailokyarājyam aiśvaryam
anyad vā nātidurlabham
saṃsāre durlabhās tāta
guravo ye bhavadvidhāḥ
body.translated_text: The kingdom of the three worlds, lordship, or anything else is not too hard to get; hard to get in <s>saṃsāra</s>, O father, are gurus such as you

body.text:
tat prasīda na me kopaṃ
kartum arhasi daityapa
tvatkopahetuduṣṭo 'haṃ
paritapye na śāpataḥ
body.translated_text: So be gracious; you ought not to be angry with me, O lord of <s>daityas</s>; vile through the cause of your anger, I am tormented, not by the curse'

body.text:
vatsa kopena moho me
janitas tena te mayā
śāpo datto vivekaś ca
mohenāpahṛto mama
body.translated_text: 'O child, delusion of mine was generated by anger; through that, the curse was given to you by me, and discrimination was carried off from me by delusion

body.text:
yadi mohena me jñānaṃ
nākṣiptaṃ syān mahāsura
tat kathaṃ sarvagaṃ jñānan
hariṃ kaṃcic chāpāmy aham
body.translated_text: If my knowledge had not been overthrown by delusion, O great <s>asura</s>, then how would I, knowing <s>Hari</s> to be all-pervading, curse anyone?

body.text:
yo 'yaṃ śāpo mayā datto
bhavato 'surapuṅgava
bhāvyam etena nūnaṃ te
tasmāt tvaṃ mā viṣīdathāḥ
body.translated_text: This curse that has been given by me to you, O bull among <s>asuras</s>—this must surely come to be for you; therefore do not despair

body.text:
adyaprabhṛti deveśe
bhagavaty acyute harau
bhavethā bhaktimān īśaḥ
sa te trātā bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: From today onward, be a devotee of the Lord of gods, the Blessed <s>Acyuta</s> <s>Hari</s>; that Lord will become your savior

body.text:
śāpaṃ prāpya ca māṃ vīra
saṃsmarethāḥ smṛtas tvayā
tathā tathā yatiṣyāmi
śreyasā yokṣyate yathā
body.translated_text: And having received the curse, O hero, remember me; remembered by you, I will so strive that you will be joined with the [highest] good'

body.text:
evam uktvā sa daityendro
virarāma mahāmatiḥ
ajāyata sa govindo
bhagavān vāmanākṛtiḥ
body.translated_text: Having said this, that lord of <s>daityas</s>, of great mind, ceased; [and meanwhile] the Blessed <s>Govinda</s> was born in the form of the dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>)

body.text:
avatīrṇe jagannāthe
tasmin sarvam aśīśamat
yad āsuram abhūd duḥkhaṃ
devānām adites tathā
body.translated_text: When the Lord of the world had descended, all of it was quelled—the <s>asura</s>-caused misery there was of the gods and of <s>Aditi</s>

body.text:
vavur vātāḥ sukhasparśā
nīrajaskam abhūn nabhaḥ
dharme ca sarvabhūtānāṃ
tadā matir ajāyata
body.translated_text: Winds of pleasant touch blew, the sky became free of dust, and then the mind of all beings turned toward <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
nodvegaś cāpy abhūd dehe
manujānāṃ janeśvara
tathā hi sarvabhūtānāṃ
bhūmyambaradivaukasām
body.translated_text: And there was no agitation in the body of men, O lord of men, and likewise of all beings—the dwellers of earth, sky, and heaven

body.text:
taṃ jātamātraṃ bhagavān
brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ
jātakarmādikāḥ kṛtvā
kriyās tuṣṭāva pārthiva
body.translated_text: Him just born, the Blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandsire of the worlds, having performed the birth-rites and the other rites, praised, O king:

body.text:
jayādyeśa jayājeya
jaya sarvātmakātmaka
jaya janmajarāpeta
jayānanta jayācyuta
body.translated_text: 'Victory, O first Lord; victory, O unconquerable; victory, O you whose self is the self of all; victory, O you free of birth and old age; victory, O infinite; victory, O <s>Acyuta</s>!

body.text:
jayājita jayāśeṣa
jayāvyakta sthite jaya
paramārthārtha sarvajña
jñāna jñeyātmaniḥsṛta
body.translated_text: Victory, O unconquered; victory, O entire one; victory, O unmanifest; victory in [the world's] maintenance! O supreme aim and object, O all-knowing, knowledge, [you who are] issued forth as the self of the knowable!

body.text:
jayāśeṣajagatsākṣiñ
jaya kartar jagadguroḥ
jagato jagadante 'nta
sthitau pālayitā jaya
body.translated_text: Victory, O witness of the entire world; victory, O maker, guru of the world; O end at the end of the world! Victory to the protector in [its] maintenance!

body.text:
jayākhila jayāśeṣa
jayākhilahṛdi sthita
jayādimadhyāntamaya
sarvajñānamayottama
body.translated_text: Victory, O all; victory, O entire; victory, O you established in every heart; victory, O you made of [the world's] beginning, middle, and end, O supreme one made of all knowledge!

body.text:
mumukṣubhir anirdeśya
svayaṃdṛṣṭa jayeśvara
yogibhir muktiphalada
damādiguṇabhūṣaṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: O you indescribable by those who seek liberation, self-seen, victory, O Lord, [you who are] giver of the fruit of liberation to yogins adorned with the virtues of self-restraint and the rest!

body.text:
jayātisūkṣma durjñeya
jagat sthūla jaganmaya
jaya sthūlātisūkṣma tvaṃ
jayātīndriya sendriya
body.translated_text: Victory, O exceedingly subtle, hard to know, gross as the world, made of the world! Victory, O you [who are] gross and exceedingly subtle; victory, O you beyond the senses [yet] with the senses!

body.text:
jaya svamāyāyogastha
śeṣabhogaśayākṣara
body.translated_text: Victory, O you established in the yoga of your own <s>māyā</s>, imperishable one who lies on the couch of <s>Śeṣa</s>!

body.text: jayaikadaṃṣṭrāprāntānta
body.translated_text: Victory, O you whose extremity is the tip of a single tusk,

body.text: samuddhṛtavasuṃdhara
body.translated_text: O you who lifted up the earth!

body.text:
nṛkesariñ jayārāti-
vakṣaḥsthalavidāraṇa
sāṃprataṃ jaya viśvātman
māyāvāmana keśava
body.translated_text: O man-lion, victory, O render of the chest of the foe! Now, victory, O Self of all, O dwarf of <s>māyā</s>, <s>Keśava</s>!

body.text:
nijamāyāpaṭacchanna
jagaddhātar janārdana
jayācintya jayāneka-
svarūpaikavidha prabho
body.translated_text: O you veiled by the cloth of your own <s>māyā</s>, upholder of the world, <s>Janārdana</s>; victory, O inconceivable; victory, O you of manifold forms [yet] of a single mode, O Lord!

body.text:
vardhasva vardhitāneka-
vikāraprakṛte hare
tvayy eṣā jagatām īśa
saṃsthitā dharmapaddhatiḥ
body.translated_text: Grow, O <s>Hari</s>, whose nature is the source of manifold transformations [you have] caused to grow! In you, O Lord of the worlds, this course of <s>dharma</s> rests

body.text:
na tvām ahaṃ na ceśāno
nendrādyās tridaśā hare
jñātum īśā na munayaḥ
sanakādyā na yoginaḥ
body.translated_text: Neither I, nor <s>Īśāna</s>, nor <s>Indra</s> and the other thirty [gods], O <s>Hari</s>, are able to know [you], nor the sages <s>Sanaka</s> and the rest, nor the yogins

body.text:
tvanmāyāpaṭasaṃvīte
jagaty atra jagatpate
kas tvāṃ vetsyati sarveśaṃ
tvatprasādaṃ vinā naraḥ
body.translated_text: When this world is wrapped in the cloth of your <s>māyā</s>, O Lord of the world, what man will know you, the Lord of all, without your grace?

body.text:
tvam evārādhito yasya
prasādasumukhaḥ prabho
sa eva kevalaṃ deva
vetti tvāṃ netaro janaḥ
body.translated_text: He alone by whom you have been worshipped, [and toward whom you are] of gracious countenance, O Lord—he alone, O god, knows you, no other person

body.text:
tad īśvareśvareśāna
vibho vardhasva bhāvana
prabhāvāyāsya viśvasya
viśvātman pṛthulocana
body.translated_text: Therefore, O Lord of the lords of lords, O all-pervading, grow, O creative one, for the [increase of the] power of this universe, O Self of the universe, O wide-eyed one!'

body.text:
evaṃ stuto hṛṣīkeśaḥ
sa tadā vāmanākṛtiḥ
prahasya bhāvagambhīram
uvācābjasamudbhavam
body.translated_text: Thus praised, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, then in the dwarf-form, laughing, deep with [inner] feeling, spoke to the lotus-born:

body.text:
stuto 'haṃ bhavatā pūrvam
indrādyaiḥ kaśyapena ca
mayā ca vaḥ pratijñātam
indrasya bhuvanatrayam
body.translated_text: 'I was praised by you formerly, and by <s>Indra</s> and the rest and by <s>Kaśyapa</s>; and by me it was promised to you [all] the three worlds for <s>Indra</s>

body.text:
bhūyaś cāhaṃ stuto 'dityā
tasyāś cāpi pratiśrutam
yathā śakrāya dāsyāmi
trailokyaṃ hatakaṇṭakam
body.translated_text: And again I was praised by <s>Aditi</s>, and to her too it was promised, that I would give to <s>Śakra</s> the three worlds with their thorns destroyed

body.text:
so 'haṃ tathā kariṣyāmi
yathendro jagataḥ patiḥ
bhaviṣyati sahasrākṣaḥ
satyam etad bravīmi te
body.translated_text: So I shall act thus, so that <s>Indra</s>, the lord of the world, the thousand-eyed one, shall come to be [restored]—this truth I tell you'

body.text:
tataḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ brahmā
hṛṣīkeśāya dattavān
yajñopavītaṃ bhagavān
dadau tasmai bṛhaspatiḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> gave the black antelope-skin to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>; the Blessed <s>Bṛhaspati</s> gave to him the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>);

body.text:
āṣāḍham adadad daṇḍaṃ
marīcir brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ
kamaṇḍaluṃ vasiṣṭhaś ca
kauśyaṃ vedam athāṅgirāḥ
akṣasūtraṃ ca pulahaḥ
pulastyaḥ sitavāsasī
body.translated_text: <s>Marīci</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, gave the staff of <s>palāśa</s> wood; and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> the water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>); <s>Aṅgiras</s> [gave] the <s>Veda</s> in a leaf-bundle; and <s>Pulaha</s> the rosary (<s>akṣasūtra</s>); <s>Pulastya</s> the white garments

body.text:
upatasthuś ca taṃ vedāḥ
praṇavasvarabhūṣaṇāḥ
śāstrāṇy aśeṣāṇi tathā
sāṃkhyayogoktayaś ca yāḥ
body.translated_text: And the <s>Vedas</s> attended upon him, adorned with the tone of the <s>praṇava</s>, and likewise all the <s>śāstras</s>, and the doctrines of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>

body.text:
sa vāmano jaṭī daṇḍī
chattrī dhṛtakamaṇḍaluḥ
sarvadevamayo bhūpa
baler adhvaram abhyayāt
body.translated_text: That dwarf, matted-haired, staff-bearing, parasol-bearing, holding the water-pot, made of all the gods, O king, went to the sacrifice of <s>Bali</s>

body.text:
yatra yatra padaṃ bhūpa
bhūbhāge vāmano dadau
dadāti bhūmir vivaraṃ
tatra tatrātipīḍitā
body.translated_text: Wherever, O king, the dwarf set his foot upon a portion of the earth, the earth, exceedingly pressed, gave way [forming] a hollow there and there

body.text:
sa vāmano jaḍagatir
mṛdu gacchan saparvatām
sābdhidvīpavatīṃ sarvāṃ
cālayām āsa medinīm
body.translated_text: That dwarf, of slow gait, moving softly, set in motion the whole earth with its mountains, and with its oceans and islands

body.text:
tataḥ saṃśayam āpannāḥ
sarve daiteyadānavāḥ
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Daiteyas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> fell into doubt

body.text:
saparvatavanām urvīṃ
dṛṣṭvā saṃkṣubhitāṃ baliḥ
papracchośanasaṃ śukraṃ
praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ
body.translated_text: Seeing the earth with its mountains and forests agitated, <s>Bali</s> asked <s>Uśanas</s> <s>Śukra</s>, bowing down with joined palms:

body.text:
ācārya kṣobham āyāti
sābdhibhūbhṛddharā mahī
kasmāc ca nāsurān bhāgān
pratigṛhṇanti vahnayaḥ
body.translated_text: 'O teacher, the earth with its oceans and mountain-supports comes to agitation; and why do the fires not accept the <s>asura</s> shares [of the offering]?'

body.text:
iti pṛṣṭo 'tha balinā
kāvyo vedavidāṃ varaḥ
uvāca daityādhipatiṃ
ciraṃ dhyātvā mahāmatiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus asked by <s>Bali</s>, <s>Kāvya</s> (Śukra), best of the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, of great mind, having meditated long, said to the lord of the <s>daityas</s>:

body.text:
avatīrṇo jagadyoniḥ
kaśyapasya gṛhe hariḥ
vāmaneneha rūpeṇa
paramātmā sanātanaḥ
body.translated_text: 'The source of the world, <s>Hari</s>, the eternal Supreme Self, has descended in the house of <s>Kaśyapa</s> here in the dwarf-form

body.text:
sa nūnaṃ yajñam āyāti
tava dānavapuṅgava
tatpadanyāsavikṣobhād
iyaṃ pracalitā mahī
body.translated_text: He, surely, comes to your sacrifice, O bull among <s>dānavas</s>; by the agitation from the setting-down of his foot, this earth has been set trembling

body.text:
kampante girayaś cāmī
kṣubhitā makarālayāḥ
nainaṃ bhūtapatiṃ bhūmiḥ
samarthā voḍhum īśvaram
body.translated_text: And these mountains quake, agitated [with] the abodes of sea-monsters [the oceans]; the earth is not able to bear this Lord of beings, the Lord

body.text:
sadevāsuragandharva-
yakṣarākṣasapannagā
anenaiva dhṛtā bhūmir
āpo 'gniḥ pavano nabhaḥ
dhārayaty akhilān deva-
manuṣyādīn mahāsura
body.translated_text: By him alone is the earth upheld, together with the gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and serpents, [and] the waters, fire, wind, [and] sky; he upholds all the gods, men, and the rest, O great <s>asura</s>

body.text:
iyam asya jagaddhātur
māyā kṛṣṇasya gahvarī
dhāryadhārakabhāvena
yayā saṃpiṇḍitaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: This is the deep <s>māyā</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the upholder of the world, by which, through the relation of the supported and the supporter, the world is compacted together

body.text:
tatsaṃnidhānād asurā
na bhāgārhāḥ suradviṣaḥ
bhuñjate cāsurān bhāgān
amī te na tavāgnayaḥ
body.translated_text: Through his presence, the <s>asuras</s>, the foes of the gods, are not worthy of [their] shares; and these fires of yours, not yours, are enjoying the <s>asura</s> shares'

body.text:
śukrasya vacanaṃ śrutvā
hṛṣṭaromābravīd baliḥ
body.translated_text: Having heard the speech of <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Bali</s>, his hair bristling [with joy], said:

body.text:
dhanyo 'haṃ kṛtapuṇyaś ca
yan me yajñapatiḥ svayam
yajñam abhyāgato brahman
mattaḥ ko 'nyo 'dhikaḥ pumān
body.translated_text: "Blessed am I, and one who has done meritorious deeds, in that the Lord of sacrifice himself has come to my sacrifice, O <s>brahman</s>; what other man is greater than I?

body.text:
yaṃ yoginaḥ sadodyuktāḥ
paramātmānam avyayam
draṣṭum icchanti devo 'sau
madadhvaram upaiṣyati
body.translated_text: He whom the <s>yogins</s>, ever striving, wish to behold, the imperishable Supreme Self—that god will come to my sacrifice

body.text:
hotā bhāgaprado yasya
yam udgātā ca gāyati
tam adhvareśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ
mattaḥ ko 'nya upaiṣyati
body.translated_text: He of whom the <s>hotṛ</s> is the giver of the [sacrificial] portion, and whom the <s>udgātṛ</s> sings—that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of sacrifice, what other than I will [he] approach?

body.text:
sarveśvareśvare viṣṇau
mamādhvaram upāgate
yan mayā cārya kartavyaṃ
tan mamādeṣṭum arhasi
body.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of the lords of all, has come to my sacrifice, whatever is to be done by me, O noble one, that you ought to instruct me"

body.text:
yajñabhāgabhujo devā
vedaprāmāṇyato 'sura
tvayā tu dānavā daityā
yajñabhāgabhujaḥ kṛtāḥ
body.translated_text: "The gods are the enjoyers of the sacrificial share, by the authority of the <s>Veda</s>, O <s>asura</s>; but by you the <s>dānavas</s> and <s>daityas</s> have been made enjoyers of the sacrificial share

body.text:
ayaṃ ca devaḥ sattvasthaḥ
karoti sthitipālanam
nisṛṣṭeś cāyam ante ca
svayam atti prajāḥ prabhuḥ
body.translated_text: And this god, abiding in goodness (<s>sattva</s>), performs the maintenance and protection [of the world]; and at the end of the creation, he, the Lord, himself devours the creatures

body.text:
tvayānubandhī bhavitā
nūnaṃ viṣṇuḥ sthitau sthitaḥ
viditvaitan mahābhāga
kuru yat te manogatam
body.translated_text: Surely <s>Viṣṇu</s>, established in [the function of] maintenance, will be one bound up with you; knowing this, O greatly fortunate one, do what is in your mind

body.text:
tvayāsya daityādhipate
svalpake 'pi hi vastuni
pratijñā naiva voḍhavyā
vācyaṃ sāma tathāphalam
body.translated_text: By you, O lord of <s>daityas</s>, even in a trifling matter, no promise should be broken; the conciliatory word (<s>sāma</s>) is [otherwise] to be spoken as fruitless

body.text:
kṛtakṛtyasya devasya
devārthaṃ caiva kurvataḥ
body.translated_text: Of the god who has accomplished his purpose, and who indeed acts for the sake of the gods,

body.text:
nālaṃ dātuṃ dhanaṃ devety
evaṃ vācyaṃ tu yācataḥ
kṛṣṇasya devabhūtyarthaṃ
pravṛttasya mahāsura
body.translated_text: 'There is not wealth enough to give, O god'—thus is it to be said to one who begs; [but] of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, engaged for the sake of the prosperity of the gods, O great <s>asura</s> [it is not to be said]"

body.text:
brahman katham ahaṃ brūyām
anyenāpi hi yācitaḥ
nāstīti kimu devena
saṃsārāghaughahāriṇā
body.translated_text: "O <s>brahman</s>, how should I say 'there is not,' even when begged by another? How much less to the god, the remover of the flood of the [ocean of] <s>saṃsāra</s>?

body.text:
vratopavāsair vividhair
yaḥ pratigrāhyate hariḥ
sa ced vakṣyati dehīti
govindaḥ kim ato 'dhikam
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, who is made to receive [offerings] by various vows and fasts—if he should say 'give,' [he being] <s>Govinda</s>, what is greater than that?

body.text:
yadartham upahārāḍhyā
damaśaucaguṇānvitaiḥ
yajñāḥ kriyante deveśaḥ
sa māṃ dehīti vakṣyati
body.translated_text: For whose sake sacrifices, rich in oblations, are performed by those endowed with the qualities of self-control and purity—that Lord of gods will say to me 'give'

body.text:
tat sādhu sukṛtaṃ karma
tapaḥ sucaritaṃ ca naḥ
yan mayā dattam īśeśaḥ
svayam ādāsyate hariḥ
body.translated_text: Then good and well-done is our deed, austerity and good conduct, in that what was given by me, the Lord of lords, <s>Hari</s> himself will take

body.text:
nāstīty ahaṃ guro vakṣye
tam apy āgatam īśvaram
yadi tad vañcyate prāpte
nūnam asmadvidhaḥ phalaiḥ
body.translated_text: Should I, O guru, say 'there is not' even to that Lord come [to me]?—If he, having arrived, is to be deceived, then surely [one] of our sort [is undone] in respect of [the] fruits

body.text:
yajñe 'smin yadi yajñeśo
yācate māṃ janārdanaḥ
nijamūrdhānam apy adya
tad dāsyāmy avicāritam
body.translated_text: If at this sacrifice the Lord of sacrifice, <s>Janārdana</s>, begs of me, then today I shall give even my own head, without hesitation

body.text:
nāstīti yan mayā noktam
anyeṣām api yācatām
vakṣyāmi katham āyāte
tad anabhyastam acyute
body.translated_text: That 'there is not' was not spoken by me even to others who begged; how should I speak it when <s>Acyuta</s> has come?—that is unpracticed [by me]

body.text:
ślāghya eva hi dhīrāṇāṃ
dānād āpatsamāgamaḥ
nābādhākāri yad dānaṃ
tad aṅgamalavat katham
body.translated_text: For the steadfast, the encounter with misfortune through giving is indeed praiseworthy; how is a gift that causes no distress [to be valued]?—it is like the filth of a limb

body.text:
madrājye nāsukhī kaścin
na daridro na cāturaḥ
nātṛṣito na codvigno
na sragādivivarjitaḥ
body.translated_text: In my kingdom no one is unhappy, none poor, none afflicted, none thirsty, none agitated, none devoid of garlands and the rest

body.text:
hṛṣṭatuṣṭaḥ sugandhī ca
tṛptaḥ sarvasukhānvitaḥ
janaḥ sarvo mahābhāga
kimutāhaṃ sadā sukhī
body.translated_text: Glad, content, fragrant, satisfied, endowed with all happiness is every person, O greatly fortunate one—how much more I, ever happy

body.text:
etad viśiṣṭapātrotthaṃ
dānabījaphalaṃ mama
viditaṃ bhṛguśārdūla
mayaitat tvatprasādataḥ
body.translated_text: This fruit of the seed of giving, arisen from an excellent recipient, is known to me, O tiger among the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, through your grace

body.text:
etad vijānato dāna-
bījaṃ patati ced guro
janārdane mahāpātre
kiṃ na prāptaṃ tato mayā
body.translated_text: If the seed of giving, of me who know this, falls upon <s>Janārdana</s>, the great recipient, what has not [then] been gained by me thereby?

body.text:
matto dānam avāpyeśo
yadi puṣṇāti devatāḥ
upabhogānvayaguṇaṃ
dānaṃ ślāghyataraṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: If the Lord, having obtained the gift from me, nourishes the deities, then the gift connected with [their] enjoyment is the more praiseworthy

body.text:
matprasādaparo nūnaṃ
yajñenārādhito hariḥ
tenābhyeti na saṃdeho
darśanād upakārakṛt
body.translated_text: Surely <s>Hari</s>, intent on grace toward me, worshipped by the sacrifice, by that comes [here]—there is no doubt—doing a benefit by [his very] sight

body.text:
atha kopena vābhyeti
devabhāgoparodhinam
māṃ nihantum ato 'pi syād
vadhaḥ ślāghyataro 'cyutāt
body.translated_text: Or if he comes in anger to slay me, the obstructer of the gods' share, then even so, the slaying by <s>Acyuta</s> is the more praiseworthy

body.text:
yanmayaṃ sarvam evedaṃ
nāprāpya yasya vidyate
sa māṃ yācitum abhyeti
nānugraham ṛte hariḥ
body.translated_text: All this consists of him; without attaining whom nothing exists—he, <s>Hari</s>, comes to beg of me [only] out of grace

body.text:
yaḥ sṛjaty ātmabhūḥ sarvaṃ
cetasaivāpahanti ca
sa māṃ hantuṃ hṛṣīkeśaḥ
kathaṃ yatnaṃ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: He who, self-born, creates all and by [mere] thought destroys [it]—how will <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> make an effort to slay me?

body.text:
etad viditvā tu guro
dānavighnapareṇa me
naiva bhāvyaṃ jagannāthe
govinde samupasthite
body.translated_text: Knowing this, O guru, I should by no means become one intent on obstructing the gift, when the Lord of the world, <s>Govinda</s>, has come"

body.text:
ity evaṃ vadatas tasya
prāptas tatra jagapatiḥ
sarvadevamayo 'cintyo
māyāvāmanarūpadhṛk
body.translated_text: While he was speaking thus, the Lord of the world arrived there, consisting of all the gods, inconceivable, bearing by <s>Māyā</s> the form of <s>Vāmana</s> (the dwarf)

body.text:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā yajñavāṭāntaḥ-
praviṣṭam asurāḥ prabhum
jagmuḥ prabhāvataḥ kṣobhaṃ
tejasā tasya niṣprabhāḥ
body.translated_text: Seeing that Lord entered within the sacrificial enclosure, the <s>asuras</s> went into agitation through his might, made dim by his splendour

body.text:
jepuś ca munayas tatra
ye sametā mahādhvare
baliś caivākhilaṃ janma
mene saphalam ātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: And the sages there, who were gathered at the great sacrifice, recited [prayers]; and <s>Bali</s> deemed his whole birth fruitful

body.text:
tataḥ saṃkṣobham āpanno
na kaścit kiṃcid uktavān
pratyeko devadeveśaṃ
pūjayām āsa cetasā
body.translated_text: Then, fallen into agitation, no one said anything; each one worshipped the Lord of the gods of gods in his mind

body.text:
athāsurapatiṃ prahvaṃ
dṛṣṭvā munivarāṃś ca tān
devadevapatiḥ sākṣād
viṣṇur vāmanarūpadhṛk
body.translated_text: Then, seeing the lord of the <s>asuras</s> bowed and those best of sages, the Lord of the gods of gods himself, <s>Viṣṇu</s> bearing the form of <s>Vāmana</s>,

body.text:
tuṣṭāva yajñaṃ vahniṃś ca
yajamānam atha rtvijaḥ
yajñakarādhikārasthān
sadasyān dravyasaṃpadam
body.translated_text: praised the sacrifice and the fire, and the sacrificer, then the priests, the assembly-members holding office in the sacrificial work, and the wealth of substances

body.text:
tataḥ prasannam akhilaṃ
vāmanaṃ prati tatkṣaṇāt
yajñavāṭasthitaṃ vīraṃ
sādhu sādhv ity udīrayan
body.translated_text: Then the whole [assembly], pleased, at that very instant cried 'Excellent, excellent!' toward <s>Vāmana</s>, the hero standing in the sacrificial enclosure

body.text:
sa cārgham ādāya baliḥ
prodbhūtapulakas tadā
pūjayām āsa govindaṃ
prāha cedaṃ vaco 'suraḥ
body.translated_text: And that <s>Bali</s>, taking the <s>argha</s>-water, then with hair bristling, worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, and the <s>asura</s> spoke this word:

body.text:
suvarṇaratnasaṃghātaṃ
gajāśvam amitaṃ tathā
striyo vastrāṇy alaṃkārān
gāvo grāmāṃś ca puṣkalān
body.translated_text: "A mass of gold and jewels, and elephants and horses without limit, women, garments, ornaments, cows, and abundant villages,

body.text:
sarvasvaṃ sakalām urvīṃ
bhavato vā yad īpsitam
tad dadāmi vṛṇuṣva tvaṃ
mamārthī satataṃ priyaḥ
body.translated_text: all my possessions, the entire earth, or whatever is desired by you—that I give; choose, you, who are ever dear to me, [my] suppliant"

body.text:
ity ukto daityapatinā
prītigarvānvitaṃ vacaḥ
prāha sasmitagambhīraṃ
bhagavān vāmanākṛtiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by the lord of <s>daityas</s> with words full of joy and pride, the Blessed Lord of the dwarf-form spoke, smiling and grave:

body.text:
mamāgniśaraṇārthāya
dehi rājan padatrayam
suvarṇagrāmaratnādi
tad arthibhyaḥ pradīyatām
body.translated_text: "For the sake of my fire-shelter, O king, give three paces [of land]; the gold, villages, jewels and the rest—let those be given to suppliants"

body.text:
tribhiḥ prayojanaṃ kiṃ te
padaiḥ padavatāṃ vara
śataṃ śatasahasraṃ vā
padānāṃ mārgatāṃ bhavān
body.translated_text: "What use to you of three paces, O best of those who possess [vast] strides? Let your honour seek a hundred or a hundred thousand paces

body.text:
etāvatā daityapate
kṛtakṛtyo 'smi mārgatām
anyeṣām arthināṃ vittam
icchayā dāsyate bhavān
body.translated_text: By [only] so much, O lord of <s>daityas</s>, I am one whose purpose is accomplished; let your honour seek [them]; the wealth of other suppliants you shall give by [their] wish"

body.text:
etac chrutvā tu gaditaṃ
vāmanasya mahātmanaḥ
vācayām āsa tat tasmai
vāmanāya padatrayam
body.translated_text: Having heard this spoken by the great-souled <s>Vāmana</s>, [Bali] formally granted to him those three paces, [decreed] for that <s>Vāmana</s>

body.text:
pāṇau tu patite toye
vāmano bhūtabhāvanaḥ
sarvadevamayaṃ rūpaṃ
darśayām āsa tatkṣaṇāt
body.translated_text: When the water fell into [Vāmana's] hand, <s>Vāmana</s>, the source of beings, showed at that very instant his form consisting of all the gods:

body.text:
candrasūryau ca nayane
dyauḥ śiraś caraṇau kṣitiḥ
pādāṅgulyaḥ piśācāś ca
hastāṅgulyaś ca guhyakāḥ
body.translated_text: the moon and sun [were] his two eyes, the heaven his head, the earth his feet; the toes [were] the <s>piśācas</s>, and the fingers the <s>Guhyakas</s>,

body.text:
viśvedevāś ca jānusthā
jaṅghe sādhyāḥ surottamāḥ
yakṣā nakheṣu saṃbhūtā
rekhāsv apsarasaḥ sthitāḥ
body.translated_text: and the <s>Viśvedevas</s> situated at the knees, the two shanks [were] the <s>Sādhyas</s>, best of gods; the <s>Yakṣas</s> were produced in the nails, the <s>Apsarases</s> stationed in the lines [of his palms]

body.text:
dṛṣṭir dhiṣṇāny aśeṣāṇi
keśāḥ sūryāṃśavaḥ prabho
tārakā romakūpāṇi
romāṇi ca maharṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: His glance [was] all the [celestial] mansions, his hairs the rays of the sun, O Lord; the stars [were] the hair-pores, and the hairs the great seers

body.text:
bāhavo vidiśas tasya
diśaḥ śrotraṃ mahātmanaḥ
aśvinau śravaṇau tasya
nāsā vāyur mahābalaḥ
body.translated_text: His arms [were] the intermediate quarters, the [main] quarters the ears of that great soul; the two <s>Aśvins</s> [were] his two ears, his nose the mighty <s>Vāyu</s> (wind)

body.text:
prasādaś candramā devo
mano dharmaḥ samāśritaḥ
satyam asyābhavad vāṇī
jihvā devī sarasvatī
body.translated_text: [His] graciousness [was] the god Moon, [his] mind <s>Dharma</s> abiding [in him]; his speech became Truth, his tongue the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>

body.text:
grīvāditir devamātā
vidyās tadvalayas tathā
svargadvāram abhūn maitraṃ
tvaṣṭā pūṣā ca vai bhruvau
body.translated_text: His neck [was] <s>Aditi</s>, mother of the gods, and likewise the sciences [were] his armlets; the door of heaven became the [constellation] <s>Maitra</s> [Anurādhā], and <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> indeed [were] his two eyebrows

body.text:
mukhaṃ vaiśvānaraś cāsya
vṛṣaṇau tu prajāpatiḥ
hṛdayaṃ ca paraṃ brahma
puṃstvaṃ vai kaśyapo muniḥ
body.translated_text: And his mouth [was] <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (fire), his testicles <s>Prajāpati</s>, and his heart the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, his virility indeed the sage <s>Kaśyapa</s>

body.text:
pṛṣṭhe 'sya vasavo devā
marutaḥ sarvasaṃdhiṣu
sarvasūktāni daśanā
jyotīṃṣi vimalaprabhāḥ
body.translated_text: On his back [were] the <s>Vasu</s> gods, the <s>Maruts</s> in all his joints; all the [Vedic] hymns [were] his teeth, the luminaries of stainless light [...]

body.text:
vakṣaḥsthale tathā rudro
dhairye cāsya mahārṇavaḥ
udare cāsya gandharvā
marutaś ca mahābalāḥ
lakṣmīr medhā dhṛtiḥ kāntiḥ
sarvavidyāś ca vai kaṭiḥ
body.translated_text: And on his chest likewise <s>Rudra</s>, and in his steadfastness the great ocean; and in his belly the <s>Gandharvas</s> and the mighty <s>Maruts</s>; <s>Lakṣmī</s>, intelligence, constancy, beauty, and all the sciences indeed [were] his loins

body.text:
sarvajyotīṃṣi yānīha
tapaś ca paramaṃ mahat
tasya devātidevasya
tejaḥ prodbhūtam uttamam
body.translated_text: All the luminaries that are here, and the supreme great austerity—of that god above gods, the splendour [therefrom] arose, the highest

body.text:
stanau kukṣau ca vedāś ca
jānū cāsya mahāmakhāḥ
iṣṭayaḥ paśubandhāś ca
dvijānāṃ ceṣṭitāni ca
body.translated_text: His two breasts and belly [were] the <s>Vedas</s>, and his two knees the great sacrifices, the <s>iṣṭi</s> and animal-bindings, and the [ritual] acts of the twice-born

body.text:
tasya devamayaṃ rūpaṃ
dṛṣṭvā viṣṇor mahābalāḥ
upasarpanti daiteyāḥ
pataṃgā iva pāvakam
body.translated_text: Seeing that god-consisting form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the mighty <s>Daiteyas</s> rushed upon [him] like moths upon a fire

body.text:
pramathya sarvān asurān
pādahastatalair vibhuḥ
kṛtvā rūpaṃ mahākāyaṃ
sa jahārāśu medinīm
body.translated_text: Having crushed all the <s>asuras</s> with the soles of his feet and hands, the all-pervading one, having made [his] form of vast body, swiftly seized the earth

body.text:
tasya vikramato bhumiṃ
candrādityau stanāntare
nabho vikramamāṇasya
sakthideśe sthitāv ubhau
body.translated_text: As he strode over the earth, the moon and sun [were] between his breasts; as he strode the sky, both [were] situated in the region of his thighs

body.text:
paraṃ vikramamāṇasya
jānumūle prabhākarau
viṣṇor āstām mahīpāla
devapālanakarmaṇi
body.translated_text: As he strode the highest [region], the two light-makers [sun and moon] were at the base of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s knees, O protector of the earth, in the work of protecting the gods

body.text:
jitvā lokatrayaṃ kṛtsnaṃ
hatvā cāsurapuṅgavān
puraṃdarāya trailokyaṃ
dadau viṣṇur urukramaḥ
body.translated_text: Having conquered the whole triple world and slain the bulls among the <s>asuras</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> of wide strides (<s>Urukrama</s>) gave the triple world to <s>Puraṃdara</s> (Indra)

body.text:
sutalaṃ nāma pātālam
adhastād vasudhātalāt
baler dattaṃ bhagavatā
viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
body.translated_text: The nether world named <s>Sutala</s>, below the surface of the earth, was given to <s>Bali</s> by the Blessed all-powerful <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
atha daityeśvaraṃ prāha
viṣṇuḥ sarveśvareśvaraḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of the lords of all, spoke to the lord of the <s>daityas</s>:

body.text:
yat tvayā salilaṃ dattaṃ
gṛhītaṃ pāṇinā mayā
kalpapramāṇaṃ tasmāt te
bhaviṣyaty āyur uttamam
body.translated_text: "Since the water given by you was received by my hand, therefore for you an excellent lifespan of a <s>kalpa</s>'s measure shall be

body.text:
vaivasvate tathātīte
bale manvantare tataḥ
sāvarṇake ca saṃprāpte
bhavān indro bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: And when the <s>Vaivasvata</s> <s>manvantara</s> has passed, O <s>Bali</s>, and the <s>Sāvarṇika</s> [manvantara] has arrived, your honour shall become <s>Indra</s>

body.text:
sāṃprataṃ devarājāya
trailokyam akhilaṃ mayā
dattaṃ caturyugānāṃ vai
sādhikā hy ekasaptatiḥ
body.translated_text: At present, to the king of the gods the entire triple world has been given by me for the four ages, indeed for a [period] exceeding seventy-one [cycles of four ages]

body.text:
niyantavyā mayā sarve
ye tasya paripanthinaḥ
tenāhaṃ parayā bhaktyā
pūrvam ārādhito bale
body.translated_text: All those who are his adversaries are to be restrained by me; therefore I was formerly worshipped by you with supreme devotion, O <s>Bali</s>

body.text:
sutalaṃ nāma pātālaṃ
tam āsādya manoramam
vasāsura mamādeśaṃ
yathāvat paripālayan
body.translated_text: Having reached that delightful nether world named <s>Sutala</s>, dwell, O <s>asura</s>, duly observing my command,

body.text:
tatra divyavanopete
prāsādaśatasaṃkule
protphullapadmasarasi
sravacchuddhasaridvare
body.translated_text: there, [in a region] possessed of divine groves, crowded with hundreds of palaces, with lakes of full-blown lotuses, with flowing, pure, excellent rivers,

body.text:
sugandhidhūpasaṃbādhe
varābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ
srakcandanādidigdhāṅgo
nṛtyagītamanoramaiḥ
body.translated_text: thick with fragrant incense, adorned with excellent ornaments, your limbs smeared with garlands, sandal and the rest, [amid] charming dances and songs,

body.text:
upabhuñjan mahābhogān
vividhān dānaveśvara
mamājñayā kālam imaṃ
tiṣṭha strīśatasaṃvṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: enjoying great and various pleasures, O lord of <s>dānavas</s>, by my command, abide for this time, surrounded by a hundred women

body.text:
yāvat suraiś ca vipraiś ca
na virodhaṃ kariṣyasi
tāvad etān mahābhogān
avāpsyasy asurottama
body.translated_text: As long as you make no opposition to the gods and the <s>vipras</s>, so long shall you obtain these great enjoyments, O best of <s>asuras</s>

body.text:
yadā ca devaviprāṇāṃ
viruddhāny ācariṣyasi
bandhiṣyanti tathā pāśā
vāruṇās tvām asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: And when you shall practice things hostile to the gods and <s>vipras</s>, then the nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s> shall bind you, without doubt

body.text:
etad viditvā bhavatā
mayājñaptam aśeṣataḥ
na virodhaḥ suraiḥ kāryo
viprair vā daityasattama
body.translated_text: Knowing this, [let it be] commanded by me to your honour entirely: no opposition is to be made to the gods or to the <s>vipras</s>, O best of <s>daityas</s>"

body.text:
ity evam ukto devena
viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
baliḥ prāha mahārāja
praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by the god <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-powerful, <s>Bali</s>, O great king, having bowed with joined palms, spoke:

body.text:
tatrāsato me pātāle
bhagavan bhavadājñayā
kiṃ bhaviṣyaty upādānam
upabhogopapādakam
body.translated_text: "For me dwelling there in the nether world, O Blessed One, by your command, what shall be the [means of] subsistence that furnishes [my] enjoyment,

body.text:
āpyāyito yena deva
smareyaṃ tvām ahaṃ sadā
body.translated_text: by which, satisfied, O god, I may ever remember you?"

body.text:
dānāny avidhidattāni
śrāddhāny aśrotriyāṇi ca
hutāny aśraddhayā yāni
tāni dāsyanti te phalam
body.translated_text: "Gifts given without [proper] rule, <s>śrāddhas</s> [given] to non-learned [brāhmaṇas], and oblations offered without faith—those shall give you their fruit

body.text:
adakṣiṇās tathā yajñāḥ
kriyāś cāvidhinā kṛtāḥ
phalāni tava dāsyanti
adhītāny avratāni ca
body.translated_text: And sacrifices without fees, and rites performed without [proper] rule, and recitations [made] without [proper] vows—they shall give their fruits to you"

body.text:
baler varam idaṃ dattvā
śakrāya trividaṃ tathā
vyāpinā tena rūpeṇa
jagāmādarśanaṃ hariḥ
body.translated_text: Having given this boon to <s>Bali</s>, and likewise the triple world to <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Hari</s>, by that all-pervading form, went to invisibility

body.text:
śaśāsa ca yathā pūrvam
indras trailokyam ūrjitam
siṣeva ca parān kāmān
baliḥ pātālam āśritaḥ
body.translated_text: And <s>Indra</s> ruled the mighty triple world as before, and <s>Bali</s>, resorting to the nether world, enjoyed supreme delights

body.text:
ity etad devadevasya
viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam
vāmanasya paṭhed yas tu
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: Thus this supreme greatness of the god of gods <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of <s>Vāmana</s>—he who reads it is freed from all sins

body.text:
baliprahrādasaṃvādaṃ
mantritaṃ baliśukrayoḥ
baliviṣṇvoś ca kathitaṃ
yaḥ smariṣyati mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: The man who shall remember the dialogue of <s>Bali</s> and <s>Prahlāda</s>, the counsel of <s>Bali</s> and <s>Śukra</s>, and the dialogue, [here] told, of <s>Bali</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

body.text:
nādhayo vyādhayo vāsya
na ca mohākulaṃ manaḥ
bhaviṣyati kuruśreṣṭha
puṃsas tasya kadācana
body.translated_text: for that man there shall never be mental ills nor diseases, nor a mind agitated by delusion, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>

body.text:
cyutarājyo nijaṃ rājyam
iṣṭaprāptiṃ viyogavān
avāpnoti mahābhāga
naraḥ śrutvā kathām imām
body.translated_text: One fallen from kingship [obtains] his own kingdom, one separated [from a loved one obtains] the attainment of what he desires—a man attains [this], O greatly fortunate one, having heard this tale

body.text:
pātāle nivasan vīras
tadā vairocanir baliḥ
kāmopabhogasaṃprāptyā
mudaṃ prāpa parāṃ vibhuḥ
body.translated_text: Dwelling in the nether world then, the hero <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>, by the attainment of the enjoyment of pleasures, attained supreme joy, the mighty one

body.text:
alaṃbuṣā miśrakeśī
puṇḍarīkātha vāmanā
ghṛtācī menakā rambhā
nanṛtus tasya saṃnidhau
body.translated_text: <s>Alaṃbuṣā</s>, <s>Miśrakeśī</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkā</s>, then <s>Vāmanā</s>, <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, <s>Menakā</s>, <s>Rambhā</s>—danced in his presence

body.text:
prajagur devagandharvā
viśvāvasupurogamāḥ
tuṣṭuvuś ca mahābhāga
baliṃ siddhāḥ sacāraṇāḥ
body.translated_text: The divine <s>Gandharvas</s>, headed by <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, sang, and the <s>Siddhas</s> together with the <s>Cāraṇas</s> praised <s>Bali</s>, O greatly fortunate one

body.text:
tasmin saṃgītagītā tu
vīṇāveṇuravākule
sragādibhūṣito daityaḥ
papau pānam anuttamam
body.translated_text: While the concert was sung there, [the place] resounding with lutes and flutes, the <s>daitya</s>, adorned with garlands and the rest, drank the most excellent drink:

body.text:
śarkārasavamādhvikāṃ
puṣpāsavaphalāsavam
divyāḥ prasannāś ca surās
tadarhāṇi madhūni ca
body.translated_text: [liquor] of sugar-syrup and honey, the wine of flowers and the wine of fruits—and the divine, clear liquors, and the meads befitting him

body.text:
parāvadaṃśān madhurāṃl
lavaṇāṃs tiktakāṇ kaṭūn
kaṣāyāṃś ca mahārāja
sumṛṣṭāny aparāṇi ca
body.translated_text: [foods] sour, pungent, sweet, salty, bitter, and sharp, and astringent, O great king, and others very well-prepared,

body.text:
suhṛṭsujanasaṃbandhi-
bhṛtyavargasamanvitaḥ
bubhuje pātālagatas
tadā vairocanir baliḥ
body.translated_text: accompanied by his host of friends, good people, kinsmen, and servants, then <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>, gone to the nether world, enjoyed [them]

body.text:
prāsādāḥ kāñcanāḥ sarve
suvarṇamaṇimaṇḍitāḥ
sphāṭikāmalasopānā
muktāhāraśatojjvalāḥ
body.translated_text: All the palaces were golden, adorned with gold and gems, with stainless crystal stairways, gleaming with a hundred strands of pearls

body.text:
teṣu sarveṣu daiteyā
baleḥ saṃbandhibāndhavāḥ
nṛtyavādyādimuditā
bubhujur viṣayān priyān
body.translated_text: In all of those the <s>daiteyas</s>, the kinsmen and relatives of <s>Bali</s>, delighting in dance, music, and the rest, enjoyed their dear sense-objects

body.text:
baliś ca bhagavān daityo
daityoragaśatair vṛtaḥ
upagīyamāno bubhuje
yatheṣṭaṃ viṣayān priyān
body.translated_text: And the Blessed <s>daitya</s> <s>Bali</s>, surrounded by hundreds of <s>daityas</s> and <s>uragas</s> (serpents), being sung to, enjoyed at will the dear sense-objects

body.text:
patnī vindhyāvalī nāma
tasya daityapater abhūt
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇā
śrīr ivābjaṃ vināparā
body.translated_text: He, that lord of the <s>daityas</s>, had a wife named <s>Vindhyāvalī</s>, complete in all auspicious marks, like <s>Śrī</s> [Lakṣmī] without [her] lotus, none other [like her]

body.text:
na devī nāpi gandharvī
nāpsarā na ca mānuṣī
tasyā rūpeṇa sadṛśī
babhūva manujeśvara
body.translated_text: Neither a goddess, nor a <s>gandharvī</s>, nor an <s>apsaras</s>, nor a human woman, similar to her in beauty came to be, O lord of men

body.text:
sā tu pīnāyataśroṇī
mṛdvaṅgī madhurasvarā
ghanonnatakucā subhrūḥ
sasmitāyatalocanā
body.translated_text: She, with full broad hips, of soft limbs, of sweet voice, with dense uplifted breasts, of fair brows, with smiling long eyes,

body.text:
mṛdvalpapāṇipādābjā
sumadhyā gajagāminī
sukeśī sumukhī śyāmā
sarvair yoṣidguṇair yutā
body.translated_text: with soft small lotus-like hands and feet, of fair waist, walking like an elephant, of fair hair, of fair face, dark-hued, endowed with all the qualities of a woman,

body.text:
tanayā merusāvarṇer
dauhitrī mṛgamokinaḥ
body.translated_text: the daughter of <s>Merusāvarṇi</s>, the granddaughter of <s>Mṛgamokin</s>,

body.text:
vapuṣā rūpasaṃpadā
pautanā mṛgalocanā
body.translated_text: by her body and wealth of beauty, [she who was] like a [daughter of] Pautana, doe-eyed,

body.text:
patnī sahasradvitaye
pradhānā tasya sābhavat
body.translated_text: she became his chief wife among two thousand

body.text:
tayā tu ramatas tasya
ramaṇīye rasātale
śaktir āsīd anudinaṃ
vivekapratilominī
body.translated_text: And as he sported with her in the delightful nether world, day by day there arose a power [in him] contrary to discrimination

body.text:
kadācid ramatas tasya
daityarājasya pārthiva
tīkṣṇāṃśur madhyamāṃ vīthīṃ
yayau vaiṣuvatīṃ raviḥ
body.translated_text: Once, as that king of the <s>daityas</s> sported, O king, the sharp-rayed sun went along the middle path, the equinoctial

body.text:
yadā yadā ca viṣuvaṃ
bhāskaraḥ pratipadyate
tadā tadā hareś cakraṃ
pātāle parivartate
body.translated_text: And whenever the sun reaches the equinox, then the discus of <s>Hari</s> revolves in the nether world

body.text:
sravanti yoṣitāṃ garbhās
tasya dhārāṃśutāpitāḥ
sahasā daityapatnīnāṃ
yāsu puṃsāṃ samudbhavaḥ
nistejaso daityabhaṭā
bhavanti ca mahīpate
body.translated_text: The wombs of the women flow, heated by the rays of its stream—suddenly, of the wives of the <s>daityas</s>, in whom there is the birth of males; and the warriors of the <s>daityas</s> become bereft of splendor, O lord of the earth

body.text:
tad dṛṣṭvā sahasāyāntam
ādityaśatatejasam
jvālāmālāsuduḥprekṣyaṃ
viṣṇucakraṃ sudarśanam
hāhākṛtam abhūt sarvaṃ
pātālam arisūdana
body.translated_text: Seeing it suddenly coming, of the splendor of a hundred suns, exceedingly hard to behold for its garland of flames, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus <s>Sudarśana</s>—all the nether world became filled with cries of woe, O slayer of foes

body.text:
jepur ye munayas tatra
sārghapātrā mahoragāḥ
babhūvuḥ praṇatāś cānye
siddhagandharvacāraṇāḥ
vaiklavyaṃ cāgatāḥ sarvāḥ
striyaḥ parapuraṃjaya
body.translated_text: The sages there muttered [prayers], the great <s>uragas</s> with oblation-vessels; others became bowed down—the <s>siddhas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>cāraṇas</s>; and all the women came to distress, O conqueror of enemy cities

body.text:
tad dṛṣṭvā vyākulībhūtaṃ
pātālam asurās tataḥ
ye tasthuḥ pauruṣaparās
te hatāḥ śataneminā
body.translated_text: Seeing the nether world thus thrown into confusion, the <s>asuras</s> who then stood, intent on their manliness, were slain by the hundred-rimmed [discus]

body.text:
bhrāmyatā tena cakreṇa
saptalokavicāriṇā
samastajagadādhāra-
karamuktena veginā
body.translated_text: by that whirling discus that ranges through the seven worlds, the support of the entire universe, released from the hand [of Viṣṇu], swift,

body.text:
tan niṣūditadaityaughaṃ
daityastrīgarbhahānidam
śrutvā cakraṃ mahācakro
niścakrāma gṛhād baliḥ
body.translated_text: Having heard of that discus, the destroyer of the host of <s>daityas</s>, the despoiler of the wombs of the <s>daitya</s>-women, <s>Bali</s>, the great wheel[-wielder], rushed out of his house

body.text:
āḥ kim etad itīty uktvā
sa tu madyamahoddhataḥ
vimalaṃ khaḍgam ādāya
śatacandraṃ ca bhānumat
body.translated_text: "Ah! what is this?"—thus saying, he, exceedingly puffed up with the great pride of intoxication, having taken up his stainless sword bright as the sun, [adorned] with a hundred moons,

body.text:
niryāntam atha vegena
tam udāraparākramam
vidhyāvalī nāma śubhā
dadhāra dayitaṃ patim
body.translated_text: then, as he went forth in haste, that one of noble prowess, the auspicious [woman] named <s>Vindhyāvalī</s> restrained her beloved husband,

body.text:
uvāca ca pariṣvajya
krodhatāmrekṣaṇaṃ balim
kalyāṇī guṇadoṣajñā
praṇayān mṛdubhāṣiṇī
body.translated_text: and embracing <s>Bali</s>, his eyes copper-red with anger, the blessed one, knower of merits and faults, soft-spoken out of love, said:

body.text:
daityarāja na kopasya
vaśam āgantum arhasi
vimṛśya tajjñaḥ sāmādīn
prayuñjīta balābalam
body.translated_text: "O king of the <s>daityas</s>, you ought not to come under the sway of anger; one who knows that [statecraft], having reflected, should apply conciliation and the rest, [weighing] strength and weakness"

body.text:
kim etat kasya vā kutra
kiṃnimittam ihāgatam
cakram itthaṃ vicārya tvaṃ
krodhaṃ yāhi praśāmya vā
body.translated_text: "What is this, or whose, or whence, for what cause has it come here?—having thus reflected on the discus, [either] go to anger or be appeased"

body.text:
etat kila jagaddhātuś
cakraṃ viṣṇoḥ sudarśanam
pratiṣaṇmāsam abhyeti
daityagarbhavināśanam
body.translated_text: "This, indeed, is the discus <s>Sudarśana</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the world-supporter; every six months it comes, the destroyer of the <s>daitya</s> wombs"

body.text:
puṅgarbhān nikhilān etad
dānavānāṃ mahāsura
vināśayaty anantarāṃ
sarvaduṣṭanibarhaṇam
body.translated_text: "This destroys all the male embryos of the <s>dānavas</s>, O great <s>asura</s>, immediately—it is the slayer of all the wicked"

body.text:
karoti duḥkham atulaṃ
ghātanāt pratipakṣajam
puruṣāṇāṃ na sarvatra
saṃsthitā jagataḥ pateḥ
body.translated_text: "It causes unequalled sorrow, born of the slaying, to the adversary; [but] of men everywhere it [the Lord's power] is not equally established—of the Lord of the world"

body.text:
mayi tvayi tathānyatra
yathā viṣṇur vyavasthitaḥ
tasyaitac cakram āyāntaṃ
puruṣaḥ ko na pūjayet
body.translated_text: "As <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established in me, in you, and likewise elsewhere—this discus of his, coming, what man would not worship?"

body.text:
yasyādhikṣepajā rājaṃs
tava trailokyavicyutiḥ
tasya cakraṃ jaganmūrteḥ
samupaiṣi ruṣā katham
body.translated_text: "He from whose contempt [arose], O king, your fall from the three worlds—to his discus, [the discus] of him who is the form of the world, how do you go with anger?"

body.text:
sadṛśe puruṣe krodhaṃ
naraḥ kurvīta daityapa
na tu sarveśvare viṣṇau
yatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
body.translated_text: "A man should make anger toward an equal man, O lord of the <s>daityas</s>, but not toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of all, in whom all is established"

body.text:
tat prasīda mahābhāga
samupaihi jagatpatim
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ
yaṃ praṇamya na sīdati
body.translated_text: "So be gracious, O greatly fortunate one; approach the Lord of the world, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the refuge, the [worthy] shelter, bowing to whom one does not sink"

body.text:
yasmin prasanne trailokyaṃ
tvattaḥ prāptaḥ śacīpatiḥ
bhraṣṭaś ca yadadhikṣepāt
taṃ tvaṃ śaraṇam āvraja
body.translated_text: "He, when gracious, [granted] the three worlds [to Indra], the lord of <s>Śacī</s>, [obtained] from you; and through whose contempt [you were] cast down—to him go for refuge"

body.text:
yatra sarveśvare sarvaṃ
sarvabhūte jagat sthitam
tasya cakram upaihi tvaṃ
vinayād asurādhipa
body.translated_text: "In whom, the Lord of all, the being of all, the world is established—approach his discus with humility, O lord of the <s>asuras</s>"

body.text:
sarvakāraṇabhūtasya
devadevasya cakriṇaḥ
kaś cakram ativarteta
martyadharmā mahāsura
body.translated_text: "Who could overstep the discus of the cause of all, the god of gods, the discus-bearer, [you being] of mortal nature, O great <s>asura</s>?"

body.text:
cakram atra jagaddhātuḥ
karoti sthitipālanam
vipakṣāsurasaṃbhūti-
garbhavisraṃsanāt prabho
body.translated_text: "The discus here effects the maintenance and preservation of the world-supporter, through the despoiling of the wombs of the births of adversary <s>asuras</s>, O Lord"

body.text:
prasādya cakranāmānaṃ
govindaṃ jagato gurum
śreyase sarvadharmajña
śaraṇaṃ vraja keśavam
body.translated_text: "Having propitiated him whose name is the discus, <s>Govinda</s>, the teacher of the world, for [your] welfare, O knower of all <s>dharma</s>, go for refuge to <s>Keśava</s>"

body.text:
saṃsmarasva ca daityendra
prahrādaṃ svapitāmaham
bhraṣṭarājyena bhavatā
smartavyo 'ham iti prabho
body.translated_text: "And remember, O lord of the <s>daityas</s>, <s>Prahrāda</s>, your grandfather; for it was said by you, of fallen kingdom, 'I am to be remembered,' O Lord"

body.text:
sa vyājahāra bhagavāṃs
tavānugrahakāmyayā
saṃsmaryatāṃ mahābhāga
sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
viṣṇubhakto mahābāhuḥ
sa te śreyo 'bhidhāsyati
body.translated_text: "He, the Blessed one, spoke out of desire for your favor: 'Let [me] be remembered, O greatly fortunate one'—the best of all bearers of <s>dharma</s>, that mighty-armed devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; he will declare your welfare"

body.text:
etad vacanam ākarṇya
tadā vairocanir baliḥ
yayau tadārgham ādāya
viṣṇoś cakrasya pūjakaḥ
body.translated_text: Having heard this word, then <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>, went, taking up the oblation, the worshipper of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus

body.text:
sa dadarśa samāyāntam
anantakarasaṅginam
cakram akṣayacakrasya
viśvasya paripālakam
body.translated_text: He beheld coming the discus, cleaving to the hand of the endless [Lord], [the discus] of the imperishable wheel[-bearer], the preserver of the universe,

body.text:
sasmāra ca baliḥ sarvaṃ
prahrādavacanaṃ nṛpa
jagāda yac ca govindaḥ
prasādasumukhaḥ prabhuḥ
body.translated_text: And <s>Bali</s> remembered all the word of <s>Prahrāda</s>, O king, and what <s>Govinda</s>, the Lord of gracious face, had said

body.text:
bhaktinamras tato bhūtvā
bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhoḥ
tuṣṭāva vāsudevasya
cakram avyaktamūrtinaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, having become bowed with devotion, he praised the discus of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Lord of past, future, and present, of unmanifest form:

body.text:
jvālāmālākarālāntam
udyadindusamaprabham
madhyāhnārkasamābhāsaṃ
tejasaḥ piṇḍasaṃsthitam
body.translated_text: [the discus] terrible at its edge with a garland of flames, of splendor equal to the rising moon, of luster like the midday sun, established as a mass of radiance,

body.text:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā tejasā rāśim
upasaṃgamya cā vibhum
uvāca daityaśārdūlaḥ
praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ
body.translated_text: Having seen that mass of splendor, and having approached the all-pervading [discus], the tiger among <s>daityas</s>, having bowed down, with joined palms, said:

body.text:
anantasyāprameyasya
viśvamūrter mahātmanaḥ
namāmi cakriṇaś cakraṃ
karasaṅgi sudarśanam
body.translated_text: "To the discus of the discus-bearer—the endless, immeasurable, world-formed, great soul—I bow, [the discus] <s>Sudarśana</s> clinging to his hand"

body.text:
sahasram iva sūryāṇāṃ
saṃghātaṃ vidyutām iva
body.translated_text: [the discus] like a thousand suns, like a mass of lightnings,

body.text: kālāgnim iva yac cakraṃ
body.translated_text: the discus which is like the fire of time—

body.text: tad viṣṇoḥ praṇamāmy aham
body.translated_text: that [discus] of <s>Viṣṇu</s> I bow to

body.text:
duṣṭarāhugalaccheda-
śoṇitāruṇatārakam
tan namāmi hareś cakraṃ
śatanemi sudarśanam
body.translated_text: "its star [-like center] red with the blood of the cleaving of the throat of the wicked <s>Rāhu</s>—that I bow to, the discus of <s>Hari</s>, the hundred-rimmed <s>Sudarśana</s>"

body.text:
yasyārakeṣu śakrādyā
lokapālā vyavasthitāḥ
tadantar vasavo rudrās
tathaiva marutāṃ gaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: "on whose spokes <s>Śakra</s> and the other world-guardians are stationed; within it the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and likewise the hosts of the <s>Maruts</s>,"

body.text:
dhārāyāṃ dvādaśādityāḥ
samastāś ca hutāśanāḥ
dhārājāle 'bdhayaḥ sarve
nābhimadhye prajāpatiḥ
body.translated_text: "on the rim the twelve <s>Ādityas</s> and all the fires; in the net of the rim all the oceans; in the middle of the hub the <s>Prajāpati</s>"

body.text:
samastanemiṣv akhilā
yasya vidyāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
yasya rūpam anirdeśyam
api yogibhir uttamaiḥ
body.translated_text: "on whose every rim-edge all the sciences are established, whose form is indefinable even by the best of yogis,"

body.text:
yad bhramat surasaṅghānāṃ
tejasaḥ paribṛṃhaṇam
daityaujasāṃ ca nāśāya
tan namāmi sudarśanam
body.translated_text: "which whirling [exists] for the augmentation of the splendor of the host of gods, and for the destruction of the might of the <s>daityas</s>—that I bow to, <s>Sudarśana</s>"

body.text:
bhraman matamahāvega-
vibhrāntākhilakhecaram
tan namāmi hareś cakram
anantāraṃ sudarśanam
body.translated_text: "whirling, bewildering with [its] great speed all the sky-goers—that I bow to, the discus of <s>Hari</s>, of endless spokes, <s>Sudarśana</s>"

body.text:
nakṣatravadvahnikaṇa-
vyāptaṃ kṛtsnaṃ nabhastalam
tan namāmi hareś cakraṃ
karasaṅgi sudarśanam
body.translated_text: "pervading the entire vault of the sky with sparks of fire like asterisms—that I bow to, the discus of <s>Hari</s>, clinging to his hand, <s>Sudarśana</s>"

body.text:
svabhāvatejasā yuktaṃ
yad arkāgnimayaṃ mahat
viśeṣato harer gatvā
sarvadevamayaṃ karam
body.translated_text: "endowed with innate splendor, that great [discus] made of the sun and fire, especially [as] the hand of <s>Hari</s>, having become consisting of all the gods,"

body.text:
durvṛttadaityamathanaṃ
jagataḥ paripālakam
tan namāmi hareś cakraṃ
daityacakraharaṃ param
body.translated_text: "the crusher of wicked <s>daityas</s>, the preserver of the world—that I bow to, the discus of <s>Hari</s>, the supreme remover of the host of <s>daityas</s>"

body.text:
karotu me sadā śarma
dharmatāṃ ca prayātu me
prasādasumukhe kṛṣṇe
tasya cakraṃ sudarśanam
body.translated_text: "May the discus <s>Sudarśana</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of gracious face ever make weal for me, and may it bring me to righteousness"

body.text:
svabhāvatejasā yuktaṃ
madhyāhnārkasamaprabham
body.translated_text: endowed with innate splendor, of luster equal to the midday sun,

body.text:
prasīda saṃyuge 'riṇāṃ
sudarśanasudarśanam
vidyujjvālāmahākakṣaṃ
dahāntar mama yat tamaḥ
body.translated_text: "Be gracious in battle—the well-seen <s>Sudarśana</s> [discus] of the foes—with great fence of flames of lightning; burn within me the darkness that is in me"

body.text:
jahi no viṣayagrāhi
mano grahaviceṣṭitam
visphoṭayākhilāṃ māyāṃ
kuruṣva vimalāṃ matim
body.translated_text: "Slay our mind that grasps after sense-objects, [its] activity [like] a seizing demon; shatter all illusion, make [my] mind stainless"

body.text:
evaṃ saṃsthūyamānaṃ tad
vahnipiṇḍopamaṃ mahat
babhūva prakaṭaṃ cakraṃ
daityacakrpates tadā
body.translated_text: Thus, as it was being praised, that great [discus] resembling a mass of fire became manifest then to the lord of the <s>daitya</s> wheel[-host]

body.text:
dadarśa sa mahābāhuḥ
prabhāmaṇḍaladurdṛśam
agnijvālāgataṃ tāmraṃ
taptacakram ivāparam
body.translated_text: That mighty-armed one beheld [it], hard to look upon for its circle of radiance, copper[-hued] within the fire-flame, like another heated discus

body.text:
bhramatas tasya cakrasya
nābhimadhye mahīpate
trailokyam akhilaṃ daityo
dṛṣṭavān bhūrbhuvādikam
body.translated_text: In the middle of the hub of that whirling discus, O lord of the earth, the <s>daitya</s> beheld the entire three worlds, [the earth,] the atmosphere, and the rest,

body.text:
mervādīn akhilāñ śailān
gaṅgādyāḥ saritas tathā
kṣīrābdhipramukhāṃś cābdhīn
dvīpāñ jambvādisaṃjñitān
body.translated_text: all the mountains beginning with <s>Meru</s>, and likewise the rivers beginning with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the oceans chief of which is the milk-ocean, and the continents named <s>Jambu</s> and the rest,

body.text:
vaimānikān sagandharvān
sūryādīṃś ca tathā grahān
nakṣatratārakākāśaṃ
śakrādīṃś ca divaukasaḥ
body.translated_text: the celestial-car-dwellers with the <s>gandharvas</s>, and the sun and the other planets, the asterisms, stars, and sky, and <s>Śakra</s> and the other sky-dwellers,

body.text:
rudrādityāṃś ca marutāṃ
sādhyānāṃ ca mahīpate
saṃnidhānaṃ nirīkṣyāsau
daityānāṃ vismito 'bhavat
body.translated_text: and the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, the assembly of the <s>Maruts</s> and the <s>Sādhyas</s>, O lord of the earth—beholding the presence [of all], he was astonished at [this presence] of the <s>daityas</s> [-vanquishing power]

body.text:
tataḥ praṇamyārtiharaṃ surāṇām
apārasāraṃ paramāyudhaṃ hareḥ
namo namas te 'stv iti daityarājaḥ
provāca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te
body.translated_text: Then, having bowed to the remover of the affliction of the gods, the boundless-essenced supreme weapon of <s>Hari</s>, the <s>daitya</s> king said, "Homage, homage be to you," and again, "Homage, homage to you"

body.text:
yan no 'śubhaṃ cetasi vāyuvega
yan no 'śubhaṃ vāci hutāśanottha
yac cāśubhaṃ kāyakṛtaṃ hares tad
varāyudhaṃ tvaṃ praśamaṃ nayāśu
body.translated_text: "Whatever evil of ours is in the mind, O wind-swift one, whatever evil of ours in speech, arisen from fire, and whatever evil done by the body—that, O excellent weapon of <s>Hari</s>, lead quickly to appeasement"

body.text:
prasīda satkārakṛtaṃ mamāghaṃ
prayātu te nāśam anantavīrya
satāṃ ca sanmārgavatāṃ manāṃsi
sthirībhavantv acyutapādayugme
body.translated_text: "Be gracious; may my sin, done [against the order] of honoring [you], go to destruction, O you of endless might; and may the minds of the good, who follow the good path, become steady upon the pair of feet of <s>Acyuta</s>"

body.text:
evaṃ stute tatas tasmin
viṣṇucakre sudarśane
puṣpavṛṣṭir baler mūrdhni
nipapātāntarikṣataḥ
parihṛtya ca daityendraṃ
yayau cakraṃ yathecchayā
body.translated_text: When the discus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, was thus praised, a rain of flowers fell upon <s>Bali</s>'s head from the sky; and having spared the <s>daitya</s> king, the discus went off at will

body.text:
bhramad eva ca daityānāṃ
yayau tadbhayam āvahat
body.translated_text: And whirling on, it went, bringing fear to the <s>daityas</s>

body.text:
tatas tad adbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā
cakrasyāgamanaṃ hareḥ
pūrvavatsmaraṇaṃ prāpya
sasmāra svapitāmaham
body.translated_text: Then, having seen that wondrous coming of the discus of <s>Hari</s>, and having attained, as before, the remembrance [of Prahrāda's word], he remembered his grandfather

body.text:
gacchatā pūrvam āryeṇa
smartavyo 'ham itīritam
taṃ smariṣyāmi daityendraṃ
sa naḥ śreyo 'bhidhāsyati
body.translated_text: "By the noble one, departing of old, it was said, 'I am to be remembered'; I shall remember that <s>daitya</s>-lord; he will declare our welfare"

body.text:
ity etad adhisaṃsmṛtya
balir ātmapitāmaham
sasmāra daityādhipatiṃ
prahrādaṃ bhagavatpriyam
body.translated_text: Thus having recalled this, <s>Bali</s>, [recalling] his own grandfather, remembered the lord of the <s>daityas</s>, <s>Prahrāda</s>, dear to the Blessed Lord

body.text:
saṃsmṛtaś ca sa pātālam
ājagāma mahāmatiḥ
cakrodyatakaraḥ sākṣād
bhagavān iva keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: And being remembered, that one of great mind came to the nether world, with the discus raised in his hand, like the Blessed <s>Keśava</s> in visible form

body.text:
tam āgatam athotthāya
yathāvat sa mahāmatiḥ
abhivādya balir bhaktyā
nivedyārgham abhāṣata
body.translated_text: Then, rising up at his coming, that one of great mind, <s>Bali</s>, having duly greeted [him] with devotion [and] offered the oblation, spoke:

body.text:
tātāṃhridarśanād adya
pāvito 'smy apakalmaṣaḥ
divaś cyuto 'py ahaṃ manye
śakrād ātmānam uttamam
body.translated_text: "By the sight of [your] feet, father, today I am purified, sinless; though fallen from heaven, I deem myself higher than <s>Śakra</s>"

body.text:
trailokyaharaṇād ugraṃ
yad duḥkhaṃ hṛdaye mama
tac chāntaṃ pādasaṃparkam
upetya bhavato mama
body.translated_text: "The fierce sorrow that was in my heart from the loss of the three worlds—that is appeased, having attained contact with your feet"

body.text:
iti saṃstūya dattvā ca
varāsanam udāradhīḥ
paryupāsata rājendro
daityānāṃ svapitāmaham
body.translated_text: Thus having praised [him] and given [him] an excellent seat, the noble-minded lord of kings attended upon his grandfather, [the lord] of the <s>daityas</s>

body.text:
tam upāsīnam anaghaḥ
prahrādo daityapuṅgavaḥ
pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ
baliṃ vairocaniṃ nṛpa
body.translated_text: To him sitting near, the sinless <s>Prahrāda</s>, the bull among <s>daityas</s>, replied to the great soul <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>, O king:

body.text:
bale brūhi yadarthaṃ te
smṛto 'ham arisūdana
tavopakāraṇe viddhi
dharme māṃ satatodyatam
body.translated_text: "O <s>Bali</s>, tell me for what purpose I am remembered by you, O slayer of foes; know me to be ever intent, in <s>dharma</s>, upon your benefit"

body.text:
tātenāhaṃ purā jñapto
bhraṣṭarājyena te bale
saṃsmartavyo 'smy asaṃdigdhaṃ
śreyo vakṣyāmy ahaṃ tadā
body.translated_text: "I was formerly instructed by my father, [that] by you, of fallen kingdom, O <s>Bali</s>, I am to be remembered, without doubt; then I shall declare [your] welfare"

body.text:
so 'haṃ rājyaparibhraṣṭo
viṣayāsaktihṛṣitaḥ
indriyair avaśas tāta
yat kāryaṃ tat praśādhi mām
body.translated_text: "I, fallen from kingship, thrilled with attachment to sense-objects, not in control of [my] senses, father—whatever is to be done, instruct me in that"

body.text:
yadi mad-vacanaṃ tāta
śraddhadhāsi hitaṃ bale
taṃ devadevam anaghaṃ
prayāhi śaraṇaṃ harim
body.translated_text: "If you have faith, father, in my word [as] beneficial, O <s>Bali</s>, go for refuge to that god of gods, the sinless <s>Hari</s>"

body.text:
śabdādiṣv anuraktāni
tavākṣāṇy asurādhipa
śabdādayaś ca govinde
santy eva vyavahārataḥ
body.translated_text: "Your senses, O lord of the <s>asuras</s>, are attached to sounds and the rest; and sounds and the rest exist in <s>Govinda</s> too, in [actual] practice"

body.text:
gītakair gīyatāṃ viṣṇur
manohāribhir ātmanaḥ
anyālambanataś cittam
ākṛṣyādhatsva keśave
body.translated_text: "Let <s>Viṣṇu</s> be sung with mind-captivating songs of one's own; drawing the mind away from other supports, fix it on <s>Keśava</s>"

body.text:
gandhān udārān bhakṣāṃś ca
srajo vāsāṃsi cāsura
prayaccha devadevāya
taccheṣāṇy upayuñja ca
body.translated_text: "Perfumes noble and eatables, and garlands and garments, O <s>asura</s>, offer to the god of gods, and partake of their remnants"

body.text:
yatra yatra ca te prītir
viṣaye ditijeśvara
tat tam acyutam uddiśya
viprebhyaḥ pratipādaya
body.translated_text: And wherever your love is, in [any] object, O lord of the sons of <s>Diti</s>, dedicate that to <s>Acyuta</s> and bestow it upon <s>vipras</s>.

body.text:
sarvabhūteṣu govindo
bahurūpo vyavasthitaḥ
iti matvā mahābāho
sarvabhūtahito bhava
body.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> is established in all beings in manifold forms; knowing this, O mighty-armed one, be the benefactor of all beings.

body.text:
ātmānam acyutaṃ viddhi
śatruṃ ca ripum ātmanaḥ
itijñānavataḥ kopas
tava kutra bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: Know yourself to be <s>Acyuta</s>, and your foe and enemy [to be him] too; for one who has this knowledge, where will your anger be?

body.text:
śabdādayo ye viṣayā
viṣayī yaś ca puruṣaḥ
tad aśeṣaṃ vijānīhi
svarūpaṃ paramātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: The sense-objects, sound and the rest, and the experiencing subject, the <s>Puruṣa</s>—know all that to be the nature of the supreme Self.

body.text:
paramātmā ca bhagavān
viṣvakseno janārdanaḥ
tadbhaktimān bhāgavato
nālpapuṇyo hi jāyate
body.translated_text: And the supreme Self is the Blessed <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>; a <s>Bhāgavata</s> devoted to him is not born of slight merit.

body.text:
bhagavacchāsanālambī
bhagavacchāsanapriyaḥ
bhagavadbhaktim āsthāya
vatsa bhāgavato bhava
body.translated_text: Relying on the teaching of the Blessed One, a lover of the teaching of the Blessed One, taking your stand on devotion to the Blessed One—O child, become a <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

body.text:
bhagavān bhūtakṛd bhavyo
bhūtānāṃ prabhavo hi yaḥ
bhāvena taṃ bhajasveśaṃ
bhavabhaṅgakaraṃ harim
body.translated_text: The Blessed One is the maker of beings, the one to be, the source indeed of beings; with [true] feeling worship that Lord <s>Hari</s>, the breaker of existence.

body.text:
bhajasva bhāvena vibhuṃ
bhagavantaṃ maheśvaram
tato bhāgavato bhūtvā
bhavabandhād vimokṣyase
body.translated_text: Worship with [true] feeling the all-pervading Blessed One, the great Lord; then, having become a <s>Bhāgavata</s>, you will be released from the bondage of existence.

body.text:
sarvabhūte manas tasmin
samādhāya mahāmate
prāpsyase paramāhlāda-
kāriṇīṃ paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: Having fixed your mind on that one [who dwells] in all beings, O greatly wise one, you will attain the supreme destination that brings the highest delight,

body.text:
yatrānandaparaṃ jñānaṃ
sarvaduḥkhavivarjitam
body.translated_text: where there is knowledge whose essence is bliss, free of all sorrow.

body.text:
tatra cittaṃ samāveṣṭuṃ
na śaknoti bhavān yadi
tadabhyāsaparas tasmin
kuru yogaṃ divāniśam
body.translated_text: If your honor is unable to settle the mind there, then, intent on the practice of that, perform <s>yoga</s> upon him day and night.

body.text:
tatrāpy asāmarthyavataḥ
kriyāyogo mahātmanā
brahmaṇā yaḥ samākhyātas
tanmanāḥ satataṃ bhava
body.translated_text: And if there too you lack the capacity, [there is] the <s>kriyā-yoga</s> (yoga of action) which was declared by the great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>—be ever with your mind on him.

body.text:
karoṣi yāni karmāṇi
tāni deve jagatpatau
samarpayasva bhadraṃ te
tataḥ karma prahāsyasi
body.translated_text: Whatever deeds you do, dedicate them to the god, the Lord of the world—blessings on you—then you will cast off [the bondage of] action.

body.text:
kṣīṇakarmā mahābāho
śubhāśubhavivarjitaḥ
layam abhyeti govinde
tad brahma paramaṃ mahat
body.translated_text: Of exhausted karma, O mighty-armed one, free of good and evil, one attains dissolution in <s>Govinda</s>, that supreme, great <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
bhoktum icchasi daityendra
karmaṇām atha cet phalam
tatas tam arcayeśeśaṃ
tataḥ karmaphalodayaḥ
body.translated_text: If you wish to enjoy the fruit of actions, O lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, then worship that Lord of lords; thence the arising of the fruit of action.

body.text:
yo 'rtham icchati daityendra
sa samārādhya keśavam
niḥsaṃśayam avāpnoti
dhundhumāro yathā nṛpaḥ
body.translated_text: He who desires wealth, O lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, having well worshipped <s>Keśava</s>, attains it without doubt, as did the king <s>Dhundhumāra</s>.

body.text:
atrigehasamudbhūtaṃ
dattātreyasvarūpiṇam
rājyam ārādhya govindaṃ
kārtavīryas tathāptavān
body.translated_text: <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, born in the house of <s>Atri</s>, of the form of <s>Dattātreya</s>, thus obtained his kingdom.

body.text:
dharmaṃ kṛṣṇaprasādena
mudgalo jājaliḥ kuṇiḥ
prāpur anye tathā kāmān
narendrā nahuṣādayaḥ
body.translated_text: By the grace of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Mudgala</s>, <s>Jājali</s>, and <s>Kuṇi</s> attained <s>dharma</s>; and other kings, <s>Nahuṣa</s> and the rest, [attained] their desires likewise.

body.text:
janakaḥ sudhvajo nāma
janakaḥ samitidhvajaḥ
dharmadhvajas tathā muktiṃ
keśavārādhanād gataḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> named <s>Sudhvaja</s>, <s>Janaka</s> <s>Samitidhvaja</s>, and likewise <s>Dharmadhvaja</s> attained release from the worship of <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
tathānye munayo daitya
rājānaś ca sahasraśaḥ
prāpur muktiṃ mahābhāgāḥ
kṛtvā bhaktiṃ janārdane
body.translated_text: Likewise other sages, O <s>Daitya</s>, and kings by the thousands, greatly fortunate, attained release, having made devotion to <s>Janārdana</s>.

body.text:
yathā hi jvalito vahnis
tamohāniṃ tadarthinām
śītahāniṃ tathānyeṣāṃ
svedaṃ svedābhilāṣiṇām
body.translated_text: For just as kindled fire makes the removal of darkness for those who seek it, the removal of cold for others, and sweat for those desiring sweat,

body.text:
karoti kṣudhitānāṃ ca
bhojyapākaṃ tathotkaṭam
tathaiva kāmān bhūteśaḥ
sa dadāti yathepsitān
body.translated_text: and makes for the hungry the abundant cooking of food—so the Lord of beings gives desires as they are wished.

body.text:
tad etad akhilaṃ jñātvā
yat taveṣṭaṃ śṛṇuṣva tat
kalpadrumād iva harer
yat te manasi vartate
body.translated_text: Knowing all this, hear that which is desired by you, which dwells in your mind, [to be granted] by <s>Hari</s> as by a wish-fulfilling tree.

body.text:
etat prahrādavacanaṃ
niśāmya ditijeśvaraḥ
pratyuvāca mahābhāgaṃ
praṇipatya pitāmaham
body.translated_text: Having heard this speech of <s>Prahlāda</s>, the lord of the sons of <s>Diti</s> replied to the greatly fortunate grandfather, having bowed:

body.text:
saṃprāptasyāmṛtasyeva
tava vākyasya nāsti me
tṛptir etad ahaṃ tāta
śrotum icchāmi vistarāt
body.translated_text: "Of your speech, like nectar attained, there is no satiety for me; this, father, I wish to hear in detail.

body.text:
akṣīṇakarmā puruṣo
maraṇe samupasthite
kīdṛśaṃ lokam āyāti
yaḥ saṃsmarati keśavam
body.translated_text: A man whose karma is not exhausted, when death is at hand, who remembers <s>Keśava</s>—to what kind of world does he go?

body.text:
yathā ca vāsudevasya
smaraṇaṃ tāta mānavaiḥ
mumūrṣubhiḥ prakartavyaṃ
tan mamācakṣva vistarāt
body.translated_text: And how should the remembrance of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, father, be performed by men about to die—tell that to me in detail.

body.text:
kiṃ japyaṃ kīdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ
smartavyaṃ ca hares tadā
kathaṃ dhyeyaṃ ca vidvadbhis
tad ācakṣva yathātatham
