body.translated_text: What is to be muttered, what kind of form of <s>Hari</s> is to be remembered then, and how is he to be meditated upon by the wise—tell that exactly."

body.text:
sādhu vatsa tvayā praśnaḥ
suguhyo 'yam udāhṛtaḥ
tapasāṃ tāta sarveṣāṃ
tapo nānaśanāt param
body.translated_text: "Well-asked, child, is this most secret question you have posed; father, of all austerities there is no austerity higher than fasting [unto death].

body.text:
kathyate ca mahābāho
saṃvādo 'yaṃ purātanaḥ
bhagīrathasya rājarṣer
brahmaṇaś ca prajāpateḥ
body.translated_text: And this ancient dialogue is told, O mighty-armed one, of the royal seer <s>Bhagīratha</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> the lord of creatures.

body.text:
atītyāmaralokaṃ ca
gavāṃ lokaṃ ca mānada
ṛṣilokaṃ ca yo 'gacchad
bhagīratha iti śrutaḥ
body.translated_text: Having passed beyond the world of the immortals and the world of cows, O honor-giver, and the world of the seers, he who went [there] is heard of as <s>Bhagīratha</s>.

body.text:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa vacaḥ prāha
brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ
kathaṃ bhagīrathāgās tvam
imaṃ deśaṃ durāsadam
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the worlds, spoke this word: "How have you come, <s>Bhagīratha</s>, to this region hard to reach?

body.text:
na hi devā na gandharvā
na manuṣyā bhagīratha
āyānty ataptatapasaḥ
kathaṃ vai tvam ihāgataḥ
body.translated_text: For neither gods nor <s>Gandharvas</s> nor men, O <s>Bhagīratha</s>, who have not practiced austerity, come [here]; how indeed have you come here?"

body.text:
niḥśaṅkam annam adadaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ
śataṃ sahasrāṇi sadaiva dāyam
brāhmaṇaṃ vrataṃ nityam āsthāya vidvan
na tv evāhaṃ tasya phalād ihāgām
body.translated_text: "Without hesitation I gave food to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, a hundred thousand [measures] ever as gift, O learned one, ever maintaining the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-vow; yet I have not come here by the fruit of that.

body.text:
daśaikarātrān daśa pañcarātrān
ekādaśaikādaśakāṃs tathaiva
jyotiṣṭomānāṃ ca śataṃ yad iṣṭaṃ
phalena tenāpi na cāgato 'ham
body.translated_text: Ten single-night [sacrifices], ten five-night ones, and likewise eleven elevens [of nights], and a hundred <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifices, which I performed—yet by that fruit too I have not come [here].

body.text:
yac cāvasaṃ jāhnavītīranityaḥ
śataṃ samās tapyamānas tapo 'ham
pradāya tatrāśvatarīsahasraṃ
phalena tasyāpi na cāgato 'ham
body.translated_text: And that I dwelt ever on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s> [Gaṅgā], practicing austerity for a hundred years, having given there a thousand she-mules—by the fruit of that too I have not come [here].

body.text:
daśa dhenusahasrāṇi
maṇiratnavibhūṣitāḥ
daśārbudāni cāśvānām
ayutāni ca viṃśatiḥ
puṣkareṣu dvijātibhyaḥ
prādāṃ gāś ca sahasraśaḥ
body.translated_text: Ten thousand cows adorned with gems and jewels, and ten hundred million horses, and twenty myriads, and cows by the thousands I gave to the twice-born at the <s>Puṣkaras</s>.

body.text:
suvarṇacandrottamadhāriṇīnāṃ
kanyottamānām adadaṃ sragviṇīnām
ṣaṣṭiṃ sahasrāṇi vibhūṣitānāṃ
jāmbūnadair ābharaṇair na tena
body.translated_text: I gave sixty thousand best-of-maidens wearing golden crescent-ornaments, garlanded, adorned with golden ornaments—not by that [did I come here].

body.text:
daśārbudāny adadaṃ gosave yās tv
ekaikaśo daśa gā lokanātha
samānavatsāḥ payasā samanvitāḥ
suvarṇakāṃsyopaduhā na tena
body.translated_text: I gave ten hundred million [cows] in the <s>Gosava</s> [sacrifices], ten cows each, O Lord of the world, with matching calves, full of milk, milked into gold and bronze—not by that.

body.text:
ahany ahani vipreṣu
ekaikaṃ triṃśato 'dadam
gṛṣṭīnāṃ kṣīradātrīṇāṃ
rohiṇīnāṃ śatāni ca
body.translated_text: Day after day I gave to <s>vipras</s>, thirty each, of young cows giving milk, and hundreds of red ones (<s>rohiṇīs</s>);

body.text:
dogdhrīṇāṃ vai gavāṃ caiva
prayutāni daśaiva tu
prādāṃ daśaguṇaṃ brahman
na ca tenāham āgataḥ
body.translated_text: and of milch-cows indeed, ten millions, O <s>brahman</s>; tenfold I gave—and not by that have I come [here].

body.text:
koṭīś ca kāñcanasyāṣṭau
prādāṃ brahman daśa tv aham
ekaikasmin kratau tena
phalenāhaṃ na cāgataḥ
body.translated_text: And eight times ten crores of gold I gave, O <s>brahman</s>, in each single sacrifice—yet by that fruit I have not come [here].

body.text:
vājināṃ śyāmakarṇānāṃ
haritānāṃ pitāmaha
prādāṃ hemasrajāṃ brahman
koṭīr daśa ca sapta ca
body.translated_text: Of horses with dark ears, bay-colored, O grandfather, wearing golden garlands, O <s>brahman</s>, I gave seventeen crores.

body.text:
īṣādantān mahākāyān
kāñcanasragvibhūṣitān
patnīvataḥ sahasrāṇi
prāyacchaṃ daśa sapta ca
body.translated_text: Great-bodied [elephants] with tusks like chariot-poles, adorned with golden garlands, with their mates, seventeen thousands I gave.

body.text:
alaṃkṛtānāṃ deveśa
divyaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ
rathānāṃ kāñcanāṅgānāṃ
sahasrāṇy adadaṃ daśa
sapta cānyāni yuktānāṃ
vājibhiḥ samalaṃkṛtaiḥ
body.translated_text: Of chariots with golden frames, adorned with divine golden ornaments, O Lord of the gods, I gave seventeen thousand, yoked and well-adorned with horses.

body.text:
dakṣiṇāvayavāḥ kecid
devair ye saṃprakīrtitāḥ
vājapeyeṣu daśasu
prādāṃ tenāpi nāgataḥ
body.translated_text: Some accessory-gifts of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> which are proclaimed by the gods—in ten <s>Vājapeya</s> [sacrifices] I gave [them]—yet by that too I have not come [here].

body.text:
śakratulyaprabhāvānām
ījyayā vikrameṇa ca
sahasraṃ niṣkakaṇṭhānāṃ
pradadan dakṣiṇām aham
body.translated_text: Giving as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> a thousand [men] of golden-neck-ornaments, equal in power to <s>Indra</s> through sacrifice and through valor,

body.text:
vijitya nṛpatīn sarvān
makhair iṣṭvā pitāmaha
aṣṭābhyo rājasūyebhyo
na ca tenāham āgataḥ
body.translated_text: having conquered all kings, having sacrificed with rites, O grandfather, through eight <s>Rājasūya</s> [sacrifices]—yet by that I have not come [here].

body.text:
srotaś ca yāvad gaṅgāyāṃ
chinnam āsīj jagatpate
dakṣiṇābhiḥ pravṛttābhir
mama nāgaṃ ca tatkṛte
body.translated_text: And as far as the current in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, it was cut [by the abundance of gifts], O Lord of the world; by the gifts that flowed forth I [gave] an elephant for that [each].

body.text:
vājināṃ ca sahasre dve
suvarṇamaṇibhūṣite
vāraṇānāṃ śataṃ cāham
ekaikasya tridhādadam
varaṃ grāmaśataṃ cāham
ekaikasya tridhādadam
body.translated_text: And two thousand horses adorned with gold and gems, and a hundred elephants—to each one I gave threefold; and an excellent hundred villages—to each one I gave threefold.

body.text:
tapasvī niyatāhāraḥ
śamam āsthāya vāgyataḥ
dīrghakālaṃ himavati
gaṅgāyāś ca durutsahām
body.translated_text: As an ascetic of restrained food, abiding in tranquility, speech restrained, for a long time on the <s>Himavat</s>, [I endured] the unbearable stream of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

body.text:
mūrdhnā dhārāṃ mahādevaḥ
śirasā yām adhārayat
na tenāpy aham āgacchaṃ
phaleneha pitāmaha
body.translated_text: the stream which the great god [Śiva] bore upon his head with his crown—yet not by that have I come here by [its] fruit, O grandfather.

body.text:
śamyākṣepair ayajaṃ devadeva
tathā kratūnām ayutaiś cāpi yattaḥ
trayodaśadvādaśāhaiś ca deva
sapuṇḍarīkair na ca teṣāṃ phalena
body.translated_text: I sacrificed with throwings of the <s>śamyā</s>-peg, O god of gods, and likewise, intent, with myriads of sacrifices, and with thirteen- and twelve-day [rites], O god, with <s>puṇḍarīka</s> [sacrifices]—yet not by their fruit [have I come].

body.text:
aṣṭau sahasrāṇi kakudminām ahaṃ
śuklarṣabhāṇām adaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ
patnīś caiṣām adadaṃ niṣkakaṇṭhīs
teṣāṃ phaleneha na cāgato 'smi
body.translated_text: Eight thousand humped white bulls I gave to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and I gave their mates [cows] with golden neck-ornaments—yet by their fruit I have not come here.

body.text:
hiraṇyaratnaracitān
adadaṃ ratnaparvatān
dhanadhānyasahasrāṃś ca
grāmāñ śatasahasraśaḥ
body.translated_text: Jewel-mountains fashioned of gold and gems I gave, and thousands [in] wealth and grain, and villages by the hundreds of thousands.

body.text:
śataṃ śatānāṃ gṛṣṭīnām
adadaṃ cāpy atandritaḥ
iṣṭvānekair mahāyajñair
brāhmaṇebhyo dhanena ca
body.translated_text: A hundred hundreds of young cows I gave, unwearied, having sacrificed with many great sacrifices, [giving] to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with wealth.

body.text:
ekādaśāhair ayajaṃ sudakṣiṇair
dvir dvādaśāhair aśvamedhaiś ca deva
body.translated_text: I sacrificed with eleven-day [rites] of rich <s>dakṣiṇās</s>, and twice with twelve-day horse-sacrifices, O god,

body.text:
bṛhadbhir dvādaśāhaiś ca
aśvamedhaiḥ pitāmaha
body.translated_text: and with great twelve-day horse-sacrifices, O grandfather,

body.text:
arkāyaṇaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiś ca brahmaṃs
teṣāṃ phaleneha na cāgato 'smi
body.translated_text: and with sixteen <s>Arkāyaṇa</s> [sacrifices], O <s>brahman</s>—yet by their fruit I have not come here.

body.text:
niṣkrāmakaṃ cāpy adadaṃ yojanānāṃ
dvir vistīrṇaṃ kāñcanapādapānām
vanaṃ cūtānāṃ ratnavibhūṣitānām
na caiva teṣām āgato 'haṃ phalena
body.translated_text: And I gave a deer-park, two <s>yojanas</s> broad, of golden trees, a grove of mango trees adorned with jewels—yet not by their fruit have I come.

body.text:
turāyaṇaṃ tu vratam apradhṛṣyam
akrodhano 'karavaṃ triṃśato 'bdān
śataṃ gavām aṣṭa śatāni cāhaṃ
dine dine prādadaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ
body.translated_text: And the <s>Turāyaṇa</s> vow, irresistible, free of anger, I performed for thirty years; a hundred cows and eight hundred I gave day after day to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>;

body.text:
payasvinīnāṃ atha rohiṇīnāṃ
tathaiva cāpy anaḍuhāṃ lokanātha
prādām nityaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sureśa
nehāgatas tena phalena cāham
body.translated_text: milch-cows and red ones (<s>rohiṇīs</s>), and likewise oxen, O Lord of the world, I gave ever to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O Lord of the gods—not have I come here by that fruit.

body.text:
triṃśataṃ vidhivad vahnīn
ayajaṃ yac ca nityaśaḥ
aṣṭābhiḥ sarvamedhaiś ca
nṛmedhair dviguṇais tathā
body.translated_text: I sacrificed with thirty fires duly, and which [I did] ever, with eight <s>Sarvamedha</s> [sacrifices], and twice as many <s>Nṛmedha</s> [human-sacrifices],

body.text:
daśabhir viśvajidbhiś ca
stobhair aṣṭādaśottaraiḥ
na caiva teṣāṃ deveśa
phalenāham ihāgamam
body.translated_text: with ten <s>Viśvajit</s> [sacrifices], and with eighteen-and-more <s>Stoma</s> [chants]—yet not by their fruit, O Lord of the gods, have I come here.

body.text:
saravyāṃ bāhudāyāṃ ca
gayāyām atha naimiṣe
gavāṃ śatānām ayutam
adadaṃ na ca tena vai
body.translated_text: At the <s>Sarayū</s>, the <s>Bāhudā</s>, at <s>Gayā</s>, and at <s>Naimiṣa</s>, I gave a myriad of hundreds of cows—and not indeed by that.

body.text:
utkrāntikāle govindaṃ
smarann anaśanasthitaḥ
tyaktavān asmi yad dehaṃ
tenedṛk prāptavān phalam
body.translated_text: [But] at the time of departure, remembering <s>Govinda</s>, abiding in fasting [unto death], in that I gave up my body—by that I attained such a fruit."

body.text:
evam etad itīty āha
brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ
bhagīrathaṃ mahīpālaṃ
puṇyalokanivāsinam
body.translated_text: "Thus it is, even so," said <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the worlds, to <s>Bhagīratha</s>, the protector of the earth, dweller in the holy worlds.

body.text:
tad etad uktaṃ tapasāṃ
samastānāṃ mahāmate
guṇair anaśanaṃ brahmā
pradhānataram abravīt
body.translated_text: Therefore this is declared, O greatly wise one, that among all austerities <s>Brahmā</s> called fasting [unto death] the foremost in qualities.

body.text:
tyajaty anaśanastho hi
prāṇān yaḥ saṃsmaran harim
sa yāti viṣṇusālokyaṃ
yāvad indrāś caturdaśa
body.translated_text: For he who, abiding in fasting [unto death], gives up his breaths while remembering <s>Hari</s>—he attains residence in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> for as long as fourteen <s>Indras</s>.

body.text:
atītānāgatānīha
kulāni puruṣarṣabha
punāty anaśanaṃ kurvan
sapta sapta ca sapta ca
body.translated_text: He purifies, O bull among men, his past and future lineages here—performing fasting [unto death]—seven and seven and seven [of them].

body.text:
ślokāś cātra mahābāho
śrūyante yān bhagīrathaḥ
jagāda brahmaṇo lokam
upetaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
body.translated_text: And here, O mighty-armed one, are heard the verses which <s>Bhagīratha</s>, the lord of the earth, having reached the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, spoke:

body.text:
brahma brahmamayaṃ viṣṇor
yaḥ padaṃ paramātmanaḥ
saṃsmaraṃs tyajati prāṇān
sa viṣṇuṃ praviśaty ajam
body.translated_text: He who, remembering the <s>Brahman</s> consisting of <s>brahman</s>, the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> the supreme Self, gives up his breaths—he enters into the unborn <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
yaḥ kṣīṇakarmā bhogena
tapasā vāpi saṃsmaran
karoti kālaṃ kālena
na paricchedyate hi saḥ
body.translated_text: He whose karma is exhausted, whether by enjoyment or by austerity, remembering [him], reaches his end through time [naturally]—he indeed is not cut off [from liberation].

body.text:
akṣīṇakarmā maraṇe
saṃsmaran devam acyutam
yathā tvam eva devānāṃ
loke bhogān upāśnute
body.translated_text: He whose karma is not exhausted, remembering at death the god <s>Acyuta</s>—just as you [Bhagīratha] do—enjoys the pleasures in the world of the gods.

body.text:
kṣutite 'pi kule kaścij
jāyeyaṃ karmaṇaḥ kṣaye
manuṣyo yena sarveśaṃ
cintayeyaṃ sadā harim
body.translated_text: [He thinks:] 'May I, even in a fallen lineage, be born at the exhaustion of my karma as a man, by which I may ever contemplate the Lord of all, <s>Hari</s>.'

body.text:
taccintayādhunāśeṣa-
puṇyapāpavivarjitaḥ
maraṇe tanmanas tatra
layam etya tam āpnuyāt
body.translated_text: By that contemplation, now freed of all merit and demerit, at death his mind there, attaining dissolution, would attain him.

body.text:
karmabhūmau samastānāṃ
karmaṇām uttamottamam
yad antakāle puruṣaiḥ
smaryate puruṣottamaḥ
body.translated_text: In the field-of-action of all, the highest of all actions is that <s>Puruṣottama</s> is remembered by men at the final time.

body.text:
ity etān āha rājarṣiḥ
ślokān ādyo bhagīrathaḥ
viṣṇusaṃsmaraṇāt prāpya
lokān anaśane mṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: These verses the royal seer <s>Bhagīratha</s>, the first, spoke, having attained the worlds by the remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, dying in fasting [unto death].

body.text:
evam atyantaśastānāṃ
karmaṇām asureśvara
nānyad utkṛṣṭam uddiṣṭaṃ
tajjñair anaśanāt param
body.translated_text: Thus, of the most highly praised actions, O lord of the <s>asuras</s>, nothing more excellent is declared by those who know than fasting [unto death].

body.text:
tasyāhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye
yac ca japyaṃ mumūrṣubhiḥ
yādṛgrūpaś ca bhagavāṃś
cintanīyo janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: I shall tell its characteristic, and what is to be muttered by those about to die, and of what kind of form the Blessed <s>Janārdana</s> is to be contemplated.

body.text:
āsannam ātmanaḥ kālaṃ
jñātvā prājño mahāsura
nirdhūtamaladoṣaś ca
snāto niyatamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: Knowing his own time to be near, the wise one, O great <s>asura</s>, his impurities and faults shaken off, bathed, of restrained mind,

body.text:
samabhyarcya hṛṣīkeśaṃ
puṣpadhūpādibhis tataḥ
praṇipātaiḥ stavaiḥ puṇyair
dhyānayogaiś ca pūjayet
body.translated_text: having well worshipped <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> then with flowers, incense, and the rest, should worship [him] with prostrations, holy hymns, and meditations of <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
dattvā dānaṃ ca viprebhyo
vikalādibhya eva ca
sabhāprapābrāhmaṇauka-
devaukādyupayogi ca
body.translated_text: Having given a gift to <s>vipras</s>, and to the crippled and the rest, and what is useful for a meeting-hall, a watering-station, a brahmin's dwelling, a temple, and the like,

body.text:
bandhuputrakalatrauka-
kṣetradhānyadhanādiṣu
mitravarge ca daityendra
mamatvaṃ vinivartayet
body.translated_text: toward kinsmen, sons, wife, dwelling, field, grain, wealth, and the rest, and toward the circle of friends, O lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, he should turn away the sense of 'mine.'

body.text:
mitrān amitrān madhyasthān
parān svāṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ
abhyarthanopacāreṇa
kṣāmayet kukṛtaṃ svakam
body.translated_text: Friends, enemies, the neutral, strangers, and his own—again and again, by entreaty and courtesy he should ask forgiveness for his own misdeeds.

body.text:
tataś ca prayataḥ kuryād
utsargaṃ sarvakarmaṇām
śubhāśubhānāṃ daityendra
vākyaṃ cedam udāharet
body.translated_text: And then, restrained, he should perform the renunciation of all deeds, the auspicious and the inauspicious, O lord of <s>daityas</s>, and should utter this speech:

body.text:
parityajāmy ahaṃ bhogāṃs
tyajāmi suhṛdo 'khilān
bhojanādi mayotsṛṣṭam
utsṛṣṭam anulepanam
body.translated_text: 'I abandon enjoyments, I abandon all my friends; food and the rest is renounced by me, anointing is renounced,

body.text:
sragbhūṣaṇādikaṃ geyaṃ
dānam ādānam eva ca
homādayaḥ padārthā ye
yāś ca nityakriyā mama
body.translated_text: garlands, ornaments, and the rest, song, gift and receiving, and the deeds beginning with <s>homa</s> that are mine, and my daily rites,

body.text:
naimittikās tathā kāmyā
varṇadharmās tathojjhitāḥ
guṇadharmādayo dharmā
yāś ca kāścin mama kriyāḥ
body.translated_text: the occasional and optional [rites], and the duties of [my] class are likewise cast off, the qualified duties and the rest, and whatever rites of mine [there are]

body.text:
padbhyāṃ karābhyāṃ viharan
kurvan vā karma na tv aham
kariṣye prāṇināṃ pīḍāṃ
prāṇinaḥ santu nirbhayāḥ
body.translated_text: Walking with feet and hands, or performing a deed, I shall not cause harm to living beings; let the living beings be free of fear

body.text:
nabhasi prāṇino ye tu
ye jale ye ca bhūtale
kṣiter antaragā ye ca
ye ca pāṣāṇasaṃpuṭe
body.translated_text: Those living beings that are in the sky, and that are in water, and that are on the earth's surface, and that move within the earth, and that are within a casket of stone,

body.text:
ye dhānyādiṣu vastreṣu
śayaneṣv āsaneṣu ca
te svapantu vibudhyantu
sukhaṃ matto bhayaṃ vinā
body.translated_text: that are in grains and the rest, in garments, in beds and in seats—let them sleep, let them wake, happily and without fear from me

body.text:
na me 'sti bāndhavaḥ kaścid
viṣṇuṃ muktvā jagadgurum
mitrapakṣe ca me viṣṇur
adhaś cordhvaṃ tathāgrataḥ
body.translated_text: I have no kinsman whatever, save <s>Viṣṇu</s> the teacher of the world; and on the side of friends [I have] <s>Viṣṇu</s>—below and above and likewise in front,

body.text:
pārśvato mūrdhni pṛṣṭhe ca
hṛdaye vāci cakṣuṣi
śrotrādiṣu ca sarveṣu
mama viṣṇuḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
body.translated_text: at my side, on my head, on my back, in my heart, in my speech, in my eye, and in my hearing and all the rest—<s>Viṣṇu</s> is established for me'

body.text:
iti sarvaṃ samutsṛjya
dhyātvā sarvatra cācyutam
vāsudevety avirataṃ
nāma devasya kīrtayan
body.translated_text: Thus having renounced all, having meditated on <s>Acyuta</s> everywhere, ceaselessly proclaiming the name of the god, '<s>Vāsudeva</s>,'

body.text:
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu
śayīta prācchirās tataḥ
udacchirā vā daityendra
cintayañ jagataḥ patim
body.translated_text: he should lie down upon <s>darbha</s>-grass with tips pointing south, head to the east, or head to the north, O lord of <s>daityas</s>, contemplating the Lord of the world,

body.text:
viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ
keśavaṃ madhusūdanam
nārāyaṇaṃ naraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ
vāsudevaṃ janārdanam
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Nara</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>,

body.text:
vārāhaṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ
puṇḍarīkākṣam acyutam
vāmanaṃ śrīdharaṃ śrīśaṃ
nṛsiṃham aparājitam
body.translated_text: <s>Vārāha</s>, the sacrifice-Person, the lotus-eyed <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, <s>Śrīśa</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the unconquered,

body.text:
padmanābham ajaṃ śaurim
dāmodaram adhokṣajam
sarveśvareśvaraṃ śuddham
anantaṃ rāmam īśvaram
body.translated_text: <s>Padmanābha</s>, the unborn <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, the Lord of the lords of all, the pure, the endless <s>Rāma</s>, the Lord,

body.text:
cakriṇaṃ gadinaṃ śārṅgiṃ
śaṅkhinaṃ garuḍadhvajam
kirīṭakaustubhadharaṃ
praṇamāmy aham avyayam
body.translated_text: the discus-bearer, the mace-bearer, the <s>Śārṅga</s>-bow-bearer, the conch-bearer, him whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s>, the wearer of the diadem and the <s>Kaustubha</s>—I bow to him, the imperishable

body.text:
aham atra jagannāthe
mayi cāstu janārdanaḥ
āvayor antaraṃ māstu
samīranabhasor iva
body.translated_text: Let me be in the Lord of the world, and let <s>Janārdana</s> be in me; let there be no interval between us two, as between the wind and the sky

body.text:
ayaṃ viṣṇur ayaṃ śaurir
ayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ puro mama
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaḥ
padmapattropamekṣaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: This is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, this is <s>Śauri</s>, this is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> before me, dark as the petal of a blue lotus, his eyes like the petals of a lotus

body.text:
eṣa paśyatu mām īśaḥ
paśyāmy aham adhokṣajam
yato na vyatirikto 'haṃ
yanmayo 'haṃ yadāśrayaḥ
body.translated_text: Let this Lord look upon me; I look upon <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, since I am not separate [from him], being made of him, having him as my support

body.text:
itthaṃ japann ekamanāḥ
smaran sarveśvaraṃ harim
āsīnaḥ sukhaduḥkheṣu
samo mitrāhiteṣu ca
body.translated_text: Thus muttering, one-minded, remembering <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of all, seated, equal in pleasures and pains and toward friends and foes,

body.text:
oṃ namo vāsudevāyety
etad vā satataṃ vadan
yad vodīrayituṃ nāma
samarthas tad udīrayan
dhyāyeta devadevasya
rūpaṃ viṣṇor manoramam
body.translated_text: saying constantly 'Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>,' or, whatever name he is able to utter, uttering that, he should meditate on the delightful form of the god of gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>:

body.text:
praśāntanetrabhrūvaktraṃ
śaṅkhacakragadādharam
śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ caiva
caturbāhuṃ kirīṭinam
body.translated_text: with tranquil eyes, brows, and face, bearing conch, discus, and mace, his chest [marked] with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, four-armed, diademed,

body.text:
pītāmbaradharaṃ viṣṇuṃ
cārukeyūradhāriṇam
cintayec ca tadā rūpaṃ
manaḥ kṛtvaikaniścayam
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> clad in yellow garments, wearing beautiful armlets—he should contemplate that form then, having made his mind of single resolve

body.text:
yādṛśe vā manaḥ sthairyaṃ
rūpe badhnāti cakriṇaḥ
tad eva cintayan nāma
vāsudeveti kīrtayet
body.translated_text: Or upon whatever form of the discus-bearer his mind binds steadiness, contemplating that very [form], he should proclaim the name '<s>Vāsudeva</s>'

body.text:
ittaṃ japan smaran vetthaṃ
svarūpaṃ paramātmanaḥ
ā prāṇoparamād vīras
taccittas tatparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus muttering, thus remembering the own-form of the Supreme Self, the hero, until the cessation of his breath, his mind on that, devoted to that,

body.text:
nirvikalpena manasā
yaḥ smaret puruṣottamam
sarvapātakayukto 'pi
puruṣaḥ puruṣarṣabha
prayāti devadeveśe
layam īḍyatame 'cyute
body.translated_text: he who, with undistracted mind, remembers <s>Puruṣottama</s>—even a man joined with all sins, O bull among men, goes to dissolution in the god of gods, the most praiseworthy <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
yathāgnis tṛṇajālāni
dahaty anilasaṃgataḥ
tathānaśanasaṃkalpaḥ
puṃsāṃ pāpam asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: As fire, joined with wind, burns webs of straw, so the resolve of fasting-unto-death [burns] the sin of men, without doubt

body.text:
viṣṇoḥ saṃsmaraṇe prāpya
lokam anaśane mṛtaḥ
evam atyantaśastānāṃ
karmaṇām asureśvara
body.translated_text: Having attained the world by the remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, dead in fasting-unto-death—thus, of utterly praiseworthy deeds, O lord of <s>asuras</s>—

body.text:
nāsti satyāt paro dharmo
nāsty adharma tathānṛtāt
nāsti vidyāsamaṃ cakṣus
tapo nānaśanāt param
body.translated_text: there is no <s>dharma</s> higher than truth, no <s>adharma</s> like untruth, no eye equal to knowledge, no austerity higher than fasting-unto-death

body.text:
nāsti jñānasamaṃ dānaṃ
na saṃtoṣasamaṃ sukham
na caiverṣyāsamaṃ duḥkhaṃ
tapo nānaśanāt param
body.translated_text: there is no gift equal to knowledge, no happiness equal to contentment, no sorrow equal to envy, no austerity higher than fasting-unto-death

body.text:
nāsty arogasamaṃ dhanyaṃ
nāsti gaṅgāsamā sarit
nāsti viṣṇusamaṃ dhyeyaṃ
tapo nānaśanāt param
body.translated_text: there is nothing blessed like freedom from disease, no river equal to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, nothing to be meditated upon equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, no austerity higher than fasting-unto-death

body.text:
utkrāntikāle bhūtānāṃ
muhyante cittavṛttayaḥ
jarāvyādhividhīnānāṃ
kimu vyādhyādidoṣataḥ
body.translated_text: At the time of departure of beings the workings of the mind become confused; for those afflicted by old age and disease, how much more through the fault of disease and the rest?

body.text:
atyantavayasā vṛddhyā
vyādhinā cātipīḍitaḥ
yadi sthātuṃ na śaknoti
kṣitisthe darbhasaṃstare
body.translated_text: If, exceedingly oppressed by extreme age and by disease, one is not able to remain on a <s>darbha</s>-spread laid on the ground,

body.text:
tat kim anyo 'py upāyo 'sti
na vānaśanakarmaṇi
viphalyaṃ yena nāpnoti
tan me brūhi pitāmaha
body.translated_text: is there then some other means too in the rite of fasting-unto-death, by which one does not attain failure [of it]—tell me that, O grandsire

body.text:
nātra bhūmir na ca kuśāḥ
saṃstaraś ca na kāraṇam
cittasyālambanībhūto
viṣṇur evātra kāraṇam
body.translated_text: Here neither the ground nor the <s>kuśa</s>-grass nor the spread is the cause; <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, becoming the support of the mind, is the cause here

body.text:
bhuñjann abhuñjan gacchaṃś ca
svapaṃs tiṣṭhann athāpi vā
utkrāntikāle govindaṃ
saṃsmaraṃs tanmayo bhavet
body.translated_text: Whether eating or not eating, walking, sleeping, or standing, at the time of departure, remembering <s>Govinda</s>, one would become made of him

body.text:
kiṃ japaiḥ kiṃ bhuvā kṛtyaṃ
kiṃ kuśair daityasattama
tathāpi kurvato yasya
hṛdaye na janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: What [use] of mutterings, what is to be done with the ground, what with <s>kuśa</s>-grass, O best of <s>daityas</s>, for one in whose heart, even while he does [these], <s>Janārdana</s> is not?

body.text:
tasmāt pradhānamantroktaṃ
vāsudevasya kīrtanam
tanmayatvena daityendra
tasyopāyaś ca vistaraḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore the proclamation of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, declared in the chief <s>mantra</s>, through becoming made of him, O lord of <s>daityas</s>—that is his means, in detail

body.text:
ity etat kathitaṃ sarvaṃ
pṛṣṭo 'haṃ yat tvayā bale
utkrāntikāle smaraṇaṃ
kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathayāmi te
body.translated_text: Thus all this has been told, since you, O <s>Bali</s>, asked me about remembrance at the time of departure; what more shall I tell you?

body.text:
kriyāyogas tvayā pūrvaṃ
mamokto yaḥ pitāmaha
tam ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi
phalaṃ cāsya yathātatham
body.translated_text: The <s>kriyāyoga</s> which was formerly told to me by you, O grandsire—that I wish to hear, and its fruit, as it truly is

body.text:
devārcāṃ devatāgāre
tanmayatvena pūjayam
yathāvac cetaso bhūmiṃ
karoti niyato hi saḥ
body.translated_text: Worshipping the god's image in the god's house, through becoming made of him, he, restrained, duly makes the [pure] ground of his mind

body.text:
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa
puṇyasvādhyāyasaṃstavaiḥ
kriyāyogaḥ sa vidvadbhir
yogināṃ samudāhṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: By austerity, by chastity, by holy self-study and hymns of praise—that <s>kriyāyoga</s> of the yogins has been declared by the wise

body.text:
tatrāhaṃ śrotum icchāmi
kriyāyogasthito naraḥ
yat phalaṃ samavāpnoti
kārayitvā harer gṛham
body.translated_text: Therein I wish to hear: a man established in <s>kriyāyoga</s>, having had a house of <s>Hari</s> made, what fruit does he obtain?

body.text:
devārcāṃ kārayitvā vā
yat puṇyaṃ puruṣo 'śnute
saṃpūjayitvā vidhivad
anulipya ca yat phalam
body.translated_text: or, having had an image of the god made, what merit does a man enjoy; and what fruit there is, having duly worshipped and anointed [it]

body.text:
kāni mālyāni śastāni
kāni nārhanti keśave
ke dhūpāḥ kṛṣṇadayitāḥ
ke varjyāś ca jagatpateḥ
body.translated_text: Which garlands are praised, which are not fit for <s>Keśava</s>? Which incenses are dear to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and which are to be avoided for the Lord of the world?

body.text:
upahāre phalaṃ kīm syāt
kiṃ phalaṃ gītavādite
ghṛtakṣīrādinā yac ca
snāpite keśave phalam
body.translated_text: What fruit might there be in an offering, what fruit in song and instrumental music, and what fruit there is when <s>Keśava</s> is bathed with ghee, milk, and the rest,

body.text:
yac copalepane tāta
phalam abhyukṣite ca yat
vāsudevagṛhe sarvaṃ
tad aśeṣaṃ vadasva me
body.translated_text: and what fruit, father, there is in the smearing and in the sprinkling [of the house]—all that, in the house of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, tell me entirely

body.text:
sādhu vatsa yad etat tvaṃ
vāsudevasya pṛcchasi
śuśrūṣaṇavidhau puṇyaṃ
tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: Well [asked], O child, this that you ask about <s>Vāsudeva</s>; hear here, one-minded, the merit in the rite of [his] service

body.text:
brahmaṇā kila devānām
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
śuśrūṣaṇaphalaṃ viṣṇoḥ
proktaṃ daityapate purā
body.translated_text: By <s>Brahmā</s> indeed, of old, to the gods and the great-souled seers, the fruit of the service of <s>Viṣṇu</s> was declared, O lord of <s>daityas</s>

body.text:
tebhyaḥ sakāśān manunā
prāptaṃ svārociṣeṇa tu
svārociṣaḥ svaputrāya
dattavān ṛtacakṣuṣe
body.translated_text: From them it was obtained by <s>Manu</s> <s>Svārociṣa</s>; and <s>Svārociṣa</s> gave it to his own son <s>Ṛtacakṣus</s>

body.text:
ṛtacakṣuś ca bhargave
śukras tasmād avāpa ca
mamākhyātaṃ ca śukreṇa
yathāvat sumahātmanā
body.translated_text: and <s>Ṛtacakṣus</s> [gave it] to <s>Bhārgava</s>, and <s>Śukra</s> obtained it from him; and it was declared to me by <s>Śukra</s>, the very great-souled one, duly,

body.text:
śuśrūṣave mahābhāga
daityācāryeṇa dhīmatā
tad etac chrūyatāṃ tāta
kriyāyogāśritaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: to me who desired to serve [Viṣṇu], O greatly fortunate one, by the wise teacher of the <s>daityas</s>; let this be heard, O child, the fruit grounded in <s>kriyāyoga</s>

body.text:
jñānayogas tu saṃyogaś
cittasyaivātmanā tu yaḥ
yas tu bāhyārthasāpekṣaḥ
sa kriyāyoga ucyate
body.translated_text: The yoga of knowledge (<s>jñānayoga</s>) is the conjunction of the mind with the Self alone; but that which depends on an external object is called <s>kriyāyoga</s>

body.text:
paramaṃ kāraṇaṃ yogo
vimukter ditikeśvara
kriyāyogaś ca yogasya
paramaṃ tāta sādhanam
body.translated_text: Yoga is the supreme cause of liberation, O lord of <s>Diti</s>'s line; and <s>kriyāyoga</s> is the supreme means of [that] yoga, O child

body.text:
yat tv etad bhavatā pṛṣṭaṃ
phalam anvicchatā phalam
devālayādikaraṇe
tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: But that which has been asked by you, desiring the fruit—the fruit in the making of a temple and the rest—hear that here, one-minded

body.text:
yas tu devālayaṃ viṣṇor
dārvaṃ śailamayaṃ tathā
kārayen mṛnmayaṃ vāpi
śṛṇu tasya bale phalaṃ
body.translated_text: He who would have a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> made, whether of wood or of stone, or even of clay—hear, O <s>Bali</s>, his fruit:

body.text:
ahany ahani yajñena
yajato yan mahāphalam
prāpnoti tat phalaṃ viṣṇor
yaḥ kārayati mandiram
body.translated_text: The great fruit which one obtains by sacrificing with a sacrifice day after day—that fruit he obtains who has a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> made

body.text:
kulānāṃ śatam āgāmi
samatītaṃ tathā śatam
kārayan bhagavaddhāma
nayaty acyutalokatām
body.translated_text: Having a house of the Blessed One made, he leads a hundred future families and likewise a hundred past to the state of the world of <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ
svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu
viṣṇor ālayavinyāsa-
prārambhād eva naśyati
body.translated_text: The sin done in seven births, whether little or much, perishes from the very commencement of the laying-out of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s temple

body.text:
saptalokamayo viṣṇus
tasya yaḥ kurute gṛham
pratiṣṭhāṃ samavāpnoti
sa naraḥ saptalaukikīm
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> consists of the seven worlds; the man who makes a house for him attains the foundation of [all] the seven worlds

body.text:
praśastadeśabhūbhāge
yaḥ śastaṃ bhavanaṃ hareḥ
kārayaty akṣayāṃl lokān
sa naraḥ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: He who has a praised house of <s>Hari</s> made in a region of praised land—that man attains imperishable worlds

body.text:
iṣṭakācayavinyāso
yāvanty ṛkṣāṇi tiṣṭhati
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi
tatkartur divi saṃsthitiḥ
body.translated_text: As long as the laying-out of the heap of bricks stands [for so many] asterisms, for that many thousands of years there is a fixed abode in heaven for its maker

body.text:
pratimāṃ lakṣaṇavatīṃ
yaḥ kārayati mānavaḥ
keśavasya sa tallokam
akṣayaṃ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: The man who has a well-charactered image of <s>Keśava</s> made attains that imperishable world of his

body.text:
ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ
sahasrāṇi sa modate
svargaukasāṃ nivāseṣu
pratyekam arisūdana
body.translated_text: He rejoices for sixty thousand-thousands of years in each of the dwellings of the heaven-dwellers, O slayer of foes

body.text:
pratiṣṭhāpya harer arcāṃ
supraśaste niveśane
puruṣaḥ kṛtakṛtyatvān
nainaṃ śvomaraṇaṃ tapet
body.translated_text: Having installed an image of <s>Hari</s> in a much-praised dwelling, a man, by [his] fulfilment of purpose, is not pained by [the prospect of] tomorrow's death

body.text:
ye bhaviṣyanti ye 'tītā
ākalpāt puruṣāḥ kule
tāṃs tārayati saṃsthāpya
devasya pratimāṃ hareḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who shall be and who have passed, [over the span] from [one] <s>kalpa</s> [to the next], in his family—those he carries across, having established an image of the god <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
anuśastāḥ kila purā
yamena yamakiṃkarāḥ
pāśodyatāyudhā daitya
prajāsaṃyamane ratāḥ
body.translated_text: Of old, indeed, the servants of <s>Yama</s> were instructed by <s>Yama</s>, with nooses and raised weapons, O <s>daitya</s>, intent on the restraining of [erring] creatures:

body.text:
viharadhvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ
niyogo me 'nupālyatām
nājñābhaṅgaṃ kariṣyanti
bhavatāṃ jantavaḥ kvacit
body.translated_text: 'Move about according to rule; let my command be observed; your creatures shall never make a breach of [my] command

body.text:
kevalaṃ ye jagaddhātum
anantaṃ samupāśritāḥ
bhavadbhiḥ parihartavyās
teṣāṃ nāsty atra saṃsthitiḥ
body.translated_text: Only those who have taken refuge in the endless creator of the world are to be shunned by you; for them there is no abode here [in Yama's realm]

body.text:
ye tu bhāgavatā loke
taccittās tatparāyaṇāḥ
pūjayanti sadā viṣṇuṃ
te vas tyājyāḥ sudūrataḥ
body.translated_text: But those who are <s>bhāgavatas</s> in the world, their minds on him, devoted to him, who ever worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>—they are to be avoided by you from afar

body.text:
yas tiṣṭhan prasvapan gacchaṃs
tattiṣṭhan skhalite kṣute
saṃkīrtayati govindaṃ
te vas tyājyāḥ sudūrataḥ
body.translated_text: He who, standing, sleeping, walking, standing still, when stumbling or sneezing, proclaims <s>Govinda</s>—they are to be avoided by you from afar

body.text:
nityanaimittikair devaṃ
ye yajanti janārdanam
nāvalokya bhavadbhis te
tattejo hanti vo gatim
body.translated_text: Those who worship the god <s>Janārdana</s> with daily and occasional [rites]—do not look upon them; that splendour of theirs destroys your course

body.text:
ye dhūpapuṣpavāsobhir
bhūṣaṇaiś cāpi vallabhaiḥ
arcayanti na te grāhyā
narāḥ kṛṣṇāśrayoddhatāḥ
body.translated_text: Those men who worship [him] with incense, flowers, garments, and beloved ornaments—they are not to be seized, the men exalted by their refuge in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

body.text:
upalepanakartāraḥ
saṃmārjanaparāś ca ye
kṛṣṇālaye parityājyaṃ
teṣāṃ tripuruṣaṃ kulam
body.translated_text: The performers of smearing and those devoted to sweeping in the house of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—their family for three generations is to be avoided

body.text:
yena cāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ
kāritaṃ tatkulodbhavam
puṃsāṃ śataṃ nāvalokyaṃ
bhavadbhir duṣṭacakṣuṣā
body.translated_text: And he by whom a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> was made—the hundred men born of that family are not to be looked upon by you with [your] evil eye

body.text:
yenārcā bhagavadbhaktyā
vāsudevasya kāritā
narāyutaṃ tatkulajaṃ
bhavatāṃ śāsanātigam
body.translated_text: And he by whom an image of <s>Vāsudeva</s> was made with devotion to the Blessed One—the ten thousand men born of that family are beyond your governance

body.text:
bhavatāṃ bhramatām atra
viṣṇusaṃśrayamudrayā
vinājñābhaṅgakṛn naiva
bhaviṣyati naraḥ kvacit
body.translated_text: As you wander here, never shall there be a man who makes a breach of [my] command [if he is] marked with the seal of refuge in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'

body.text:
vatsa vaivasvatasyaitāḥ
śrutvā gāthā marīcinā
purukutsāya kathitāḥ
pārthivendrāya dhīmate
body.translated_text: O child, having heard these verses of <s>Vaivasvata</s> [Yama] from <s>Marīci</s>, they were told to <s>Purukutsa</s>, the wise lord of kings

body.text:
etāṃ mahāphalāṃ yo 'rcāṃ
viṣṇoh kārayate naraḥ
tavākhyātaṃ mahābāho
gṛhakārayituś ca yat
body.translated_text: The man who has this greatly fruitful image of <s>Viṣṇu</s> made—it has been declared to you, O mighty-armed one, and what [is the fruit] of him who has a house made

body.text:
yajñā narāṇāṃ pāpaugha-
kṣālakāḥ sarvakāmadāḥ
tathaivejyo jagaddhātuḥ
sarvayajñamayo hariḥ
body.translated_text: Sacrifices are the cleansers of the flood of men's sins, granters of all desires; and likewise the world's creator, <s>Hari</s>, consisting of all sacrifices, is to be worshipped

body.text:
sthāpitāṃ pratimāṃ viṣṇoḥ
samyak saṃpūjya mānavaḥ
yaṃ yaṃ prārthayate kāmaṃ
taṃ tam āpnoty asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: The man who, having duly worshipped an installed image of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whatever desire he prays for, that he attains, without doubt

body.text:
yaḥ snāpayati devasya
ghṛtena pratimāṃ hareḥ
prasthe prasthe dvijāgryāṇāṃ
sa dadāti gavāṃ śatam
body.translated_text: He who bathes the god's image of <s>Hari</s> with ghee gives, prastha by prastha, a hundred cows to the foremost of the twice-born

body.text:
gavāṃ śatasya viprāṇāṃ
yad dattasya bhavet phalam
ghṛtaprasthena tad viṣṇor
labhet snānopayoginā
body.translated_text: The fruit which would be of giving a hundred cows to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>—that he obtains with a prastha of ghee used for bathing <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
bhūridyumnena saṃprāptā
saptadvīpā vasuṃdharā
ghṛtāḍhakena govinda-
pratimāsnāpanāt kila
body.translated_text: By <s>Bhūridyumna</s> the seven-continent earth was attained, indeed by bathing the image of <s>Govinda</s> with an <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee

body.text:
pratimāsaṃ sitāṣṭamyāṃ
ghṛtena jagataḥ patim
snāpayitvā samastebhyaḥ
pāpebhyo vipramucyate
body.translated_text: Having bathed the Lord of the world with ghee each month on the bright eighth, one is freed from all sins

body.text:
dvādaśyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ ca
gavyena haviṣā hareḥ
snāpanaṃ daityaśārdūla
mahāpātakanāśanam
body.translated_text: On the twelfth and the fifteenth, the bathing of <s>Hari</s> with an oblation of cow-[ghee], O tiger among <s>daityas</s>, is the destroyer of great sins

body.text:
jñānato 'jñānato vāpi
yat pāpaṃ kurute naraḥ
tat kṣālayati saṃdhyāyāṃ
ghṛtena snāpayan harim
body.translated_text: Whatever sin a man does, knowingly or unknowingly, that he washes away at twilight, bathing <s>Hari</s> with ghee

body.text:
sarvayajñamayo viṣṇur
havyānāṃ paramaṃ ghṛtam
tayor aśeṣapāpānāṃ
kṣālakaḥ saṃgamo 'sura
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> consists of all sacrifices, [and] ghee is the supreme of oblations; the union of those two is the washer-away of all sins, O <s>asura</s>

body.text:
yeṣu kṣīravahā nadyo
hradāḥ pāyasakardamāḥ
tāṃl lokān puruṣā yānti
kṣīrasnānakarā hareḥ
body.translated_text: Those worlds in which the rivers flow with milk and the lakes are mires of milk-rice—to those worlds men go who perform the milk-bathing of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
āhlādaṃ nirvṛtiṃ svāsthyam
ārogyaṃ cārurūpatām
sapta janmāny avāpnoti
kṣīrasnānakaro hareḥ
body.translated_text: He who performs the milk-bathing of <s>Hari</s> attains delight, contentment, well-being, health, and beauty of form for seven births

body.text:
dadhyādīnāṃ vikārāṇāṃ
kṣīrataḥ saṃbhavo yathā
tathaivāśeṣakāmānāṃ
kṣīrasnāpanato hareḥ
body.translated_text: As the arising of the transformations such as curds and the rest is from milk, so too [is the arising] of all desires from the milk-bathing of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
yathā ca vimalaṃ jñānaṃ
yathā nirvṛtikārakam
tathāsya nirmalaṃ jñānaṃ
bhavaty atiphalapradam
body.translated_text: And as knowledge is stainless and as it is the cause of bliss, so his knowledge becomes stainless and the giver of exceeding fruit

body.text:
grahānukūlatāṃ puṣṭiṃ
priyatvaṃ cākhile jane
karoti bhagavān viṣṇuḥ
kṣīrasnāpanatoṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, gratified by the milk-bathing, brings about the favorableness of the planets, nourishment, and dearness among all people

body.text:
sarvo 'sya snigdhatām eti
dṛṣṭamātraḥ prasīdati
ghṛtakṣīreṇa deveśe
snāpite madhusūdane
body.translated_text: When the Lord of gods, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, is bathed with ghee and milk, everyone comes to a feeling of tenderness toward him; merely seen, [the worshipper] is favored

body.text:
atrāpy udāharantīmaṃ
saṃvādaṃ keśavāśritam
śāṇḍilyā saha kaikeyyāḥ
sumanāyāḥ surālaye
body.translated_text: Here too they relate this dialogue connected with <s>Keśava</s>, of <s>Śāṇḍilī</s> with <s>Sumanā</s> the Kaikeyī, in the abode of the gods

body.text:
svarge 'tiśobhanāṃ dṛṣṭvā
kaikeyīṃ patinā saha
brāhmaṇī śāṇḍilī nāma
paryapṛcchata vismitā
body.translated_text: Having seen in heaven the exceedingly resplendent Kaikeyī together with her husband, the brahmin woman named <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>, astonished, inquired:

body.text:
śataśaḥ santi kaikeyi
devāḥ svarganivāsinaḥ
devapatnyas tathaivaitāḥ
siddhāḥ siddhāṅganās tathā
body.translated_text: 'There are hundreds, O Kaikeyī, of gods dwelling in heaven, and likewise these wives of the gods, the <s>Siddhas</s>, and the wives of the <s>Siddhas</s>;

body.text:
na teṣām īdṛśo gandho
na kāntir na surūpatā
na vāsasāṃ ca śobheyaṃ
yathā te patinā saha
body.translated_text: they do not have such fragrance, nor loveliness, nor beauty of form, nor this splendor of garments, as you have together with your husband

body.text:
naivābharaṇajātāni
teṣāṃ bhrājanti vai tathā
yathā tava yathā patyus
tava svarganivāsinaḥ
body.translated_text: Nor do their kinds of ornaments shine so as yours and your husband's, O you who dwell in heaven

body.text:
svasthatā cetasaś ceyaṃ
yuvayor atiricyate
śakrādyānām apīsānāṃ
kṣayātiśayavarjitaḥ
body.translated_text: And this well-being of mind of you two surpasses [that] even of <s>Śakra</s> and the other lords, free of decline and excess

body.text:
tapaḥprabhāvo dānaṃ vā
karma vā homasaṃjñitam
yuvayor yan mamācakṣva
tat sarvaṃ varavarṇini
body.translated_text: The power of austerity, or gift, or the act called oblation—of you two—tell me all that, O fair-complexioned one'

body.text:
yajñair yajñeśvaro viṣṇur
āvābhyāṃ yat tu toṣitaḥ
svargaprāptir iyaṃ tasya
karmaṇaḥ phalam uttamam
body.translated_text: '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of sacrifice, with sacrifices was gratified by us two; this attainment of heaven is the supreme fruit of that act

body.text:
surūpatāṃ manaḥprīti
paśyatāṃ cāruveṣatām
yat pṛcchasi mahābhāge
tad apy eṣā vadāmi te
body.translated_text: [As for] the beauty of form, delight of mind, and charming appearance of those who behold [us], which you ask about, O greatly fortunate one—that too I tell you:

body.text:
tīrthodakais tathā snānaiḥ
snāpito 'yaṃ janārdanaḥ
tena kāntir atītyaitān
devāṃs tribhuvaneśvarān
body.translated_text: This <s>Janārdana</s> was bathed with the waters of sacred fords and with [other] bathings; thereby this loveliness, surpassing these gods who are lords of the three worlds [arose]

body.text:
manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ
śārīrā yā ca nirvṛtiḥ
yat priyatvaṃ ca sarvasya
tad ghṛtasnānajaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: The grace of mind, the gentleness, and the bodily contentment, and the dearness to all—that is the fruit born of the ghee-bathing

body.text:
yāny abhīṣṭāni vāsāṃsi
yac cābhīṣṭaṃ vibhūṣaṇam
ratnāni yāny abhīṣṭāni
yat priyaṃ cānulepanam
body.translated_text: Whatever garments were desired, and whatever ornament was desired, whatever jewels were desired, and whatever dear unguent,

body.text:
ye dhūpā yāni mālyāni
dayitāny abhavaṃs tadā
mama bhartus tathaivāsya
mama rājyaṃ praśāsataḥ
body.translated_text: whatever incenses, whatever garlands, were beloved then to me, and likewise to my husband, when he was ruling my kingdom—

body.text:
tāni sarvāṇi sarvajñe
sarvakartari keśave
dattāni tatsamuttho 'yaṃ
gandhabhūṣātmako guṇaḥ
body.translated_text: all those, given to the all-knowing <s>Keśava</s>, the maker of all—from that arose this quality consisting of fragrance and adornment

body.text:
āhārā dayitā ye ca
pavitrāś ca niveditāḥ
te lokakartre kṣṛṇāya
tṛptis tadguṇasaṃbhavā
body.translated_text: And the foods that were beloved and pure, [when] offered to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the maker of the world—[from that came] this satisfaction born of their quality

body.text:
svargakāmena me bhartrā
mayā ca śubhadarśane
kṛtam etad ato nābhūd
āvayor bhavasaṃkṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: By my husband, desiring heaven, and by me, O you of auspicious sight, this was done; therefore there was no destruction of [our] existence [-bonds] for us two

body.text:
ye tv akāmāṃ narāḥ samyag
etat kurvanti śobhane
teṣāṃ dadāti viśveśo
bhagavān muktim acyutaḥ
body.translated_text: But for those men who, without desire, perform this rightly, O lovely one, the Lord of all, the Blessed <s>Acyuta</s>, grants liberation'

body.text:
evam abhyarcya govindaṃ
sarvabhūteśvareśvaram
prāpnoty abhimatān kāmān
daityāha sumanā yathā
body.translated_text: Thus, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, the Lord of the lords of all beings, one attains the desired wishes—[so] said the <s>daitya</s>, just as <s>Sumanā</s> [had told]

body.text:
candanāgarukarpūra-
kuṅkumośīrapadmakaiḥ
anulipto harir bhaktyā
varān bhogān prayacchati
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, anointed with devotion with sandal, aloe, camphor, saffron, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>, grants excellent enjoyments

body.text:
kāleyakaṃ tuṅgakaṃ ca
padmacandanam eva ca
nṝṇāṃ bhavanti rogāya
dattāni puruṣottame
body.translated_text: <s>Kāleyaka</s>, <s>tuṅgaka</s>, and <s>padmacandana</s>, given to the Supreme Person, become [a cause] of disease for men

body.text:
tasmād ebhir na govindaḥ
pūjanīyo mahāsura
yāny ātmanaḥ sadeṣṭāni
tāni śastāny upākuru
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Govinda</s> is not to be worshipped with these, O great <s>asura</s>; the things that are ever dear to oneself, those commended ones offer

body.text:
tathaiva śubhagandhā ye
dhūpās te jagataḥ pateḥ
vāsudevasya dharmajñair
nivedyā dānaveśvara
body.translated_text: Likewise those incenses which are of auspicious fragrance are to be offered, by the knowers of <s>dharma</s>, to the Lord of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O lord of the <s>dānavas</s>

body.text:
na śallakījaṃ nākṣaulaṃ
na śuktāsavasaṃbhṛtam
dadyāt kṛṣṇāya dharmajño
dhūpān ārādhanodyataḥ
body.translated_text: The knower of <s>dharma</s>, intent on worship, should not give to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> incenses produced from <s>śallakī</s>, nor from <s>akṣaula</s>, nor those compounded with the fermented-juice of oysters (<s>śukti</s>)

body.text:
mālatī mallikā caiva
yūthikāthātimuktakā
pāṭalā karavīraś ca
javā pārantir eva ca
body.translated_text: <s>Mālatī</s> and <s>mallikā</s>, <s>yūthikā</s>, then <s>atimuktaka</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s> and <s>karavīra</s>, <s>javā</s> and <s>pārantī</s>,

body.text:
kubjakas tagaraś caiva
karṇikāraḥ kuraṇṭakaḥ
campako rotakaḥ kundo
bāṇo varvaramālikāḥ
body.translated_text: <s>kubjaka</s> and <s>tagara</s>, <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>rotaka</s>, <s>kunda</s>, <s>bāṇa</s>, [and] <s>varvara</s> garlands,

body.text:
aśokatilakā rodhrās
tathā caivāṭarūṣakaḥ
amī puṣpaprakārās tu
śastāḥ keśavapūjane
body.translated_text: <s>aśoka</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, <s>rodhra</s>, and likewise <s>aṭarūṣaka</s>—these kinds of flowers are commended in the worship of <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
bilvapatraṃ śamīpatraṃ
patraṃ bhṛṅgārakasya ca
tamālapatraṃ ca bale
sadaiva bhagavatpriyam
body.translated_text: The <s>bilva</s> leaf, the <s>śamī</s> leaf, the leaf of the <s>bhṛṅgāraka</s>, and the <s>tamāla</s> leaf, O <s>Bali</s>, are ever dear to the Blessed Lord

body.text:
tulasīkālatulasī-
patraṃ bhṛṅgarajasya ca
ketakīpatrapuṣpaṃ ca
sadyas tuṣṭikaraṃ hareḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Tulasī</s>, the leaf of the black <s>tulasī</s>, and of the <s>bhṛṅgaraja</s>, and the leaf and flower of the <s>ketakī</s>, give instant satisfaction to <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
padmāny ambusamutthānāṃ
raktanīle tathotpale
sitotpalaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya
dayitāni sadāsura
body.translated_text: Lotuses arising from water, and likewise the red and blue water-lilies, and the white water-lily, are ever dear to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>asura</s>

body.text:
nārkaṃ nonmattakaṃ kāṃcit
tathaiva girikarṇikām
na kaṇṭakārikāpuṣpam
acyutāya nivedayet
body.translated_text: One should not offer to <s>Acyuta</s> the <s>arka</s> [flower], nor any <s>unmattaka</s> (datura), and likewise the <s>girikarṇikā</s>, nor the <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s> flower

body.text:
kauṭajaṃ śālmalīpuṣpaṃ
śairīṣaṃ ca janārdane
nivedite bhayaṃ rogaṃ
niḥsvatāṃ ca prayacchati
body.translated_text: The <s>kuṭaja</s>, the <s>śālmalī</s> flower, the <s>śirīṣa</s>—[these], offered to <s>Janārdana</s>, grant fear, disease, and poverty

body.text:
yeṣāṃ na pratiṣedho 'sti
gandhavarṇānvitāni ca
tāni puṣpāṇi deyāni
viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave
body.translated_text: Those flowers for which there is no prohibition, and which are endowed with fragrance and color—those flowers are to be given to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-powerful one

body.text:
sugandhaiś ca surāmāṃsī-
karpūrāgarucandanaiḥ
tathānyaiś ca śubhair dravyair
arcayej jagataḥ patim
body.translated_text: And with fragrant [substances] and with <s>surāmāṃsī</s> (spikenard), camphor, aloe, and sandal, and with other auspicious substances, one should worship the Lord of the world

body.text:
dukūlapaṭukauśeya-
vārkṣakarpāsikādibhiḥ
vāsobhiḥ pūjayed viṣṇuṃ
daiteyendrātmanaḥ priyaiḥ
body.translated_text: With garments of fine cloth, <s>paṭu</s>, silk, bark-cloth, cotton, and the rest—garments dear to oneself—O lord of the <s>Daiteyas</s>, one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
bhakṣyāṇi yāny abhīṣṭāni
bhojyāny abhimatāni ca
phalaṃ ca vallabhaṃ yat syāt
tat tad deyaṃ janārdane
body.translated_text: Whatever eatables are desired, and whatever foods are agreeable, and what fruit may be beloved—each of those is to be given to <s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
suvarṇamaṇimuktādi
yac cānyad ativallabham
tat tad devātidevāya
keśavāya nivedayet
body.translated_text: Gold, gems, pearls, and the rest, and whatever else is most dear—each of those one should offer to <s>Keśava</s>, the god beyond gods

body.text:
ātmānaṃ keśavaṃ matvā
yad yat tasyaiva rocate
tat tad avyaktarūpāya
keśavāya nivedayet
body.translated_text: Deeming oneself to be <s>Keśava</s>, whatever pleases him alone—each of those one should offer to <s>Keśava</s> of unmanifest form

body.text:
cakravartī mahāvīryo
māndhātā yuvanāśvajaḥ
śaśāsa sa mahābāhuḥ
saptadvīpāṃ vasuṃdharām
body.translated_text: The universal emperor, of great valor, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, that mighty-armed one ruled the earth with its seven continents

body.text:
agāyanta ca yā gāthā
ye purāṇavido janāḥ
māndhātari mahābāho
yauvanāśve samāśritāḥ
body.translated_text: And the verses which they sang—the people who know the ancient lore—relating to <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, the mighty-armed son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>:

body.text:
yāvat sūrya udeti sma
yāvac ca pratitiṣṭhati
sarvaṃ tad yauvanāśvasya
māndhātuḥ kṣetram ucyate
body.translated_text: 'As far as the sun rises and as far as it sets, all that is called the domain of <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>'

body.text:
sa yauvanagataḥ saṃrāṭ
saptadvīpavatīṃ mahīm
śaśāsa dharmeṇa purā
cakravartī mahābalaḥ
body.translated_text: That emperor, in his youth, ruled by <s>dharma</s>, of old, the earth with its seven continents, the universal emperor of great strength

body.text:
nānyāyakṛn na cāśakto
na daridro na kīkaṭaḥ
tasyābhūt puruṣo rājye
samyagdharmānuśāsinaḥ
body.translated_text: There was in the kingdom of that one, rightly governing by <s>dharma</s>, no man who acted unjustly, nor incapable, nor poor, nor a <s>kīkaṭa</s> (barbarian/miser)

body.text:
catasro gatayas tasya
yauvanāśvasya dhīmataḥ
babhūvur apratihatā
hatārātibalasya vai
body.translated_text: Four [unimpeded] courses were there for that wise son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, unobstructed, who had destroyed the strength of his foes

body.text:
tasya bhaktir atīvābhūn
nisargād eva bhūpateḥ
vāsudeve jagaddhāmni
sarvakāraṇakāraṇe
body.translated_text: His devotion was exceedingly great, by nature itself, [that] of the lord of the earth toward <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the abode of the world, the cause of all causes

body.text:
tasya rddhiṃ mahimānaṃ ca
vilokya pṛthivīpateḥ
na kevalaṃ janasyābhūt
tasyāpy atyantavismayaḥ
body.translated_text: Beholding the prosperity and greatness of that lord of the earth, not only the people but he himself too was exceedingly astonished

body.text:
sa cintayām āsa nṛpaḥ
samṛddhyā vismitas tayā
kathaṃ syāt sampad eṣā me
punar apy anyajanmani
body.translated_text: That king pondered, astonished at that prosperity: 'How might this fortune of mine come to be again in another birth?'

body.text:
evaṃ subahuśo rājā
daityendra sumahābalaḥ
cintayann api tanmūlaṃ
na cāsīn niścayānvitaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus very many times the king, O lord of <s>daityas</s>, of very great strength, though pondering its root, did not come to a conclusion

body.text:
yadā na niścayaṃ rājā
sa yayau yuvanāśvajaḥ
tadā papraccha dharmajñān
sa viprān samupāgatān
body.translated_text: When the king, the son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, did not come to a conclusion, then he asked the knowers of <s>dharma</s>, the <s>vipras</s> who had come near—

body.text:
vasiṣṭhapramukhān vatsa
viviktāntaḥpurasthitaḥ
praṇipatya mahābāhur
gṛhītāsanasatkriyān
body.translated_text: those headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, O child—being in a secluded inner chamber, the mighty-armed one, having bowed down, [the sages] honored with the giving of seats:

body.text:
yadi sānugrahā buddhir
bhavatāṃ mayi sattamāḥ
tad ahaṃ praṣṭum icchāmi
kiṃcit tad vaktum arhatha
body.translated_text: 'If your minds are favorable toward me, O most excellent ones, then I wish to ask something—you ought to declare it

body.text:
sametyākhilavijñānaṃ
samyagdhautāntarātmabhiḥ
bhavadbhir yady ahaṃ na syāṃ
vimalas tan mahādbhutam
body.translated_text: Having come together [with you], possessed of all knowledge, with your inner selves rightly cleansed—if I should not become stainless [in your company], that would be a great marvel

body.text:
yad yathā tan mayā pṛṣṭā
bhavanto matprasādhitāḥ
vaktum arhanti vidvāṃsaḥ
sarvasyaivopakāriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: What I ask of you, in whatever manner, you who are propitiated by me, you learned ones, benefactors of all, ought to declare'

body.text:
yas te manasi saṃdehas
taṃ pṛcchādya mahīpate
gadiṣyāmo yathānyāyaṃ
yat te sāṃśayikaṃ hṛdi
body.translated_text: 'Whatever doubt there is in your mind, ask that today, O lord of the earth; we shall declare duly whatever is doubtful in your heart

body.text:
vayaṃ hi naraśārdūla
bhavatā paritoṣitāḥ
samyak prajāḥ pālayatā
saptadvīpe mahītale
body.translated_text: For we, O tiger among men, have been well satisfied by you, who rightly protect [your] people on the seven-continented surface of the earth

body.text:
sutuṣṭo brāhmaṇo 'śnīyāc
chindyād vā dharmasaṃśayam
hitaṃ vopadiśed dharmam
ahitād vā nivartayet
body.translated_text: A well-satisfied brahmin may eat, or cut [resolve] a doubt of <s>dharma</s>, or teach beneficial <s>dharma</s>, or turn [one] away from the non-beneficial'

body.text:
vivakṣum atha bhūpālaṃ
bhāryā tasyaiva dhīmataḥ
praṇāmapūrvam āhedaṃ
vinayāt praṇayānvitam
body.translated_text: Then to the king who wished to speak, the wife of that very wise one said this, prefaced with obeisance, out of modesty, joined with affection:

body.text:
na strīṇām avanīpāla
vaktum īdṛg iheśyate
tathāpi bhūpate vakṣye
saṃpad īdṛk sudurlabhā
body.translated_text: 'It is not approved here, O protector of the earth, for women to speak in such a way; nevertheless, O king, I shall speak—such fortune is very hard to obtain

body.text:
bhūyo 'pi saṃśayaṃ praṣṭum
alam īśa bhavān ṛṣīn
na tv ahaṃ puruṣavyāghra
sadāntaḥpuracāriṇī
body.translated_text: You are well able, O Lord, to ask the seers about a doubt yet again; but I, O tiger among men, am ever one moving within the inner apartments

body.text:
sa prasādaṃ yadi bhavān
karoti mama pārthiva
tan madīyam ṛṣīn praṣṭuṃ
saṃśayaṃ pārthivārhasi
body.translated_text: If you do me a favor, O king, then, O king, you ought to ask the seers this doubt of mine'

body.text:
brūhi subhru mataṃ yat te
praṣṭavyā yan mayā dvijāḥ
bhūyo 'ham ātmasaṃdehaṃ
prakṣyāmy etān dvijottamān
body.translated_text: 'Tell me, O fair-browed one, what is your view, what is to be asked by me of the brahmins; I shall further ask these best of the twice-born about my own doubt'

body.text:
śrūyante pṛthivīpāla
nṛpa ye ca purātanāḥ
teṣāṃ na saṃpad bhūpāla
yathā tava kilābhavat
body.translated_text: 'There are heard of, O protector of the earth, the kings who were of old; their fortune, O lord of the earth, was not such as yours has indeed become

body.text:
tad īdṛksaṃpadāṃ dhāma
tvam aśeṣakṣitīśvaraḥ
yena karmavipākena
tad vadantu maharṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: [As to] that abode of such fortunes [which] you [are], the lord of the entire earth—by what ripening of action that [came to be], let the great seers declare

body.text:
ahaṃ ca bhavato bhāryā
sarvasīmantinī bhuvi
vidhinā kena tapasā
niyuktā bhavato gṛhe
atīva karmaṇā yena
tadvijñāne kutūhalam
body.translated_text: And I, your wife, [highest] of all women on earth—by what rite, by what austerity, was I appointed in your house, by what exceedingly [great] action—there is curiosity for the knowledge of that

body.text:
tāratamyatayeśitvam
anyeṣv api hi vidyate
nirastātiśayatvena
nūnaṃ nālpena karmaṇā
body.translated_text: Lordship by gradation exists in others too; but surely [such lordship] free of [all] superiority [does] not [arise] from a small action

body.text:
tad anyajanmacaritaṃ
naranātha nijaṃ bhavān
munīn pṛcchatu yā cāhaṃ
yan mayā ca purā kṛtam
body.translated_text: So, O lord of men, [as to] that deed of [your] other birth, your own, let your Honor ask the sages; and [as to] what I am, and what was done by me of old'

body.text:
sa tathoktas tayā rājā
patnyā vismitamānasaḥ
munīnāṃ purato bhāryāṃ
praśaṃsan vākyam abravīt
body.translated_text: That king, thus addressed by his wife, his mind astonished, praising his wife before the sages, spoke [these] words:

body.text:
sādhu devi mataṃ yan me
tvayā tad idam īritam
satyaṃ munivacaḥ puṃsām
ardhaṃ vai gṛhiṇī yathā
body.translated_text: 'Well [said], O goddess; the view of mine, that very thing has been uttered by you; true is the saying of the sages, that the housewife is verily the half of men

body.text:
mamāpy etad abhipretam
imān praṣṭuṃ mahāmunīn
yat tvayābhihitaṃ bhadre
matsvabhāvānuyātayā
body.translated_text: This too is intended by me—to ask these great sages [that] which has been spoken by you, O blessed one, who follow my own nature

body.text:
so 'ham etan mahābhāge
prakṣyāmy etān mahāmunīn
naiṣām aviditaṃ kiṃcit
triṣu lokeṣu vidyate
body.translated_text: So I, O greatly fortunate one, shall ask these great sages this; there is nothing unknown to them that exists in the three worlds'

body.text:
evam uktvā priyāṃ bhāryāṃ
praṇipatya ca tān ṛṣīn
yathāvad etad akhilaṃ
papracchāsurasattama
body.translated_text: Having thus spoken to his dear wife, and having bowed to those seers, he duly asked all this, O best of <s>asuras</s>:

body.text:
bhagavanto mamāśeṣaṃ
prasādāhṛtacetasaḥ
kathayantu yathāvṛttaṃ
yan mayā sukṛtaṃ kṛtam
body.translated_text: 'O blessed ones, whose minds are drawn by [my] propitiation, declare to me entirely, as it [truly] happened, what good deed was done by me

body.text:
ko 'ham āsaṃ purā viprāḥ
kiṃ ca karma mayā kṛtam
kiṃ vānayā sucārvaṅgyā
mama patnyā kṛtaṃ dvijāḥ
body.translated_text: Who was I formerly, O <s>vipras</s>, and what action was done by me? And what was done by this fair-limbed wife of mine, O twice-born,

body.text:
yenāvayor iyaṃ sphītir
martyaloke sudurlabhā
catvāraś cāpratihatā
gatayo mama gacchataḥ
body.translated_text: by which this prosperity of us two, very hard to obtain in the mortal world, [arose], and [by which] four unimpeded courses are mine as I go,

body.text:
aśeṣā bhūbhṛto vaśyāḥ
kośasyānto na vidyate
balaṃ caivāpratihataṃ
śarīrārogyam uttamam
body.translated_text: all the rulers of the earth are subject [to me], there is no end to the treasury, and [my] strength is unobstructed, [my] bodily health supreme,

body.text:
atibhāti ca me kāntyā
bhāryeyam akhilaṃ jagat
mamāpi vapuṣas tejo
na kaścit sahate dvijāḥ
body.translated_text: and this wife of mine outshines the entire world with [her] loveliness, and the splendor of my body too no one can endure, O twice-born

body.text:
so 'ham icchāmi vijñātuṃ
tathaiveyam aninditā
nijānuṣṭhānam akhilaṃ
yasyāśeṣam idaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: So I wish to know, and likewise this blameless one, [our] entire own [past] practice, of which all this is the fruit'

body.text:
iti praṣṭā narendreṇa
samastās te tapodhanāḥ
vasiṣṭhaṃ codayām āsuḥ
kathyatām iti bhūbhṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus asked by the king, all those rich in austerity urged <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>: 'Let it be told to the king'

body.text:
coditaḥ so 'pi dharmajñair
maitrāvaruṇir ātmavān
yogam āsthāya suciraṃ
yathāvad yatamānasaḥ
jñātavān nṛpates tasya
pūrvadehaviceṣṭitam
body.translated_text: Urged by the knowers of <s>dharma</s>, he too, the self-possessed son of <s>Mitrā</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> (<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>), having taken up <s>yoga</s> for a long while, with striving mind, duly came to know the doings of that king's former body

body.text:
sa tam āha munir bhūpaṃ
viditārtho mahāsura
māndhātāraṃ mahābuddhiṃ
sapatnīkam idaṃ vacaḥ
body.translated_text: That sage, having known the matter, said this to the king, O great <s>asura</s>—to <s>Māndhātṛ</s> of great mind, together with his wife:

body.text:
śṛṇu bhūpāla sakalaṃ
yasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam
tava rājyādikaṃ subhrūr
yeyaṃ cāsīn mahīpate
body.translated_text: 'Hear, O lord of the earth, all of it—of which deed your kingdom and the rest is the fruit, O fair-browed [queen], and [the deed] which this [queen] performed, O lord of the earth:

body.text:
tvam āsīḥ śūdrajātīyaḥ
parahiṃsāparāyaṇaḥ
vākkrūro daṇḍapāruṣyo
niḥsnehaḥ sarvajantuṣu
body.translated_text: You were of the <s>śūdra</s> class, intent on harming others, harsh of speech, cruel in punishment, devoid of affection toward all creatures

body.text:
tatheyaṃ bhavato bhāryā
pūrvam apy āyatekṣaṇā
dveṣyā babhūva taccittā
tava śuśrūṣaṇe ratā
body.translated_text: And likewise this wife of yours, even formerly long-eyed, was hateful, of [such] a mind, [yet] devoted to your service

body.text:
pativratā mahābhāgā
bhartsyamānāpy aniṣṭhurā
tvadvākyād anu sarveṣu
vīrakarmasu codyatā
body.translated_text: A devoted wife (<s>pativratā</s>), greatly fortunate, though reviled [she was] not harsh; at your word she was eager in all heroic deeds

body.text:
naiṣṭhuryād asahāyasya
tyajyamānasya bandhubhiḥ
kṣayaṃ jagāma yo 'rtho 'bhūt
saṃcitaḥ prapitāmahaiḥ
body.translated_text: Through the harshness of [your relations], you being without help and abandoned by your kinsmen, the wealth which had been accumulated by your forefathers went to ruin

body.text:
tasmin kṣīṇe kṛṣiparas
tvam āsīḥ pṛthivīpate
sāpi karmavipākena
kṛṣir viphalatāṃ gatā
body.translated_text: When that was exhausted, you became intent on agriculture, O lord of the earth; but that agriculture too, by the ripening of [past] deeds, went to fruitlessness

body.text:
tato niḥsvaṃ parikṣīṇaṃ
pareṣāṃ bhṛtyatāṃ gatam
tatyāja sādhvī veyaṃ tvāṃ
tyajyamānāpi pārthiva
body.translated_text: Then, though you were destitute, utterly impoverished, [and] reduced to servitude to others, this virtuous woman did not abandon you, O prince, even when [she herself was] being abandoned

body.text:
anayā ca samaṃ sādhvyā
viṣṇor āvasathe tvayā
kṛtaṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ vīra
parivrāḍbrahmacāriṇām
body.translated_text: And together with this virtuous woman, in the dwelling of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, service was rendered by you, O hero, to the wandering ascetics and <s>brahmacārins</s>

body.text:
bhagnehaḥ sarvakāmebhyas
tanmayas tvaṃ tadarpaṇaḥ
ananyagatir ekasthas
tasminn āyatane hareḥ
body.translated_text: Your longings broken off from all desires, [you became] consisting of him, devoting [all] to him, having no other recourse, abiding solely in that temple of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
tadvṛttilipsuḥ śuśrūṣāṃ
janarañjanahetukaḥ
kṛtavān yogināṃ vīra
kṛṣṇasya jagataḥ pateḥ
body.translated_text: Desiring [merely] a livelihood thereby, you rendered service—[ostensibly] for the sake of pleasing people—to the <s>yogins</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord of the world, O hero

body.text:
vāsudevājire nityaṃ
kṛtaṃ saṃmārjanaṃ tvayā
tathaivābhyukṣaṇaṃ vīra
nityaṃ caivānulepanam
patnyānayā ca dharmajña
yaṣmaccittānuvṛttayā
body.translated_text: In the courtyard of <s>Vāsudeva</s> the daily sweeping was done by you, and likewise the sprinkling [with water], O hero, and the daily smearing [of the floor], and by this wife [of yours], O knower of <s>dharma</s>, devoted to following your mind

body.text:
ahany ahani tat karma
yuvayor nṛpa kurvatoḥ
tatra caitanmayatvena
pāpahānir ajāyata
body.translated_text: As the two of you performed that work day after day, O king, there, through [your] becoming consisting of him, a loss of sin came about

body.text:
viṣṇoḥ kāryaṃ mayā kāryaṃ
yogiśuśrūṣaṇaṃ tathā
na prabhātaṃ prabhātaṃ tu
cinteyam abhavan niśi
body.translated_text: 'The work of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be done by me, and likewise the service of the <s>yogins</s>; would that it were not dawn'—but when it dawned, this was your thought in the night

body.text:
evam āyatanaṃ ramyam
ity evaṃ ca sukhāvaham
sthairyaṃ na caivam etat syād
ity āsīt te manaḥ sadā
body.translated_text: 'Thus the temple is delightful, and thus it brings happiness; would that this steadiness might [last]'—thus was your mind always

body.text:
yogināṃ sukhadaṃ tv evaṃ
karmaivaṃ naivam ity api
tava cittam abhūt tatra
yogikarmaṇy aharniśam
body.translated_text: 'This work, the giver of happiness to the <s>yogins</s>, [should] be thus and not otherwise'—thus was your mind there, day and night, upon the work of the <s>yogins</s>

body.text:
evaṃ tanmanasas tatra
kṛtodyogasya pārthiva
bhṛtyāvasāyinaḥ samyag
yathoktādhikakāriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, of you, your mind there [fixed], having made [such] effort, O prince, of you abiding as a servant, performing rightly even more than was enjoined,

body.text:
smarataḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
kāryeṇātidṛḍhātmanaḥ
niḥśeṣam upaśāntaṃ tat
pāpaṃ yoginiṣevaṇāt
body.translated_text: remembering <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, of exceedingly firm self [fixed] on the task, that sin was wholly appeased through the service of the <s>yogins</s>

body.text:
tato 'dhikaṃ puras tasmād
ādarād anulepanam
saṃmārjanaṃ ca bahuśaḥ
sapatnikena te kṛtam
body.translated_text: Then, more than before, out of reverence, the smearing and the sweeping, many times over, was done by you together with your wife

body.text:
tatrāgataś ca sauvīraḥ
purujin nāma bhūpatiḥ
mahāsainyaparīvāraḥ
prabhūtagajavāhanaḥ
body.translated_text: And there came a king of <s>Sauvīra</s> named <s>Purujit</s>, surrounded by a great army, with abundant elephants and mounts

body.text:
sarvasaṃpadupetaṃ taṃ
sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam
vṛtaṃ bhāryāsahasreṇa
dṛṣṭvā srakcandanojjvalam
spṛhā kṛtā tvayā tatra
cārumaulini pārthive
body.translated_text: Seeing him endowed with all prosperity, adorned with all ornaments, attended by a thousand wives, resplendent with garlands and sandal, a longing was made by you there, O prince of fair crown

body.text:
sarvakāmapradaṃ karma
devadevasya kurvatā
tenaitad akhilaṃ rājyam
aśeṣadvīpavat tava
body.translated_text: By you who performed the all-desire-granting work of the god of gods, this entire kingdom, [extending] like the whole continent, [came] to you

body.text:
tejaś caivādhikaṃ yat te
tathaitac chṛṇu pārthiva
yogaprabhāvopalabdhaṃ
kathayāmy akhilaṃ tava
body.translated_text: And the splendour too of yours which is [so] great—hear of that, O prince; obtained through the power of [that] yoga[-service], I declare the whole of it to you

body.text:
tatraivāvasathe dīpaḥ
praśāntaḥ snehasaṃkṣayāt
nijabhojanatailena
punaḥ prajvālitas tvayā
body.translated_text: There, in that very dwelling, a lamp, extinguished by the exhaustion of its oil, was re-kindled by you with your own eating-oil

body.text:
anayā cottarīyānta-
cīravartyupavṛṃhitaḥ
tava patnyā sa jajvāla
kāntir asyās tato 'dhikā
body.translated_text: And it was nourished by this wife of yours with a wick made from the end-fringe of her upper garment; it blazed [the more], and her beauty thereafter became the greater

body.text:
tavāpy akhilabhūpāla-
manaḥkṣobhakaraṃ tataḥ
tejo narendra na syāc ca
kim ārādhya janārdanam
body.translated_text: Therefore that splendour of yours which agitates the minds of all kings, O lord of men—what would not be [attained], having worshipped <s>Janārdana</s>?

body.text:
evaṃ narendra śūdratvād
viṣṇukarmaparāyaṇaḥ
tanmayatvena saṃprāpto
mahimānam anuttamam
body.translated_text: Thus, O lord of men, [though] from śūdrahood, [being] devoted to the work of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, through becoming consisting of him, you have attained unsurpassed greatness

body.text:
kiṃ punar yo naro bhaktyā
viṣṇuśuśrūṣaṇādṛtaḥ
karoti satataṃ pūjāṃ
niṣkāmo nānyamānasaḥ
body.translated_text: How much more [then] the man who, with devotion, reverent in the service of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, performs worship constantly, free of desire, with mind on no other?

body.text:
sa tvam ṛddhim imāṃ labdhvā
sarvalokeśvareśvaram
pūjayācyutam īśeśaṃ
tam ārādhya na sīdati
body.translated_text: So you, having obtained this prosperity, worship <s>Acyuta</s>, the Lord of the lords of all worlds, the Lord of lords; having worshipped him, one does not sink down

body.text:
puṣpair dhūpais tathā gandhair
dīpavastrānulepanaiḥ
ārādhayācyutaṃ tadvad
veśmasaṃmārjanādibhiḥ
body.translated_text: With flowers, incense, and perfumes, with lamps, garments, and unguents, worship <s>Acyuta</s> likewise, with the sweeping of his house and the rest

body.text:
yad yad iṣṭatamaṃ kiṃcid
yad yad atyantadurlabham
tat tad dāttvā jagaddhātre
vaikuṇṭhāya na sīdati
body.translated_text: Whatever is most cherished, whatever is exceedingly hard to get—giving that to the Maker of the world, to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, one does not sink down

body.text:
sugandhāgarukarpūra-
candanākṣodakuṃkumaiḥ
vāsobhir vividhair dhūpaiḥ
puṣpasragcāmarair dhvajaiḥ
body.translated_text: With fragrant aloe-wood, camphor, sandal-powder, and saffron, with various garments, with incenses, with flower-garlands, yak-tail whisks, and banners,

body.text:
annopahārair vividhair
ghṛtakṣīrābhiṣecanaiḥ
gītavāditanṛtyādyais
toṣayasvācyutaṃ nṛpa
body.translated_text: with various food-offerings, with bathings of ghee and milk, with song, instrumental music, dance and the rest, gratify <s>Acyuta</s>, O king

body.text:
puṇyarātriṣu govindaṃ
nṛtyagītaravojjvalaiḥ
bhūpa jāgaraṇair bhaktyā
toṣayācyutam avyayam
body.translated_text: On holy nights gratify <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Acyuta</s> the imperishable, with vigils resplendent with the sounds of dance and song, O king, with devotion

body.text:
evaṃ saṃtoṣyate bhaktyā
bhagavān bhavabhaṅgakṛt
bhūpa bhāgavatair bhūta-
bhavyakṛt keśavo naraiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, O king, the Blessed Lord, the breaker of [the cycle of] existence, <s>Keśava</s>, the maker of past and future, is well gratified by devotion by men who are <s>Bhāgavatas</s>

body.text:
yeṣāṃ na vittaṃ tair bhaktyā
mārjanādyupalepanaiḥ
toṣito bhagavān viṣṇur
dadāty abhimataṃ phalam
body.translated_text: By those who have no wealth, the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, gratified with devotion by sweeping and smearing and the rest, gives the desired fruit

body.text:
devakarmāsamarthāṇāṃ
prāṇināṃ smṛtisaṃstavaiḥ
toṣito 'bhimatān kāmān
prayacchati janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: For living beings incapable of the [costly] worship of the god, <s>Janārdana</s>, gratified by remembrances and hymns, grants the desired wishes

body.text:
naiṣa vittair na ratnaughaiḥ
puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ
sadbhāvenaiva govindas
toṣam āyāti saṃsmṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: He, <s>Govinda</s>, comes to satisfaction not by riches, nor by masses of jewels, nor by flowers, incense, and unguents, but by [right] disposition alone, when remembered

body.text:
tvayaikāgramanaskena
gṛhasaṃmārjanādikam
kṛtvālpam īdṛśaṃ prāptaṃ
rājyam atyantadurlabham
body.translated_text: By you, of single-pointed mind, having done such a small thing as the sweeping of [his] house and the rest, this kingdom, exceedingly hard to get, was obtained

body.text:
prāptopakaraṇo yas tvam
ekāgramatir acyutam
toṣayiṣyasi nendro 'pi
bhavitā tena te samaḥ
body.translated_text: You, having obtained the [royal] equipment, of single-pointed mind, will gratify <s>Acyuta</s>; not even <s>Indra</s> will [then] become your equal

body.text:
tasmāt tvam anayā devyā
sahātyantavinītayā
keśavārādhane yatnaṃ
kuru dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
body.translated_text: Therefore you, together with this queen, exceedingly humble, make effort in the worship of <s>Keśava</s>, O best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
tataḥ prāpsyasi bhaktyaiva
yat tapobhiḥ sudurlabham
body.translated_text: Then by devotion alone you shall attain that which is very hard to get by austerities

body.text:
etan muner vasiṣṭhasya
niśāmya vacanaṃ nṛpaḥ
bhāryāsahāyaḥ sa tadā
saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ
body.translated_text: Having heard this word of the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the king then, accompanied by his wife, his hair bristling [with joy],

body.text:
kṛtakāryam ivātmānaṃ
manyamāno 'surottama
uvāca praṇato bhūtvā
māndhātā vāruṇiṃ vacaḥ
body.translated_text: deeming himself as one whose purpose was accomplished, O best of <s>asuras</s>, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, having become bowed, spoke a word to the son of <s>Varuṇa</s> [Vasiṣṭha]:

body.text:
yathāmaratvaṃ saṃprāpya
yathā vā brahma śāśvatam
paraṃ nirvāṇam āpnoti
tathāhaṃ vacasā tava
body.translated_text: "As one having attained immortality, or as [one attaining] the eternal <s>Brahman</s>, attains supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s>, so [am] I, by your word

body.text:
kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhī cāsmi
nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ
ajñānatamasāchanne
yat pradīpas tvayaidhitaḥ
body.translated_text: I am one whose purpose is accomplished and happy, having attained supreme contentment, in that, [when I was] covered by the darkness of ignorance, a lamp was kindled by you

body.text:
aham eṣā ca tanvaṅgī
vibhūtibhraṃsabhīrukau
āḍhyāv āpāditau brahmann
ihādya vacasā tava
body.translated_text: I and this slender-limbed one, fearful of the loss of [our] fortune, have been made rich, O <s>brahman</s>, here today by your word

body.text:
saṃpadāṃ kathitaṃ bījam
āvayor bhavatā mune
taduptāv udyatāv āvāṃ
vijānīhi dvijottama
body.translated_text: The seed of prosperities of the two of us has been told by you, O sage; know us two to be ready for the sowing of that [seed], O best of the twice-born"

body.text:
na ratnair na ca vittaughair
na ca puṣpānulepanaiḥ
ārādhyate jagannātho
bhāvaśūnyair janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: "Not by jewels, nor by masses of wealth, nor by flowers and unguents is the Lord of the world, <s>Janārdana</s>, worshipped [by those] devoid of [right] disposition

body.text:
bāhyārthanirapekṣaiś ca
manasaiva manogatiḥ
niḥsvair ārādhyate devo
viṣṇuḥ sarveśvareśvaraḥ
body.translated_text: And indifferent to external means, [he, whose] course is the mind, [is worshipped] by the mind alone; the god <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of the lords of all, is worshipped [even] by the destitute

body.text:
sarvam etan mayā jñātaṃ
yat tvam āttha mahāmune
yat tvāṃ pṛcchāmi tan me tvaṃ
prasādasumukho vada
body.translated_text: All this is known by me, what you say, O great sage; but what I ask you, that, O you of gracious face, tell me:

body.text:
kāni vratāni yair devo
naraiḥ strībhiś ca keśavaḥ
toṣam ārādhito 'bhyeti
kaiś ca dānair mahāmune
body.translated_text: Which are the vows by which the god <s>Keśava</s>, worshipped by men and by women, comes to satisfaction, and by which gifts, O great sage?

body.text:
rahasyāni ca devasya
prītaye yāni cakriṇaḥ
tāny aśeṣāṇi me brūhi
kṛṣṇārādhanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: And the secret [rites] of the god, the discus-bearer, which are for [his] pleasure—tell me all those, [I] who desire the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>"

body.text:
śṛṇu bhūpāla yair viṣṇur
narair ārādhyate vrataiḥ
nārībhiś cātighore 'smin
patitābhir bhavārṇave
body.translated_text: "Hear, O lord of the earth, the vows by which <s>Viṣṇu</s> is worshipped by men, and by women fallen into this exceedingly terrible ocean of existence

body.text:
samabhyarcya jagannāthaṃ
vāsudevaṃ samādhinā
ekam aśnāti yo bhaktaṃ
dvitīyaṃ brāhmaṇātmakam
karoti keśavaprītyai
kārttikaṃ māsam ātmavān
body.translated_text: He who, having worshipped the Lord of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, with concentration, eats one [meal as] a devotee [and] makes a second consisting of [feeding] a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, [thus] self-possessed, [passes] the month of <s>Kārttika</s> for the pleasure of <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
pūrve vayasi yat tena
jñānato 'jñānato 'pi vā
pāpam ācaritaṃ tasmān
mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: Whatever sin was committed by him in the earlier part of his life, knowingly or unknowingly, from that he is freed; there is no doubt here

body.text:
anenaiva vidhānena
mārgaśīrṣe 'pi mādhavam
samabhyarcyaikabhaktaṃ vai
varṇibhyo yaḥ prayacchati
bhagavatprīṇanārthāya
phalaṃ tasya śṛṇuṣva me
body.translated_text: By this very ordinance, in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> too, having worshipped <s>Mādhava</s> [with] a single meal, he who gives [food] to the religious students for the sake of pleasing the Blessed Lord—hear from me the fruit of that:

body.text:
madhye vayasi yat pāpaṃ
yoṣitā puruṣeṇa vā
kṛtaṃ tasmāc ca tenokto
vimokṣaḥ paramātmanā
body.translated_text: Whatever sin was committed in the middle part of life by a woman or a man, from that the release was declared by the Supreme Self

body.text:
tathā caivaikabhaktaṃ vai
varṇāgrebhyaḥ prayacchati
puṇḍarīkākṣam abhyarcya
pauṣamāse mahīpate
body.translated_text: And likewise, [eating] a single meal, he gives to the foremost of the classes [brāhmaṇas], having worshipped <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, O lord of the earth

body.text:
tatprīṇanāya yat pāpaṃ
vārddhike tena vai kṛtam
sa tasmān mucyate rājan
pumān yoṣid athāpi vā
body.translated_text: Whatever sin was committed in old age for [the purpose of] pleasing him—from that, O king, a man or a woman is freed

body.text:
traimāsikavratam idaṃ
yaḥ karoti nareśvara
sa viṣṇuprīṇanāt pāpair
laghubhir vipramucyate
