body.translated_text: He who performs this three-monthly vow, O lord of men, is freed by the pleasing of <s>Viṣṇu</s> from the lighter sins

body.text:
dvitīye vatsare rājan
mucyate copapātakaiḥ
tadvat tṛtīye 'pi kṛtaṃ
mahāpātakanāśanam
body.translated_text: In the second year, O king, one is freed from the minor sins (<s>upapātaka</s>); likewise in the third too, [the vow] performed is the destroyer of the great sins (<s>mahāpātaka</s>)

body.text:
vratam etan naraiḥ strībhis
tribhir māsair anuṣṭhitam
tribhiḥ saṃvatsarair eva
pradadāti phalaṃ nṛṇām
body.translated_text: This vow, observed by men and women for three months, [each year] for three years indeed, yields its fruit to men

body.text:
tribhir māsais trir avasthās
trividhāt pātakān nṛpa
trīṇi nāmāni devasya
mocayanti trivārṣikaiḥ
body.translated_text: By three months [it covers] the three conditions [of life]; from the threefold sin, O king, the three names of the god, by [observance over] three years, release [one]

body.text:
yatas tato vratam idaṃ
trikramaṃ samudāhṛtam
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ
keśavārādhanaṃ param
body.translated_text: Since [it is] so, this vow is proclaimed [as] the three-step (<s>trikrama</s>); the appeaser of all sins, the supreme worship of <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
śṛṇuṣva ca mahīpāla
vrataṃ viṣṇupadatrayam
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ
yaj jagāda purā hariḥ
body.translated_text: And hear, O lord of the earth, the vow of the three steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>viṣṇupadatraya</s>), the appeaser of all sins, which <s>Hari</s> declared of old

body.text:
prācetasāya dakṣāya
dakṣaś cāha vivasvate
vivasvān alasidhrāya
alasidhro 'sitāya ca
body.translated_text: to <s>Prācetasa</s> <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Dakṣa</s> told it to <s>Vivasvat</s>, <s>Vivasvat</s> to <s>Alasidhra</s>, and <s>Alasidhra</s> to <s>Asita</s>

body.text:
asitena samākhyātam
alpāyāsaṃ mahāphalam
tad idaṃ śrūyatāṃ samyag
vrataṃ viṣṇupadatrayam
body.translated_text: By <s>Asita</s> it was declared [to be] of little exertion [yet] great fruit; let this very [vow], the vow of the three steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, be heard rightly

body.text:
dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ
viṣṇum ārādhya pṛṣṭavān
bahuśas tu vipannāyāṃ
sṛṣṭāv arinisūdana
body.translated_text: <s>Dakṣa</s> <s>Prajāpati</s>, of old, having worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, asked—the creation having repeatedly failed, O slayer of foes:

body.text:
bhagavan sarvakaṛtvaṃ
mamādiṣṭaṃ svayaṃbhuvā
brahmaṇā devadeveśa
tavādeśena keśava
body.translated_text: "O Blessed One, the doing of all [creation] was enjoined to me by the self-existent <s>Brahmā</s>, O god of gods, by your command, O <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
vipannā ca jagannātha
mama sṛṣṭiḥ kṛtā kṛtā
pūrvakarmavipākena
vyākulaś cāsmi cetasā
body.translated_text: And my creation, O Lord of the world, [though] made, made [again], failed through the ripening of past deeds; and I am agitated in mind

body.text:
yathā ca deva mucyeya
asmāt saṃsārasaṃkaṭāt
viṣayāsaṅgaviṣamāt
tan mamājñāpayācyuta
body.translated_text: And how I might be freed, O god, from this peril of <s>saṃsāra</s>, fraught with attachment to sense-objects—command me in that, O <s>Acyuta</s>"

body.text:
ity evam ukto dakṣeṇa
devadevo janārdanaḥ
ācaṣṭa duḥkhakṣayadaṃ
vrataṃ viṣṇupadatrayam
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Dakṣa</s>, the god of gods <s>Janārdana</s> related the vow of the three steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the bestower of the destruction of sorrow,

body.text:
sarvārambhaviniṣpatti-
kārakaṃ pāpanāśanam
saṃsārocchedakaṃ dhīrair
ācīrṇaṃ sthirabuddhibhiḥ
body.translated_text: the effecter of the accomplishment of all undertakings, the destroyer of sin, the cutter-off of <s>saṃsāra</s>, practiced by the steadfast of firm intellect

body.text:
tad ahaṃ tava rājendra
vratānām uttamottamam
kathayāmi samācaṣṭa
yathā pūrvaṃ mamāsitaḥ
body.translated_text: So I, O king of kings, tell you the best of the best of vows, [the vow] which <s>Asita</s> related to me as before:

body.text:
āṣāḍhe māsi pūrvāsu
tathāṣāḍhāsu pārthiva
samabhyarcya jagannātham
acyutaṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ
body.translated_text: In the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, [when the moon is] in the former <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> [asterism], O prince, having worshipped the Lord of the world, <s>Acyuta</s>, restrained and pure,

body.text:
puṣpair hṛdyais tathā dhūpair
gandhaiḥ sāgarucandanaiḥ
yathāvibhavataś cānyair
annair vāsobhir eva ca
body.translated_text: with pleasing flowers and likewise with incenses, with perfumes of sea[-foam camphor] and sandal, and with other [offerings] according to [one's] means, with foods and garments too,

body.text:
kṣīrasnehasthitaṃ tadvat
paiṣṭaṃ viṣṇupadadvayam
samabhyarcya yathānyāyaṃ
keśavasyāgrato nyaset
body.translated_text: and a pair of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-feet (<s>viṣṇupada</s>) made of flour set in milk and oil, having worshipped [them] according to rule, he should place before <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
yavāṃś ca dadyād viprāya
bhūgatiḥ prīyatām iti
naktaṃ bhuñjīta rājendra
haviṣyānnaṃ susaṃskṛtam
body.translated_text: And he should give barley to a <s>vipra</s> [saying] 'May the support of the earth be pleased'; he should eat at night, O king of kings, well-prepared sacrificial food (<s>haviṣya</s>)

body.text:
tathottarāsv āṣāḍhāsu
śrāvaṇe māsi mānavaḥ
tathaivābhyarcya govindaṃ
tadvad viṣṇupadadvayam
body.translated_text: And likewise [when the moon is] in the latter <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>, in the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, the man, having likewise worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, and likewise the pair of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-feet,

body.text:
viprāya ca yavān dadyāt
prīṇayitvā ca bhūgatim
naktaṃ bhūñjīta rājendra
naro yoṣid athāpi vā
body.translated_text: should give barley to a <s>vipra</s>, and having pleased the support of the earth, should eat at night, O king of kings, [whether] a man or a woman

body.text:
prāpte bhādrapade māsi
pūrvabhadrapadāsu ca
tathaivābhyarcya govindaṃ
tadvad viṣṇupadadvayam
body.translated_text: When the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s> has arrived, [the moon being] in [the asterism] <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, having likewise worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, and likewise the pair of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-feet,

body.text:
viprāya ca yavān dattvā
prīṇayitvā bhuvogatim
bhuñjīta gorasaprāyaṃ
naro yoṣid athāpi vā
body.translated_text: and having given barley to a <s>vipra</s>, having pleased the support of the earth, [a man] should eat food consisting mostly of milk-products, [whether] a man or a woman

body.text:
tadvad āśvayuje dānaṃ
tadvad govindapūjanam
padadvayasya pūjāṃ ca
prīṇanaṃ ca bhuvogateḥ
body.translated_text: Likewise the gift in <s>Āśvayuja</s>, likewise the worship of <s>Govinda</s>, and the worship of the pair of feet, and the pleasing of the support of the earth

body.text:
tathaiva naktaṃ bhuñjīta
gorasaṃ maunam āsthitaḥ
strī vā rājendra pūrvāsu
tathā bhadrapadāsu vai
body.translated_text: Likewise he should eat at night milk-products, observing silence, [or] a woman [should], O king of kings, [the moon being] in the former [asterism] and likewise in [Pūrva]bhādrapadā

body.text:
phālgune phalgunī pūrvā
bhavatī ha yadā nṛpa
trivikramaṃ tadā devaṃ
pūrvoktavidhinārcayet
body.translated_text: In <s>Phālguna</s>, when the former <s>Phalgunī</s> [asterism] occurs, O king, then he should worship the god <s>Trivikrama</s> by the rule stated before

body.text:
padadvayaṃ ca devasya
samyag abhyarcya pārthiva
hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā
svargatiḥ prīyatām iti
body.translated_text: And the pair of feet of the god, having worshipped rightly, O prince, having given gold [as] a fee, [saying] 'May the journey to heaven be pleased',

body.text:
naktaṃ bhuñjīta rājendra
vahnipākavivarjitam
eṣa evottarāyoge
caitre māse vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: he should eat at night, O king of kings, [food] free of fire-cooking; this very same rule is recorded for the month of <s>Caitra</s> in conjunction with the northward [course]

body.text:
etaj jagāda govindaḥ
purā dakṣāya pṛcchate
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ
vrataṃ viṣṇupadatrayam
body.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> declared this of old to <s>Dakṣa</s> who asked—the all-sin-removing, meritorious vow of the three steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
yathoktam etad yo bhakto
karoti nṛpasattama
sarvakāmān avāpnoti
keśavasya vaco yathā
body.translated_text: He, a devotee, who performs this as declared, O best of kings, attains all desires, as the word of <s>Keśava</s> [promises]

body.text:
aputro labhate putram
apatir labhate patim
samāgamaṃ proṣitaiś ca
tathā prāpnoti bāndhavaiḥ
body.translated_text: The sonless obtains a son, the husbandless obtains a husband, and likewise one attains reunion with departed kinsmen

body.text:
dravyam aiśvaryam ārogyaṃ
saubhāgyaṃ cārurūpatām
prāpnuvanty akhilān etān
pūjayitvā padatrayam
body.translated_text: Wealth, lordship, health, good fortune, and lovely form—all these they obtain, having worshipped the three steps [of Viṣṇu]

body.text:
yān yān kāmān naraḥ strī vā
hṛdayenābhivāñchanti
tāṃs tāṃś cāpnoti niṣkāmo
viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
body.translated_text: Whatever desires a man or a woman longs for with the heart, those one obtains—and one free of desire goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
pūrvaṃ kṛtvāpi pāpāni
naraḥ strī vā narādhipa
padatrayavrataṃ cīrtvā
mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
body.translated_text: Even having formerly done sins, a man or a woman, O lord of men, having performed the vow of the three steps, is released from all sins

body.text:
viṣṇor ārādhanārthāya
yāni dānāni sattama
deyāni tāny aśeṣāṇi
mamācakṣva dvijottama
body.translated_text: Tell me, O best of the twice-born, the most excellent one, all those gifts that are to be given for the sake of the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
yena caiva vidhānena
dānaṃ puṃsaḥ sukhāvaham
prīṇanāya ca kṛṣṇasya
tan mamākhyāhi vistarāt
body.translated_text: And by what rule a gift brings happiness to a man and is for the gladdening of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—tell me that in detail

body.text:
kṛtopavāsaḥ saṃprāśya
pañcagavyaṃ nareśvara
ghṛtakṣīrābhiṣekaṃ ca
kṛtvā viṣṇoḥ samāhitaḥ
body.translated_text: Having kept a fast, having eaten the <s>pañcagavya</s> (five products of the cow), O lord of men, and having made the ablution [of the image] with ghee and milk, of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, concentrated,

body.text:
samabhyarcya ca govindaṃ
puṣpādibhir ariṃdama
udaṅmukhīm arcayitvā
tathā gṛṣṭiṃ payasvinīm
body.translated_text: and having worshipped <s>Govinda</s> with flowers and the rest, O subduer of foes, having worshipped a north-facing milk-giving young cow,

body.text:
saputrāṃ vastrasaṃvītāṃ
sitayajñopavītinīm
svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ śubhākārāṃ
hiraṇyoparisaṃsthitām
body.translated_text: together with her calf, wrapped in a cloth, wearing a white sacred thread, with golden horns, of auspicious form, standing upon gold,

body.text:
hiraṇyaṃ vācayitvāgre
brāhmaṇāyopapādayet
imāṃ tvaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva
govindaḥ prīyatām iti
body.translated_text: having first declared [the gift of] gold, one should present [her] to a brahmin [saying]: "Receive this; may <s>Govinda</s> be pleased"

body.text:
samyag uccārya taṃ vipraṃ
govindaṃ nṛpa kalpayet
anuvrajec ca gacchantaṃ
padāny aṣṭau narādhipa
body.translated_text: Having rightly addressed that <s>vipra</s> [as] <s>Govinda</s>, O king, one should so regard [him], and should follow him as he goes for eight steps, O lord of men

body.text:
anena vidhinā dhenuṃ
yo viprāya prayacchati
govindaprīṇanād rājan
viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
body.translated_text: He who by this rule presents a cow to a <s>vipra</s>, through the gladdening of <s>Govinda</s>, O king, goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
saptāvarāṃs tathā pūrvān
saptātmānaṃ ca mānavaḥ
saptajanmakṛtāt pāpān
mocayaty avanīpate
body.translated_text: And the man delivers the seven later [descendants] and the seven former [ancestors], and his [seventh] self, from the sin committed in seven births, O lord of the earth

body.text:
pade pade ca yajñasya
gosavasya sa mānavaḥ
phalam āpnoti rājendra
dakṣāyaivaṃ jagau hariḥ
body.translated_text: And at every step that man obtains the fruit of the <s>Gosava</s> sacrifice, O lord of kings—thus <s>Hari</s> sang to <s>Dakṣa</s>

body.text:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya
sarvakāleṣu pārthiva
bhavaty aghaughāpaharā
yāvad indrāś caturdaśa
body.translated_text: It becomes the remover of the flood of sins, [the giver] of all desires fulfilled at all times, O king, for as long as the fourteen <s>Indras</s> [endure]

body.text:
sarveṣām eva pāpānāṃ
kṛtānām avijānatā
prāyaścittam idaṃ śastam
anutāpopavṛṃhitam
body.translated_text: Of all sins committed unknowingly, this expiation, augmented by remorse, is commended

body.text:
ikṣvākunaiṣā rājendra
pūrvaṃ dattā mahātmanā
tataḥ sa lokān amalān
prāptavān avanīpatiḥ
body.translated_text: By <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, O lord of kings, this was formerly given, by the great soul; thereupon that lord of the earth attained the stainless worlds

body.text:
tathaivānyair mahīpālair
dvijavaiśyādibhis tathā
lokāḥ kāmadughāḥ prāptā
dattvedṛgvidhinā nṛpa
body.translated_text: And likewise by other kings, and by brahmins, vaiśyas, and the rest, the wish-yielding worlds were attained, having given by such a rule, O king

body.text:
tiladhenuṃ pravakṣyāmi
keśavaprīṇanāya yā
dattā bhavati yaś cāsyā
narendra vidhir uttamaḥ
body.translated_text: I shall declare the sesame-cow, which when given is for the gladdening of <s>Keśava</s>, and what, O king, is its supreme rule

body.text:
phalam āpnoti rājendra
tadvad vā vidhivat tadā
body.translated_text: one obtains the fruit, O lord of kings, likewise, when [given] according to rule then

body.text:
yāṃ dattvā brahmahā goghnaḥ
pitṛghno gurutalpagaḥ
āgāradāhī garadaḥ
sarvapāparato 'pi vā
body.translated_text: Having given which, a slayer of a brahmin, a cow-killer, a slayer of his father, a violator of his guru's bed, a house-burner, a poisoner, or even one devoted to all sins,

body.text:
mahāpātakayukto yo
yukto yaś copapātakaiḥ
sa mucyate 'khilaiḥ pāpair
viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati
body.translated_text: he who is joined with the great sins and he who is joined with the minor sins—he is released from all sins [and] goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
svanulipte mahīpṛṣṭe
vastrājinasamāvṛte
dhenuṃ tilamayīṃ kṛtvā
sarvaratnaiḥ samanvitām
body.translated_text: Upon a well-smeared surface of the ground, covered with cloth and antelope-skin, having made a cow consisting of sesame, endowed with all jewels,

body.text:
suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ
gandhaghrāṇavatīṃ śubhām
mṛṣṭānnajihvāṃ kurvīta
guḍāsyāṃ sūtrakambalām
body.translated_text: with golden horns, silver hooves, fragrant of smell, auspicious, one should make her tongue of fine food, her mouth of raw sugar, her [cover] of woolen thread,

body.text:
ikṣupādāṃ tāmrapṛṣṭhāṃ
kuryān muktāphalekṣaṇām
praśastapatraśravaṇāṃ
phaladantavatīṃ śubhām
body.translated_text: one should make her feet of sugar-cane, her back of copper, her eyes of pearls, her ears of excellent leaves, her teeth of fruit, auspicious,

body.text:
sragdāmapucchāṃ kurvīta
navanītastanānvitām
phalair manoharair bhakṣair
maṇimuktāphalānvitām
tiladroṇena kurvīta
āḍhakena tu vatsakam
body.translated_text: one should make her tail of a garland-string, provided with udders of fresh butter, [adorned] with charming fruits and eatables, endowed with gems and pearls; one should make [her] with a <s>droṇa</s>-measure of sesame, and the calf with an <s>āḍhaka</s>

body.text:
śubhavastrayugacchannāṃ
cārucchattrasamanvitām
īdṛksaṃsthānasaṃpannāṃ
kṛtvā śrāddhasamanvitaḥ
kāṃsyopadohanāṃ dadyāt
keśavaḥ prīyatām iti
body.translated_text: covered with a pair of fine cloths, provided with a lovely umbrella, having made [her] complete in such a configuration, [the giver,] accompanied by a <s>śrāddha</s>, should give [her] with a bronze milking-vessel, [saying] "May <s>Keśava</s> be pleased"

body.text:
samyag uccārya vidhinā
dattvaitena narādhipa
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ
pitaraṃ sapitāmaham
body.translated_text: Having rightly addressed [the vipra] by the rule, having given by this [rite], O lord of men, [the giver,] released from all sins, [delivers] his father with [his] grandfather,

body.text:
prapitāmahaṃ tathā pūrvaṃ
puruṣāṇāṃ catuṣṭayam
ātmānaṃ tanayaṃ pautraṃ
tadadhas tu catuṣṭayam
tārayaty avanīpāla
tiladhenuprado naraḥ
body.translated_text: and likewise his great-grandfather, the four former persons [ancestors], and himself, his son, his grandson, and the four below that—the man who gives the sesame-cow delivers [them], O protector of the earth

body.text:
yaś ca gṛhṇāti vidhivat
tasyāpy evaṃvidhān kulān
caturdaśa tathā caiva
dadataś cānumodakāḥ
body.translated_text: And he who duly receives [her]—of him too [are delivered] fourteen such families; and likewise those who, of the giver, rejoice [in approval]

body.text:
dīyamānāṃ prapaśyanti
tiladhenuṃ ca ye narāḥ
te 'py aśeṣāghanirmuktāḥ
prayānti paramāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: And those men who behold the sesame-cow being given—they too, released from all sins, proceed to the supreme goal

body.text:
praśāntāya suśīlāya
tathāmatsariṇe budhaḥ
tiladhenuṃ naro dadyād
vedasnātāya dharmiṇe
body.translated_text: The wise man should give the sesame-cow to one who is tranquil, of good conduct, and free of envy, bathed in the <s>Veda</s>, righteous

body.text:
trirātraṃ yas tilāhāras
tiladhenuṃ prayacchati
dattvaikarātraṃ ca punas
tilān atti nareśvara
body.translated_text: He who, eating sesame for three nights, presents the sesame-cow, and again, having given [her], for one night eats sesame, O lord of men,

body.text:
dātur viśuddhapāpasya
tasya puṇyavato nṛpa
cāndrāyaṇād abhyadhikaṃ
śastaṃ tat tilabhakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: of that giver, of cleansed sin, of that meritorious one, O king, that eating of sesame is commended as superior even to the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>

body.text:
tilābhāve tathā dadyād
ghṛtadhenuṃ yatavrataḥ
kalpayitvā yathānyāyaṃ
tiladhenvā yatavrataḥ
yena bhūpa vidhānena
tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: In the absence of sesame, one of restrained vows should likewise give a ghee-cow, having fashioned [her] in due manner, as [with] the sesame-cow, one of restrained vows; by what rule, O king, [that is done]—hear it here single-minded

body.text:
vāsudevaṃ jagannāthaṃ
puruṣeśam ajaṃ vidhum
sarvapāpanihantāraṃ
ghṛtakṣīrābhiṣecanāt
saṃpūjya pūrvavat puṣpa-
gandhadhūpādibhir naraḥ
body.translated_text: [Having worshipped] <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Lord of the world, the Lord of <s>Puruṣa</s>, the unborn, the moon[-like], the destroyer of all sins, by ablution with ghee and milk, having worshipped [him] as before with flowers, perfumes, incense, and the rest, the man

body.text:
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā
tatparaḥ prayataḥ śuciḥ
parameśam atho nāmnā
abhiṣṭūya ghṛtārciṣā
body.translated_text: having become one who has fasted a day and night, intent on that, restrained, pure, then having lauded the supreme Lord by name with a ghee-flame [lamp],

body.text:
gavyasya sarpiṣaḥ kumbhaṃ
puṣpamālyādibhūṣitam
kāṃsyopadhānasaṃyuktaṃ
sitavastrayugena ca
hiraṇyagarbhasahitaṃ
maṇividrumamuktikaiḥ
body.translated_text: [having made] a pot of cow's ghee, adorned with flowers, garlands, and the rest, joined with a bronze stand, and with a pair of white cloths, together with [a gift of] gold, [adorned] with gems, coral, and pearls,

body.text:
ikṣuyaṣṭimayān pādān
khurān raupyamayāṃs tathā
sauvarṇe cākṣiṇī kuryāc
śṛṅge cāgarukāṣṭhaje
body.translated_text: the feet of sugar-cane stalk, and the hooves of silver, the two eyes one should make of gold, and the horns of aloe-wood,

body.text:
saptadhānyamaye pārśve
pattrorṇāni ca kambalam
kuryāt turuṣkakarpūrau
ghrāṇaṃ phalamayān stanān
body.translated_text: the two sides of the seven grains, and the woolen cover of leaf-wool; one should make the smell of frankincense and camphor, the udders of fruit,

body.text:
maṇiratnasuvarṇānāṃ
samyakkalpanayā kṛtām
body.translated_text: made with a proper fashioning of gems, jewels, and gold,

body.text:
tadvac charkarayā jihvāṃ
guḍakṣīramayaṃ mukham
kṣaumasūtreṇa lāṅgūlaṃ
romāṇi sitasarṣapaiḥ
tāmrapātramayaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ
kuryāc chraddhāsamanvitaḥ
body.translated_text: likewise the tongue of sugar, the mouth made of raw sugar and milk, the tail of linen thread, the hairs of white mustard, the back made of a copper vessel—one should make [her], endowed with faith

body.text:
īdṛksvarūpāṃ saṃkalpya
ghṛtadhenuṃ narādhipa
tadvatkalpanayā dhenvā
ghṛtavatsaṃ prakalpayet
body.translated_text: Having resolved upon a ghee-cow of such a form, O lord of men, with a like fashioning to the cow one should fashion a ghee-calf

body.text:
taṃ ca vipraṃ mahābhāga
manasaiva ghṛtārciṣam
kalpayitvā tatas tasmai
prayataḥ pratipādayet
body.translated_text: And that <s>vipra</s>, O greatly fortunate one, having mentally fashioned [him as] the ghee-flame[-Lord], [the giver,] restrained, should then present [her] to him,

body.text:
etāṃ mamopakārāya
ghṛhṇīṣva tvaṃ dvijottama
prīyatāṃ mama deveśo
ghṛtāṛciḥ puruṣottamaḥ
ity udāhṛtya viprāya
dadyād dhenuṃ narottama
body.translated_text: [saying]: "For my benefit, receive this, O best of the twice-born; may the Lord of gods, the ghee-flame[-Lord] <s>Puruṣottama</s>, be pleased with me"—thus having uttered, one should give the cow to the <s>vipra</s>, O best of men,

body.text:
maṇimuktāsuvarṇānāṃ
samyakkalpanayā kṛtām
body.translated_text: made with a proper fashioning of gems, pearls, and gold

body.text:
dattvaikarātraṃ sthitvā ca
ghṛtāhāro narādhipa
mucyate sarvapāpebhyas
tathā dānaphalaṃ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: Having given [her] and having remained for one night eating ghee, O lord of men, [the giver] is released from all sins; now hear the fruit of the gift

body.text:
ghṛtakṣīravahā nadyo
yatra pāyasakardamāḥ
teṣu lokeṣu lokeśa
sa puṇyeṣūpajāyate
body.translated_text: Rivers flowing ghee and milk, where there are mires of milk-rice—in those holy worlds, O lord of the world, he is born

body.text:
pitur ūrdhvena ye sapta
puruṣāḥ sapta ye 'py adhaḥ
tāṃs teṣu nṛpa lokeṣu
sa nayaty astakalmaṣaḥ
body.translated_text: The seven persons above by [way of] the father, and the seven who are also below—those he leads into those [holy] worlds, O king, his sins cast off

body.text:
sakāmānām iyaṃ vyuṣṭiḥ
kathitā nṛpasattama
viṣṇulokaṃ narā yānti
niṣkāmā ghṛtadhenudāḥ
body.translated_text: This reward of those with desire has been told, O best of kings; men free of desire who give a ghee-cow go to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
ghṛtam agnir ghṛtaṃ somas
tanmayāḥ sarvadevatāḥ
ghṛtaṃ prayacchatā dattā
bhavanty akhiladevatāḥ
body.translated_text: Ghee is fire, ghee is <s>Soma</s>, of ghee consist all the deities; by one who presents ghee, all the deities are [thereby] given [worship]

body.text:
jaladhenuṃ pravakṣyāmi
prīyate dattayā yayā
devadevo hṛṣīkeśaḥ
sarveśaḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ
body.translated_text: I shall declare the water-cow, by the giving of which is pleased the god of gods <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the Lord of all, who fosters all

body.text:
jalakumbhaṃ naravyāghra
suvarṇarajatānvitam
ratnagarbham aśeṣais tu
grāmyair dhānyaiḥ samanvitam
body.translated_text: [Take] a water-pot, O tiger among men, [adorned] with gold and silver, with jewels within, and provided with all the village-grains entire,

body.text:
sitavastrayugacchannaṃ
dūrvāpallavaśobhitam
kuṣṭhaṃ māṃsīm uśīraṃ ca
vālakāmalakair yutam
body.translated_text: covered with a pair of white cloths, beautified with sprouts of <s>dūrvā</s> grass, joined with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, and <s>uśīra</s>, with <s>vālaka</s> and <s>āmalaka</s>,

body.text:
priyaṅgupātrasahitaṃ
sitayajñopavītinam
sacchattraṃ saupānatkaṃ
darbhavistarasaṃsthitam
body.translated_text: together with a vessel of <s>priyaṅgu</s>, [the pot] wearing a white sacred thread, with an umbrella, with sandals, set upon a spread of <s>darbha</s>-grass,

body.text:
caturbhiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ bhūpa
tilapātraiś caturdiśam
sthagitaṃ dadhipātreṇa
ghṛtakṣaudravatā mukhe
body.translated_text: surrounded, O king, on the four sides by four vessels of sesame, covered with a vessel of curds, with ghee and honey at the mouth

body.text:
upoṣitaḥ samabhyarcya
vāsudevaṃ janeśvaram
puṣpadhūpopahārais tu
yathāvibhavam ādṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Having fasted, having worshipped <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Lord of men, with flowers, incense, and offerings, according to his means, reverently,

body.text:
saṃkalpya jaladhenuṃ ca
kumbhaṃ samabhipūjya ca
pūjayed vatsakaṃ tadvat
kṛtaṃ jalamayaṃ budhaḥ
body.translated_text: and having resolved upon a water-cow, and having worshipped the pot, the wise man should likewise worship the calf made of water

body.text:
evaṃ saṃpūjya govindaṃ
jaladhenuṃ savatsakām
sitavastradharaḥ śānto
vītarāgo vimatsaraḥ
body.translated_text: Having thus worshipped <s>Govinda</s> [and] the water-cow with [her] calf, [the giver,] wearing a white cloth, tranquil, free of passion, free of envy,

body.text:
dadyād viprāya rājendra
prītyarthaṃ jalaśāyinaḥ
jalaśāyī jagadyoniḥ
prīyatāṃ mama keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: should give [her] to a <s>vipra</s>, O lord of kings, for the sake of the pleasure of him who reclines on the waters, [saying]: "May he who reclines on the waters, the source of the world, my <s>Keśava</s>, be pleased"

body.text:
iti coccārya bhūnātha
viprāya pratipādyatām
apakvānnāśinā stheyam
ahorātram ataḥparam
body.translated_text: And having so uttered, O lord of the earth, [she] should be presented to a <s>vipra</s>; thereafter one should remain a day and night eating uncooked food

body.text:
anena vidhinā dattvā
jaladhenuṃ janādhipa
sarvāhlādān avāpnoti
ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ
body.translated_text: Having given the water-cow by this rule, O lord of men, [the giver] attains all delights, those which are divine and those which are human

body.text:
śarīrārogyam ābādhā-
praśamaḥ sārvakāmikaḥ
nṛṇāṃ bhavati dattāyāṃ
jaladhenvāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: Bodily health, the appeasement of affliction, the granting of all desires comes to be for men when the water-cow has been given, there is no doubt

body.text:
atrāpi śrūyate bhūpa
pudgalena mahātmanā
jātismareṇa yad gītam
ihābhyetya purā kila
body.translated_text: Here too it is heard, O king, what was sung by the great soul <s>Pudgala</s>, the rememberer of [past] births, having come here of old, indeed

body.text:
sa pudgalaḥ purā vipro
yamalokagato muniḥ
dadarśa yātanā ghorāḥ
pāpakarmakṛtāṃ kila
body.translated_text: That <s>Pudgala</s> was formerly a <s>vipra</s>, a sage gone to the world of <s>Yama</s>; he beheld the terrible torments of the doers of sinful deeds, indeed

body.text:
dīptāgnitīkṣṇaśastrotthāḥ
kvāthatailagatās tathā
uṣṇakṣāranadīpātā
bhairavāḥ puruṣarṣabha
body.translated_text: [torments] arising from blazing fire and sharp weapons, and [bodies] plunged in boiling oil, the falling into rivers of hot lye, dreadful, O bull among men,

body.text:
vraṇāḥ kṣāranipātogrāḥ
kumbhīpākamahābhayāḥ
tā dṛṣṭvā yātanā vipraś
cakāra paramāṃ kṛpām
body.translated_text: wounds fierce with the pouring of lye, with the great terror of the <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> [hell]—having seen those torments, the <s>vipra</s> felt supreme compassion

body.text:
āhlādaṃ te tadā jagmuḥ
pāpās tadanukampitāḥ
taṃ dṛṣṭvā nārakāḥ kecit
kecit tadavalokinaḥ
body.translated_text: Then those sinners, pitied by him, went to delight; seeing him, some of the hell-dwellers, [and] some who looked upon that [compassion of his],—

body.text:
tadā svasthaṃ vilokyaiva
munir nārakamaṇḍalam
dharmarājaṃ sa papraccha
teṣāṃ praśamakāraṇam
body.translated_text: Then, beholding the circle of hell-dwellers become at ease, the sage asked the King of <s>Dharma</s> [Yama] the cause of their appeasement

body.text:
tasmai cācaṣṭa rājendra
tadā vaivasvato yamaḥ
āhlādahetuṃ viprāya
pṛcchate pṛthivīpate
body.translated_text: And to him then <s>Vaivasvata</s> <s>Yama</s> declared, O lord of kings, the cause of the delight, to the <s>vipra</s> who asked, O lord of the earth:

body.text:
tavānubhāvād eteṣāṃ
nārakāṇāṃ dvijottam
saṃpravṛtto 'yam āhlādaḥ
kāraṇaṃ yac chṛṇuṣva tat
body.translated_text: "Through your influence, O best of the twice-born, of these hell-dwellers this delight has arisen; hear that cause"

body.text:
tvayābhyarcya jagannāthaṃ
sarveśaṃ jalaśāyinam
jaladhenuḥ purā dattā
vidhivan munipuṅgava
body.translated_text: "By you, having worshipped the Lord of the world, the Lord of all, who reclines on the waters, a water-cow was formerly given according to rule, O bull among sages"

body.text:
asmāt tu janmano 'tīte
tṛtīye dvija janmani
tasya dānasya te vyuṣṭir
iyam āhlādadāyinī
body.translated_text: "Now, in the third birth past from this birth, O twice-born, of yours, this reward of that gift is the giver of delight"

body.text:
yena tvaṃ tapasā yukto
mānavānām agocaram
saṃprāpto 'si mahāprajña
sarvaśāstraviśārada
body.translated_text: "by which you, joined with austerity, have attained what is beyond the range of [ordinary] men, O greatly wise one, versed in all the <s>śāstras</s>"

body.text:
ye tvāṃ paśyanti śṛṇvanti
ye ca dhyāyanti pāpinaḥ
śṛṇoṣi yāṃs tvaṃ viprendra
yāṃś ca dhyāyasi paśyasi
body.translated_text: "Those sinners who see you, who hear [you], and who meditate [on you]; those whom you, O lord of <s>vipras</s>, hear, and those whom you meditate on [and] see—"

body.text:
nirvṛtiḥ paramā teṣāṃ
sarvāhlādapradāyinī
sadyo bhavati mātra tvaṃ
dvijendra kuru vismayam
body.translated_text: "of them there is supreme felicity, the giver of all delight, at once; so, O lord of the twice-born, you, [yourself], be amazed"

body.text:
āhlādahetujananaṃ
nāsti viprendra tādṛśam
jaladhenur yathā nṝṇāṃ
janmāny ekonasaptatiḥ
body.translated_text: "There is no such producer of the cause of delight to men, O lord of <s>vipras</s>, as the water-cow [is]—[delivering] sixty-nine births"

body.text:
na dāgho na klamo nārtir
na moho vipra jāyate
api janmasahasreṣu
jaladhenupradāyinām
body.translated_text: "No scorching, no weariness, no affliction, no delusion, O <s>vipra</s>, arises even in thousands of births for the givers of the water-cow"

body.text:
ekajanmakṛtaṃ vāñchā
trijanmotthaṃ samāhṛtā
saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ
hanti dattāmbugaur nṛṇām
body.translated_text: "the wish [-fruit] made [of merit] in one birth, [her gift] gathers up [the fruit] arising over three births; the water-cow given destroys the sin committed in seven births, of men"

body.text:
sa tvaṃ gaccha gṛhītvārgham
asmatto dvijasattama
yeṣāṃ samāśrayaḥ kṛṣṇo
na niyamyā hi te mayā
body.translated_text: "So you, go, having taken the oblation from us, O best of the twice-born; for those whose refuge is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are not to be restrained by me"

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ saṃpūjito yais tu
ye kṛṣṇārtham upoṣitāḥ
yaiś ca nityaṃ smṛtaḥ kṛṣṇo
na te madviṣayopagāḥ
body.translated_text: "Those by whom <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has been worshipped, those who have fasted for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sake, and those by whom <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is ever remembered—they do not come within my domain"

body.text:
namaḥ kṛṣṇācyutānanta
vāsudevety udīritam
yair bhāvabhāvitair vipra
na te madviṣayopagāḥ
body.translated_text: "By whom 'Homage, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>' has been uttered with [a mind] suffused with [his] presence, O <s>vipra</s>—they do not come within my domain"

body.text:
dānaṃ dadadbhir yair uktam
acyutaḥ prīyatām iti
śraddhāpuraḥsarair vipra
na te madviṣayopagāḥ
body.translated_text: "By those givers of gifts by whom it is said 'May <s>Acyuta</s> be pleased,' [acting] with faith foremost, O <s>vipra</s>—they do not come within my domain"

body.text:
uttiṣṭhadbhiḥ svapadbhiś ca
vrajadbhiś ca janārdanaḥ
yaiḥ saṃsmṛto dvijaśreṣṭha
na te madviṣayopagāḥ
body.translated_text: "By whom, rising up, sleeping, and walking, <s>Janārdana</s> has been remembered, O best of the twice-born—they do not come within my domain"

body.text:
kṣutaskhalitabhītyādāv
asahadbhiś ca vedanām
kṛṣṇety udīritaṃ yaiś ca
na te madviṣayopagāḥ
body.translated_text: "And by those who, in [moments of] sneezing, stumbling, fear, and the like, not enduring the pain, have uttered 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'—they do not come within my domain"

body.text:
sarvābādhāsu ye kṛṣṇaṃ
smaranty uccārayanti ca
tadbhāvabhāvitā vipra
na te madviṣayopagāḥ
body.translated_text: "Those who, in all afflictions, remember <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and utter [his name], suffused with his presence, O <s>vipra</s>—they do not come within my domain"

body.text:
sa eva dhātā sarvasya
tanniyogakarā vayam
janasaṃyamanodyuktāḥ
so 'smatsaṃyamano hariḥ
body.translated_text: "He alone is the ordainer of all; we are the doers of his command, engaged in the restraint of mankind; he, the restrainer of us, is <s>Hari</s>"

body.text:
itthaṃ niśāmya vacanaṃ
yamasya vadato munim
ūcus te nārakāḥ sarve
vahniśastrāstrabhīravaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, having heard the word of <s>Yama</s> speaking to the sage, all those hell-dwellers, terrified of fire, weapons, and missiles, said:

body.text:
namaḥ kṛṣṇāya haraye
viṣṇave jiṣṇave namaḥ
hṛṣīkeśāya devāya
jagaddhātre 'cyutāya ca
body.translated_text: 'Homage to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Hari</s>; homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to <s>Jiṣṇu</s>; to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the god, the world's creator, and to <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
namaḥ paṅkajanetrāya
namaḥ paṅkajanābhaye
janārdanāya śrīśāya
śrīpate pītavāsase
body.translated_text: Homage to the lotus-eyed one; homage to the lotus-naveled one; to <s>Janārdana</s>, to <s>Śrīśa</s>, to <s>Śrīpati</s>, clad in yellow garments

body.text:
govindāya namo nityaṃ
namaś codadhiśāyine
namaḥ karālavaktrāya
nṛsiṃhāyātinādine
body.translated_text: To <s>Govinda</s> homage ever, and homage to him who sleeps upon the ocean; homage to him of the terrible mouth, to <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> of mighty roar,

body.text:
śārṅgiṇe sitakhaḍgāya
śaṅkhacakragadādhṛte
namo vāmanarūpāya
krāntalokatrayāya ca
body.translated_text: to the <s>Śārṅga</s>-bow-bearer, to him with the bright sword, the bearer of conch, discus, and mace; homage to the form of <s>Vāmana</s>, and to him who strode over the three worlds,

body.text:
varāharūpāya tathā
namo yajñāṅgadhāriṇe
vyāptāśeṣadigantāya
śāntāya paramātmane
body.translated_text: and to the form of <s>Varāha</s>, homage to the bearer of the limbs of sacrifice, to him who pervaded all the ends of the directions, to the tranquil Supreme Self

body.text:
vāsudeva namas tubhyaṃ
namaḥ kaiṭabhasūdana
keśavāya namo vyāpin
namas te 'stu mahīdhara
body.translated_text: O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, homage to you; homage, O slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>; to <s>Keśava</s> homage, O pervader; homage be to you, O upholder of the earth'

body.text:
namo 'stu vāsudevāyety
evam uccārite tataḥ
śastrāṇi kuṇṭhatāṃ jagmur
analaś cāpy aśīśamat
body.translated_text: When 'Homage be to <s>Vāsudeva</s>' was thus uttered, then the weapons came to bluntness, and the fire too grew cool

body.text:
abhajyanta ca yantrāṇi
samutpetur ayomukhāḥ
saṃśuṣkāḥ kṣārasaritaḥ
patitaḥ kūṭaśālmaliḥ
body.translated_text: And the machines [of torture] broke, the iron-beaked [birds] flew up, the rivers of alkali dried up, the <s>Kūṭaśālmali</s> [thorn-tree] fell

body.text:
prakāśatāmasītattvaṃ
narakaś cāgatas tu saḥ
vivān babhañja pavano 'py
asipatravanaṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: The dark essence [of hell] became bright, and that <s>Naraka</s> [hell] was reversed; the blowing wind too broke down the forest of sword-leaves then

body.text:
nirutsāhā jaḍadhiyo
babhūvur yamakiṃkarāḥ
āsan gandhāmbuvāhinyaḥ
pūyaśoṇitanimnagāḥ
body.translated_text: The servants of <s>Yama</s> became spiritless and dull-witted; the rivers that had flowed with pus and blood became carriers of fragrant water

body.text:
vavau sugandhī pavano
manaḥprītikaras tataḥ
veṇuvīṇāsvanayutān
gītaśabdāṃś ca śuśruvuḥ
body.translated_text: A fragrant wind, giving delight to the mind, then blew; and they heard sounds of song joined with the notes of flute and lute

body.text:
taṃ tādṛśam athālakṣya
nṛpa vaivasvato yamaḥ
narakasya viparyāsaṃ
saṃkṣuddhahṛdayas tataḥ
body.translated_text: Then beholding it of such a kind, O king, <s>Vaivasvata</s> <s>Yama</s>, with heart agitated at the overturning of hell,

body.text:
dadarśa nārakān sadyo
divyasraganulepanān
jājvalyamānāṃs tejobhir
amalāmbaravāsasaḥ
body.translated_text: saw at once the hell-dwellers adorned with divine garlands and unguents, blazing with splendour, clad in stainless garments,

body.text:
namo namo 'stu kṛṣṇāya
govindāyāvyayātmane
vāsudevāya devāya
viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave
body.translated_text: [saying] 'Homage, homage be to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Govinda</s>, the imperishable-souled, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the god, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-powerful'

body.text:
ity evaṃ vādinas tatra
prajāsaṃyamano yamaḥ
kṣīṇapāpacayāṃs tāṃs tu
pādyārghyādibhir arcayan
body.translated_text: While they spoke thus there, <s>Yama</s>, the restrainer of creatures, worshipping them, whose heap of sin was now exhausted, with water-for-the-feet, the <s>arghya</s>, and the rest,

body.text:
pūjayitvā ca tān āha
sa kṛṣṇāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
samāhitamanā bhūtvā
dharmarājo nareśvara
body.translated_text: and having worshipped them, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, O lord of men, with folded hands toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, his mind concentrated, said:

body.text:
viṣṇor devātidevasya
jagaddhātuḥ prajāpateḥ
praṇāmaṃ ye 'pi kurvanti
teṣām api namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Those who make obeisance to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god above gods, the world's creator, the <s>Prajāpati</s>—to them too homage and homage

body.text:
sarvasya sarvasaṃsthasya
sarvādhārasya yoginaḥ
ye viṣṇoḥ praṇatās tebhyo
namaḥ sadyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: To those who are bowed to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all, established in all, the support of all, the yogin—to them homage at once, again and again

body.text:
tasya yajñavarāhasya
viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ
praṇāmaṃ ye 'pi kurvanti
teṣām api namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: Those who make obeisance to that sacrifice-boar <s>Viṣṇu</s> of measureless splendour—to them too homage and homage'

body.text:
evaṃ te saṃstutās tena
dharmarājena nārakāḥ
vimānāni samārūḍhā
nṛttagāndharvavanti vai
body.translated_text: Thus praised by him, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, the hell-dwellers, mounted on celestial cars, were possessed indeed of dance and <s>gandharva</s>-music

body.text:
pudgalo 'pi mahābuddhir
dṛṣṭvaitad akhilaṃ nṛpa
jātismaro 'bhavad bhūpa
kaṇvagotre mahāmuniḥ
body.translated_text: And <s>Pudgala</s> too, of great intellect, having seen all this, O king, became a remember-er of [past] births, O king, a great sage in the <s>Kaṇva</s> lineage

body.text:
saṃsmṛtya yamavākyāni
viṣṇor māhātmyam eva ca
jaladhenvāś ca māhātmyaṃ
saṃsmṛtyaitad agāyata
body.translated_text: Having recalled the words of <s>Yama</s> and the greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the greatness of the water-cow [milk-cow gift], having recalled this, he sang:

body.text:
aho duruttarā viṣṇor
māyeyam atigahvarī
yayā mohitacittas taṃ
na vetti parameśvaram
body.translated_text: 'Ah, hard to cross over is this <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, exceedingly deep, by which one whose mind is deluded does not know him, the Supreme Lord

body.text:
jīvo vāñchati kīṭatvaṃ
yūkāmatkuṇayonitaḥ
tasmāc ca śalabhādīnāṃ
yoniṃ tasmāc ca pakṣiṇām
body.translated_text: The living being [first] desires insecthood, from the womb of a louse or a bug; and from that, the womb of locusts and the rest, and from that, of birds

body.text:
tataś ca paśutāṃ prāpya
naratvam abhivāñchati
vimuktihetukī dhanyā
narayoniḥ kṛtātmanām
body.translated_text: and then, having attained beasthood, longs for human existence; the human womb, the cause of liberation, is blessed for those of perfected self

body.text:
na prāpnuvanti saṃsāre
vibhrāntamanaso gatim
jīvā mānuṣyatām anye
janmanām ayutair api
body.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s>, beings of bewildered mind do not attain that destiny; others [do not attain] human existence even through ten thousand births

body.text:
viṣṇumāyāparītās te
prāpyāpi na taranti ye
body.translated_text: those who, encompassed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s>, even having attained [it] do not cross over

body.text:
tad īdṛgdurlabhaṃ prāpya
muktidvāram acetasaḥ
patanti bhūyaḥ saṃsāre
viṣṇumāyāvimohitāḥ
body.translated_text: So, having attained such a hard-to-get door of liberation, the witless ones fall again into <s>saṃsāra</s>, deluded by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s>

body.text:
dustarāpi tu sādhyāsau
māyā kṛṣṇasya mohanī
chidyate yāmanonyaste
mudhaiva hi janārdane
body.translated_text: But that bewildering <s>māyā</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though hard to cross, is yet to be accomplished; it is cut through merely by setting the mind on <s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
asaṃtyajya ca gārhasthyam
ataptvaiva tathā tapaḥ
chindanti vaiṣṇavīṃ māyāṃ
keśavārpitamānasāḥ
body.translated_text: Even without abandoning householder-life, and without performing austerity, they cut through the Vaiṣṇava <s>māyā</s>, their minds offered to <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
avirodhena viṣayām
bhuñjan viṣṇuvyapāśrayaḥ
kṛtvā manas taraty etāṃ
viṣṇor māyāṃ sudustarām
body.translated_text: Enjoying sense-objects without conflict [with dharma], dependent on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having made [up] his mind, one crosses this very hard-to-cross <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
īdṛgbahuphalāṃ bhaktiṃ
sarvadhātari keśave
māyayā tasya devasya
na kurvanti vimohitāḥ
body.translated_text: Such richly-fruitful devotion toward <s>Keśava</s>, the creator of all, the deluded do not perform, through the <s>māyā</s> of that god

body.text:
mudhaivoktaṃ mudhāyātaṃ
mudhā tad vidhiceṣṭitam
mudhaiva janma tan naṣṭaṃ
yatra nārādhito hariḥ
body.translated_text: In vain was [his life] spoken of, in vain did it come, in vain that effort at ritual; in vain indeed is that birth lost, wherein <s>Hari</s> was not worshipped

body.text:
ārādhito hi yaḥ puṃsām
aihikāmuṣmikaṃ phalam
dadāti bhagavān devaḥ
kas taṃ na pratipūjayet
body.translated_text: For the Blessed god, who, when worshipped, gives men the fruit of this world and the next—who would not worship him in return?

body.text:
saṃvatsarās tathā māsā
viphalā divasāś ca te
narāṇāṃ viṣayāndhānāṃ
yeṣu nārādhito hariḥ
body.translated_text: The years, the months, and those days are fruitless of men blinded by sense-objects, wherein <s>Hari</s> is not worshipped

body.text:
yo na vittarddhivibhavair
na vasobhir na bhūṣaṇaiḥ
tuṣyate hṛdayenaiva
kas tam īśaṃ na pūjayet
body.translated_text: He who is gratified not by wealth, abundance, and riches, nor by garments, nor by ornaments, but by the heart alone—who would not worship that Lord?

body.text:
jaladhenvāś ca māhātmyaṃ
niśāmyāpīdṛśaṃ narāḥ
tāṃ na yacchanti ye teṣāṃ
vivekaḥ kutra tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: Hearing too such a greatness of the water-cow [gift], the men who do not give it—where does their discernment stand?

body.text:
karmabhūmau hi mānuṣyaṃ
janmanām ayutair api
svargāpavargaphaladaṃ
kadācit prāpyate naraiḥ
body.translated_text: For in the land of [meritorious] action, human existence, the giver of the fruit of heaven and release, is attained by men but rarely, even through ten thousand births

body.text:
saṃprāpya tan na yair viṣṇus
toṣito nāmbudhenukā
dattā ca samyak te muṣṭā
janmani subahūni bhoḥ
body.translated_text: Having attained that, those by whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> was not gratified, and the water-cow not given—they, rightly, have been robbed in very many births, ho!

body.text:
ūrdhvabāhur viraumy eṣa
dṛṣṭalokadvayo 'smi bhoḥ
ārādhayata govindaṃ
jaladhenuṃ prayacchata
body.translated_text: With arms upraised I cry out, I who have seen the two worlds: ho! worship <s>Govinda</s>, give the water-cow!

body.text:
duḥsaho nārako vahnir
aviṣahyāś ca yātanāḥ
jñānaṃ mamaitad ālambya
kṛṣṇe bhavata susthirāḥ
body.translated_text: The hell-fire is unbearable, and the torments insufferable; relying on this knowledge of mine, be steadfast in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

body.text:
adeśike deśiko 'ham
atra mārge mayoditam
vimṛṣya satyam ity etan
manaḥ kṛṣṇe niveśyatām
body.translated_text: I, a guide on this guideless path, [speak] what is spoken by me; having reflected that this is true, let the mind be set on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

body.text:
prātaḥ kṛṣṇeti deveti
govindeti ca jalpatām
madhyāhne cāparāhne ca
yo 'vasādaḥ sa ucyatām
body.translated_text: At dawn, for those who babble "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>," "O god," and "<s>Govinda</s>," what languor there is at midday and afternoon—let that be spoken [i.e. there is none]

body.text:
anekaviṣayālambi
yac cittaṃ taj janārdane
kurudhvam ālambanavat
saṃsmṛtaḥ puṇyado hi saḥ
body.translated_text: The mind that clings to many sense-objects—make that [cling] to <s>Janārdana</s> as its support; for he, when remembered, is the giver of merit

body.text:
mudhaiva jihvā kṛṣṇeti
keśaveti ca vakṣyati
mudhā ca cittaṃ tadgāmi
yadi syāt kim ato 'dhikam
body.translated_text: In vain will the tongue say "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" and "<s>Keśava</s>," and in vain the mind go to him, if it should be [so]—what is greater than this?

body.text:
mayoktam etad bahuśo
vinaṣṭe tu śarīrake
manuṣyatvaṃ vinā viṣṇur
durlabho vo bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: This has been spoken by me many times: when the little body is destroyed, <s>Viṣṇu</s> will be hard for you to attain without human existence'

body.text:
etāḥ pudgalagāthās te
yamavākyaṃ tavoditam
jaladhenvāś ca māhātmyaṃ
viṣṇusaṃpūjanasya ca
body.translated_text: These are the <s>Pudgala</s>-verses for you, the speech of <s>Yama</s> declared to you, and the greatness of the water-cow and of the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
vratāni sopavāsāni
sarvakāmapradāni te
vratam anyan mahābhāga
sarvakāmapradaṃ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: Those vows with fasts are granters of all desires; another vow, O greatly fortunate one, the granter of all desires—hear it

body.text:
bhaviṣyaṃ cāparaṃ bhūpa
mamaitac chrotum arhasi
yat prakṣyati mahīpālaḥ
parikṣit svapurohitam
body.translated_text: And another future [account], O king, you ought to hear this from me, which King <s>Parikṣit</s> will ask of his own <s>purohita</s>

body.text:
parīkṣitaḥ purodhās tu
dvijo gauramukho nṛpa
bhaviṣyati śamīkasya
śiṣyaḥ paramasaṃmataḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>purohita</s> of <s>Parikṣit</s>, a twice-born named <s>Gauramukha</s>, O king, shall be the highly-esteemed pupil of <s>Śamīka</s>

body.text:
sa ca rājā jagaddhātur
devadevasya śārṅginaḥ
sadaivārādhane yatnaṃ
bhaktiyuktaḥ kariṣyati
body.translated_text: And that king, devoted, will ever make effort in the worship of the world's creator, the god of gods, the <s>Śārṅga</s>-bow-bearer

body.text:
purodhasaṃ gauramukhaṃ
praṇipatya sa pārthivaḥ
prakṣyaty ārādhanārthāya
devadevasya cakriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Prostrating to his <s>purohita</s> <s>Gauramukha</s>, that king will ask, for the sake of the worship of the god of gods, the discus-bearer:

body.text:
bhagavan bhavabhīto 'ham
abhavāya tato bhavān
ārādhayitum icchāmi
sarvecchāpūrakaṃ hariṃ
body.translated_text: 'O blessed one, I am afraid of [worldly] existence; therefore, for [the sake of] non-existence [of rebirth], I wish to worship <s>Hari</s>, the fulfiller of all desires

body.text:
saṃkuruṣva mahābhāga
prasādaṃ mama suvrata
kṛṣṇārādhanakāmasya
manaso deśiko bhava
body.translated_text: Bestow your grace upon me, O greatly fortunate one, O you of good vows; be the guide of my mind, which desires the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

body.text:
ārādhanena yeneśo
jagatām īśvareśvaraḥ
viṣṇur ārādhyate puṃbhiḥ
saṃsārābdhiparikṣataiḥ
body.translated_text: That worship by which the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of lords, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is worshipped by men afflicted by the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>—

body.text:
tan mamopadiśa brahman
prasādapravaṇaṃ manaḥ
kṛtvā sadaivārtimatāṃ
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ guruḥ
body.translated_text: that teach me, O <s>brahman</s>, having made [your] mind inclined to grace; for ever the guru is the refuge, the shelter of the afflicted'

body.text:
evaṃ sa tena bhūpāla
bhūpālena rṣipuṅgavaḥ
keśavārādhanārthāya
samyak pṛṣṭaḥ pravakṣyati
body.translated_text: Thus, O king, well asked by that king, the bull among sages will declare, for the sake of the worship of <s>Keśava</s>:

body.text:
namaskṛtya jagaddhātre
devadevāya śārṅgine
parameśasureśāya
hṛṣīkeśāya vedhase
body.translated_text: Having made obeisance to the world's creator, the god of gods, the <s>Śārṅga</s>-bow-bearer, the Supreme Lord, the lord of the gods, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the creator,

body.text:
varārthinām amoghāya
parasmai harimedhase
sarvakalyāṇabhūtāya
śaṅkhacakragadādhṛte
body.translated_text: unfailing to those who seek boons, the supreme wise <s>Hari</s>, the being of all welfare, the bearer of conch, discus, and mace,

body.text:
varāsicarmāvitate
krūraśāntātmamūrtaye
yadyadbhūtopakārāya
tattadrūpavikāriṇe
body.translated_text: [him] outstretched with excellent sword and shield, of form whose self is [both] cruel and tranquil, who transforms into this and that form for the benefit of this and that being,

body.text:
paramāṇvantaparyanta-
sahasrāṃśāṇumūrtaye
jaṭharāntāyutāśānta-
sthitabrahmāṇḍadhāriṇe
body.translated_text: of a form [as small as] an atom, a thousandth fraction down to the very limit of the smallest atom, who bears within his belly the cosmic egg established with countless un-tranquil [worlds],

body.text:
śvetādidīrghahrasvādi-
kaṭhinādivikalpanā
yogicintye jagaddhāmni
yatra nāsty akhilātmani
body.translated_text: in the world's abode, conceivable [only] by yogins, wherein there is no distinction of white and the rest, long and short and the rest, hard and the rest, the Self of all—

body.text:
tam ajaṃ śāśvataṃ nityaṃ
pariṇāmavivarjitam
yogibhiś cintyate mūrtir
yatra tatrākhilātmani
body.translated_text: him, the unborn, eternal, perpetual, devoid of change, whose form is contemplated by yogins here and there, the Self of all,

body.text:
tatra tatrātmano nityaṃ
pariṇāmavivarjitam
praṇamya jagatām īśam
anantaṃ parataḥ param
body.translated_text: there and there [the Self] of the [individual] self, ever devoid of change—having bowed to the Lord of the worlds, the endless, higher than the highest,

body.text:
paraṃ parāṇāṃ sraṣṭāraṃ
purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ prabhum
varaṃ vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ
sthūlasūkṣmasvarūpiṇam
body.translated_text: the supreme of the supreme, the creator, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Lord, the boon, the choicest, the boon-giver, of gross and subtle form,

body.text:
aśeṣajagatāṃ mūlam
anādinidhanasthitim
parāparasvarūpastham
avikārasvarūpiṇam
body.translated_text: the root of all the worlds, the abiding-state without beginning or end, established in the form of the higher and the lower, of changeless form,

body.text:
yasyopacārataḥ svargaṃ
svarūpaṃ vyatiricyate
jñānajñeyasya munibhir
jñānavidbhir mahātmabhiḥ
body.translated_text: from whose [mere] attendant-attribute heaven [arises], whose own form is set apart [as transcendent], [the form] of him who is the knowledge and the knowable, by sages, by the knowers of knowledge, by the great-souled—

body.text:
tasmai pārthivamukhyāya
raghuvaryamahātmane
śrūyatāṃ sa muniśreṣṭho
yad vakṣyati parīkṣite
body.translated_text: to that chief of kings, the great-souled best of the <s>Raghus</s>—let it be heard, what that best of sages will declare to <s>Parikṣit</s>:

body.text:
devakī nāma rājendra
devakasyābhavat sutā
anapatyā tapas tepe
putrārthaṃ kila bhāminī
body.translated_text: '<s>Devakī</s> by name, O lord of kings, was the daughter of <s>Devaka</s>; childless, she performed austerity for the sake of a son, indeed, the lovely one,

body.text:
bhāryā sā vasudevasya
satyadharmaparāyaṇā
na cātuṣyata govindas
tatas tām āha bhārgavaḥ
body.translated_text: she, the wife of <s>Vasudeva</s>, devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s>; and <s>Govinda</s> was not [yet] pleased; then the <s>Bhārgava</s> said to her:

body.text:
kimarthaṃ tapyate bhadre
tapaḥ paramaduścaram
ko 'rthas tavābhilaṣito
gantuṃ kutra tavepsitam
body.translated_text: "For what purpose do you perform, O blessed one, this most-difficult austerity? What is the object desired by you, [or] where is your wished-for [place] to go?"

body.text:
aputrāhaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha
patyur me nāsti saṃtatiḥ
sāham ārādhya govindaṃ
putram icchāmi śobhanam
body.translated_text: "I am sonless, O best of the twice-born; my husband has no progeny; so I, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, desire a beautiful son

body.text:
tapas tāvat kariṣyāmi
parameṇa samādhinā
yāvad ārādhito viṣṇur
dāsyaty abhimataṃ mama
body.translated_text: I shall perform austerity, with supreme concentration, until <s>Viṣṇu</s>, worshipped, will grant my desire"

body.text:
govindārādhane yatno
yadi te kulanandini
tad idaṃ vratam āsthāya
toṣayāśu janārdanam
body.translated_text: "If [there is] effort in you in the worship of <s>Govinda</s>, O delight of your family, then, resorting to this vow, gratify <s>Janārdana</s> quickly:

body.text:
prathame kārttikasyāhni
saṃprāpte devakātmaje
pañcagavyajalasnātaḥ
pañcagavyakṛtāśanaḥ
body.translated_text: On the first day of <s>Kārttika</s> arrived, O daughter of <s>Devaka</s>, bathed in the water of the <s>pañcagavya</s>, eating the <s>pañcagavya</s>,

body.text:
bāṇapuṣpaiḥ samabhyarcya
vāsudevam ajaṃ vibhum
dattvā ca candanaṃ dhūpaṃ
paramānnaṃ nivedayet
ghṛtena vācayed vipraṃ
gṛhṇīyāc ca tato vratam
body.translated_text: having worshipped <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the unborn pervading Lord, with <s>bāṇa</s>-flowers, and having offered sandal and incense, she should present the supreme food [pāyasa]; she should have a <s>vipra</s> recite [the formula] with ghee, and then take up the vow:

body.text:
adyaprabhṛty ahaṃ māsaṃ
virataḥ prāṇināṃ vadhāt
asatyavacanāt stainyān
madhumāṃsādibhakṣaṇāt
body.translated_text: 'From today onward, for a month I am abstained from the slaying of living beings, from untrue speech, from theft, from the eating of honey, meat, and the rest;

body.text:
svapan vibudhyan gacchaṃś ca
smariṣyāmy aham acyutam
parāpavādapaiśūnyaṃ
parapīḍākaraṃ tathā
body.translated_text: sleeping, waking, and walking, I shall remember <s>Acyuta</s>; censure of others and slander, and what causes harm to others,

body.text:
sacchāstradevatāyajvi-
nindām anyasya vā bhuvi
na vakṣyāmi jagaty asmin
paśyan sarvagata harim
body.translated_text: and the reviling of holy <s>śāstras</s>, deities, and sacrificers, or of another, upon the earth—I shall not speak in this world, beholding the all-pervading <s>Hari</s>'

body.text:
ity anyac cāpi śaknoti
yan nirvoḍhuṃ yaśasvini
kurvīta niyamaṃ tasya
tyāgo dharmāya yasya ca
body.translated_text: And whatever else of this kind she is able to carry out, O glorious one, let her make the restraint of it, whose abandonment is for [the sake of] <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
kṛtvaivaṃ purato viṣṇor
nivṛttiṃ pāpataḥ śubhe
naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyān
maunī nityam udaṅmukhaḥ
body.translated_text: Having thus made, before <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the cessation from sin, O auspicious one, she should herself eat the food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>), silent, ever facing north

body.text:
mārgaśīrṣe tathā māsi
jātipuṣpair janārdanam
samabhyarcya śubhe dhūpaṃ
candanaṃ saṃnivedya ca
body.translated_text: And likewise in the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, having worshipped <s>Janārdana</s> with <s>jāti</s>-flowers, O auspicious one, and having presented incense and sandal,

body.text:
paramānnaṃ ca devāya
viprāya ca punar ghṛtam
dattvā tathaiva gṛhṇīyān
niyamaṃ cāsya rocate
body.translated_text: and the supreme food to the god and again ghee to the <s>vipra</s>, having given [these], she should likewise take up the restraint, and as pleases her

body.text:
tathaiva naktaṃ bhuñjīta
naivedyaṃ kulanandini
sarveṣv eva tu māseṣu
pañcagavyādikaṃ samam
body.translated_text: And likewise she should eat the food-offering at night, O delight of the family; and in all the months the <s>pañcagavya</s> and the rest is the same

body.text:
puṣpadhūpopahāreṣu
viśeṣo dakṣiṇāsu ca
snānaprāśanayoḥ sāmyaṃ
tathā vai naktabhojane
body.translated_text: In the flowers, incenses, and offerings there is a difference, and in the fees; in the bathing and consuming there is sameness, and likewise in the night-eating

body.text:
arcayet pratimāsaṃ ca
yaiḥ puṣpais tāni me śṛṇu
ye ca dhūpāḥ pradātavyā
naivedyānnaṃ ca yad yadā
body.translated_text: And she should worship [him] each month; with which flowers [she should worship], hear those from me, and which incenses are to be given, and the food-offering, what and when:

body.text:
bāṇasya jātikusumais
tathaiva ca kuruṇṭhakaiḥ
kundātimuktakai rakta-
karavīraiś ca devaki
body.translated_text: with the <s>jāti</s>-blossoms of the <s>bāṇa</s>, and likewise with <s>kuruṇṭhaka</s> flowers, with <s>kunda</s> and <s>atimuktaka</s>, and with red oleander, O <s>Devakī</s>,

body.text:
śvetais tato mālikayā
tathā mallikayā tataḥ
dadhipiṇḍyātha ketakyā
padmaraktotpalena ca
krameṇābhyarcito viṣṇur
dadāti manasepsitam
body.translated_text: then with white [flowers], with the <s>mālikā</s>, then with the <s>mallikā</s>, with the <s>dadhipiṇḍī</s>, then with the <s>ketakī</s>, and with the lotus and the red water-lily—worshipped in [this] sequence, <s>Viṣṇu</s> grants the heart's desire

body.text:
kārttike mārgaśīrṣe ca
dhūpaḥ pauṣe ca candanam
māghaphālgunacaitreṣu
dadyād viṣṇos tathāgarum
body.translated_text: In <s>Kārttika</s> and <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, incense; and in <s>Pauṣa</s>, sandal; in <s>Māgha</s>, <s>Phālguna</s>, and <s>Caitra</s>, she should likewise give <s>aguru</s> [aloe-wood] to <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

body.text:
vaiśākhādiṣu māseṣu
triṣu devaki bhaktitaḥ
karpūraṃ devadevāya
guggulaṃ śrāvaṇādiṣu
body.translated_text: in the three months beginning with <s>Vaiśākha</s>, O <s>Devakī</s>, with devotion, camphor to the god of gods; <s>guggulu</s> [bdellium] in [the three] beginning with <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>

body.text:
kārttikādiṣu māseṣu
paramānnaṃ śubhe triṣu
kāsāraṃ māghapūrveṣu
yavānnaṃ ca tatas triṣu
body.translated_text: In the three auspicious months beginning with <s>Kārttika</s>, [one should give] rice cooked with milk (<s>paramānna</s>); in those beginning with <s>Māgha</s>, gruel; and then in the [next] three, food of barley.

body.text:
ghṛtaṃ tilāñ jalaghaṭān
hiraṇyam athavājinam
pratimāsaṃ tathā dadyād
brāhmaṇāya śubhavrate
body.translated_text: Ghee, sesame, water-jars, gold, or a deerskin one should likewise give each month to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, O you of auspicious vows.

body.text:
yathoktaṃ niyamānāṃ ca
grahaṇaṃ pratimāsikam
kurvañ jagatpatir viṣṇuḥ
prīyatām iti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: Performing the monthly undertaking of the observances as enjoined, [the man should think] 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of the world, be pleased.'

body.text:
yoṣid apy amalaprajñe
vratam etad yathāvidhi
karoti yā sā sakalān
avāpnoti manorathān
body.translated_text: Even a woman, O you of stainless wisdom, who performs this vow according to rule—she attains all her heart's desires.

body.text:
vratenārādhito viṣṇur
anena jagataḥ patiḥ
dadāty abhimatān kāmān
alpakālena bhāmini
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of the world, worshipped by this vow, gives the desired objects of wish in a short time, O lovely one.

body.text:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ
saubhāgyārogyadaṃ tathā
vratam etat priyatamaṃ
vratebhyo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ
body.translated_text: This vow of the one of unmanifest birth [Viṣṇu] is wealth-giving, fame-giving, life-giving, and the giver of good fortune and health—the dearest of vows.

body.text:
vratenānena śuddhānām
abdenaikena keśavaḥ
sukhadṛśyo na saṃdeho
dīpenaivāgrataḥ sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: By this vow, for those purified, in a single year <s>Keśava</s> is happily visible—there is no doubt—standing right before [them] like a lamp.

body.text:
kāyavāṅmanaso śuddhiṃ
karoty etan mahāvratam
śuddhānāṃ cāmalo devo
dṛśya eva janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: This great vow makes the purification of body, speech, and mind; and to the purified, the stainless god <s>Janārdana</s> is indeed visible.

body.text:
tasminn ekāgracittānāṃ
prāṇināṃ varavarṇini
viprā eva prayatnena
muktibhājo vibhūtayaḥ
body.translated_text: For living beings of one-pointed mind upon him, O excellent-complexioned one, [it is] the <s>vipras</s> alone, by effort, [who become] partakers of release and of [divine] powers.

body.text:
yathā kalpataruṃ prāpya
yad yad icchati cetasā
tat tat phalam avāpnoti
tathā saṃprāpya taṃ vibhum
body.translated_text: As, having reached a wish-fulfilling tree, whatever one desires in mind, that fruit one obtains—so, having reached that all-pervading one.

body.text:
śuddhivratam idaṃ tasmān
mahāpātakanāśanam
ārādhanāya kṛṣṇasya
kuru devaki pāvanam
body.translated_text: Therefore this purification-vow, the destroyer of great sins, perform, O <s>Devakī</s>, the purifying one, for the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
tasmiṃś cīrṇe hṛṣīkeśas
tubhyaṃ dāsyati darśanam
dṛṣṭe cābhimataṃ yat te
tad aśeṣaṃ bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: When it is performed, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> will grant you his sight; and when he is seen, whatever is desired by you, all of it will come to be.

body.text:
devakī bhārgavasyaitac
śrutvā vākyaṃ narādhipa
śuddhikāmā cacārātha
sarvakāmapradaṃ vratam
body.translated_text: <s>Devakī</s>, O king, having heard this speech of <s>Bhārgava</s>, desiring purification, then practiced the vow that grants all desires.

body.text:
vratenārādhitas tena
tadā devyā janārdanaḥ
dadau darśanam īśeśaḥ
śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ
body.translated_text: Worshipped by that vow, then, by the goddess, <s>Janārdana</s>, the Lord of lords, the bearer of conch, discus, and mace, gave [her] his sight.

body.text:
dṛṣṭe tasminn aśeṣeśe
jagaddhātari keśave
kṛtvā praṇāmam āhedaṃ
bhaktinamrātha devakī
body.translated_text: When that <s>Keśava</s>, the lord of all, the upholder of the world, was seen, <s>Devakī</s>, bowed with devotion, having made obeisance, said this:

body.text:
jagatām īśvareśeśa
jñāna jñeya bhavāvyaya
samastadevatādeva
vāsudeva namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: "O Lord of lords of the worlds, O knowledge, O object of knowledge, O imperishable existence, O god of all deities, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, homage be to you.

body.text:
pradhānapuṃsor ajayor
yaḥ kāraṇam akāraṇam
aviśeṣyam ajaṃ rūpaṃ
tava tasmai namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: He who is the causeless cause of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit), the two unborn—to that form of yours, undifferentiated and unborn, homage be to you.

body.text:
tvaṃ pradhānaṃ pumāṃś caiva
kāraṇākāraṇātmakaḥ
sad asac cākhilaṃ deva
kenoktena tava stavaḥ
body.translated_text: You are <s>Pradhāna</s> and also the <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the nature of cause and non-cause; the whole, existent and non-existent, O god—by what utterance [can there be] your praise?

body.text:
prasīda deva devānām
ariśātana vāmana
lobhābhibhūtā yad ahaṃ
varayāmi prayaccha tat
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O god of gods, O slayer of foes, O dwarf; what I, overcome by greed, beg for, grant that."

body.text:
aditis tvaṃ mahābhāge
bhuvaṃ prāptā surāraṇi
bhartā ca te kaśyapo 'yaṃ
deyas tava varo mayā
body.translated_text: "You are <s>Aditi</s>, O greatly fortunate one, come to the earth, O mother of the gods; and your husband is this <s>Kaśyapa</s>; a boon is to be given to you by me.

body.text:
aputrāsmi na me bhartur
asti keśava saṃtatiḥ
prasīda dehi me putram
aridurdhārapauruṣam
body.translated_text: "I am sonless; for my husband there is no offspring, O <s>Keśava</s>; be gracious, give me a son of manhood unbearable to foes."

body.text:
bhaviṣyaty acirād devi
madaṃśena sutas tava
hantavyā dānavās tena
saddharmaparipanthinaḥ
body.translated_text: "There will be ere long, O goddess, a son of yours by a portion of myself; by him are to be slain the <s>dānavas</s>, the adversaries of true <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
tvām ahaṃ jagaddhātāram
udāroruparākramam
dhārayiṣyāmi garbheṇa
katham acyuta śaṃsa me
body.translated_text: "You, the upholder of the world, of noble and great prowess—how shall I bear [you] with [my] womb, O <s>Acyuta</s>? Tell me.

body.text:
tavodare 'vatāraṃ vai
purāpi balibandhane
kurvatā vidhṛtāḥ sapta
lokās tvaṃ cātmamāyayā
body.translated_text: "Making your descent into your womb, formerly too at the binding of <s>Bali</s>, the seven worlds were upheld by you by your own <s>māyā</s>;

body.text:
tathā sāṃpratam apy etāṃl
lokān sasthāṇujaṅgamān
dhārayiṣyāmy athātmānaṃ
tvāṃ ca devaki līlayā
body.translated_text: so now too I shall bear these worlds with their stationary and moving [beings], and myself, and you, O <s>Devakī</s>, in sport."

body.text:
ity evam uktvā tāṃ devīṃ
devakīṃ bhagavān prabhuḥ
tirobabhūva govindo
bhūrbhuvaḥprabhavo vibhuḥ
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus to that goddess <s>Devakī</s>, the Blessed Lord <s>Govinda</s>, the all-pervading source of earth and sky, vanished.

body.text: avāpa ca tato garbhaṃ
body.translated_text: And then she conceived the embryo,

body.text: devakī vasudevataḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Devakī</s>, from <s>Vasudeva</s>.

body.text:
ajāyata ca viśveśaḥ
svenāṅgena janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: And the Lord of the universe, <s>Janārdana</s>, was born by his own [self], in [his own] body—

body.text:
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaṃ
tāmrāyatavilocanam
caturbāhum udārāṅgaṃ
śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam
body.translated_text: dark as the petal of a blue lotus, with long copper-red eyes, four-armed, of noble limbs, his breast marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.

body.text:
taṃ jātaṃ devakī devaṃ
nidhānaṃ sarvatejasām
praṇipatyābhituṣṭāva
saṃprastutapayodharā
body.translated_text: Him, the god born, the repository of all splendors, <s>Devakī</s>, having bowed, praised, her breasts flowing [with milk]:

body.text:
abālo bālarūpeṇa
yeneśa tvam ihāsthitaḥ
tvadrūpaṃ praṇipatyāhaṃ
yad bravīmi nibodha tat
body.translated_text: "Not a child, [yet] in the form of a child, by which, O Lord, you stand here—having bowed to your form, what I say, listen to that.

body.text:
namas te sarvabhūteśa
namas te madhusūdana
namas te puṇḍarīkākṣa
namas te 'stu janārdana
body.translated_text: "Homage to you, O Lord of all beings; homage to you, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>; homage to you, O lotus-eyed; homage be to you, O <s>Janārdana</s>.

body.text:
namas te śārṅgacakrāsi-
gadāparighapāṇaye
upendrāyāprameyāya
hṛṣīkeśāya vai namaḥ
body.translated_text: "Homage to you, in whose hand are the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, discus, sword, mace, and iron club; to <s>Upendra</s>, the immeasurable, to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> indeed, homage.

body.text:
namo 'stu te 'ṇurūpāya
bṛhadrūpāya vai namaḥ
aśeṣabhūtarūpāya
tathārūpāya te namaḥ
body.translated_text: "Homage be to you of atomic form; homage indeed to [you of] vast form; to [you] of the form of all beings, and to your formless [self], homage.

body.text:
anirdeśyaviśeṣāya
tubhyaṃ sarvātmane namaḥ
sarveśvarāya sarvāya
sarvabhūtāya te namaḥ
body.translated_text: "To the one of indefinable distinction, to you, the Self of all, homage; to the Lord of all, to the all, to [you] who are all beings, homage to you.

body.text:
namo 'stu te vāsudeva
namo 'stu kamalekṣaṇa
body.translated_text: "Homage be to you, <s>Vāsudeva</s>; homage be [to you], O lotus-eyed.

body.text:
aśeṣabhūtarūpāya
tathābhūtāya te namaḥ
namo 'stu te 'śvarūpāya
tathārūpāya te namaḥ
anirdeśyaviśeṣāya
tubhyaṃ sarvātmane namaḥ
namo 'stu te vāsudeva
namas te puṣkarekṣaṇa
body.translated_text: "To [you] of the form of all beings, and to [you] who have so become, homage to you; homage be to you of horse-form [Hayagrīva], and to your [other] forms, homage to you; to the one of indefinable distinction, to you, the Self of all, homage; homage be to you, <s>Vāsudeva</s>; homage to you, O lotus-eyed.

body.text:
namo 'stu te sadācintya
yogicintya jagatpate
body.translated_text: "Homage be to you, O ever-inconceivable, O contemplated by yogins, O Lord of the world.

body.text:
viṣṇo namo 'stu te kṛṣṇa
namas te puruṣottama
namo nārāyaṇa hare
namas te 'stu sadācyuta
body.translated_text: "<s>Viṣṇu</s>, homage be to you, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; homage to you, <s>Puruṣottama</s>; homage, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>; homage be to you, ever-<s>Acyuta</s>.

body.text:
namo namas te govinda
namas te garuḍadhvaja
śrīśa śrīvatsa yogīśa
śrīkānteśa namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: "Homage, homage to you, <s>Govinda</s>; homage to you, whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s>; O lord of <s>Śrī</s>, O <s>Śrīvatsa</s>-bearer, O lord of yogins, O lord beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, homage be to you.

body.text:
nīlotpaladalaśyāma
daṃṣṭroddhṛtavasuṃdhara
hiraṇyākṣaripo deva
namas te yajñasūkara
body.translated_text: "O dark as a blue-lotus petal, O you who lifted up the earth with your tusk, O foe of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, O god, homage to you, O sacrificial Boar.

body.text:
nṛsiṃha jaya viśvātman
daityoraḥsthaladāraka
namo namas te 'stu sadā
vikṣepadhvastatāraka
body.translated_text: "O <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, victory [to you], O Soul of the universe, O render of the breast of the <s>Daitya</s>; homage, homage be to you ever, O destroyer of the [demon] star by [your] hurling.

body.text:
māyāvāmanarūpāya
tubhyaṃ deva namo namaḥ
trivikrama namas tubhyaṃ
trailokyakrānti durjaya
body.translated_text: "To the form of the dwarf [made] by <s>māyā</s>, to you, O god, homage, homage; <s>Trivikrama</s>, homage to you, O unconquerable strider over the three worlds.

body.text:
ṛgyajuḥsāmabhūtāya
vedāharaṇakarmaṇe
praṇavodgītavacase
mahāśvaśirase namaḥ
body.translated_text: "To [you] who became the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, to the deed of recovering the <s>Vedas</s>, to [you] whose utterance is the <s>Praṇava</s> and the <s>Udgītha</s>, to the great Horse-head [Hayagrīva], homage.

body.text:
niḥkṣatriyorvīkaraṇa
vikarālaparākrama
jāmadagnya namas tubhyaṃ
kārtavīryāsutaskara
body.translated_text: "O you who made the earth free of <s>kṣatriyas</s>, of exceedingly terrible prowess, O son of <s>Jamadagni</s> [Paraśurāma], homage to you, O destroyer of the son of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>.

body.text:
paulastyakulanāśāya
sādhumārgavicāriṇe
nalasetukṛte tubhyaṃ
namo rāghavarūpiṇe
body.translated_text: "To you, the destroyer of the lineage of <s>Pulastya</s> [Rāvaṇa], traversing the path of the good, the builder of <s>Nala</s>'s bridge, homage, in the form of the <s>Rāghava</s>.

body.text:
sāṃprataṃ matprasannāya
saṃbhūtāya mamodare
svamāyābālarūpāya
namaḥ kṛṣṇāya vai hare
body.translated_text: "And now, gracious to me, come to be in my womb, in the child-form of your own <s>māyā</s>—homage to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, indeed, O <s>Hari</s>.

body.text:
yāvanti tava rūpāṇi
yāvatyaś ca vibhūtayaḥ
namāmi kṛṣṇa sarvebhyas
tebhyas tābhyaś ca sarvadā
body.translated_text: "As many as are your forms, and as many as your powers—I bow, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to all those [forms] and all those [powers], always.

body.text:
svarūpaceṣṭitaṃ yat te
yad devatve viceṣṭitam
yac ca tiryaṅmanuṣyatve
ceṣṭitaṃ tan namāmy aham
body.translated_text: "Whatever is your action in your own [supreme] form, and what is enacted in godhood, and what is enacted in the animal and human states—to that I bow.

body.text:
parameśa pareśeśa
tiryagīśa nareśvara
sarveśvareśvareśeśa
namas te puruṣottama
body.translated_text: "O supreme Lord, O Lord of the lords beyond, O Lord of the animals, O Lord of men, O Lord of the lords of the lords of all lords, homage to you, <s>Puruṣottama</s>."

body.text:
evaṃ stutas tayā devyā
devakyā madhusūdanaḥ
bālarūpī jagādaivaṃ
vasudevasya śṛṇvataḥ
body.translated_text: Thus praised by that goddess <s>Devakī</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, in child-form, spoke thus, while <s>Vasudeva</s> listened:

body.text:
samyag ārādhitenoktaṃ
yat prasannena vai śubhe
tat kṛtaṃ sakalaṃ bhūyo
yad vṛṇoṣi dadāmi tat
body.translated_text: "What was said by me, well-worshipped and gladdened, O auspicious one—all that is done; further, what you beg, that I give.

body.text:
avatāre tathaivāsmin
varṣāṇām adhikaṃ śatam
sthāsyāmi naratāṃ prāpto
duṣṭadaityanibarhaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: "And in this descent too I shall abide more than a hundred years, having attained humanity, the slayer of wicked <s>daityas</s>.

body.text:
tat tvaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te
varaṃ yan manasecchasi
dāsyāmy aham asaṃdigdhaṃ
yady api syāt sudurlabham
body.translated_text: "So you—blessings on you—beg the boon which you wish in mind; I shall give it, undoubtedly, even if it be very hard to obtain."

body.text:
yadi deva prasannas tvaṃ
pradadāsi mamepsitam
vṛṇomi tad ahaṃ nityaṃ
tava keśava darśanam
body.translated_text: "If, O god, you are pleased and grant me what is desired, I beg this: ever your sight, O <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
tavedṛgrūpam ālokya
hārdaprasrutalocanā
nālaṃ viyogaṃ saṃsoḍhuṃ
tavāhaṃ madhusūdana
body.translated_text: "Beholding such a form of yours, my eyes streaming from the heart's [love], I am not able to bear separation from you, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>."

body.text:
dākṣāyaṇī tvam aditiḥ
saṃbhūtā vasudhātale
nityam eva jagaddhātri
prasādaṃ te karomy aham
body.translated_text: "You, O <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, are <s>Aditi</s>, come to be on the surface of the earth; ever, O upholder of the world, I do you a favor.

body.text:
ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe tadā pakṣe
dine 'sminn eva bhāmini
tvaṃ māṃ drakṣyasy asaṃdigdhaṃ
prasādas te kṛto mayā
body.translated_text: "Then on each sixth fortnight, on this very day, O lovely one, you shall see me undoubtedly; a favor is done to you by me.

body.text:
anenaiva mahābhāge
bālarūpeṇa saṃvṛtaḥ
tava darśanam eṣyāmi
yatra te snehavan manaḥ
body.translated_text: "By this very child-form, O greatly fortunate one, covered, I shall come to your sight, where your mind is filled with affection.

body.text:
tasmin kāle ca lokās tvāṃ
pūjayiṣyanti devaki
māṃ ca puṣpādibhir devi
tavotsaṅgavyavasthitam
body.translated_text: "And at that time the worlds will worship you, O <s>Devakī</s>, and me with flowers and the rest, O goddess, [me] situated in your lap.

body.text:
saṃpūjito 'haṃ lokānāṃ
tasmin kāle sutoṣitaḥ
pradāsyāmi jagaddhātri
yathābhilaṣitaṃ varam
body.translated_text: "Worshipped at that time by the worlds, well gladdened, I shall grant, O upholder of the world, the boon as desired.

body.text:
aputrāṇāṃ varān putrān
adhanānāṃ tathā dhanam
śubhān dārān adārāṇāṃ
sarogāṇām arogatām
body.translated_text: "Excellent sons to the sonless, and likewise wealth to the wealthless, good wives to the wifeless, health to the diseased,

body.text:
sugatiṃ gatikāmānāṃ
vidyāṃ vidyārthinām api
pradāsyasi mahābhāge
matprasādopavṛṃhitā
body.translated_text: "a good destination to those desiring [good] destinations, learning too to the seekers of learning, you shall grant, O greatly fortunate one, augmented by my grace.

body.text:
prasāditā hi martyānāṃ
yat tvaṃ dāsyasi śobhane
tat teṣāṃ matprasādena
bhaviṣyati na durlabham
body.translated_text: "For whatever, propitiated, you shall give to mortals, O beautiful one, that, by my grace, will become not hard to obtain for them.

body.text:
tvām abhyarcyopacāreṇa
snāpayitvā ghṛtena mām
sarvakāmān avāpsyanti
kāle ṣaṭpakṣasaṃjñite
body.translated_text: "Having worshipped you with [due] service, and having bathed me with ghee, they will attain all desires at the time named the sixth-fortnight.

body.text:
tvadaṅkasthaṃ ca māṃ bālaṃ
saṃsmariṣyanti bhaktitaḥ
body.translated_text: "And they will remember me, the child situated in your lap, with devotion.

body.text:
pratimāsaṃ ca te pūjām
aṣṭamyāṃ yaḥ kariṣyati
mama caivākhilān kāmān
saṃprāpnoty apakalmaṣaḥ
body.translated_text: "And he who each month performs your worship on the eighth, and mine, attains all [his] desires, freed of sin."

body.text:
evaṃ pūrvaṃ hṛṣīkeśo
devakyāḥ pradadau varam
tasmāt kṛṣṇāṣṭamī puṃsām
aśeṣāghaughahāriṇī
body.translated_text: Thus formerly <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> granted the boon to <s>Devakī</s>; therefore the eighth of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī] is the remover of the whole flood of men's sins.

body.text:
tasyāṃ hi pūjitaḥ kṛṣṇo
devakī ca samādhinā
pāpāpanodaṃ kurute
dadāti ca manorathān
body.translated_text: For on it <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worshipped, and <s>Devakī</s>, with concentration, make the removal of sin and grant the heart's desires.

body.text:
tad eṣa puṣṭikāmānāṃ
nṝṇāṃ puṇyārthinām api
upavāso mahīpāla
śastaḥ keśavatoṣadaḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore this fast, O king, is commended for men desiring nourishment and also desiring merit, the granter of the contentment of <s>Keśava</s>.

body.text:
śrāvaṇe śuklapakṣe tu
dvādaśyāṃ prīyate nṛpa
gopradānena govindo
yat pūrvaṃ kathitaṃ tava
body.translated_text: But in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, in the bright fortnight, on the twelfth, O king, <s>Govinda</s> is pleased by the gift of a cow, as was formerly told to you.

body.text:
pauṣaśukle tu tadvac ca
dvādaśyāṃ ghṛtadhenukām
ghṛtārciḥ prīṇanāyālaṃ
pradadyāt phaladāyinīm
body.translated_text: And likewise, in the bright [fortnight] of <s>Pauṣa</s>, on the twelfth, one should give a ghee-cow whose flame is ghee, fit for [his] gladdening, fruit-giving.

body.text:
tathaiva māghadvādaśyāṃ
pradattā tilagaur nṛpa
keśavaṃ prīṇayaty āśu
sarvakāmān prayacchati
body.translated_text: Likewise, on the twelfth of <s>Māgha</s>, O king, a sesame-cow given gladdens <s>Keśava</s> at once and grants all desires.

body.text:
jyaiṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe
dvādaśyāṃ jaladhenukā
dattā yathāvad vidhinā
prīṇayaty ambuśāyinam
body.translated_text: In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, in the bright fortnight, on the twelfth, a water-cow given duly according to rule gladdens the one who lies on the waters [Viṣṇu].

body.text:
lavaṇaṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu
kṛṣṇam abhyarcya yo naraḥ
prayacchati dvijāgryāya
sa sarvarasadāyakaḥ
body.translated_text: And in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, the man who, having worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, gives salt to a foremost twice-born—he is the giver of all flavors.

body.text:
sarvabhogamahābhogān
bhrājiṣmanto manoramān
lokān avāpnoti nṛpa
prasanne garuḍadhvaje
body.translated_text: He attains worlds of all enjoyments and great pleasures, shining and delightful, O king, when the one whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s> is pleased.

body.text:
pauṣamāse tu yo dadyād
ghṛtaṃ viprāya pārthiva
samabhyarcyācyutaṃ so 'pi
sarvakāmān avāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: And in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, he who, having worshipped <s>Acyuta</s>, gives ghee to a <s>vipra</s>, O king—he too would attain all [his] desires.

body.text:
māghamāse tu saṃpūjya
mādhavaṃ brāhmaṇāya yaḥ
prayacchati tilāṃl lokān
saṃprāpnoty abhivāñchitān
body.translated_text: And in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, he who, having well worshipped <s>Mādhava</s>, gives sesame to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, attains the worlds [he] wishes for.

body.text:
phālgune puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
yaḥ samabhyarcya yacchati
saptadhānyaṃ naraśreṣṭha
sa sarvasyeśvaro bhavet
body.translated_text: In <s>Phālguna</s>, he who, having well worshipped <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, gives the seven grains, O best of men—he would become lord of all.

body.text:
caitre citrāṇi vastrāṇi
yaḥ prayacchati keśavam
pūjayitvā sa vai bhogān
vicitrāṃl labhate naraḥ
body.translated_text: In <s>Caitra</s>, the man who, having worshipped <s>Keśava</s>, gives variegated garments—he indeed obtains varied enjoyments.

body.text:
vaiśākhe viṣṇum abhyarcya
yavagodhūmado naraḥ
lokān aindrān samāsādya
modate vigatajvaraḥ
body.translated_text: In <s>Vaiśākha</s>, the man who, having worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, gives barley and wheat, attaining the worlds of <s>Indra</s>, rejoices free of fever [sorrow].

body.text:
durnivartyam ahaṃ manye
cañcalaṃ hi mano yataḥ
body.translated_text: "I think [the mind] hard to turn back, for the mind indeed is fickle."

body.text:
jyaiṣṭhe 'bhyarcya hṛṣīkeśam
udakumbhaprado hi yaḥ
sa parāṃ nirvṛtiṃ yāti
sapta janmāntarāṇi vai
body.translated_text: In <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, he who, having worshipped <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, is the giver of a water-jar—he goes to supreme bliss for seven future births.

body.text:
āṣāḍhamāse ca hariṃ
yaḥ samabhyarcya yacchati
viprāya candanaṃ so 'pi
paramāhlādabhājanam
body.translated_text: And in the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, he who, having well worshipped <s>Hari</s>, gives sandal to a <s>vipra</s>—he too is a vessel of supreme delight.

body.text:
yo nṛsiṃhaṃ samabhyarcya
brāhmaṇāya prayacchati
śrāvaṇe navanītaṃ tu
sa svargaṃ sukṛtī vrajet
body.translated_text: He who, having well worshipped <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, gives fresh butter to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>—he, of good deeds, would go to heaven.

body.text:
