chattraṃ ca yo bhādrapade
vāsudevābhipūjakaḥ
prayacchati dvijāgryāya
sa cchattrādhipatir bhavet
body.translated_text: And he who, in <s>Bhādrapada</s>, a worshipper of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, gives a parasol to a foremost twice-born—he would become a lord of [those who hold the] parasol [a king].

body.text:
guḍaśarkarayā yuktaṃ
modakaṃ ca prayacchati
tathaivāśvayuje 'bhyarcya
yo 'nantaṃ so 'maro bhavet
body.translated_text: And he who gives a sweetmeat (<s>modaka</s>) made with molasses and sugar, and likewise, having worshipped <s>Ananta</s> in <s>Āśvayuja</s>—he would become immortal.

body.text:
nārāyaṇaṃ samabhyarcya
yaḥ prayacchati kārttike
dīpakaṃ viprageheṣu
vimānaṃ so 'dhirohati
body.translated_text: He who, having well worshipped <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, gives a lamp in the houses of <s>vipras</s> in <s>Kārttika</s>—he mounts a celestial chariot.

body.text:
kāmyāny etāny aśeṣāṇi
yaḥ saṃpūjya jagatpatim
dānāni yacchati naraḥ
sa saṃpūrṇamanorathaḥ
sarvaśreṣṭhaḥ samastānāṃ
bandhūnām āśrayo bhavet
body.translated_text: The man who, having worshipped the Lord of the world, gives all these desire-fulfilling gifts entirely—he, his heart's desire fulfilled, becomes the best of all, the refuge of all his kinsmen.

body.text:
evaṃ sarvāṇi dānāni
prīṇanāyācyutasya yaḥ
prayacchati sa sarveṣāṃ
phalānāṃ bhuvi bhājanam
body.translated_text: Thus, he who gives all these gifts for the gladdening of <s>Acyuta</s>—he is on earth the vessel of all the fruits [of them].

body.text:
tasmān narendra viprebhyaḥ
prīṇanāya jagadguroḥ
prayacchaitāni dānāni
yac cānyad dayitaṃ tava
body.translated_text: Therefore, O lord of men, for the gladdening of the world's teacher, give these gifts to the <s>vipras</s>, and whatever else is dear to you.

body.text:
yadīcchasi punaḥ prāptuṃ
bhūtim abhraṃśanīṃ nṛpa
tadārādhaya govindaṃ
nānyathā syur vibhūtayaḥ
body.translated_text: If you wish to attain again unfading prosperity, O king, then worship <s>Govinda</s>; not otherwise would there be [enduring] powers

body.text:
evaṃ vasiṣṭhena tadā
māndhātā nṛpa bodhitaḥ
saha patnyā mahīpālaḥ
paritoṣaṃ paraṃ yayau
body.translated_text: Thus then, O king, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, the lord of the earth, awakened by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> together with his wife, came to supreme satisfaction

body.text:
jagāda ca mudā yuktaḥ
praṇipatya purohitam
saha patnyā naraśreṣṭhaḥ
samutthāya varāsanāt
body.translated_text: And, joined with joy, having bowed to the domestic priest, that best of men together with his wife, having risen from his excellent seat, said:

body.text:
dhig dhig vṛthaiva yātāni
mamaitāni dināny aho
anāsajya manaḥ kṛṣṇe
viṣayāsaktacetasaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Fie, fie! Vainly indeed have these days of mine passed, alas, without fixing the mind on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, my heart being attached to sense-objects

body.text:
tā niśās te ca divasās
te rtavas te ca vatsarāḥ
narāṇāṃ saphalā yeṣu
cintito bhagavān hariḥ
body.translated_text: Those nights and those days, those seasons and those years, are fruitful for men in which the Blessed <s>Hari</s> is contemplated

body.text:
cintyamānaḥ samastānāṃ
pāpānāṃ hāṇido hi saḥ
samutsṛjyākhilaṃ cintyaṃ
so 'cyutaḥ kiṃ na cintyate
body.translated_text: For he, being contemplated, is the remover of all sins; abandoning all [else] to be contemplated, why is that <s>Acyuta</s> not contemplated?

body.text:
kaṣṭaṃ muṣṭo 'smi śiṣṭeṣu
vidyamāneṣu mantriṣu
parāṅmukhānāṃ govinde
yat prāptaṃ paramaṃ vayaḥ
body.translated_text: Alas, I have been robbed, [though] there were learned counselors present, in that the highest age has been reached by those turned away from <s>Govinda</s>'

body.text:
evaṃ vinindya so 'tmānāṃ
māndhātā pṛthivīpatiḥ
cakārārādhane yatnaṃ
devadevasya śārṅgitiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus reproaching himself, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, the lord of the earth, made effort in the worship of the god of gods, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow

body.text:
tam ārādhya ca viśveśam
upendram asureśvara
prāpa siddhiṃ parāṃ pūrvaṃ
dakṣaḥ prācetaso yathā
body.translated_text: And having worshipped that Lord of all, <s>Upendra</s>, O lord of <s>asuras</s>, he attained supreme perfection, as <s>Dakṣa</s> the son of <s>Pracetas</s> [had] of old

body.text:
tathā tvam api rājendra
sarvabhāvena keśavam
samārādhaya govindaṃ
tam ārādhya na sīdati
body.translated_text: So you too, O king of kings, with your whole being worship <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Govinda</s>; having worshipped him, one does not sink

body.text:
evaṃ sa daityarājendraḥ
prahrādenāvabodhitaḥ
balir ārādhane yatnaṃ
cakre cakrabhṛtas tadā
body.translated_text: Thus that lord of the <s>daitya</s> kings, <s>Bali</s>, awakened by <s>Prahrāda</s>, made effort then in the worship of the discus-bearer,

body.text:
puṣpopahārair dhūpaiś ca
tathā caivānulepanaiḥ
vāsobhir bhūṣaṇaiḥ samyag
brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ
body.translated_text: with flower-offerings and incenses, and likewise with unguents, with garments, with ornaments, rightly, and with the gratifying of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

body.text:
japair homair vrataiś caiva
yathoktaṃ puruṣarṣabha
saha patnyā tathaiva tvaṃ
samārādhaya keśavam
body.translated_text: with mutterings, oblations, and vows as declared, O bull among men; and you too, likewise, together with your wife, worship <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
bhagavaṃś cañcalaṃ cittaṃ
manuṣyāṇām aharniśam
viṣayāsaṅgadurduṣṭaṃ
pāpāyaiva pravartate
body.translated_text: 'O Blessed One, the fickle mind of men, day and night, exceedingly corrupted by attachment to sense-objects, proceeds toward sin alone

body.text:
maunena vācikaṃ pāpaṃ
puṃbhir brahman nivartyate
śārīram apy akaraṇāt
sunivartyaṃ mataṃ mama
body.translated_text: Verbal sin is averted by men through silence, O <s>brahman</s>; and bodily [sin] too, through non-doing, is in my view easily averted

body.text:
yat tv etan mānasaṃ pāpaṃ
manuṣyais tan mahāmate
durnivartyam ahaṃ manye
cañcalaṃ hi mano yataḥ
body.translated_text: But that mental sin which [is done] by men, O greatly wise one—I deem it hard to avert, for the mind is fickle

body.text:
tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi
manuṣyair durvicintitaiḥ
yat smartavyaṃ ca japyaṃ ca
mānasāghapraśāntaye
body.translated_text: So I wish to hear what is to be remembered and to be muttered by men [whose minds are] ill-disposed, for the appeasement of mental sin'

body.text:
tvadyukto 'yam anupraśnaḥ
sādhv etad bhavatoditam
cañcalatvād dhi cittānāṃ
mānasaṃ bahu pātakam
body.translated_text: 'This further question is fitting for you; well has this been uttered by you; for, from the fickleness of minds, mental sin is abundant

body.text:
bhūmau tṛṇam asaṃkhyātaṃ
yathā ca divi tārakāḥ
tathā pāpam asaṃkhyeyaṃ
cetasā kriyate tu yat
body.translated_text: As the blades of grass on earth are countless, and as the stars in heaven, so is the sin, uncountable, that is done by the mind

body.text:
paradāraparadravya-
parahiṃsāsu mānasam
aharniśaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ
sātatyena pravartate
body.translated_text: The mind of men proceeds continuously, day and night, toward [the coveting of] another's wife, another's wealth, and the harming of others

body.text:
yady asyopaśamo rājan
bhuvi na kriyate nṛbhiḥ
tan nāsti narakottāro
varṣakoṭīśatair api
body.translated_text: If its appeasement is not effected by men on earth, O king, then there is no rescue from hell even in hundreds of millions of years

body.text:
tad asya praśamāyālaṃ
prāyaścittaṃ narādhipa
śṛṇuṣva yena cittotthaṃ
sadyaḥ pāpaṃ vyapohati
body.translated_text: So, for its appeasement, the expiation [suffices], O lord of men; hear it, by which mind-born sin is at once driven away:

body.text:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya
puruṣāya mahātmane
hiraṇyaretase 'cintya-
svarūpāyātivedhase
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Person, the great soul, the golden-seeded (<s>Hiraṇyaretas</s>), of inconceivable form, exceedingly wise,

body.text:
viṣṇave jiṣṇave nityaṃ
śāntāyānagharūpiṇe
sarvasthityantakaraṇa-
vratine pītavāsase
body.translated_text: to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the victorious, ever tranquil, of sinless form, vowed to effect the maintenance and ending of all, clad in yellow,

body.text:
nārāyaṇāya viśvāya
viśveśāyeśvarāya ca
namaḥ kamalakiñjalka-
suvarṇamukuṭāya ca
body.translated_text: to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the universe, the Lord of the universe, and the Lord; and homage to him whose golden crown is [like] the filament of a lotus,

body.text:
keśavāyātisūkṣmāya
brahmamūrtimate namaḥ
namaḥ paramakalyāṇa-
kalyāṇāyātmayonaye
body.translated_text: homage to <s>Keśava</s>, the exceedingly subtle, who has the form of <s>Brahman</s>; homage to the supremely auspicious of the auspicious, the self-born,

body.text:
janārdanāya devāya
śrīdharāya sumedhase
mahātmane vareṇyāya
namaḥ paṅkajanābhaye
body.translated_text: to <s>Janārdana</s>, the god, to <s>Śrīdhara</s>, the most wise, to the great soul, the choicest; homage to the lotus-naveled one,

body.text:
smṛtamātrāghaghātāya
kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe
namo natāya namreśair
aśeṣair vāsavādibhiḥ
body.translated_text: to the destroyer of sin by mere remembrance, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of untroubled action; homage to him bowed to by all the [gods], bending low, <s>Vāsava</s> [Indra] and the rest,

body.text:
namo māyāvine tubhyaṃ
haraye harimedhase
hiraṇyagarbhagarbhāya
jagataḥ kāraṇātmane
body.translated_text: homage to you, the master of <s>māyā</s>, to <s>Hari</s> of tawny intellect, to him who is the womb of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the causal self of the world,

body.text:
govindāyādibhūtāya
śrādīnāṃ mahātmane
namo bhūtātmabhūtāya
ātmane paramātmane
body.translated_text: to <s>Govinda</s>, the first being, the great soul of <s>Śrī</s> and the rest; homage to him who is the self of [all] beings, to the Self, the Supreme Self,

body.text:
acyutāya namo nityam
anantāya namo namaḥ
dāmodarāya śucaye
yajñeśāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: homage ever to <s>Acyuta</s>, homage, homage to the infinite; to <s>Dāmodara</s>, the pure, to the lord of sacrifice, homage, homage,

body.text:
namo māyāpaṭacchanna-
jagaddhāmne mahātmane
hṛṣīkeśāya ceśāya
sarvabhūtātmarūpiṇe
body.translated_text: homage to the great soul, the abode of the world veiled by the cloth of <s>māyā</s>, to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the Lord, who has the form of the self of all beings,

body.text:
dayālave namo nityaṃ
kapilāya sumedhase
saṃsārasāgarottāra-
jñānapotapradāyine
body.translated_text: homage ever to the merciful one, to <s>Kapila</s>, the most wise, the giver of the boat of knowledge for crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text:
akuṇṭhamataye dhātre
sargasthityantakarmaṇi
karālasaumyarūpāya
vaikuṇṭhāya namo namaḥ
body.translated_text: to the one of unblunted intellect, the creator in the work of creation, maintenance, and ending, of terrible and gentle form, to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, homage, homage

body.text:
yathā hi vāsudeveti
prokte naśyati pātakam
tathā vilayam abhyetu
mamaitad durvicintitam
body.translated_text: As, indeed, when '<s>Vāsudeva</s>' is uttered, sin perishes, so may this ill-conceived [sin] of mine come to dissolution

body.text:
yathā na viṣṇubhakteṣu
pāpam āpnoti saṃsthitim
tathā vināśam abhyetu
mamaitad durvicintitam
body.translated_text: As sin does not attain establishment among the devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so may this ill-conceived [sin] of mine come to destruction

body.text:
smṛtamātro yathā viṣṇuḥ
sarvaṃ pāpaṃ vyapohati
tathā praṇāśam abhyetu
mamaitad durvicintitam
body.translated_text: As <s>Viṣṇu</s>, merely remembered, drives away all sin, so may this ill-conceived [sin] of mine come to ruin

body.text:
yathā sarvatrago viṣṇus
tatra sarvaṃ ca saṃsthitam
upayātu tathā nāśaṃ
mamāghaṃ cittasaṃbhavam
body.translated_text: As <s>Viṣṇu</s> is all-pervading, and in him all is established, so may this sin of mine, born of the mind, come to ruin

body.text:
pāpaṃ praṇāśaṃ mama saṃprayātu
yan mānasaṃ yac ca karomi vācā
śārīram apy ācaritaṃ ca yan me
smṛte jagaddhātari vāsudeve
body.translated_text: May my sin come to ruin, [that] which is mental, and which I do by speech, and the bodily [deed] too that I have practiced, when <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the upholder of the world, is remembered

body.text:
prayāntu doṣā mama nāśam āśu
rāgādayaḥ kāraṇakāraṇeśe
vijñānadīpāmalamārgadṛśye
smṛte jagaddhātari vāsudeve
body.translated_text: May my faults—passion and the rest—come quickly to ruin, when the Lord of the cause of causes is remembered, the upholder of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [seen] by the stainless path of vision [that is] the lamp of knowledge

body.text:
bhavantu bhadrāṇi samastadoṣāḥ
prayāntu nāśaṃ jagato 'khilasya
mayādya bhaktyā parameśvareśe
smṛte jagaddhātari vāsudeve
body.translated_text: May there be blessings; may all the faults of the entire world come to ruin, when by me today, with devotion, the Lord of the supreme Lord is remembered, the upholder of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
ye bhūtale ye divi ye 'ntarikṣe
rasātale prāṇigaṇāś ca kecit
bhavantu te siddhiyujo mayādya
smṛte jagaddhātari vāsudeve
body.translated_text: May those hosts of living beings—whoever are on the earth, in heaven, in the atmosphere, in the nether world—become endowed with [spiritual] success through me today, when the upholder of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is remembered

body.text:
puṣyantu maitrīṃ viramantu rāgād
ujjhantu lobhaṃ kṣamiṇo bhavantu
ābrahmavṛkṣāntaragā mayādya
smṛte jagaddhātari vāsudeve
body.translated_text: May they nourish friendliness, desist from passion, abandon greed, become forbearing—[all beings] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the trees—through me today, when the upholder of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is remembered

body.text:
ye prāṇinaḥ kutracid atra santi
brahmāṇḍamadhye parataś ca kecit
te yāntu siddhiṃ paramāṃ mayādya
smṛte jagaddhātari vāsudeve
body.translated_text: Whatever living beings are anywhere here, within the cosmic egg and beyond, may they attain the supreme success through me today, when the upholder of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is remembered

body.text:
ajñānino jñānavido bhavantu
praśāntibhājaḥ satatogracittāḥ
kurvantu bhaktiṃ paramām anante
matstotratuṣṭasya hareḥ prasādāt
body.translated_text: May the ignorant become knowers of knowledge; may those of ever-fierce mind become sharers of tranquility; may they make supreme devotion toward the infinite one, through the grace of <s>Hari</s>, pleased by my hymn

body.text:
śṛṇvanti ye me paṭhatas tathānye
paśyanti ye mām idam īrayantam
devāsurādyā manujās tiraśco
bhavantu te 'py acyutayogabhājaḥ
body.translated_text: Those who hear me reciting, and likewise others who see me uttering this—gods, <s>asuras</s>, and the rest, men, beasts—may they too become sharers in union with <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
ye cāpi mūkā vikalendriyatvāc
śṛṇvanti no naiva vilokayanti
paśvādayaḥ kīṭapipīlikāś ca
bhavantu te 'py acyutayogabhājaḥ
body.translated_text: And those too who, dumb through defectiveness of the senses, neither hear nor behold [me]—beasts and the rest, and worms and ants—may they too become sharers in union with <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
nāmasv anantasya ca kīrtiteṣu
yad atra puṇyaṃ jagataḥ prasūteḥ
tenāvivekopahatātmabodhā
bhavantu puṃsāṃ matayaḥ suśīlāḥ
body.translated_text: Whatever merit there is here in the proclaiming of the names of the infinite source of the world—by it may the minds of men, [whose] self-awareness was destroyed by lack of discrimination, become of good disposition

body.text:
ye duḥkhitās te sukhino bhavantu
dveṣānvitā maitraguṇopapannāḥ
satyārjavādyās tv anṛtā vimāyā
matsaṃstavārādhitakṛṣṇadṛṣṭāḥ
body.translated_text: May those who are sorrowful become happy; may those filled with hatred become endowed with the quality of friendliness; may the untruthful, the deceitful, become [endowed with] truth, uprightness, and the rest, [as those] who have seen <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worshipped by my hymn

body.text:
naśyantu duḥkhāni jagaty apaitu
lobhādiko doṣaguṇaḥ prajābhyaḥ
yathātmani bhrātari cātmaje ca
tathā janasyāstu jane 'pi hārdam
body.translated_text: May sorrows perish in the world; may greed and the other faulty qualities depart from the people; as toward oneself, toward a brother and a son, so may there be affection of people toward [other] people too

body.text:
saṃsāravaidye 'khiladoṣahāni-
vicakṣaṇe nirvṛtihetubhūte
saṃsārabandhāḥ śithilībhavantu
hṛdi sthite sarvajanasya viṣṇau
body.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s>—the physician of <s>saṃsāra</s>, skilled in the removal of all faults, the cause of bliss—abides in the heart of all people, may the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s> become loosened

body.text:
etat paṭhan pārthiva sarvapāpair
vimucyate viṣṇuparaḥ sadaiva
prāpnoti siddhiṃ vipulaṃ maharddhim
na cāpy anartheṣu matiṃ karoti
body.translated_text: Reciting this, O king, one devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is ever freed from all sins; he attains success, abundant great prosperity, and does not set his mind upon harmful things

body.text:
uddiśya sattvāni ca yāni yāni
stotraṃ paṭhante kṛpayā manuṣyāḥ
sarvāṇi tāny apratighā bhavanti
prayānti siddhiṃ bhagavatprasādāt
body.translated_text: And whatever beings men recite the hymn for, with compassion, all those [recitations] become unobstructed [and] attain success through the grace of the Blessed Lord

body.text:
tasmāt tvayaitat satataṃ niśāsu
dineṣu caiveśvara mādhavasya
saṃkīrtanaṃ kāryam aśeṣapāpa-
vimokṣahetor abhavāya caiva
body.translated_text: Therefore by you, O Lord, the proclaiming of <s>Mādhava</s> is ever to be performed, by night and by day, for the sake of release from all sin and for [release from] [re]birth

body.text:
iti sakalajanopakārakārī
haricaraṇābjaviniṣṭaśuddhabuddhiḥ
paṭhati khalu mahīpa yo manuṣyaḥ
sa layam upaiti harau hṛtākhilāghaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, O king, the man who, doing benefit to all people, his pure mind fixed on the lotus-feet of <s>Hari</s>, recites [this]—he attains absorption in <s>Hari</s>, all his sin removed

body.text:
idaṃ ca śṛṇu bhūpāla
naśyate durvicintitam
yenopāyena vai puṃsāṃ
yoṣitāṃ vāpy asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: And hear this too, O lord of the earth, [by which] ill-conceived [sin] is destroyed, by which means indeed, for men or for women, without doubt

body.text:
paradāraparadravya-
jīvahiṃsādike sadā
pravartate nṛṇāṃ cittaṃ
tad etad abhisaṃsmaret
body.translated_text: The mind of men ever proceeds toward [coveting] another's wife, another's wealth, the harming of living beings, and the rest; that [man] should remember this:

body.text:
viṣṇave viṣṇave nityaṃ
viṣṇave viṣṇave namaḥ
jiṣṇave jiṣṇave sarvaṃ
jiṣṇave jiṣṇave namaḥ
body.translated_text: To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s> ever, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s> homage; to the victorious, to the victorious all, to the victorious, to the victorious homage

body.text:
namāmi viṣṇuṃ buddhistham
ahaṃkāra-gataṃ harim
cittastham īśam avyaktam
anantam aparājitam
viṣṇum īḍyam aśeṣeśam
anādinidhanaṃ vibhum
body.translated_text: I bow to <s>Viṣṇu</s> abiding in the intellect, to <s>Hari</s> present in the ego, to the Lord abiding in the mind, the unmanifest, the infinite, the unconquered, to <s>Viṣṇu</s> the praiseworthy, the Lord of all, without beginning or end, the all-pervading

body.text:
viṣṇuś cittagato yan me
viṣṇur buddhigataś ca yat
yac cāhaṃkārago viṣṇur
yad viṣṇur mayi saṃsthitaḥ
body.translated_text: That <s>Viṣṇu</s> who has entered my mind, and the <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is in my intellect, and the <s>Viṣṇu</s> gone into the ego, and the <s>Viṣṇu</s> established in me—

body.text:
karoti kartṛbhūto 'sau
sthāvarasya carasya ca
tat pāpaṃ nāśam āyātu
tasminn eva vicintite
body.translated_text: he, being the doer, performs [the actions] of the stationary and the moving; may that sin come to ruin when he alone is contemplated

body.text:
dhyāto harati yaḥ pāpaṃ
svapne dṛṣṭaḥ śubhāvahaḥ
tam upendram ahaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇato 'rtiharaṃ harim
body.translated_text: He who, meditated upon, removes sin, [who] seen in a dream is bringer of auspiciousness—to that <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the remover of distress, <s>Hari</s>, I am bowed down

body.text:
jagaty asmin nirādhāre
majjamāne tamasy adhaḥ
hastāvalambadaṃ viṣṇuṃ
praṇato 'smi parātparam
body.translated_text: In this world without support, sinking down into the darkness, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the giver of the support of [his] hand, the supreme beyond the supreme, I am bowed down

body.text:
sarveśvareśvara vibho
paramātmann adhokṣaja
hṛṣīkeśa hṛṣīkeśa
hṛṣīkeśa namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: O Lord of the lords of all, all-pervading, Supreme Self, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, homage be to you

body.text:
nṛsiṃhānanta govinda
bhūtabhāvana keśava
duruktaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ dhyātaṃ
praśamāgrya namo 'stu te
body.translated_text: O <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, source of beings, <s>Keśava</s>—[for] what is ill-spoken, ill-done, ill-thought, O foremost appeaser, homage be to you

body.text:
yan mayā cintitaṃ duṣṭaṃ
svacittavaśavartinā
narakāvaham atyugraṃ
tac chamaṃ naya keśava
body.translated_text: Whatever wicked [thing] was thought by me, swayed by my own mind, exceedingly fierce, bringing hell—lead that to appeasement, O <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
brahmaṇyadeva govinda
paramārtha parāyaṇa
jagannātha jagaddhātaḥ
pāpaṃ praśamayācyuta
body.translated_text: O god kind to brahmins, <s>Govinda</s>, intent on the supreme aim, Lord of the world, upholder of the world, appease [my] sin, O <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
yac cāparāhne pūrvāhne
madhyāhne ca tathā niśi
kāyena manasā vācā
kṛtaṃ pāpam ajānatā
body.translated_text: And whatever sin was done in the afternoon, the forenoon, at midday, and likewise at night, by body, by mind, by speech, unknowingly

body.text:
jānatā vā hṛṣīkeśa
puṇḍarīkākṣa mādhava
nāmatrayoccāraṇatas
tat prayātu mama kṣayam
body.translated_text: or knowingly, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>—by the uttering of the three names may that come to destruction for me

body.text:
śārīraṃ me hṛṣīkeśa
puṇḍarīkākṣa mānasam
pāpaṃ praśamayādya tvaṃ
vākkṛtaṃ mama mādhava
body.translated_text: My bodily [sin], O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, [my] mental [sin], O <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>—appease today, O <s>Mādhava</s>, [and] the sin done by me through speech

body.text:
yad vrajan yat svapan bhuñjan
yad uttiṣṭhan yad āsthitaḥ
kṛtavāṃś cāpi yac cāhaṃ
kāyena manasā girā
body.translated_text: Whatever I have done while walking, while sleeping, while eating, while rising, while seated, by body, by mind, by speech—

body.text:
mahat svalpam atisthūlaṃ
kuyoninarakāvaham
tad yātu praśamaṃ sarvaṃ
vāsudevasya kīrtanāt
body.translated_text: great, small, exceedingly gross, bringing [rebirth in] an evil womb or hell—may all that come to appeasement through the proclaiming of <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma
pavitraṃ paramaṃ ca yat
tasmin saṃkīrtite viṣṇoḥ
pade pāpaṃ praṇaśyatu
body.translated_text: When that supreme <s>Brahman</s>, supreme abode, supremely pure thing—the [supreme] state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—is proclaimed, may sin perish

body.text:
sūrayo yat pravekṣyanti hy
apunarbhavakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
mamākhilaṃ daha tvaṃ hi
tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: That which the wise, desirous of no-rebirth, shall enter—do you burn up all of mine—that supreme state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
yat prāpya na ninvartante
gandhasparśādivarjitam
pāpaṃ praṇāśayatv adya
tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: That which, having attained, they do not return [from], free of smell, touch, and the rest—may it destroy [my] sin today—that supreme state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
sadasad yat tathā vyaktā-
vyaktarūpam ajājaram
praṇamāmi jagaddhāma
tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: I bow to the abode of the world—[that] which is the existent and the non-existent, and likewise the manifest and unmanifest form, the unborn, the undecaying—that supreme state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
śārīre mānase caiva
pāpe vāgje ca pārthiva
kṛte samyaṅ naro bhaktyā
paṭhec chraddhāsamanvitaḥ
mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ
kṛṣṇanāmaprakīrtanāt
body.translated_text: When bodily and mental and verbal sin has been committed, O king, a man, having recited [this] rightly with devotion, endowed with faith, is freed from all sins through the proclaiming of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s name

body.text:
uccāryamāne caitasmin
devadevasya saṃstave
vilayaṃ pāpam āyāti
bhāṇḍam āmam ivāmbhasi
body.translated_text: When this hymn of the god of gods is being uttered, sin comes to dissolution, like an unbaked clay vessel in water

body.text:
tasmāt saṃcintite pāpe
samanantaram eva te
japtavyam etat pāpasya
praśamāya mahīpate
body.translated_text: Therefore, when sin has been conceived, immediately thereafter this is to be muttered by you for the appeasement of the sin, O lord of the earth'

body.text:
saṃsārārṇavamagnena
puruṣeṇa mahāmune
viṣayāsaktacittena
yat kāryaṃ tad vadasva me
body.translated_text: 'By a man sunk in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, O great sage, whose mind is attached to sense-objects, what is to be done—tell me that

body.text:
bhrāmyatāṃ saṃkaṭe durge
saṃsāre viṣayaiṣiṇām
svakarmabhir manuṣyāṇām
upakārakam ucyatām
body.translated_text: For men wandering in the dangerous, impassable [ocean of] <s>saṃsāra</s>, seeking sense-objects, [bound] by their own deeds—let what is beneficial be told

body.text:
kṣīpte manasy anāyatte
vṛddhe lobhādike gaṇe
śaraṇaṃ yan manuṣyāṇāṃ
tad ācakṣva mahāmune
body.translated_text: When the mind is cast about [and] uncontrolled, [and] the host of greed and the rest has grown—let that which is the refuge of men be declared, O great sage'

body.text:
saṃsārāṇavapotāya
haraye harimedhase
namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi
narāṇām upakārakam
body.translated_text: Having paid homage to <s>Hari</s> of tawny intellect, the boat for the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, I shall declare what is beneficial for men

body.text:
samyag ārādhito bhaktyā
vedabhāraguror guruḥ
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prāha
yac chiṣyāya sumantave
body.translated_text: Well worshipped with devotion, the teacher of the teacher of the burden of the <s>Veda</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> [Vyāsa], related [this] which [he taught] to his pupil <s>Sumantu</s>:

body.text:
purā kila durācāro
durbuddhir ajitendriyaḥ
kṣatrabandhur abhūt pāpaḥ
paramarmāvaghaṭṭakaḥ
body.translated_text: Of old, it is said, there was a base <s>kṣatriya</s> (<s>kṣatrabandhu</s>), of wicked conduct, of evil intellect, of unconquered senses, a sinner, one who struck at the very vital points [of others]

body.text:
mātāpitror aśuśrūṣur
drogdhā bandhujanasya ca
gurudevadvijātīnāṃ
nindāsu satatodyataḥ
body.translated_text: no servant of his mother and father, an injurer of his kinsfolk, ever intent on the reviling of gurus, gods, and the twice-born

body.text:
moṣṭā viśvasatāṃ nityam
aprītiḥ prītim icchatām
ṛjūnām anṛjuḥ kṣudraḥ
parahiṃsāparāyaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: a constant robber of those who trusted [him], an enemy to those who desired [his] friendship, crooked toward the upright, mean, devoted to the injury of others

body.text:
sa bāndhavaiḥ parityaktas
tathānyaiḥ sādhuvṛttibhiḥ
avṛttimān aviśvāsyo
mṛgayājīvano 'bhavat
body.translated_text: He, abandoned by his kinsmen and likewise by others of good conduct, without [proper] livelihood, untrustworthy, became one who lived by hunting

body.text:
ahany ahani cakrāṅgān
eṇakādīṃs tathā mṛgān
hatvātmapoṣaṇaṃ cakre
vyādhavṛttirato 'dhamaḥ
body.translated_text: Day after day, having slain <s>cakra</s>-marked birds and <s>eṇa</s>-deer and other beasts, the base one made his self-nourishment, taking pleasure in the hunter's livelihood

body.text:
etayā tasya duṣṭasya
kuvṛttyā pāpacetasaḥ
jagāma sumahān kālaḥ
kurvato dārapoṣaṇam
body.translated_text: By this evil livelihood of that wicked one of sinful mind, a very long time passed as he did the nourishing of his wife

body.text:
ekadā tu munis tena
nidāghe vijane vane
mṛgayām aṭatā dṛṣṭo
vartmanaḥ pracyutaḥ pathi
body.translated_text: But once, in the hot season, in a desolate forest, he was seen by a sage [whom he was] wandering after on a hunt—[the sage] fallen from his road, [strayed] from the path,

body.text:
kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhaḥ suśrāntaḥ
śuṣkajihvāsyatālukaḥ
tṛṭparīto 'tivibhrāntaḥ
kāṃdigbhūto 'lpacetanaḥ
body.translated_text: his throat parched with hunger, exhausted, his tongue, mouth, and palate dry, beset by thirst, exceedingly bewildered, gone in all directions [confused], of little awareness,

body.text:
śvāsāyāsaślathair aṅgaiḥ
kṛcchrād ātmānam udvahan
sūryāṃśutāpāt pragalat-
svedārdracaraṇo nṛpa
body.translated_text: his limbs slackened by the exertion of breathing, bearing himself along with difficulty, his feet moist with sweat trickling down from the heat of the sun's rays, O king

body.text:
tasmin dṛṣṭe tatas tasya
kṣatrabandhor ajāyata
kāruṇyaṃ dāruṇasyāpi
vyādhavṛttiparigrahāt
body.translated_text: When [the sage] was seen, then compassion arose in that <s>kṣatrabandhu</s>, dreadful though he was through his adoption of the hunter's livelihood

body.text:
tam upetya ca bhūpāla
kṣatrabandhuḥ sa tāpasam
uvāca viprapravaraṃ
vimārge vartate bhavān
body.translated_text: And approaching that ascetic, O lord of the earth, that <s>kṣatrabandhu</s> said to the foremost of <s>vipras</s>: "Your honour is going on a wrong path

body.text:
naiṣa panthā dvijaśreṣṭha
vipino 'yaṃ mahāṭaviḥ
mām anvehi tvarāyukto
mā vipattiṃ sameṣyasi
body.translated_text: This is no road, O best of the twice-born; this is a wild, great forest; follow me, with haste, lest you meet with calamity"

body.text:
niśāmya tad vacaḥ śrāntaḥ
kṣatrabandhor mahānuniḥ
anuvavrāja rājendra
jalāśājanitodyamaḥ
body.translated_text: Hearing that word, the great sage, exhausted, followed the <s>kṣatrabandhu</s>, O king of kings, his effort roused by hope of water

body.text:
kiṃcid bhūbhāgam āsādya
dadarśa ca mahāmuniḥ
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇaṃ
protphullanalinaṃ saraḥ
body.translated_text: Reaching some part of the ground, the great sage saw a lake strewn with swans and <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, with full-blown lotuses,

body.text:
sārasābhirutaṃ ramyaṃ
sūpatīrtham akardamam
padmotpalayutaṃ cāru
pūrṇaṃ svacchena vāriṇā
body.translated_text: resounding with cranes, delightful, with good landing-banks, free of mud, charmingly furnished with lotuses and water-lilies, full of clear water,

body.text:
suśītavanaṣaṇḍaiś ca
samantāt pariveṣṭitam
tatkṣaṇāt tṛṭparītānāṃ
cakṣuṣo hlādakāriṇam
body.translated_text: and surrounded all around with cool thickets of trees, instantly bringing gladness to the eyes of those beset by thirst

body.text:
dṛṣṭvaiva sa munis tatra
tadāmalajalaṃ saraḥ
sūryāṃśutapto gharmārto
nipapāta tadambhasi
body.translated_text: Seeing there that lake of stainless water, that sage, scorched by the sun's rays, afflicted by the heat, fell into its water

body.text:
tatrāśvāsya kṛtāhlādaḥ
papau vāri narādhipa
ujjīvayan munivaro
jihvātālu śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
body.translated_text: There, having refreshed himself and made [himself] glad, he drank the water, O lord of men, the best of sages reviving his tongue and palate little by little

body.text:
so 'pi kṣatriyadāyādo
munitrāṇaparāyaṇaḥ
vihāya saśaraṃ cāpam
ujjahāra bisāny atha
body.translated_text: And that <s>kṣatriya</s>-scion too, intent on the rescue of the sage, having laid aside his bow and arrows, then plucked up lotus-stalks

body.text:
dadau ca tasmai rājendra
kṣudhitāya tapasvine
yayau ca tṛptiṃ vipro 'pi
bisanālāmbubhakṣaṇāt
body.translated_text: And he gave them, O king of kings, to that hungry ascetic; and the <s>vipra</s> too came to satisfaction by eating the lotus-stalks, fibres, and water

body.text:
tam āśvastaṃ kṛtāhāram
upaviṣṭaṃ suśītale
nyagrodhaśākhāsaṃchanne
niṣpaṅke sarasas taṭe
saṃvāhayām āsa ca taṃ
kṣatrabandhuḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
body.translated_text: Him, refreshed, having taken food, seated on the cool, mudless bank of the lake covered by the branches of a banyan, the <s>kṣatrabandhu</s> massaged little by little

body.text:
pādajaṅghorupṛṣṭeṣu
tena saṃvāhito muniḥ
jahau śramam amitraghna
vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
body.translated_text: Massaged by him on his feet, shanks, thighs, and back, the sage put off his fatigue, O slayer of foes, and spoke this word:

body.text:
kas tvaṃ bhadramukhādyeha
mama prāṇaparikṣaye
hastāvalambado dhātrā
janito vipine vane
body.translated_text: "Who are you, O gracious-faced one, who here, at the [near] destruction of my life, were created by the Ordainer as a giver of hand-support in the wild forest?

body.text:
vibhraṣṭamārgo mūḍho 'haṃ
kṣutpipāsāśramāturaḥ
trātas tvayā mahābhāga
kas tvam atra vane 'jane
body.translated_text: Strayed from my path, deluded, afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, I was saved by you, O greatly fortunate one; who are you here in this peopleless forest?

body.text:
kṣutpipāsāśramārtasya
yas trāṇaṃ vipine vane
karoti puruṣavyāghra
tasya lokā madhuścyutaḥ
body.translated_text: He who renders rescue, in a wild forest, to one afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, O tiger among men—his worlds drip with honey

body.text:
sa tvaṃ brūhi mahābhāga
mamābhyuddhārakārakaḥ
yeṣāṃ prakhyātayaśasāṃ
samutpannaḥ kule bhavān
body.translated_text: So tell, O greatly fortunate one, [you] who are the rescuer of me, in [the family] of which men of renowned fame your honour was born"

body.text:
haryaśvasya kule jātaḥ
putraś citrarathasya ca
vimatir nāma nāmnāhaṃ
hantum abhyāgato mṛgān
body.translated_text: "Born in the family of <s>Haryaśva</s>, the son also of <s>Citraratha</s>, <s>Vimati</s> by name am I; I have come [here] to slay deer

body.text:
pitrarthaṃ mṛgayeyaṃ te
lakṣyārthaṃ vā mahāmate
āhārārtham utāho 'tra
mṛgayā vyasanaṃ tu te
body.translated_text: Is this hunting of yours for the sake of your father, or for [target-]practice, O wise one, or for the sake of food, or rather is hunting here a vice for you?"

body.text:
vṛttir eṣā mama brahman
parityaktasya bāndhavaiḥ
bhṛtyair anyaiś ca naṣṭe 'rthe
nirdhanasyāmiṣāśinaḥ
body.translated_text: "This is my livelihood, O <s>brahman</s>, [I] being abandoned by my kinsmen, by servants and others, my wealth lost, [I being] penniless, an eater of flesh"

body.text:
kimarthaṃ tvaṃ parityakto
bhṛtyasvajanabandhubhiḥ
pātakī kīkaṭaḥ kṣudrair
upajaptaḥ pareṇa vā
body.translated_text: "For what reason were you abandoned by servants, your own people, and kinsmen? [Are you] a sinner, a base wretch, [or were you] suborned by mean people, or by another [enemy]?"

body.text:
ity uktaḥ so 'bhavan maunī
paśyan doṣaṃ nṛpātmani
aduṣṭāṃś cātmano bhṛtyān
vicintyātīva durmanāḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, he became silent, seeing the fault in himself, the king's son, and reflecting that his servants were not at fault—exceedingly downcast

body.text:
avekṣya taṃ sādhvasinaṃ
kṣatrabandhuṃ mahāmuniḥ
dhyātvā ciram athāpaśyat
kṣatrabandhuṃ svadoṣiṇam
body.translated_text: Observing that distressed <s>kṣatrabandhu</s>, the great sage, having pondered long, then saw the <s>kṣatrabandhu</s> [to be] at fault toward himself

body.text:
saṃtyaktabandhuloke ca
tasmin durvṛttacetasi
kṛpāṃ cakāra sa muniḥ
kṣatrabandhau dayāparaḥ
body.translated_text: And toward that one of evil-conducted mind, abandoned by the world of kinsmen, the sage made compassion, [being] intent on pity toward the <s>kṣatrabandhu</s>

body.text:
uvāca ca munir bhūyaḥ
kṣatrabandhuṃ kṛpālukaḥ
upakāriṇam ugreṇa
karmaṇā taṃ vidūṣitam
body.translated_text: And the compassionate sage spoke again to the <s>kṣatrabandhu</s>, the benefactor [yet] sullied by [his] fierce occupation:

body.text:
api śaknoṣi saṃyantum
akāryaprasṛtaṃ manaḥ
prāṇi pīḍānivṛttiṃ ca
kartuṃ krodhādisaṃyamam
body.translated_text: "Are you able to restrain [your] mind which is given to improper acts, and to effect cessation from the tormenting of living beings, [and] the restraint of anger and the rest?

body.text:
api maitrīṃ jane kartuṃ
śaknoṣi tvaṃ mudhaiva yā
aihikāmuṣmikī vīra
kriyamāṇā mahāphalā
body.translated_text: Are you able to make friendliness toward people—[friendliness] which, even when done in vain, O hero, [yet] done, [is] of great fruit here and in the hereafter?"

body.text:
na śaknomi kṣamāṃ kartuṃ
na maitrīṃ mama cetasi
prāṇinām avadhād brahman
nāsti dārādipoṣaṇam
body.translated_text: "I am not able to make forbearance, nor friendliness, in my mind; without the slaying of living beings, O <s>brahman</s>, there is no nourishing of my wife and the rest

body.text:
anāyattaṃ ca me cittaṃ
viṣayān eva dhāvati
tadaprāptau ca sarveṣāṃ
krodhādīnāṃ samudbhavaḥ
body.translated_text: And my mind, not under [my] control, runs only after sense-objects; and on the non-attainment of those, there arises of all [the passions], anger and the rest

body.text:
so 'haṃ na maitrīṃ na kṣāntiṃ
na hiṃsādivivarjanam
kartuṃ śaknomi yat kāryaṃ
tadanyad upadiśyatām
body.translated_text: So I am not able to make friendliness, nor forbearance, nor the renunciation of injury and the rest; let some other thing that can be done be taught [to me]"

body.text:
tenaivam ukto vipro 'sau
tam upekṣyam amanyata
tathāpy atikṛpālutvāt
kṣatrabandhum abhāṣata
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by him, that <s>vipra</s> thought him one to be given up; yet, out of exceeding compassion, he spoke to the <s>kṣatrabandhu</s>:

body.text:
yady etad akhilaṃ kartuṃ
na śaknoṣi bravīhi me
svalpam anyan mayoktaṃ hi
kariṣyati bhavān yadi
body.translated_text: "If you are not able to do all this, tell me; for if I tell [you] some other trifling [thing], will your honour do it?"

body.text:
aśakyam uktaṃ bhavatā
cañcalatvād dhi cetasaḥ
vākśarīraviniṣpādyaṃ
yac chakyaṃ tad udīraya
body.translated_text: "What has been spoken by you is impossible [for me], because of the fickleness of my mind; speak that which can be done, accomplishable by speech and body"

body.text:
uttiṣṭhatā prasvapatā
prasthitena gamiṣyatā
govindeti sadā vācyaṃ
kṣutapraskhalitādiṣu
body.translated_text: "While rising, while sleeping, while setting out, while about to go, 'Govinda' is ever to be uttered, on sneezing, stumbling, and the like

body.text:
kāryaṃ vartmani mūḍhānāṃ
kṣemamārge 'vatāraṇam
hitaṃ ca vācyaṃ pṛṣṭena
śatrūṇām api jānatā
body.translated_text: There is to be done, on the road, the setting of the deluded onto the path of safety; and a beneficial [thing] is to be said when asked, even [for] one's enemies, by a knowing [person]

body.text:
etat tavopakārāya
bhaviṣyaty anupālitam
yady anyad upasaṃhartuṃ
na śaknoṣi mahīpate
body.translated_text: This, observed, will be for your benefit, if you are not able to undertake [anything] else, O lord of the earth"

body.text:
ity uktvā prayayau vipras
tena vartmani darśite
so 'pi tac chāsanaṃ sarvaṃ
kṣatrabandhuś cakāra ha
body.translated_text: Having said this, the <s>vipra</s> went on by the path shown by him; and that <s>kṣatrabandhu</s> too did all that instruction

body.text:
govindeti kṣute gacchan
prasthānaskhalitādiṣu
udīrayann avāpāgryāṃ
ratiṃ tatra śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
body.translated_text: Going [along], uttering 'Govinda' on sneezing, on setting out, on stumbling and the like, he attained there, little by little, the highest delight [in it]

body.text:
tataḥ kālena mahatā
kṣatrabandhur mamāra vai
ajāyata ca viprasya
kule jātismaro nṛpa
body.translated_text: Then after a great time the <s>kṣatrabandhu</s> died indeed, and was born in the family of a <s>vipra</s>, remembering his [past] births, O king

body.text:
tasya saṃsmarato jātīḥ
śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
nirvedaḥ sumahāñ jajñe
saṃsāre 'trātiduḥkhade
sa cintayām āsa jagat
sarvam etad acetanam
body.translated_text: As he remembered his births by the hundreds and then by the thousands, a very great disgust [with existence] arose in him, in this exceedingly painful <s>saṃsāra</s>; and he reflected: "All this world is unconscious;

body.text:
aham eko 'tra saṃjñāvān
govindodīritaṃ hi yat
yac cādhvani vimūḍhānāṃ
kṛtaṃ vartmāvatāraṇam
hitam uktaṃ ca pṛṣṭena
tasya jātismṛtiḥ phalam
body.translated_text: I alone here am possessed of [discriminating] awareness, [because] of that which was uttered, 'Govinda,' and [because of] the setting on the path of the deluded that was done on the road, and the beneficial [thing] spoken when asked—the remembrance of [past] births is the fruit of that

body.text:
so 'haṃ jātismaro bhūyaḥ
kariṣyāmy atisaṃkaṭe
tadā saṃsāracakre 'smin
yena prāpsyāmi nirvṛtim
body.translated_text: So I, remembering my births, shall again act, in this exceedingly perilous wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, in such a way that I shall thereby attain contentment

body.text:
yasyoccāraṇamātreṇa
jātā jātismṛtir mama
tam evārādhayiṣyāmi
jagatām īśvaraṃ harim
body.translated_text: By the mere utterance of whom the remembrance of births arose in me—him alone shall I worship, <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of the worlds

body.text:
yanmayaṃ paramaṃ brahma
tad avyaktaṃ ca yanmayam
yanmayaṃ vyaktam apy etad
bhaviṣyāmi hi tanmayaḥ
body.translated_text: That of which the supreme <s>Brahman</s> consists, and that of which the unmanifest consists, and that of which this manifest too consists—I shall indeed become consisting of him

body.text:
yady anārādhite viṣṇau
mamaitaj janma yāsyati
dhruvaṃ bandhavato muktir
naiva jātūpapadyate
body.translated_text: If, <s>Viṣṇu</s> being unworshipped, this birth of mine shall pass, then surely, [I being] in bondage, liberation will never come about

body.text:
aho duḥkham aho duḥkham
aho duḥkham atīva hi
svarūpam atighorasya
saṃsārasyātidurlabham
body.translated_text: Alas the misery, alas the misery, alas the exceeding misery indeed! The very form of <s>saṃsāra</s>, exceedingly terrible, [and] very hard to escape!

body.text:
viṇmūtrapūyakalile
garbhavāse 'tipīḍanāt
aśucāv atibībhatse
duḥkham atyantaduḥsaham
body.translated_text: In the dwelling of the womb, filthy with excrement, urine, and pus, from the exceeding torment, in the impure, most loathsome [place], the misery is exceedingly unbearable

body.text:
duḥkhaṃ ca jāyamānānāṃ
gātrabhaṅgādipīḍanāt
vātena preryamāṇānāṃ
mūrchākāry atibhītidam
body.translated_text: And [there is] the misery of those being born, from the torment of the breaking of the limbs and the rest, of those driven by the [birth-]wind, causing fainting, exceedingly terrifying

body.text:
bālatve nirvivekānāṃ
bhūtadevātmasaṃbhavam
yauvane vārddhake caiva
maraṇe cātidāruṇam
body.translated_text: In childhood, [for] those without discrimination, [there is misery] arising from [hostile] beings, gods, and one's own self; and in youth and in old age, and in death, the most dreadful [misery]

body.text:
śītoṣṇatṛṣṇākṣudroga-
jvarādiparivāritaḥ
sarvadaiva pumān āste
yāvaj janmāntasaṃsthitiḥ
body.translated_text: Surrounded by cold, heat, thirst, hunger, disease, fever, and the rest, a man dwells ever, as long as [his] existence lasts till the end of [his] life

body.text:
duḥkhātiśayabhūtaṃ hi
yad ante vāsukhaṃ nṛṇām
tasyānumānaṃ naivāsti
kāryeṇaivānumīyate
body.translated_text: For that surpassing-misery, unhappy [state] of men at the end [death]—there is no [direct] inferring of it; it is inferred only by [its] effect [their fear]

body.text:
kṛṣyamāṇasya puruṣair
yad yamasyātiduḥsaham
duḥkhaṃ tatsaṃsmṛtiprāptaṃ
karoti mama vepathum
body.translated_text: The misery, exceedingly unbearable, of [the man] of <s>Yama</s>, being dragged off by [Yama's] men—reaching the remembrance of that, it makes me tremble

body.text:
kumbhīpāke taptakumbhe
mahārauravaraurave
kālasūtre mahāyantre
śūkare kūṭaśālmalau
body.translated_text: In <s>Kumbhīpāka</s>, in <s>Taptakumbha</s>, in <s>Mahāraurava</s> and <s>Raurava</s>, in <s>Kālasūtra</s>, in the great machine, in <s>Sūkara</s>, in <s>Kūṭaśālmali</s>,

body.text:
asipatravane duḥkham
apratiṣṭhe ca yan mahat
viḍālavaktre ca tathā
tamasy ugre ca duḥsaham
body.translated_text: in <s>Asipatravana</s>, the misery, and that great [misery] in <s>Apratiṣṭha</s>, and likewise in <s>Viḍālavaktra</s>, and in the fierce darkness, unbearable,

body.text:
śastrāgniyantravegeṣu
śītoṣṇādiṣu dāruṇam
tataś ca muktasya punar
yonisaṃkramaṇeṣu yat
body.translated_text: in the violences of weapons, fire, and machines, [and] in cold, heat, and the rest, dreadful—and then, of one released from that, again in the passings through wombs that [occur],

body.text:
garbhasthasya ca yad duḥkham
atiduḥsaham ulvaṇam
punaś ca jāyamānasya
janma yauvanajaṃ ca yat
body.translated_text: and the misery of one situated in the womb, exceedingly unbearable, fierce, and again of one being born, and the [misery] born of youth that [there is]—

body.text:
duḥkhāny etāny asahyāni
saṃsārāntarvivartibhiḥ
puruṣair anubhūyante
sukhabhrāntivimohitaiḥ
body.translated_text: these unbearable miseries are experienced by men revolving within <s>saṃsāra</s>, deluded by the illusion of happiness

body.text:
na vai sukhakalā kācit
tatrāsty atyantaduḥkhade
saṃsārasaṃkaṭe tīvre
upetānāṃ kadācana
body.translated_text: There is not any particle of happiness there, in [that] exceedingly painful, fierce peril of <s>saṃsāra</s>, ever, for those who have entered it

body.text:
viṣayāsaktacittānāṃ
manuṣyāṇāṃ kadā matiḥ
saṃsārottāraṇe vāñchāṃ
kariṣyati hi cañcalā
body.translated_text: When will the mind of men, their minds attached to sense-objects, fickle, make a wish for crossing over <s>saṃsāra</s>?

body.text:
govindanāmnā satataṃ
samuccāraṇasaṃbhavam
jātismaratvam etan naḥ
kiṃ vṛthaiva prayāsyati
body.translated_text: This remembrance of births of ours, arisen constantly from the utterance of the name 'Govinda'—shall it pass [away] in vain?

body.text:
so 'haṃ muktipradānārtham
anantam ajam avyayam
taccittas tanmayo bhūtvā
toṣayiṣyāmi keśavam
body.translated_text: So I, having become with my mind on him, consisting of him, shall gratify <s>Keśava</s>, the endless, unborn, imperishable, for the sake of [his] bestowing liberation"

body.text:
ātmānam ātmanaivaṃ sa
proktvā jātismaro dvijaḥ
tuṣṭāva vāgbhir iṣṭābhiḥ
praṇataḥ puruṣottamam
body.translated_text: Having thus addressed himself by himself, that twice-born who remembered his births praised <s>Puruṣottama</s> with cherished words, bowed down:

body.text:
praṇipatyākṣaraṃ viśvaṃ
viśvahetuṃ nirañjanam
yat prārthayāmy avikalaṃ
sakalaṃ tat prayacchatu
body.translated_text: "Having bowed to the imperishable, [who is] the universe, the cause of the universe, the stainless one—what I pray for, may he grant that, [each] part [and] the whole

body.text:
kartāram akṛtaṃ viṣṇuṃ
sarvakāraṇakāraṇam
aṇor aṇīyāṃsam ajaṃ
sarvavyāpinam īśvaram
body.translated_text: the Maker, the uncreated <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the cause of all causes, smaller than the smallest, unborn, the all-pervading Lord,

body.text:
parāt parataraṃ yasmān
nāsti sarveśvarāt param
taṃ praṇamyācyutaṃ devaṃ
prārthayāmi yad astu tat
body.translated_text: than whom—higher than the highest—there is none higher than the Lord of all; having bowed to that god <s>Acyuta</s>, I pray that it may be

body.text:
sarveśvarācyutānanta
paramātmañ janārdana
saṃsārābdhimahāpota
samuddhara mahārṇavāt
body.translated_text: O Lord of all, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, Supreme Self, <s>Janārdana</s>, great boat upon the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, rescue [me] from the great ocean

body.text:
vyomānilāgnyambudharāsvarūpa
tanmātrasarvendriyabuddhirūpa
antaḥsthitātman paramātmarūpa
prasīda sarveśvara viśvarūpa
body.translated_text: O you whose form is sky, wind, fire, water, and cloud, whose form is the subtle elements and all the senses and the intellect, O Self abiding within, of the form of the Supreme Self—be gracious, O Lord of all, O Universal Form

body.text:
tam ādir anto jagato 'sya madhyam
ādes tvam ādiḥ pralayasya cāntaḥ
tvatto bhavaty etad aśeṣam īśa
tvayy eva cānte layam abhyupaiti
body.translated_text: You are the beginning, the end, [and] the middle of this world; you are the beginning of the beginning and the end of the dissolution; from you arises all this, O Lord, and in you alone, at the end, it comes to dissolution

body.text:
pradīpavartyantagato 'gnir alpo
yathātikakṣe vitataṃ prayāti
tadvad visṛṣṭer amarādibhinnair
vikāśam āyāsi vibhūtibhedaiḥ
body.translated_text: As a small fire, gone to the end of the lamp's wick, when [it reaches] very dry [fuel] proceeds [to spread] wide, so from creation you come to expansion through the distinctions of manifestation differentiated as the immortals and the rest

body.text:
yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo 'mbuvegāḥ
samantato 'bdhiṃ bhagavan viśanti
tvayy antakāle jagad acyutedaṃ
tathā layaṃ gacchati sarvabhūte
body.translated_text: As the many water-floods of the rivers enter the ocean from all sides, O Blessed One, so in you, at the end-time, this world, O <s>Acyuta</s>, O you who are all beings, goes to dissolution

body.text:
tvaṃ sarvam etad bahudhaika eva
jagatpate kāryam ivābhyupetam
yad asti yan nāsti ca tat tvam eva
hare tvadanyad bhagavan kim asti
body.translated_text: You are all this, [though] one, in many [forms], O Lord of the world, [the world] presented as if [your] effect; whatever is and whatever is not, that too is you alone, O <s>Hari</s>; what is there, O Blessed One, other than you?

body.text:
kiṃtv īśa māyā bhavato nijeyam
āviṣkṛtāviṣkṛtalokasṛṣṭe
yayāham eṣo 'nyatamo mameti
madīyam asyābhivadanti mūḍhāḥ
body.translated_text: But, O Lord, this is your own <s>Māyā</s>, in the creation of the world both manifested and unmanifested, by which [the deluded say] 'I,' 'this is another,' 'this is mine'—the deluded speak of [things as] belonging to themselves

body.text:
tayā vimūḍhena mayābhanābha
na yat kṛtaṃ tat kvacid asti kiṃcit
bhūmyambarāgnisalileṣu deva
jāgratsuṣuptādiṣu duḥkhitena
body.translated_text: By me, deluded by that [Māyā], O lotus-naveled one, that which has not been done—[there is] not anything anywhere [I have not done], in earth, ether, fire, and water, O god, in waking, deep sleep, and the rest, [I] being made miserable

body.text:
na santi tāvanti jalāny apīḍya
sarveṣu nāthābdhiṣu sarvakālam
stanyāni yāvanti mayātighore
pītāni saṃsāramahāsamudre
body.translated_text: So many waters do not exist, [even] pressing out all the oceans at all times, O Lord, as the [streams of] breast-milk are which were drunk by me in the exceedingly terrible great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>

body.text:
saṃpac chilānāṃ himavanmahendra-
kailāsamervādiṣu naiva tādṛk
dehāny anekāny anugṛhṇato me
prāptāsthisaṃpan mahati yatheśa
body.translated_text: "The wealth of stones [accumulated] on the <s>Himavat</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Kailāsa</s>, <s>Meru</s>, and the rest is not such [in quantity] as the wealth of bones I have obtained, O Lord, while I have passed through bodies many beyond counting—[a heap] as great [as those mountains]"

body.text:
tvayy arpitaṃ nātha punaḥ punar me
manaḥ samākṣipya sudurdharo 'pi
rāgo hi vaśyaṃ kurute tato 'nu
lobhādayaḥ kiṃ bhagavan karomi
body.translated_text: "Offered to you, O Lord, again and again, my mind—seizing it forcibly, passion, hard though it is to bear, makes [it] subject [to itself]; thereupon follow greed and the rest; what, O Blessed Lord, am I to do?"

body.text:
ekāgratāmūlyabalena labhyaṃ
bhavauṣadhaṃ tvaṃ bhagavan kilaikaḥ
manaḥ parāyattam idaṃ bhave 'smin
saṃsāraduḥkhāt kim ahaṃ karomi
body.translated_text: "The medicine for [the disease of] existence is to be obtained, O Blessed Lord, by the price-power of one-pointedness—you alone, indeed; [yet] this mind is dependent on another in this existence; what am I to do amid the sorrow of <s>saṃsāra</s>?"

body.text:
na santi te deva bhuvi pradeśā
na yeṣu jāto 'smi tathā vinaṣṭaḥ
attā mayā yeṣu na jantavaś ca
saṃbhakṣito yaiś ca na jantusaṃghaiḥ
body.translated_text: "There are no regions on earth, O god, in which I have not been born and likewise destroyed, in which beings have not been eaten by me, and by whose hosts of beings I have not been devoured"

body.text:
siṃhena bhūtvā bahavo mayāttā
vyāghreṇa bhūtvā bahavo mayāttāḥ
tathānyarūpair bahavo mayāttāḥ
saṃbhakṣito 'haṃ bahubhis tataś ca
body.translated_text: "Having become a lion, many were eaten by me; having become a tiger, many were eaten by me; and likewise in other forms many were eaten by me; and I in turn was devoured by many"

body.text:
utkrāntiduḥkhāny atiduḥsahāni
sahasraśo yāny anusaṃsmarāmi
taiḥ saṃsmṛtais tat kṣaṇam eva deva
taḍid yathā me hṛdayaṃ prayāti
body.translated_text: "The pains of departure [from the body], most unbearable, which I recall in their thousands—by the recalling of those, at that very moment, O god, my heart goes [trembling] like lightning"

body.text:
tataś ca duḥkhāny anivāraṇāni
yantrāgniśastraughasamudbhavāni
bhavanti yāny acyuta nārakānāṃ
tāny eva teṣām upamānamātram
body.translated_text: "And then the pains, unwardable, arising from machines, fire, and floods of weapons, which there are, O <s>Acyuta</s>, of the hell-dwellers—those [past pains of mine] are but the very measure [the standard of comparison] for theirs"

body.text:
duḥkhāny asahyāni ca garbhavāse
viṇmūtramadhye 'tinipīḍitasya
bhavanti yāni cyavataś ca garbhāt
teṣāṃ svarūpaṃ gadituṃ na śakyam
body.translated_text: "And the unbearable pains in the womb-dwelling, of one greatly oppressed amid feces and urine, and those which there are of one slipping forth from the womb—their nature is not possible to tell"

body.text:
duḥkhāni bāleṣu mahanti nātha
kaumārake yauvaninaś ca puṃsaḥ
jvarātisārākṣirugādikāni
samastaduḥkhālaya eva vṛddhaḥ
body.translated_text: "Great are the pains in childhood, O Lord, in boyhood, and of a man in his youth—fever, dysentery, eye-disease, and the like; the aged man is the very abode of all pains"

body.text:
karoti karmācyuta tatkṣaṇena
pāpaṃ naraḥ kāyamanovacobhiḥ
yasyābdalakṣair api nāntam eti
śastrādiyantrāgninipīḍaneṣu
body.translated_text: "A man, O <s>Acyuta</s>, performs in a moment, by body, mind, and speech, a sinful deed of which one does not reach the end even in hundreds of thousands of years, amid the oppressions of weapons and the rest, machines, and fire"

body.text:
duḥkhāni yānīṣṭaviyogajāni
bhavanti saṃsāravihārabhājām
pratyekaśas teṣu narā vināśam
icchanty asūnāṃ mamatābhibhūtāḥ
body.translated_text: "The pains born of separation from what is dear, which arise for those who partake of the sporting of <s>saṃsāra</s>—at each of these men long for the destruction of [their] life-breaths, overcome by the sense of 'mine'"

body.text:
śokābhibhūtasya mamāśru deva
yāvatpramāṇaṃ na jalaṃ payodā
tāvatpramāṇaṃ na jalaṃ payodā
muñcanty anekair api varṣalakṣaiḥ
body.translated_text: "The tears of me overcome with grief, O god—as great a measure of water as the clouds, [even] they do not release in many hundreds of thousands of years"

body.text:
manye dharitrī paramāṇusaṃkhyām
upaiti pitror gaṇanāmaśeṣam
mitrāṇy amitrāṇy anujīvibandhūn
saṃkhyātam īśo 'smi na devadeva
body.translated_text: "I think the earth comes to a [countable] number of atoms, [as does] the entire counting of [my] parents; but the count of friends, foes, dependents, and kinsmen I am unable [to make], O god of gods"

body.text:
so 'haṃ bhṛśārtaḥ karuṇāṃ kuru tvaṃ
saṃsāragātre patitasya viṣṇo
mahātmanāṃ saṃśrayam abhyupeto
naivāvasīdaty atidurgato 'pi
body.translated_text: "So I, greatly afflicted—show compassion, you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to me fallen into the body [-net] of <s>saṃsāra</s>; one who has come to the refuge of the great souls does not sink, even though most fallen"

body.text:
parāyaṇaṃ rogavatāṃ hi vaidyo
mahābdhimagnasya ca naur narasya
bālasya mātāpitarau sughora-
saṃsārakhinnasya hare tvam ekaḥ
body.translated_text: "For the supreme resort of the diseased is the physician, and of a man sunk in the great ocean, the boat; of a child, the mother and father; of one wearied by the most dreadful <s>saṃsāra</s>, you, <s>Hari</s>, are the one [resort]"

body.text:
prasīda sarveśvara sarvabhūta
sarvasya heto paramārthasāra
mām uddharāsmād uruduḥkhapaṅkāt
saṃsāragartāt svaparigraheṇa
body.translated_text: "Be gracious, Lord of all, [self] of all beings, cause of all, essence of the supreme reality; lift me up out of this vast mire of sorrow, out of the pit of <s>saṃsāra</s>, by taking [me as] your own"

body.text:
dharmātmanām avikalāṃ tvayi nātha bhaktiṃ
śraddhāvatāṃ satatam udvahatāṃ vareṇya
kāryaṃ kiyan mama vimūḍhadhiyo 'dhamasya
bhūtvā kṛpālur amalām aja dehi buddhim
body.translated_text: "To the righteous, who bear unfailing devotion to you, O Lord, the faithful who ever uphold [it], O most choice one—what is [my] task, mine, of deluded mind, the lowest one? Becoming compassionate, O unborn one, grant [me] a stainless understanding"

body.text:
jñātvā yayākhilam asāram asāram eva
bhūtendriyādikam apāram amuktimūlam
māyāntareyam acalāṃ tava viśvarūpa
saṃmohitaṃ sakalam eva jagad yayaitat
body.translated_text: "by which, having known the whole [world]—the elements, senses, and the rest—to be sapless, sapless indeed, boundless, the root of non-liberation, [grant me to know] this unshakable inner-māyā of yours, O world-formed one, by which this whole world is deluded"

body.text:
brahmendrarudramarudaśvidivākarādyā
jñātuṃ na yaṃ paramaguhyatamaṃ samarthāḥ
na tvām alaṃ stutipatheṣv aham īśitāraṃ
stoṣyāmi mohakaluṣālpamatir manuṣyaḥ
body.translated_text: "<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, the sun, and the rest are not able to know you, the supreme most secret one; I am not able [to praise] you, the Ruler, on the paths of praise—I, a man of small wit muddied by delusion, shall [yet] praise [you]"

body.text:
yasmād idaṃ bhavati yatra jagat tathedaṃ
yasmiṃl layaṃ vrajati yaś ca jagatsvarūpaḥ
taṃ sargasaṃsthitivināśanimittabhūtaṃ
stotuṃ bhavantam alam īśa na kaścid asti
body.translated_text: "He from whom this [world arises], in whom is this world thus, in whom it goes to dissolution, and who is the form of the world—you, who are the cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction, there is no one able to praise, O Lord"

body.text:
mūḍho 'yam alpamatir alpasuceṣṭito 'yaṃ
kliṣṭaṃ mano 'sya viṣayair na mayi prasaṅgi
itthaṃ kṛpāṃ kuru mayi praṇate kileśa
tvāṃ stotum ambujabhavo 'pi hi deva neśaḥ
body.translated_text: "'This one is deluded, of small wit, of small good conduct; his mind is afflicted by sense-objects, not attached to me'—even so, show compassion to me bowed down, O Lord; for even the lotus-born [Brahmā] is not able to praise you, O god"

body.text:
yasyodare sakala eva mahīdhracandra-
devendrarudramarudaśvidivākarāgni-
bhūmyambuvāyugaganaṃ jagatāṃ samuhāṃ
stoṣyāmi taṃ stutipadaiḥ katamair bhavantam
body.translated_text: "He within whose belly is the whole assemblage of worlds—mountains, moon, Indra of the gods, Rudra, Maruts, Aśvins, the sun, fire, earth, water, wind, and sky—you, that one, with what words of praise shall I praise?"

body.text:
yasyāgnirudrakamalodbhavavāsavādyaiḥ
svāṃśāvatārakaraṇeṣu sadāṅghriyugmam
abhyarcyate vada hare sa kathaṃ mayādya
saṃpūjitaḥ param upaiṣyasi toṣam īśa
body.translated_text: "He whose pair of feet is ever worshipped by Agni, Rudra, the lotus-born [Brahmā], Vāsava [Indra], and the rest in [their] making of their own partial incarnations—tell [me], O <s>Hari</s>: how, worshipped by me today, will you, O Lord, come to supreme satisfaction?"

body.text:
na stotum acyuta bhavantam ahaṃ samartho
naivārcanair alam ahaṃ tava deva yogyaḥ
cittaṃ ca na tvayi samāhitam īśa doṣair
ākṣipyate kathaya kiṃ nu karomi pāpaḥ
body.translated_text: "I am not able to praise you, O <s>Acyuta</s>; nor am I, O god, worthy [enough] for worshipping you; and my mind is not concentrated on you—it is dragged off by faults, O Lord; tell [me], what indeed am I to do, [I who am] sinful?"

body.text:
tat tvaṃ prasīda bhagavan kuru mayy anāthe
viṣṇo kṛpāṃ paramakāruṇikaḥ kila tvam
saṃsārasāgaranimagnam ananta dīnam
uddhartum arhasi hare puruṣottamo 'si
body.translated_text: "So be gracious, O Blessed Lord; show compassion to me, [who am] without a protector, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; you are indeed supremely compassionate; you ought to lift up the wretched one sunk in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, O endless <s>Hari</s>; you are <s>Puruṣottama</s>"

body.text:
itthaṃ tena naravyāghra
stuto bhaktimatā tataḥ
saṃsārabandhabhītena
kṛṣṇaḥ pratyakṣatāṃ yayau
body.translated_text: Thus praised by him, O tiger among men, by that devout one, then, [by him] who feared the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> came to visible presence

body.text:
sa taṃ pratyakṣam īśānam
anantam aparājitam
devadevam uvācedam
anādinidhanaṃ harim
body.translated_text: He, to that visibly present Lord, the endless, the unconquered, the god of gods, <s>Hari</s> without beginning or end, said this—

body.text:
śirasā dharaṇīṃ gatvā
yatavākkāyamānasaḥ
parāpareśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ
jiṣṇum ādyam anopamam
body.translated_text: having gone to the ground with [his] head, restrained in speech, body, and mind, [to] the Lord of the higher and lower, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the victorious, the primordial, the unequalled:

body.text:
divyākṣarapadānanta
prasanno bhagavān yadi
tad deva dehi dīnāya
mahyam ekam imaṃ varam
body.translated_text: "O endless one [made] of divine syllables and words, if you, O Blessed Lord, are pleased, then, O god, grant to me, [your] wretched [devotee], this one boon"

body.text:
varaṃ varaya mattas tvaṃ
yat te manasi vartate
varārthināṃ dvijaśreṣṭha
nāphalaṃ mama darśanam
body.translated_text: "Choose a boon from me—whatever is in your mind; for those who seek a boon, O best of the twice-born, my sight is not fruitless"

body.text:
janmasaṃpaccitā deva
pāpasaṃpan mamākhilā
prayātu nāśam īśeśa
tvatprasādād adhokṣaja
body.translated_text: "O god, the whole wealth of sin of me, accumulated through [many] births, may it go to destruction, O Lord of lords, by your grace, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>"

body.text:
bhaktibhāvapareṇādya
manmayena dvijottama
yaḥ stuto 'smi kṣayaṃ pāpaṃ
tenaivākhilam āgatam
body.translated_text: "By you today, O best of the twice-born, intent on the disposition of devotion, [your mind] consisting of me, [I,] having been praised—by that itself the entire sin has come to destruction"

body.text:
asmatto varayehādya
dvijavaryāparaṃ varam
mayi bhaktimatām atra
loke kiṃcin na durlabham
body.translated_text: "Choose from us here today, O best of the twice-born, a further boon; for those who have devotion to me, here in this world nothing is hard to obtain"

body.text:
dhanyo 'smi sarvanāthena
yatkṛto mayy anugrahaḥ
tad ekam eva tvatto 'haṃ
varam icchāmi keśava
body.translated_text: "I am blessed by the Lord of all, in that favor was shown by you to me; that one boon alone I desire from you, <s>Keśava</s>"

body.text:
nirdhūtasarvapāpebhyo
nātha puṇyakṣayān mama
tvatparasyāstu govinda
mā punar dehasaṃbhavaḥ
body.translated_text: "For me, freed from all sins, O Lord, [and freed] from the destruction of [my] merit, [for me] devoted to you, O <s>Govinda</s>, may there be no further arising of a body"

body.text:
yad akṣaraṃ yad acalaṃ
vyāpi sūkṣmaṃ ca yat param
viśeṣāir aviśeṣaṃ ca
gaccheyaṃ tat padaṃ tava
body.translated_text: "That which is imperishable, that which is unmoving, all-pervading, subtle, and supreme, [free] from particularities and [yet] without particularity—may I go to that abode of yours"

body.text:
evaṃ bhaviṣyatīty uktvā
prasādasumukhas tataḥ
bhūpāla taṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ
gato 'ntardhānam īśvaraḥ
body.translated_text: Having said "So it shall be," then, of gracious face, O protector of the earth, the Lord went into invisibility from that best of the twice-born

body.text:
tatprasādād dvijaḥ so 'pi
tanmayas tadvyapāśrayaḥ
prakṣīṇakarmabandhas tu
prayātaḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: By his grace that twice-born one too, consisting of him, taking refuge in him, his bondage of <s>karma</s> exhausted, proceeded to the supreme abode

body.text:
evam akṣīṇapāpo 'pi
jagatām īśvareśvaram
vyapāśrito hariṃ yāti
pāpamuktaḥ paraṃ padam
body.translated_text: Thus, even one whose sin is not exhausted, having taken refuge in the Lord of the lords of the worlds, <s>Hari</s>, freed from sin, goes to the supreme abode

body.text:
etat tvayā nāvratine
na cāśuśrūṣave param
ākhyeyaṃ rājaśārdūla
yaś ca nārcayate harim
body.translated_text: This is not to be told by you, O tiger among kings, to one without vows, nor to one who is unwilling to hear, nor to one who does not worship <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
viṣṇubhaktāya dāntāya
vratine puṇyaśīline
kathanīyam idaṃ bhūpa
rahasyaṃ paramaṃ hareḥ
body.translated_text: To a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, self-restrained, of vows, of meritorious conduct—to him this is to be told, O king, the supreme secret of <s>Hari</s>

body.text:
bahuśo bhavatā proktaṃ
sāṃprataṃ ca yad īritam
śrotum icchāmi viprendra
tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: "Much has been declared by you, and what has now been told [as well]; I wish to hear, O lord of the twice-born, that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>"

body.text:
yatsvarūpaṃ yadādhāraṃ
yatpramāṇaṃ yadātmakam
sarvadhātuḥ padaṃ tan me
śrotum icchā pravartate
body.translated_text: "Of what nature it is, what its support, what its measure, of what essence—that abode of the supporter of all, I have an urge arising to hear"

body.text:
sādhv etad bhavatā pṛṣṭaṃ
pṛṣṭam ātmajñānasamāśritam
tat kathyamānam ekāgraḥ
śṛṇu viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam
body.translated_text: "Well [is] this asked by you, [a question] grounded in the knowledge of the self; that being declared—single-minded, hear the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>"

body.text:
yat tad brahma yataḥ sarvaṃ
yad sarvaṃ sarvasaṃsthitiḥ
agrāhyakam anirdeśyaṃ
tad eva bhagavatpadam
body.translated_text: "That which is <s>Brahman</s>, from which is all, which is all, the establishment of all, ungraspable, indefinable—that itself is the abode of the Blessed Lord"

body.text:
tatsvarūpaṃ ca rājendra
śṛṇuṣveha samāhitaḥ
viṣṇoḥ padasyāvyayasya
brahmaṇo gadato mama
body.translated_text: "And its nature, O lord of kings, hear here, concentrated, of the imperishable abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, [which is] <s>Brahman</s>—as I declare [it]"

body.text:
pradhānādiviśeṣāntaṃ
yad etat paṭhyate jagat
carācarasya tasyādyaṃ
paraṃ brahma vilakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: "That which is recited [as] this world, [extending] from <s>pradhāna</s> to the [last] particular—the primordial, supreme <s>Brahman</s> of that moving and unmoving [world], distinct [from it]"

body.text:
janmasvapnādirūpādi-
duḥkhādirahitaṃ ca yat
nopacaryam anirdeśyaṃ
svapratiṣṭhaṃ ca tat param
body.translated_text: "and which is free from birth, dream-states, and the like forms, [and] from sorrow and the rest, not to be [approached by ordinary] usage, indefinable, self-established—that is the supreme"

body.text:
kṣīṇakleśās tu saṃsāra-
vimuktipatham āśritāḥ
yoginas tat prapaśyanti
samarthā naiva coditum
body.translated_text: "But those whose afflictions are exhausted, who have resorted to the path of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>, the yogis, behold that; [yet even they are] not able to declare [it]"

body.text:
tat sarvaṃ sarvabhāvasthaṃ
viśeṣeṇa vivarjitam
paśyatām apy anirdeśyaṃ
yato vāgviṣaye na tat
body.translated_text: "That, [present] in all states of being, devoid of [any] particularity—even for those who behold [it], [it is] indefinable, since it is not within the province of speech"

body.text:
kurvanty ālambanatvena
yatprāptyarthaṃ ca devatāḥ
brahma prakāśate teṣāṃ
tad vareṇaiva sarvagam
body.translated_text: "And for the sake of attaining which the deities make [it] their support—for them <s>Brahman</s>, the all-pervading, manifests by that very boon [of grace]"

body.text:
pradhānādiviśeṣāntaṃ
yatraitad akhilaṃ jagat
tasyānantasya kaḥ śaktaḥ
pramāṇaṃ gadituṃ naraḥ
body.translated_text: "In which is this entire world, from <s>pradhāna</s> to the [last] particular—of that endless [Brahman], what man is able to declare the measure?"

body.text:
sūkṣmāṇāṃ tat paraṃ sūkṣmaṃ
sthūlānāṃ tan mahattaram
sarvavyāpy api rājendra
dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat
body.translated_text: "It is the supreme subtle of the subtle, the greater of the great; though all-pervading, O lord of kings, it is [both] far-standing and near"

body.text:
parāṅmukhānāṃ govinde
viṣayākrāntacetasām
teṣāṃ tat paramaṃ brahma
dūrād dūratare sthitam
body.translated_text: "For those averse to <s>Govinda</s>, whose minds are seized by sense-objects, for them that supreme <s>Brahman</s> stands farther than the far"

body.text:
na prāpnuvanti gacchanto
yato janmāyutair api
saṃsārādhvani rājendra
tato dūratare hi tat
body.translated_text: "Going, they do not attain [it], even in myriads of births, on the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>, O lord of kings; therefore it is farther than the far"

body.text:
tanmayatvena govinde
ya narā nyastacetasaḥ
viṣayatyāginas teṣāṃ
vijñeyaṃ ca tadantike
body.translated_text: "For those men who, [with mind] consisting of him, have laid their minds upon <s>Govinda</s>, abandoners of sense-objects—for them it is to be known [as] near"

body.text:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādāntaṃ
sarvato 'kṣiśiromukham
sarvataḥ śrutimal loke
sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: "With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side, possessed of hearing on every side, it stands, having enveloped all in the world"

body.text:
sarvendriyagunābhāsaṃ
sarvendriyavivarjitam
asaktaṃ sarvabhṛc cainan
nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca
body.translated_text: "appearing as the qualities of all the senses, [yet] devoid of all the senses, unattached, and [yet] the bearer of all, without qualities, and [yet] the enjoyer of qualities"

body.text:
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu
vibhaktam iva ca sthitam
bhūtabhartṛ ca taj jñeyaṃ
grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
body.translated_text: "undivided among beings, and [yet] standing as if divided; and that is to be known [as] the upholder of beings, the devourer [at dissolution], and the bringer-forth [at creation]"

body.text:
jyotiṣām api taj jyotis
tamasaḥ param ucyate
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ
hṛdi sarvasy adhiṣṭhitam
body.translated_text: "It is called the light even of lights, beyond darkness; knowledge, the knowable, attainable by knowledge, seated in the heart of all"

body.text:
tac cādyo jagatām īśaḥ
pareśaḥ parameśvaraḥ
parāparasvarūpeṇa
viṣṇuḥ sarvahṛdi sthitaḥ
body.translated_text: "And that [is] the primordial Lord of the worlds, the supreme Lord, the highest Sovereign; in the form of the higher and lower, <s>Viṣṇu</s> stands in the heart of all"

body.text:
yajñeśaṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ
kecid icchanti tatparam
kecid viṣṇuṃ hariṃ kecit
kecit keśavasaṃjñitam
body.translated_text: "Some wish [to know] that supreme [one as] the Lord of sacrifice, the sacrifice-Person; some [as] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, some [as] <s>Hari</s>, some [as] him named <s>Keśava</s>"

body.text:
kecid govindanāmānaṃ
puṇḍarīkākṣam acyutam
kecij janārdanaṃ tv anye
vadanti puruṣottamam
body.translated_text: "some [as] him whose name is <s>Govinda</s>, the lotus-eyed, <s>Acyuta</s>; but some [as] <s>Janārdana</s>, [and] others call [him] <s>Puruṣottama</s>"

body.text:
kecid viriñciṃ brāhmaṇam
abjayoniṃ tathāpare
śarvam īśam ajaṃ rudraṃ
śūlinaṃ cāpare nṛpa
body.translated_text: "some [as] <s>Viriñci</s> [Brahmā], the brahman, the lotus-born; and likewise others [as] <s>Śarva</s>, the Lord, the unborn <s>Rudra</s>, the trident-bearer, O king"

body.text:
varuṇaṃ kecid ādityam
indram agnim athāpare
yamaṃ dhaneśam apare
somam anye prajāpatim
body.translated_text: "some [as] <s>Varuṇa</s>, [some as] the sun, [some as] <s>Indra</s>, then others [as] <s>Agni</s>, others [as] <s>Yama</s>, [as] the Lord of wealth, others [as] <s>Soma</s>, [as] <s>Prajāpati</s>"

body.text:
hiraṇyagarbhaṃ kapilaṃ
kṣetrajñaṃ kālam īśvaram
svabhāvam antarātmānam
ātmānaṃ buddhirūpiṇam
vadanti nāmabhiś cānyair
anāmānam arūpiṇam
body.translated_text: "[as] <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, the field-knower, time, the Lord, [as] [one's own] nature, the inner self, the self in the form of the intellect; and by other names they call [him], the nameless, the formless"

body.text:
śrūyatāṃ tu naravyāghra
vedavedāntaniścayaḥ
yajñeśo yajñapuruṣo
puṇḍarīkākṣasaṃjñitaḥ
body.translated_text: "But let it be heard, O tiger among men, the determination of the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedānta</s>—the Lord of sacrifice, the sacrifice-Person, named the lotus-eyed,"

body.text:
tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ brahma
yato nāvartate punaḥ
sa eva rudraś candro 'gniḥ
sūryo vaiśravaṇo yamaḥ
body.translated_text: "that is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, from which one does not return again; he alone is <s>Rudra</s>, the moon, fire, the sun, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Yama</s>,"

body.text:
brahmā prajāpatiḥ kālaḥ
svabhāvo buddhir eva ca
kṣetrajñākhyas tathaivānyāḥ
saṃjñābhiḥ procyate budhaiḥ
body.translated_text: "<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, time, [one's own] nature, and the intellect too, and likewise the others named the field-knower—he is spoken of by [these] names by the wise"

body.text:
saṃjñā tu tasya naivāsti
na rūpaṃ nāpi kalpanā
sa sarvabhūtānugataḥ
paramātmā sanātanaḥ
body.translated_text: "But of him there is no [proper] name, nor form, nor conception; he is the eternal supreme self, [present in and] following upon all beings"

body.text:
ākhyātaṃ bhavatā brahmann
etad brahma sanātanam
yasmād utpadyate kṛtsnaṃ
jagad etac carācaram
body.translated_text: "This eternal <s>Brahman</s>, from which the entire moving and unmoving world is produced, has been declared by you, O <s>brahman</s>"

body.text:
kiṃtu kautukam atrāsti
mama bhārgavanandana
tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi
tvattaḥ saṃdeham uttamam
body.translated_text: "But there is here a curiosity of mine, O delight of [the line of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> [Bhārgava's son]; that supreme doubt I wish to hear [resolved] from you"

body.text:
yad etad bhavatākhyātaṃ
brahma brahmavidāṃ vara
pariṇāmo na tasyāsti
nirguṇaṃ sarvagaṃ yataḥ
body.translated_text: "This <s>Brahman</s> which has been declared by you, O best of the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>—of it there is no transformation, since it is without qualities [and] all-pervading"

body.text:
sanātanāt sarvagatāt
pariṇāmavivarjitāt
kathaṃ saṃjāyate kṛtsnaṃ
tasmād apaguṇād api
body.translated_text: "From the eternal, all-pervading, [Brahman] devoid of transformation, [and] also free of qualities—how is the entire [world] produced?"

body.text:
dvividhaṃ kāraṇaṃ bhūpa
nibodha gadato mama
nimittakāraṇaṃ pūrvaṃ
dvitīyaṃ pariṇāmi ca
body.translated_text: "There are two kinds of cause, O king—understand, as I declare [them]: the first is the instrumental cause, and the second is the [material] cause that undergoes transformation"

body.text:
yathā kumbhasya karaṇe
kulālaḥ prathamaṃ nṛpa
kāraṇaṃ pariṇāmākhyaṃ
mṛddravyam aparaṃ smṛtam
body.translated_text: As in the making of a pot, O king, the potter is the first cause—the one called the efficient—and the substance of clay is reckoned the other [cause], [the material, or that] called transformation

body.text:
dharmādharmādayas tadvaj
jagatsṛṣṭer mahīpate
kāraṇaṃ pariṇāmākhyaṃ
nimittākhyaṃ tu tat param
body.translated_text: Likewise <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the rest, O lord of the earth, are the cause of the world's creation called transformation [material], but that other [the Brahman] is called the efficient cause

body.text:
kāraṇaṃ kālagagane
yathā saṃnidhimātrataḥ
avikāritayā brahma
tathā sṛṣṭer nareśvara
body.translated_text: As [there is] a cause in time and space by mere proximity, so <s>Brahman</s>, by its changelessness, [is the cause] of creation, O lord of men

body.text:
ajñānapaṭalācchanair
ekadeśātmavṛttibhiḥ
anātmavedibhir jīvair
nijakarmanibandhanaiḥ
body.translated_text: By living beings veiled by the film of ignorance, whose self-functioning is [confined] to one region, who do not know the Self, bound by their own deeds,

body.text:
kurvadbhir nṛpate karma
kartṛtvam upacārataḥ
kriyate sarvabhūtasya
sarvagasyāvyayātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: performing action, O king, agency is figuratively imputed; it is imputed to [Brahman,] the all-pervading, imperishable-souled [Self] of all beings

body.text:
yataḥ saṃbandhavān ebhir
aśeṣaiḥ prāṇibhiḥ prabhuḥ
kartṛtvam upacāreṇa
tatas tasyāpi bhūpate
body.translated_text: Since the Lord is in relation with all these countless living beings, agency [is imputed] to him too figuratively, O lord of the earth

body.text:
bhedābhedasvarūpeṇa
tatra brahma vyavasthitam
tayoḥ svarūpaṃ nṛpate
śrūyatām ubhayor api
body.translated_text: There <s>Brahman</s> is established in a form of difference and non-difference; let the own-nature of both of those, O king, be heard

body.text:
anādisaṃbandhavatyā
kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetravidyayā
vyāptaḥ paśyaty abhedena
brahma tad dhy ātmani sthitam
body.translated_text: By the knowledge of the field [body], which is in beginningless relation [with the Self], the knower-of-the-field [individual self] is pervaded; he sees, by non-difference, that <s>Brahman</s> abiding in the Self

body.text:
paśyatv ātmānam anyatra
yāvad vai paramātmanaḥ
tāvat saṃbhrāmyate jantur
mohito nijakarmaṇā
body.translated_text: As long as the creature sees the Self elsewhere than [in] the Supreme Self, so long is it whirled about, deluded by its own deeds

body.text:
saṃkṣīnāśeṣakarmā tu
paraṃ brahma prapaśyati
abhedenātmanaḥ śuddhaṃ
śuddhatvād akṣayo 'kṣayam
body.translated_text: But one whose deeds are all exhausted perceives the supreme <s>Brahman</s> as not different from the Self, pure—through its purity, the imperishable [perceives] the imperishable

body.text:
bhedaś ca karmajanitaḥ
kṣetrajñaparamātmanoḥ
saṃkṣīṇakarmabandhasya
na bhedo brahmaṇā saha
body.translated_text: And difference, born of action, [is] of the knower-of-the-field and the Supreme Self; for one whose bond of action is exhausted there is no difference from <s>Brahman</s>

body.text:
upāsyopāsyakatayā
bhedo yair api kathyate
tau hi śuddhyartham icchanti
malānāṃ tad upāsanam
paro 'sāv apareṇātmā
saṃtyaktamamatena tu
upāsyate tadā so 'pi
tadbhāvaṃ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: And the difference which is stated by some [in terms] of worshipped and worshipper—they too desire that worship for the sake of purification, of the impurities; that supreme [Self] is worshipped by the lower self, [now] having abandoned the sense of mine—and then that [lower self] too attains the being of that [supreme Self]

body.text:
karmiṇāṃ karmabhedena
bhedād evādayo yataḥ
karmakṣayād aśeṣāṇāṃ
bhedānāṃ saṃkṣayas tataḥ
body.translated_text: Since, through difference of action, [there arise] the gradations of difference for the doers of deeds, therefore from the exhaustion of action [comes] the utter destruction of all the differences

body.text:
avidyā tu kriyā sarvā
vidyā jñānaṃ pracakṣate
karmaṇā jāyate jantur
vidyayā tu vimucyate
body.translated_text: But all action is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); knowledge they declare to be wisdom (<s>vidyā</s>); by action a creature is born, but by knowledge it is liberated

body.text:
advaitaṃ paramārtho hi
dvaitaṃ tadbheda ucyate
ubhayaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ
dvaitādvaitavibhedataḥ
tayoḥ svarūpaṃ vadato
nibodha mama pārthiva
body.translated_text: For non-duality is the supreme truth; duality is called the difference of that; both are the form of <s>Brahman</s>, through the distinction of duality and non-duality; as I tell the own-nature of those two, understand from me, O king

body.text:
devatiryaṅmanuṣyākhyas
tathaiva nṛpa tārakaḥ
caturvidho hi bhedo yo
mithyājñānanibandhanaḥ
body.translated_text: [The difference] called god, beast, and man, and likewise, O king, [that] which is the [un-real] crosser-over—the fourfold difference which is bound up with false knowledge:

body.text:
aham anyo 'paraś cāyam
amī cātra tathāpare
vijñānam etat tad dvaitaṃ
yad anyac chrūyatāṃ param
body.translated_text: 'I [am one], another [is], and this is yet another, and these [are here], and likewise others'—this cognition is that duality; what is other [than it], the supreme, let it be heard:

body.text:
mametyahamitiprajñā-
viyuktam avikalpavat
avikāram anākhyeyam
advaitam api bhūpate
body.translated_text: freed of the notions of 'mine' and 'I,' as if without [mental] construction, changeless, indescribable—[that is] non-duality, O king

body.text:
abhedena tavākhyātaṃ
yad etad brahma śāśvatam
jñānajñeyaikyasadbhāvaṃ
tad evādvaitasaṃjñitam
