body.translated_text: That eternal <s>Brahman</s> which has been declared to you by [the term] non-difference, whose true being is the oneness of knowledge and the knowable—that very [thing] is named non-duality

body.text:
yaś ca dvaite prapañcaḥ syān
nivartyobhayacetasaḥ
manovṛttimayaṃ dvaitam
advaitaṃ paramārthataḥ
body.translated_text: And the manifold-appearance (<s>prapañca</s>) that may be in duality is to be removed for one whose mind is [free of] both; duality consists of the functions of the mind, [but] non-duality [is the case] in supreme truth

body.text:
manaso vṛttayas tasmād
dharmādharmanimittajāḥ
nirodhavyās tannirodhād
dvaitaṃ naivopapadyate
body.translated_text: The functions of the mind, therefore, are born from the occasioning cause of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; they are to be restrained; from their restraint, duality does not arise

body.text:
manodṛśyam idaṃ dvaitaṃ
yat kiṃcit sacarācaram
manaso hy amatībhāve
dvaitābhāvāt tad āpnuyāt
body.translated_text: This duality—whatever there is, with its moving and unmoving—is the mind's object of vision; for when the mind comes to the no-mind state, through the absence of duality one would attain that [Brahman]

body.text:
mano hi viṣayaṃ yadvad
ādatte tadvad eva tat
bhavaty apāstaviṣayaṃ
grāhidharme ca jāyate
body.translated_text: For just as the mind takes on an object, so does it become; when its object is removed, it arises in the nature of the grasper [alone]

body.text:
agrāhi tac ca vidhṛtaṃ
yogināṃ viṣayaṃ prati
nirodhe yogasāmarthyād
brahmagrāhy eva jāyate
body.translated_text: And that [mind], non-grasping, held back from [its] object for yogins, in restraint—through the power of yoga it becomes a grasper of <s>Brahman</s> alone

body.text:
grāhyaṃ ca paramaṃ brahma
yogicittasya pārthiva
samujjhitagrāhyavṛttir
amalasya malaṃ mahat
body.translated_text: And the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is the [object] to be grasped by the yogin's mind, O king, [its] function of grasping [other] objects abandoned; the great impurity of the impure [is removed]

body.text:
kṣīṇakleśās tu saṃsāra-
vimuktipatham āśritāḥ
body.translated_text: But those whose afflictions are exhausted have resorted to the path of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>

body.text:
ye 'pi karmāṇi kurvanti
bhagavantam apāśritāḥ
kriyāyogaparā rājan
kāmākāṅkṣāvivarjitāḥ
brahmaniṣṭhā dhyānaparā
brahmaṇy eva vyavasthitāḥ
te 'pi tadbhāvam āyānti
vimuktipatham āśritāḥ
body.translated_text: Even those who perform actions, dependent on the Blessed One, devoted to <s>kriyāyoga</s>, O king, devoid of [the longing of] desires and wishes, fixed on <s>Brahman</s>, devoted to meditation, established in <s>Brahman</s> alone—they too attain the being of that [Brahman], having resorted to the path of liberation

body.text:
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti
samarthā naiva coditum
body.translated_text: The yogins perceive him, [yet] are not able to express [him]

body.text:
karmaṇo bhāvanā yeyaṃ
sā brahmaparipanthinī
karmabhāvanayā tulyaṃ
vijñānam upapadyate
body.translated_text: This conception which is of action—it is the adversary of <s>Brahman</s>; cognition [conditioned by action] arises equal to the conception of action

body.text:
tādṛg bhavato vijñaptir
yādṛśī karmabhāvanā
kṣaye tasyāḥ paraṃ brahma
svayam eva prakāśate
body.translated_text: Your cognition becomes such as is the conception of action; on the exhaustion of that [conception], the supreme <s>Brahman</s> shines forth of itself

body.text:
evam etan mayā bhūpa
yathāvat kathitaṃ tava
dvaitādvaitasvarūpeṇa
yathā brahma vyavasthitam
body.translated_text: Thus this has been duly told by me to you, O king—how <s>Brahman</s> is established in a form of duality and non-duality

body.text:
yathāvat karmaniṣṭhānāṃ
tatprāptiḥ kathitaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: And duly the attainment of that [Brahman] for those fixed on action has likewise been told

body.text:
svarūpaṃ brahmaṇaś coktam
ubhayatrāpi te pṛthak
vāsudevamayasyānyat
kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathayāmi te
body.translated_text: And the own-nature of <s>Brahman</s> has been told to you separately in both [aspects]; what else of him who consists of <s>Vāsudeva</s> shall I further tell you?'

body.text:
ākhyātaṃ bhagavan samyak
paraṃ brahma tvayā mama
viṣṇur eva jagaddhātā
yogināṃ vartate yataḥ
body.translated_text: 'The supreme <s>Brahman</s> has been rightly declared to me by you, O Blessed One; since <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, the world's creator, exists for the yogins,

body.text:
upāyas tasya yaḥ prāpto
viṣṇor īśasya bhārgava
advaitadvaitarūpasya
tan me vistarato vada
body.translated_text: the means by which he is attained—of <s>Viṣṇu</s> the Lord, O <s>Bhārgava</s>, of him whose form is non-duality and duality—that tell me in detail,

body.text:
yena janmajarāmṛtyu-
mahāgrāhabhavārṇavam
tvadvākyanāvam āruhya
muktitīram avāpnuyām
body.translated_text: by which, having mounted the boat of your speech, I may reach the shore of liberation [across] the ocean of [worldly] existence, [infested with] the great sharks of birth, old age, and death

body.text:
tan mama brūhi tattvena
prāpnuyāṃ yena tat padam
body.translated_text: That tell me in truth, by which I may attain that [supreme] state'

body.text:
bandhaḥ karmamayo hy atra
yathāmuktivighātakṛt
tasyāpagamane yatnaḥ
kāryaḥ saṃsārabhīruṇā
body.translated_text: 'The bond here, consisting of action, is what obstructs liberation; effort at its removal is to be made by one who fears <s>saṃsāra</s>

body.text:
suvarṇādimahādāna-
puṇyatīrthāvagāhanaiḥ
śārīraiś ca tathā kleśaiḥ
śāstroktais tacchamo bhavet
body.translated_text: By great gifts of gold and the rest, by bathing at holy fords, and likewise by bodily austerities declared in the <s>śāstras</s>, its [the bond's] appeasement would occur

body.text:
devatāstutisacchāstra-
śravaṇaiḥ puṇyadarśanaiḥ
guruśuśrūṣaṇāc caiva
pāpabandhaḥ praṇaśyati
body.translated_text: By praises of the deity, by hearing the holy <s>śāstras</s>, by holy sights, and by the service of the guru, the bond of sin perishes

body.text:
prapākūpataḍāgāni
devatāyatanāni ca
kārayan puruṣavyāghra
pāpabandhāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: Having water-sheds, wells, and tanks, and temples of the deity made, O tiger among men, one is freed from the bond of sin

body.text:
yoginām atha śuśrūṣāṃ
tathaivāvasathān nṛpa
kurvan pūrtāśritaṃ cānyat
pāpabandhāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: And performing the service of yogins, and likewise [providing] rest-houses, O king, and other [acts] grounded in [pious works of] charity, one is freed from the bond of sin

body.text:
viṣṇuḥ kṛṣṇo vāsudevo
govindaḥ puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ
ityādi vyāharan nityaṃ
pāpabandhāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, the lotus-eyed'—uttering this and the like ever, one is freed from the bond of sin

body.text:
viśvo viśveśvaro viśva-
vidhātā dhāma śāśvatam
viṣṇur ityādi ca japan
pāpabandhāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: 'The universe, the Lord of the universe, the disposer of the universe, the eternal abode, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'—muttering this and the like, one is freed from the bond of sin

body.text:
padmanābho hṛṣīkeśaḥ
keśavo madhusūdanaḥ
ityādi vyāharan nityaṃ
pāpabandhāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: '<s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>'—uttering this and the like ever, one is freed from the bond of sin

body.text:
nārāyaṇaś cakradharo
viśvarūpas trivikramaḥ
ityādi vyāharan nityaṃ
pāpabandhāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the discus-bearer, the universe-formed, <s>Trivikrama</s>'—uttering this and the like ever, one is freed from the bond of sin

body.text:
viṣṇau pratiṣṭhitaṃ viśvaṃ
viṣṇur viśve pratiṣṭhitaḥ
viṣṇur viśveśvaro viśvam
iti bhāvāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Viṣṇu</s> the universe is established, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established in the universe, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the Lord of the universe, the universe'—through this contemplation one is freed

body.text:
evaṃ saṃśāntapāpasya
puṇyavṛddhimato nṛpa
icchā pravartate pūṃso
muktidāyiṣu karmasu
body.translated_text: Thus, for the man whose sin is appeased and whose merit is increasing, O king, a wish arises toward the deeds that grant liberation

body.text:
muktidāyīni karmāṇi
niṣkāmena kṛtāni tu
bhavanti doṣakṣayakāḥ
puṇyabandhāt pramucyate
body.translated_text: The deeds that grant liberation, performed without desire [for fruit], become destroyers of fault; one is freed from the bond of [even] merit

body.text:
nityanaimittikānīha
karmāṇy uktāni yāni vai
teṣāṃ niṣkāmakāraṇāt
puṇyabandhaḥ praśāmyati
body.translated_text: Those daily and occasional deeds which are here declared—through their being done without desire, the bond of merit is appeased

body.text:
anekajanmasaṃsāra-
citasyāpi dṛḍhātmanaḥ
karmabandhasya śaithilya-
kāraṇaṃ cāparaṃ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: And hear another cause of the loosening of the bond of action, of one of firm self, though heaped up by the <s>saṃsāra</s> of many births:

body.text:
ahiṃsā nātimānitvam
adambhitvam amatsaram
titikṣā samadarśitvaṃ
maitryādau daṇḍasaṃyamaḥ
body.translated_text: non-injury, not being overly proud, freedom from hypocrisy, freedom from envy, forbearance, equal-mindedness, restraint of the rod [punishment] in friendliness and the rest,

body.text:
ṛjutvam indriyajayaḥ
śaucam ācāryapūjanam
puṇyastavādipaṭhanam
apaiśunyam akatthanam
body.translated_text: uprightness, conquest of the senses, purity, worship of the teacher, recitation of holy hymns and the rest, freedom from slander, freedom from boasting,

body.text:
viṣayān prati vairāgyam
anahaṃkāram eva ca
akāmitvaṃ manaḥsthairyam
adrohaḥ sarvajantuṣu
body.translated_text: dispassion toward sense-objects, and freedom from egoism, desirelessness, steadiness of mind, the absence of malice toward all creatures,

body.text:
avivādas tathā mūḍhair
amūḍhaiḥ praśnasatkathā
viviktadeśe 'bhiratir
mahājanavivarjanam
body.translated_text: freedom from dispute with the deluded, and good discourse and questioning with the undeluded, delight in a secluded place, the avoidance of crowds,

body.text:
sadbhiḥ sahāsya satataṃ
yogābhyāso mitoktitā
strībhartsotsavasaṃlāpa-
vivarjanam avekṣaṇam
body.translated_text: constant association with the good, the practice of yoga, measured speech, the avoidance of [idle] talk about the scolding and merry-making of women, [and] not gazing [at them],

body.text:
parayoṣidvilāsānāṃ
kāvyālāpavivarjanam
gītavāditanṛtteṣu
mṛdaṅgeṣv apareṣu ca
body.translated_text: the avoidance of poetic talk about the dalliances of others' wives, [non-attachment] in song, instrumental music, and dance, and in drums and the rest,

body.text:
asaktir manaso maunam
ātmatattvāvalokanam
tapaḥ saṃtoṣaḥ satyeṣu
sthitir lobhavivarjanam
body.translated_text: non-attachment, silence of the mind, the beholding of the truth of the Self, austerity, contentment, steadiness in truths, freedom from greed,

body.text:
tathā parigraho rājan
māyāvyājavivarjanam
asṛṅmāṃsādibhūtatvān
nijadehajugupsanam
body.translated_text: and likewise [moderation in] acquisition, O king, the avoidance of illusion and pretext, the disgust toward one's own body because of its being [made] of blood, flesh, and the rest,

body.text:
sarvāṇy etāni bhūtāni
viṣṇur ity acalā matiḥ
tatraivāśeṣabhūteśe
bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī
body.translated_text: the unshakable conviction that 'All these beings are <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' [and] in him alone, the Lord of all beings, unswerving devotion

body.text:
ete guṇā mayākhyātā
manonirvṛtikārakāḥ
śaithilyahetavaś caite
karmabandhasya pūrthiva
body.translated_text: These qualities have been declared by me, the producers of the mind's repose, and these are the causes of the loosening of the bond of action, O king

body.text:
ebhiḥ śāntiṃ gate citte
dhyānākṛṣṭaḥ sthito hariḥ
śamaṃ nayati karmāṇi
sitamiśrāsitāni vai
body.translated_text: When the mind has reached tranquility through these, <s>Hari</s>, drawn by [their] meditation, abiding [in it], leads to appeasement the deeds—the white, the mixed, and the black indeed

body.text:
bhūyaś ca śṛṇu śāstrārthaṃ
saṃkṣepād vadato mama
yathā saṃprāpyate muktir
manujendra mumukṣubhiḥ
body.translated_text: And hear further the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s>, as I tell it in brief—how liberation is attained, O lord of men, by those desiring liberation:

body.text:
nityanaimittikānāṃ tu
niṣkāmasya hi yā kriyā
nisiddhānāṃ sakāmānāṃ
tathaivākaraṇaṃ nṛpa
body.translated_text: the action of the daily and occasional [rites] that is without desire, and likewise the non-performance of the forbidden and the desire-prompted [rites], O king,

body.text:
sarveśvare ca govinde
bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī
prayacchati nṛṇāṃ muktiṃ
mā te bhūd atra saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: and unswerving devotion to the Lord of all, <s>Govinda</s>—[these] grant liberation to men; let there be no doubt of yours in this

body.text:
ākhyātam etad akhilaṃ
yat pṛṣṭo 'si mayā dvija
jāyate śamakāmānāṃ
praśamaḥ karmaṇāṃ yathā
body.translated_text: This has been declared entirely, what you asked of me, O twice-born—how, for those desiring appeasement, the appeasement of [their] deeds [comes about]'

body.text:
kiṃtv atra bhavatā proktā
praśāntiḥ sarvakarmaṇām
nātyantanāśaḥ śāntānām
udbhavo bhavitā punaḥ
nijakāraṇam āsādya
stokasyāgner yathā tṛṇam
body.translated_text: 'But here the appeasement of all deeds has been declared by you, [yet] not the utter destruction of the appeased [deeds]; [their] arising will [occur] again, having reached their own cause, as straw [reaches] a small fire

body.text:
tad ācakṣva mahābhāga
prasādasumukho mama
saṃkṣayo yena bhavati
mūlodvartena karmaṇām
body.translated_text: Therefore declare, O greatly fortunate one, gracious-faced toward me, that by which there is the utter destruction of deeds, by uprooting [them] from the root'

body.text:
na karmaṇāṃ kṣayo bhūpa
janmanām ayutair api
karmakṣayam ṛte yogād
yogāgniḥ kṣapayet param
body.translated_text: 'There is no destruction of deeds, O king, even through ten thousand births; without the destruction of deeds—[which comes] from yoga—the fire of yoga would destroy [them] supremely

body.text:
taṃ yogaṃ mama viprarṣe
praṇatasyābhiyācataḥ
tvam ācakṣva kṣayo yena
jāyate 'khilakarmaṇām
body.translated_text: That yoga, O sage among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, [tell] me, who am bowed and entreating you—do you declare it, by which there is the destruction of all deeds

body.text:
hiraṇyagarbho bhagavān
anādir munibhiḥ purā
pṛṣṭaḥ provāca yaṃ yogaṃ
taṃ samāsena me śṛṇu
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the beginningless one, asked of old by the sages, declared a certain yoga—hear that from me in brief

body.text:
anādikālaprasṛtā
yathā vidyā mahīpate
tathā tatkṣayahetutvād
yogo vidyāmayo 'vyayaḥ
body.translated_text: As ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is spread out from beginningless time, O lord of the earth, so yoga, consisting of knowledge, imperishable, [exists], being the cause of the destruction of that [ignorance]

body.text:
taṃ paraṃparayā śrutvā
munayo 'tra dayālavaḥ
prakāśayanti bhūtānām
upakāracikīrṣavaḥ
body.translated_text: Having heard that [yoga] through the [teacher-]succession, the sages here, compassionate, reveal it, desiring to do benefit to beings

body.text:
devā maharṣayo rājaṃs
tathā rājarṣayo 'khilāḥ
śreyo'rthinaḥ purā jagmuḥ
śaraṇaṃ kapilaṃ kila
body.translated_text: The gods, the great seers, O king, and likewise all the royal seers, desiring the highest good, of old went, indeed, for refuge to <s>Kapila</s>

body.text:
te tam ūcur bhavān nityaṃ
dayāluḥ sarvajantuṣu
so 'smān uddhara saṃmagnān
itaḥ saṃsārakardamāt
body.translated_text: They said to him: 'You are ever compassionate toward all creatures; lift us up, sunk [as we are], from this mire of <s>saṃsāra</s>

body.text:
yac chreyaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ
strīṇām apy upakārakam
yasmāt parataraṃ nānyac
śreyas tad brūhi naḥ prabho
body.translated_text: That which is the highest good of all classes, and beneficial even to women, than which there is nothing else higher—that highest good tell us, O Lord

body.text:
ādāv ante ca madhye ca
nṝṇāṃ yad upakārakam
api kīṭapataṃgānāṃ
tan naḥ śreyaḥ paraṃ vada
body.translated_text: That which is beneficial to men at the beginning, at the end, and in the middle, and even to worms and insects—that, our supreme good, declare'

body.text:
ity uktaḥ kapilaḥ sarvair
devair devarṣibhis tathā
nāsti yogāt paraṃ śreyaḥ
kiṃcid ity uktavān purā
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by all the gods and the divine seers, <s>Kapila</s> of old said: 'There is no good higher than yoga whatever'

body.text:
yathā janmāyutaiḥ kleśāḥ
sthairyaṃ cetasy upāgatāḥ
tacchāntaye tathā yogo
bahujanmārjito bhavet
body.translated_text: Just as the afflictions, through ten thousand births, have come to steadiness in the mind, so for their appeasement yoga must be acquired through many births

body.text:
sa evābhyasatāṃ nṝṇāṃ
tīvrasaṃvegicetasām
āsannatāṃ prayāty āśu
viṣṇuḥ saṃnyastakarmaṇām
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> comes swiftly to nearness to those very men who practice [it], whose minds are of fierce ardour, who have renounced action

body.text:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ
strīśūdrasya ca pāvanam
śāntaye karmaṇāṃ nānyad
yogād asti hi muktaye
body.translated_text: It is the purifier of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, and <s>vaiśya</s>, and of woman and <s>śūdra</s>; for the appeasement of deeds, for liberation, there is nothing other than yoga

body.text:
abhyastaṃ janmabhir naikaiḥ
śubhajātibhaveṣu yat
yogasvarūpaṃ tat teṣāṃ
strīśūdratve vyavasthitam
body.translated_text: That nature of yoga which has been practiced through not a few births in [their] good-class existences—that, for those [now] established in womanhood or śūdrahood,

body.text:
yogābhyāso nṛṇāṃ yeṣāṃ
nāsti janmāntarāhṛtaḥ
yogasya prāptaye teṣāṃ
śūdravaiśyādikaḥ kramaḥ
body.translated_text: [remains latent]; those men who have no practice of yoga brought from another birth—for them, for the attainment of yoga, [there is] the sequence beginning with śūdrahood and vaiśyahood

body.text:
strītvāc chūdratvam abhyeti
tato vaiśyatvam āpnuyāt
tataś ca kṣatriyo vipraḥ
kriyāhīnas tato bhavet
body.translated_text: From womanhood one comes to śūdrahood, then would attain vaiśyahood, and then [becomes] a <s>kṣatriya</s>, [then] a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, then becomes one devoid of [interested] action,

body.text:
anūcānas tathā yajvī
karmanyāsī tataḥ param
tato jñānitvam abhyetya
yogī muktiṃ kramāl labhet
body.translated_text: then learned [in the Veda] and a sacrificer, then beyond that a renouncer of action; then, having come to the state of a knower, the yogin gradually attains liberation

body.text:
yeṣāṃ tu jātimātreṇa
yogābhyāsas tirohitaḥ
āste tatraiva mucyante
jātihetau kṣayaṃgate
body.translated_text: But those whose practice of yoga is [merely] hidden by their birth-[condition] alone—it abides there itself; they are liberated when the cause [conditioning their] birth has gone to destruction

body.text:
asatkarma kṛtaṃ pūrvam
asajjātipradāyi yat
tasmin yogāgninā dagdhe
tasya jāter balaṃ kutaḥ
body.translated_text: The bad action done before, which gave [them] a bad birth—when that has been burned by the fire of yoga, whence [comes] the force of that birth?

body.text:
yathā vāteritaḥ kakṣaṃ
dahaty ūrdhvaśikho 'nalaḥ
sarvakarmāṇi yogāgnir
bhasmasāt kurute tathā
body.translated_text: Just as fire with upward flame, fanned by the wind, burns the bush, so the fire of yoga reduces all deeds to ashes

body.text:
yathā dagdhatuṣaṃ bījam
abījatvān na jāyate
yogadagdhais tathā kleśair
nātmā saṃjāyate punaḥ
body.translated_text: As a seed whose husk is burnt does not sprout, from its seedlessness, so, when the afflictions are burnt by <s>yoga</s>, the self is not born again.

body.text:
adṛṣṭā dṛṣṭatattvānāṃ
yogināṃ yogavicyutiḥ
yeṣāṃ bhavati yogitvaṃ
prāpnuvantīha te punaḥ
body.translated_text: Unseen [in its cause] is the falling-from-<s>yoga</s> of <s>yogins</s> who have seen the truth; those who have the state of <s>yogin</s> attain it again here.

body.text:
sajjātiprāpakaṃ karma
kṛtaṃ tena tadātmanā
jātiṃ prayānti viprādyā
yogakarmānurañjitāḥ
body.translated_text: An action that brings [rebirth in] a good birth has been done by that self; <s>vipras</s> and the rest attain [their good] birth, colored by [their former] <s>yoga</s>-action.

body.text:
tatrāpy anekajanmottha-
yogābhyāsānurañjitāḥ
tenaivābhyāsayogena
hriyante tattvavidyayā
body.translated_text: There too, colored by the practice of <s>yoga</s> arisen in many [former] births, by that very practice of <s>yoga</s> they are drawn [on] by the knowledge of the truth.

body.text:
jaigīṣavyo yathā vipro
yathā caivāsitādayaḥ
hiraṇyanābho rājanyas
tathā vai janakādayaḥ
body.translated_text: Just as <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> the <s>vipra</s>, and likewise <s>Asita</s> and the rest, [and] <s>Hiraṇyanābha</s> the royal one, and likewise <s>Janaka</s> and the rest;

body.text:
pūrvābhyastena yogena
tulādhārādayo viśaḥ
saṃprāptāḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ
śūdrāḥ pailavakādayaḥ
body.translated_text: by <s>yoga</s> practiced before, <s>Tulādhāra</s> and the rest, [who were] <s>vaiśyas</s>, attained the supreme success; [and] <s>śūdras</s>, <s>Pailavaka</s> and the rest.

body.text:
maitreyī sulabhā gārgī
śāṇḍilī ca tapasvinī
strītve prāptāḥ parāṃ siddhim
anyajanmasamādhitaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreyī</s>, <s>Sulabhā</s>, <s>Gārgī</s>, and the ascetic <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>, in [their] womanhood attained the supreme success, from concentration in another birth.

body.text:
dharmavyādhādayo 'py anye
pūrvābhyāsāj jugupsite
varṇāvaratve saṃprāptāḥ
saṃsiddhiṃ śravaṇī tathā
body.translated_text: And other [people], the hunter <s>Dharmavyādha</s> and the rest, from former practice, even in a despised, low-class state attained perfect success—and likewise <s>Śravaṇī</s>.

body.text:
pūrvābhyastaṃ ca tat teṣāṃ
yogajñānaṃ mahātmanām
suptotthitapratyayavad
upadeśādinā vinā
body.translated_text: And that <s>yoga</s>-knowledge of those great-souled ones, practiced before, [arose] like the recognition of one risen from sleep, without instruction and the rest.

body.text:
tasmād yogaḥ paraṃ śreyo
vimuktiphalado hi yaḥ
vimuktau sukham atyantaṃ
saṃmohas tv itarat sukham
body.translated_text: Therefore <s>yoga</s> is the supreme good, which gives the fruit of liberation; in liberation [there is] exceeding happiness, whereas the other [worldly] happiness is [mere] delusion.

body.text:
etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ
mayā manujakuñjara
śreyaḥ parataraṃ yogāt
kiṃcid anyan na vidyate
body.translated_text: All this has been told to you by me, O elephant among men; there is nothing else higher than the good [that comes] from <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
kathitaṃ yogamāhātmyaṃ
bhavatā munisattama
svarūpaṃ tu na me proktaṃ
śrotum icchāmi tad dhy aham
body.translated_text: The greatness of <s>yoga</s> has been told by you, O best of sages; but its nature has not been told to me—I wish to hear that indeed.

body.text:
dvaividhyaṃ nṛpa yogasya
paraṃ cāparam eva ca
tac chṛṇuṣva vadāmy eṣa
vācyaṃ śuśrūṣatāṃ satām
body.translated_text: There is a twofold nature of <s>yoga</s>, O king, the higher and the lower as well; hear that—I declare it, which is to be spoken to the good who desire to hear.

body.text:
yo dadyād bhagavajjñānaṃ
kuryād vā dharmadeśanām
kṛtsnāṃ vā pṛthivīṃ dadyān
na tattulyaṃ kathaṃcana
body.translated_text: He who would give the knowledge of the Blessed One, or make a teaching of <s>dharma</s>, or give the whole earth—[the latter] is in no way equal to that.

body.text:
kṣayiṣṇūny aparāṇīha
dānāni manujādhipa
ekam evākṣayaṃ śastaṃ
jñānadānam anuttamam
body.translated_text: Other gifts here are perishable, O lord of men; the one unsurpassed gift of knowledge alone is praised as imperishable.

body.text:
dānāny ekaphalānīha
trailokye dadatā satām
jñānaṃ prayacchatā samyak
kiṃ na dattaṃ bhaven nṛpa
body.translated_text: Gifts here are of single fruit; for the good who give in the three worlds, by [a man] rightly giving knowledge—what is not given, O king?

body.text:
jñānāny anyāny asārāṇi
śilpinīva nareśvara
ekam eva paraṃ jñānaṃ
yad yogaprāptikārakam
body.translated_text: Other knowledges are without essence, like the craftsman's [skills], O lord of men; the one supreme knowledge alone is that which brings the attainment of <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
ahaṃ vaktā bhavāñ śrotā
vācyo yogo vimuktidaḥ
prāṇinām upakārāya
saṃpad eṣā guṇādhikā
body.translated_text: I am the speaker, your honor the hearer, and the topic [is] <s>yoga</s>, the giver of liberation, for the benefit of living beings; this is a treasure surpassing in quality.

body.text:
pareṇa brahmaṇā sārdham
ekatvaṃ yan nṛpātmanaḥ
sa eva yogo vikhyātaḥ
kim anyad yogalakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: That oneness of the king's own self with the supreme <s>Brahman</s>—that very thing is renowned as <s>yoga</s>; what other definition of <s>yoga</s> [is there]?

body.text:
aparaṃ ca paraṃ caiva
dvau yogau pṛthivīpate
tayoḥ svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi
tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: Both a lower and a higher [yoga], two <s>yogas</s>, O lord of the earth; I shall tell their nature—hear that here, one-minded.

body.text:
sattāmātraṃ paraṃ brahma
viṣṇvākhyam aviśeṣaṇam
durvicintyaṃ yataḥ pūrvaṃ
tatprāptyartham athocyate
body.translated_text: The supreme <s>Brahman</s>, named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is mere being, without distinction; since it is hard to contemplate first [directly], it is now told for the sake of its attainment.

body.text:
vātālīcañcalaṃ cittam
anālambanam asthiti
sūkṣmatvād brahmaṇo rājann
agrāhy agrāhyadharmiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: The mind is fickle like a whirlwind, without support, without stability; from the subtlety of <s>Brahman</s>, O king, it is ungraspable, [Brahman] being of an ungraspable nature.

body.text:
samyag abhyasyato 'jasram
upavṛṃhitaśaktimat
janmāntaraśatair vāpi
brahmagrāhy abhijāyate
body.translated_text: But for one practicing rightly, ceaselessly, endowed with augmented power, even over hundreds of [further] births, [the mind] becomes able to grasp <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
yady antarāya doṣeṇa
nāpakarṣo narādhipa
yogino yogarūḍhasya
tālāgrāt patanaṃ yathā
body.translated_text: If, by the fault of an obstacle, there is no falling-away, O lord of men, of the <s>yogin</s> established in <s>yoga</s>—[else it is] like falling from the top of a palm tree.

body.text:
jñānaṃ prayacchatāṃ samyak
kiṃ vadatu bhaven nṛpa
body.translated_text: By [a man] rightly giving knowledge—what shall one say [is not given], O king?

body.text:
tad āpnoti paraṃ brahma
kleśena mahatā nṛpa
janmābhyāsāntarotthena
vijñānena samedhitaḥ
body.translated_text: He attains that supreme <s>Brahman</s> with great toil, O king, made to thrive by the special knowledge arisen from practice through [many] births.

body.text:
viṣṇvākhyaṃ brahma duṣprāpaṃ
viṣayākṛṣṭacetasā
manuṣyeṇeti tatprāptāv
upāyam aparaṃ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Viṣṇu</s> is hard to attain for a man whose mind is dragged off by sense-objects; hear, then, another means for attaining it.

body.text:
surūpāṃ pratimāṃ viṣṇoḥ
prasannavadanekṣaṇām
kṛtvātmanaḥ prītikarīṃ
suvarṇarajatādibhiḥ
body.translated_text: Having made a fair image of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, with gracious face and eyes, dear to oneself, of gold, silver, and the rest—

body.text:
tasyāś ca lakṣaṇaṃ bhūpa
śṛṇuṣva gadato mama
yaddravyā yatsvarūpā ca
kartavyā dhyānakarmaṇi
body.translated_text: and hear from me, O king, as I tell it, its characteristic: of what material and of what form it is to be made, in the work of meditation.

body.text:
suvarṇarūpyatāmrais tu
ārakūṭamayīṃ tathā
śailadārumṛdā vāpi
lekhyajāṃ vāpi kārayet
body.translated_text: One should have it made of gold, silver, copper, and likewise of brass, or even of stone, wood, or clay, or even painted.

body.text:
kāryas tu viṣṇur bhagavān
saumyarūpaś caturbhujaḥ
salilādhmātameghābhaḥ
śrīmāñ śrīvatsabhūṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: And the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be made of gentle form, four-armed, of the hue of a water-swollen cloud, glorious, adorned with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>,

body.text:
ābaddhamakuṭaḥ sragvī
hārabhārārpitodaraḥ
svakṣeṇa cārucipukaḥ
sulalāṭena subhruṇā
body.translated_text: wearing a bound diadem, garlanded, his belly bearing the weight of a necklace, with a fair chin [from] his good [features], with a fair forehead and fair brows,

body.text:
svoṣṭhena sukapolena
vadanena virājatā
kaṇṭhena śubhalekhena
varābharaṇadhāriṇā
body.translated_text: with a fair lip and fair cheek, with a radiant face, with a neck of auspicious lines, wearing excellent ornaments,

body.text:
nānāratnānatārtābhyāṃ
śravaṇābhyām alaṃkṛtaḥ
puṣṭaśliṣṭāyatabhujas
tanutāmranakhāṅguliḥ
body.translated_text: adorned with two ears bent down [under the weight] of various jewels, his arms full, joined [at the shoulder], and long, with slender copper-red nails and fingers,

body.text:
madhyena trivalībhaṅga-
bhūṣitena ca cāruṇā
supādaḥ sūruyugalaḥ
sukaṭīgulphajānukaḥ
body.translated_text: with a beautiful waist adorned with the folds of the three [belly-]lines, fair-footed, with a fair pair of thighs, with fair hips, ankles, and knees.

body.text:
vāmapārśve gadādevī
cakraṃ devasya dakṣiṇe
śaṅkho vāmakare deyo
dakṣiṇe padma suprabham
body.translated_text: On the god's left side [is to be] the mace, [as a goddess], the discus on his right; the conch is to be placed in the left hand, in the right a bright lotus.

body.text:
ūrdhvadṛṣṭim adhodṛṣṭiṃ
tiryagdṛṣṭiṃ na kārayet
nimīlitākṣo bhagavān
na praśasto janārdanaḥ
saumyā tu dṛṣṭiḥ kartavyā
kiṃcit prahasiteva ca
body.translated_text: One should not make the gaze upward, nor downward, nor sideways; the Blessed <s>Janārdana</s> with closed eyes is not praised; the gaze is to be made gentle, and as if somewhat smiling.

body.text:
kāryaś caraṇavinyāsaḥ
sarvataḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ
caraṇāntarasaṃsthā ca
bibhratī rūpam uttamam
kāryā vasuṃdharā devī
tatpādataladhāriṇī
body.translated_text: The placing of the feet is to be made well-established on all sides; and standing between the feet, bearing an excellent form, the goddess Earth (<s>Vasundharā</s>) is to be made, bearing the soles of his feet.

body.text:
yādṛgvidhā vā manasaḥ
sthairyalambhopapādikā
nṛsiṃhavāmanādīnāṃ
tādṛśīṃ kārayed budhaḥ
body.translated_text: And of whatever kind [it be] that is conducive to attaining the steadiness of the mind, the wise one should make such [a form] of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and the rest.

body.text:
brahma tasyāṃ samāropya
manasā tanmayo bhavet
tām ārcayet tāṃ praṇamet
tāṃ smaret tāṃ vicintayet
body.translated_text: Having placed <s>Brahman</s> upon that [image] with the mind, one should become made of it; one should worship it, bow to it, remember it, contemplate it.

body.text:
tām arcayaṃs tāṃ praṇamaṃs
tāṃ smaraṃs tāṃ ca cintayan
viśaty apāstadoṣas tu
tām eva brahmarūpiṇīm
body.translated_text: Worshipping it, bowing to it, remembering it, and contemplating it, [the man], his faults cast off, enters that very [image] which has the form of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
saṃkalpanakriyārūḍhaḥ
svarūpeṇa nṛpātmanaḥ
kurvīta bhāvanāṃ tatra
tadbhāvotpattikāraṇāt
nānyatra manasāneyā
buddhir īṣad api kvacit
body.translated_text: Mounted on the act of resolve (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), [the man], by his own nature, O king, should make contemplation upon it, because of [its] causing the arising of [oneness with] its being; the intellect is not to be led elsewhere by the mind even slightly, anywhere.

body.text:
yamaiś ca niyamaiś caiva
pūtātmā pṛthivīśvara
mūrtiṃ bhagavataḥ saṃyak
pūjayet tanmayaḥ sadā
body.translated_text: With self purified by the <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s>, O lord of the earth, one should rightly worship the image of the Blessed One, ever made of him.

body.text:
yamāṃś ca niyamāṃś caiva
śrotum icchāmi bhārgava
yair dhūtakalmaṣo yogī
muktibhāg upajāyate
body.translated_text: I wish to hear the <s>yamas</s> and the <s>niyamas</s>, O <s>Bhārgava</s>, by which the <s>yogin</s>, his sins shaken off, comes to be a partaker of liberation.

body.text:
ahiṃsā satyam asteyaṃ
brahmacaryāparigrahau
yamās tavaite kathitā
niyamān api me śṛṇu
body.translated_text: Non-injury (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truth, non-stealing, chastity (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possession—these <s>yamas</s> have been told to you; hear the <s>niyamas</s> too from me.

body.text:
saṃtoṣaśaucasvādhyāyās
tapaś ceśvarabhāvanā
niyamāḥ kauravaśreṣṭha
yogasaṃsiddhihetavaḥ
body.translated_text: Contentment, purity, self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), austerity, and contemplation of the Lord—[these are] the <s>niyamas</s>, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>, the causes of the perfecting of <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
ebhir mūlaguṇaiḥ sadbhir
viṣṇor bhaktimatas tathā
śraddadhānasya cānyāni
yogāṅgāni nibodha me
body.translated_text: By these good root-qualities, [in one] devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and faithful, learn from me the other limbs of <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
madhyamaprāṇam acalaṃ
sukhadāyi śubhaṃ śuci
yogasaṃsiddhaye bhūpa
yoginām āsanaṃ smṛtam
body.translated_text: With the breath in the middle [course], unmoving, happiness-giving, auspicious, pure—for the perfecting of <s>yoga</s>, O king, the posture (<s>āsana</s>) of <s>yogins</s> is remembered.

body.text:
prāṇāyāmas tridhā vāyoḥ
prāṇasya hṛdi dhāraṇam
kumbharecakapūrākhyās
tasya bhedās trayo nṛpa
body.translated_text: <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) is the holding of the breath of the air in the heart, threefold; its three divisions, O king, are named <s>kumbha</s> (retention), <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), and <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation).

body.text:
ete nibodha mātrās tu
nālambanaguṇānvitāḥ
sālambanaś caturtho 'nyo
bāhyāntarviṣayaḥ smṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Learn that these are [its] measures, endowed with the quality of having no [external] support; the fourth, another, with [external] support, is remembered as having outer and inner objects.

body.text:
indriyāṇāṃ svaviṣayād
buddhiḥ pratyekaśas tu yat
karoty āharaṇaṃ jñeyaḥ
pratyāhāraḥ sa paṇḍitaiḥ
body.translated_text: When the intellect, in each individual case, makes the withdrawing of the senses from their own objects—that is to be known as <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal) by the wise.

body.text:
śubhe hy ekatra viṣaye
cetaso yac ca dhāraṇam
niścalatvāt tu sā sadbhir
dhāraṇety abhidhīyate
body.translated_text: And that holding of the mind on a single auspicious object—because of [its] steadiness, that is named <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) by the good.

body.text:
paunaḥpunyena tatraiva
viṣaye saiva dhāraṇā
dhyānākhyā labhate rājan
samādhim api me śṛṇu
body.translated_text: By repetition upon that very object, that same <s>dhāraṇā</s> attains the name <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), O king; hear from me <s>samādhi</s> too.

body.text:
arthamātraṃ ca yad grāhye
cittam ādāya pārthiva
arthasvarūpavad bhāti
samādhiḥ so 'bhidhīyate
body.translated_text: And when the mind, taking the object alone in the thing to be grasped, O king, shines forth as if having the nature of [only] the object—that is named <s>samādhi</s> (absorption).

body.text:
kathitāni tavaitāni
yogāṅgāni kṛtais tu yaiḥ
utkarṣo jāyate vyastaiḥ
samastair heyasaṃkṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: These limbs of <s>yoga</s> have been told to you, by which, when performed separately, there arises exaltation, [and] when [performed] all together, the destruction of what is to be abandoned.

body.text:
yogāṅgāny aṅgabhūtāni
dhyānasyaitāny aśeṣataḥ
dhyānam apy avanīpāla
yogasyāṅgatvam archati
body.translated_text: The limbs of <s>yoga</s> are all entirely the constituent parts of <s>dhyāna</s>; and even <s>dhyāna</s>, O protector of the earth, attains the state of being a limb of <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
dhyānam ekavratānāṃ tu
kuśalākuśaleṣu tat
artheṣv āśaktim abhyeti
sarvadaiva nareśvara
body.translated_text: But the <s>dhyāna</s> of those of single vows—that, in regard to good and bad objects, comes to attachment to objects always, O lord of men.

body.text:
śubhāvyāvartitaṃ dhyānam
avivekasya jāyate
saṃsāraduḥkhadaṃ rājann
aśubhālambi tad yataḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Dhyāna</s> turned away from the auspicious arises for one without discrimination, the giver of the sorrow of <s>saṃsāra</s>, O king, since it has an inauspicious support.

body.text:
tad evākṛṣya duṣṭebhyo
viṣayebhyaḥ śubhāśubham
sarvasaṃsārakāntāra-
pāram abhyeti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: Drawing that very [meditation] away from the evil sense-objects, [whether] good or bad, a man comes to the far shore of the whole wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text:
duḥkhadāghapraśamane
yā cintāharniśaṃ nṛṇām
taddhyānam aviśuddhārthaṃ
sukhadānām apālane
body.translated_text: That thought which men have day and night for the quelling of the burning of sorrow—that is <s>dhyāna</s> of impure object, in [the matter of] not preserving the happiness-givers.

body.text:
kathaṃ saṃsārabandho 'yam
asmān muktiḥ kathaṃ tv iti
manovṛttir manuṣyāṇāṃ
dhyānam etac chubhaṃ dvidhā
body.translated_text: 'How is this bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and how [is there] release from it?'—this mental activity of men is auspicious <s>dhyāna</s>, [yet] twofold.

body.text:
śuddham apy etad akhilaṃ
lobhakāryatayānayā
sukhābhilāṣo yanmuktau
bandhuduḥkhādipīḍanāt
body.translated_text: Even this whole [meditation], though pure, [is tainted] by this [its] being an effect of greed—in that there is desire for the happiness in liberation, from the affliction of the sorrow of kinsmen and the rest.

body.text:
avāñchitaphalaṃ lobham
alobhāṃśavivarjitam
śubhāśubhaphalaṃ dhyānam
araktaṃ dviṣṭam iṣyate
body.translated_text: Greed of unwished-for fruit, free of any portion of [proper] non-greed—[such is impure]; <s>dhyāna</s> of good and bad fruit is desired [to be] unattached [and] unaverse.

body.text:
dṛṣṭānumānāgamikaṃ
dhyānasyālambanaṃ tridhā
na hi nirviṣayaṃ dhyānaṃ
mūḍhavṛttir iveṣyate
body.translated_text: The support of <s>dhyāna</s> is threefold: from perception, inference, and scripture; for <s>dhyāna</s> without an object is not desired, [it being] like the activity of a fool.

body.text:
prāk sthūleṣu padārtheṣu
tataḥ sūkṣmeṣu paṇḍitaḥ
dhyānaṃ kurvīta tatpaścāt
paramāṇau mahīpate
body.translated_text: First on gross objects, then on subtle ones, the wise one should make <s>dhyāna</s>, after that upon the atom, O lord of the earth.

body.text:
dhyānābhyāsaparasyaivaṃ
heyālambanabādhane
tacchāntaye tadvipakṣa-
bhāvanām eva bhāvayet
body.translated_text: For one intent on the practice of <s>dhyāna</s>, when there is harm from an abandonable support, for its quelling one should cultivate the very contemplation of its opposite.

body.text:
taccittas tanmayo jñānī
bhavaty asmān na doṣavat
kurvītālambanaṃ kāle
kasmiṃścid api pārthiva
body.translated_text: The knower, his mind on that, made of that, becomes [free] from it [the support], not faulty; he should make [his] support, at some time, on something or other, O king.

body.text:
ābrahmastambaparyanta-
jagadantarvyavasthitāḥ
prāṇinaḥ karmajanita-
saṃskāravaśavartinaḥ
body.translated_text: From <s>Brahmā</s> to a clump of grass, the living beings established within the world are subject to the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born of [their] action.

body.text:
yatas tato na te dhyāne
dhyāninām upakārakāḥ
avidyāntargatāḥ sarve
te hi saṃsāragocarāḥ
body.translated_text: Since [it is] thus, they are not helpers in the <s>dhyāna</s> of those who meditate; for all of them, being within ignorance, are within the range of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text:
paścād udbhūtabodhāś ca
dhyātā naivopakārakāḥ
naisargiko na vai bodhas
teṣām apy anyato yataḥ
body.translated_text: And meditators whose awakening has arisen afterward [i.e. acquired, not innate] are not helpers; for their awakening too is not innate, [coming] from elsewhere.

body.text:
tasmāt tad amalaṃ brahma
nisargād eva bodhavat
dhyeyaṃ dhyānavidāṃ samyag
yad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: Therefore that stainless <s>Brahman</s>, whose awakening is from its very nature, is rightly to be meditated upon by the knowers of <s>dhyāna</s>—that which is the supreme state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text:
na tad yajñair na dānena
na tapobhir na tad vrataiḥ
paśyanty ekāgramanaso
dhyānenaiva sanātanam
body.translated_text: Not by sacrifices, not by gift, not by austerities, not by vows do they behold that eternal one—[only] those of one-pointed mind, by <s>dhyāna</s> alone.

body.text:
tac ca viṣṇoḥ paraṃ rūpam
anirdeśyam ajaṃ sthiram
yataḥ pravartate sarvaṃ
layam abhyeti yatra ca
body.translated_text: And that is the supreme form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, indescribable, unborn, stable, from which the whole proceeds, and into which it comes to dissolution.

body.text:
anidram ajam asvapnam
arūpānāma śāśvatam
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti
jñānadṛśyaṃ sanātanam
body.translated_text: Sleepless, unborn, dreamless, formless, nameless, eternal—the <s>yogins</s> behold that one, the everlasting, seen by knowledge.

body.text:
nirdhūtapuṇyapāpā ye
te viśanty evam īśvaram
body.translated_text: Those whose merit and sin are shaken off—they thus enter into the Lord.

body.text:
tac ca sarvagataṃ brahma
viṣṇuḥ sarveśvareśvaraḥ
paramātmā paraḥ proktaḥ
sarvakāraṇakāraṇam
body.translated_text: And that all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of all lords, is declared the supreme Supreme Self, the cause of all causes.

body.text:
anantaśaktim īśeśaṃ
svapratiṣṭham anopamam
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti
bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
body.translated_text: Of infinite power, the Lord of lords, self-established, incomparable—the <s>yogins</s> behold that eternal Blessed One.

body.text:
yatra sarvaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ
yaḥ sarvaṃ sarvataś ca yaḥ
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti
bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
body.translated_text: In whom is all, from whom is all, who is all and [comes] from all—the <s>yogins</s> behold that eternal Blessed One.

body.text:
sargādikāraṇaṃ yasya
svabhāvād eva śaktayaḥ
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti
bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
body.translated_text: Whose powers, the cause of creation and the rest, [arise] from [his] very nature—the <s>yogins</s> behold that eternal Blessed One.

body.text:
nirdhūtapuṇyapāpā yaṃ
viśanty avyayam īśvaram
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti
bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
body.translated_text: Whom those of shaken-off merit and sin enter, the imperishable Lord—the <s>yogins</s> behold that eternal Blessed One.

body.text:
tatra yogavataḥ samyak
puruṣasya nareśvara
yad uktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tan me
gadataḥ śrotum arhasi
body.translated_text: There, of a man rightly endowed with <s>yoga</s>, O lord of men, the characteristic that is declared—you ought to hear it from me as I tell it.

body.text:
brahmaṇy eva sthitaṃ cittaṃ
sarvataḥ saṃnivartitam
nānyālambanasāpekṣaṃ
yoginaḥ siddhikārakam
body.translated_text: The mind established in <s>Brahman</s> alone, turned back from everything, not depending on another support—[that is] the bringer of success for the <s>yogin</s>.

body.text:
saṃsthānam avikāreṇa
cetaso brahmasaṃsthitau
nivāta iva dīpasya
yoginaḥ siddhilakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: The remaining of the mind without modification in establishment in <s>Brahman</s>, like [the flame] of a lamp in a windless place—[that is] the mark of the <s>yogin</s>'s success.

body.text:
evam ekāgracittasya
puṇyāpuṇyam aśeṣataḥ
prayāti saṃkṣayam ṛte
dehārambhakare nṛpa
body.translated_text: Thus, for one of one-pointed mind, merit and demerit entirely go to destruction, except that which brings about [the present] body, O king.

body.text:
dehārambhakarasyāpi
karmaṇaḥ saṃkṣayāvahaḥ
yo yogaḥ pṛthivīpāla
śṛṇu tasyāpi lakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: That <s>yoga</s> which brings the destruction even of the action that brings about the body, O protector of the earth—hear its characteristic too.

body.text:
yat tad brahma paraṃ proktaṃ
viṣṇvākhyam ajam avyayam
cetasaḥ pralayas tatra
yoga ity abhidhīyate
body.translated_text: That supreme <s>Brahman</s> which is declared, named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, unborn, undecaying—the dissolution of the mind into that is called <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
yogasevānirodhena
pralīne tatra cetasi
puruṣaḥ kāranābhāvād
bhedaṃ naivānupaśyati
body.translated_text: When, by the restraint [practiced] in the service of <s>yoga</s>, the mind is dissolved into that, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, from the absence of [any] cause, sees no difference [any longer].

body.text:
parātmanor manuṣyendra
vibhāgo jñānakalpitaḥ
kṣaye tasyātmaparayor
vibhāgābhāga eva hi
body.translated_text: The division of the supreme [Brahman] and the self, O lord of men, is fashioned by knowledge; on the destruction of that [knowledge], for the self and the supreme there is indeed the absence of division.

body.text:
paramātmātmanor yo 'yam
avibhāgaḥ paraṃtapa
sa eva paramo yogaḥ
samāsāt kathitas tava
body.translated_text: This non-division of the Supreme Self and the [individual] self, O scorcher of foes—that very thing is the supreme <s>yoga</s>, declared to you in brief

body.text:
yathā kamaṇḍalau bhinne
tattoyaṃ salile gatam
vrajaty aikyaṃ tathaivaitad
ubhayaṃ kāraṇakṣayāt
body.translated_text: As, when the water-pot is broken, its water goes into [the surrounding] water [and] passes to unity, so too do these two [selves] [become one] through the destruction of [their] cause

body.text:
yathāgnir agnau saṃkṣiptaḥ
samānatvam anuvrajet
tadākhyas tanmayo bhūtvā
gṛhyate na viśeṣataḥ
body.translated_text: As fire cast into fire goes to sameness, becoming of that name and made of that, [and] is not grasped as distinct,

body.text:
evaṃ brahmātmanor yogād
akatvam upapannayoḥ
na bhedaḥ kalaśākāśa-
nabhasor iva jāyate
body.translated_text: so, through the union of <s>Brahman</s> and the self, of the two arrived at oneness, no difference arises, as [there is none] between the space-in-a-pot and the [open] sky

body.text:
prakṣīṇāśeṣakarmā tu
yadā brahmamayaḥ pumān
tadā svarūpam asyokter
gocare nopapadyate
body.translated_text: But when a man, his every [trace of] action wholly destroyed, becomes made of <s>Brahman</s>, then his essential nature does not fall within the range of [verbal] expression

body.text:
ghaṭadhvaṃse ghaṭākāśaṃ
na bhinnaṃ nabhaso yathā
brahmaṇā heyavidhvaṃse
viṣṇvākhyena pumāṃs tathā
body.translated_text: As, at the destruction of a pot, the space-in-the-pot is not distinct from the [open] sky, so a man, at the destruction of [all] that is to be discarded, [becomes one] with <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
bhinne dṛtau yathā vāyur
naivānyaḥ saha vāyunā
kṣīṇapuṇyāghabandhas tu
tathātmā brahmaṇā saha
body.translated_text: As, when the bellows is broken, the wind [within] is not other than [the surrounding] wind, so the self, when the bond of merit and sin is destroyed, [is one] with <s>Brahman</s>

body.text:
tataḥ samastakalyāṇa-
samastasukhasaṃpadām
āhlādam anyam atulaṃ
kam apy āpnoti śāśvatam
body.translated_text: Then he attains some other, incomparable, eternal delight of all auspiciousness and all the wealth of happiness

body.text:
brahmasvarūpasya tadā hy
ātmano nityadaiva saḥ
vyuttānakāle rājendra
āste heyatirohitaḥ
body.translated_text: For then, ever indeed, of the self that is of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, O king of kings, at the time of [its] emergence [from worldly bondage], it abides with [all] that is to be discarded hidden away

body.text:
ādarśasya malābhāvād
vaimalyaṃ kāśate yathā
jñānāgnidagdhaheyasya
so 'hlādo hy ātmanas tathā
body.translated_text: As, from the absence of impurity, the clearness of a mirror shines forth, so is that delight of the self whose discardable [faults] have been burned by the fire of knowledge

body.text:
yathā na kriyate jyotsnā
malaprakṣālanādinā
doṣaprahāṇaṃ na jñānam
ātmanaḥ kriyate tathā
body.translated_text: As moonlight is not produced by the washing away of impurity and the like, so the removal of fault [as] knowledge of the self is not [newly] produced

body.text:
yathodupānakaraṇāt
kriyate na jalāmbaram
sadaiva nīyate vyaktim
asataḥ saṃbhavaḥ kutaḥ
body.translated_text: As, by the making of a well, the water-laden sky [-reflection] is not produced, [but] is ever [only] brought to manifestation—whence the arising of the non-existent?

body.text:
yathā heyagaṇadhvaṃsād
avabodhādayo guṇāḥ
prakāśyante na janyante
nityā evātmano hite
body.translated_text: As, from the destruction of the host of discardable [faults], the qualities such as awareness are [merely] revealed, not generated—they are eternal indeed in the welfare of the self

body.text:
jñānavairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ
dharmaś ca manujeśvara
ātmano brahmabhūtasya
nityam eva catuṣṭayam
body.translated_text: Knowledge, dispassion, lordliness, and <s>dharma</s>, O lord of men—of the self that has become <s>Brahman</s>, this fourfold [set] is eternal indeed

body.text:
etad advaitam ākhyātam
eṣa yogas tavoditaḥ
ayaṃ viṣṇur idaṃ brahma
tathaitat satyam uttamam
body.translated_text: This non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) has been declared, this <s>yoga</s> has been spoken to you; this is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, this is <s>Brahman</s>, and this is the supreme truth

body.text:
punaś ca śrūyatām eṣa
saṃkṣepād gadato mama
nānādvaikatvavijñāna-
svarūpam avanīpate
body.translated_text: And again let this be heard, as I declare in brief, [the teaching whose] nature is the discriminative knowledge of plurality and oneness, O lord of the earth

body.text:
ātmā kṣetrajñasaṃjño 'yaṃ
saṃyuktaḥ prākṛtair guṇaiḥ
tair eva vigataiḥ śuddhaḥ
paramātmā nigadyate
body.translated_text: This self, called the field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), joined with the qualities of primordial matter (<s>prakṛti</s>)—when those very [qualities] are gone, [it,] pure, is called the Supreme Self

body.text:
dhyeyaṃ brahma pumān dhyātā
upāyo dhyānasaṃjñitaḥ
yas tv etat karaṇeṣv āste
tadvarge kā vibhāgatā
body.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is the object of meditation, the man the meditator, the means is what is called meditation; but for him who abides in [pure] instruments [of unity], what division is there in that group [of three]?

body.text:
saṃkṣepād api bhūpāla
saṃkṣepan aparaṃ śṛṇu
putrāya yat pitā brūyāt
svaśiṣyāyāthavā guruḥ
body.translated_text: In brief too, O king, hear another brief [teaching], [such] as a father would speak to a son, or a guru to his own pupil:

body.text:
na vāsudevāt param asti kiṃcin
na vāsudevād gaditaṃ paraṃ ca
satyaṃ paraṃ vāsudevo 'mitātmā
namo namo vāsudevāya nityam
body.translated_text: There is nothing higher than <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and nothing declared higher than <s>Vāsudeva</s>; the supreme truth is <s>Vāsudeva</s> of immeasurable self; homage, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s> ever

body.text:
tasmāt tam ārādhaya cintayeśam
abhyarcayānantam atandritātmā
saṃsārapāraṃ param īpsamānair
ārādhanīyo harir eka eva
body.translated_text: Therefore worship him, contemplate the Lord, reverence the infinite one, untiring of self; by those who desire the supreme far shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>Hari</s> alone is to be worshipped

body.text:
ārādhito 'rthān dhanakāṅkṣakānāṃ
dharmārthināṃ dharmam aśeṣadharmī
dadāti kāmāṃś ca manoniviṣṭān
mokṣārthināṃ muktida eva viṣṇuḥ
body.translated_text: Worshipped, he gives wealth to those who long for wealth, <s>dharma</s> to those who seek <s>dharma</s>, [he] the all-righteous one, and desires fixed in the mind; and to those who seek liberation, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is verily the giver of release

body.text:
mamaitat kathitaṃ samyag
ātmavidyāśritaṃ mune
yat tv anyac chrotum icchāmi
tat prasanno vadasva me
body.translated_text: 'This has been rightly told to me, resting on the knowledge of the self, O sage; but that other thing which I wish to hear, that, being gracious, tell me

body.text:
yeyaṃ muktir bhagavatā
proktā varṇakramān mama
tatrecchāmi mune śrotuṃ
varṇād varṇottarocchrayam
body.translated_text: This liberation which was declared by your honor to me by the gradation of the classes (<s>varṇa</s>)—therein I wish to hear, O sage, the ascent from class to higher class

body.text:
śūdro vaiśyatvam abhyeti
kathaṃ vaiśyaś ca bhārgava
kṣatriyatvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha
brāhmaṇatvaṃ kathaṃ tataḥ
body.translated_text: How does a <s>śūdra</s> come to the state of a <s>vaiśya</s>, and a <s>vaiśya</s>, O <s>Bhārgava</s>, to the state of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, O best of the twice-born, [and] how then to brahminhood?

body.text:
vipratvān muktiyogyatvaṃ
yathā yāti mahāmune
tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi
tvatto bhārgavanandana
body.translated_text: How, from brahminhood, one comes to fitness for liberation, O great sage—that I wish to hear from you, O son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'

body.text:
tvadyukto 'yam anupraśnaḥ
kuruvarya śṛṇuṣva tam
mayocyamānam akhilaṃ
varṇānām upakārakam
body.translated_text: 'This further question is fitting for you, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>; hear it, [as it is] being told by me entirely, [as something] beneficial to the classes

body.text:
śūdradharmān aśeṣeṇa
kurvañ śūdro yathāvidhi
vaiśyatvam eti vaiśyaś ca
kṣatriyatvaṃ svakarmakṛt
body.translated_text: Performing the <s>śūdra</s>-duties entirely according to rule, a <s>śūdra</s> comes to the state of a <s>vaiśya</s>; and a <s>vaiśya</s>, doing his own duty, [comes] to the state of a <s>kṣatriya</s>;

body.text:
vipratvaṃ kṣatriyaḥ samyag
dvijadharmaparo nṛpa
vipraś ca muktilābhena
yujyate satkriyāparaḥ
body.translated_text: a <s>kṣatriya</s>, rightly devoted to the <s>dharma</s> of the twice-born, [comes] to brahminhood, O king; and a <s>vipra</s>, intent on good rites, is joined with the gaining of liberation

body.text:
sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ
svadharmam anuvartatām
sadocchritir nyūnakṛto
hāniś cotkṛṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: For all the classes who follow their own <s>dharma</s>, there is ever ascent; for one who falls short there is loss, and [also] for one who [usurps] a superior [class's] work

body.text:
teṣāṃ ca brāhmaṇādīnāṃ
varṇadharmān anukramāt
samucchritipradān rājan
gadato me niśāmaya
body.translated_text: And of those [classes] beginning with the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, hear from me as I declare, in order, O king, the class-duties that grant ascent:

body.text:
anasūyā dayā kṣāntiḥ
śaucaṃ maṅgalam aspṛhā
akārpaṇyam anāyāsas
tathānyaḥ sārvavarṇikaḥ
body.translated_text: Freedom from envy, compassion, forbearance, purity, [doing of] the auspicious, freedom from craving, freedom from miserliness, [acting] without [excessive] toil, and likewise the other [virtue] common to all classes—

body.text:
aṣṭāv ete guṇāḥ puṃsāṃ
paratreha ca bhūtaye
bhavanti kuruśārdūla
pṛthagdharmāṃś ca me śṛṇu
body.translated_text: these eight virtues of men are, for [their] welfare here and in the next world, O tiger of the <s>Kurus</s>; and hear from me the separate duties:

body.text:
yajñādhyayanadānāni
brahmakṣatraviśāṃ nṛpa
sādhāraṇāni teṣāṃ tu
jīvikākarma kathyate
body.translated_text: Sacrifice, [Vedic] study, and gifts, O king, [are common] to the brahmin, kṣatriya, and vaiśya; these are shared by them; but [their] livelihood-work is [now] declared

body.text:
yājanādhyāpanair vipras
tathā śastapratigrahaiḥ
bhṛtyādibharaṇaṃ kuryād
yajñāṃś ca vibhave sati
body.translated_text: A <s>vipra</s> should, by officiating at sacrifices and teaching, and by approved acceptance of gifts, support his dependents and the rest, and [perform] sacrifices when there is wealth

body.text:
bhṛtyādibharaṇe nālaṃ
svavṛttyā hi yadā dvijaḥ
tadā jīvet samālambya
vṛttiṃ kṣatriyavaiśyayoḥ
body.translated_text: When the twice-born is not able to support his dependents and the rest by his own livelihood, then he may live, relying on the livelihood of the kṣatriya and vaiśya

body.text:
saṃtyajeta samastāṃs tān
na kuryād vṛttisaṃkaram
āpatkāle 'pi viprasya
śūdrakarma na śasyate
body.translated_text: He should abandon all those [improper means]; he should not make a confusion of livelihoods; even in time of distress, the <s>śūdra</s>-work is not approved for a <s>vipra</s>

body.text:
prajānāṃ pālanaṃ samyag
vidhiḥ prathamakalpitaḥ
rājanyasya mahīpāla
śastrājīvena vā bhṛtiḥ
body.translated_text: The right protection of the people is the first-ordained duty of the kṣatriya, O lord of the earth; or [his] livelihood [may be] by living on weapons [warfare]

body.text:
tadutpannair dhanaiḥ kuryāt
samastāḥ kṣatriyakriyāḥ
tasyāpy āpadi vaiśyasya
yā vṛttiḥ sā vidhīyate
body.translated_text: With the wealth arising from that he should perform all the kṣatriya rites; for him too, in distress, the livelihood of the vaiśya is enjoined

body.text:
vāṇijyaṃ vaiśyajātasya
paśūnāṃ pālanaṃ kṛṣiḥ
dadyād yajec ca vidhivat
tadutpannadhanena saḥ
body.translated_text: Trade, the protection of cattle, [and] agriculture are [the work] of one born a vaiśya; he should give and sacrifice according to rule with the wealth arising from that

body.text:
dvijātijanaśuśrūṣāṃ
krayavikrayajair dhanaiḥ
śūdro yajet pākayajñair
dadyād iṣṭāni cārthinām
body.translated_text: A <s>śūdra</s> [should perform] service to the twice-born people; with wealth arising from buying and selling he should sacrifice with cooked-food sacrifices (<s>pākayajña</s>) and give the desired things to those who beseech

body.text:
tasmai śuśrūṣave deyaṃ
jīrṇavastram upānahau
chattrādikaṃ tathā kuryāt
samyagdharmopapādanam
body.translated_text: To that one [who is] of [serviceable] disposition, worn garments, sandals, a parasol, and the like are to be given; thus one should effect the right fulfillment of <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
caturṇām api varṇānāṃ
dharmas te kathito mayā
śṛṇuṣva ca mahīpāla
dharmam āśramiṇām ataḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> of all four classes has been told to you by me; hear now, O lord of the earth, the <s>dharma</s> of those in the [four] stages of life (<s>āśrama</s>)

body.text:
kṛtopanayanaḥ pūrvaṃ
brahmacārī guror gṛhe
guruśuśrūṣaṇaṃ kuryād
bhaikṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ
body.translated_text: Having had his initiation performed, first a <s>brahmacārin</s> in the house of his guru should do service to the guru, eating food obtained by begging

body.text:
nivedya gurave bhaikṣam
attavyaṃ tadanujñayā
guror bhuktavataḥ paścān
nātisvādumudāvatā
body.translated_text: Having presented the begged [food] to the guru, it is to be eaten with his permission; after the guru has eaten, [the pupil eats] not with [over-]relish or [over-]joy

body.text:
vahniśuśrūṣaṇaṃ kruyād
vedāharaṇam eva ca
guror arthe sadā toyaṃ
samidāharaṇaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: He should do service to the fire and the fetching of [fuel for] the <s>Veda</s>-[study]; ever, for the guru's sake, [he should fetch] water, and likewise the fetching of fuel-sticks,

body.text:
puṣpādīnāṃ ca kurvīta
supte tasmiñ śayīta ca
śayane ca samuttiṣṭhet
taṃ vrajantam anuvrajet
body.translated_text: and he should do [the gathering] of flowers and the rest; when [the guru] sleeps he should sleep, and at [the guru's] rising he should rise; he should follow [the guru] as he walks

body.text:
āhūtaś ca paṭhet tena
tanmanā nānyatomukhaḥ
vratāni caratā saṃyag
grāhyo vedo yatātmanā
daṇḍavatplavanaṃ snāne
śastaṃ nāsyāṅgaśodhanam
body.translated_text: And summoned by him he should recite, his mind on that, not facing elsewhere; the <s>Veda</s> is to be grasped by one properly observing the vows, of restrained self; the diving prostrate-like (<s>daṇḍavat</s>) is approved in bathing, [but] not the cleansing of his limbs [by scrubbing]

body.text:
adhītya vedān vedau vā
vedaṃ vāpi yathākramam
aviplutabrahmacaryo
gṛhasthāśramam āvaset
body.translated_text: Having studied the four <s>Vedas</s>, or two <s>Vedas</s>, or even one <s>Veda</s> in due order, [a man] of unbroken <s>brahmacarya</s> should enter the householder stage (<s>gārhasthya</s>)

body.text:
yatheṣṭāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā
gurave kurunandana
tato 'nujñāṃ samāsādya
gṛhasthāśramam āvaset
body.translated_text: Having given the desired fee to the guru, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>, then, having obtained [his] permission, he should enter the householder stage

body.text:
tenaivāntaṃ vrajet prājñas
tacchuśrūṣaṇatatparaḥ
vānaprasthāśramaṃ tasmāc
caturthaṃ vāpi saṃśrayet
yathākramaṃ vā kurvīta
vidhivad dārasaṃgraham
body.translated_text: By that [stage] the wise man may go to the end [of life], intent on its [proper] service; or from that he may resort to the forest-dweller stage (<s>vānaprastha</s>), the fourth too; or he may, in due order, duly perform the taking of a wife

body.text:
tatas tv arogikulajāṃ
tulyāṃ patnīṃ samudvahet
gṛhasthāśramavṛttyartham
avyaṅgāṃ vidhinā nṛpa
body.translated_text: Then he should marry a wife of disease-free family, his equal, for the sake of the householder-stage practice, unblemished, according to rule, O king

body.text:
ākhyātavarṇadharmeṇa
dhanaṃ labdhvā mahīpate
kurvīta śraddhayā yukto
nityanaimittikīḥ kriyāḥ
body.translated_text: Having gained wealth by the declared class-duty, O lord of the earth, endowed with faith, he should perform the regular and occasional rites

body.text:
abhyāgatātithīn bandhūn
bhṛtyādīn āturāṃs tathā
toṣayec chaktito 'nnena
vayāṃsy antyapaśūn api
body.translated_text: He should satisfy with food, according to his ability, arrived guests, kinsmen, dependents and the rest, and the sick, [and even] birds and outcaste animals

body.text:
ṛtāv upagamaś caiva
gṛhasthasyāpi śabditaḥ
dharmo dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha
yajñocchiṣṭaṃ ca bhojanam
body.translated_text: And approaching [the wife] in [her] season is declared the <s>dharma</s> even of the householder, O best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>, and the eating of the remnants of sacrifice

body.text:
havyena prīṇayed devān
pitṛn kavyena śaktitaḥ
manuṣyān annapānena
svādhyāyena rṣitarpaṇam
body.translated_text: He should gratify the gods with the <s>havya</s> offering, the ancestors with the <s>kavya</s> offering according to ability, men with food and drink, [and effect] the gratifying of the seers by [Vedic] self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>)

body.text:
kuryāc ca prīṇanaṃ nityaṃ
bhūtānāṃ balikarmaṇā
prajāpatiṃ sutotpattyā
hārdena sakalaṃ janam
body.translated_text: And he should ever effect the gratifying of [all] beings by the offering-rite (<s>bali</s>), of <s>Prajāpati</s> by the begetting of sons, [and] of all people by affection

body.text:
śubhena karmaṇātmānam
upadeśena cātmajān
anujīvijanaṃ vṛtyā
gṛhasthas toṣayet sadā
body.translated_text: By auspicious action [he gratifies] himself, by instruction his sons, the dependent folk by [their] livelihood—thus the householder should ever give satisfaction

body.text:
tathaivāparamānebhyaḥ
pradeyaṃ gṛhamedhinā
annaṃ bhikṣārthino ye ca
parivrāḍbrahmacāriṇaḥ
body.translated_text: And likewise to the other [mendicants] food is to be given by the householder—those who are seekers of alms, the wandering ascetics and the <s>brahmacārins</s>

body.text:
evaṃ gṛhāśrame devāḥ
pitaro munayas tathā
sarvakāmān prayacchanti
manuṣyāś ca supūjitāḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, in the householder stage, the gods, the ancestors, and likewise the sages and men, well honored, grant all desires

body.text:
gṛhasthas tu yadā paśyed
valīpalitam ātmanaḥ
apatyasya tathāpatyaṃ
tadāraṇyaṃ samāśrayet
body.translated_text: But when the householder beholds the wrinkles and grey hair of himself, and the offspring of his offspring, then he should resort to the forest

body.text:
pitṛdevātithīnāṃ tu
smṛtaṃ tatrāpi pūjanam
tathaivāraṇyabhogaś ca
tapobhiś cātmakarṣaṇam
body.translated_text: There too the worship of ancestors, gods, and guests is enjoined, and likewise enjoyment of the forest [produce], and the drawing of the self [toward liberation] by austerities

body.text:
brahmacaryaṃ mahīśayyā
homas triṣavaṇāplutiḥ
maunādikaraṇaṃ śastaṃ
jaṭāvalkaladhāraṇam
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmacarya</s>, sleeping on the ground, oblation, the triple-time ablution, the practice of silence and the like are approved, [and] the wearing of matted hair and bark-garments

body.text:
grīṣme pañcatapobhiś ca
varṣāsv abhrāvakāśikaiḥ
jalaśayyā ca hemante
bhāvyaṃ vananiketanaiḥ
body.translated_text: In summer with the five fires, in the rains [staying] under the open clouds, and a couch of water in winter—he is to dwell with the forest as his abode

body.text:
iṅgudairaṇḍatailena
gātrābhyaṅgāni ceṣyate
śyāmākanīvāramayaṃ
phalamūlaiś ca bhojanam
body.translated_text: And anointing of the limbs with <s>iṅgudī</s> and castor oil is desired, and the eating of <s>śyāmāka</s> and <s>nīvāra</s> [wild grains] and of fruits and roots

body.text:
apraveśas tathā grāme
vānaprasthavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
vānaprasthasya te proktaṃ
dharmalakṣaṇam āditaḥ
body.translated_text: And non-entry into a village—[such] is the recorded rule of the forest-dweller; the characteristic <s>dharma</s> of the forest-dweller has been told to you from the beginning

body.text:
āśramaṇaṃ tv aparaṃ bhikṣoḥ
śṛṇuṣva gadato mama
grāmaikarātrir vasatir
nagare pañcarātrikā
body.translated_text: Hear now from me as I declare the other stage, that of the mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>): a single night's stay in a village, a five-night stay in a town,

body.text:
sarvasaṅgaparityāgaḥ
kṣāntir indriyasaṃyamaḥ
vikālabhaikṣacaraṇam
anārambhas tathā nṛpa
body.translated_text: the abandonment of all attachment, forbearance, restraint of the senses, the begging-round at the off-hour, and likewise non-undertaking [of works], O king,

body.text: ātmajñānāvabodhecchā
body.translated_text: the desire for awakening to self-knowledge,

body.text: brahmacaryaṃ samādhinā
body.translated_text: <s>brahmacarya</s> through <s>samādhi</s>,

body.text:
ātmāvalokanaṃ caiva
bhikṣoḥ śastāni pārthiva
body.translated_text: and the beholding of the self—these are approved for the mendicant, O king

body.text:
caturthaś caiṣa kathitas
tava bhikṣor mayāśramaḥ
kramād vimuktikāmānāṃ
puruṣāṇām ayaṃ vidhiḥ
body.translated_text: And this fourth stage of the mendicant has been told to you by me; this is the rule for men desiring liberation in due gradation

body.text:
evaṃ tu varṇadharmeṇa
tathā cāśramakarmanā
nijena saṃpūjya hariṃ
siddhim āpnoti mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, having worshipped <s>Hari</s> with the class-duty and likewise with the work of [one's] stage of life, [each] his own, a man attains [spiritual] success

body.text:
brahmacārī gṛhasthaś ca
bhikṣur vaikhānasas tathā
kurvanto nijakarmāṇi
viṣṇum eva yajanti te
body.translated_text: The <s>brahmacārin</s> and the householder, the mendicant and the forest-dweller (<s>vaikhānasa</s>), performing their own duties, they worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone

body.text:
yato hi devatāḥ sarvā
brahmādyāḥ kurunandana
aṃśabhūtā jagaddhātur
viṣṇor avyaktajanmanaḥ
body.translated_text: For all the deities, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>, are portions of the upholder of the world, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of unmanifest birth

body.text:
viśve devā yato viṣṇur
viṣṇuḥ pitṛgaṇo yataḥ
devā yajñabhujaś ceśo
yataḥ pāpaharo hariḥ
body.translated_text: Since the <s>Viśvedevas</s> are from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, [since] <s>Viṣṇu</s> is [the source] from which the host of ancestors [comes], and the gods who eat the sacrifice, and the Lord [Śiva]—since [all are] from <s>Hari</s>, the remover of sin—

body.text:
viśve bhūtāni bhūtāni
yato viṣṇus tatharṣayaḥ
tataḥ sarvāśramāṇāṃ hi
pūjya eko janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: since [all] the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, and the beings [there are], are from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and likewise the seers, therefore the one to be worshipped of all the stages of life is the one <s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
sarveśvaraṃ sarvamayaṃ samasta-
saṃsārahetukṣayakāraṇeśam
varaṃ vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ variṣṭhaṃ
viṣṇuṃ kriyāvān yajate manuṣyaḥ
body.translated_text: The Lord of all, made of all, the Lord [who is] the cause of the destruction of the cause of all <s>saṃsāra</s>, the choicest, the most choice-worthy, the boon-giver, the most excellent—<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the man of [right] action worships

body.text:
yasyodare jagad idaṃ paramāṇubhūtaṃ
candrendrarudramarudaśvivasuprajeśaiḥ
sarvaiḥ sametam amitātmatanos tam ekam
abhyarcya viṣṇum abhivāñchitam asty alabhyam
body.translated_text: He in whose belly this world, become an atom, [exists] together with all—the moon, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and the lords of creatures—having worshipped that one <s>Viṣṇu</s> of measureless self and body, is there anything desired that is unobtainable?

body.text:
ārādhya yaṃ bhuvanabhāvanam acyutākhyam
aiśvaryam īpsitam avāpa patiḥ surāṇām
trailokyasāram amarārcitapādapadmam
ekaṃ tam eva harim arcayatārcanīyam
body.translated_text: Having worshipped whom—the world-creator called <s>Acyuta</s>—the lord of the gods obtained the desired lordship, the essence of the three worlds, his lotus-feet honored by the immortals—do you all worship that one venerable <s>Hari</s> alone

body.text:
yasyāṅghripadmagalitāmbhasi deva daitya-
yakṣādibhiḥ sakalapāpam apohya siddhiḥ
saṃprāpyate maraṇajanmajarāpahantrī
viṣṇor ajāt kathaya ko 'bhyadhikas tato 'sti
body.translated_text: In the water dropped from whose lotus-feet, the gods, <s>daityas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and the rest, having driven off all sin, attain perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), the destroyer of death, birth, and old age—tell [me], who is there higher than that unborn <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

body.text:
kamalajaharasūryacandraśakraiḥ
satatam abhiṣṭutam ādyam īśitāram
sakalabhuvanakāryakāraneśaṃ
puruṣatanuṃ praṇato 'smi vāsudevam
body.translated_text: Ever praised by the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Hara</s>, the sun, the moon, and <s>Śakra</s>—the first one, the Lord, the Lord of the cause and effect of all the worlds' works, of Person-body—I am bowed down to <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
śrutaṃ bhagavato rūpam
advaite yat tvayoditam
viṣṇor bhṛgukulaśreṣṭha
yac ca dvaite mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: 'The form of the Blessed One in non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) that has been declared by you, O best of the <s>Bhṛgu</s> family, [the form] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and [the form] in duality (<s>dvaita</s>) of the great soul—[I have] heard it

body.text:
avidyābhinnadṛgbuddhiḥ
puruṣo munipuṅgava
dvaitabhūte jagaty asminn
advaitaṃ bhāvayet katham
body.translated_text: A man, O bull among sages, whose vision and intellect are split by ignorance, in this world become [a place of] duality—how should he cultivate non-duality?

body.text:
krodhalobhādayo doṣā
ye mukteḥ paripanthinaḥ
vinivṛttirūpā yena
teṣāṃ yena vader ha tam
body.translated_text: The faults such as anger and greed, which are the obstructors of liberation—by what [means] they come to be of the form of cessation, [tell] me that here'

body.text:
sarveśvareśvareśasya
yac ca rūpaṃ hareḥ param
tac cāhaṃ śrotum icchāmi
tvatto bhṛgukulodvaha
body.translated_text: And that supreme form of <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of the lords of all—that too I wish to hear from you, O upholder of the <s>Bhṛgu</s> family

body.text:
samyak pṛṣṭam idaṃ bhūpa
bhavatā guhyam uttamam
dvaitādvaitakathālāpa-
saṃbandhād upakārakam
body.translated_text: Well asked is this, O king, by you—the supreme secret, helpful through [its] connection with the discourse on duality and non-duality

body.text:
purā dharmagṛhe jajñe
caturmūrtir nareśvara
devadevo jagaddhātā
paramātmā janārdanaḥ
body.translated_text: Of old, in the house of <s>Dharma</s>, was born, O lord of men, the four-formed god of gods, the Maker of the world, the Supreme Self, <s>Janārdana</s>

body.text:
jagataḥ pālanārthāya
durvṛttanidhanāya ca
svecchayā bhagavān viṣṇuḥ
saṃbhavaty eva bhūtale
body.translated_text: For the protection of the world and for the destruction of the wicked, the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> by his own will indeed comes into being on the earth's surface

body.text:
svarge vāpi bhūloke vā
bhuvarloke 'thavā vibhuḥ
yatra vā rocate tatra
cikīrṣur jagato hitam
body.translated_text: Whether in heaven, or in the earth-world, or in the <s>Bhuvarloka</s>, the all-pervading one—wherever it pleases [him], there, desiring to do the welfare of the world

body.text:
turīyāṃśena dharmasya
bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ
yadāvatāraṃ kṛtavāṃs
tadā taccaritaṃ śṛṇu
body.translated_text: When the Blessed source of beings made an incarnation by a fourth portion of <s>Dharma</s>, then hear his deeds

body.text:
naro nārāyaṇaś caiva
hariḥ kṛṣṇas tathaiva ca
viṣṇor aṃśāṃśakā hy ete
catvāro dharmasūnavaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Nara</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Hari</s>, and likewise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—these four sons of <s>Dharma</s> are indeed portions of portions of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
teṣāṃ nārāyaṇanarau
gandhamādanaparvate
ātmany ātmānam ādhāya
tepate paramaṃ tapaḥ
body.translated_text: Of them, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Nara</s>, on Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>, having placed the self within the self, practiced supreme austerity

body.text:
dhyāyamānāv anaupamyaṃ
svakāraṇam akāraṇam
vāsudevam anirdeśyam
apratarkyam ajaṃ param
yogayuktau mahāmaunam
āsthitau gurutejasau
body.translated_text: meditating on the incomparable, [his] own cause [yet] causeless, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, indefinable, unarguable, unborn, supreme; joined in yoga, abiding in great silence, of weighty splendour

body.text:
tayos tapaḥprabhāveṇa
na tatāpa divākaraḥ
vavau cāśaṅkito vāyuḥ
sukhasparśo hy asarkaraḥ
body.translated_text: By the power of their austerity the sun did not scorch, and the wind blew unanxious, of pleasant touch, free of grit

body.text:
śiśiro 'bhavad atyarthaṃ
jvalann api vibhāvasuḥ
siṃhavyāghrādayaḥ saumyāś
ceruḥ saha mṛgair girau
body.translated_text: Cool became, exceedingly, the fire-god, though blazing; lions, tigers and the rest, benign, roamed together with the deer on the mountain

body.text:
tayor gauravabhārārtā
pṛthivī pṛthivīpate
cacāla bhūdharāś celuś
cukṣubhuś ca mahābdhayaḥ
body.translated_text: Afflicted by the weight of their gravity, the earth, O lord of the earth, trembled; the mountains shook, and the great oceans were agitated

body.text:
devāś ca sveṣu dhiṣṇyeṣu
niṣprabheṣu hataprabhāḥ
babhūvur avanīpāla
paramaṃ kṣobham āgatāḥ
body.translated_text: And the gods, their splendour smitten in their now-dim abodes, became, O protector of the earth, [the gods] who had reached supreme agitation

body.text:
devarājas tataḥ śakraḥ
saṃtrastas tapasas tayoḥ
yuyojāpsarasaḥ śubhrās
tayor vighnacikīrṣayā
body.translated_text: Then the king of the gods, <s>Śakra</s>, terrified of their austerity, set the bright <s>Apsarases</s> [upon them] with the wish to make an obstacle for the two

body.text:
rambhe tilottame kuṇṭhe
ghṛtāci lalitāvati
umloce subhrupramloce
saurabhe 'pi madoddhate
body.translated_text: <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Tilottamā</s>, <s>Kuṇṭhā</s>, <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, <s>Lalitāvatī</s>, <s>Umlocā</s>, <s>Subhrū</s>, <s>Pramlocā</s>, and <s>Saurabhī</s> [excited] with passion,

body.text:
alambuṣe miśrakeśi
puṇḍarīke varūthini
vilobhanīyaṃ bibhrāṇā
vapur manmathabodhanam
gandhamādanam āsādya
kurudhvaṃ vacanaṃ mama
body.translated_text: <s>Alambuṣā</s>, <s>Miśrakeśī</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkā</s>, <s>Varūthinī</s>—[Indra said:] 'Bearing an alluring body, awakening the god of love, having reached <s>Gandhamādana</s>, do my bidding

body.text:
naranārāyaṇau tatra
tapodīkṣānvitau dvijau
tapyete dharmatanayau
tapaḥ paramaduścaram
body.translated_text: <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> there, the two twice-born endowed with the consecration of austerity, practice—the sons of <s>Dharma</s>—an austerity exceedingly hard to perform

body.text:
tāv asmākaṃ varārohāḥ
kurvāṇau paramaṃ tapaḥ
karmātiśayaduḥkhārti-
pradāvayatināśakau
body.translated_text: Those two, O fair-hipped ones, practicing supreme austerity, are bringers of grievous pain to us through the excess of [their] deeds, and destroyers [of our station]

body.text:
tad gacchata na bhīḥ kāryā
bhavatībhir idaṃ vacaḥ
smaraḥ sahāyo bhavitā
vasantaś ca varāṅganāḥ
body.translated_text: So go; no fear is to be entertained by you at this word; <s>Smara</s> [Kāma, the god of love] will be [your] helper, and <s>Vasanta</s> [Spring], O fair-limbed ones

body.text:
rūpaṃ ca vaḥ samālokya
madanoddīpanaṃ param
kandarpavaśam abhyeti
vivaśaḥ ko na mānavaḥ
body.translated_text: And beholding your beauty, supremely inflaming of love, what man, helpless, does not come under the sway of <s>Kandarpa</s> [Kāma]?'

body.text:
ity uktā devarājena
madanena samaṃ tadā
jagmur apsarasaḥ sarvā
vasantaś ca mahīpate
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by the king of the gods, then, together with <s>Madana</s> [Kāma], all the <s>Apsarases</s> went, and <s>Vasanta</s>, O lord of the earth

body.text:
gandhamādanam āsādya
puṃskokilakulākulam
cakāra mādhavo ramyaṃ
protphullavanapādapam
body.translated_text: Having reached <s>Gandhamādana</s>, thronged with flocks of male cuckoos, <s>Mādhava</s> [Spring] made [it] delightful, its forest-trees in full bloom

body.text:
pravavau dakṣiṇaḥ sadyo
malayānugato 'nilaḥ
bhṛṅgamālārutaravair
ramaṇīyam abhūd vanam
body.translated_text: At once the southern wind, [come] following [Mount] <s>Malaya</s>, blew; the forest became charming with the sounds and cries of swarms of bees

body.text:
gandhaś ca surabhiḥ sadyo
vanarājisamudbhavaḥ
kiṃnaroragayakṣāṇāṃ
babhūva ghrāṇatarpaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: And at once a fragrant scent, arising from the rows of forest [-trees], became a gratifier of the noses of the <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, serpents, and <s>Yakṣas</s>

body.text:
varāṅganāś ca tāḥ sarvā
naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī
vilobhayitum ārabdhā
varāṅgalalitaiḥ smitaiḥ
body.translated_text: And all those fair-limbed ones began to allure the two seers <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with charming, graceful smiles

body.text:
jagur manoharaṃ kāścin
nanṛtuś cātra cāparāḥ
avādayaṃs tathaivānyā
manoharataraṃ nṛpa
body.translated_text: Some sang ravishingly, and others there danced, and likewise still others, O king, played [instruments] yet more ravishingly

body.text:
hāvair bhāvaiḥ smitais trāsais
tathānyā valgubhāṣitaiḥ
tayoḥ kṣobhāya tanvaṅgyaś
cakrur udyamam aṅganāḥ
body.translated_text: With amorous gestures, emotions, smiles, and feignings of fear, and likewise others with sweet speech, the slender-limbed women made effort for the agitation of those two

body.text:
tathāpi na tayoḥ kaścin
manasaḥ pṛthivīpate
vikāro 'bhavad adhyātma-
pārasaṃprāptacetasoḥ
body.translated_text: Yet even so there was no alteration of mind in those two, O lord of the earth, whose minds had reached the far shore of the inner [Self]

body.text:
nivātasthau yathā dīpāv
akampau nṛpa tiṣṭhataḥ
vāsudevārpaṇe svacche
tathaiva manasī tayoḥ
body.translated_text: As two lamps standing in a windless place stand unshaken, O king, so were the minds of those two, pure in [their] dedication to <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
pūryamāṇo 'pi cāmbhobhir
bhuvam anyāṃ mahodadhiḥ
yathā na yāti na yayau
tathā tanmānasaṃ kvacit
body.translated_text: As the great ocean, though being filled with waters, neither goes nor went to [flood] another land, so their mind [went] not anywhere

body.text:
sarvabhūtahitau brahma
vāsudevamayaṃ param
manyamānau na rāgasya
dveṣasya ca vaśaṃgatau
body.translated_text: [They,] the benefactors of all beings, deeming [all] the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, consisting of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, came not under the sway of passion nor of hatred

body.text:
smaro 'pi na śaśākātha
praveṣṭuṃ hṛdayaṃ tayoḥ
vidyāmayaṃ dīpayutam
andhakāram ivālayam
body.translated_text: And then <s>Smara</s> [Kāma] too was not able to enter the heart of those two, [which was] consisting of knowledge, furnished with a lamp [of wisdom], like a darkened dwelling [now lit]

body.text:
puṣpojjvalāṃs taruvarān
vasantaṃ dakṣiṇānilam
tāś caivāpsarasaḥ sarvāḥ
kandarpaṃ ca mahāmunī
body.translated_text: [They] beheld the excellent trees ablaze with flowers, <s>Vasanta</s>, the southern wind, and all those <s>Apsarases</s>, and <s>Kandarpa</s>, those two great sages,

body.text:
yac cārabdhaṃ tapas tābhyām
ātmānaṃ gandhamādanam
dadṛśāte 'khilaṃ rūpaṃ
brahmaṇaḥ puruṣarṣabha
body.translated_text: and the austerity which had been begun by the two, [their own] self, <s>Gandhamādana</s>—[they beheld it] all [as] the form of <s>Brahman</s>, O bull among men

body.text:
dāhāya nānalo vahner
nāpaḥkledāya cāmbhasaḥ
taddravyam eva taddravya-
vikārāya na vai yataḥ
