body.translated_text: Since fire does not [serve] for the burning of fire, nor water for the wetting of water—a substance does not [serve] for the modification of that very substance—

body.text:
tato vijñānavijñāta-
parabrahmasvarūpayoḥ
madhukandarpayoṣitsu
vikāro nābhavat tayoḥ
body.translated_text: therefore in those two, whose nature was the supreme <s>Brahman</s> known by [their] discriminative knowledge, there was no alteration [caused] by <s>Madhu</s> [Spring], <s>Kandarpa</s>, or the women

body.text:
tato gurutaraṃ yatnaṃ
vasantamadanau nṛpa
cakrāte tāś ca tanvaṅgyas
tatkṣobhāya punaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vasanta</s> and <s>Madana</s>, O king, made a weightier effort, and those slender-limbed ones [too], for the agitation of the two, again and again

body.text:
atha nārāyaṇo dhairya-
gāmbhīryodāryamānasaḥ
ūror utpādayām āsa
tāṃ varorubalāṃ tadā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, his mind [full of] steadfastness, gravity, and nobility, produced from his thigh that fair-thighed [maiden] of [great] power then

body.text:
trailokyasundarīratnam
aśeṣam avanīpate
guṇalāghavam abhyeti
yasyāḥ saṃdarśanād anu
body.translated_text: The entire jewel of [all] the beauties of the three worlds comes to [seem] a paltry quality after the sight of her, O lord of the earth

body.text:
tāṃ vilokya mahīpāla
cakampe mādhavānilam
vasanto vismayaṃ yātaḥ
saṃyātaḥ saṃsmaraṃ smaraḥ
body.translated_text: Beholding her, O lord of the earth, the spring-wind trembled; <s>Vasanta</s> went to astonishment; <s>Smara</s> [Kāma] himself came to be smitten with love

body.text:
rambhātilottamādyāś ca
vilakṣā devayoṣitaḥ
na rejur avanīpāla
tallakṣahṛdayekṣaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: And <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Tilottamā</s>, and the others, the divine women, abashed, shone not, O lord of the earth, their hearts and eyes [fixed] on her marks [of beauty]

body.text:
tataḥ kāmo vasantaś ca
pārthivāpsarasaś ca tāḥ
praṇamya bhagavantau tau
tuṣṭuvur munisattamau
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Vasanta</s> and those royal <s>Apsarases</s>, having bowed to those two Blessed Ones, praised those best of sages:

body.text:
prasīdatu jagaddhātā
yasya devasya māyayā
mohitāḥ sma vijānīmo
nāntaraṃ vandyanindyayoḥ
body.translated_text: 'May the Maker of the world be gracious, by whose god's <s>Māyā</s> we have been deluded; we do not know the difference between the praiseworthy and the blameworthy

body.text:
prasīdatu sa no devo
yasya rūpam idaṃ dvidhā
dhāma bhūtasya lokānām
anāder atra tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: May that god be gracious to us, whose form is this twofold [one]; the abode of the being of the worlds, [the god] without beginning, abides here

body.text:
naranārāyaṇau devau
śārṅgacakrāyudhāv ubhau
āstāṃ prasādasumukhāv
asmākam aparādhinām
body.translated_text: <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the two gods, both bearing the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow and the discus as weapons—may they be gracious-faced toward us offenders

body.text:
nidhānaṃ sarvavidyānāṃ
sarvapāpendhanānalaḥ
nārāyaṇo no bhagavān
sarvapāpaṃ vyapohatu
body.translated_text: The repository of all sciences, the fire to the fuel of all sins, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, our Blessed One—may he remove all sin

body.text:
śārṅgacakrāyudhaḥ śrīmān
ātmajñānamayo 'naghaḥ
naraḥ samastapāpāni
hatvātmā sarvadehinām
body.translated_text: The glorious bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow and discus, consisting of self-knowledge, the sinless one, <s>Nara</s>, the Self of all embodied beings, having slain all sins—

body.text:
jaṭākalāpabandho 'yam
anayor akṣayātmanoḥ
saumyā ca dṛṣṭiḥ pāpāni
hantu sarvāṇi naḥ śubhā
body.translated_text: This binding of the mass of matted locks of these two imperishable-selved ones, and [their] benign, auspicious glance—may they slay all our sins

body.text:
prasīdatu naro 'smākaṃ
tathā nārāyaṇo 'vyayaḥ
aparādhaḥ kṛto 'smābhir
yayor avyaktajanmanoḥ
body.translated_text: May <s>Nara</s> be gracious to us, and likewise the imperishable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, against whom an offense was committed by us, [those two] of unmanifest birth

body.text:
kva mūrtir aiśvaryaguṇair
yuktā divyair mahātmanoḥ
kva naḥ śarīrakāṇīdṛg
miśrakarmacitāni vai
body.translated_text: Where [is] the form, endowed with divine qualities of lordship, of [those] two great souls, and where [are] our bodies, such as they are, heaped up of mixed deeds?

body.text:
tathāpy avidyāduṣṭena
manasā yaḥ kṛto hi vām
asmābhir aparādho 'yaṃ
kṣamyatāṃ sumahādyutī
body.translated_text: Yet this offense which was done to you two by [our] mind, sullied by ignorance—may it be forgiven, O you two of mighty splendour

body.text:
śaraṇaṃ ca prapannānāṃ
tavāsmīti ca vādinām
prasādaṃ pitṛhantṝṇām
api kurvanti sādhavaḥ
body.translated_text: And the good show grace even to the slayers of [their] fathers who have come for refuge and who say 'I am yours'

body.text:
eṣa eva varo 'smākam
avivekāhṛto mahān
trailokyavandyau yannāthau
vilobhayitum āgatāḥ
body.translated_text: This very [thing] is our great boon, [though] won by [our] lack of discrimination, in that we have come to allure [those two] who, lords [of all], are worthy of the homage of the three worlds

body.text:
prasīda deva vijñāna-
ghanamūḍhadṛśām api
bhavanti santaḥ satataṃ
saddharmanyavatārakāḥ
body.translated_text: Be gracious, O god; the good ever become, even toward those whose sight is deluded by the density of [their] cognition, the bringers-down of true <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
dṛṣṭvaitan naḥ samutpannaṃ
yathā strīratnam īdṛśam
tvayi nārāyaṇotpannā
śreṣṭhā pāravatī matiḥ
body.translated_text: Beholding this, which has arisen for us—since such a jewel of a woman [has arisen]—in you, O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, an excellent, surpassing conviction has arisen

body.text:
tena satyena satyātman
paramātman sanātanam
nārāyaṇa prasīdeti
sarvalokaparāyaṇa
body.translated_text: By that truth, O Self of truth, O Supreme Self, eternal, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, be gracious—O you who are the supreme resort of all worlds

body.text:
prasannabuddhe śāntātman
prasannavadanekṣaṇa
prasīda yoginām īśa
nara sarvagatācyuta
body.translated_text: O you of serene intellect, of tranquil self, of gracious face and eyes, be gracious, O Lord of yogins, O <s>Nara</s>, all-pervading <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
namasyāmo naraṃ devaṃ
tathā nārāyaṇaṃ harim
namo narāya namyāya
namo nārāyaṇāya ca
body.translated_text: We do homage to the god <s>Nara</s>, and likewise to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> <s>Hari</s>; homage to <s>Nara</s>, worthy of homage, and homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

body.text:
prasannānām anāthānām
aparādhavatāṃ prabhuḥ
śaṃ karotu naro 'smākaṃ
śaṃ nārāyaṇa dehi naḥ
body.translated_text: The Lord of the gracious, the helpless, [and] the offending—may <s>Nara</s> make weal for us; grant us weal, O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'

body.text:
evam abhyarthitaḥ stutyā
rāgadveṣādivarjitaḥ
prāheśaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ
sādhyo nārāyaṇo nṛpa
body.translated_text: Thus entreated by [their] praise, free of passion, hatred and the rest, the Lord of all beings, <s>Sādhya</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, spoke, O king:

body.text:
svāgataṃ madhave kāma
bhavato 'psarasām api
yat kāryam āgatānāṃ va
ihāsmābhis tad ucyatām
body.translated_text: 'Welcome to <s>Mādhava</s> [Spring], to <s>Kāma</s>, to your honours [the Apsarases] too; whatever the business of you who have come here—let that be spoken by us [i.e. tell us]

body.text:
yūyaṃ saṃsiddhaye nūnam
asmākaṃ valaśatruṇā
saṃpreṣitās tato 'smākaṃ
nṛttageyādidarśitam
body.translated_text: You have surely been sent by the foe of <s>Bala</s> [Indra] for our accomplishment [success], and thence [you have] shown us dance, song, and the rest

body.text:
na vayaṃ nṛttagītena
nāṅgaceṣṭādibhāṣitaiḥ
lubhyāmo viṣato manye
viṣayā dāruṇātmakāḥ
body.translated_text: We are not allured by dance and song, nor by the gestures of the limbs and the rest, [nor] by speech; I deem the sense-objects to be of dreadful nature

body.text:
śabdādisaṅgaduṣṭāni
yadā nākṣāṇi naḥ śubhāḥ
tadā nṛttādayo bhāvāḥ
kathaṃ lobhapradāyinaḥ
body.translated_text: When our senses, O auspicious ones, are not sullied by attachment to sound and the rest, then how are the states of dance and the rest givers of allurement [to us]?

body.text:
te siddhāḥ sma na vai sādhyā
bhavatīnāṃ smarasya ca
mādhavasya ca śakro 'pi
svāsthyaṃ yātv aviśaṅkitaḥ
body.translated_text: We are [already] perfected; we are not to be subdued by you, nor by <s>Smara</s> [Kāma] and <s>Mādhava</s>; let even <s>Śakra</s> go to ease, free of anxiety

body.text:
yo 'sau parasmāt paramaḥ
puruṣāt parameśvaraḥ
paramātmā hṛṣīkeśaḥ
sthāvarasya carasya ca
body.translated_text: He who is supreme beyond the supreme, the Supreme Lord beyond the [Supreme] <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Supreme Self, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, of the stationary and the moving,

body.text:
utpattihetur ante ca
yasmin sarvaṃ pralīyate
sa sarvavāsidevatvād
vāsudevety udāhṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: the cause of [their] arising, and at the end he in whom all dissolves—he, through his being the deity dwelling in all (<s>sarva-vāsi-deva</s>), is declared <s>Vāsudeva</s>

body.text:
vayam aṃśāṃśakās tasya
caturvyūhasya māyinaḥ
tadādeśitavartmano
jagadbodhāya dehinaḥ
body.translated_text: We are portions of portions of that <s>Caturvyūha</s> (Fourfold) wielder of <s>Māyā</s>, embodied [beings] following the path instructed by him, for the awakening of the world

body.text:
taṃ sarvabhūtaṃ sarveśaṃ
sarvatra samadarśinaḥ
paśyantaḥ kutra rāgādīn
kariṣyāmo vibhedakān
body.translated_text: We, beholding him, the being of all, the Lord of all, everywhere with an equal eye—where shall we make passion and the rest, the dividers [of vision]?

body.text:
vasante mayi cendre ca
bhavatīṣu tathā smare
yadā sa eva viśvātmā
tadā dveṣādayaḥ katham
body.translated_text: In <s>Vasanta</s> [Spring] and in me and in <s>Indra</s>, and likewise in your honours and in <s>Smara</s>—when he alone, the Self of the universe, [is present], then how [come] hatred and the rest?

body.text:
tanmayāny avibhaktāni
yadā sarveṣu jantuṣu
pṛthivy āpas tathā tejo
vāyur ākāśam eva ca
body.translated_text: When [all], consisting of him, undivided, [is] in all creatures—earth, water, and likewise fire, wind, and ether,

body.text:
tathendriyāṇy ahaṃkāro
buddhiś ca na pṛthag yataḥ
samadṛṣṭir yataḥ kutra
rāgadveṣau pravartataḥ
body.translated_text: and likewise the senses, egoism, and intellect, are not [from him] separate—since [there is] equal vision, where do passion and hatred operate?

body.text:
ātmā cāyam abhedena
yataḥ sarveṣu jantuṣu
sarveśvareśvaro viṣṇuḥ
kutra rāgādayas tataḥ
body.translated_text: And since this Self, undividedly, [abides] in all creatures, [as] <s>Viṣṇu</s> the Lord of the lords of all—where then [come] passion and the rest?

body.text:
brahmāṇam indram īśānam
ādityān maruto 'khilān
viśvedevān ṛṣīn sādhyān
vasūn pitṛgaṇāṃs tathā
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Īśāna</s> [Śiva], the <s>Ādityas</s>, all the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the seers, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and likewise the hosts of the fathers,

body.text:
yakṣarākṣasabhūtādīn
nāgasarpasarīsṛpān
manuṣyapakṣigorūpa-
gajasiṃhajalecarān
body.translated_text: the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, ghosts and the rest, the <s>Nāgas</s>, serpents, and reptiles, [those] of the form of men, birds, cattle, elephants, lions, and water-dwellers,

body.text:
makṣikāmaśakādaṃśāñ
śalabhān alasān kṛmīn
gulmavṛkṣalatāvalli-
tvaksāratṛṇajātijān
body.translated_text: flies, gnats, gadflies, locusts, sluggish [creatures], worms, [those] born of bushes, trees, creepers, vines, bark, pith, grass, and [all their] kinds,

body.text:
yac ca kiṃcid adṛśyaṃ vā
dṛśyaṃ vā tridaśāṅganāḥ
manyadhvaṃ rūpam ekasya
tat sarvaṃ paramātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: and whatever invisible or visible [thing there is], O women of the gods—deem it the form of the One, the Supreme Self; that is all [his]

body.text:
jānamānaḥ kathaṃ viṣṇum
ātmānaṃ paramaṃ ca yat
rāgadveṣau tathā lobhaṃ
kaḥ kuryād amarāṅganāḥ
body.translated_text: Knowing <s>Viṣṇu</s> to be the Self and the supreme—who would make passion, hatred, and likewise greed, O women of the immortals?

body.text:
sarvabhūtasthite viṣṇau
sarvage sarvadhātari
nipātyatāṃ pṛthagbhūte
kutra rāgādiko gaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s>, abiding in all beings, all-pervading, the support of all, is [thus] cast down [comprehended] [yet seen] as separate—where [is] the host of passion and the rest?

body.text:
evam asmāsu yuṣmāsu
sarvabhūteṣu cābalāḥ
tanmayatvaikabhūteṣu
rāgādyavasaraḥ kutaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, in us, in you, and in all beings, [all] of which are one being consisting of him—whence [comes] the occasion for passion and the rest, O women?

body.text:
samyagdṛṣṭir iyaṃ proktā
samastaikyāvalokinī
pṛthagvijñānam atraiva
lokasaṃvyavahāravat
body.translated_text: This right vision (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) has been declared, beholding the unity of all; the separate cognition [is valid] only here, in the ordinary dealings of the world

body.text:
bhūtendriyāntaḥkaraṇa-
pradhānapuruṣātmakam
jagad yad etad akhilaṃ
tadā bhedaḥ kimātmakaḥ
body.translated_text: When this whole world consists of the [gross] elements, the senses, the inner organ, <s>pradhāna</s>, and <s>Puruṣa</s>—then of what does the difference consist?

body.text:
bhavanti layam āyānti
samudre salilormayaḥ
na vāribhedato bhinnās
tathaivaikyād idaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: The water-waves in the ocean come into being and go to dissolution, [yet] are not different by a difference of water; just so, by [their] unity, [is] this world

body.text:
yathāgner arciṣaḥ pītāḥ
piṅgalāruṇadhūsarāḥ
bhavanti nāgnibhedena
tathaitad brahmaṇo jagat
body.translated_text: As the yellow flames of fire, tawny, ruddy, [and] grey, come to be, [yet] not by a difference of fire—so [is] this world of <s>Brahman</s>

body.text:
bhavatībhiś ca yat kṣobham
asmākaṃ sa puraṃdaraḥ
kārayaty asad etac ca
vivekādhāracetasām
body.translated_text: And that agitation [made] by your honours toward us—it is <s>Puraṃdara</s> [Indra] who causes [it]; and this [agitation] is unreal for those whose minds [rest] on the ground of discrimination

body.text:
bhavatyaḥ sa ca devendro
lokāś ca sasurāsurāḥ
samudrādrivanopetā
maddehāntaragocarāḥ
body.translated_text: Your honours and that king of the gods [Indra], and the worlds with their gods and <s>asuras</s>, furnished with oceans, mountains, and forests, are [all] within the range of my body

body.text:
yatheyaṃ cārusarvāṅgī
bhavatīnāṃ mayorutaḥ
darśitā darśayiṣyāmi
tathātraivākhilaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: As this fair-limbed one was produced from my thigh [and] shown to your honours, so I shall show, right here, the entire world

body.text:
prayātu śakro mā garvam
indratvaṃ kasya susthiram
yūyaṃ ca mā smayaṃ yāta
santi rūpānvitāḥ striyaḥ
body.translated_text: Let <s>Śakra</s> go [home]; let him not [feel] pride; for whom is Indrahood firmly fixed? And let you not go to vanity; [other] women endowed with beauty exist

body.text:
kiṃ surūpaṃ kurūpaṃ vā
yadā bhedo na dṛśyate
tāratamyaṃ surūpatve
satataṃ bhinnadarśinām
body.translated_text: What [is] fair-formed or ill-formed, when the difference is not seen? The gradation in fair-formedness [is] ever [only] for those who behold difference

body.text:
bhavatīnāṃ smayaṃ matvā
rūpaudāryaguṇodbhavam
mayeyaṃ darśitā tanvī
tatas tacchamam icchatā
body.translated_text: "Deeming the pride of you [apsarases], arisen from [your] beauty, nobility, and qualities, this slender one was displayed by me, [I] then desiring the quelling of that [pride]"

body.text:
yasmān madūror udbhūtā
iyam indīvarekṣaṇā
urvaśī nāma kalyāṇī
bhaviṣyati tato 'psarāḥ
body.translated_text: "Since from my thigh has arisen this lotus-eyed one, she shall become an apsaras named <s>Urvaśī</s>, the auspicious"

body.text:
tad iyaṃ devarājāya
nīyatāṃ varavarṇinī
bhavatyas tena cāsmākaṃ
preṣitāḥ prītim icchatā
body.translated_text: "So let this lovely-hued one be led to the king of the gods; and you [apsarases] are sent by him [Indra] to us, desiring [his] pleasure"

body.text:
vaktavyaś ca sahasrākṣo
nāsmākaṃ bhogakāraṇāt
tapaścaryā na cāprāpya-
phalaṃ prāptum abhīpsitam
body.translated_text: "And it should be said to the thousand-eyed one [Indra]: not for the sake of [our] enjoyment [do I perform] the practice of austerity, nor is it desired to obtain an unobtainable fruit"

body.text:
sanmārgam asya jagato
darśayiṣyan karomy aham
tapo nareṇa sahito
jagataḥ pālanodyataḥ
body.translated_text: "Intending to show this world the good path, I perform austerity, together with <s>Nara</s>, intent on the protection of the world"

body.text:
yadi kaścit tavābādhāṃ
karoti tridaśeśvara
tam ahaṃ vārayiṣyāmi
nirvṛto bhava vāsava
body.translated_text: "If anyone causes obstruction to you, O lord of the thirty [gods], I shall ward him off; be at ease, O <s>Vāsava</s>"

body.text:
kartāsi cet tvam ābādhām
aduṣṭasyeha kasyacit
tavāpi śāstaitad ahaṃ
pravartiṣyāmy asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: "[But] if you cause obstruction here to some innocent one, I shall, without doubt, set in motion this chastisement of you too"

body.text:
etaj jñātvā na saṃtāpas
tvayā kāryo hi māṃ prati
upakārāya jagatām
avatīrṇo 'smi vāsava
body.translated_text: "Knowing this, no anguish is to be felt by you regarding me; I have descended for the benefit of the worlds, O <s>Vāsava</s>"

body.text:
yā ceyam urvaśī mattaḥ
samudbhūtā puraṃdara
tretāgnihetubhūteyam
ailaṃ prāpya bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: "And this <s>Urvaśī</s> who has arisen from me, O <s>Puraṃdara</s>—she, becoming the cause of the <s>tretā</s>-fires [sacrificial fires], shall come to be, having attained <s>Aila</s> [Purūravas]"

body.text:
ity ukte 'psarasaḥ sarvāḥ
praṇipatyātivismitāḥ
ūcur nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ
taddarśanakutūhalāḥ
body.translated_text: When this was said, all the apsarases, having bowed down, exceedingly astonished, said to the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, eager for the sight of that [form]:

body.text:
ukto bhagavatā yo 'yam
upadeśo hitārthinām
proktaḥ sa sarvo vijñāto
māhātmyaṃ viditaṃ ca te
body.translated_text: "This instruction which has been spoken by the Blessed Lord for those who seek [their] welfare—all that, spoken [by you], is understood, and your greatness is known"

body.text:
yat tv etad bhavatā proktaṃ
prasannenāvyayātmanā
darśiteyaṃ viśālākṣī
darśayiṣyāmi vo jagat
body.translated_text: "But this which has been spoken by you, gracious one, of imperishable self—'this wide-eyed one has been shown [to you]; I shall show you the world'—"

body.text:
tannātha sarvabhāvena
prapannānāṃ jagatpate
darśayātmānam akhilaṃ
darśiteyaṃ yathorvaśī
body.translated_text: "that, O Lord, with all [our] being, of [us] who have taken refuge, O Lord of the world, show [us] your whole self, as this <s>Urvaśī</s> has been shown"

body.text:
yadi devāparāddheṣu
nāsmāsu kupitaṃ tava
manas taj jagatam īśa
darśayātmānam ātmanā
body.translated_text: "If your mind is not angered at us in [our] offenses against the gods, O Lord of the world, show [your] self by [your] self"

body.text:
paśyatehākhilāṃl lokān
mama dehe surāṅganāḥ
madhuṃ madanam ātmānaṃ
yac cānyad draṣṭum icchatha
body.translated_text: "Behold here all the worlds in my body, O divine women, [and] <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Madana</s> [Kāma], myself, and whatever else you wish to see"

body.text:
ity uktvā bhagavān devas
tadā nārāyaṇo nṛpa
uccair jahāsa svanavat
tatrābhūd akhilaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: Having said this, the Blessed god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> then, O king, laughed aloud, like [a peal of] thunder; therein came to be the entire world:

body.text:
brahmā prajāpatiḥ śakraḥ
saha rudraiḥ pinākadhṛk
ādityā vasavaḥ sādhyā
viśvedevā maharṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> together with the <s>Rudras</s>, the bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> [bow], the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the great sages,

body.text:
nāsatyadasrāv anilāḥ
sarve sarve tathāgnayaḥ
yakṣagandharvasiddhāś ca
piśācāḥ kiṃnaroragāḥ
body.translated_text: the <s>Nāsatya-Dasras</s> [Aśvins], the winds, all [of them], and likewise all the fires, the <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>siddhas</s>, and the <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, and <s>uragas</s>,

body.text:
samastāpsaraso vidyāḥ
sāṅgā vedās taduktayaḥ
manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ kīṭāḥ
pakṣiṇaḥ pādapās tathā
body.translated_text: all the apsarases, the sciences, the <s>Vedas</s> with their limbs and their utterances, men, beasts, insects, birds, and trees likewise,

body.text:
sarīsṛpāś ca ye sūkṣmā
yac cānyaj jīvasaṃjñitam
samudrāḥ sakalāḥ śailāḥ
saritaḥ kānanāni ca
body.translated_text: and the creeping things that are minute, and whatever else is named a living being, all the oceans, the mountains, the rivers, and the forests,

body.text:
dvīpāny aśeṣāṇi tathā
nadāḥ sarvasarāṃsi ca
nagaragrāmapūrṇā ca
medinī medinīpate
devāṅganābhir devasya
dehe dṛṣṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: and all the continents entire, the streams and all the lakes, and the earth full of cities and villages, O lord of the earth—[all this] was seen by the divine women in the body of the god, the great soul

body.text:
nakṣatragrahatārābhiḥ
samavetaṃ nabhastalam
dadṛśus tāḥ sucārvaṅgyas
tasyāntar viśvarūpiṇaḥ
body.translated_text: The vault of the sky, set with asterisms, planets, and stars, those fair-limbed ones beheld within him of cosmic form

body.text:
nordhvaṃ na tiryaṅ nādhaś ca
yadāntas tasya dṛśyate
tam anantam anādiṃ ca
tatas tās tuṣṭuvuḥ prabhum
body.translated_text: Neither above, nor across, nor below was the inside of him [seen to] appear; that one, the endless and the beginningless—therefore those [women] praised the Lord

body.text:
madanena samaṃ sarvā
madhunā ca surāṅganāḥ
sasādhvasā bhaktimatyaḥ
paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ
body.translated_text: All the divine women, together with <s>Madana</s> and <s>Madhu</s>, full of awe, full of devotion, came to supreme amazement:

body.text:
paśyāma nādiṃ tava deva nāntam
na madhyam avyākṛtarūpapāram
parāyaṇaṃ tvā jagatām anantam
natāḥ sma nārāyaṇam ātmabhūtam
body.translated_text: "We behold not your beginning, O god, nor [your] end, nor [your] middle, [you] whose limit of unmanifest form [is unseen]; the supreme resort of the worlds, the endless—we are bowed to you, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the self of [all] beings"

body.text:
mahī divaṃ vāyujalāgnayas tvaṃ
śabdādirūpaś ca parāparātman
tvatto bhavaty acyuta sarvam etad
abhedarūpo 'si vibho tvam ebhiḥ
body.translated_text: "You are the earth, heaven, wind, water, and fires, and of the form of sound and the rest, O self of the higher and lower; from you, O <s>Acyuta</s>, comes all this; you, O all-pervading one, are of a nature non-different from these"

body.text:
draṣṭāsi rūpasya rasasya vettā
śrotā ca śabdasya hare tvam ekaḥ
spraṣṭā bhavān spraśavato 'khilasya
ghrātāsi gandhasya pṛthakśarīrī
body.translated_text: "You are the beholder of form, the knower of taste, and the hearer of sound, O <s>Hari</s>, you alone; you are the toucher of all that is tangible, you are the smeller of scent, [yet] of a separate body [from each]"

body.text:
sureṣu sarveṣu na so 'sti kaścin
manuṣyaloke ca na so 'sti kaścit
paśvādivarge ca na so 'sti kaścid
yo nāṃśabhūtas tava devadeva
body.translated_text: "Among all the gods there is none, and in the world of men there is none, and in the class of beasts and the rest there is none, who is not a portion of you, O god of gods"

body.text:
brahmādyupendrapramukhāni saumyeṣv
indrāgnirūpāṇi ca vīryavatsu
rudrāntakādīni ca raudravatsu
rūpeṣu rūpāṇi tavottamāni
body.translated_text: "<s>Brahmā</s> and the rest, chief of whom is <s>Upendra</s>, [are your forms] among the gentle ones; and the forms of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> among the valorous; and <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Antaka</s> [Yama], and the rest among the wrathful—[these] supreme forms of yours [are] among [those] forms"

body.text:
samudrarūpaṃ tava dhairyavatsu
tejasvirūpeṣu ravis tathāgniḥ
kṣamādhaneṣu kṣitirūpam agryaṃ
rūpaṃ tavāgryaṃ balavatsu vāyuḥ
body.translated_text: "Your ocean-form [is] among the steadfast; among the splendid forms, the sun and likewise fire; among those rich in forbearance, the foremost earth-form; your foremost form among the strong, the wind"

body.text:
manuṣyarūpaṃ tava rājaseṣu
mūḍheṣu sarveśvara pādapo 'si
darpānviteṣv acyuta dānavas tvaṃ
sanatsujātaś ca vivekavatsu
body.translated_text: "Your human-form [is] among the passionate; among the deluded, O Lord of all, you are a tree; among those filled with arrogance, O <s>Acyuta</s>, you are a <s>dānava</s>; and <s>Sanatsujāta</s> among those endowed with discrimination"

body.text:
rasasvarūpeṇa jale sthito 'si
gandhasvarūpo bhavato dharitryam
dṛśyasvarūpaś ca hutāśane tvaṃ
sparśasvarūpo bhagavān samīre
body.translated_text: "In the form of taste you abide in water; you are in the form of scent in the earth; and in the form of the visible you [abide] in fire; in the form of touch, the Blessed One, in the wind"

body.text:
śabdātmakaṃ te nabhasi svarūpaṃ
mantavyarūpo manasi prabho tvam
bodhavyarūpaś ca vibho tvam ekaḥ
sarvatra sarveśvara sarvabhūtaḥ
body.translated_text: "In the sky [is] your form consisting of sound; in the mind, O Lord, you are of the form of the thinkable; and of the form of the cognizable, O all-pervading one, you alone, everywhere, O Lord of all, [you who] are all beings"

body.text:
paśyāma te nābhisarojamadhye
brahmāṇam etaṃ ca haraṃ bhrukūṭyam
tatrāśvinau karṇagatau samastāṇ
avasthitān bāhuṣu lokapālān
body.translated_text: "We behold in the midst of your navel-lotus this <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Hara</s> [Śiva] on [your] frowning brow, [and] there the <s>Aśvins</s> gone to [your] ears, all the world-guardians stationed in [your] arms"

body.text:
ghrāṇe 'nilaṃ netragatau ravīndū
jihvā ca te nātha sarasvatīyam
pādau dharitrīṃ jaṭharaṃ samastāṃl
lokān hṛṣīkeśa vilokayāmaḥ
body.translated_text: "the wind in [your] nose, the sun and moon gone to [your] eyes, and your tongue [is] this <s>Sarasvatī</s>, O Lord; [your] feet [are] the earth, [your] belly all the worlds—we behold [them], O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>"

body.text:
jaṅghe viyat pādakarāṅgulīṣu
piśācarakṣoragasiddhasaṅghān
puṃstve prajānāṃ patir oṣṭhayugme
pratiṣṭhitās te kratavaḥ samastāḥ
body.translated_text: "[your] shanks the sky; on the fingers of [your] feet and hands the hosts of <s>piśācas</s>, <s>rakṣases</s>, <s>uragas</s>, and <s>siddhas</s>; in [your] virility the lord of creatures; on [your] pair of lips all your sacrifices are established"

body.text:
sarveṣṭayas te daśaneṣu deva
daṃṣṭṛāsu vidyā bhavataś catasraḥ
romasv aśeṣās tava devasaṅghā
vidyādharā nātha karāṅghrirekhāḥ
sāṅghāḥ samastās tava deva vedāḥ
samāsthitā bahuṣu saṃdhibhūtāḥ
body.translated_text: "all the [sacrificial] rites [are] on your teeth, O god; on [your] tusks the four sciences of yours; on [your] body-hairs all your hosts of gods, [and] the <s>vidyādharas</s>, O Lord, [are] the lines of your hands and feet; all your <s>Vedas</s> with their limbs, O god, stand abiding in [your] many joints"

body.text:
varāharūpaṃ dharaṇīdhṛtas te
nṛsiṃharūpaṃ ca saṭākarālam
paśyāma te vājiśiras tathoccais
trivikrame yaś ca tavāprameyaḥ
body.translated_text: "Your earth-upholding <s>Varāha</s>-form, and [your] <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>-form terrible with [its] mane—we behold [them], [and] your horse-head, and that which, on high in [your] <s>Trivikrama</s> [stride], is your immeasurable [form]"

body.text:
amī samudrās tava deva dehe
mervādayaḥ śailavarās tavāmī
imāś ca gaṅgāpramukhāḥ sravatyo
dvīpāny aśeṣāṇi vanāni caiva
body.translated_text: "These oceans [are] in your body, O god; these best of mountains, <s>Meru</s> and the rest, [are] yours; and these streams, chief of which is the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and all the continents and the forests too"

body.text:
stuvanti caite munayas taveśa
dehe sthitās tvanmahimānam agryam
tvām īśitāraṃ jagatām anantam
yajñeśam arcanti ca yajvino 'mī
body.translated_text: "And these sages, stationed in your body, praise your foremost greatness, O Lord; and these sacrificers worship you, the endless Ruler of the worlds, the Lord of sacrifice"

body.text:
tvatto na saumyaṃ jagatīha kiṃcit
tvatto na raudraṃ ca samastamūrte
tvatto na śītaṃ na ca keśavoṣṇaṃ
sarvasvarūpātiśayī tvam ekaḥ
body.translated_text: "Apart from you there is nothing gentle here in the world, and apart from you nothing wrathful, O you of all forms; apart from you no cold, and no heat, O <s>Keśava</s>; you alone surpass [all], being of the nature of all"

body.text:
prasīda sarveśvara sarvabhūta
sanātanātman parameśvareśa
tvanmāyayā mohitamānasābhir
yat te 'parāddhaṃ tad idaṃ kṣamasva
body.translated_text: "Be gracious, O Lord of all, [self] of all beings, eternal self, Lord of the supreme lords; whatever offense against you [was committed] by [us] whose minds were deluded by your <s>māyā</s>, forgive that"

body.text:
kiṃ vāparāddhaṃ tava deva mūḍhair
yan māyayā no hṛdayaṃ tathāpi
pāpāvaśaṃ kiṃ praṇatārtihārin
mano hi no viṅkalatām upaiti
body.translated_text: "Yet what offense [is there] against you, O god, by [us] deluded ones, since it is by [your] <s>māyā</s> [that] our heart [erred]? [Is] our mind, under the sway of sin, [to blame], O remover of the affliction of those who bow? For our mind indeed comes to bewilderment"

body.text:
na te 'parāddhaṃ yadi vāparāddham
asmābhir unmārgavivartanībhiḥ
tat kṣamyatāṃ sṛṣṭikaras tavaiva
devāparādhaṃ sṛjato vivekān
body.translated_text: "[There is] no offense against you; or if there [be] an offense by us, who turn aside onto the wrong path, let that be forgiven by you, the very maker of creation, who [yourself] create the gods' offense from [the lack of] discrimination"

body.text:
namo namas te govinda
nārāyaṇa janārdana
tvannāmasmaraṇāt pāpam
aśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu
body.translated_text: "Homage, homage to you, O <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>; from the remembrance of your name may our sin, entire, perish"

body.text:
tato 'nanta namas tubhyaṃ
viśvātman viśvabhāvana
tvannāmasmaraṇāt pāpam
aśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu
namo namas te vaikuṇṭha
śrīvatsāṅkābjalocana
vareṇya yajñapuruṣa
prajāpālaka vāmana
body.translated_text: "Then, O <s>Ananta</s>, homage to you, O self of the universe, fosterer of the universe; from the remembrance of your name may our sin, entire, perish; homage, homage to you, O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, marked with <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, lotus-eyed, O most choice one, sacrifice-Person, protector of creatures, <s>Vāmana</s>"

body.text:
namo 'stu te 'bjanābhāya
prajāpatikṛte hare
tvannāmasmaraṇāt pāpam
aśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu
body.translated_text: "Homage be to you, O lotus-naveled one, maker of the lord of creatures, O <s>Hari</s>; from the remembrance of your name may our sin, entire, perish"

body.text:
saṃsārārṇavapotāya
namas tubhyam adhokṣaja
tvannāmasmaraṇāt pāpam
aśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu
body.translated_text: "To the boat across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, homage to you, O <s>Adhokṣaja</s>; from the remembrance of your name may our sin, entire, perish"

body.text:
namaḥ parasmai śrīśāya
vāsudevāya vedhase
svecchayā guṇabhoktṛtve
sargāntasthitikāriṇe
body.translated_text: "Homage to the supreme, the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the ordainer, the enjoyer of qualities by his own will, the maker of creation, dissolution, and maintenance"

body.text:
upasaṃhāra viśvātman
rūpam etat samantataḥ
vardhamānaṃ na no draṣṭuṃ
samarthaṃ cakṣur īśvara
body.translated_text: "Withdraw, O self of the universe, this form on every side; growing [ever larger], our eye is not able to behold [it], O Lord"

body.text:
pralayāgnisahasrasya
samā dīptis tavācyuta
pramāṇena diśo bhūmir
gaganaṃ ca samāvṛtam
body.translated_text: "The splendor of you, O <s>Acyuta</s>, is equal to a thousand fires of dissolution; by [its] measure the directions, the earth, and the sky are enveloped"

body.text:
na vidmaḥ kva nu vartāmo
bhavān naivopalakṣyate
sarvaṃ jagad ihaikasthaṃ
piṇḍitaṃ lakṣayāmahe
body.translated_text: "We know not where indeed we stand; you cannot even be discerned; we discern the whole world here as standing in one place, condensed into a mass"

body.text:
kiṃ varṇayāmo rūpaṃ te
kiṃ pramāṇam idaṃ hare
māhātmyaṃ kiṃtu te deva
jihvāyā yan na gocaram
body.translated_text: "What shall we describe of your form, what [is] this measure, O <s>Hari</s>? But your greatness, O god, [is] that which is not within the province of the tongue"

body.text:
vaktrāṇām ayutenāpi
buddhīnām ayutāyutaiḥ
guṇānāṃ varṇanaṃ nātha
tava vaktuṃ na śakyate
body.translated_text: "Even with a myriad of mouths, with myriads of myriads of minds, the describing of [your] qualities, O Lord, is not possible to utter, of you"

body.text:
tad etad darśitaṃ rūpaṃ
prasādaḥ paramaḥ kṛtaḥ
chandato jagatām īśa
tad etad upasaṃhara
body.translated_text: "So this form has been shown, the supreme grace has been done; willingly, O Lord of the worlds, withdraw this same [form]"

body.text:
ity evaṃ saṃstutas tābhir
apsarobhir janārdanaḥ
divyajñānopapannānāṃ
tāsāṃ pratyakṣam īśvaraḥ
viveśa sarvabhūtāni
svair aṃśair bhūtabhāvanaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus praised by those apsarases, <s>Janārdana</s>, the Lord, in the visible presence of those [women] endowed with divine knowledge, entered into all beings by his own portions, the fosterer of beings

body.text:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvabhūteṣu
līyamānam adhokṣajam
vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmuḥ
samastā devayoṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, dissolving into all beings, all the divine women came to supreme amazement

body.text:
sa ca sarveśvaraḥ śailān
pādapān sāgarān bhuvam
jalam agniṃ tathā vāyum
ākāśaṃ ca viveśa ha
body.translated_text: And that Lord of all entered the mountains, the trees, the oceans, the earth, water, fire, and likewise wind, and the sky

body.text:
kāle dikṣv atha sarvātmā
manuṣyātmany athāpi ca
ātmarūpaḥ sthitaḥ svena
mahimnā bhāvayañ jagat
body.translated_text: and then into time, into the directions, the self of all; and then also into the human self; abiding in [his own] self-form by his own greatness, fostering the world

body.text:
devadānavarakṣāṃsi
yakṣavidyādharoragān
manuṣyapaśukīṭādīn
mṛgapakṣyantarikṣagān
body.translated_text: Into gods, <s>dānavas</s>, and <s>rakṣases</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>vidyādharas</s>, and <s>uragas</s>, men, beasts, insects, and the rest, deer, birds, and the air-goers,

body.text:
ye 'ntarikṣe tathā bhūmau
divi ye ye jalāśrayāḥ
tān praviśya sa viśvātmā
punas tad rūpam āsthitaḥ
nareṇa sārchaṃ yat tābhir
dṛṣṭapūrvam ariṃdama
body.translated_text: those who [dwell] in the atmosphere and likewise on the earth, those in heaven and those who have water for their abode—having entered them, that self of the universe again stood in that [former] form, [the form] together with <s>Nara</s> which had been seen by those [women] before, O subduer of foes

body.text:
tāḥ paraṃ vismayaṃ gatvā
sarvās tridaśayoṣitaḥ
praṇemuḥ sādhyasāḥ pāṇḍu-
vadanā nṛpasattama
body.translated_text: Those, having come to supreme amazement—all the women of the thirty [gods]—and the <s>Sādhyas</s>, bowed down, their faces pale [with awe], O best of kings

body.text:
nārāyaṇo 'pi bhagavān
āha tās tridaśāṅganāḥ
nīyatām urvaśī bhadrā
yatrāste tridaśeśvaraḥ
body.translated_text: And the Blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> too said to those divine women: "Let the auspicious <s>Urvaśī</s> be led to where the lord of the thirty [gods] abides"

body.text:
bhavatīnāṃ hitārthāya
sarvabhūteṣv asāv iti
jñānam utpāditaṃ bhūyo
layaṃ bhūteṣu kurvatā
body.translated_text: "For the sake of your welfare, [the teaching] 'he is in all beings'—this knowledge was again produced by [me], effecting [my] dissolution into beings"

body.text:
tad gacchata samasto 'yaṃ
bhūtagrāmo madaṃśakaḥ
aham apy ātmabhūtasya
vāsudevasya yoginaḥ
body.translated_text: "So go; this entire host of beings is a portion of me, and I too [am a portion] of the self-existent <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the <s>yogin</s>"

body.text:
yasmāt parataraṃ nāsti
yo 'nantaḥ paripaṭhyate
tam ajaṃ sarvabhūteśaṃ
jānīta paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: "Than whom there is nothing higher, who is recited [as] the endless—know him, the unborn, the Lord of all beings, [as] the supreme abode"

body.text:
ahaṃ bhavatyo devāś ca
manuṣyāḥ paśavaś ca ye
etat sarvam anantasya
body.translated_text: "I, you [apsarases], and the gods, and men, and the beasts that there are—all this [is] of the endless one,"

body.text:
devadevasya vistṛtiḥ
etaj jñātvā samaṃ sargaṃ
sadevāsuramānuṣam
sapaśvādigaṇaṃ caiva
draṣṭavyaṃ tridaśāṅganāḥ
body.translated_text: "[all this is] the extension of the god of gods; knowing this, the creation is to be beheld [as] equal [and one], O divine women, [the creation] with its gods, <s>asuras</s>, and men, and the host of beasts and the rest"

body.text:
ity uktas tena devena
samastās tāḥ surastriyaḥ
praṇamya tau samadanāḥ
savasantāś ca pārthiva
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by that god, all those women of the gods, having bowed, together with <s>Madana</s> and <s>Vasanta</s>, O king,

body.text:
ādāya corvaśīṃ bhūyo
devarājam upāgatāḥ
ācakhyuś ca yathāvṛttaṃ
devarājāya tat tathā
body.translated_text: and having taken <s>Urvaśī</s>, again came to the king of the gods, and related to the king of the gods that [event] as it had happened

body.text:
tathā tvam api rājendra
sarvabhūteṣu keśavam
cintayan samatāṃ gaccha
samataiva hi muktaye
body.translated_text: So you too, O lord of kings, contemplating <s>Keśava</s> in all beings, attain equanimity; for equanimity itself [is the path] to liberation

body.text:
jānann evam aśeṣeṣu
bhūteṣu parameśvaram
vāsudevaṃ kathaṃ doṣāṃl
lobhādīn na prahāsyasi
body.translated_text: Knowing thus the supreme Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> in all beings entire, how will you not abandon the faults of greed and the rest?

body.text:
sarvabhūtāni govindād
yadā nānyāni bhūpate
tadā vairādayo bhāvāḥ
kriyatāṃ kutra pārthiva
body.translated_text: When all beings are not other than <s>Govinda</s>, O lord of the earth, then the states of enmity and the rest—where are they to be enacted, O king?

body.text:
iha paśyañ jagat sarvaṃ
vāsudevātmakaṃ nṛpa
etad eva hi kṛṣṇena
rūpam āviṣkṛtaṃ tadā
body.translated_text: Beholding here the whole world as consisting of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O king—this very [form] was made manifest by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> then [to the apsarases]

body.text:
paramasmād api mahad
rūpaṃ yat kathitaṃ tava
janmādibhāvarahitaṃ
tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
body.translated_text: That great form which has been told to you, [the form] greater even than the supreme, free of the states of birth and the rest—that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

body.text:
saṃkṣepeṇa ca bhūpāla
śrūyatāṃ yad vadāmi te
yan matau puruṣaḥ kṛtvā
paraṃ nirvāṇam ṛcchati
body.translated_text: And in brief, O protector of the earth, let it be heard, what I tell you—that, having placed [it] in his mind, a man attains the supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s>

body.text:
sarvaṃ viṣṇuḥ samastau hi
bhāvābhāvau ca tanmayau
sadasat sarvam īśeśo
vāsudevaḥ paraṃ padam
body.translated_text: All is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; for both existence and non-existence, entire, consist of him; the existent and the non-existent, all [of it], the Lord of lords <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [is] the supreme abode

body.text:
bhavajaladhigatānāṃ dvandvavātāhatānāṃ
sutaduhitṛkalatratrāṇabhārārditānām
viṣamaviṣayatoye majjatām aplavānāṃ
bhavati śaraṇam eko viṣṇupoto narāṇām
body.translated_text: For men sunk in the ocean of existence, struck by the winds of the pairs of opposites, afflicted by the burden of protecting sons, daughters, and wife, sinking in the water of harmful sense-objects, without a boat—the one boat that is <s>Viṣṇu</s> becomes [their] refuge

body.text:
ity uktaṃ tava dharmajña
viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam
svarūpaṃ ca jagaddhātur
ārādhanaviniścayaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus has been told to you, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, the supreme greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the nature of the upholder of the world, and the ascertainment of [his] worship.

body.text:
ārādhitāt phalaṃ yac ca
keśavāt prāpyate naraiḥ
kathitaś ca mahābhāga
dānānāṃ vistarād vidhiḥ
body.translated_text: And the fruit which is obtained by men from the worshipped <s>Keśava</s>, and the rule of gifts has been told in detail, O greatly fortunate one.

body.text:
yogadvaidhaṃ ca kathitam
advaitaṃ dvaitam eva ca
advaitabhāvanopāyo
vistarāc ca tavoditaḥ
body.translated_text: And the twofold <s>yoga</s> has been told, the non-dual and the dual, and the means of the contemplation of non-duality has been told to you in detail.

body.text:
saṃkṣepavistarābhyāṃ ca
sarvam etat tavoditam
devadevasya māhātmyaṃ
sarvagasyāvyayātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: And in brief and in detail all this has been told to you—the greatness of the god of gods, the all-pervading, of imperishable nature.

body.text:
sa eṣa sarvapravaraḥ
sarvabhūtaś ca mādhavaḥ
sarvam atra ca sarvasminn
eṣa eva pratiṣṭhitaḥ
body.translated_text: He, this <s>Mādhava</s>, is the foremost of all, and is all beings; everything is here, and in everything he alone is established.

body.text:
triyugaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣam
apavargamahāhradam
samutpatya parāhlādam
anantaṃ pratipadyate
body.translated_text: Having sprung up [out of saṃsāra], one attains the three-aged (<s>Triyuga</s>) lotus-eyed one, the great lake of liberation, the supremely blissful, the infinite.

body.text:
śrutam etan mayā pūrvaṃ
vistareṇa tvayoditam
yat tv etat triyugety uktaṃ
tasya nirvacanaṃ vada
body.translated_text: This was heard by me before, told by you in detail; but as for this that was said, '<s>Triyuga</s>'—tell the explanation of it.

body.text:
caturyugena kālasya
parisaṃkhyā yadā dvija
triyugena tadā viṣṇoḥ
kriyate kiṃ viśeṣaṇam
body.translated_text: Since the reckoning of time is by [groups of] four ages (<s>caturyuga</s>), O twice-born, then why is the epithet 'three-aged' (<s>triyuga</s>) made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

body.text:
kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca
kaliś ceti caturyugam
yadā jagati vikhyātaṃ
tadā triyugatā kutaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s>—when this set of four ages is renowned in the world, then whence the 'three-aged-ness'?

body.text:
sādhu pṛṣṭo 'smi bhūpāla
bhavatā triyugāśritam
viśeṣaṇam anantasya
gadatas tan niśāmaya
body.translated_text: Well have I been asked, O protector of the earth, by you, the epithet of the infinite one grounded in 'three-aged'; hear that as I tell it.

body.text:
kāṣṭhā pārthiva vijñeyā
nimeṣā daśa pañca ca
kāṣṭhātriṃśat kalā jñeyā
muhūrtaṃ tāvatīḥ kalāḥ
body.translated_text: A <s>kāṣṭhā</s>, O king, is to be known as fifteen <s>nimeṣas</s>; thirty <s>kāṣṭhās</s> are to be known as a <s>kalā</s>; a <s>muhūrta</s> is so many <s>kalās</s> [thirty].

body.text:
triṃśanmuhūrtā bhūpāla
tathāhorātram ucyate
tatsaṃkhyātair ahorātrair
māsaḥ pārthivasattama
body.translated_text: Thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, O king, are likewise called a day-and-night; by that number of days-and-nights [is] a month, O best of kings.

body.text:
ayanaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ māsāḥ
ṣaṇ māsāś ca tathottaram
ayanadvitayākhyaś ca
kālaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ smṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Six months are the southern course (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>), and likewise six the northern; the time called the pair of courses is remembered as a year.

body.text:
dakṣiṇaṃ tv ayanaṃ rātrir
devānām uttaraṃ dinam
saṃvatsareṇa devānām
ahorātram ihocyate
body.translated_text: The southern course is the night of the gods, the northern their day; by [one] year [of men], a day-and-night of the gods is here reckoned.

body.text:
śatatrayeṇa varṣāṇāṃ
ṣaṣṭyā ca pṛthivīpate
manuṣyasaṃkhyayā varṣaṃ
devānām api gaṇyate
body.translated_text: By three hundred and sixty years in human reckoning, a year of the gods too is counted, O lord of the earth.

body.text:
iti divyena mānena
caturyugavikalpanām
kathyamānāṃ mayā rājan
yathāvac chrotum arhasi
body.translated_text: Thus, by divine measure, the division of the four ages, being told by me, O king, you ought to hear duly.

body.text:
catvāri tu sahasrāṇi
varṣāṇāṃ kṛtam ucyate
tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā
saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tathāvidhaḥ
body.translated_text: Four thousand years [of the gods] are called the <s>Kṛta</s> [age]; its twilight (<s>saṃdhyā</s>) is so many hundreds [four hundred], and the twilight-portion (<s>saṃdhyāṃśa</s>) likewise.

body.text:
tretā trīṇi sahasrāṇi
divyābdānāṃ nararṣabha
tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā
saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tathāvidhaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Tretā</s> [is] three thousand of divine years, O bull among men; its twilight is so many hundreds [three hundred], and the twilight-portion likewise.

body.text:
dvāparaṃ dve sahasre tu
varṣāṇām abhidhīyate
tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā
saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tathāvidhaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Dvāpara</s> is said to be two thousand years; its twilight is so many hundreds [two hundred], and the twilight-portion likewise.

body.text:
kaliḥ sahasram ekaṃ tu
divyābdānāṃ nararṣabha
tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā
saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tathāvidhaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Kali</s> [is] one thousand of divine years, O bull among men; its twilight is so many hundreds [one hundred], and the twilight-portion likewise.

body.text:
kṛtaṃ nāmayugaṃ pūrvaṃ
yatra dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
kṛtam eva ca kartavyaṃ
tasmin kāle nṛpepsitam
body.translated_text: The age named <s>Kṛta</s> [is] the first, where <s>dharma</s> is eternal; and what is to be done is [already] done in that time, [as] desired, O king.

body.text:
na tatra dharmāḥ sīdanti
na ca kṣīyanti vai prajāḥ
tataḥ kṛtayugaṃ nāma
guṇataḥ procyate yugam
body.translated_text: There the <s>dharmas</s> do not decline, nor do the creatures dwindle; thence the age is called <s>Kṛta</s> by name, on account of [its] qualities.

body.text:
devadānavagandharvā
yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ
nāsan kṛtayuge rājan
na tadā krayavikrayaḥ
body.translated_text: Gods, <s>Dānavas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and serpents were not [present] in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, O king; nor then [was there] buying and selling.

body.text:
na sāmayajurṛgvarṇāḥ
kriyā nāsīc ca mānavī
nābhisaṃdhāya ca phalaṃ
kaścid dharme pravartate
body.translated_text: There were no classes of <s>Sāma</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Ṛc</s> [Vedas], nor was there human ritual action; and no one engages in <s>dharma</s> with [his] eye on the fruit.

body.text:
na tasmin yugasaṃsarge
vyādhayo nendriyakṣayaḥ
nāsūyā nāpi ruditaṃ
na darpo nāpi paiśunam
body.translated_text: In that conjunction of the age there were no diseases, no decay of the senses, no envy nor weeping, no arrogance nor backbiting,

body.text:
na vigrahaḥ kutas tandrī
na dveṣo nāpi dambhanam
na bhayaṃ nāpi saṃtāpo
na cerṣyā nāpi matsaraḥ
body.translated_text: no quarrel—whence sloth?—no hatred nor hypocrisy, no fear nor anguish, nor jealousy nor envy.

body.text:
tataḥ paramakaṃ brahma
yā gatir yogināṃ parā
ātmā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ
śuklo nārāyaṇas tadā
body.translated_text: Then [there was] the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is the supreme goal of <s>yogins</s>, and the self of all beings—white <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> then.

body.text:
tasminn ātmani lokānāṃ
sarvalokamaye 'cyute
svecchayā śauklyam āpanne
sarvaṃ bhavati nirmalam
body.translated_text: In that self of the worlds, made of all the worlds, the <s>Acyuta</s>, having come by his own will to whiteness, all becomes stainless.

body.text:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ
śūdrāś ca kṛtalakṣaṇāḥ
kṛte yuge bhavantīha
svakarmaniratāḥ prajāḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s>, of [duly distinguished] marks, are here, in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, the creatures intent on their own duties.

body.text:
svam āśramaṃ svam ācāraṃ
samyagjñānasamanvitam
jagad bhavati rājendra
satyaprāyaṃ taporatam
body.translated_text: Each [keeping to] his own stage of life, his own conduct, endowed with right knowledge, the world becomes, O lord of kings, abounding in truth, delighting in austerity.

body.text:
ekavedasamāyuktā
ekamantravidhikriyāḥ
pṛthagdharmās tv ekavedā
dharmam ekam anuvratāḥ
body.translated_text: United with the single <s>Veda</s>, with the single rite of the single mantra—with distinct <s>dharmas</s> yet [one] single <s>Veda</s>, faithful to the one <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
caturāśramayuktena
karmaṇā kālayoginā
akāmaphalasaṃyogāt
prāpnuvanti parāṃ gatim
body.translated_text: By action joined with the four stages of life, suited to the time, through the non-conjunction with [desire for] fruit, they attain the supreme goal.

body.text:
ātmayogasamāyukto
dharmo 'yaṃ kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ
kṛte yuge catuṣpādaś
caturvarṇyasya śāśvataḥ
body.translated_text: United with the <s>yoga</s> of the Self, this <s>dharma</s> of [established] marks, four-footed in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, [is] eternal for the four classes.

body.text:
etat kṛtayugaṃ nāma
traiguṇyaparivarjitam
tretām api nibodha tvaṃ
yādṛgrūpaṃ pravartate
body.translated_text: This is the age named <s>Kṛta</s>, free of the three [degrading] qualities; learn now of the <s>Tretā</s> too, of what form it proceeds.

body.text:
pādena hrasate dharmo
raktatāṃ yāti cācyutaḥ
satyapravṛttāś ca narāḥ
kriyādharmaparāyaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: By a quarter <s>dharma</s> diminishes, and the <s>Acyuta</s> goes to redness; and men, engaged in truth, are devoted to ritual <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
tato yajñāḥ pravartante
dharmāś ca vividhāḥ kriyāḥ
tretāyāṃ bhāvasaṃkalpāḥ
kriyādānaphalodayāḥ
body.translated_text: Then sacrifices come into being, and <s>dharmas</s> and various rites; in the <s>Tretā</s> [there are] resolves of the heart, the rising of the fruit of rite and gift.

body.text:
pracaranti tato varṇās
tapodānaparāyaṇāḥ
svakarmasthāḥ kriyāvantaḥ
samatvād rajasānvitāḥ
body.translated_text: Then the classes proceed, devoted to austerity and gift, established in their own duties, performing rites, endowed—by their equality—with <s>rajas</s>.

body.text:
dvāpare 'pi yuge dharmo
dvibhāgonaḥ pravartate
viṣṇuḥ pītatvam abhyeti
caturdhā veda eva ca
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dvāpara</s> age too, <s>dharma</s> proceeds reduced by two parts; <s>Viṣṇu</s> goes to yellowness, and the <s>Veda</s> [becomes] fourfold.

body.text:
tato 'nye ca caturvedās
trivedāś ca tathāpare
dvivedāś caikavedāś ca
anṛcaś ca tathāpare
body.translated_text: Then [there are] others of four <s>Vedas</s>, and likewise others of three <s>Vedas</s>, of two <s>Vedas</s> and of one <s>Veda</s>, and likewise others without [any] <s>Ṛc</s>.

body.text:
evaṃ śāstreṣu bhinneṣu
bahudhā nīyate kriyā
tapodānapravṛttā ca
rājasī bhavati prajā
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>śāstras</s> are divided, ritual action is conducted in many ways; and the creature, engaged in austerity and gift, becomes <s>rājasic</s>.

body.text:
alpāyuṣo narā vedaḥ
sumahāṃś ceti dustaraḥ
karoti bahudhā vedān
vyāsarūpī tadā hariḥ
body.translated_text: Men [are] short-lived, and the <s>Veda</s> [is] very vast and hard to cross; then <s>Hari</s>, in the form of <s>Vyāsa</s>, makes the <s>Vedas</s> manifold.

body.text:
sattvasya cāpy avijñānāt
sattve kaścid vyavasthitaḥ
sattvāt pracyavamānānāṃ
vyādhayo bahavo 'bhavan
body.translated_text: And from the lack of understanding of <s>sattva</s>, [only] someone [rare] is established in <s>sattva</s>; for those falling away from <s>sattva</s>, many diseases arose.

body.text:
kāmāś copadravāś caiva
tadā daivatakāritāḥ
yair ardyamānāḥ subhṛśaṃ
tapas tapyanti mānavāḥ
body.translated_text: And desires and calamities then [were] brought about by the deities, oppressed exceedingly by which, men practice austerity.

body.text:
dhanakāmāḥ svargakāmā
yajñāṃs tanvanti cāpare
evaṃ dvāparam āsādya
prajāḥ kṣīyanty adharmataḥ
body.translated_text: Desiring wealth, desiring heaven, others perform sacrifices; thus, having reached the <s>Dvāpara</s>, the creatures dwindle from unrighteousness.

body.text:
pādenaikena rājendra
dharmaḥ kaliyuge 'pi hi
tāmasaṃ yugam āsādya
kṛṣṇo bhavati keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: By a single quarter, O lord of kings, [is] <s>dharma</s> in the <s>Kali</s> age too; having reached the <s>tāmasic</s> age, <s>Keśava</s> becomes black (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>).

body.text:
vratācārāḥ praśāmyanti
dharmayajñakriyās tathā
ītayo vyādhayas tandrī
doṣāḥ krodhādayas tathā
upadravāś ca vardhante
manastāpāś ca saṃgatāḥ
body.translated_text: Vow-observances grow calm [cease], and likewise the rites of <s>dharma</s> and sacrifice; calamities, diseases, sloth, the faults of anger and the rest, and afflictions increase, and mental anguishes come together.

body.text:
yugeṣv āvartamāneṣu
loko vyāvartate punaḥ
loke kṣīṇe kṣayaṃ yānti
bhāvā lokapravartakāḥ
yugadvayakṛtān dharmān
prārthanā na ca kurvate
body.translated_text: As the ages revolve, the world turns about again; when the world is diminished, the dispositions that set the world in motion go to destruction; men do not even make a prayer for the <s>dharmas</s> performed in the two [earlier] ages.

body.text:
etat kaliyugaṃ bhūpa
yatra jāto 'si pārthiva
nātrāvatāraṃ kurute
kṛṣṇāṃśena svarūpiṇā
body.translated_text: This is the <s>Kali</s> age, O king, in which you are born, O lord of the earth; in it [Viṣṇu] does not make a descent in his own form by a portion of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

body.text:
kṛtādiṣu jagat pāti
daityebhyo rūpadhṛd dhariḥ
kalau tv anyaṃ samāviśya
pūrvotpannaṃ bibharti tam
body.translated_text: In the <s>Kṛta</s> and the rest, <s>Hari</s>, bearing a [bodily] form, protects the world from the <s>daityas</s>; but in the <s>Kali</s>, having entered into another, born before, he sustains that one.

body.text:
pratyagrarūpadhṛg devo
dṛśyate na kalau hariḥ
kṛtādiṣv eva tenaiṣa
triyugaḥ paripaṭhyate
body.translated_text: The god <s>Hari</s>, bearing a fresh [new] form, is not seen in the <s>Kali</s>; only in the <s>Kṛta</s> and the rest [does he do so]—therefore this one is recited as 'three-aged' (<s>Triyuga</s>).

body.text:
kaler ante ca saṃprāpte
kalkinaṃ brahmavādinam
anupraviśya kurute
vāsudevo jagatsthitim
body.translated_text: And when the end of the <s>Kali</s> is reached, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, having entered into <s>Kalkin</s>, the proclaimer of <s>Brahman</s>, makes the [re-]establishment of the world.

body.text:
pūrvotpanneṣu bhūteṣu
teṣu teṣu kalau prabhuḥ
kṛtvā praveśaṃ kurute
yad abhipretam acyutaḥ
body.translated_text: Into beings born before, this one or that, in the <s>Kali</s>, the Lord, having made [his] entrance, does what is intended, the <s>Acyuta</s>.

body.text:
svecchāśukle jagac chuklaṃ
rakte raktaṃ ca jāyate
pīte ca pītatām asmin
kṛṣṇe cātrāsitaṃ nṛpa
body.translated_text: When by his own will [Viṣṇu becomes] white, the world is born white; when [he is] red, red; and when yellow in him, [the world goes to] yellowness; and when black, black here, O king.

body.text:
eṣa eva jagaddevo
jagatsraṣṭā jagadguruḥ
yadrūpa eva devo 'yaṃ
tadrūpaṃ jāyate jagat
body.translated_text: He, this god of the world, the creator of the world, the teacher of the world—of whatever form this god [is], of that form the world is born.

body.text:
caturyugaṃ naḥ kathitaṃ
saṃkṣepād bhavatākhilam
kaliṃ vistarato brūhi
yatra jāto 'smi bhārgava
body.translated_text: The four ages have been told to us in brief by your honor, entirely; tell the <s>Kali</s> in detail, in which I am born, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.

body.text:
bhagavaty amale viṣṇau
krīḍayā kṛṣṇatāṃ gate
kimāhārāḥ kimācārā
bhaviṣyanti prajās tadā
body.translated_text: When the Blessed stainless <s>Viṣṇu</s> has, in sport, gone to blackness (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>-state), of what food, of what conduct will the creatures then be?

body.text:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ
śūdrāś ca dvija kīdṛśāḥ
bhaviṣyanti kalau prāpte
tan mamācakṣva vistarāt
body.translated_text: Of what kind, O twice-born, will the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s> be when the <s>Kali</s> is reached—tell me that in detail.

body.text:
tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge
tretāyāṃ yajña eva hi
pradhānaṃ dvāpare dānaṃ
satyam eva kalau yuge
body.translated_text: Austerity is supreme in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, sacrifice indeed in the <s>Tretā</s>, gift is chief in the <s>Dvāpara</s>, [and] truth alone in the <s>Kali</s> age.

body.text:
kṛte yuge manaḥśuddhir
asty evāyatnatas tapaḥ
tapo niṣpādyate bhūpa
yogasaṃsādhanaṃ param
body.translated_text: In the <s>Kṛta</s> age there is purity of mind; austerity, indeed, [is attained] effortlessly; austerity is accomplished, O king, [as] the supreme means of attaining <s>yoga</s>.

body.text:
rāgādidoṣaduṣṭena
manasā yat tapo nṛpa
kriyate kleśanāśāya
tat tapo na vimuktaye
body.translated_text: But the austerity which is performed, O king, with a mind sullied by the faults of passion and the rest, for the destruction of affliction—that austerity is not for liberation.

body.text:
tretāyāṃ tu kriyāyajñān
manoyajñāṃs tato narāḥ
vitanvate sthūlataraḥ
panthā dharmasya sa prabho
body.translated_text: In the <s>Tretā</s>, then, men extend ritual sacrifices and then mental sacrifices; that path of <s>dharma</s> is grosser, O Lord.

body.text:
dvāpare nātividvattā
yathā tretāyuge 'bhavat
tataḥ sthūlataraḥ panthā
dānātmā kriyate naraiḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dvāpara</s> [there is] not such great learning as there was in the <s>Tretā</s> age; therefore a grosser path, consisting of gift, is made by men.

body.text:
na vidvattā na śuddhārtho
na śuddhir manasaḥ kalau
yato 'taḥ satyam evaikam
ekāntenopakārakam
body.translated_text: In the <s>Kali</s> [there is] no learning, no pure aim, no purity of mind; therefore truth alone is the one thing of exclusive benefit.

body.text:
yathā satyaṃ tathā kṣāntir
ahiṃsā ca kalau yuge
paropatāpād viratir
narāṇām upakārikā
body.translated_text: As truth, so forbearance and non-injury in the <s>Kali</s> age—the abstaining from tormenting others is beneficial for men.

body.text:
tasmin ghore yuge prāpte
kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvam āgate
yādṛgrūpaṃ jagad idaṃ
bhavatīha śṛṇuṣva tat
body.translated_text: When that terrible age is reached, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has come to blackness, of what form this world becomes here—hear that.

body.text:
rājāno brāhmaṇā vaiśyāḥ
śūdrāś ca manujeśvara
vyājadharmaparāś caiva
dharmavaitaṃsikā janāḥ
body.translated_text: Kings, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s>, O lord of men, [will be] devoted to a pretense of <s>dharma</s>, people who use <s>dharma</s> as a snare [for gain].

body.text:
satyaṃ saṃkṣipyate loke
naraiḥ paṇḍitamānibhiḥ
satyahānyā tatas teṣāṃ
svalpam āyur bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: Truth is curtailed in the world by men who fancy themselves learned; then, from the loss of truth, their life-span will be short.

body.text:
āyuṣaḥ prakṣayād vidyāṃ
na śakṣyanty upaśikṣitum
vidyāhīnān abuddhīṃs tāṃl
lobho 'py abhibhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: From the decay of life-span they will not be able to learn knowledge well; and greed too will overcome those knowledge-less, witless ones.

body.text:
lobhakrodhaparā mūḍhāḥ
kāmavaśyāś ca mānavāḥ
baddhavairā bhaviṣyanti
parasparavadhepsavaḥ
body.translated_text: Fools given to greed and anger, men subject to desire, will become bound in enmity, desirous of slaying one another.

body.text:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ
saṃkīryantaḥ parasparam
śūdratulyā bhaviṣyanti
tapaḥsatyavinākṛtāḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>vaiśyas</s>, mixing together with one another, will become equal to <s>śūdras</s>, bereft of austerity and truth.

body.text:
antyā madhyā bhaviṣyanti
madhyāś cāntāvasāyinaḥ
īdṛśo bhavitā lokaḥ
kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvam āgate
body.translated_text: The lowest will become the middle, and the middle will become the lowest dwellers; such will the world be when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has come to blackness.

body.text:
vastrāṇāṃ pravarā śāṇī
dhānyānāṃ koradūṣakaḥ
bhāryāmitrāś ca puruṣā
bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge
body.translated_text: The best of garments [will be] hempen; of grains, the <s>koradūṣaka</s> [a coarse millet]; and men will become friends of [only] their wives in the <s>Kali</s> age.

body.text:
matsyāmiṣeṇa jīvanto
duhantaś cāpy ajāvikāḥ
goṣu naṣṭāsu puruṣā
bhaviṣyanti tadā nṛpa
body.translated_text: Living by the flesh of fish, and milking even goats and sheep when the cows are gone—such will men become then, O king.

body.text:
sarittīreṣu kuddālair
vāpayiṣyanti cauṣadhīḥ
tāś cāpy alpaphalās teṣāṃ
bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
body.translated_text: On the banks of rivers they will sow herbs with hoes; and those too, of little fruit, will be theirs at the decline of the age.

body.text:
aniṣkrāntās tu saṃbandhāḥ
svagotrāt puruṣarṣabha
aniṣkrāntāni śrāddhāni
bhaviṣyanti ca gehataḥ
body.translated_text: Marriage-bonds will not go forth [outside] from one's own <s>gotra</s>, O bull among men; and <s>śrāddhas</s> (funeral rites) will not go forth from the house.

body.text:
na vratāni cariṣyanti
brāhmaṇā vedanindakāḥ
na yakṣyanti na hoṣyanti
hetuvādavikūlinaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> will not practice vows, [being] revilers of the <s>Veda</s>; they will not sacrifice nor offer oblations, perverse with rationalist argument.

body.text:
prāyaśaḥ kṛpaṇānāṃ ca
tathā bandhimatām api
vidhavānāṃ ca vittāni
hariṣyanti balānvitāḥ
body.translated_text: For the most part, the men endowed with [mere] force will carry off the wealth of the wretched, and likewise of those who are bound, and of widows.

body.text:
anyāyopāttavitteṣu
kariṣyanti narāḥ spṛhām
veśyālāvaṇyabhāveṣu
spṛhāṃ yoṣit kariṣyati
body.translated_text: Men will make longing for wealth gotten by unjust means; women will make longing for the [mere] charms and beauty of harlots.

body.text:
kanyāṃ na yācitā kaścin
na ca kanyāprado naraḥ
kanyā varaś ca cchandena
gṛhīṣyanti parasparam
body.translated_text: No one, unasked, [will give] a maiden, nor [will any] man be a giver of a maiden; the maiden and the bridegroom, by [mere] desire, will take each other.

body.text:
bhāryā na patiśuśrūṣāṃ
tadā kācit kariṣyati
narā devadvijāṃs tyaktvā
bhaviṣyanty anyatomukhāḥ
body.translated_text: No wife then will perform service to [her] husband; men, having abandoned the gods and the twice-born, will become turned toward other things.

body.text:
yajñabhāgabhujo devā
ye vedapaṭhitā dvijāḥ
brahmādyās tān parityajya
narāḥ kālabalātkṛtāḥ
hetuvādaparā devān
kariṣyanty aparāṃs tadā
body.translated_text: The gods who enjoy the sacrificial portions, the twice-born who recite the <s>Veda</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest—abandoning them, men, compelled by the force of the age, devoted to rationalist argument, will then make other [false] gods.

body.text:
ye yavānnā janapadā
godhūmānnās tathaiva ca
tān deśān saṃśrayiṣyanti
narāḥ kaliyuge nṛpa
body.translated_text: Those provinces which [eat] food of barley and likewise food of wheat—those regions men will resort to in the <s>Kali</s> age, O king.

body.text:
na śrāddhaiś ca pitṝṃś cāpi
tarpayiṣyanti mānavāḥ
bahu maṃsyanti te snānaṃ
nāpi śaucaparā narāḥ
body.translated_text: And men will not gratify the ancestors with <s>śrāddhas</s>; they will think bathing of little account, nor [will] men [be] intent on purity.

body.text:
na viṣṇubhaktipravaṇaṃ
narāṇāṃ nṛpa mānasam
bhavitā tu yuge prāpte
kṛṣṇe kārṣṇyopalakṣite
body.translated_text: The mind of men, O king, will not be inclined to devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, when the age is reached, [when] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is marked by blackness.

body.text:
vinindāṃ prathame pāde
kariṣyanti harer narāḥ
yugānte tu harer nāma
naiva kaścid gṛhīṣyati
body.translated_text: In the first quarter [of the Kali] men will make reviling of <s>Hari</s>; but at the end of the age no one at all will even take up the name of <s>Hari</s>.

body.text:
dhanyās te puruṣavyāghra
pāpāmbhodhāv apāpinaḥ
ye nāmāpi kalau viṣṇor
gṛhīṣyanty akṣayātmanaḥ
body.translated_text: Blessed are those, O tiger among men, who, [though] in the ocean of sin, [are] sinless—who, even in the <s>Kali</s>, will take up the very name of <s>Viṣṇu</s> of imperishable nature.

body.text:
dhyāyan hariṃ kṛtayuge
tretādvāparayor yajan
yad āpnoti kalau nāmnā
tad eva parikīrtayan
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Hari</s> in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, sacrificing [to him] in the <s>Tretā</s> and <s>Dvāpara</s>—what one attains [thereby], in the <s>Kali</s> one [attains] by proclaiming that very [name of his].

body.text:
harir harati pāpāni
nāma bhaktyā yadīritam
vāsudeveti na janas
tad evoccārayiṣyati
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> removes sins, [his] name, when uttered with devotion—but the people will not even utter that '<s>Vāsudeva</s>'

body.text:
bahupāṣaṇḍasaṃkīrṇe
jagaty asmin kalau yuge
kṛṣṇāyeti namo 'stv atra
sukṛtī yadi vakṣyati
body.translated_text: In this world mingled with many heretics, in the <s>Kali</s> age, [only] a man of good deeds, if [any], will say here 'Homage to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'

body.text:
hetuvādabalair mohaṃ
kuhakaiś ca jane tadā
pāṣaṇḍinaḥ kariṣyanti
cāturāśramyadūṣakāḥ
body.translated_text: By the force of [false] argumentation and by trickeries, the heretics will then [cause] delusion in the people, defaming the system of the four stages of life

body.text:
pāṣaṇḍabhūtam atyarthaṃ
jagad etad asatkṛtam
bhaviṣyati tadā bhūpa
vṛthāpravrajitotkaṭam
body.translated_text: This world, become exceedingly heretical, ill-made, will then come to be, O king, abounding in those who have vainly taken to wandering-ascetic life

body.text:
na tu dvijātiśuśrūṣāṃ
na svadharmānupālanam
kariṣyanti tadā śūdrāḥ
pravrajyāliṅgino vṛthā
body.translated_text: The <s>śūdras</s>, vainly wearing the marks of [ascetic] wandering, will then perform neither service to the twice-born nor the keeping of their own <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
utkocāḥ saugatāś caiva
mahāyānaratās tathā
bhaviṣyanty atha pāṣaṇḍāḥ
kāpilā bhikṣavas tathā
body.translated_text: Bribe-takers (?) and Buddhists, and likewise those devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, will then become heretics—and the <s>Kāpila</s> mendicants likewise,

body.text:
vṛddhāḥ śrāvakanirgranthāḥ
siddhaputrās tathāpare
bhaviṣyanti durātmānaḥ
śūdrāḥ kaliyuge nṛpa
body.translated_text: the elders, the <s>śrāvakas</s>, the <s>nirgranthas</s> (Jains), and likewise others, the <s>siddhaputras</s>—these wicked-souled <s>śūdras</s> will come to be in the <s>Kali</s> age, O king,

body.text:
niḥśaucā vakramatayaḥ
parapākānnabhojanāḥ
bhaviṣyanti durātmānaḥ
śūdrāḥ pravrajitās tadā
body.translated_text: impure, of crooked minds, eaters of food cooked by others—these wicked-souled <s>śūdras</s>, [having] become wandering ascetics, will then come to be

body.text:
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ
pāṣaṇḍāḥ puruṣarṣabha
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā
bhaviṣyanti tathā pare
body.translated_text: These and many others [will be] heretics, O bull among men; and others likewise will become [false] brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas—

body.text:
rājaśulkaharāḥ kṣudrā
gṛhasthaparimoṣakāḥ
muniveṣākṛticchannā
vāṇijyam upajīvikāḥ
body.translated_text: petty [men] who seize the king's tax-dues, robbers of householders, concealed in the garb and appearance of sages, living by trade

body.text:
na dvijān na kalau devān
pūjayiṣyanti mānavāḥ
mlecchabhāṣānibandhais tu
hetuvādair vikūlitāḥ
body.translated_text: Men will worship neither the twice-born nor the gods in the <s>Kali</s> age, but [will be] led astray by the compositions of <s>mleccha</s> tongues and by [false] argumentation

body.text:
evaṃ teṣv atiduṣṭeṣu
vimārgapathivartinaḥ
bhaviṣyanty apare duṣṭās
teṣāṃ mārgānuyāyinaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, among those exceedingly wicked ones who walk the wrong path, others, wicked, will come to be, the followers of their path

body.text:
asaṃskṛtoktivaktāro
vedaśāstravinindakāḥ
jagadunmārgakartāro
bhaviṣyanti tadā narāḥ
body.translated_text: Speakers of unrefined speech, revilers of the <s>Veda</s> and <s>śāstra</s>, makers of the world's [going on the] wrong path, men will then come to be

body.text:
tacchīlavartibhir bhūpa
manuṣyaiḥ paripūrite
jagaty atra tadā nṝṇāṃ
svalpam āyur bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: When this world is filled, O king, with men of that conduct, then the life-span of men will be short

body.text:
paramāyuś ca bhavitā
tadā varṣāṇi ṣoḍaśa
tataḥ prāṇān prahāsyanti
kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvam āgate
body.translated_text: And the maximum life-span will then be sixteen years; then they will give up their breaths, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [the dark age] has come to [its full] blackness

body.text:
pañcame vātha ṣaṣṭhe vā
varṣe kanyā prasūyate
saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣā vā
prajāsyanti narās tadā
body.translated_text: In the fifth or the sixth year a girl will give birth; and at seven or eight years men will then beget offspring

body.text:
alpadravyā vṛthāliṅgā
hiṃsāratiparāyaṇāḥ
hartāro na tu dātāro
bhaviṣyanti kalau narāḥ
body.translated_text: Of little substance, vainly bearing [ascetic] marks, intent on the delight of violence, robbers and not givers—such will men come to be in the <s>Kali</s> [age]

body.text:
śuklādānaparāḥ kṣudrāḥ
parapākāśino dvijāḥ
vaiśyās tathā tu rājāno
na tu kṣatriyavaṃśajāḥ
body.translated_text: Petty [men] intent on the taking of [others'] property (?), eaters of food cooked by others, [will be the] twice-born; and likewise the vaiśyas [will be] kings, and not those born of the kṣatriya line;

body.text:
śūdrā bhikṣavatā viprāḥ
śuśrūṣāvipaṇāśritāḥ
bhaviṣyanti nṛpaśreṣṭha
kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvam āgate
body.translated_text: the <s>śūdras</s> [will be] mendicant [false] brahmins, [and the brahmins] dependent on service and trade, they will come to be, O best of kings, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [the age] has come to its blackness

body.text:
na śiṣyo na guruḥ kaścin
na putro na pitā tathā
na bhāryā na patir bhūpa
bhavitā tatra saṃkule
body.translated_text: No pupil, no guru, no son and likewise no father, no wife and no husband, O king, will there be in that confusion

body.text:
etat kālasvarūpaṃ te
śatānīka mayoditam
viṣṇubhaktān naraśreṣṭha
na narān bādhate kaliḥ
body.translated_text: This essential nature of the [Kali] age has been declared by me to you, O <s>Śatānīka</s>; but the men who are devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of men, <s>Kali</s> does not afflict

body.text:
ye 'harniśaṃ jagaddhātur
vāsudevasya kīrtanam
kurvanti tān naravyāghra
na kalir bādhate narān
body.translated_text: Those who, day and night, perform the proclaiming of the upholder of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>—those men, O tiger among men, <s>Kali</s> does not afflict

body.text:
ye tanmanaskās tiṣṭhanti
prayāntaḥ saṃsthitās tathā
svapantaś ca naravyāghra
tān kalir na prabādhate
body.translated_text: Those who abide with their minds on him, going [about], standing, and likewise sleeping, O tiger among men—them <s>Kali</s> does not afflict

body.text:
sarvatra bhagavān viṣṇur
govindaḥ keśavo hariḥ
yasya bhāvo na taṃ bhūpa
kadācid bādhate kaliḥ
body.translated_text: He in whose [heart] is the disposition [that] everywhere is the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Hari</s>—him, O king, <s>Kali</s> never afflicts

body.text:
na kalau kaliceṣṭo 'sau
mūḍheṣu na sa muhyate
bhagavaty acyute nityaṃ
yena bhāvaḥ samarpitaḥ
body.translated_text: That [Kali] does not act as Kali toward him, nor is he deluded among the deluded, by whom the [whole] disposition is ever offered to the Blessed <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
kaliprabhāvo duṣṭoktiḥ
pāṣaṇḍānāṃ tathoktayaḥ
na krāmante manas tasya
yasya cetasi keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: The power of <s>Kali</s>, the wicked sayings, and likewise the utterances of the heretics, do not overcome the mind of him in whose heart is <s>Keśava</s>

body.text:
kalau kṛtayugaṃ tasya
kalis tasya kṛte yuge
yasya cetasi govindo
hṛdaye yasya nācyutaḥ
body.translated_text: For him the <s>Kṛta</s> age [exists] within the <s>Kali</s>, [and] the <s>Kali</s> [exists] for him within the <s>Kṛta</s> age, in whose heart is <s>Govinda</s>, [but] in whose heart <s>Acyuta</s> is not

body.text:
aniṣṭvāpi mahāyajñair
akṛtvāpi pitṛsvadhām
kṛṣṇam abhyarcya yad bhaktyā
nainaṃ śvomaraṇaṃ tapet
body.translated_text: Even without sacrificing with the great sacrifices, even without performing the ancestral offering, [for him] who, having worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with devotion—even tomorrow's death does not torment him

body.text:
yasyāgratas tathā pṛṣṭhe
gacchatas tiṣṭhato 'pi vā
govinde niyataṃ cetaḥ
kṛtakṛtyaḥ sadaiva saḥ
body.translated_text: He before whom, and behind whom, [whether] walking or standing, the mind is fixed on <s>Govinda</s>—he is ever indeed one whose duty is fulfilled

body.text:
etad viditvā bhūpāla
sarve sarveśvare harau
tanmanā bhava taccittas
tanmanā nāvasīdati
body.translated_text: Knowing this, O king, in <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of all, become one whose mind is on him, whose heart is on him; one whose mind is on him does not sink down

body.text:
paramārtham aśeṣasya
jagataḥ prabhavāvyayam
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchan
govindaṃ nāvasīdati
body.translated_text: Going for refuge to <s>Govinda</s>, the supreme aim, the imperishable source of the entire world, the [sole] refuge worthy of refuge, one does not sink down

body.text:
kalikalmaṣakakṣāgniṃ
nirvāṇaṃ padam avyayam
sarvakāraṇam avyaktaṃ
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati
body.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>—the fire to the thicket of the sin of <s>Kali</s>, the imperishable state of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the cause of all, the unmanifest—one does not sink

body.text:
yatra sarvamaye dhyāte
dhyeyam anyan na vidyate
yatrārcite 'rcanīyaś ca
jāyate taṃ namāmy aham
body.translated_text: When that one, made of all, is meditated upon, no other object of meditation exists; and when he, the worshipful one, is worshipped, no other worshipful one arises—to him I bow

body.text:
jagatsraṣṭāram iśeśam
anādiṃ parataḥ param
sarvāspadaṃ sarvabhūtaṃ
gacchan sarvātmanā harim
body.translated_text: Going with one's whole self to <s>Hari</s>—the creator of the world, the Lord of lords, the beginningless, the supreme beyond the supreme, the abode of all, the all-being—

body.text:
haraty agham aśeṣaṃ yo
harir ity abhisaṃstutaḥ
aśeṣāghaharaṃ viṣṇuṃ
harivarṇaṃ hariṃ namaḥ
body.translated_text: He who removes all sin, praised as '<s>Hari</s>'—to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the remover of all sin, of tawny color, <s>Hari</s>, homage

body.text:
yatkīrtanād aghaḥ śuddhaḥ
smṛte yatrāśuciḥ suciḥ
tam ātmani sthitaṃ bhūpa
puṇḍarīkekṣaṇaṃ namaḥ
body.translated_text: By the proclaiming of whom sin is cleansed, [and] when he is remembered the impure becomes pure—to him, abiding in the self, O king, the lotus-eyed one, homage

body.text:
apavitraḥ pavitro vā
sarvāvasthagato 'pi vā
yaḥ smaret puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ
sa bāhyābhyantaraḥ śuciḥ
body.translated_text: Whether impure or pure, or [if he be] gone into any condition whatever, he who remembers the lotus-eyed one (<s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>) is pure outwardly and inwardly

body.text:
yady apy upahataḥ pāpair
yadi vātyantaduṣkṛtaiḥ
tathāpi saṃsmaran viṣṇuṃ
sa bāhyābhyantaraḥ śuciḥ
body.translated_text: Even if smitten by sins, or even if [smitten] by exceeding misdeeds, even so, remembering <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he is pure outwardly and inwardly

body.text:
kalāv atrātidoṣāḍhye
viṣayāsaktamānasaḥ
kṛtvāpi pāpaṃ govindaṃ
dhyāyan pāpair vimucyate
body.translated_text: In this <s>Kali</s> [age], abounding in exceeding faults, [a man] of mind attached to sense-objects, even having committed sin, meditating on <s>Govinda</s>, is freed from [his] sins

body.text:
tad dhyānaṃ yatra govindaḥ
sā kathā yatra keśavaḥ
tat karma yat tadarthīyaṃ
kim anyair bahubhāṣitaiḥ
body.translated_text: That meditation in which is <s>Govinda</s>, that tale in which is <s>Keśava</s>, that action which is for his sake—what [need] of other much-talking?

body.text:
naitat pitā tanūjāya
na śiṣyāya gurur nṛpa
paramārthapadaṃ brūyād
yad etat te mayoditam
body.translated_text: Not [even] to a son does a father, nor to a pupil does a guru, O king, declare this supreme-aim state which has been told to you by me

body.text:
saṃsāre bhramatā labhyaṃ
putradāradhanaṃ vasu
suhṛdaś ca tathivānye
nopadeśo nṛpedṛśaḥ
body.translated_text: Sons, wife, wealth, and substance, and likewise friends and others, are obtained by one wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>; [but] such instruction [as this], O king, [is not so obtained]

body.text:
kiṃ putradārair vittair vā
na mitre kṣetrabāndhavaiḥ
upadeṣṭā paro bandhur
īdṛśo yo vimuktaye
body.translated_text: What [use is there] in sons, wife, or wealth, [or] in a friend, [or] in field-kinsmen? The supreme kinsman is the instructor, such a one [who instructs] for liberation

body.text:
yo naikāgramanā viṣṇāv
iti jñātvāpi pārthiva
sa nūnam acyutasyaiva
nānugrāhyo 'tra pāpakṛt
body.translated_text: He who is not single-minded toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, even though he has known this, O king—he is surely not to be favored here by <s>Acyuta</s>, [being] a doer of sin

body.text:
dvividho bhūtasargo 'yaṃ
daiva āsura eva ca
viṣṇubhaktiparo daivo
viparītas tathāsuraḥ
body.translated_text: This creation of beings is twofold: the divine (<s>daiva</s>) and the demonic (<s>āsura</s>); intent on devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the divine, [and] the opposite is the demonic

body.text:
upadeśapradānena
saṃbhūtitraya āsuraḥ
naiva viṣṇuparo bhūpa
bhavaty akṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ
body.translated_text: By the giving of instruction, the demonic [man], of [all] three [castes] arising [from the giving] (?), does not become devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O king, [his] sin being undestroyed

body.text:
upadeśeṣu so 'tyantaṃ
saṃrambhī yuktiyojitam
hetuvādāśrito mūḍho
dadāty uttaram akṣayam
body.translated_text: In [response to] instructions, he, exceedingly contentious, [armed] with applied logic, deluded, relying on [false] argumentation, gives an endless retort

body.text:
snātasya devakāryeṣu
tathāpatsu kathāsu ca
āsurasyāpi tanmātrā
jāyate nṛpate matiḥ
body.translated_text: [But] for one bathed, in the rites of the gods, and in calamities and in [sacred] tales, even of a demonic [nature], a mind in [some] small measure of that [devotion] arises, O king

body.text:
iti matvātisadbhāvaṃ
rahasyaṃ param īritam
tvayācyutān matir bhūpa
nāpaneyā kathaṃcana
body.translated_text: Knowing this, [as] a thing of exceeding good disposition, the supreme secret has been uttered [to you]; by you, O king, the mind is in no way to be drawn away from <s>Acyuta</s>

body.text:
aprāpya vāñchati ratiṃ
sarvadaiva nṛṇāṃ manaḥ
ihaivācyutasaṃsargi
yadi tat kiṃ prahīyate
body.translated_text: Not having attained [it], the mind of men ever desires delight; if that delight, here itself, is one that consorts with <s>Acyuta</s>, what is lost?

body.text:
tad alaṃ tava rājyena
balakośādibhis tathā
cintitair acyutaś cintyo
yadbhāvi na tadanyathā
body.translated_text: So enough of your kingdom, [your] army, treasury, and the rest; <s>Acyuta</s> is to be thought of [rather] than [these] things thought about, for what is to be will not be otherwise

body.text:
etat pavitram ārogyaṃ
dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam
sukhaprītikaraṃ nṝṇāṃ
patatāṃ nirvṛtipradam
body.translated_text: This [text] is purifying, [giver of] health, blessed, the destroyer of bad dreams, the bringer of happiness and joy to men, the giver of bliss to those who are falling

body.text:
yeṣāṃ gṛheṣu likhitam
etat sthāsyati nityadā
na tadgṛhāṇi daivotthā
bādhiṣyante hy upadravāḥ
body.translated_text: In whose houses this will stand ever written, those houses fate-arisen calamities will not afflict

body.text:
kiṃ tīrthaiḥ kiṃ pradānair vā
kiṃ yajñaiḥ kim upoṣitaiḥ
ahany ahany etad eva
tanmayatvena śṛṇvataḥ
body.translated_text: What [need] of sacred fords, what of gifts, or what of sacrifices, what of fasts, for one who hears this very [text] day after day, [becoming] made of him [Viṣṇu]?

body.text:
yao dadāti tilaprasthaṃ
suvarṇasya ca māsakam
śṛṇoti ślokam ekaṃ ca
dharmasyāsya samaṃ hi tat
body.translated_text: He who gives a <s>prastha</s> of sesame and a <s>māṣaka</s> of gold, and he who hears a single verse [of this]—that indeed is equal to [the merit of] this <s>dharma</s>

body.text:
adhyāyapāraṇaṃ cāsya
gopradānāh viśiṣyate
śṛṇvaṃś cāsya daśādhyāyān
sadyaḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: And the completing of a chapter of this is more distinguished than the gift of a cow; and one hearing ten chapters of it is at once freed from [his] sins

body.text:
