rātryā yad enaḥ kurute
divasena ca mānavaḥ
śrotuṃ vāñchā samastaṃ tat
pārthivasya vyapohati
body.translated_text: Whatever sin a man does by night and by day, the wish to hear all this drives away [the sin] of the king

body.text:
kapilānāṃ śate datte
yad bhavej jyeṣṭhapuṣkare
narendra viṣṇudharmāṇāṃ
tadāvāpnoti pāraṇe
body.translated_text: Whatever [merit] there might be, O king, in the giving of a hundred tawny cows at the elder [pond] of <s>Puṣkara</s>—that [merit] one attains at [each] breaking-of-the-fast of the <s>Viṣṇudharmas</s>

body.text:
pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca
dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
nāsty anyad viṣṇudhamāṇāṃ
sadṛśaṃ śāstram uttamam
body.translated_text: In [the path of] engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and in [the path of] cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>), [in respect of] <s>dharma</s>, O best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>, there is no other supreme scripture equal to the <s>Viṣṇudharmas</s>

body.text:
maitrīṃ karoti bhūteṣu
bhaktim atyantam acyute
śrutvā dharmān imān vetti
abhedenātmano jagat
body.translated_text: [He who hears them] makes friendliness toward [all] beings, exceeding devotion toward <s>Acyuta</s>; having heard these <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the world to be non-different from the self

body.text:
paṭhann anudinaṃ dharmān
etāñ śṛṇvaṃs tathāpi vā
bhaktyā matimatāṃ śreṣṭha
sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
body.translated_text: Reciting these <s>dharmas</s> daily, or likewise hearing [them], with devotion, O best of the wise, one is freed from all sins

body.text:
nopasargo na cānartho
na caurāgnibhayaṃ gṛhe
tasmin bhavati bhūpāla
yatraitat pustakaṃ sthitam
body.translated_text: No attack, no misfortune, and no fear of thieves or fire is there in that house, O king, in which this book stands

body.text:
na garbhahāriṇī bhītir
na ca bālagrahā gṛhe
yatraitad bhūpate tatra
na piśācādikād bhayam
body.translated_text: There is no fear of the snatcher of the embryo, nor child-seizing demons in the house; where this is, O king, there is no fear from <s>piśācas</s> and the rest

body.text:
śṛṇvan vipro vedavit syāt
kṣatriyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
ṛddhiṃ prayāti vaiśyaś ca
śūdraś cārogyam ṛcchati
body.translated_text: A <s>vipra</s> hearing [it] becomes a knower of the <s>Veda</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s> [becomes] a lord of the earth, a <s>vaiśya</s> attains prosperity, and a <s>śūdra</s> attains health

body.text:
yaś caitān niyatān dharmān
paṭhec chraddhāsamanvitaḥ
viṣṇau manaḥ samāveśya
sarvatra samadarśanaḥ
body.translated_text: And he who recites these prescribed <s>dharmas</s>, endowed with faith, having absorbed his mind in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of equal vision everywhere—

body.text:
tasya pāpaṃ tathā rogān
duḥsvapnādyābhicārukān
yac cānyad duritaṃ kiṃcit
tat sarvaṃ hanti keśavaḥ
body.translated_text: his sin and likewise diseases, the bad-dream and other bewitching [afflictions], and whatever other evil [there is]—all that <s>Keśava</s> destroys

body.text:
hemante ya imān dharmāñ
śṛṇoti vasudhādhipa
śraddhāsamanvitaḥ samyak
so 'gniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
body.translated_text: He who in the cold season (<s>hemanta</s>) hears these <s>dharmas</s>, O lord of the earth, endowed with faith, rightly, would obtain the fruit of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [sacrifice]

body.text:
śiśire ca naravyāghra
yaḥ śṛṇoti yathāvidhi
puṇḍarīkasya yajñasya
sa prāpnoti phalaṃ naraḥ
body.translated_text: And in the cool season (<s>śiśira</s>), O tiger among men, the man who hears [them] according to rule attains the fruit of the <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> sacrifice

body.text:
madhumādhavasaṃjñe tu
yaḥ śṛṇoti naras tv imān
so 'śvamedhakrator bhūpa
prāpnoty avikalaṃ phalam
body.translated_text: And in [the season] called <s>Madhu-Mādhava</s> (spring), the man who hears these [dharmas], O king, attains the undiminished fruit of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> rite

body.text:
śṛṇvann etān nidāghe ca
dharmān dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
vājapeyasya yajñasya
phalaṃ prāpnoty asaṃśayam
body.translated_text: Hearing these <s>dharmas</s> in the hot season (<s>nidāgha</s>), O best of the upholders of <s>dharma</s>, one attains the fruit of the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice without doubt

body.text:
varṣāsu cemān yo dharmān
saṃśṛṇvan vasudhādhipa
rājasūyakratoḥ puṇyam
akhilaṃ samavāpnuyāt
body.translated_text: And he who, in the rains (<s>varṣā</s>), hears these <s>dharmas</s>, O lord of the earth, would attain the entire merit of the <s>Rājasūya</s> rite

body.text:
śaratkāle ca saṃśṛṇvan
dharmān etān nararṣabha
prāpnoti gosavaphalaṃ
samyak śraddhāsamanvitaḥ
body.translated_text: And hearing these <s>dharmas</s> in the autumn (<s>śarad</s>), O bull among men, one attains the fruit of the <s>Gosava</s>, rightly, endowed with faith

body.text:
ṛtuṣv eteṣv etad eva
paṭhatām api pārthiva
phalaṃ bhavati duṣṭeṣu
graheṣv ete śubhapradāḥ
body.translated_text: In these seasons this very [fruit comes] even to those who [merely] recite [it], O king; and in [the time of] evil planets, these are the bestowers of auspiciousness

body.text:
kapilānāṃ śatasyoktaṃ
yat phalaṃ jyeṣṭhapuṣkare
bhūyo bhūyas tad āpnoti
pāraṇe pāraṇe gate
body.translated_text: The fruit declared [for the giving] of a hundred tawny cows at the elder [pond] of <s>Puṣkara</s>—that one attains again and again at [each] breaking-of-the-fast as it comes

body.text:
bhaktyā paṭhati yaś caitān
devasya purato hareḥ
so 'rcayaty avanīpāla
jñānayajñena keśavam
body.translated_text: And he who recites these with devotion before the god <s>Hari</s>—he worships, O lord of the earth, <s>Keśava</s> with the sacrifice of knowledge (<s>jñānayajña</s>)

body.text:
sarvābādhās tathā pāpam
akhilaṃ manujeśvara
viṣṇudharmā vyapohanti
saṃsmṛtāḥ paṭhitāḥ śrutāḥ
body.translated_text: All afflictions and likewise all sin entire, O lord of men, the <s>Viṣṇudharmas</s> drive away [when] remembered, recited, [or] heard

body.text:
etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ
rahasyaṃ paramaṃ hareḥ
nātaḥ parataraṃ kiṃcic
śrāvyaṃ śrutisukhāvaham
body.translated_text: All this supreme secret of <s>Hari</s> has been declared to you; there is nothing whatever higher than this worth hearing, [nothing] that brings such delight to the ear

body.text:
atroktavidhiyuktasya
puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ
na durlabhaṃ naravyāghra
paramaṃ brahma śāśvatam
body.translated_text: For the man learned [and] endowed with the rule declared here, the supreme eternal <s>Brahman</s> is not hard to attain, O tiger among men
